units.la: ABSOLVI tandem aspirante mihi gratuita Dei misericordia, alteram quoque Homiliarum in Euangelium secundum Matthaeum partem: quae, ut ingenuè fatear quod res est, non exiguo labore nobis constitit: Non quòd mihi unquam laboriosum aut molestum fuerit per amoenissimos Sacrae Scripturae hortos apum instar volitare, & flosculos illos decerpere, ex quibus non solum ferta dilectae IESV CHRISTI Sponsae, Ecclesiae, contexuntur, verumetiam pharmaca illa salutaria conficiuntur, quae sola animam languentem recreare & confirmare possunt. (Quod enim de philosophia sua olim Cicero dixit, id multò rectius de sacrarum literarum studio dici meretur, hanc esse unicam, & veram animorum medicinam & culturam, virtutum indagatricem & expultricem vitiorum.) Sed quod qui cum iunior aetate essem, corporis viribus & animi alacritate valebam, nunc per senectam viribus multum decessisse, & ad lucubrandum porrò minus idoneum me factum esse sentiam. Nam ut Divi Hieronymi verbis utar, solet interdum terram, ex qua desumpta sunt corpora nostra, percutere Deus, ut contremiscat, & cum ita postulat aetatis ratio, nos variis casibus & infirmitatibus exercet, ut nos terram, & mortales esse meminerimus, eòque alacriores & magis industrii simus in iis, quae nobis mandavit; ne quid eorum nobis hinc migraturis imperfectum relinquatur. Ego certè dissimulare neque volo neque debeo, me propter senectam, cuius limen iam pridem transgressus sum, & crebros capitis dolores, non semel solicitum fuisse, ne huic labori absoluendo possem sufficere. Itaque cum mihi haud dubiè Ecclesiae precibus adiuto, praeter opinionem vires dederit Dominus, ut opus istud, in quo prae aliis remoras & obstacula multa & gravia mihi obiici sensi, ad finem deduxerim, quid mihi porrò reliquum est, quàm ut Dei gratiam toties expertus, Christo Seruatori gratias agam, qui ministerio meo in Ecclesia sua, qua nihil pretiosius, nihil carius habet, per annos amplius quadraginta uti dignatus est, & eundem toto animo invocem, ut quos ille mihi dedit labores, Ecclesiae & electis suis utiles facere dignetur: & ut quod reliquum mihi addet vitae huius mortalis tempus, ita dispenset, ut gloriae suae illustrandae, Ecclesiae item aedificandae, & multis servandis inserviat. Scio enim verissimè dixisse Apostolus lum:Ecclesiam Dei aruum,Dei ædificium esse : & proinde neque eum qui plantat,esse aliquid,neque eum qui rigat:sed Deum qui dat incrementum. Itaque quoad meas lucubrationes,nihil mihi tribui uolo,præter colligendi & meditandi laborem & industriam : in qua etsi fidem mihi nunquam defui sse affirmare ausim,non diffiteor tamen,ne in eo quidem aliquid meum esse,& interdum bonum quoque dormitare Homerum. Vt ergo omnia mea orthodoxo Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Christi iudicio subijcio : Ita Lectores admonitos & rogatos uelim,ut me hominem fuisse ita meminerint, ut interea me fratrem in Christo fuisse non obliuiscantur, cui in omnibus suis studijs gloria Dei & hominum salute nihil antiquius fuerit. Porrò dum alteram hanc Homiliarum partem in Euangelicam Matthæi historiam, ut in lucem prodeat,adorno,magna me cura & solicitudine leuatum esse senstio. Solent enim fere qui simile quid instituunt,anxij patronos quærere, qui fœtus illorum teneros in tutelam recipere dignentur, & eosdem suo patrocinio contra zoilorum dentes tueri, aut saltem apud pios & bonos illis aliquam gratiam conciliare possint. At ego ingratus & inhumanus, nedum imprudens & ineptus essem,præstantissime losua , si quem huic libro alium patronum aut tutorem quærerem quàm te, cuius summa est apud omnes tuos authoritas,pietas uero ita nota, ut de uoluntate tua dubitare mihi nefas sit. Priorem enim Matthæi nostri partem tam amicè & humaniter excepisti,ut me tibi obstrictum esse fateri debeam , quoad huius uitæ usuram mihi Deus concesserit. Fui quidem ego Vuittenbachiæ dopmui propter multa beneficia iam ante obstrictus : at inter alios , quos illa nobis genuit uirtute & pietate præclaros & præstantes uiros , te præ alijs semper amaui & colui , propterea quòd mihi ab ipsa adolescentia familiariter non notus modo,uerumetiam addictus fuisti : quando propter egregiæ indolis indicia te in Repub. & Ecclesia talem aliquando fore præuidi, qualem te nunc esse omnes boni prædicant. Accipies ergo hoc quoque nouum mei amoris & obseruantiæ pignus ea fronte , qua me iam olim complexus es; & Ecclesias Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI, quæ hactenus sub tuo dominio,ceu umbra lætissima uersantur, in posterum quoque fideliter tuetor. Ita officium gratum illi præstabis, qui illud æternis regni sui cœlestis præmijs remunerabitur. In hoc te cum tuis omnibus feliciter uiuere & ualere opto. Tiguri iiii, Nonas Februarij. Anno nati in carne æterni Filij Dei M. D. LXXXIIII. secundum uerem & receptum Ecclesiæ calculum.
units.tr: Finished at last, with the free mercy of God breathing upon me, is the second part of my Homilies on the Gospel according to Matthew. To be honest about it, as the matter stands, it has cost me no small labour. Not that it was ever troublesome or tiresome for me to flit like a bee through the most pleasant gardens of Holy Scripture and pluck those little flowers, from which not only garlands for Jesus Christ's beloved Bride, the Church, are woven, but also those healing medicines are made, which alone can refresh and strengthen a languishing soul. (What Cicero once said of his philosophy deserves to be said far more correctly of the study of the sacred letters: that it is the only true medicine and cultivation of souls, the seeker out of virtues and the expeller of vices.) But I feel that, when I was younger and had strength of body and liveliness of mind, I was able; now, in old age, I have lost much of my strength and have become less fit for late-night study. For, to use the words of Saint Jerome, God sometimes strikes the earth from which our bodies were taken, so that it trembles; and when the reason of our age so requires, He exercises us with various misfortunes and infirmities, so that we remember that we are earth and mortal, and therefore may be more eager and more diligent in those things He has entrusted to us, lest anything be left unfinished for us when we depart hence. Certainly I neither wish nor ought to conceal that, because of my old age, over which I long ago crossed the threshold, and my frequent headaches, I have more than once been anxious lest I should be unequal to finishing this labour. Therefore, since the Lord, undoubtedly aided by the prayers of the Church, has beyond my expectation given me strength to bring to completion this work, in which I have felt many serious hindrances and obstacles thrown in my way more than in others, what remains for me but to give thanks to Christ my Saviour, who has deigned to use my ministry in His Church, which has nothing more precious and holds nothing dearer, for more than forty years; and to call upon Him with my whole heart, that He may deign to make the labours He has given me useful to His Church and His elect; and that He may so dispense the remaining time of this mortal life that it may serve to illustrate His glory, to build up the Church likewise, and to help save many. For I know that the Apostle said most truly that the Church of God is God's field, God's building: so neither is he who plants anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase. Therefore, as far as my studies are concerned, I want nothing ascribed to me beyond the labour and diligence of gathering and meditating; and in this, although I would not dare to affirm that I have ever been lacking in faithfulness, I do not deny that even here nothing is mine, and that sometimes even good Homer nods. So I submit all that is mine to the orthodox judgement of the Catholic Church of Christ; and I would have the readers admonished and asked to remember that I was a man, yet at the same time not to forget that I was a brother in Christ, for whom in all his studies the glory of God and the salvation of men were nothing more important. Moreover, while I prepare this second part of the Homilies on the Gospel history of Matthew for publication, I feel that I am relieved of a great care and anxiety. For those who undertake something similar are usually anxious to find patrons who will deign to take their tender offspring under their protection, and to defend them by their patronage against the teeth of Zoilus, or at least to win them some favour among the pious and good. But I would be ungrateful and inhumane, and not only unwise and foolish, most excellent Josua, if I sought any other patron or guardian for this book than you, whose authority is great among all your people, and whose piety is so well known that it would be wrong for me to doubt your goodwill. For you received the first part of my Matthew so kindly and humanely that I must confess myself bound to you for as long as God grants me the use of this life. I was indeed previously bound by many benefits to the house of Wittenbach; but among the other men whom that house has produced, distinguished and eminent in virtue and piety, I have always loved and honoured you above the rest, because from your very youth you have been not only familiarly known to me but even devoted to me; since, from the signs of your outstanding character, I foresaw that you would one day become in the Commonwealth and the Church what all good men now proclaim you to be. Accept, then, this new pledge of my love and esteem with the same countenance with which you have already embraced me; and continue faithfully to protect the Churches of the Son of God Jesus Christ, which hitherto have flourished under your rule as in a most joyful shade. Thus you will render a grateful service to Him who will reward it with the eternal prizes of His heavenly kingdom. I pray that you may live and fare well with all yours. At Zurich, on the fourth day before the Nones of February, in the year of the eternal Son of God born in the flesh, 1584, according to the true and accepted reckoning of the Church.

units.la: IN EVANGELIVM IESV CHRISTI SECVNDVM MATTHAEVM RODOLPHI GVALTHERI TIGVRINI Homiliarum pars altera. CAPVT XV. KOMILIA CXCV.
units.tr: IN THE GOSPEL OF JESUS CHRIST ACCORDING TO MATTHEW, BY RODOLPH GWALTHER OF ZURICH, Homilies, second part. CHAPTER XV. HOMILY CXCV.

units.la: TVnc accedunt ad IESVM Ierosolymitani quidā Scribę & Pharisæi, dicentes: Quare discipuli tui transgrediuntur traditionem seniorum? Non enim lauant manus suas, cum edunt panem.
units.tr: Then certain scribes and Pharisees who had come from Jerusalem came to Jesus and said, "Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."

units.la: PRIMA huius Cap. parte memorabilis actio narratur, quæ Domino nostro IESV CHRISTO cum Scribis & Pharisæis intercessit de humanis traditionibus: Num videlicet hæ observatu necessariæ sint? vel num tantī fieri debeant, ut propter ipsas ea negligi debeant, quæ Deus nobis diserte mandauit. Estq; hæc actio consideratu plus, quā necessaria, quia hic ferè omnium superstitionum fons est, quod homines non contenti Verbo Dei, in religione ex seipsis sapere volunt, & cultus ex suo cerebro nouos instituunt. Etenim iam inde ab origine rerum Deus suam voluntatem reuelauit, quid de se credi, & quomodo a nobis coli velit. At hic duo genera hominum inueniuntur. Vnum eorum est, qui Deum vel omnino nullum esse, vel si quis sit, ea, quæ in terris fiunt, nihil curare sibi persuadent, ideoque nihil referre quid quisq; credat, aut quo ritu illum colat. Alterum eorum, qui cultum omnem in externis ritibus & horum splendore constituunt, quasi Deus ijs delectetur, quæ nobis magnifica videntur. Et hi tantum sibi ipsis tribuunt, ut se putent aliquid perfectius instituere posse, quam in Scripturis traditur: quo fit, ut si in aliqua authoritate sint, sua commenta aliis quoque violenta obtrudere non verentur: quæ causa est, quod tyrannis ferè superstitiones comitari solet. Exempla sunt omnium secularum, quibus hoc probari potest, sed veteribus minimè opus est, quando hodie hæc vnica omnium concertationum de religione causa est. Enimuero vniuersam veræ fidei atque cultus rationem, ex qua salus omnis dependet, in Scripturis prolixè traditam inuenimus: & harum compendium in Decalogo, Symbolo Apostolico & Oratione Dominica nobis Spiritus sanctus proposuit. In horum professione vnanimiter consentiunt, quotquot Christiani dici volunt, adeo ut plerique iam morituri in his acquiescant. Vnde ergo superstitionum diuersitas? vnde differentiones atq; lites enascuntur, quibus hodie orbis Christianus turbatur? Ex ijs solis, quæ posteris temporibus demum ab hominibus superstitiosis inuenta sunt: qualia sunt, Diuorum cœlitum inuocatio & intercessio, imaginum cultus, peregrinationes, feriæ, ciborum delectus, vota monastica, indulgentiæ papales, purgatorius ignis et exequiæ siue sacra pro defunctis, & quæ alia sunt huius generis, quorum nulla in Scripturis fit mentio, & quæ sola hominum authoritate nituntur. Est ergo per quam necessaria huius causæ cognitio, cuius arbiter melior constitui non potest, quam æternus Dei Filius IESVS CHRISTVS, qui nobis æterno Patris decreto Seruator et doctor totius generis humani datus est. Is verò in præsenti sententiam suam diserte & graviter pronuntiat, idq; non in angulo aliquo obscuro, aut inter homines plebeios & rerum eiusmodi ignorantes, sed in publico, & quidem ab ijs prouocatus, qui in Dei populo antistites erant, & supremam doctrinæ & pietatis existimationem sustinebant. Ideo quæ his dicuntur ad omnes pertinent, qui in Ecclesia aliquam authoritatem decernendi de cultu Dei sibi vendicant.
units.tr: The first part of this chapter relates a memorable action that took place between our Lord Jesus Christ and the scribes and Pharisees concerning human traditions: namely, whether these are to be kept at all, or whether they are to be valued so highly that, for their sake, what God has plainly commanded us may be neglected. This action deserves careful consideration, and indeed it is necessary, because here is nearly the fountain of all superstitions: men, not content with the Word of God, want to be wise in religion on their own, and they devise new forms of worship out of their own brains. For God has revealed his will from the beginning of things: what is to be believed about him, and how he wishes to be worshipped by us. Yet two kinds of men are to be found here. One kind persuades itself that God either does not exist at all, or, if he does, that he takes no care of what happens on earth; and therefore it makes no difference what anyone believes or in what manner he worships. The other kind places all worship in external rites and in their splendour, as if God were delighted by those things which seem magnificent to us. And these men attribute so much to themselves that they think they can institute something more perfect than what is handed down in the Scriptures. As a result, if they hold some authority, they do not hesitate to force their inventions upon others as well. This is why superstition usually accompanies tyranny. There are examples from every age by which this can be proved, but there is little need to go back to earlier times, since today this is the one cause of all disputes about religion. Indeed, we find the whole rule of true faith and worship, on which all salvation depends, set out at length in the Scriptures, and the Holy Spirit has given us its summary in the Decalogue, the Apostles' Creed and the Lord's Prayer. All who wish to be called Christians agree unanimously in professing these, so much so that most people, when about to die, rest in them. Whence then the diversity of superstitions? Whence the differences and quarrels by which the Christian world is today troubled? They arise solely from those things which were invented by superstitious men in later times: such as the invocation and intercession of the saints, the veneration of images, pilgrimages, holy days, the selection of foods, monastic vows, papal indulgences, purgatorial fire, and funerals or masses for the dead, and whatever else is of this kind. None of these is mentioned in the Scriptures, and they rest on human authority alone. It is therefore very necessary to know the truth of this matter, and no better judge of it can be appointed than the eternal Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was given by the eternal decree of the Father as Saviour and teacher of the whole human race. Now in this passage he pronounces his judgment plainly and seriously, and not in some dark corner or before common folk ignorant of such matters, but in public, and indeed when challenged by those who were leaders among God's people and held the highest reputation for teaching and piety. Therefore what is said to them pertains to all who in the Church claim for themselves some authority to decide about the worship of God.

units.la: Ordo tractationis hic est. Principio cum ipsis præsulibus & doctoribus agit, quorū res hic potissimum agebatur. Deinde ne horum ambitio & avaritia populo fraudi esset, publicè omnes admonet, quid sentire & facere debeant. Tertio cum discipulis de eo colloquitur, quod disputationi huic occasionem dederat: quo loco fontes peccati & pollutionis omnis monstrat, & docet e contra, quae vera ablutio sive purgatio sit, cui studere debeant, quotquot sanctimoniam, quae sola Deo probatur, sectari volunt. In praesenti occasio totius actionis praemittitur: quae fuit (ut Marcus animadvertit) quod Scribae & Pharisaei aliquos ex IESV discipulis viderunt illotis manibus ad cibum capiendum accumbere. Mox ergo illum aggressi quaestionem movent, qua ipsum populo suspectum atque invisum reddant. At quia derelicto (ut diximus) graui agitur, praestat omnes circumstantias exordine videre.
units.tr: The order of the discussion is this. First, he deals with the very prelates and teachers themselves, whose case was chiefly at issue here. Then, so that their ambition and greed should not be a loss to the people, he publicly admonishes everyone as to what they ought to think and do. Third, he speaks with the disciples about that which had given occasion for this dispute; in this place he shows the sources of all sin and pollution, and teaches on the contrary what the true washing or cleansing is, to which all who wish to pursue that holiness which alone is approved by God ought to devote themselves. In the present case the occasion of the whole action is set out first: it was (as Mark observes) that the scribes and Pharisees saw some of Jesus' disciples eating with unwashed hands. Therefore they at once attack him and raise a question by which they might make him suspect and hateful to the people. But because we have passed over (as we said) the weighty matter, it is better to see all the circumstances in order.

units.la: Primo tempus huius controversiae indicat Matthaeus, quando huius narrationem cum ijs quae praecesserunt connectens, ait: Tunc accedunt, &c. Factum igitur hoc est, quando Genezarethani Christum amice exceperunt, & ipse omnes qui ad ipsum adducebantur, sanauit: quae procul dubio causa fuit, ut in eius cognitione atque fide proficerent. Lucet ergo hic ingenium Satanae, qui tunc potissimum Christo insidiatur, quando eius gloriam illustrari, & regnum Dei surgere videt. Sic quando a Ioanne baptizatus Patris publico testimonio inaugurabatur, confessim illum in desertum eduxit, ut tentationibus insidiosis ipsum ab officio revocaret. Idem ex illius suggestione faciunt hypocritae & impij sive prophani homines. Neutri enim veritatis lucem ferre possunt, quae scelera arguit & larvam eis detrahit, sub qua se occultare student. Et haec causa est dissidiorum, quae oriri solent, ubi Euangelium aliquo cum successu praedicatur. Debent autem tunc vetera exempla in memoriam revocari, ne eorum calumniis moveamur, qui (ut olim Iudaeus ille Sophista, Tertullus garriebat) nostri saeculi turbas Euangelio acceptas ferunt. Actor. 24.
units.tr: First, Matthew indicates the time of this controversy, when, connecting this narrative with what went before, he says: "Then they came," and so on. This therefore happened when the people of Gennesaret had welcomed Christ kindly, and he healed all who were brought to him; this was without doubt the reason why they grew in knowledge and faith of him. The spirit of Satan shines out here, for he lays his snares for Christ especially when he sees his glory made manifest and the kingdom of God rising. Thus, when Christ had been baptized by John and was inaugurated by the public testimony of the Father, at once Satan led him into the desert, so that by insidious temptations he might turn him from his office. The hypocrites and the impious or profane do the same at his prompting. For neither can bear the light of truth, which exposes their crimes and tears away the mask under which they try to hide. This is the cause of the quarrels that usually arise wherever the Gospel is preached with some success. Ancient examples should then be recalled to mind, lest we be moved by the slanders of those who (as the Jewish orator Tertullus once babbled) blame the disturbances of our age on the Gospel. Acts 24.

units.la: Secundo antagonistas Christi videamus, qui item ipsi moverunt. Fuerunt hi Scribae & Pharisaei, & quidem non vulgares, quales per totam Iudaeam & Galilaeam inveniebantur, sed qui Ierosolyma venerant. Erant autem Scribae Legis & Prophetarum interpretes, adeoque ordinarij doctores quorum sententia potissimum rogabantur, si quae causae graviores & dubiae inciderent.
units.tr: Second, let us look at the opponents of Christ who likewise stirred up this trouble. They were the scribes and Pharisees, and not ordinary ones, of the sort found throughout Judaea and Galilee, but men who had come from Jerusalem. The scribes were interpreters of the Law and the Prophets, and so they were the ordinary teachers, whose opinion was chiefly sought if more serious or doubtful cases arose.

units.la: Unde apparet illos non postremam Sacerdotalis muneris dignitatem tenuisse, nimirum quod Sacerdotes otio & fastui diediti, labores subterfugerent. Pharisaei vero praeterea sanctimoniam quoque singularem profitebantur, zelum item cultus divini & populi Dei: eoque magis hi formidabiles erant, quod non vulgaris esset eorum in Republ. authoritas. Cum enim regnante Alexandra, Alexandri Pontificis uxore eius filij Hircanus & Aristob. de Sacerdotio & regno hostiliter contenderent, illa Pharisaeos, quod aliis iustiores & sanctiores haberentur, rerum gubernaculis adhibuit, ut per ipsos Iudaeorum Respub. potissimum administraretur. In primis autem pro patria religionis vindicibus vulgo agnoscebantur, adeo ut penes ipsos esset potestas in eos inquirendi, qui doctrinam novam aut cultus peregrinos introducere putabantur. Apparet hoc ex Ioannis Baptistae historia, ad quem in deserto docentem & baptizantem Ierosolyma missi sunt Sacerdotes & Levitae, quos ex Pharisaeis fuisse, Euangelista docet. Habuerunt ergo vbiq; suos Coricaeos, & si quando necesse videretur, ipsi ex suis aliquos emittebant, qui reliquos in observatione cultus per ipsos institutos retinerent.
units.tr: From this it appears that they held no small dignity of the priestly office, though the priests, given over to idleness and pride, shunned labour. The Pharisees moreover professed a singular sanctity, and likewise zeal for divine worship and for the people of God; and they were all the more formidable because their authority in the commonwealth was not slight. For when Alexandra, the wife of the high priest Alexander, reigned, and her sons Hyrcanus and Aristobulus contended hostilely over the priesthood and the kingdom, she put the Pharisees in charge of the helm of government, because they were considered more righteous and holier than others, so that the Jewish commonwealth might be administered chiefly through them. They were especially recognised by the common people as the defenders of the religion of their country, so much so that the power of inquiring into those who were thought to introduce new teaching or foreign worship lay in their hands. This appears from the history of John the Baptist, to whom priests and Levites were sent from Jerusalem while he was teaching and baptizing in the desert, and the evangelist tells us that these were Pharisees. They therefore had their own Korahites everywhere, and if ever it seemed necessary, they sent some of their own men to keep the rest to the observance of the worship they had instituted.

units.la: Nec temere factum putabimus, quod iflos ex Ierosolyma ad Genezaretanos venisse scribitur. Erat Ierosolyma caput gentis Iudaicae, sedes antiqua regum & verae adorationis atque divini cultus, ubi asseruabatur quicquid Iudaeis memorabile & in pretio habebatur: arca foederis nimirum, Legis sive Decalogi tabulae, Manna, virga Aaronis. Ibidem Sacerdotio functi erant praestantissimi viri, germani successores Aaronis, & inde exire debebat Lex Euangelij per totum orbem: Deniq; Ecclesia IESV CHRISTI omnes promissiones sub typo Ierosolymae terrestris datae erant. At nunc ex eadem prodeunt acerrimi hostes Christi, & eo vsq; res deuenit, ut Propheta non possit alibi mori quam Ierosolymae. Arguunt haec corruptissimum, qui tunc erat, statu religionis inter Iudaeos. Expectabatur Messias iam longo tempore magno cum desiderio per totam Iudaeam et Galilaeam. In sola Ierosolyma idem negligitur, imo inuisus est ijs, qui illic regnabant: nimirum quod sibi derogari sentirent, quicquid ipsi tribuebatur. Et hoc est quod hodie etiam fieri solet ab hypocritis, qui suam exstimatione gloriae Dei & saluti publicae praeferunt. Nulli enim nocentiores Christi & Euangelicae veritatis hostes sunt. Et observare hic debet, quam falluntur, qui religionem doctrinam certis locis astringunt. Quod enim de Ierosolyma dicitur, hoc ipsum de Alexandria, de Antiochia, vbi primum Christiani nominis professio initium habuit; de Constantinopoli item & Roma, cuius fides per omnem orbem celebrata fuit. Ex his locis olim veræ fidei et religionis acerrimi vindices & gloriosissimi Martyres prodierunt. Quid vero hodie in ijsdem fiat, satis notum est. Meminerimus ergo Christi regnum nullo loco alligatum esse, sed Spiritu huius spirare, vbicunque vult, & proinde hunc in Scripturis loquentem audiamus, quæ nos falli & errare non sinent.
units.tr: Nor shall we think it was done rashly that these men are written as coming from Jerusalem to the people of Gennesaret. Jerusalem was the head of the Jewish nation, the ancient seat of kings and of the true worship and divine service, where everything memorable and held in esteem by the Jews was kept: namely, the ark of the covenant, the tables of the Law or the Decalogue, the manna, and Aaron's rod. There the most excellent men, the true successors of Aaron, had performed the priestly office; and from there the Law of the Gospel ought to go out through the whole world. Finally, all the promises of the Church of Jesus Christ had been given under the type of earthly Jerusalem. But now from the same city come the fiercest enemies of Christ, and matters have reached such a point that a prophet cannot die anywhere but in Jerusalem. These things show how thoroughly corrupt was the state of religion among the Jews at that time. The Messiah had long been expected with great longing throughout Judaea and Galilee. In Jerusalem alone he is neglected, and indeed he is hated by those who ruled there, because they felt that whatever was attributed to him was taken away from themselves. And this is what hypocrites are still wont to do today, who put their own reputation before the glory of God and the public welfare. For there are no more harmful enemies of Christ and of evangelical truth. And here we should observe how mistaken are those who tie religion and doctrine to certain places. For what is said of Jerusalem is equally true of Alexandria, of Antioch, where the profession of the Christian name first began; of Constantinople likewise, and of Rome, whose faith was celebrated throughout the whole world. From these places, in former times, the fiercest defenders of true faith and religion and the most glorious martyrs came forth. What is done in these same places today is well enough known. Let us remember, then, that the kingdom of Christ is bound to no place, but breathes where it wills by his Spirit; and therefore let us listen to him speaking in the Scriptures, which will not allow us to be deceived and to err.

units.la: Tertio sequitur occasio, qua Christum aggrediuntur. Vident Scribæ & Pharisæi discipulos non lotis manibus cibum capere. Id eos grauiter offendit, partim quod Deus in Lege externam munditiem diligenter requirit, partim quod hanc illi & omnes Iudæi in ablutionibus externam sjtam existimarent, & (vt Marcus scribit) no manus modo certatim lauarent, verumetiam pocula, sextarios, æramenta, lectos & omnis generis vasa sine suppellectilem. Videntur autem discipuli hoc fecisse secundum exemplum Christi, quem hoc in more habuisse, si quando cum Pharisæis & Scribis ei res fuit, vel quod hoc in præsenti mandauit, ne horum hypocrisim probare putaretur, & vt hanc confutandi occasionem captaret.
units.tr: Thirdly, there follows the occasion on which they attack Christ. The Scribes and Pharisees see his disciples taking food without washing their hands. This offended them greatly, partly because God in the Law diligently requires external cleanness, and partly because they and all the Jews thought this external holiness lay in ablutions. As Mark writes, they not only washed their hands eagerly, but also cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, couches and every sort of vessel or household goods. The disciples seem to have done this following Christ's example, since he had this custom whenever he had to deal with the Pharisees and Scribes, or else because he commanded it on this occasion, so that he would not seem to approve their hypocrisy, and so that he might seize an opportunity to refute it.

units.la: Et docemur illius exemplo, vt nos cum hypocritisset superstitiosis versari conueniat. Manus abluere priusquam ad mensam accedas, & idem post cibum sumptum, mane item & vespere facere, nequaquam illicitum, sed honestum et ciuilitatis morum species est, cui studere conueniet pios, ne rusticitate & sordicie sua sibi ipsis inuidiam & odium accersant. Et potest huc referri admonitio illa Pauli: Quod reliquum est, fratres, quæcunque sunt vera, quæcunque honesta, quæcunque pura, quæcunque amabilia, quæcunque boni nominis, si qua virtus & si qua laus, hæc cogitate. Quia vero sciebat Dominus Pharisæos in his ablutionibus partem cultus diuini, adeoque salutis meritum constituere, mauult inciuiles & sordidus, imo contemptor traditionum a Patribus traditarū habere, quam horum similis fieri, & suo exemplo superstitionibus eorum patrocinari. Debebant hoc obseruare hodie, qui cum Euangelij doctrinam profitentur, tamen manifestis superstitionibus communicant cum ijs, qui preces ad campana pulsum astringunt, & has non soli Deo per Christum, sed Diuis quoq; nuncupant: qui item imagines pro indifferentibus habent, traditiones de ciborum delectu ex cuiusdam sub ciuilis constitutionis prætextu, & alia huius generis faciunt, quæ absq; infirmorum scandalo non possunt fieri ab illis, qui fidem in vnum IESVM CHRISTVM profitentur. Sunt hi Corinthiorum similes, qui ad idolothytorum epulas accedebant, & hoc nomine a Paulo corripiuntur. Quid, quod huic dissimulationes eiusmodi ita displicuerunt, vt Petro quoq; in faciem resistere, cum id in Iudæorum gratiam ab eorum consortio se subduceret, qui ex gentibus crediderant, quibuscum paulo ante familiariter versatus fuerat. Vide Gal.2.
units.tr: We are taught by his example that when we live among superstitious hypocrites we should conduct ourselves fittingly. To wash the hands before approaching the table, and likewise after eating, morning and evening, is by no means unlawful but an honourable appearance of civility, which the godly ought to cultivate, lest by their rudeness and filthiness they bring hatred and odium upon themselves. That exhortation of Paul may be applied here: "Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever honourable, whatever just, whatever pure, whatever lovely, whatever of good report, if there is any virtue and if any praise, think on these things." But since the Lord knew that the Pharisees in these ablutions set up a part of divine worship, and so the merit of salvation, he preferred to appear uncivil and dirty, indeed a despiser of the traditions handed down by the Fathers, rather than to be like them and by his example lend support to their superstitions. Those who today profess the doctrine of the Gospel ought to observe this, yet they take part in manifest superstitions with those who bind their prayers to the sound of the bell, and who address these not only to God through Christ but also to the saints; who likewise regard images as indifferent; who make traditions about the choice of foods under the pretext of some civil regulation; and who do other things of this kind, which cannot be done by those who profess faith in the one Jesus Christ without scandal to the weak. They are like the Corinthians who went to feasts of idol-meat, and for this Paul rebukes them. What of the fact that such dissimulations displeased him so much that he resisted Peter to his face when, out of regard for the Jews, Peter withdrew from the company of those from the Gentiles who had believed, with whom shortly before he had associated familiarly? See Gal. 2.

units.la: Porro audiamus quæstionem, quam Scribæ & Pharisæi mouent. Quare (inquiunt) discipuli tui transgrediuntur traditionem Seniorum? Non absque authoritatis ostentatione, & pro imperio Christi copellant, vtpote quod ipsis cura religionis commendata esset, quam (vt supra dictum est) in eiusmodi nugis magna ex parte consistere arbitrabantur. Initio autem non simpliciter factum discipulorum accusant, ne de re leuicula quærere dicantur: sed a generali criminatione exordiuntur, quod Seniorum siue Patrum traditionem violent: vt sic impietatis reos agant, qui nulla Patrum sanctissimorum religione ducantur, neq; aliquam eorum rationem habeant, quæ illi pie & religiose constituerint, & hucusq; sancte obseruata sint. Et vt crimen discipulis intentatum confirment, præsens hoc illorum factum allegant: Quod non lauent manus suas, cum edut panem. Quis vero non rideat ambitiosos illos sanctimonia ostentatores a tam Tragico exordio ad crimen tam leuiculum transilire, quod in hominibus plebeis & piscatoribus, quibus vsitatissimum erat plus satis quotidie ablui, risum potius, quam reprehensionem, nedum accusationem tam grauem merebatur.
units.tr: Next let us hear the question which the Scribes and Pharisees raise: "Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders?" They put this not without a display of authority, and they press Christ as if by right of command, since the care of religion had been entrusted to them, which (as said above) they judged to consist for the most part in such trifles. At first, however, they do not accuse the disciples' act simply, lest they be said to be seeking a charge over a trifling matter. Instead they begin with a general accusation, that the disciples violate the tradition of the elders or Fathers, so that they make guilty of impiety those who pay no reverence to the most holy Fathers and take no account of what they piously and religiously established and have hitherto observed holily. To confirm the charge brought against the disciples, they cite this present act of theirs: that they do not wash their hands when they eat bread. Who would not laugh at those ambitious displayers of sanctimony, who leap from so tragic a beginning to so trivial a crime? In plebeian men and fishermen, to whom it was most customary to wash quite enough every day, this deserved laughter rather than rebuke, let alone so grave an accusation.

units.la: Sed ita solent superstitiosi, qui veritatis doctrinam persequi semel in animum induxerunt. Quia enim vulgò apud omnes, qui honestatis & pietatis sensu tanguntur, magna est Patrum sive Maiorum authoritas, nefas videtur a religionis forma et ritibus, quos ab illis quasi per manus accepimus, deficere. Ita enim illi damnari videntur. Quapropter hodie etiam frequenter hæ voces audiuntur, contemnina nobis Patrum pijssimorum religionem, Ecclesiæ constitutiones violari, Conciliorum decreta reijci, Canones apostolicos conculcari, & disciplinam ecclesiasticam euerti, &c. Quòd si quæras, quæ nam illa sint, de quorum contemptu & violatione illi tam acerbè queruntur? ridicula illa proferent, Cerea & lampades, aquam consecratam, salem benedictum, campanarum pulsum, ferias, ieiunia siue ciborum delectum, cucullas, liripippia, &c. Quibus deinde nonnulla mo-ra & granium (vt ipsis videntur) adiecerunt. Purgatorium ignem, sacra pro defunctis, Missas, imaginum cultum, indulgentias, & alia sexcenta, quorum nulla fit in sacris literis mentio, et quæ pia & erudita vetustati omnino ignota fuerunt. Attamen ista plus quàm apostolica authoritate omnibus obtrudunt, & ne nimium ridiculi putentur, eadè palliant longi temporis praescriptione, patrum in his pie defunctorum exemplo, prioris seculi felicitate, victoriis, regum & principum con-sensu. Itaq; vt olim, ita hodie adhuc, de foliis traditionibus hominum lis est, quibus superstitiosi homines eandem cum Verbo Dei authoritatem tribuunt.
units.tr: But this is how superstitious people behave, once they have made up their minds to persecute the doctrine of truth. For since among all who are moved by a sense of honesty and piety the authority of the Fathers or ancestors is great, it seems wrong to depart from the form and rites of religion which we have received, as it were, from their hands. For in this way they seem to be condemned. Therefore today too one often hears these cries: that the pious religion of our Fathers is despised, that the constitutions of the Church are violated, that the decrees of councils are rejected, that the apostolic canons are trampled underfoot, and that church discipline is overturned, and so on. But if you ask what those things are over whose contempt and violation they complain so bitterly, they will bring forward those ridiculous things: wax candles and lamps, holy water, blessed salt, the ringing of bells, feast days, fasts or the choice of foods, hoods, liripipes, and so on. To these they have then added some matters of greater weight (as they seem to them): purgatory fire, masses for the dead, the Mass, the cult of images, indulgences, and six hundred other things, of which there is no mention in the sacred letters and which were wholly unknown to pious and learned antiquity. Yet they force these upon everyone with more than apostolic authority, and lest they be thought too ridiculous, they cloak them with prescription of long time, the example of Fathers who died piously in these things, the happiness of the previous century, victories, and the consent of kings and princes. So, as once, so today too there is a dispute about the traditions of men, to which superstitious men attribute the same authority as to the Word of God.

units.la: At ne quem hæ præstigiæ fallant, tenendum est, Traditionis nomine intelligi quasuis constitutiones, quæ non habent expressum Verbu Dei in Scripturis. Et sunt traditiones in triplici differentia. Aliæ enim de doctrina sunt, aliæ de ritibus Ecclesiæ, aliæ de moribus. Quoad doctrinam, nemini fas est huius generis mutare, aut dogma nouum inuehere, quod a Scripturis vel latu pilum differant. Dei enim mandatum est, ne quid eius Verbo addamus, aut ex eo auferamus. Et graui ter testatur Apostolus, anathema censeri debere eu, qui Euangelizare ausit præter id quod euangelizatum est, licet quis Apostolus aut Angelus de cœlo fuerit. Quid enim paleæ cum tritico? inquit Dominus? Traditionis quidem Apostolicæ in doctrina fidei alicubi veteres meminerunt, sed sub hac non aliud quàm symbolum Apostolicum intelligi debere, ex Irenæo constat: cuius articuli omnes ex Scripturis desumpti sunt, & expresso Dei Verbo nituntur. Quoad ritus Ecclesiasticos, sunt hi quoq; partim a Deo instituti, partim ab hominibus inuenti. A Deo institutorum eadem est, quæ doctrina a Deo tradita, authoritas, et proinde a nemine mutari, multò minus aboleri debet.
units.tr: But lest these tricks deceive anyone, it must be held that by the name of tradition are understood any constitutions which do not have the express Word of God in Scripture. There are traditions of three kinds. Some concern doctrine, others the rites of the Church, others morals. As regards doctrine, no one may lawfully change this kind, or introduce a new dogma which differs from the Scriptures even by a hair's breadth. For God commands that nothing be added to his Word or taken away from it. And the Apostle solemnly testifies that whoever dares to preach beside what has been preached should be held accursed, even if he be an apostle or an angel from heaven. "For what has chaff to do with wheat?" says the Lord. The ancients do indeed mention apostolic tradition in matters of faith in places, but it is clear from Irenaeus that under this name nothing else should be understood than the Apostles' Creed, whose articles are all taken from Scripture and rest upon the express Word of God. As regards ecclesiastical rites, these too are partly instituted by God and partly devised by men. Those instituted by God have the same authority as the doctrine delivered by God, and therefore ought to be changed by no one, much less abolished.

units.la: Docet hoc suo exemplo Paulus, qui Cœnam Dominicam in Corinthiorum Ecclesia reformaturus, ad primam illius institutionem eos reuocat, neq; permittit, vt aliam eius formulam recipiant. Idem in cætibus sacris, publicis precibus, baptismo & aliis obseruari debet, ne quid Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI instituto contrarium fiat. Interim fateor, pro temporum & locorum ratione, non eandem esse Ecclesiarum conditionem, & proinde non ijsdem horum vbiq; locorum posse 'catus cogi, neque eundem ordinem in omnibus seruari, quæ tamen varietas Christi institutis nihil derogat, vt quæ non in substantia rerum (vt sic loquar) sed in foliis accidentibus hæret. In his Ecclesiæ sua libertate fruantur, sed ita vt omnia fiant ad ædificationem, neque nouationes non necessariæ introducantur. Et de his illud Pauli intelligi debet: Cætera, cum venero, disponam.
units.tr: Paul teaches this by his example. When he was about to reform the Lord's Supper in the Corinthian church, he recalls them to its first institution and does not allow them to receive any other form of it. The same must be observed in sacred assemblies, public prayers, baptism and the other things, so that nothing contrary to the institution of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, is done. Meanwhile I admit that, according to the circumstances of times and places, the condition of the churches is not everywhere the same, and therefore the same rites cannot be compelled everywhere, nor the same order kept in all. Yet this variety takes nothing away from Christ's institutions, since it clings not to the substance of things (so to speak) but to outward and accidental circumstances. In these matters the churches should enjoy their liberty, but in such a way that all things are done for edification, and no unnecessary innovations are introduced. That saying of Paul should be understood concerning these: "The rest I will set in order when I come."

units.la: Qui tamen generalem hanc regulam præscribit: Omnia decenter & secundum ordinem fiant. Quoad mores, in his quoque constanter Dei Verbo in Scripturis tradito nos insistere conuenit, ne quod olim Deus vetuit, hodie licitum putemus: aut è contra profcelere ducamus, quod ille permisit, imò diserte insfit. Etenim constat sibi ipsi semper Dei voluntas, neq; vnquam virtus probè custodita in vitiu degenerat, neq; vitium virtutis nomen accipit, quacunq; hominum authoritate comendetur. Debent ergo traditiones omnes ad Dei Verbu reuocari, nec vlla recipi, quæ huius voluntati per Verbum tradita aduersatur.
units.tr: Yet he prescribes this general rule: "Let all things be done decently and in order." As regards morals, here too we ought to abide steadfastly by the Word of God delivered in Scripture, so that we do not think lawful today what God once forbade, nor on the contrary count a crime what he permitted, or rather expressly commanded. For God's will is always consistent with itself, and virtue rightly observed never degenerates into vice, nor does vice take the name of virtue, however much it may be commended by human authority. Therefore all traditions ought to be referred back to the Word of God, and none received which runs counter to his will as delivered in the Word.

units.la: Neq; aliquem moueat, quòd multi Iudæorum more & exemplo Seniores siue Patres nobis obiiciunt. Sunt enim Patres in duplici differentia. Primi et veri sine genuini patres sunt ij, quorum fides & religio in Scripturis probatur. Tales in veteri Testamento fuerunt, Abraham pater credentium, Isaac, Iacob, Ioseph, Moses, & post hunc Prophetæ & alij similes: in nouo autem Ioannes Baptista & Apostoli cum viris Apostolicis. De his vere & pie intelligi potest, quod in Lege scripsit Moses: Ne transferas limite proximi tui, quem posuerunt maiores. Et illud Solomonis: ne loco moueas perennes terminos, quos maiores tui constituerunt. Nam ad hos omnes pertinet quod Petrus dicit, sanctos Dei homines non ex suo priuato arbitrio locutos esse, sed ex Spiritu sancti instinctu. E contra Patrum & Seniorum nomine ab aduersarijs commendantur, quinimo quidem seculis aliquot præcesserunt, nō autem perstiterunt in priorum Patrum vestigijs, sed reliquerunt horum fide & religione, ad superstitiones declinarunt, quas vel ipsi commenti sunt vel ab aliis accepeacceperunt. Ex horum numero olim fuerunt, de quibus per Prophetas Deus loquitur: Mendacia ipsorum seduxerunt eos, post quae & patres eorum ambulauerunt. Item, In statutis patrum vestro rum ne ambuletis, & iudicia eorum ne custodiatis, neq; polluamini in idolis eorum: Ego Dominus Deus vester, ambulate in statutis meis. Et rursus: Annon in via patrū vestrum polluti estis? &c. Quod ipsum dici potest de nostri saeculi superstitionum sectatoribus, qui praeterea nouum Patrum genus sectantur, Monachos nimirum, quos suorum Ordinum siue sectarum Patres vocant, in quo rum verba etiam iurant & votis certis sese obstringunt, qua violare maius nefas esse iudicant, quam si quis in Baptismo factum votum impie transgrediatur. Quod quam diuplicuerit olim piis & sanctis viris, quos Spiritus sancti numen propius afflauit, ex D. Hieron. audiant volo, qui in suis ad Galatas commentarijs sic scribit: Cum Abba pater, Hebraeo Syroq; sermone dicatur, & Dominus noster in Euangelio praecipiat, nullum Patrem vocandum, nisi Deum, nescio qua licen- tia in monasterijs vel vocemus hoc nomine alios, vel vocari nos acquiescamus: Et sane ipse praecepit hoc, qui dixerat non esse iurandum: Si non iuramus, ne patrem quidē quempiam nominemus: Si de Patre interpretabimur aliter, & de iurando aliter sentire cogemur. Haec Hieron. At quia de his plura sequentur deinceps, nunc sufficiat monuisse, neminē plausibilibus Patrum aut Seniorum titulis moueri debere. Habent Christiani homines vnum Patrem suum, qui in caelis est: habent praeterea vnicum fidei & salutis magistrum siue doctorem, aeternum Dei Filium IESVM CHRISTVM. Hunc audiant & sequantur, qui est via, lux & veritas. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Nor should anyone be moved by the fact that many, after the manner and example of the Jews, throw in our faces the elders or fathers. For there are fathers in a twofold sense. The first and true, or genuine, fathers are those whose faith and religion are attested in the Scriptures. In the Old Testament these were Abraham, the father of believers, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, and after him the prophets and others like them; in the New Testament, John the Baptist and the apostles together with apostolic men. Of these it can truly and piously be understood what Moses wrote in the Law: "You shall not move your neighbour's landmark, which the fathers have set." And that saying of Solomon: "Do not move the ancient landmarks which your fathers have set." For to all these applies what Peter says, that the holy men of God spoke not from their own private judgment but moved by the impulse of the Holy Spirit. On the other hand, those who are commended by our adversaries under the name of fathers and elders did indeed precede us by some centuries, but they did not persist in the footsteps of the earlier fathers. Rather, they abandoned the faith and religion of those men and turned aside to superstitions, which either they themselves invented or they received from others. Of this number were those of whom God speaks through the prophets: "Their lies have led them astray, after which their fathers also walked." Likewise: "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their judgments, nor be defiled with their idols; I am the Lord your God, walk in my statutes." And again: "Are you not defiled in the way of your fathers? etc." The same may be said of the followers of the superstitions of our own age, who moreover follow a new kind of fathers, namely the monks, whom they call the fathers of their orders or sects, and by whose words they even swear, and to whom they bind themselves by certain vows, which they judge it a greater crime to violate than if anyone impiously broke a vow made at baptism. How much this displeased pious and holy men of old, whom the power of the Holy Spirit inspired more closely, I want you to hear from St. Jerome, who writes thus in his commentary on Galatians: "Since 'Abba, Father' is said in the Hebrew and Syriac tongue, and our Lord in the Gospel commands that no one be called father except God, I do not know by what license in the monasteries we either call others by this name or consent to be called so. And indeed he himself commanded this, who also said that one should not swear: 'If we do not swear, let us not even name any father'; if we interpret it of father, we shall be compelled to think otherwise of swearing." Thus Jerome. But since more about these matters will follow later, it is enough for now to have warned that no one should be moved by the plausible titles of fathers or elders. Christians have one Father, who is in heaven; moreover they have the one teacher and master of faith and salvation, the eternal Son of God, JESUS CHRIST. Let them hear him and follow him, who is the way, the light and the truth. To him belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CXCVI.
units.tr: HOMILIA CXCVI.

units.la: At ille respondens, dixit eis: Quare & vos transgredimini mandatum Dei per traditionem vestram? Nam Deus mandauit, dicens: Honora patrem tuum & matrem. Et qui maledixerit patri aut matri, morte moriatur. Vos autem dicitis: Quicunque dixerit patri aut matri: Donum quodcunque a me erit, tibi proderit: etiamsi nequaquam honorauerit patrem suum aut matrem suam, insons erit. Et irritum fecistis mandatum Dei per traditionem vestram. Hypocritae, bene de vobis prophetauit Isaias, dicens: Appropinquat mihi populus hic ore suo, & labijs me honorat: cor autem eorum procul abest a me. Sed frustra me colunt docentes doctrinas, quae sunt mandata hominum.
units.tr: But he answered and said to them: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying: Honour your father and your mother. And whoever curses father or mother, let him die the death. But you say: Whoever shall say to father or mother, "Whatever gift is from me will profit you," even though he has in no way honoured his father or his mother, he will be blameless. And you have made the commandment of God void by your tradition. Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well of you, saying: This people draws near to me with its mouth, and honours me with its lips, but their heart is far from me. But in vain they worship me, teaching doctrines which are the commandments of men.

units.la: Dominus Deus noster in Scripturis sacris per Verbum suum non modo seipsum et voluntatem suam nobis manifestat, sed insuper grauiter monet, ne quid Verbo ipsius addamus, aut ex eo aliquid auferamus, neue ex nobis ipsis cultus nouos instituamus. Madati huius causae graues sunt: Prima, quia homo animalis non percipit ea quae sunt Spiritus Dei, fieri non potest, quin hallucinen- tur & errent, quicunque in ijs quae ad Deum spectant, volunt ex seipsis sapere, & (vt Scriptura loquitur) post oculos suos scortantur. Altera, quod qui id faciunt, ij non solum ipsi errant, sed ita sibi- ipsis placent in suis figmentis, vt eadem alijs etiam obtrudere conentur. Hinc dissensiones & lites surgunt, & fere fit, vt dum de externis ritibus, qui per homines instituti sunt, contenditur, magis ne cessaria negligantur, sine quibus religio non potest consistere. Et hoc illud est, de quo in praesenti actione Christus cum Scribis & Pharisaeis disserit. Occasione ipsi praebuerunt, quando discipulos eius accusarunt, quod contra traditionem Seniorum ad mensam accubuissent, non prius ablutis manibus. Quibus ita respondet Dominus, vt demonstret, hominum traditiones in religione non solum inutiles, verumetiam impias & noxias esse, eo quod a Deo abducant, & verum cultum impediant.
units.tr: The Lord our God, in the holy Scriptures, through his Word not only makes himself and his will known to us, but moreover earnestly warns that we add nothing to his Word, or take anything away from it, nor institute new forms of worship from ourselves. The reasons for this command are weighty. First, because the natural man does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit of God, it cannot but be that whoever, in matters that pertain to God, wishes to be wise from himself, will go astray and err, and (as Scripture says) play the harlot after his own eyes. Second, those who do this not only err themselves, but are so pleased with their own fictions that they try to force the same upon others. From this arise dissensions and quarrels, and it usually happens that, while contention is waged over external rites instituted by men, the necessary things, without which religion cannot stand, are neglected. And this is the very matter about which Christ, in the present action, disputes with the Scribes and Pharisees. They themselves gave the occasion when they accused his disciples of sitting down to table, without first washing their hands, contrary to the tradition of the elders. The Lord answers them in such a way as to show that human traditions in religion are not only useless but also impious and harmful, because they lead us away from God and hinder true worship.

units.la: Quia vero sibi rem esse sciebat cum contumacibus hypocritis, initio crimen in ipsos regerit, imo Christus crimen graviorum criminum reos agit, quam illud erat, quod discipulis intentabat. Nam dicit, Quare etiam vos in Scribis regetis transgredimini mandatum Dei per traditionem vestram? Poterat factum discipulorum simplici ter defendere, quod cum fecisse suo loco audiemus, quando cum rudis vulgi turba ageret, cui cauteri oportuit, ne illorum exemplo offenderetur. At alia fuit conditio Scribarum, quorum hypocrisim, et impudentiam prius perstringere voluit, ut demonstret indignos esse, quibus ipse rationem reddat de iis, quae sui discipuli faciebant, cum ipsi maiore cum impietate mandata Dei aperte violent, imo eiusmodi traditiones publice doceant, per quas Dei praecepta aboleantur et irrita fiant. Seruit ergo hoc Domini dictum admonitioni omnibus, qui vel in Ecclesia vel Reipub. sibi ipsis ius et authoritatem vendicant in alios, atque indignius ferunt, si quae ipsi sanciunt, non ab omnibus observentur. Fit enim fere hoc iusto Dei iudicio, ut qui huius decreta transgredi audent, eadem opera sibi ipsis et suis constitutionibus authoritatem omnem derogent. Et qua fronte ab aliis factorum rationem exigunt, qui ita res suas instituunt, ut ipsi non possint, aut etiam nolint Deo rationem reddere? Tales certe digni sunt, ut publice arguantur, et larua detrahatur arrogantibus, ut minus noceant suo exemplo.
units.tr: But since he knew that he had to deal with stubborn hypocrites, at the outset he turns the charge back upon them; indeed Christ brings them to account as guilty of a greater crime than the one he had laid against the disciples. For he says: Why do you also, in your turn, transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? He could have defended the disciples' deed simply, as we shall hear him do in its place, when he dealt with the rude crowd, to whom it was necessary to be cautious, lest they be offended by their example. But the situation of the Scribes was different, whose hypocrisy and impudence he wished first to expose, to show that they were unworthy that he should give an account to them of what his disciples did, since they themselves openly violate the commandments of God with greater impiety, and indeed publicly teach such traditions by which God's precepts are abolished and made void. Therefore this saying of the Lord serves as a warning to all who, whether in the Church or in the commonwealth, claim for themselves right and authority over others, and bear it the more indignantly if what they decree is not observed by all. For it generally happens, by the just judgment of God, that those who dare to transgress his decrees thereby strip themselves and their own constitutions of all authority. And with what face do they demand an account of deeds from others, when they so order their own affairs that they cannot, or even will not, render an account to God? Such people certainly deserve to be publicly exposed, and their mask torn off from the arrogant, so that they may do less harm by their example.

units.la: At ne temere eos accusare putetur, qui tunc summa doctrinae et religionis existimationem sustinebant, exemplum adducit, quod tunc nimis vulgare et omnibus notum erat. Deus (inquit) mandauit, dicens: Honora patrem tuum et matrem. Item qui maledixerit patri aut matri, morte moriatur. Vos autem dicitis: Quicunque dixerit patri aut matri, Donum quodcunque a me erit, tibi proderit: etiamsi non honorauerit patrem suum et matrem suam, infans erit, et Legi Dei satisfecisse iudicabitur. Opponit inter se praeceptum Dei de parentibus honorandis, et traditionem pharisaicam, qua filij pro parentum salute sacra facere et donaria in templum afferre, aut in gazophilacium deponere iubebantur. Et verbo Christi sensus hic est: Deus dum parentes honorare iubet, vno verbo omnia, quae hus debentur, pietatis officia complectitur, et haec tanta cum seueritate exigit, ut capitis poenam illis decernat, qui parentes vel maledicto laeserint, vel debitum obsequium contumacius negarint. Quid vero vos? Aliam certe compendiosiorem et vobis quaestuosiorem parentum honorandorum rationem commenti estis. Nam hos inuare docetis, si qui pecunias, quae ipsorum alimonia debebantur, ad vos afferat, et parentum nomine sacrificium aut epulum sacrum instituat. Itaque si patri aut matri egenti et opem flagitanti filius possit dicere: Ego mi pater et mea mater, ut anima tua saluti consulerem, donum magnificum et liberale templo consecraui, ut ibi pro vobis preces fiant et victimae immolentur, etc. Is vestro iudicio, erga parentes omni pietatis officio defunctus erit, etiamsi parentes eius inter ea fame ringantur, et inopia maxima laborent. Atqui nulla Dei Lex est, quae filios pro parentum salute sacra facere, aut sacrificios conducere, vel precus las meritorias pecuniis redimere iubeat. Vt ergo vestro quaestui priuato consuleretis, traditionem istam vos inuexistis in Ecclesiam, quia praeceptum Dei, ex naturae legibus et communi sensu petitum, abrogatur. Et huius generis multa alia constituistis. De his ergo respondeatis mihi velim, priusquam quaeratis, cur mei discipuli manibus illotis panem comedant, etc.
units.tr: But lest it be thought that they are accused rashly, those who then held the highest reputation for teaching and religion, he adduces an example which was then very common and known to all. God, he says, commanded, saying: Honour your father and your mother. Likewise: whoever curses father or mother, let him die the death. But you say: Whoever shall say to father or mother, "Whatever gift is from me will profit you," even though he has not honoured his father and his mother, he will be blameless and will be judged to have satisfied the Law of God. He sets against one another the precept of God concerning the honouring of parents and the Pharisaic tradition, by which sons were ordered to offer sacrifices for the safety of their parents and to bring gifts into the temple, or deposit them in the treasury. And the sense of Christ's words is this: God, while bidding us honour parents, embraces in one word all the duties of piety owed to them, and demands them with such strictness that he decrees the penalty of death for those who have injured parents even by cursing, or have refused the due obedience with stubborn contempt. But what do you do? You have devised another, shorter and more profitable to yourselves, way of honouring parents. For you teach that they are helped if someone brings to you the money which was owed for their maintenance, and establishes a sacrifice or a sacred feast in the name of the parents. So if a son could say to his father or mother, who is needy and begs for help: "I have consecrated a magnificent and generous gift to the temple, so that prayers may be made there for you and victims offered, etc.," then in your judgment he will have discharged every duty of piety towards his parents, even though meanwhile his parents are starving and suffer the greatest want. Yet there is no law of God which commands sons to offer sacrifices for the salvation of parents, or to hire sacrifices, or to buy off meritorious prayers with money. So in order to serve your private gain, you have introduced this tradition into the Church, whereby the commandment of God, drawn from the laws of nature and common sense, is abrogated. And you have established many other things of this kind. Concerning these, therefore, I would like you to answer me, before you ask why my disciples eat bread with unwashed hands, etc.

units.la: Obseruari autem debet, quod Scribas praeceptum Dei de parentibus honorandis irritum fecisse, dicit Dominus. Atqui constat illos nunquam prohibuisse, quo minus filij parentibus debita obsequia praestarent: multo minus decalogu aboleuerunt, quo praeceptorum Dei summa continetur. Dicit tamen illud Christus, quod traditionem eiusmodi introduxissent, quae occasionem praebebat filijs, ut in parentibus alendis effent negligentiores, et alio transferrent quae illorum alimonia debebant seruire. Eadem ergo culpa cum Scribis et Pharisaeis tenentur, quotquot hodie non contenti praeceptis Dei, traditiones nouas inuehunt. Hic enim omnium traditionum effectus est, ut primum diuinis praeceptis aequiparantur, quod horum authoritati derogant, et hominum mentes irritiunt, ut ijs minus attendant. Factum hoc etiam inter Christianos, postquam hominum decretis et statutis locus est datus. Nam licet retineantur passim et recitentur praecepta Dei, orationis itemque Dominicae formula et Symboli Apostolicum, nullus tamen in his omnibus articulus, nullum membrum est, quod saluum et integrum reliquerint traditiones, quae posteris temporibus irrepserunt.
units.tr: But it must be observed that the Lord says that the Scribes made void the commandment of God concerning the honouring of parents. Yet it is certain that they never forbade sons to render the due obedience to their parents; much less did they abolish the Decalogue, in which the sum of God's precepts is contained. Nevertheless Christ says that they had introduced such a tradition as gave occasion to sons to be more negligent in maintaining their parents, and to transfer to other uses what ought to have served for their support. Therefore all who today, not content with God's precepts, bring in new traditions are held under the same fault as the Scribes and Pharisees. For this is the effect of all traditions: first they are placed on a par with divine precepts, and then, because they detract from the authority of these, they dull men's minds so that they attend less to them. This has also happened among Christians, since room has been given to the decrees and statutes of men. For although the precepts of God, the form of the Lord's Prayer and the Apostles' Creed are everywhere retained and recited, yet in all these there is no article, no member, which the traditions that crept in during later times have left safe and whole.

units.la: Etenim primo praecepto Deus, ut sibi uni fidamus, ipsum unum inuocemus, iubet, idem Christus docet, et nos hoc ipsum in primo Symboli articulo profitemur. At per hominum traditiones factum est, ut nouos Deos tutelares sibi fecerint plerique, in quibus spe collocarunt, et quos ijs ipsis verbis inuocarunt, quibus solus Deus caelestis Pater proprie inuocari potest. Deinde ne quam Deo imagnem ponamus, ipse graviter vetat, et ut illum in Spiritu et veritate adoremus, Christus iubet.
units.tr: For in the first precept God commands that we trust in him alone and call upon him alone; Christ teaches the same, and we profess this very thing in the first article of the Creed. Yet through human traditions it has come about that many have made for themselves new guardian gods, in whom they have placed their hope, and whom they have invoked with those very words by which the heavenly God alone, the Father, can properly be invoked. Next, that we should not set up any image of God, he himself forbids gravely, and Christ commands that we worship him in Spirit and truth.

units.la: Quis vero negare poterit, hoc quoq; mandatum Dei, quo nullum frequentius, nullum seuerius in omnibus Scripturis vrgetur, per hominū traditiones abolitum atq; abrogatum fuisse, adeo vt Christiana religio in imaginum cultu potissimum consistere & statuam violare, grauius scelus putetur quàm hominem iugulare? Ne nomen suum temere vsurpemus, vetat Deus, & vt per illud solum iuremus iubet. At hodie nisi per omnes Diuos, quotquot in coelis esse creduntur, iures, nequaquam catholicus & obediens matris Ecclesiae filius esse diceris. Vt sex dies operemur, septimū vero sancto otio & quieti consecremus Dei mandatum est. Diuersum aut traditiones & Ecclesiae statuta iubent: vt nimirum intermisso omni opere necessario otiemur, & dies festos agamus non vni Deo, sed Diuis quoq; & Angelis. Quod si videas, quot modis praeceptum Dei de parentibus honorandis abolitum conculcarint superstitiosarum traditionum patroni, Deum immortale, quàm immane, quàm impudens, quàm insatiabile auaritiae chaos siue barathrum sese proferet? quàm barbara saeuities quàm dira & omnis humanitatis expers ἀσπορία sub traditionum monasticarum velo deprehendetur? Hic certè non pudet illos plus quàm Pharisaica audacia filijs mandare, vt abiecta omni pietate a parentibus discedant, sibi solis viuant, & ne moriturus quidem aliquod officium praestent. Vicissim parentibus authores sunt, vt fraudatis suis liberis atq; alijs legitimis haeredibus, opes suas coenobijs legent, & Christi siue Mariae (vt ipsi loquuntur) peculium faciant, id est, vt sub religionis praetextu sacerdotum luxuriae & faustui seruiant. Dei pronuntiatum est, Non est bonum, hominem esse solum, &c. & Christus coniugij institutū ad primam eius originem reuocans, illius vsum omnibus liberum facit, & per Apostolum dicit: Propter fornicationem suā quisq; vxorem habeat, & propriū quaq; virū habeat. At nostri illi Scribae, vt se eius spiritu agitari demonstrent qui (vt Daniel praedixit) neq; Deum Patrum suorum curat, neq; mulierum legitima cupiditate ducitur, caelibatum commenti sunt, quo nihil impurius orbis vidit, e contra coniuges in carne viuere aiunt, & Deo placere negant. Christus aqua baptizare iussit in nomen Dei Patris, Filij & Spiritus sancti: Idē coenam mysticam in mortis sui commemorationem instituit, & vt ex eodem pane omnes edāt, ex eodē poculo omnes bibant, diserte mandauit: At illi suis traditionibus baptismi formulā abolauerunt, in exorcismos horribiles commutarunt, totū deniq; sale, oleo, sputo prophanarūt: Coenam vero in sacrificiū couerterunt, eandem mutilarunt, & calycem Domini ex illa non abstulerunt. Negent ista posse fieri. At cur negarent, cùm his glorientur atq; superbiant? Quoties ergo illi nobis lite mouent, cur contra maiorū traditiones atq; statuta reformationem in Ecclesijs nostris instituerimus, nos vicissim cum Christo illos interrogabimus, cur ipsi praecepta & instituta Dei transgrediantur, vt suas traditiones feruent atq; stabiliant? Quia vero qui tales sunt, sub pia & bona intentionis praetextu Iefe occultant, obiurgatione graui & seria hanc laruam ipsis detrahit, dicens: Hypocritae, bene de vobis prophetauit Isaias, &c. Hypocritas vocat, & ita criminis reos agit, quo in ijs, quae ad Deum spectant, vix aliud grauius & Deo magis exosum est, qui cum ipsa sit veritas, fucum & simulationem ferre nequaquam poterit. Erant autem hypocritae quoad Deum & homines. Nam illum externa pietatis & sanctimoniae specie placare conabantur, cùm corde ab omni pietate essent alienissimi. Deinde similiter fuco hominibus quoq;, seipsos commendabant, & toti populo cultus siue religionis simulatae erant authores. Itaq; nefarij & scelerati erant impostores, & in hoc vnum intenti, vt extincta veritatis lucem, quàm Dei Filius inferebat, suae existimationi & quaestui prospicerent. Deinde ne affectui indulgere, & conuicium ipsis facere putaretur, se non primum esse docet, qui hoc nomine eos accusat, cùm idem de illis olim dixerit Isaias. Bene (inquit) aut vere de vobis prophetauit Isaias, dicens, Appropinquat mihi hic populus ore suo, & labijs me honorat, &c. At constat, Isaiam de sui seculi hypocritis ista dixisse. Attamen Christus suis aduersarijs illam descriptionem applicat, eò quòd veterum illorum essent similes. Vt enim hypocrisis sui semper similis est, ita Deus quoq; sibi ipsi semper constat, & quae olim ipsi displicuerunt, ea illi hodie etiam improbantur. Testatur hoc ipse per Ieremiam dicens: An super his non visitabo, & gentem huic similem non vlciscere tur anima mea? Quae ergo olim Prophetae de hypocritis, idololatris, auaris & raptoribus, adulteris, homicidis, aliisq; scelera tis, ex Spiritus sancti suggestione dixerunt, eadem sibi dicta existiment, quotquot ijsdem moribus viuunt.
units.tr: Yet who could deny that this command of God, which is urged more often and more sternly than any other in all the Scriptures, has been abolished and set aside by human traditions, so that the Christian religion is thought to consist chiefly in the worship of images, and to break a statue is considered a graver crime than to cut a man's throat? God forbids us to use his name rashly and commands that we swear by it alone. Yet today, unless you swear by all the saints, however many are believed to be in heaven, you are not considered a catholic and obedient son of mother Church. God's command is that we work six days and consecrate the seventh to holy rest and quiet. But traditions and the statutes of the Church command the opposite: namely, that we should give up all necessary work and keep festival days not to God alone, but also to the saints and the angels. And if you look at the many ways in which the defenders of superstitious traditions have trampled underfoot God's command to honour parents, O immortal God, what a monstrous, shameless, insatiable chasm or abyss of greed will reveal itself! What barbarous cruelty, what dreadful lack of all humanity [ἀστοργία], will be discovered under the veil of monastic traditions! Here they are certainly not ashamed, with more than Pharisaical boldness, to instruct their sons to cast off all piety, to leave their parents, to live for themselves alone, and not to render any duty even to a dying parent. In turn, they advise parents to bequeath their wealth to the monasteries, defrauding their own children and other lawful heirs, and to make it a property of Christ or of Mary (as they themselves put it), that is, to serve, under the pretext of religion, the luxury and pomp of the priests. It has been declared by God, "It is not good for man to be alone," etc. And Christ, recalling the institution of marriage to its first origin, makes its use free for all, and through the Apostle says: "Because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, and each woman her own husband." But those Scribes of ours, to show that they are driven by the spirit of him who (as Daniel foretold) regards neither the God of his fathers nor the lawful desire of women, have invented celibacy, than which the world has never seen anything more impure; on the contrary, they say that spouses live in the flesh and deny that they please God. Christ commanded baptism with water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. He likewise instituted the mystical supper in remembrance of his death, and he expressly commanded that all should eat of the same bread and all drink from the same cup. But they, by their traditions, have abolished the form of baptism, changed it into horrible exorcisms, and finally profaned the whole rite with salt, oil and spittle. The Supper they have turned into a sacrifice, mutilated it, and did not take the cup of the Lord away from it. They may deny that these things can be done; but why would they deny them, when they boast of them and take pride in them? Therefore, whenever they bring lawsuits against us because we have instituted reform in our churches against the traditions and statutes of our forefathers, we in turn will ask them, with Christ, why they themselves transgress the precepts and institutions of God, in order to preserve and establish their own traditions. But because such men hide themselves under the pious and good pretext of intention, a serious and weighty rebuke tears this mask from them, saying: "Hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you," etc. He calls them hypocrites and so holds them guilty of crime; for in matters that concern God, scarcely anything is more grievous or more hateful to God, who is truth itself and can by no means bear pretence and feigning. Now they were hypocrites both towards God and towards men. For they tried to placate him with an outward appearance of piety and sanctity, when in heart they were most alien from all piety. Then, in the same way, they commended themselves to men by deception, and were the authors of a whole people's worship or religion that was only pretended. Therefore they were wicked and criminal impostors, intent on this one thing: that, with the light of truth that the Son of God brought being extinguished, they might look out for their own reputation and gain. Then, lest it be thought that he is indulging feeling or heaping abuse upon them, he teaches that he is not the first to accuse them under this name, since Isaiah had said the same of them long ago. "Well," he says, "or truly, did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying: This people draws near to me with its mouth, and honours me with its lips," etc. It is agreed that Isaiah said these things about the hypocrites of his own age. Yet Christ applies that description to his adversaries, because they were like those ancients. For just as hypocrisy is always like itself, so God too is always consistent with himself, and what once displeased him is still disapproved today. He bears witness to this himself through Jeremiah, saying: "Shall I not visit these things upon them? Shall not my soul take vengeance on a nation like this?" Therefore, whatever the prophets once said by the prompting of the Holy Spirit about hypocrites, idolaters, the greedy and plunderers, adulterers, murderers and other criminals, let all who live by the same morals consider these words to be said to themselves.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: Caeterum duo in hypocritis ifiis Dominus per Isaiae testimonium reprehendit. Primum, quod ore suo appropinquent, & labiis Deum honorent, id est, quod se veri Dei cultores esse profitean-tur, hunc magnifice praedicent, et eius opera atq; beneficia laudet, cum cordibus ab illo sint prorsus alieni. Hypocrisim ergo accusat, quae semper animos a vera Dei cognitione & timore alienos ar-guit. Etenim qui Deum vere norunt, ij eundem non possunt non timere, ideoq; sibi ab omni dolo & simulatione diligenter cauent, qua ipsum offendi ficiunt. Alterum, quod timor eorum, id est, religio & cultus omnis, quo Dei timorem simulent, ex hominum mandatis siue traditionibus pendeat, quibus imbuti, circa externas modo ceremonias occupentur, ea autem negligant, quibus solus Deus colì potest. Hoc dicto autem hypocrisis & superstitionis fontem detegit. Enimuero norunt homines ex communi sensu, qui in nobis reliquum mansit, esse Deu, qui omnia gubernet, & eundem timeri atq; coli debere. At quia nostri intellectus acumine (ut saepe diximus) non possumus percipere ea, quae sunt Spiritus Dei; quis & qualis hic sit, & quae vera sit eius colendi ratio, ex nobis ipsis non vide-mus. Ex eius igitur Verbo haec discamus oportet, cuius lucerna sola mentes illuminat, & vias nostras dirigit. Vt primum ergo ab hac recedituir, mox nostra intentionis caligine decepti, cultus ex nobis ipsis inflituimus, magnificos quidem in specie, sed qui praeter splendorem externum nihil habent, quod hominis mentem aliquo religionis sensu afficere possit. Nam etsi aliquid restet, quod cum Dei inflitutis conuenit, tamen hoc quoq; fuco & simulatione adulteratur, dum solis externis inten-ti, eo longius a Deo discedimus, quo pertinacius illis adhaerem us, quibus illi neq; opus est, neq; coli aut honorari potest. Et talem quidem olim fuisse religionem Iudaeorum, sermones Prophetarum docent, per quos Deus ea quoq; sacra damnat & reicit, quae ipse patribus eorum tradiderat, cum ijs vaca-rent abs fide, quae sola cor hominis purificat, & nos Deo commendat. Vsus ergo huius loci nobis hic est, ut procul relictis hominum traditionibus, Deum in spiritu & veritate adoremus per fi-dem in Filium illum Vnigenitum IESVM CHRISTVM, cuius foliis merito ille nobis pla-catus est. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Furthermore, the Lord, through the testimony of Isaiah, rebukes two things in these hypocrites. The first is that they draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, that is, they profess to be true worshippers of the true God, they praise him magnificently and extol his works and benefits, while their hearts are utterly far from him. He therefore accuses hypocrisy, which always proves that minds are estranged from the true knowledge and fear of God. For those who truly know God cannot but fear him, and therefore they carefully guard themselves against all deceit and pretence by which they would make him offended. The second is that their fear, that is, their religion and all their worship by which they pretend to fear God, depends on the commandments or traditions of men; imbued with these, they busy themselves only with external ceremonies, while neglecting those things by which God alone can be worshipped. In this saying, moreover, he uncovers the source of hypocrisy and superstition. Indeed, men know from the common sense that remains in us that there is God, who governs all things, and that he ought to be feared and worshipped. But because we cannot, by the keenness of our intellect (as we have often said), perceive those things which are of the Spirit of God, we do not see from ourselves who and what he is, and what the true way of worshipping him is. We must therefore learn these things from his Word, the only lamp that illumines minds and directs our paths.
