Sibi ergo applicet singuli, quod fui seculi hominibus Isaias dicit: Quòd si dixerint vobis, Sciscitamini a pythonicis, diuinis, qui murmurant & susurrant: Annon quaeq; gens suos deos consulit? Num pro viuis ad mortuos. Ad Legem & testimonium. Et qui non dixerint secundum Verbum hoc, ijs non erit lux matutina, &c. Isa. 8.
units.tr: But we must carefully observe what we also noted above: that although God could have used quite different words, he repeats those things which he once declared through his servants the Prophets, and which had long since been committed to writing. For through David he had once said to the predestined Saviour of the human race: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee." Through Isaiah, moreover, he had testified concerning the same: "Behold my servant, in whom I uphold; my elect, in whom my soul delighteth." And when he promised the same under the name of that great and catholic Prophet through Moses, he likewise added: "Hear ye him." Therefore, just as Moses and Elijah, who represented the person of all the servants of God of the Old Testament, appeared here with him, so he wished to speak in their words too. This contributes greatly to the commendation of the Old Scripture, so that we may not doubt that it (as Paul afterwards plainly affirmed) was inspired by God, and that the words of God are those which are written in its books. Therefore let all who desire to hear God speaking turn to these books, and not (as that rich man in the parable) demand that other teachers be sent from another world. For if God himself wished to speak to us with a human voice as he once did, he would say nothing other than what he once said. For his will is always consistent with itself, and therefore his Word also remains forever. Thus the Son of God appealed to the Scriptures, and not only before he died but even after he rose from the dead he drew the arguments of his discourses from Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms. Therefore those who seek a new kind of doctrine act very foolishly; and those who dare to preach anything beyond what has been proclaimed as the gospel ought to be judged by Christians as anathema, even if they were angels from heaven or Apostles. Let us then look at this oracle, which consists of three parts. Let each one apply to himself what Isaiah says to the people of his own age: "And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards, that peep, and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead? To the law and to the testimony: and if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Isaiah 8.

units.la: Prima docet, quis sit IESVS hic quoad suam personam sine essentiam, nimirum Filius suus dilectus. Quo epitheto eum a nobis distinguit, qui cum natura filij irae & inimici simus, propter adoptionis gratuitam beneficiū filij & haeredes Dei dicimur. At IESVS Filius Dei semper dilectus est, vtpote verus & germanus Filius adeoq; naturalis & Patri coessentialis & aeternus, cui cum Patre nulla vnquam lis aut dissensio intercesserit. Et cum talem agnoscat Deus IESVM hunc qui ex Maria Virgine caro factus est, id est, Abrahami semen (vt Apostolus interpretatur) vel verum hominem assumpsit, constat illum in vna eademq; persona Deum simul & hominem esse, quam lem tota veteris & noui Testamenti Scriptura esse docet: & ipse non verbis modò, sed re ipsa & factis abundè demonstrauit. Testimonia autem Scripturarum, quia alibi allegauimus, non opus nunc repetere. Vt vero talem illum agnoscamus, necesse est: quia in hoc fidei Christianae & totius salutis cardo versatur, & ideo talem in Symbolo quoq; Apostolico profitemur.
units.tr: The first part teaches who Jesus is, as to his person or essence, namely, his beloved Son. By this epithet he distinguishes him from us, who, since by nature we are children of wrath and enemies, are called sons and heirs of God through the free benefit of adoption. But Jesus, the Son of God, is always beloved, being a true and genuine Son, and thus natural, co-essential with the Father, and eternal, with whom the Father never had any quarrel or dissension. And since God acknowledges Jesus as such, who was made flesh from the virgin Mary, that is, the seed of Abraham (as the Apostle explains), or took upon himself a true man, it is clear that he is at the same time God and man in one and the same person, which the whole Scripture of the Old and New Testament teaches; and he himself has abundantly demonstrated this not only in words but in fact and deeds. The testimonies of Scripture, since we have cited them elsewhere, need not be repeated now. But it is necessary that we acknowledge him as such, because on this hinges the foundation of the Christian faith and of all salvation, and therefore we also profess him as such in the Apostles' Creed.

units.la: Secunda parte officium describit, cui ipsum destinauit, dicens: In quo mihi bene complacitum est: Vel in quo placatus sum, siue acquiesco. Ita ergo Filium diligit Pater, vt in eo nos quoq; sibi gratos & acceptos habeat, vt Paulus ad Ephesios ait: Est enim Mediator inter Patrem & nos, qui cum propter peccatum filij irae & a Deo alieni essemus, Mediatore & sequestro nobis opus erat, qui nos illi reconciliaret. Atqui talis nemo ex hominibus poterat inueniri, eo quòd eadem esset omnium fors & conditio. Suum ergo Filium huic muneri destinauit Deus, qui ideo homo factus est, vt cum carne peccata quoq; nostra in se reciperet, & ea mortis sua merito expiaret, nobis item ipsi persidem infitis suam communicaret iustitiam. Docent hoc passim sacrae literae, & est hoc praecipuum bonitatis Dei argumentum, qui nos ita dilexit, vt Filium suum Vnigenitum pro nobis tradere dignatus sit. Et debet eius consideratio nos consolari in tentationibus, ne dubitemus, quin reliqua quoq; omnia in illo nobis gratificetur. Vide Rom. 8.
units.tr: The second part describes the office to which he has appointed him, saying: "in whom I am well pleased," or, in whom I am appeased or find rest. Thus the Father so loves the Son that in him he also holds us as pleasing and acceptable to himself, as Paul says to the Ephesians: "For there is one Mediator between God and men." For since we, on account of sin, were children of wrath and aliens from God, we needed a Mediator and go-between who would reconcile us to him. But no such person could be found among men, because the lot and condition of all was the same. Therefore God appointed his own Son to this office, who for this reason was made man, so that he might take upon himself our sins together with our flesh and expiate them by the merit of his death, and likewise impart his own righteousness to us who are engrafted into him by faith. The holy Scriptures teach this everywhere, and this is the chief proof of the goodness of God, who loved us so much that he deigned to deliver his only-begotten Son for us. And consideration of this ought to comfort us in temptations, so that we do not doubt that he will grant us all other things in him. See Romans 8.

units.la: At simul quid nos vicissim facere conueniat, meminisse oportet. Admonet de hoc Pater vno verbo, dicens: Ipsum audite. Ergo illum nobis non Mediatorem modò & Seruatorem, verumetiam doctorem dedit. Ideo per Isaiam olim de illo dicebat: Ecce testem populis dedi eum, principem item & magistrum populis. Et talem Moses fore dixit, quando Prophetam illum magnum pollicetur, quem IESVM CHRISTVM Petrus & Stephanus testantur. Et talis quidem, etiam priusquam in mundum veniret, & homo fieret, fuit. Ipse enim cum prisci s patribus egit. Ipse per Spiritum suum in Prophetis locutus est, Petro teste. Et vt talem in praesenti illum producit Pater, ita ipse se ad Euangelizandum misiuum esse, publice fatetur, & in eo assiduus fuit. Ipse postea discipulos toti orbi terrarum doctores dedit, & in ipsis Euangelij ministerium sanciuit, quod in Ecclesia semper retineri debet. Idem de dextera Patris dona Spiritus sui distribuit, & Ecclesiae sua dat Apostolos, Prophetas, Euangelistas & doctores, quorum ministerio illa aedificetur & seruetur. Nostrum ergo est illum in ministris suis & Euangelio loquentem audire: Ad omnes enim Euangelij praecones pertinet, quod Apostolus dicebat: Qui vos audit, me audit: qui verò me audit, audit eum qui misit me. Ideo antiquitus, cum primum inciperet Ecclesia, qui Christo nomen dabant & tandem Christiani dicti sunt, discipuli dicebantur, vt hoc nomine admonerentur, Christianam religionem non consistere sine doctrina, quae fidem & obedientiam requirit: fidem nimirum, quae nos Christo vnit, & eidem mancipat, vt illi omnes sensus, intellectum & nos totos subijciamus. Opus aut ad hoc diligenti attentione, de qua in sementis parabola diximus: fide ita, ne de Euangelij veritate dubitemus, sed ipsum plane agnoscamus talem, qualem Apostoli praedicarunt: fidem vero testemur obedientia, qua nos & sensus nostros omnes ipsius voluntati, quam per Euangelium nobis reuelat, subijciamus. Etenim sine hac nihil proficitur, vt supra Cap. 7. ipse testatur, dicens: Non omnis qui dicit mihi Domine Domine intrabit in regnum meum, sed qui fecerit voluntatem Patris, &c. Et notum est illud: Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei & custodiunt illud. Luc. 11.
units.tr: But at the same time we must remember what we in turn ought to do. The Father admonishes us about this in one word, saying: Hear him. So he has given us Him not only as Mediator and Saviour but also as teacher. Therefore through Isaiah he said of him long ago: Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, also a prince and teacher to the peoples. Moses said that he would be such a one when he promised that great Prophet, whom Peter and Stephen testify to be Jesus Christ. And indeed he was such a one even before he came into the world and became man. For he himself dealt with the fathers of old. He himself spoke through his Spirit in the Prophets, as Peter testifies. And just as the Father now presents him as such, so he himself openly confesses that he was sent to preach the gospel, and he was constant in it. Afterwards he gave his disciples as teachers to the whole world, and in them he established the ministry of the Gospel, which must always be retained in the Church. The same one distributes the gifts of his Spirit from the right hand of the Father, and gives to his Church apostles, prophets, evangelists and teachers, by whose ministry it is built up and preserved. It is therefore our duty to hear him speaking in his ministers and in the Gospel. For what the Apostle said pertains to all heralds of the Gospel: He who hears you hears me, and he who hears me hears him who sent me. Therefore in ancient times, when the Church first began, those who gave their name to Christ, and who at last were called Christians, were called disciples, so that by this name they might be reminded that the Christian religion cannot exist without doctrine, which requires faith and obedience: faith, namely, which unites us to Christ and binds us to him, so that we subject to him all our senses, our understanding, and ourselves wholly. The work for this requires diligent attention, of which we spoke in the parable of the sower: with faith, so that we do not doubt the truth of the Gospel but plainly acknowledge it to be such as the Apostles preached; and we bear witness to our faith by obedience, by which we subject ourselves and all our senses to his will, which he reveals to us through the Gospel. For nothing is gained without this, as he himself testifies above in chapter 7, saying: Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter into my kingdom, but he who does the will of the Father, etc. And that saying is well known: Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it. Luke 11.

units.la: Porrò videamus, vt his omnibus affecti fuerint tres illi discipuli, quos prae aliis sua clarificationis testes esse voluit. His auditis ceciderunt in faciem suam, & timuerunt vehementer. Est hoc argumentum naturae humanae per omnia corrupta & vitiosa. Quia enim in peccatis concepti & nati in multis peccamus, fit, ut male nobis conscij, non possimus coram Deo Creatore nostro comparere. Exemplum huius infirmitatis primus parens noster Adam praebuit, quando Dei in Para diso ambulantis, & ipsum quaerentis voce territus in pedes se coniecit & fugit. Quod ipsum adhuc hodie omnibus accidit, qui seipsos recte noverunt, & suam infirmitatem cum Dei iustitia & malitiae conferunt. Simile quid de Petro Lucas scribit, quod miraculosa piscium captura territus ad pedes IESV acciderit, dicens: Exi a me Domine, quia homo peccator sum. At si tanta est nostra infirmitas, ut ad opera Dei, quibus suam bonitatem nobis ille commendat, expanescamus: si item discipuli isti, qui reliquis omnibus praestabant, hanc voce gratiae & consolationis plenissimam non potuerunt sustinere, quid fiat, quando iustitia sua rigorem, & Legis minas Deus proferat, & iure nobiscum agat? Nimium ergo infelices sunt, qui suis viribus & meritis aliquid tribuunt, & non potius cum Davide clamant: Ne ingrediaris in iudicium cum servo tuo, &c. Psal. 143. Discamus ergo nos quoque humiliari in conspectu Domini, & nostrijpsorum nos pudeat, ne cum Pharisaeis confidentibus & superbis condemnemur.
units.tr: Let us look further at how all these things affected those three disciples, whom he wanted to be witnesses of his glorification above the others. Hearing these things they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid. It is this argument: human nature is corrupt and faulty in every respect. For since we are conceived and born in sins, and sin in many ways, we are, being conscious of our evil, unable to stand before God our Creator. Our first parent Adam gave an example of this weakness, when, terrified by the voice of God walking in Paradise and seeking him, he threw himself at his feet and fled. The same thing still happens today to all who know themselves rightly and compare their weakness with the justice and malice of God. Luke writes something similar about Peter: that he, struck with terror by the miraculous catch of fish, fell at the feet of Jesus, saying: Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man. But if our weakness is so great that we shrink back from the works of God, by which he commends his goodness to us, and if those disciples, who excelled all the others, could not bear this voice, so full of grace and consolation, what will happen when God shows the rigour of his justice and the threats of the Law, and deals with us by right? Those therefore are very unhappy who attribute anything to their own strength and merits, and do not rather cry out with David: Do not enter into judgment with your servant, etc. Psalm 143. Let us therefore learn to humble ourselves before the face of the Lord, and let us be ashamed of ourselves, lest we be condemned with the confident and proud Pharisees.

units.la: Consoletur autem nos, quod Dominus discipulos prostratos non neglexit, sed propius accedes tetigit eos, & amice eosdem compellans ait: Surgite, & ne timete. Etenim ideo nos terrere solet, ut nos consolandi occasionem habeat. Ideo (ut Anna Samuelis mater canebat) occidit, ut vitae restituat: ideo deiicit, ut erigat & exaltet. Audiamus ergo nos consolantem, & animos nostros attollamus ex terrore, quem spiritus de illius bonitate opinio in nobis peperit: & mox sentiemus nos ipsius manu subleuari, qui nos supra vires tentari non finit. 1. Cor. 10.
units.tr: Yet it comforts us that the Lord did not neglect the disciples lying prostrate, but drew near and touched them, and speaking to them kindly said: Rise, and do not be afraid. For he is accustomed to frighten us in order to have an occasion of comforting us. Therefore (as Hannah, the mother of Samuel, sang) he kills, so that he may restore to life; he casts down, so that he may raise up and exalt. Let us therefore hear him consoling us, and let us lift up our spirits out of the terror which the thought of his goodness has produced in us; and soon we shall feel ourselves raised by his hand, who does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength. 1 Cor. 10.

units.la: At hic diligenti consideratione dignum est, quod discipuli isti sublatis oculis neminem viderunt, nisi IESVM solum. Antea cum ipso collocuti sunt Moses & Elias, & quid ei Hierosolymae eventurum esset, exposuerunt, & (ut Lucas scribit) his peractis digressi sunt: Quo adumbratu fuit, quod alibi dicitur, Legem & Prophetas ad Ioannem usque durare, qui Christum, cuius praecur sor erat, coram monstrauit. Itaque isti quasi iam officio suo defuncti discesserunt. Itaque quando voce illa Deus Pater intonuit HIC EST FILIVS ILLE MEVS DILECTVS IN QVO PLACATVS SVM: IPSVM AVDITE: neque Moses neque Elias adfuit, & solum IESVM viderunt discipuli, ut constet, voce illa de illo solo intelligi, & ipsum solum pro mediatore & redemptore agnosci debere, qui nos cum Deo Patre in gratiam reducat, & verba vitae aeternae habeat. Coti net ergo historia ista certa & perfecta doctrina de salutis ratione, de qua hodie passim cotenditur: in qua contentione pleriq; Concilij vniuersalis determinatione expectant, aut decretis eorum Cocilio rustandum esse existimant, quae a paucis seculis ex Romanorum Pontificum authoritate indicta et celebrata sunt. At quod Concilium dabimus huic conferendum, quod in monte isto IESVS coegit? Ad hoc secum adduxit ex viuentibus tres discipulos, quos sibi familiarissimos habuit, & qui totum caetu discipulorum eius repraesentarunt, quos tunc in terris habuit, Petrum, Ioannem & Iacobum. Ex defunctorum & iam in caelis agentium Sanctorum numero adfuerunt Moses & Elias, qui cum illo de morte eius colloquuntur, in cuius merito omnis nostra redemptio consistit. Et Moses quidem illi testimonium tulit, & adhuc hodie paedagogus est ad illum omnes deducens. Idem de Prophetis omnibus dicere possumus, quorum omnium personam Elias sustinuit. Fuerunt ergo in hoc caetu coiuncti, Moses, Patriarchae, Prophetae & Apostoli. In Spiritu Sancto autem collectos fuisse, nemo negare poterit, nisi qui hunc a Deo Patre & Filio auellere velit. Decretum vero huius Concilij promulgat ipse Pater ex nube. Et quale nam? HIC EST Filius ille meus dilectus, in quo placatus sum: Ipsum audite. Et dum hoc promulgatur, Moses & Elias, quasi suo officio defuncti, nulli adsunt, discipuli vero & Apostoli prostrati & inutiles iacent, & ab ipsdem a Domino relictus nemo praeter solum IESVM cernitur. Ergo hic solus est, qui Patrem nobis placavit, solus noster apud hunc Mediator est & Sacerdos aeternus, solus Rex. Idem ad se solum vocat omnes esurientes, sitientes, qui laborant & onerati sunt. Ipse nobis pastor, panis & fons vitae, lux denique & via est. Hunc solum praedicarunt Apostoli, quos ipse orbis doctores constituit. Hunc solum nouerunt, & aliud nomen sub caelo datum esse negauerunt, in quo nos seruari oporteat. Quid ergo opus est disputare & contendere? Num nos plura quam
units.tr: But here it is worth careful consideration that when the disciples lifted up their eyes they saw no one except Jesus alone. Before this Moses and Elijah had talked with him and explained what was to happen to him at Jerusalem, and (as Luke writes) when these things were done they departed. This was foreshadowed by what is said elsewhere, that the Law and the Prophets lasted until John, who pointed out Christ, whose forerunner he was, before them. And so these men, as if their office was now finished, departed. Therefore when God the Father thundered with that voice: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him, neither Moses nor Elijah was present, and the disciples saw only Jesus, so that it is clear that this voice refers to him alone, and that he alone must be acknowledged as Mediator and Redeemer, who reconciles us with God the Father and has the words of eternal life. This story therefore contains a sure and complete doctrine of the way of salvation, about which there is everywhere dispute today. In this dispute many await the decision of a universal council, or think that they must yield to the decrees of councils, which in the last few centuries were called and held by the authority of the Roman Pontiffs. But what council shall we set against this one, which Jesus gathered on that mountain? To this he brought with him from among the living three disciples, whom he held as his most intimate, and who represented the whole company of his disciples whom he then had on earth: Peter, John and James. From the number of the saints who have died and now live in heaven, Moses and Elijah were present, who talked with him about his death, on whose merit all our redemption rests. And Moses indeed bore witness to him, and still today is a guide leading all to him. The same we can say of all the Prophets, whose person Elijah sustained. In this assembly, therefore, were gathered Moses, the Patriarchs, the Prophets and the Apostles. That they were gathered in the Holy Spirit no one can deny, except one who wishes to tear this assembly away from God the Father and the Son. But the decree of this council is announced by the Father himself out of the cloud. And what is it? This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear him. And while this is being proclaimed, Moses and Elijah, as if finished with their office, are not present, while the disciples and Apostles lie prostrate and useless, and, the Lord having left them, no one is seen except Jesus alone. So he alone is the one who reconciled the Father to us; he alone is our Mediator and eternal Priest before him; he alone is King. He alone calls to himself all who hunger, thirst, labour and are burdened. He is our shepherd, bread and fountain of life, and finally light and way. The Apostles, whom he himself appointed teachers of the world, preached him alone. They knew him alone, and they denied that there is any other name under heaven given by which we must be saved. Why then is there need to dispute and contend? Do we want more than

units.la: Discipuli vi- sione & voce Dei consternatur. Gen.3. Luc.5.
units.tr: The disciples are dismayed by the vision and voice of God. Gen. 3; Luc. 5.

units.la: Christus terrretos solacur. 1.Sam.3.
units.tr: Christ comforts the terrified. 1 Sam. 3.

units.la: Solus Iesus Seruator. Iuc.16.
units.tr: Jesus alone is Saviour. Iuc. 16.

units.la: Concilium Thaboriunm.
units.tr: The assembly on Mount Tabor.

units.la: Gal.3.
units.tr: Gal. 3.

units.la: Matth.17. Ioan.7.10. 6.8.14. 1.Cor.3. Act.4. Prophetā & Apostoli nouisse volumus? num ipso inuito gloriam, quæ illi debetur, in alios aut nos ipsos transferre volumus? num regni Dei noua iura, nouas leges ipsi constituere audemus? Num Deo Patri alium Mediatore obtrudere, aut in eius conspectu alia via, quàm qua ille nos ingredi iubet, penetrabimus? Quin ipsum audiamus idem cum Patre dicente: Ego sum Via, Veritas & Vita: nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: Matth. 17; Ioan. 7, 10, 6, 8, 14; 1 Cor. 3; Act. 4. Do we wish to know the prophets and the Apostles? Do we wish, against his will, to transfer to others, or to ourselves, the glory that is due to him? Do we dare to lay down for ourselves new laws and new rights of the kingdom of God? Do we want to force another Mediator on God the Father, or to find our way into his presence by a route other than the one by which he bids us enter? Rather, let us listen to him, since the Father says the same: "I am the Way, the Truth and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through me." To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 213.

units.la: Et cum descenderent de monte, mandauit eis Iesus, dicens: Nemini dixeritis hanc visionem vsquequo filius hominis a mortuis resurgat. Tunc interrogauerunt eum discipuli sui, dicentes: Quid igitur Scribæ dicunt, oportere vt Elias primum veniat? Iesus autem respondens dixit eis: Elias quidem venit primum, & restituet omnia. Sed dico vobis, Eliā iam venisse, & non agnouerunt eum, sed fecerunt ei quæcunque voluerunt. Ita futurum est vt & Filius hominis patiatur ab eis. Tunc intellexerunt discipuli, hæc eum de Ioanne Baptista ipsis dixisse.
units.tr: And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, "Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from the dead." And his disciples asked him, saying, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?" But he answered and said to them, "Elijah indeed comes first and will restore all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognise him, but did to him whatever they pleased. So also the Son of Man will suffer at their hands." Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist. (Matt. 17:9-13)

units.la: Filius Dei & Seruator noster IESVS CHRISTVS se discipulos non seruorum, sed amicorum loco habere ait, idque eo argumento probat, quòd nihil eos celet, sed ipsis nota faciat, quæcunque a Patre suo audierit. Eius fidei & bonitatis indicium certissimum est, quòd non solum Patris voluntatem ipsis docendo exposuit, & diuinam suam virtutem per opera miraculosa manifestauit, verumetiam seipsum illis in cælesti gloria, in qua olim ad iudicium veniet, spectandū præbuit: vt nimirum hoc gustu beatæ immortalitatis confirmati crucem & persecutionum certamina, quæ ipsos manebant, facilius superarent. Cæterum quia in visionibus eiusmodi multa nos impediunt, vt verum earum vsum non percipiamus, multa etiam alio vocant, nouum cum discipulis colloquium orditur Dominus, quo illos plenius instituit de ijs, in quibus adhuc hærebant.
units.tr: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and our Saviour, says that he regards his disciples not as servants but as friends, and he proves this by the fact that he hides nothing from them but makes known to them everything he has heard from his Father. The surest sign of his faithfulness and kindness is that he not only explained the Father's will to them by teaching, and revealed his divine power through miraculous works, but also showed them himself in the heavenly glory in which he will one day come to judgment. The purpose, of course, was that, strengthened by this taste of blessed immortality, they might more easily overcome the cross and the struggles of persecution that awaited them. But since many things in visions of this kind hinder us from grasping their true use, and many things also draw us elsewhere, the Lord begins a new conversation with the disciples, in which he more fully instructs them about the matters on which they were still stuck.

units.la: Principio cum de monte descenderent, mandat eis, ne quod viderant & audierant, cuiquam enuntient, vsquequo ipse a mortuis resurgat. Causa huius mandati eadem fuit, quæ nuper, quando prohibuit, ne ipsum dicerent esse CHRISTVM: quòd nimirum neq; ipsi satis instructi essent adhuc, vt plenam eius cognitionem possent tradere, neq; populus huic visioni fidem habiturus fuisset, cum omnium mentes falsa de regno Messiæ terreno & temporali opinione essent fascinatæ. Itaq; opus erat, vt præcederet signum Ionæ Prophetæ, quod semel atq; iterum promiserat, id est, vt Christus morte & resurrectione sua demonstraret, se promissum illi Seruatorē esse, qui mundo in suis delictis & sceleribus perdito salutē afferat. Quod autē idem mandatum in præsenti repetit & inculcat, non absq; certa ratione fit. Primò nō ignorabat Christus humani ingenij curiositatē et confidentiā quā sublimia cognoscere cupimus, & deinde eorundem cognitione efferri & superbire solemus, atq; alios præ nobis contemnere: cuius vitij exemplū in Corin. Paulus proponit, quibus dicit: Scientia inflat, charitas vero ædificat. Quin ipsemet vitiū istud in sanctissimis Dei seruis locū habere proprio exemplo docet, quando de reuelationibus et visionibus Domini loquēs, addit: Ne excellentia reuelationum supra modū efferrer, datus est mihi surculus vel aculeus carni infixus, et angelus Satanæ, vt me colaphis cedat, ne supra modū efferar. Quòd si Paulū hoc modo subigi & coerceri oportuit, cui tantū agmen laborū atq; curarū incumbebat, & qui ipse in istar strenui & fortis athletæ corpus suū cōtundere et in seruitutē redigere solebat, ne aliqua ex parte reprobus fieret, quid sibi de seipsis alij polliceantur, quos Dei Spiritus non tanta donorū copia afflauit? Ne ergo tres illi discipuli, quos præ cæteris ipso honore dignatus erat Dominus, vt eos diuino huic cœcilio & spectaculo planè cælesti adhiberet, aliquid humanū paterentur, et cofidentius gloriarentur de ijs, quæ viderat, peccatum mandato illos coerceri opus fuit. Deinde alia quoq; causa accessit, vt ex ijs quæ sequuntur appareat. Nam dubiū quid ipsorum animis inhærebat de Elia quē in monte cum Domino colloqui, mox autem ab eo discedere, & cū Mose in suū locū abire viderant. Cum ergo communi errore ex falsa Scribarum traditione concepto putarent, Eliam Messiæ præcursorem fore illum ab hoc abiisse mirantur, nec possunt videre, quomodo ista inter se conveniant, ut IESVS dicatur esse Christus, non autem eum Elias praecedat. Rursus igitur hoc mandato illis occasionem praebere voluit inter rogandi de eo, quod illos dubios tenebat, & simul cavere, ne intempestive quid effutiant.
units.tr: First, as they come down from the mountain, he commands them not to tell anyone what they had seen and heard until he himself is raised from the dead. The reason for this command was the same as before, when he forbade them to say that he was Christ. Clearly the disciples were not yet sufficiently instructed to be able to pass on a full knowledge of him, and the people would not have believed this vision, since everyone's minds were bewitched by the false opinion of a earthly and temporal kingdom of the Messiah. So it was necessary that the sign of the prophet Jonah, which he had promised once and again, should come first, that is, that Christ should demonstrate by his death and resurrection that he is the promised Saviour who brings salvation to a world lost in its sins and crimes. Now, that he repeats and presses the same command here is not done without a definite reason. First, Christ did not fail to notice the curiosity and self-confidence of the human mind, by which we desire to know sublime things, and by which we are wont to be puffed up and to become proud through that knowledge, and to despise others in comparison with ourselves. Paul sets before the Corinthians an example of this vice when he says: "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up." Indeed, he himself shows by his own example that this vice has a place even among the most holy servants of God, when, speaking of the revelations and visions of the Lord, he adds: "Lest I be exalted above measure by the greatness of the revelations, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, to buffet me, lest I be exalted above measure" (2 Cor. 12:7). But if Paul had to be subdued and restrained in this way, he to whom so great a host of labours and cares pressed, and who, like a vigorous and brave athlete, was wont to beat down his body and bring it into servitude, lest he become in any way reprobate, what should others promise themselves, whom the Spirit of God has not inspired with such an abundance of gifts? So, lest those three disciples, whom the Lord had deigned to honour above the rest by admitting them to this divine secret and to a truly heavenly spectacle, should suffer some human weakness and boast more confidently of what they had seen, it was necessary that they be restrained by this command. Then another reason also came in, which will appear from what follows. For there was doubt in their minds about Elijah, whom they had seen conversing with the Lord on the mountain, and who then soon departed from him and went away to his place with Moses. Therefore, since by a common error, conceived from the false tradition of the scribes, they supposed that Elijah would be the forerunner of the Messiah, they wonder that he had gone away, and they cannot see how these things agree with one another: that Jesus should be called Christ, and yet Elijah not go before him. So once again by this command he wanted to give them an occasion to ask about what held them in doubt, and at the same time to take care that they did not blurt out anything at the wrong time.

units.la: Hoc ut Domini nostri divinam & paternam erga nos bonitatem commendat, qui nos vult salvos fieri, & ideo discendi occasiones nobis offert: ita monet, ut quiduis suo loco & tempore tradatur, & simul auditorum ratio habeatur, ne forte qui adhuc infirmiores sunt offendantur, si sublimiora mysteria audiant, quorum ipsi nondum capaces sunt. Solet hoc frequenter fieri, & tunc quidem in primis, quando sublimia illa hi tractant, qui ne ipsi quidem ea adhuc intelligunt, ingenii autem ostentando vel eruditionis vel sanctimoniae laudem privatam potius captant, quam ut audito res ad regnum Dei solide instituantur. Tales erant apud Corinthios & in aliis quoque Ecclesiis scioli quidam, qui ut se plus aliis profecisse ostenderent, ad idolothytorum epulas accumbebant magno cum infirmorum scandalo, qui libertatis Christianae beneficium nondum intelligebant: Alii item rigidiores aequo temeri damnabant omnes, quos sua libertate videbant offendi. Et nostro saeculo multi dum sibi ipsis nimium indulgent, sua importunitate multos privatim offendunt, & publice Ecclesias periculose turbant. Quisque ergo seipsum suo pede metiatur, aliorum vero quibus cum versatur diligentem rationem habeat, ut reliquis non necessariis disputationibus alii alios in vera fide & pietate aedificent.
units.tr: By this the divine and fatherly kindness of our Lord towards us is commended, since he wishes us to be saved, and therefore offers us opportunities for learning. He thus advises that whatever is taught be taught in its proper place and time, and at the same time that the capacity of the hearers be taken into account, lest perhaps those who are still weaker be offended if they hear the higher mysteries, for which they are not yet capable. This happens often, and especially when those who do not yet understand these lofty matters themselves take them up, seeking, by showing off their cleverness, the private praise of learning or holiness, rather than that, once the matter is heard, the kingdom of God be solidly established. Such were certain half-learned men among the Corinthians and in other churches as well, who, to show that they had advanced further than others, reclined at feasts of idol-meat, to the great scandal of the weak, who did not yet understand the benefit of Christian liberty. Others again, being too harsh and rash, condemned all those whom they saw offended by that liberty. And in our own age many, while they indulge themselves too much, privately offend many by their unseemly conduct, and publicly disturb the churches dangerously. Let each therefore measure himself by his own foot, and let him have careful regard for others among whom he lives, so that, by avoiding unnecessary disputes, they may build one another up in true faith and piety.

units.la: Sed ad discipulos Christi transeamus, qui bene quidem vtuntur occasione per Dominum oblata, ita tamen, ut rursus prodant suam in regni Dei mysteriis tarditatem. Nam etsi non ita pridem diserte illis dixisset, se Hierosolymae moriturum & a mortuis resurrecturum tertio die, tamen (ut Marcus annotavit) de eo disputant inter se, quid sit a mortuis resurgere. Quia enim illum in terris regnaturum putant more regum huius saeculi, non possunt videre, quomodo mors tristis & infamis cum regno conveniat, & quia non credunt moriturum, resurrectione etiam non opus fore arbitrantur, & proinde per hanc nescio quid aliud intelligunt, imo quid intelligere debeant, nesciunt. Caeterum correptione veriti, omissa hac quaestione, alia movent de Elia, quae est huiusmodi: Quid igitur Scribae dicunt, oportere ut Elias primum veniat? Quaestioni huius occasionem praebuit Malachiae oraculum, per quem olim Deus patribus dixerat: En ego mitto vobis Eliam Prophetam, priusquam dies Domini magnus et terribilis veniat. Is reducet cor patrum in filios, & cor filiorum in patres suos, ne veniat, & terram percutiat anathemate. Quem locum vulgo secundum literam de Elia Thesbite reversuro in terras intelligebant Iudaei, & proinde Scribae vel Legis interpretes ex eo contra Christum & huius discipulos sic argumentabantur: Messiae adventum magnum & illustrem praecedet Elias e caelo aut beatorum sedibus, in quas translatus est, reversus, & omnia instaurabit & restituet: At hucusque Elias nullus venit: Ergo Messias quoque nondum exhibitus est, & pro inde turpis error est, quod multi IESVM hunc Messiam esse arbitrantur.
units.tr: But let us turn to the disciples of Christ, who indeed use well the occasion offered by the Lord, yet in such a way that they again reveal their slowness in the mysteries of the kingdom of God. For although not long before he had plainly told them that he would die at Jerusalem and rise from the dead on the third day, nevertheless (as Mark noted) they dispute among themselves what it is to rise from the dead. For since they think he will reign on earth in the manner of the kings of this age, they cannot see how a sad and shameful death fits with a kingdom; and because they do not believe he will die, they think there is no need of a resurrection either, and therefore they do not understand, or rather do not know what they ought to understand, by it. But fearing rebuke, they set aside this question and raise another about Elijah, which is of this kind: "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?" The occasion for this question was the oracle of Malachi, through whom God once said to the fathers: "Behold, I send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes. He will turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a curse." The Jews generally understood this passage literally, of Elijah the Tishbite returning to the earth, and therefore the scribes, or interpreters of the Law, argued from it against Christ and his disciples in this way: "Before the great and illustrious coming of the Messiah, Elijah will go before him, returning from heaven or from the abodes of the blessed into which he was taken, and he will restore and renew all things. But so far Elijah has not come. Therefore the Messiah also has not yet appeared, and so it is a foolish error that many think this Jesus is the Messiah."

units.la: Adumbratur in hoc sophismate communis nostri hostis diaboli astutia, qui Scripturis & oraculis Dei contra veritatem abuti novit, ut simpliciores a fide abducat. Promiserat quidem Deus, se Eliam missurum, qui instar praecursoris populum in Messiae adventum excitet, & viam huic aeternat, ad regnum suum instaurandum. Sed quis Elias ille futurus esset, annis fere trecentis ante Malachiam docuerat per Isaiam, qui vocem clamantis, id est, praeconis cuiusdam illustris in deserto Iudaeae exoriturae praedixerat, quae promisso Seruatori viam sternere, & omnes in eius occursum paratos esse iuberet. Et postea cum iam tempus illud fatale appropinquaret, Angelus Gabriel Zachariae apparens, verumque locum de Ioanne Baptista, quem Elizabetha ipsi paritura esset, exposuit, inter alia dicens: Ipse praecedet in conspectu Domini in spiritu & virtute Eliae, ut conuertat corda patrum in filios, & contumaces ad prudentiam iustorum, ut paret Domino populum instructum. Quibus consentiunt, quae postea illo nato Zachariae ex Spiritus Sancti suggestione magna cum exultatione dixit: Et tu puerule, Propheta Altissimi vocaberis: praibis enim ante faciem Domini, ut pares vias, &c. Neque hoc ipse Ioannes dissimulavit, qui a legatis Hierosolyma ad ipsum missis, quis nam esset, interrogatus, respondit: Ego sum vox clamantis in deserto, Purgate viam Domini, sicut dixit Isaias Propheta. Erant haec tam clara & perspicua, ut ex eis liquido constare posset, Ioannem Baptistam esse Eliam illum, IESVM vero esse Christum sue Seruatorem, cui ille viam parare debuit. Sed ea Satanae astutia in Scribis fuit, ut vaticinio isto Malachiae potuerit abuti, ut per illud plerosque a Christo abduceret, & domesticos quoque eius discipulos rerum incertos & dubios faceret, dum ipsi quoque Eliam Thesbitem ex altera vita reducem expectant. Simili errore totam Iudaeorum gentem fascinauit sub terreni regni praetextu, quod in Christo somniarunt, ut saepe iam diximus. Et nostro tempore multa huius generis fiunt, dum per Scripturas male detortas fidei dogmata corrumpit. Sacramentorum verum obscurat, ut quae fidei adminicula & sigilla, adhaec Christianae societatis vincula esse debebant, superstitionum seminaria sint, & lites pariant, quibus Ecclesiae horribiliter dissipantur. At tunc nos veterum exemplorum meminisse oportet, & Satanae insidias observare, nec statim fidem habere iis, qui sua commenta plausibili Scripturarum allegatione palliant, sed res ipsas, de quibus agitur cum illarum diligenti collatione excutere.
units.tr: In this sophism the cunning of our common enemy, the devil, is foreshadowed. He knows how to abuse the Scriptures and oracles of God against the truth, in order to lead the simpler sort away from faith. God had indeed promised that he would send Elijah, who like a forerunner would stir up the people for the coming of the Messiah and prepare the way for the restoration of his kingdom. But what sort of Elijah he would be, Isaiah had taught nearly three hundred years before Malachi, when he foretold the voice of one crying, that is, of a certain famous herald who would arise in the wilderness of Judaea to make a road for the promised Saviour and to bid everyone be ready to meet him. Later, when that fated time was drawing near, the angel Gabriel, appearing to Zechariah, explained the true meaning concerning John the Baptist, whom Elizabeth was to bear to him, saying among other things: He shall go before the face of the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready. What Zechariah said afterwards, when that son was born, moved by the Holy Spirit and with great exultation, agrees with this: And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Highest, for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, etc. John himself did not hide this either, when the messengers sent to him from Jerusalem asked who he was, and he answered: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said. These things were so clear and plain that from them it could be plainly established that John the Baptist was that Elijah, and that Jesus was truly Christ his Saviour, for whom he ought to prepare the way. But by Satan's cunning it came about among the scribes that they could abuse that prophecy of Malachi, so that through it they might draw many away from Christ, and make even his own disciples uncertain and doubtful, while they themselves still expected Elijah the Tishbite to return from the other life. By a similar error he bewitched the whole Jewish nation under the pretext of an earthly kingdom, which they had dreamed up in Christ, as we have often said already. And in our own time many things of this kind happen, while the doctrines of faith are corrupted by Scriptures wrongly twisted. The truth of the sacraments is obscured, so that what ought to be aids and seals of faith and bonds of Christian fellowship become seedbeds of superstitions and give rise to quarrels by which the Churches are dreadfully torn apart. But then we ought to remember the examples of the ancients and watch for the snares of Satan, and not believe at once those who cloak their own inventions with a plausible appeal to Scripture, but examine the matters themselves, with a careful comparison of the Scriptures.

units.la: In primis autem proderit discipulos imitari, qui duplici nomine laudem merentur. Primo quod ignorantiam suam non dissimulant, ut ambitiosi solent, qui in errore haerere malunt, quam videri aliquid ignorasse. Sentiunt illi cum recepta opinione non posse consistere quae a Christo fiebant. Ita quae errore liberari, & in veritate erudiri cupiunt. Deinde non alibi quaerunt veritatem quam apud Christum et in eo caelesti voci obediunt, quae illum audire iuberat. Est enim hic vere catholicus & orthodoxus doctor, qui solus verba vitae aeternae habet, ut nuper diximus. Ad hunc ergo recurrant, qui incerti haerent, aut quaedam obscurius dicta putant. Quia enim illae lux quoque est, quae sola mentis tenebras discutit, non possunt incertis opinionibus fluctuare, qui illum audiunt & sequuntur. Hoc si hodie fieret ab omnibus, mox finis esset controversiarum, quibus Ecclesiae turbantur, & plerique maiores in veri cognitione & pietate profecissent.
units.tr: In the first place, it will be useful to imitate the disciples, who deserve praise on two counts. First, they do not conceal their ignorance, as ambitious men usually do, who would rather remain in error than appear to have not known something. They perceive that what was being done by Christ could not stand together with the accepted opinion, and so they desire to be freed from error and instructed in the truth. Second, they seek the truth nowhere else than with Christ, and they obey that heavenly voice which commanded them to hear him. For he is truly the catholic and orthodox teacher, who alone has the words of eternal life, as we said recently. So those who hesitate in uncertainty, or think some things said rather obscurely, should have recourse to him. For he is also the light which alone dispels the darkness of the mind, so those who hear and follow him cannot waver in uncertain opinions. If this were done today by everyone, soon there would be an end to the controversies by which the Churches are troubled, and many more would have advanced in the knowledge of the truth and in piety.

units.la: Porro Christum audiamus amice & diligenter discipulis respondentem: Elias quidem venisse primum, & restituet omnia: Sed dico vobis, Eliam iam venisse, & non agnouerunt eum, sed fecerunt ei, quaecunque voluerunt: Ita futurum est ut & Filius hominis patiatur ab eis. Tria agit hoc responsio. Primum Malachiae vaticinio fidem suam asserit, ut ostendat Dei promissis nihil decedere propter hominum incredulitatem & diffidentia. Quid tum enim (inquit Paulus) si quidam fuerunt increduli? num incredulitas eorum fidem Dei faciet irritam? Absit. Imo sit Deus verax, omnis autem homo mendax. Enimuero manet Verbum Domini in aeternum, & habet cursum suum certum, quem nemo impediet. Quod si qui illud nolunt amplecti, aut illud falsis interpretationibus corrumpunt, ut ipsis non possit salutare esse, in vero tamen & germano suo sensu sem per ratum manet, & credentium saluti seruiet, alteris autem illis cedet in iusta condemnationis testimonium, qui sermonem veritatis in iniustitia detinent.
units.tr: Let us then hear Christ answering his disciples kindly and carefully: Elijah indeed has come first, and will restore all things. But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did not recognise him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of man will suffer at their hands. This reply does three things. First, it asserts the truth of Malachi's prophecy, to show that nothing is taken from God's promises by the unbelief and distrust of men. For what then, says Paul, if some were unbelieving? Will their unbelief make the faith of God void? God forbid. Rather let God be true, but every man a liar. Indeed the word of the Lord remains for ever and has its sure course, which no one will hinder. And if some are unwilling to embrace it, or corrupt it with false interpretations, so that it cannot be saving for them, yet in its true and genuine sense it always remains fixed, and it will serve the salvation of believers, while to those others it will be a witness of just condemnation, since they hold the word of truth captive in unrighteousness.

units.la: Secundo Iudaeorum fo cordia perstringit, qui scientes volentes cacutiant. Etenim habebant in ore frequenter promissiones de Messia, sciebant praeterea hunc habiturum praecursorem, qui spiritu propheticō instruere ei viam praepararet, & quoad hunc Eliae nomen vulgo obtinuerat.
units.tr: Second, he exposes the hardness of heart of the Jews, who, knowing and willing, made themselves blind. For they often had on their lips the promises about the Messiah; they knew moreover that he would have a forerunner, who by the prophetic Spirit would prepare the way for him, and as regards this, the name of Elijah had commonly prevailed.

units.la: At cum hoc de Ioanne Baptista interpretatus esset Angelus, & post hunc Zacharias, cuius historia non ignota erat, cum deniq; Ioannes reuera Elias ageret, & eius habitus, mores, certamina cum regibus per omnia Eliae historiae consentirent, tamen illum non modo non agnouerunt, sed indignissime tractarunt. Initio Inquisitores ad illum emisserunt, qui quaestionibus insidiosis eum aggrederentur. Deinde seipsum illis manifestantem neglexerunt. Tandem iniustis vinculis eum detineri & occidi passi sunt, & ne post fata quidem liuor illorum quieuit, quo minus eius doctrinam & Baptismum calumniari pergerent, aut illi Veritatis testimonium perhiberent. Haec omnia completitur breui hoc dicto Domi-
units.tr: But although the angel had interpreted this of John the Baptist, and after him Zechariah, whose history was not unknown, and although finally John truly acted as Elijah, and his dress, manner of life and conflicts with kings agreed in every respect with the history of Elijah, yet they not only did not recognise him, but treated him most shamefully. At first they sent inquisitors to him, who assailed him with insidious questions. Then they neglected him when he revealed himself to them. At last they allowed him to be held in unjust chains and put to death, and not even after his death did their malice cease, so that they went on slandering his teaching and baptism, and would not bear witness to the truth of him. All these things are summed up in the Lord's brief saying

units.la: nus, quando illos Eliae promisso fecisse dicit quaecunque voluerunt. Postremo, quia eadem ipsius fors futura erat, ad se transfert exemplu Ioannis, ut discipulos aduersus crucis standalu amplius confirmet, neue sibi propter laetam & consolationis plenam clarificationis historiam otium & quietem perpetuam pollicerentur. Quasi diceret: Quicquid illud fit quod vidistis paulo ante, fiet tamen breui, ut ego quoque indignissima quaeque ab ijsdem hostibus perpetiar.
units.tr: when he says that they did to Elijah's promised one whatever they wished. Finally, because the same fate was to await himself, he applies the example of John to himself, so as to confirm his disciples more firmly against the stumbling-block of the cross, and that they should not promise themselves rest and perpetual quiet because of the joyful and consoling account of his brightness. As if he said: Whatever that is which you saw a little while ago, soon it will happen that I too shall suffer the most unworthy things from the same enemies.

units.la: At quia sibi ipsi semper similis est mundus, meminerimus hic communem hominum sociordiam & contumaciam perstringi, quae fit ut plerique futura inquirant, praeterita accusent, praesentia autem, quae ipsis ob oculos & in manibus versantur, negligant. Factum hoc est ab origine rerum.
units.tr: But since the world is always like itself, let us remember that here the common sluggishness and obstinacy of men is censured, which causes most of them to inquire into future things, to accuse past things, and to neglect present things, which lie before their eyes and in their hands. This has been so from the beginning of the world.

units.la: Etenim temporibus Noe & Lothi non defuerunt admonitiones, quibus Deus totum mundum ab exitio Diluuij, & Sodomas cum vicinis vrbibus ex imminenti interitu revocabat. At infelicibus illis aures deerant & oculi, quibus ea obseruarent, quae ad ipsorum salutem faciebant. Nam vt apud Lucam Dominus ait, edebant, bibebant, vxores ducebant & nuptui dabantur, emebant item, vendebant, plantabant, aedificabant vsque ad eum diem, quo Noe in arcam ingressus est, & quo Loth ex Sodomis exiit, & venit Diluuium, atque omnes perdidit, ignis item & sulphur coelitus omnes exussit. Idem postea facti inter Israelitas ante Samariae & regni totius excidium, & ante Hierosolymae ac templi destructionem, & gentis infelicis deportationem in Babylonios. Et cum in terris ageret Dei Filius maiorum contumaciam, & indignas Prophetarum caedes accusabant, Messias venturi spem totis animis fouebant, praesentem vero oderant, perseguebatur, admonitiones riddebant, minas eludebant, & cum sub iugo Romana tyrannidis se miseros & infelices esse indies sentirent, non tamen adduci potuerunt, vt de sua salute serio cogitarent: sed indigna Filii Dei nece mensuram patrum impleuerunt, quod ipsis excidium horrendum & irreparabile peperit. Vide Luc. 10. Matth. 23. 24.
units.tr: For in the times of Noah and Lot there were no lack of warnings, by which God called back the whole world from the destruction of the Flood, and Sodom with the neighbouring cities from impending ruin. But those unhappy people lacked ears and eyes to observe what was for their own salvation. For, as the Lord says in Luke, they ate and drank, took wives and were given in marriage, bought too, sold, planted, built, until the day when Noah entered the ark and Lot went out of Sodom, and the Flood came and destroyed them all; fire and brimstone likewise came from heaven and burned them all. The same happened afterwards among the Israelites before the destruction of Samaria and of the whole kingdom, and before the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple, and the deportation of the unhappy nation to Babylon. And while the Son of God was on earth, the fathers' obstinacy was accused and the unworthy slaughter of the prophets; they cherished with all their hearts the hope of the coming Messiah, but hated and persecuted the present one, rejected the warnings, mocked the threats, and though they felt day by day that they were wretched and unhappy under the yoke of Roman tyranny, they could not be brought to think seriously about their salvation. Instead they filled up the measure of their fathers by the unworthy killing of the Son of God, which brought upon them a horrible and irreparable destruction. See Luke 10, Matthew 23, 24.

units.la: Habemus autem in his nostri seculi speculum, in quo nostros mores & fata contemplemur. Extant vaticinia de nouissimorum temporum periculis, & in omnium ore sunt, quae de Antichristo & eius emissarijs Prophetae & Apostoli praemonuerunt. Interim plerique, sese illi seducendos praebent, & luporum, quos ille submittit, faucibus & unguibus se & suae fidei creditos ingerunt. Idem plane fit in ijs, quae ad mores spectant. Sunt plena exemplorum historiae, quae docent, quam infelicitatis olim omnia regna & gentes corruerint, in quibus otium, luxus, intemperantia, ebrietas, libidines vagae, vsurae, monopolia, & quae alia sunt huius generis licenter regnarunt: quod (inquâ) quae eiusmodi mores comitatur securitas talibus semper exitium attulit. Attamen ista hodie longe lateque in terris dominantur, & multos quotidie perdunt. Ipsi quoque horum triste ssima effecta experimur. Nam vt taceam seditiones & bella, quibus orbis terrarum turbatur, concutitur, euertitur: morbos item, quos multi sibi ipsis cum praematura morte accersunt: tempestates quoque praeteream, quae famem frequenter inuehunt, & tantumnon vniuersam mundi machinam attrerunt & labefactant: quis non videt fatali egestate & penuria omnes loci & ordinis homines laborare, & cum alij alios deglubant, expilent, deuorent, interim tamen omnes egent, adeo vt paucos reges & principes videas, qui suam dignitatem & statum tueri possint. Eo autem deterior est nostra fors, quod nec isti quidem sapimus, & quae sentimus magno nostro malo, videre nolumus, multo minus de effugij via cogitare, aut meliora monentes audire.
units.tr: We have in this age of ours a mirror in which we may contemplate our own morals and fates. There are prophecies about the dangers of the last times, and they are on everyone's lips: the prophets and apostles forewarned of what Antichrist and his emissaries would do. Meanwhile, many let themselves be led astray by them, and thrust themselves and their faith, entrusted to them, into the jaws and claws of the wolves he sends out. The same is plainly true of matters of morals. Histories are full of examples which teach how unhappily all kingdoms and peoples once collapsed, in whose midst idleness, luxury, intemperance, drunkenness, wandering lusts, usury, monopolies, and other things of this kind ruled without restraint; and security, which accompanies such morals, has always brought ruin on such people, I say. Yet these things now hold sway far and wide over the lands and destroy many every day. We ourselves also experience their most sorrowful effects. To pass over the seditions and wars by which the world is disturbed, shaken, and overturned; likewise the diseases which many bring upon themselves along with premature death; and I will pass over the storms too, which often bring famine and nearly shatter and weaken the whole machinery of the world: who does not see that people of every place and rank suffer from fatal want and poverty, and while some strip, plunder, and devour others, all nonetheless are in need, so that you may see few kings and princes who can maintain their dignity and station? Our lot is all the worse because we are not wise even in this, and we are unwilling to see what we feel to our great harm, much less to think about the way of escape, or to listen to those who advise better things.

units.la: Vt igitur nostri seculi mores eorum similes sunt, qui olim Iudaeos & multas alias gentes perdiderunt: ita eadem quoque seruorum Dei fors est, quae Ioannis Baptistae, Christi & Apostolorum fuit. Faciunt hi, quod in mandatis acceperunt a Domino. Monent, docent, hortantur, corripiunt, minantur: sed nequicquam. Nam interea de illis etiam facit mundus infelix, quacunque ipse vult. Id est, illos odit, persequitur, calumniatur, in exilium eijcit, carceribus mancipat, occidit denique, & ex eorum sanguine & lanienâ voluptatem capit. Sed tunc recordemur, nihil nouum aut insolens nobis accidere, neque meliorem fortem nobis a Christo esse promissam. In primis autem obseruatu dignum est, quod Marcus in huius colloquij descriptione annotauit, Eliae aut Ioannis factu, sicuti de eo scriptum erat. Nihil ergo fortuitum ei accidit: quare neque nobis aliquid temere fiet, sed dies nostri (vt Dauid dicebat) sunt in manu Domini, qui fugas nostras numerat, & quia nostri amans atque fidelis est, nos supra vires tentari non finit, &c. 1. Cor. 10.
units.tr: Therefore, just as the morals of our age are like those of the men who once destroyed the Jews and many other nations, so too the lot of God's servants is the same as that of John the Baptist, Christ, and the Apostles. They do what they have received in command from the Lord: they admonish, teach, exhort, rebuke, and threaten, but to no avail. For meanwhile the unhappy world does to them whatever it wishes. That is, it hates them, persecutes and slanders them, drives them into exile, consigns them to prisons, finally kills them, and takes pleasure in their blood and slaughter. But then let us remember that nothing new or unusual happens to us, nor has a better lot been promised us by Christ. Above all, it is worth noting what Mark recorded in describing this conversation: that Elijah, or John, was treated as had been written of him. Nothing, therefore, happens to anyone by chance; so nothing will happen to us rashly either, but our days (as David said) are in the hand of the Lord, who numbers our flights, and because he loves us and is faithful, he does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength, etc. 1 Cor. 10.

units.la: Discipuli intelligunt tandem quid sibi Christus velit, & de quo loquatur. Fit hoc, quando hunc audimus. Hic enim est doctor ille verus, qui (vt nuper diximus) mentes nostras illuminat, & nobis a Deo Patre sapientia factus, securos salutis facit, & nos omni dubitatione liberat. Vt sus ergo praecipuus huius loci nobis esto, vt discipulos imitemur, & si quid nos latet, non vulgi errores sectemur, sed ad IESVM CHRISTVM contendamus, hunc docentem audiamus, precemur denique, vt ipse nobis nota faciat, quae ad salutem sunt necessaria, nosque Spiritu suo dirigat, vt in ipsius semitis ambulemus, qui solus Via est, Veritas & Vita. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: The disciples finally understand what Christ means and about whom he is speaking. This happens when we hear him. For he is that true teacher who (as we said recently) illuminates our minds, and who, made wisdom for us by God the Father, makes us secure of salvation and frees us from all doubt. Let this, then, be the chief lesson of this passage for us: that we imitate the disciples, and if anything is hidden from us, we should not follow the errors of the crowd, but turn to Jesus Christ, listen to him teaching, and finally pray that he himself make known to us what is necessary for salvation and direct us by his Spirit, so that we may walk in his paths, he who alone is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power forever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCXIIII.

units.la: Et cum venissent ad turbam, adijt eum quidam accedens ei ad genua, & dicens: Domine, miserere filij mei, quoniam lunaticus est, & male afficitur: nam saepe cadit in ignem, & saepe in aquam. Et obtuli eum discipulis tuis, nec cum potuerunt sanare. Respondens autem IESVS dixit: O natio incredula & peruersa, quousque tandem ero vobiscum? quousque tandem tolerabo vos? adducite mihi eum huc. Et obiurgauit daemonium IESVS, exijtq; illud ab eo: & sanatus est puer ex illo momento.
units.tr: And when they came to the multitude, there came to him a certain man, kneeling down to him and saying: "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is lunatic and is grievously afflicted; for often he falls into the fire, and often into the water. And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him." Then Jesus answered and said: "O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him here to me." And Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.

units.la: Christiana religio ab aliis sectis & superstitionibus eo potissimum differt, quod vt Deum vnum modo colit & invocat, ita Mediatorem quoque inter hunc & nos vnicum agnoscit IESVM CHRISTVM, cui omnis Scriptura testimonium perhibet. Vidimus hoc euidenter in Clarificationis eius historia. Cum enim coram discipulis transformaretur Dominus, videntur cum eo Moses & Elias, & cum illo de morte eius colloquuntur. Sed quando vox illa dulcissima auditur: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo placatus sum, hunc audite, solus Christus cernitur. Soli ergo huic gloria ista debetur, neque (vt Apostoli testantur) aliud nomen sub caelo hominibus datum est, in quo nos seruari oporteat, praeter illum vnum, qui nobis sapientia, iustitia, sanctifica-tio & redemptio a Patre factus est. Sequitur noua historia, qua hoc amplius confirmatur, & docetur illum esse semen illud benedictum, quod solum sua virtute & merito caput veteris serpentis conculcet, & sine cuius ope vires nostrae prorsus nullae sint. Sed & alia multa hic continentur, quae nostrae institutioni & consolationi seruiunt, de quibus cum in Marco & Luca prius dictum sit, consulto nunc erimus breviores.
units.tr: The Christian religion differs from other sects and superstitions chiefly in this: just as it worships and calls upon one God alone, so it acknowledges one Mediator between God and us, Jesus Christ, to whom all Scripture bears witness. We saw this clearly in the history of his Transfiguration. For when the Lord was transfigured before his disciples, Moses and Elijah appeared with him and spoke with him about his death. But when that most sweet voice was heard, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him," Christ alone was seen. So this glory is due to him alone, and (as the Apostles testify) there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved, except that one who was made for us by the Father wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. Then follows a new history, by which this is confirmed further and it is taught that he is that blessed seed who alone, by his own power and merit, crushes the head of the old serpent, and without whose help our own strength is altogether nothing. Many other things are also contained here which serve our instruction and comfort; since these were already spoken of in Mark and Luke, we will now deliberately be briefer.

units.la: Praemittitur occasio, quae fuit, quod cum Dominus in monte fuisset cum tribus discipulis, quidam ad reliquos nouem adduxit filium lunaticum, qui secundum Lunae motum aut incrementa morbo sacro aut comitiali grauiter laborabat. Quem cum hi curare vellent, non potuerunt. Ex eo Scribae occasione arrepta, disputationem aduersus illos instituunt, cuius procul dubio statim fuit, quod Christum voluerunt omnibus suppeditum & contemptum facere, qui hucusque fictis & falsis miraculis simplici vulgo imposuerit. Quo loco considerandi nobis primum veniunt discipuli, qui etsi iam pridem accepissent potestatem aduersus spiritus immundos, & plures iam eiecissent, hunc tamen eicere nequeunt. Facit hoc quidem ad afferendam Christi virtutem, vt hunc omnibus Dei seruis tanto praestare credamus, quanto Deus homine maior est: at simul docemur, ne optimos quidem & sanctissimos homines abs-que Christo quicquam posse, sicut ipse in vitis & palmitum parabola docet. Etenim ex nobis ipsis ne ad cogitandum quidem idonei sumus: Christus autem est, qui nobis Deum Patrem conciliat, qui donis necessariis instruit, & Satanam coercet, ne nobis in opere Domini occupatis possit resistere. Atqui a nobis non facile discedit Dominus, qui vt nobis salutem afferret, in mundum venire & homo fieri dignatus est: nos vero illum arcemus a nobis, quando in precibus cessamus, & nostra socordia lucem fidei in nobis extingui patimur, vel etiam morum licentia & impuritate illam obruimus. Tunc occasione captata Satan nos, vt olim Euam solitariam, aggreditur, & huic aliquid permittit Dominus, vt experiamur, quam nihil ipsi possimus, si suam manu ille nobis subducat. Quod ne nobis fiat, in Verbo Domini nos assiduos esse oportet, & precibus indesinenter vacare, quae hostem illum nobis appropinquare non sinunt. Docuit hoc olim eleganti typo Spiritus Sanctus, quando Israelitis aduersus Amalekitas pugnantibus, Moses in sublimi monte manibus ad Deum expansis precabatur. Quoties enim ille manus attollebat, terga dabant hostes, rursus quando manibus remissis precari desinebat, hostibus inferiores erant Israelitae. Solet hoc ipsum in pugna illa spirituali fieri, vt non possit consistere Satan contra Dei seruos, qui vera fide armati in precibus ardent, & illius conatibus Verbu Domini opponunt, qui gladius ille Spiritus est, cuius fulgorem tenebrae ille non potest ferre. Ista sibi ipsis applicent omnes loci &
units.tr: The occasion is set out first. When the Lord had been on the mountain with three disciples, a certain man brought his lunatic son to the other nine. The boy was grievously troubled by a sacred disease or epilepsy that followed the motions or the waxing of the moon. When the disciples tried to cure him, they could not. The scribes then seized the occasion and began a dispute against them, the purpose of which was undoubtedly to make Christ himself despised and held in contempt by all, as one who until then had imposed fictitious and false miracles on the simple crowd. Here we must first consider the disciples, who, although they had long before received power against unclean spirits and had already cast out many, yet could not cast out this one. This indeed serves to establish the power of Christ, so that we may believe he surpasses all the servants of God as much as God is greater than man; but at the same time we are taught that not even the best and holiest men can do anything without Christ, as he himself teaches in the parable of the vine and branches. For of ourselves we are not even fit to think; it is Christ who reconciles us to God the Father, who furnishes us with the necessary gifts, and who restrains Satan, lest he be able to resist us while we are occupied in the Lord's work. And yet the Lord does not easily depart from us: he deigned to come into the world and become man in order to bring us salvation. But we push him away from us when we cease to pray, and by our sloth allow the light of faith to be extinguished in us, or even overwhelm it by licence and impurity of life. Then Satan, seizing the occasion, attacks us as he once attacked Eve when she was alone, and the Lord permits him something, so that we may learn how little we can do if he withdraws his hand from us. To prevent this from happening to us, we ought to be constant in the Word of the Lord and to devote ourselves without ceasing to prayer, which does not allow that enemy to draw near to us. The Holy Spirit taught this long ago by a fine type, when the Israelites were fighting against the Amalekites and Moses, on the high mountain, prayed to God with his hands stretched out. For whenever he raised his hands, the enemies turned their backs, but when he let his hands drop and ceased to pray, the Israelites were inferior to their enemies. It is usually the same in that spiritual battle: Satan cannot stand against the servants of God who, armed with true faith, burn in prayer and oppose his attempts with the Word of the Lord, which is the sword of the Spirit, whose brightness that darkness cannot bear. Let all men of every place and rank apply these things to themselves, and they will indeed feel that Christ will not fail their efforts.

units.la: 1.Cor.8 / 1.Tim.2 / Act.4 / 1.Cor.1 / Matth.10 / Ioan.11 / 2.Cor.3 / Exod.17 / Ephes.6 loci & ordinis homines, & reuera sentient, Christum ipsorum conatibus non defuturum: E contra vero haec praecipua malorum cum priuatorum tum publicorum causa est hodie, quod pleriq; sine Christo res suas aggrediuntur, & carnis consilium secuti, in mundum potius quam hunc respiciunt.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 8 / 1 Tim. 2 / Acts 4 / 1 Cor. 1 / Matt. 10 / John 11 / 2 Cor. 3 / Exod. 17 / Eph. 6. On the contrary, this is today the chief cause of evils, both private and public: that most people undertake their affairs without Christ, and, following the counsel of the flesh, look rather to the world than to him.

units.la: Caeterum Scribas quoq; videamus, quos Marcus cum discipulis altercatos fuisse dicit. Fuit hoc deplorata impietatis & malitiae exemplum, quod cum diuinam Christi virtutem ex fexcentis (vt ita dicam) signis cognouissent, eius cauillanda aut neganda occasionem ex discipulorum defectu aut infirmitate tam aptae arripiunt. Atqui nisi cum pietate hominem quoq; exuissent, misereri illos decebat infelicis pueri, in quo curando virtus Christi deficere videbatur, quae tam multis hactenus salutaris fuerat. Sed est hoc proprium hostibus Veritatis, quod cum contra hanc nihil possint, aliunde corradant, quo eam in suspicionem & contemptum adducant. Hinc fit, vt clades & infortunia illius studiosis exprobrent, aut morum vitia odiose in eis obseruent, aut si ex ignorantia in aliquo haereant, in cachinnos effundantur, & sibijpsis de deuicta veritate triumphum promittant. Fiunt huius generis multa hodie, quibus pij non debet offendi. Manet enim inuicta Veritas, neq; perpetua caligine sepeliri poterit. Meminerint autem Christi serui, cum quibus aduersarijs ipsis res sit: & primo quidem innocentiae studeant, ne quam praebeant calumniandi occasionem maleuolis: deinde lectioni & Scripturis intenti sese ad disputationum certamina praeparent, ne ridiculi fiant Sophistis, qui nulla reperinde delectantur, quam si pijs insultare possint. In ijs vero, quae res huius faculi sectantur, prudenter & circumspecte res agant, ne improbi illi aliquam ridendi occasionem ex illorum imprudentibus factis possint apprehendere.
units.tr: Let us also consider the scribes, with whom Mark says the disciples disputed. It was an example of deplorable impiety and malice: although they had recognised the divine power of Christ from countless signs (so to speak), they seized upon the weakness and failure of the disciples as a fitting occasion to carp at it or deny it. Yet unless they had stripped off humanity along with piety, it would have become them to pity the unhappy boy, in whose healing the power of Christ seemed to fail, though it had hitherto been saving so many. But it is characteristic of the enemies of the truth that, since they can do nothing against it, they gather material from elsewhere by which to bring it into suspicion and contempt. Hence it comes about that they reproach its adherents with calamities and misfortunes, or spitefully note the vices of their conduct, or, if they cling to some error through ignorance, burst into laughter and promise themselves a triumph over the defeated truth. Many things of this kind happen today, by which the godly ought not to be offended. For the truth remains unconquered, and it cannot be buried in perpetual darkness. Let the servants of Christ remember, however, with whom they have to deal: first let them strive for innocence, so as not to give the malicious any occasion for slander; then let them, intent on reading and the Scriptures, prepare themselves for the contests of disputation, lest they become a laughing-stock to the Sophists, who take no greater delight than in being able to insult the godly. And in the matters that pursue the things of this age, let them act prudently and circumspectly, lest those wicked men seize some occasion for ridicule from their imprudent deeds.

units.la: In turba inconstantia popularis exemplum habetur. Quando Christum appropinquare vident, obuiam illi occurrunt, Luca teste, quod reuerentiae indicium est: At idem absente illo, omnes eius cauillandi occasiones captant, & eum in discipulis non contemnunt modo, verumetiam exibilat. Tales sunt, qui fide vera destituuntur, & in religione huius faculi commoda potius quam Dei gloriam & caelestia quaerunt. Si quando pios Christi cultores ab omnibus relictos periclitari vident, ipsi quoq; illos non negligunt modo, sed ludibrijs prosequuntur, & omni iniuriarum genere lacessunt. Quod si Deus suum rursus propitius affulgeat, mox mutantur, & adulari ijs incipiunt, quibus paulo ante hostiliter insultabant. Prodest mores ipsos mundi obseruare, vt non offendamur eius inconstantia, neq; fauori eiusdem aliquid tribuamus, sed vni Deo fidamus, cuius veritas inconcussa est, & bonitas Jempiterna.
units.tr: In the crowd we have an example of the fickleness of the populace. When they see Christ approaching, they run to meet him, as Luke testifies, which is a sign of reverence. But when he is absent, the same people seize every occasion to carp at him, and they not only despise his disciples but even hiss at them. Such are those who lack true faith and in religion seek the advantages of this age rather than the glory of God and heavenly things. If at any time they see the pious worshippers of Christ in danger, forsaken by all, they not only neglect them but pursue them with mockery and assail them with every kind of injury. But if God shines upon his own again with favour, they quickly change and begin to flatter those whom a little before they had insulted with hostility. It is useful to observe the very ways of the world, so that we are not offended by its inconstancy, nor give any credit to its favour, but trust in the one God, whose truth is unshaken and whose goodness is eternal.

units.la: Docet hoc proprio exemplo Christus, qui populi concurrentis applausum non multum moratur, sed quid rerum agatur, quaerit: Non quidem quod aliquid horum ipsum lateret, sed vt pueri lunatici pater ea occasione filij calamitatem exponeret, & opem eius flagitaret. Etenim prodest inter precandum diligentius explicare mifferias, quibus vrgemur, vt maior animi deuotio accendatur, & ad fidem in Deum magis excitemur. Et huc facit oratio Patris ipsius admodum pathetica. Propositio est: Domine, miserere fili mei. Quod vt facilius impetret, ad genua ipsi accidit, qui olim supplicantium gestus fuit. Apud Lucam, hunc sibi vnigenitum esse dicit: quod quam maxime faciebat ad mouendum commiserationem. Et mox vim morbi exponens, docet, necesse esse, vt infelici subueniat. Nam lunaticus est, quod genus morbi varium, instabile, & in primis graue est. Marcus mutuum quoq; fuisse scribit. Deinde cum quidam lunatici lenius habeant, hic (inquit) male afflictatur, & interdum cadit in ignem, sepe in aquam. In Luca addit: Ecce spiritus capit eum, & repente clamat, & discerpit eum cum spuma, vix ab eo discedens, ipsum conuellens & atterens. Et quod potissimum animum patris discruciabat, hoc erat, quod ad discipulos eum adduxerat, qui nihil auxilij aut remedij afferre potuerunt. Itaq; immedicabilis videri poterat hic morbus. Apparet autem in exemplis eiusmodi, quam saeuus & crudelis sit Satan, & quam infelix sit eorum conditio, quos ille semel in suam potestatem redegit. Etenim Christo ipso teste, homicida est iam inde ab initio, neq; aliud quaerit, quam vt in suam naufam illectos perdat. Nec illi satis est corpus perdidisse, sed animabus quoq; interitum struit. Nam si quibus vitiorum laqueos iniecerit, Deum immortalem, per quae praecipitia tales rapit? quam diris & horrendis modis illos torquet? Spumant illi inter cupiditates nefarias, quae tandem praecipites agunt in exitium: ijdem clamosi sunt in illicitis, muti apud Deum in precibus & alijs, quae salutem nostram iuuare, aut nobis honorifica
units.tr: Christ teaches this by his own example: he does not linger long over the applause of the crowd that gathers, but asks what is going on. Not that any of these things were hidden from him, but so that the father of the lunatic boy, on that occasion, might lay open his son's calamity and beg for his help. For indeed it is useful, when praying, to explain more carefully the miseries by which we are pressed, so that greater devotion of mind is kindled and we are more stirred up to faith in God. The father's own prayer is also very moving to this end. The proposition is: "Lord, have mercy on my son." So that he may obtain it more easily, he falls to his knees, a gesture that was once the posture of suppliants. In Luke he says that this boy is his only son, which greatly served to move compassion. And presently, setting out the force of the disease, he shows that it is necessary for the unhappy boy to be helped. For he is lunatic, a kind of illness that is varied, unstable and above all grievous. Mark also writes that he was dumb. Then, since some lunatics are less severely affected, the father says that this one is grievously afflicted, and sometimes falls into the fire, often into the water. Luke adds: "Behold, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it tears him with foam, scarcely leaving him, tormenting and wearing him down." And what especially tormented the father's mind was this: that he had brought him to the disciples, who could bring no help or remedy. So this disease might seem incurable. Now in cases of this kind one sees how cruel and savage Satan is, and how unhappy is the condition of those whom he has once brought under his power.
