The disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them. They brought the ass and the colt, and laid their garments on them, and set him upon them. A very large crowd spread their garments on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and strewed them on the road. And the crowds that went before him and that followed kept crying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"

units.la: QVemadmodum Dominus noster IESVS CHRISTVS in postrema sua professione, qua Ierosolymam venit, vt pro peccatis mundi corporis sui sacrificio perlitaret, se Regem esse testatus est omniscium & omnipotentem, quem nihil lateat, & cui in corda quoq; & voluntatem hominum ius sit atq; potestas, vt ita crucis scandalo occurreret, quo fides discipulorum labefactari poterat: Sic ingressu illo docuit quoq; quale nam regnum in terris habeat, & quæ huius sit condicio, quod item officium eorum, qui huius ciues esse, & in illo seruari volunt. De his quædam nuper dicta sunt: sequuntur nunc plura de ipso ingressu in vrbem, quo ista clarius adumbrantur. Narrat enim Euangelista primum, cur hoc modo & tam vili apparatu vrbem ingredi voluerit. Deinde, quomodo a populo deductus & exceptus sit.
units.tr: Just as our Lord Jesus Christ, on his final journey, when he came to Jerusalem, so that by the sacrifice of his body he might make atonement for the sins of the world, bore witness that he is the King, all-knowing and all-powerful, from whom nothing is hidden, and who has the right and the power over men's hearts and wills as well, so he met the scandal of the cross, by which the faith of the disciples could have been shaken. In the same way, by that entry he also taught what kind of kingdom he has on earth, what its condition is, and likewise what duty belongs to those who wish to be its citizens and to be kept in it. Some of these things have been said recently; now more follows about the entry into the city itself, by which these matters are more clearly foreshadowed. For the Evangelist first relates why he wished to enter the city in this way and with such a humble equipage, and then how he was escorted and received by the people.

units.la: Quoad primum non temere aliquis miretur, Dei Filium, & Regem gloriæ, in cuius natiuitate Angelorum chori exultarunt, nunc tam ridicula (vt sic dicam) pompa vrbem, quæ olim regni & religionis sedes fuit, sit ingressus? Qui enim alinos accersere potuit, eadem virtute & opera militares equos & cataphractorum equitum turmas, & alia, quibus reges huius saeculi suam maiestatem cum terrore ostentant, sibi parare poterat: vel etiam Angelorum legiones euocare, qui (vt Daniel scribit) ad eius obsequium semper parati sunt. At causam huius instituti Matthæus paucis exponit, dicens: Hoc autem totum factum est, vt impleretur quod dictum est per Prophetam, &c. Quibus verbis docet, hoc omne ex Dei decreto & voluntate factum esse, quam olim per Prophetas reuelarit. Vt ergo illi se accommodauit Christus, vt Patri ad mortem crucis vsq; obediret: ita etiam vaticinij veteris veritatem afferere & confirmare voluit: vt Iudæorum contumaciam inexcusabilem redderet, qui tunc quoq; se illi hostiliter opposuerunt, quando ea aperte ea facta sunt, quæ de Messia Prophetæ prædixerant. Quod si amplius quæras, Cur hoc ita a Deo decretum, & à Zacharia ex Spiritus revelatione prædictum sit? In promptu sunt causæ iustæ & graues, quæ possunt adduci. Nam primo sic confutari oportuit vulgo inter Iudæos receptam de regno Messiae terreno opinionem, & discipulos in vera sententia confirmari, quam nuper illis tradiderat, quando suum regnum ab huius sæculi regnis distinxit. Et sane Ioannes testatur, illos post eius mortem demum intellexisse, quod hactenus non potuerunt intelligere. Deinde pullo asina insidens vrbem voluit ingredi, vt doceret, quales esse oporteat suos discipulos, qui in regno suo locum aliquem habere cupiunt: modestos nimirum & humiles, qui de seipsis nihil asino maius aut præstantius sentiant. Asinus animal est stupidum & tardum, vecors, contumax item, & ad onera quæuis ferenda conditum, & proinde laboriosum & robustum. Tales fere sunt omnes homines: Stupidi nimirum & tardi in percipiendis iis, quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: contumaces interim si quando incedendum est in via præceptorum Dei: tunc enim vel resistunt, & vix vllis rationibus sibi persuaderi sinunt, vt recta progrediantur: vel postquam rationis peruersum sensum & belluinos carnis affectus declinant: & cum in Dei seruitio plane langueant, in solis peccati oneribus, quæ ipsis Satan imponit, perferendis laboriosos & industrios se præbent. Et hæc quidem vitia eo grauiora sunt et magis nocent, quod illa pauci in seipsis agnoscunt, quin potius in illis sibi placent, & voluptate ex eis captant. Sumus ergo inepti ad regnum Christi, quoad non solutis corrupta natura capistrus, per Apostolorum doctrinam, id est, Euangelij prædicationem ad illum adducimur. Qui vero hanc audiunt, ij intra semetipsos conuicti ad illum accedunt, & eum seruorem admittunt, qui fræno Spiritus ipsos regit, vt se totos illi per fidei obedientiam subijciant: De his vt admonerentur omnes homines, ita a Deo constitutum fuit, vt pullo asina insidens Christus Ierosolymam ingrederetur, quando iam instabat hora vt per mortem ignominiosam in possessionem regni cœlestis ex hoc mundo transiret.
units.tr: As to the first point, no one should wonder rashly why the Son of God, the King of glory, at whose birth the choirs of angels rejoiced, entered the city, which was once the seat of the kingdom and of religion, with such a ridiculous, so to speak, procession. For he who could summon asses could by the same power and effort have provided himself with warhorses and troops of armoured horsemen, and the other things with which the kings of this age display their majesty with terror; or he could even have called forth legions of angels, who (as Daniel writes) are always ready for his service. But Matthew explains the reason for this arrangement in a few words, saying: "All this was done that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled," and so on. By these words he teaches that all this was done by God's decree and will, which he had revealed of old through the prophets. Therefore, just as Christ accommodated himself to the Father, obeying him even unto the death of the cross, so he also wished to assert and confirm the truth of the ancient prophecy, so as to render the obstinacy of the Jews inexcusable, who then also opposed him with hostility, when those things foretold of the Messiah by the prophets were openly fulfilled. But if you ask further, why this was so decreed by God and foretold by Zechariah through the revelation of the Spirit, there are weighty and just reasons that can readily be adduced. For first, it was necessary to refute the opinion of an earthly kingdom of the Messiah, commonly received among the Jews, and to confirm the disciples in the true teaching, which he had lately delivered to them, when he distinguished his kingdom from the kingdoms of this age. Indeed John testifies that they understood only after his death what they had not been able to understand until then. Next, by riding on a colt, the foal of an ass, he wished to enter the city, to teach what kind his disciples ought to be who desire to have some place in his kingdom: namely, modest and humble, who think nothing of themselves greater or more excellent than an ass. The ass is a stupid and slow animal, foolish and also stubborn, and made for carrying any burdens whatever, and therefore laborious and sturdy. Almost all men are of this kind: stupid and slow to perceive the things of the Spirit of God; stubborn whenever they must walk in the way of God's commandments, for then they either resist and let themselves be persuaded by scarcely any reasons to advance aright, or, after they have turned aside from the perverse sense of reason and the brutish desires of the flesh, while they languish in the service of God, they show themselves diligent and industrious only in bearing the burdens of sin, which Satan places on them. And these vices are the more grievous and do the more harm because few recognize them in themselves; rather, they please themselves in them and take pleasure from them. We are therefore unfit for the kingdom of Christ, as long as our corrupt nature has not had its bridle loosened; we are led to him through the teaching of the Apostles, that is, through the preaching of the Gospel. Those who hear this come to him convicted within themselves, and they admit that ardour which governs them with the bridle of the Spirit, so that they may submit themselves wholly to him through the obedience of faith. That all men might be admonished of these things, God ordained that Christ should enter Jerusalem riding on the foal of an ass, when the hour was already at hand in which he would pass out of this world, through an ignominious death, into the possession of the heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Sed audiamus Prophetam Zachariam, per quem ista prædici voluit Deus, vt ne quem humilis illa & contemptibilis rerum facies offenderet, sed potius ex ea consolationem possent petere omnes, qui intra conscientias suas innata vitiositatis & peccatorum sensu cruciantur. Quod vt commodius fiat, totum locum recitabimus, qui eiusmodi est: Exulta vehementer filia Zion, iubila
units.tr: But let us hear the prophet Zechariah, through whom God wished these things to be foretold, so that that humble and contemptible appearance of things might offend no one, but rather that all who are tormented in their consciences by the sense of their innate sinfulness and sins might draw consolation from it. So that this may be done more conveniently, we shall recite the whole passage, which is of this kind: "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your King comes to you, just and a saviour, himself poor or meek, riding on an ass and on a colt, the foal of an ass. I will also cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off..."

units.la: {y} Cur Christus hoc apparatu vrbem ingressus sit. filia Ierusalem: Ecce Rex tuus venit tibi iustus & seruator, pauper ipse vel mansuetus, vehens super asino, & pullo asinarū. Excindam quoq; currum ex Ephraim, & equos ex Ierusalē, excindetur arcus bellicus, loquetur pace gentibus, & imperium eius a mari ad mare, & a fluuio vsq; ad fines terræ. Principio Zionem & Ierosolymam copellat Propheta, sub cuius nomine vniuersa electorum & fidelium Ecclesia intelligitur, quam vt Christum cum gaudio & exultatione excipiat, hortatur. Fuit enim hic ipse patrum, qui omnes nihil magis in votis habuerunt, quam vt dies ille illucesceret, quo promissus Messias venire debebat. Et de Abrahamo ipse testatur, quod gestierit, vt diem suum videret. De Simeone vero iam sene & iusto scribit Lucas, quod cum IESVM infantulum, quando in templum inferebatur, ex Spiritus Sancti suggestione agnouisset, gaudio magno repletus illum in vlnas acceperit, & exultabundus exclamauit: Nunc dimittis seruum tuum Domine secundum Verbum tuum, in pace: Quia viderunt oculi mei salutem tuam, id est, eum, quem tu destinasti, vt nobis salutis author ac mediator sit, &c. Eodem igitur respiciens Propheta, pios exultare iubet, & prae gaudio iubilare, vt doceat hoc ipsis non fraudi fore, quod maior sit impiorum & contumacium numerus, qui illum recipere dedignantur. Et huc pertinet, quod Matthaeus Zacharia vaticinium adduxerat, de suo addidit: Dicite filiae Zion: Nimirum, vt omnes doctores officij admoneat, quod est, aduentum IESV CHRISTI praedicere, vt ex eo afflictae conscientiae consolationem percipiant. Eiusdem generis est, quod Dauid aduentum Filij Dei in carne nascituri praeuidens, dicit: Cantate Domino cantionem nouam, quia mirabilia fecit, & salutem ipsi suppeditauit dextra sua brachiumque eius sanctum: Notam fecit Iehoua salutem suam, in oculis gentium patefecit iustitiam suam, &c. Et hus consentit, quod Angelus, cum Christi natiuitate pastoribus nunciaret, gaudij magni meminit, quod ad totum populum ex illo fit reditura. Sunt ergo alieni a regno Dei, qui ad Euangelij praedicationem trepidant & tumultuantur: nimirum quod legibus & disciplina Christi coercere nolunt. Sunt illi hostili in eum animo, & ideo ipse illos iusto iudicio vulcitur, vt ferreo suo sceptro eos comminuat, sicuti olim Dauid illis minatus est. Psal. 2.
units.tr: {y} Why Christ entered the city with this equipage. "Exult greatly, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, daughter of Jerusalem: behold, your King comes to you, just and a saviour, poor himself or gentle, riding on an ass and on a colt, the foal of asses. I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem; the battle bow shall be cut off; he shall speak peace to the nations, and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth." First, the prophet addresses Zion and Jerusalem, under whose name the whole Church of the elect and faithful is understood, and urges her to receive Christ with joy and exultation. For this was the longing of all the fathers, who desired nothing more than that the day should dawn on which the promised Messiah was to come. Abraham himself bears witness of him that he rejoiced to see his day. Luke writes of Simeon, now an old and righteous man, that when he recognised the infant Jesus, as he was carried into the temple, by the prompting of the Holy Spirit, he was filled with great joy, took him in his arms, and exclaimed exultantly: "Now, Lord, you let your servant depart in peace according to your word, because my eyes have seen your salvation," that is, him whom you appointed to be for us the author and mediator of salvation, and so on. Looking to this same thing, the prophet therefore bids the godly to exult and to shout for joy, to teach that it will not be to their disadvantage that the number of the ungodly and stubborn, who disdain to receive him, is greater. To this belongs also what Matthew added on his own to the prophecy of Zechariah: "Tell the daughter of Zion." Plainly, he thereby reminds all teachers of their office, which is to proclaim the coming of Jesus Christ, so that afflicted consciences may receive consolation from it. Of the same kind is what David, foreseeing the coming of the Son of God to be born in the flesh, says: "Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things, and his right hand and his holy arm have gained him victory. The Lord has made known his salvation; in the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness," and so on. The angel also agrees with this, when announcing the birth of Christ to the shepherds, and mentions the great joy which is to come from it to the whole people. Therefore those who tremble and riot at the preaching of the gospel are strangers to the kingdom of God, namely because they are unwilling to be restrained by the laws and discipline of Christ. They bear a hostile spirit against him, and for that reason he rightly judges them, so that he may crush them with his iron sceptre, as David once threatened them. Ps. 2.

units.la: Caeterum quia electi interdum ex innata omnibus infirmitate trepidant, gaudij & exultationis ipsius causam Propheta subtexit, dicens: Ecce Rex tuus venit tibi. Demonstratiua particula ad certitudinem salutis facit, dum illum ceu praesentem monstrat, qui post annos quingentos demum venturus erat. Deinde venit TIBI, inquit, id est, tuo bono, vt tibi salutem & gaudium afferat. Id vero omnes sibi ipsis priuatim applicare debent, vt Dei Filium ipsis venisse, id est, propter ipsos hominem factum & mortuum esse, & a mortuis resurrexisse credant. Etenim non sui ipsius causa hoc fecit, sed vt nobis salutifer esset, & miseros mortales Deo Patri reconciliaret. Idco Isaias de illo vaticinans, similiter dicebat: Puer natus est nobis, Filius datus est nobis. Et Euangelij promissiones omnes vniuersales sunt, vt quisque eas ad se transferre, & in suis tentationibus consolationem ex illis percipere possit.
units.tr: Since the elect sometimes tremble because of the weakness innate in all, the prophet adds the cause of joy and exultation, saying: Behold, your King comes to you. The demonstrative particle gives certainty of salvation, since it presents as present the one who was to come only after five hundred years. Then he says "to you," that is, for your good, so that he may bring you salvation and joy. Each person must apply this to himself individually, believing that the Son of God came to him, that is, was made man and died for him and rose again from the dead. For he did not do this for his own sake, but so that he might be our Saviour and reconcile wretched mortals to God the Father. Therefore Isaiah, prophesying of him, said in a similar way: "A child is born to us, a son is given to us." And all the promises of the Gospel are universal, so that each person may apply them to himself and receive consolation from them in his temptations.

units.la: Ad confirmationem huius facit descriptio Regis & regni ipsius, qua docet, qualis ille sit, & quae sit regni eius conditio. Et primum quidem Iustum vocat, quod Matthaeus omisit, vt pote ijs contentus, quae ad humilitatem Christi pertinebant. At nobis diligenter obseruandum est hoc eius Epithetum. Iustus enim dicitur, non solum quoad suam personam, in cuius ore non est inuentus dolus, neque alicuius peccati vnquam redargui aut conuinci potuit: sed quod nobis a Patre iustitia factus, omnes in se credentes iustificat. Idcirco Seruatorem dicit Zacharias, eiusmodi nimirum, qui (vt Angelus interpretatur) populum suum ab omnibus peccatis Ieruet & liberet. Talem Isaias quoq; fore promisit, cum diceret: Deus ipse veniet, & seruabit nos. Item, propter transgressiones nostras vulneratus est, & attritus propter iniquitates nostras. Multa nostrae correctionis ipsi impositae est, & eius liuore sanati sumus. Et hac quidem vera & vnica salus est, quia peccato expiato & sublato, vt nobis non amplius imputetur, nullus praeterea damnationi ac morti locus est. Itaque sic nos seruauit Christus, vt si quis fontem non modo ex carnificis manu eripiat, sed in super crucem seu patibulum, ex quo debebat suspendi, funditus euertat. Vocat praeterea Mansuetum & humilem, eo quod neminem fastidit, neque ius suum rigide persequitur, sed omnes amice inuitat, qui sibi refocillatione opus esse sentiunt. Et tollite (inquit) iugum meum super vos, & discite a me quod mitis sum, & humilis corde. Quasi diceret: Si me totum habitum & mores fiue gestus, dicta deniq; & facta mea omnia excutiatis, nihil inuenietis, quod aliquem terrere possit. Et hoc sensu Propheta addit: Vehens super asino. Innuit enim, longe alienum fore a Regum huius seculi moribus, qui intolerabili fastu, immodico luxu, sumptibus & pro dignitate sua, adhæc equitatu & apparatu magnifico subditis suis molesti, & sæpe etiam terrori sunt. Nec enim exactionibus aliquos gravat, non minus diris territat, sed amicè compellat omnes, promissis inuitat, gratia sua thesauros aperit, ut omnibus suæ opis indigis benefaciat, quoad corpus & animam: nihil autem vicissim exigit, quam quod præstitu facile, commodum, iucundum & salutare est, adeoq; necessarium præstitu: ut nimirum vni Deo Patri per ipsum fidamus, in ipsius solius merito acquiescamus, & alij alios diligamus: quæ quicunq; observuant, ij vitam hanc mortalem sibi ipsis iucundam faciunt, & salutem æternam in ipso consequuntur. Præterea cum huius seculi Reges fere bella non necessaria gerant, quæ subditis grauia & pernitiosa sunt, Christus pacis princeps est, & ad pacem suos instituit, adeo ut posito armorum studio hanc inter se, & quantum in ipsis est cum omnibus colant. Et id facile potest, quia regnum habet, quod latissime per totum orbem extenditur.
units.tr: The description of the King and of his kingdom serves to confirm this, teaching what kind of king he is and what the condition of his kingdom is. First he calls him Just, which Matthew omitted, being content with those things that pertained to the humility of Christ. But we must carefully observe this epithet. He is called just not only with regard to his own person, in whose mouth no deceit was found, and who could never be charged with or convicted of any sin; but because he has been made our righteousness by the Father, and justifies all who believe in him. For this reason Zechariah calls him Saviour, one who (as the angel explains) will deliver and free his people from all sins. Isaiah also promised that he would be such: "God himself will come and save us." Likewise: "He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed." And this is the true and only salvation, because once sin has been expiated and taken away, so that it is no longer imputed to us, there is no place left for condemnation and death. Thus Christ has saved us in the way that if someone not only snatches a man from the hand of the executioner, but also utterly overturns the cross or gallows on which he was to be hanged. He is also called Meek and humble, because he despises no one, nor does he rigidly press his own right, but kindly invites all who feel they need refreshment. "Take my yoke upon you," he says, "and learn from me, for I am meek and lowly in heart." As if he were saying: If you examine my whole bearing and manners or gestures, and finally all my words and deeds, you will find nothing that could terrify anyone. In this sense the prophet adds: "Riding on an ass." For he indicates that he would be far removed from the customs of the kings of this age, who by their intolerable pride, immoderate luxury, and expenditure appropriate to their rank, and moreover by their magnificent retinues and display, burden their subjects and are often a terror to them. For he does not weigh anyone down with exactions, nor frighten them with dreadful threats, but kindly addresses all, invites them with promises, opens the treasures of his grace, so that he may bless all who are in need of his help, both in body and in soul. In return he demands nothing except what is easy to perform, convenient, pleasant and salutary, and indeed so necessary to perform: namely that we trust in the one God the Father through him, rest in the merit of him alone, and love one another. All who observe these things make this mortal life pleasant for themselves, and obtain eternal salvation in him. Moreover, whereas the kings of this age mostly wage unnecessary wars, which are grievous and destructive to their subjects, Christ is the Prince of peace, and he trains his people for peace, so that, with the pursuit of arms laid aside, they cultivate peace among themselves and, as far as it lies in them, with all people. And this is easily possible, because he has a kingdom that extends most widely throughout the whole world.

units.la: Arguunt ista personatos Christi vicarios, & simul illorum insaniam, qui relicto hoc Rege tam miti & benefico, illos sequuntur, qui fastu, luxu & libidine huius seculi Reges superant, & in super iam seculis aliquot orbem terrarum bellis non necessarijs & seditionibus turbarunt: ut nihil de immani illa conscientiarum carnificina dicamus, qua multos in horribilem desperationem & æternæ damnationis periculum adducunt. Sunt hi plane Corinthiorum similes, qui Paulum, fidelem Christi ministrum contemnebant, in pretio autem habebant impostores, a quibus in seruitutem adigebantur, expilabantur & cædebantur. Sed est hoc iustum Dei iudicium, ut qui a Deo missum seruatorem nolunt recipere, eos admittant, qui in proprio nomine veniunt, & ex auditorum certa perditione quæstum faciunt. Et hoc est, quod Iudæis interminatur Christus, dicens: Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, nec recipitis me: Si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum recipietis. Ioannis quinto.
units.tr: These things accuse the men who pose as Christ's vicars, and at the same time the madness of those who, abandoning this so gentle and beneficent King, follow those who surpass the kings of this age in pride, luxury and lust, and who have moreover for some centuries troubled the world with unnecessary wars and seditions; not to mention that monstrous butchery of consciences by which they bring many into dreadful despair and the danger of eternal damnation. These men are plainly like the Corinthians, who despised Paul, the faithful minister of Christ, but held in high esteem impostors, by whom they were reduced to slavery, plundered and beaten. But it is the just judgment of God that those who are unwilling to receive the Saviour sent by God should admit those who come in their own name and make profit from the certain ruin of their hearers. And this is what Christ threatens the Jews with, saying: "I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, you will receive him." John 5.

units.la: Sed ad discipulos Christi reuertamur, qui etsi multa prætexere possent & causari, simpliciter tamen illius mandato paruerunt, & cum asinum atque pullum eius adduxissent, hunc instrauerunt vestibus suis, & hic imposuerunt Dominum. Quod nouum est humilitatis Christi argumentum. Solent principes equos suos instruere serico & purpura, & mulas suas Episcopi & Cardinales sellis pretiosis, phaleris item & frænis multo auro radiantibus exornant: quem luxum ante annos quadringentos D. Bernhardus illis exprobrauit, Satyricum illud in eos detorquens: Infrænis quid facit aurum. At Christus asino, quem in precario sumpserat vehitur, qui nec sella quidem vulgari instructus fuit, adeo ut illi vestes aut pallia sua discipulos insternere oportuerit, ut commodius in his sederet. Docent autem suo exemplo discipuli, ut ne grauemur Christo ea, quæ nobis charissima & necessaria sunt, commodare, si his illi opus sit. Eget autem ille interdum in membris suis, pauperibus nimirum: qui etsi vulgo contemptissimi sint, & interdum vix asinorum loco habeantur, nobis tamen sufficiat, quod Christi asini sint, quorum ferocitio ille vti dignatur, ut in eis habeamus occasionem, qua ipsi gratificemur, & ut simul in ijsdem nomen illius glorificetur.
units.tr: But let us return to the disciples of Christ, who, although they could have pleaded many excuses and objections, nevertheless simply obeyed his command, and when they had brought the ass and its colt, they laid their garments on them and set the Lord upon them. This is a new argument for the humility of Christ. Princes are accustomed to adorn their horses with silk and purple, and bishops and cardinals decorate their mules with costly saddles, and likewise with bridles and trappings gleaming with much gold. St Bernard reproached them for this luxury four hundred years ago, turning against them that satirical line: "What good is gold in a bridle?" But Christ rides on an ass, which he had borrowed, and which was not even fitted with an ordinary saddle, so that the disciples had to spread their garments or cloaks on it, so that he might sit more comfortably. By their example the disciples teach us that we should not be reluctant to lend Christ those things that are most dear and necessary to us, if he has need of them. He indeed sometimes lacks in his members, namely the poor; and although they are commonly most despised, and sometimes scarcely held in higher regard than asses, let it suffice us that they are Christ's asses, whose service he deigns to use, so that we may have an occasion in them to show him kindness, and that in them his name may at the same time be glorified.

units.la: Sequitur pompa, qua IESVS in urbem vsq; deducitur, & qua ibidem exceptus est. Fit hic turba magna & ex multis collecta mentio. Ex his autem alij illum ex Galilæa vsq; comitati, & passim toto illo itinere ad eum collecti fuerunt: alij vero qui iam Ierosolymam ad festum venerant, cum (ut Ioannes scribit) audijssent illum aduenire, ei obuiam egressi sunt, ut venientem honorifice exciperent. Inter omnes vero iustos nulli numerantur aulico luxu aut ornatu superbi, vel armorum strepitu & tubarum clangore terribiles: sed ex vulgo fuere, qui illum aliquando docentem audiuerant, miraculorum spectatores fuerant, & ex his beneficia receperant, per illum curati a morbis quibus tenebantur. Et horum alij præcedunt, alij subsequuntur, omnes vero certatim illum honorare & celebrare studebant. Nam qui ex vrbe obuiam veniebant, ramos palmarum manibus gestabant, quod antiquitus victoriæ symbolum fuit, & Iudæi in festo tabernaculorum idem facere: alij ramos ex arboribus vicinis cadunt, quos in via sternunt: multi vestes quoque
units.tr: There follows the procession by which Jesus is led into the city, and by which he was received there. A great crowd, gathered from many places, is mentioned here. Of these, some had accompanied him from Galilee and had gathered to him at various points along that whole journey; others, who had already come up to Jerusalem for the feast, when (as John writes) they heard that he was coming, went out to meet him, so as to receive him honourably as he arrived. Among all of them, however, none are counted among the just who were proud of courtly luxury or display, or terrifying with the clash of arms and the blare of trumpets; but they were of the common people, who had at some time heard him teaching, had been spectators of his miracles, and had received benefits from him, being cured by him of the diseases from which they suffered. Some of these went before him, others followed after, and all were eager to honour and celebrate him with rivalry. For those who came out from the city carried branches of palm in their hands, which was of old a symbol of victory, and the Jews did the same at the Feast of Tabernacles; others cut branches from nearby trees and strewed them along the way; many also spread their garments

units.la: Ioan. 12. substernunt in via. Addunt his faustas & laetas acclamationes, quibus ut regi victori & triumphanti gratulantur: Hosanna Filio Dauid, benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini: Hosanna in excelsis. Desumpta sunt haec ex Psalmo 118. qui in festis solennibus, praecipue autem in tabernaculorum festo decantari solebat, & ideo omnibus notus erat, & solennem precationem pro regno Messiae instaurando continet, cuius aduentum ab illis magno desiderio expectatum suisse, supra diximus. Itaque quando hac acclamatione in IESV excipiendo vtuntur, & eundem Dauid filium vocant, & vt ipsis opem ferat precantur (id enim Hosanna vox significat) non obscure fatentur, se illum pro Messia agnoscere, quem suo tempore venturum esse Deus Patribus promiserat. Apud Lucam ex Angelorum hymno, quem hi in illius natali cecinerunt, addunt: Pax in coelo, & gloria in altissimis. Et merito quidem hoc additur: quia Filius ille dileetus est, in quo placuit Patri, vt omnis plenitudo inhabitaret, & per eum reconciliaret sibi omnia, pacificatus per sanguinem crucis eius, tum quae in terra, tum quae in coelis sunt. Nec dubium est Spiritum San-ctum linguas ipsorum rexisse, vt de illo aliquid homine mortali maius & praestantius profiteren-tur, etiamsi ne discipuli quidem eius doctissimi mysterium hoc vere & perfecte intelligerent.
units.tr: John 12. They spread their garments on the road. To these they add joyful and happy acclamations, by which they congratulate him as a victorious and triumphant king: "Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest." These words are taken from Psalm 118, which was customarily sung at solemn festivals, especially the Feast of Tabernacles, and so was known to everyone. It contains a solemn prayer for the establishing of the kingdom of the Messiah, whose coming, as we said above, they had awaited with great longing. So when they use this acclamation in welcoming Jesus, and call him the same Son of David, and pray that he would bring them help (for the word Hosanna means this), they plainly confess that they recognise him as the Messiah whom God had promised to the Fathers would come at his appointed time. In Luke they add the words of the angels' hymn, which the angels sang at his birth: "Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest." And this is rightly added, because that beloved Son, in whom the Father was well pleased, was to have all fullness dwell in him, and through him to reconcile all things to himself, having made peace through the blood of his cross, both things on earth and things in heaven. Nor is there any doubt that the Holy Spirit guided their tongues so that they professed something greater and more excellent about him than about any mortal man, even though not even his most learned disciples truly and fully understood this mystery.

units.la: Est autem hic multa obseruatione dignum admirabile Dei consilium, qui istos excitauit, vt aduersus Pharisaeorum edicta, quae Christi feetatoribus excommunicationem minabantur, quaeque multos principes terruerunt, ne illum consiterentur, haec ausi sint: ita etiam illuminauit, vt veteris Scripturae verbis eum celebrarint, quem Sacerdotes & Scribae neque ex prophetijs, quas quotidie videbant impleri, neque ex signis & miraculis potuerunt agnoscere. Adhaec peregrinis ista tribuunt Euangelistae, quod hunc honorem Christo habuerint, cessantibus intereain officio Ierosolymita-nis, qui prae aliis instrudi esse debebant in cognitione Scripturarum & mysteriorum regni Dei. Habemus ergo hic exemplum eius, quod Dominus alibi testatur, Patrem mysteria ista abscondisse a sapientibus huius mundi, reuelare autem ea paruulis. Possumus ergo ex huius loci historia respon-dere aduersarijs, qui in receptis dogmatibus & ritibus Ecclesiae nihil a quoquam mutari debere contendunt, sed expectandam esse Pontificum & Imperatorum authoritatem, aut vniuersalis con-ciliij definitionem. Idem enim istis quoque dici potuisset, & hoc solicitos fuisse suis occinere Sacerdo-tes & Pharisaeos, ex iis constat, quae aliquando feruiu suis, quos ad Christum capiendum miserant, cum eos de illo quaedam honorifice loqui audirent. At laudantur isti, quod non expectata illorum authoritate, qui Mosis cathedram tunc occupabant, IESVM CHRISTVM secuti sunt, & eundem publice celebrarunt. Non igitur peccant pij principes, qui vt publicae saluti consulant, inconsultis Pontificibus, qui nunquam sibi ipsis cauterium adhibebunt, reformationem in suis terris instituunt, & Regi gloriae portas suas aperiunt. Merentur hi quoque immortalem gloriam, & reuera Ecclesiae nutritij sunt, quo titulo per Isaiam Reges pios Deus exornat. Isa.49.
units.tr: Here there is a wonderful counsel of God, worthy of close attention. He stirred these people up so that they dared to do this in defiance of the decrees of the Pharisees, which threatened excommunication for the followers of Christ and which terrified many rulers so that they would not confess him. He also enlightened them so that they honoured Christ with the words of the old Scripture, whom the priests and scribes could not recognise either from the prophecies, which they saw being fulfilled every day, or from the signs and miracles. Moreover, the evangelists attribute this honour paid to Christ to outsiders, because the Jerusalemites, who above all others ought to have been instructed in the knowledge of the Scriptures and the mysteries of the kingdom of God, were failing in their duty. So here we have an example of what the Lord testifies elsewhere: the Father has hidden these mysteries from the wise of this world and revealed them to little children. From this account we can therefore answer our opponents, who contend that nothing in the accepted doctrines and rites of the Church should be changed by anyone, but that we must await the authority of the Popes and emperors, or the definition of a universal council. For the same could have been said to these people too, and that the priests and Pharisees were anxious to have their own servants sing this, is clear from what they once did, when they sent servants to seize Christ and heard them speak of him in terms of honour. Yet these men are praised because, without waiting for the authority of those who then occupied the seat of Moses, they followed Jesus Christ and publicly celebrated him. Therefore the godly princes do not sin who, in order to care for the public good, without consulting the Popes, who will never apply the cautery to themselves, institute reformation in their lands and open their gates to the King of glory. These men also deserve immortal glory, and truly they are nursing fathers of the Church, a title with which God adorns pious kings through Isaiah. Isa. 49.

units.la: Docet item huius loci historia, quid eos facere conueniat, ad quos Christus venit per Euangelij praedicationem. Primo agnoscant eum esse regem a Deo nobis datum, qui expiato peccato mundi, de morte, inferis & diabolo triumpharit, & nobis benedictionem & salutem certam acquisiuerit. Deinde agnitum publice confiteantur, neque ipsos illius inter hostes apertos pudeat. Praeterea adiuuent illum in regni sui propagatione, & ipsi adducant asinos, id est, homines obstinatos, & qui hactenus essraenes vixerunt. Vestes deniq; illi substernant, per quas vitae totius conuersatio denotatur. Exuant ergo veterem hominem & priuatae iustitiae centones, seq; totos illi subijciant per fidei obedientiam. Sunt ista hodie rara admodum inter eos, qui Christianum nomen profiten-tur. Quam multos vero inuenias, qui portas suas occludunt ad illius aduentum, & appropinquan-tem impie reijciunt? Alij contemptim negligunt sese ipsis offerentem, & mundo potius eiusq; prin-cipi seruire malunt, quam Deo fidelissimo remuneratori. Qui vero optimi videntur, non exuunt veterem hominem, sed hunc & huius studia cum Euangelio conciliari posse arbitrantur, & centonibus superstitionum, quibus assueuerunt, nouum pannum assuere student. Qua causa est, vt in ve-ra pietate pauci proficiant, Deus autem passim iram suam diris indicijs manifestet. Haec igitur emendemus, & assiduis precibus petamus a Dei Filio IESV CHRISTO, vt ad nos quoq; di-uertere, nobiscum manere, & nos sibi mancipare dignetur, vt in ipso viuamus & feruemur. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: The account of this passage also teaches what those to whom Christ comes through the preaching of the gospel ought to do. First, they should acknowledge that he is the King given to us by God, who, having expiated the sin of the world, has triumphed over death, hell and the devil, and has won for us blessing and certain salvation. Next, having recognised him, they should publicly confess him, and not be ashamed to be counted among his open enemies. Moreover, they should help him in the extension of his kingdom, and themselves bring the donkeys, that is, obstinate men who until now have lived wild. Finally, they should spread their garments before him, by which the whole manner of life is signified. Let them therefore put off the old man and the patchwork of their own righteousness, and submit themselves wholly to him through the obedience of faith. Such things are today very rare among those who profess the Christian name. But how many do you find who shut their gates against his coming, and impiously reject him as he approaches? Others contemptuously neglect him when he offers himself, and prefer to serve the world and its prince rather than God, the most faithful rewarder. Those who seem the best do not put off the old man, but think that he and his pursuits can be reconciled with the gospel, and they strive to sew new cloth onto the patches of superstitions to which they have grown accustomed. This is why few make progress in true godliness, and God everywhere makes his wrath plain by dreadful signs. Let us therefore amend these things, and with constant prayers ask the Son of God, Jesus Christ, that he would deign to turn towards us also, to remain with us, and to bind us to himself, so that we may live and be kindled in him. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: Et cum introiuisset Ierosolymam, commota est vniuersa vrbs, dicens: Quis est hic? Turba autem dicebat: Hic est IESVS ille propheta ex Nazareth Galilææ. Et introiuit IESVS in templum Dei, & eiecit omnes vendentes & ementes in templo: mensasq; numulariorum & cathedras vendentium columbas subuertit, & dixit eis: Scriptum est, domus mea, domus orationis vocabitur: at vos fecistis eam speluncam latronum. Tunc venerunt ad eum caeci & claudi in templo & sanauit eos.
units.tr: And when he had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was moved, saying: "Who is this?" But the crowd said: "This is Jesus the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee." And Jesus went into the temple of God and drove out all who sold and bought in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who sold doves, and said to them: "It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of thieves." Then the blind and lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

units.la: NArrauit nuper Matthaeus regium Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI in vrbem Ierosolymam ingressum, & vt homines peregrini, quorum aliqui cum ipso ex Galilaea aduentarunt, alii vero aliunde ante illum priores ad festum venerant, ipsum deduxerint & exceperint. Vidimus illic in vili & contemptibili apparatu illius non obscura diuinae virtutis & potentiae indicia, & (vt diximus) ita totam hanc actionem instituere voluit, vt doceret, se quidem esse Regem illum olim promissum, regnum autem suum non esse ex hoc mundo, ideoq; de eius successu non dubitari aut desperari debere, etiamsi nulla huius seculi pompa commendetur. Etenim in tota regni Christi consideratione perpetuo teneri debet quod ipse Apostolo dixit: Potentia mea in infirmitate perficitur vel ad finem suum perducitur. Ad huius confirmationem facit etiam hic locus, quo narratur, quo modo Ierosolymitani ciues ad hunc eius ingressum affecti fuerint: deinde quid ille fecerit postquam in vrbem venit.
units.tr: Matthew recently related the entry of our Lord Jesus Christ into the city of Jerusalem, and how the pilgrims, some of whom had come with him from Galilee and others earlier from elsewhere for the festival, escorted and received him. We saw there, in his humble and despised equipage, clear signs of divine power and might, and (as we have said) he wished to arrange this whole action so as to teach that he is indeed that King promised long ago, but that his kingdom is not of this world, and therefore one ought not to doubt or despair of its success, even though it is commended by no pomp of this age. For throughout the whole consideration of Christ's kingdom we must hold fast to what he himself said to the Apostle: "My power is made perfect in weakness," or is brought to its end. This passage also serves to confirm this point, in which it is told how the citizens of Jerusalem were affected by his entry, and then what he did after he came into the city.

units.la: De illis dicitur, commotam siue turbatam fuisse vniuersam vrbem, nimirum terrore & metu. Ita vero fieri necesse fuit: quia nisi timor obstitisset, nunquam passi fuissent ista fieri. Et appareret non Iudaeos modo, verumetiam Pilatum praesidem cum suis nouo hoc & insolito spectaculo per turbatum fuisse, vt nihil aduersus Christum ausus fuerit nunc, qui alias ob minutiora leuiora causas ad arma & caedes solebat prosilire, si quae tumultus publici species in populo appareret. Interrogarunt autem inista trepidatione Ierosolymitani, Quis est hic? Quibus a turba peregrinorum, qui illum comitabantur & deducebant, respondetur: hic est IESVS ille propheta ex Nazareth Galilaeae. Prophetam dicunt, non aut vulgarem, cum addant articulum demonstrationis, ILLE: vt se de eo loqui testentur, de quo olim Moses Patribus dixerit: Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus Deus vester ex fratribus vestris, sicut me, &c. Idem ergo isti nunc dicunt, quod initio Philippus Nathanaeli de illo dixerat: Inuenimus illum, de quo scripsit Moses in lege & prophetis, &c. Nec dubium est Spiritum sanctum, qui primus populo rudi & nondum instituto in perfecta illius cognitione acclamationes illas solennes ex Psalmis suggessit, vt eas IESV CHRISTO accommodarent, nunc iam quoq; cofessionem in ore ipsorum formauisse: vt quamuis ipsi tanquam Regi acclamarent, tamen non Regem, sed Prophetam dixerint: ne in seditionis suspicionem venirent, & Romano praesidi ante horam eius neci praefinitam aliquid aduersus illum tentandi occasio daretur.
units.tr: Of those people it is said that the whole city was moved or troubled, clearly by terror and fear. And indeed it had to be so, for unless fear had stood in the way, they would never have allowed these things to happen. And it appears that not only the Jews but also the governor Pilate, with his men, were thrown into confusion by this new and unusual spectacle, so that he then dared nothing against Christ, though on other occasions, for smaller and lighter causes, he was accustomed to rush to arms and slaughter if any sign of public disturbance appeared among the people. In that trembling, however, the Jerusalemites asked: "Who is this?" To which the crowd of pilgrims who accompanied and escorted him replied: "This is Jesus the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee." They call him a prophet, and not an ordinary one, since they add the demonstrative article, THE, so as to bear witness that they speak of him of whom Moses long ago told the Fathers: "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brethren, like me," etc. So these men now say what Philip earlier said to Nathanael about him: "We have found him, of whom Moses wrote in the law and the prophets," etc. Nor is there doubt that the Holy Spirit, who first suggested those solemn acclamations from the Psalms to a rude people, not yet instructed in the full knowledge of him, so that they might apply them to Jesus Christ, had now also shaped a confession in their mouths, so that, although they acclaimed him as a King, they called him a prophet, lest they fall under suspicion of sedition, and lest the Roman governor be given an occasion to attempt something against him before the hour of his death, which had been appointed.

units.la: EST autem hoc nouum & memorabile virtutis & potentiae diuinae argumentum, quod cum tota haec actio ridicula potius quam formidabilis videri posset, tamen ad eius spectaculum vniuersa urbs commouetur. Simile quid IESV primum nato factum fuisse legimus, quando ad Magorum ex Oriente aduentantium praedicationem Herodes Rex turbatus est, & cum eo tota Ierosolyma. Adumbratur autem exemplis istis Euangelicae praedicationis vis, cuius stultitia (vt Paulus scribit) sapientiam mundi huius confundit & infatuat, vt plus quam panicis terroribus consternati tumultuentur etiam illi, qui paulo ante omnibus admirationi & terrori erant. Ita in praesenti urbs populosissima cum omnibus qui in illa religionis, sapientiae & potentiae existimationem sustinebant, anxia turbatur, exultante interea in Christo peregrinorum turba. Et hodie videmus ex Euangelij praedicatione gaudium percipere vulgus hominum, miserè autem tumultuari & rerum suarum incertos fremere alios quorum maxima est in mundo potentia & authoritas. Et hoc illud est, quod futurum esse olim Dauid praedixit. Non igitur offendamur, si quid huius hodie fiat, & homines obscuri ac contempti Euangelio exultent, insanientibus aduersus illud Regibus
units.tr: This is a new and memorable proof of divine power and might: although this whole affair might seem ridiculous rather than frightening, the whole city is nevertheless stirred at the sight of it. We read that something similar happened when Christ was first born, when King Herod was troubled by the announcement of the Magi arriving from the East, and all Jerusalem with him. These examples foreshadow the force of the Gospel preaching, whose foolishness (as Paul writes) confounds and befuddles the wisdom of this world, so that even those who a little before were objects of admiration and terror riot in greater alarm than men struck by panic. So now the most populous city is thrown into anxiety, together with all who held the reputation for religion, wisdom and power in it, while meanwhile a crowd of strangers exults in Christ. And today we see the common people receive joy from the preaching of the Gospel, while others, in whose hands lies the greatest power and authority in the world, rage miserably and fume, uncertain of their own affairs. This is what David long ago foretold would happen. Let us not, therefore, be offended if anything of this kind happens today, and obscure and despised men exult in the Gospel while kings rage against it

units.la: & tyrannis. Sed tunc meminerimus, hoc Dei placitum esse, vt mysteria regni fui paruulis manife-stentur, celentur autem ijs, qui sapere videntur. At si ad lætum IESV CHRIST inuntium terrentur impij & prophani homines, quid fiet in nouissimo die, quando ad Archangeli vocem, & terribilem illam tubam Dei mortui resurgent, & Filius hominis apparebit in gloria Patris sui cœlestis ad iudicandum viuos & mortuos? Tunc plangent omnes tribus terræ, & se miserrimos mortalium esse sentient, qui nunc se solos regnare arbitrantur. Harum consideratio nos ad serium & indesinens sanctitatis & inn: entiæ studiü excitet: adhæc consoletur nos, ne prophanorum ho-minum successibus offendamur, qui nobis insultare non verentur.
units.tr: and tyrants. But then let us remember that it is God's good pleasure that the mysteries of his kingdom be revealed to little ones and hidden from those who seem to be wise. If wicked and profane men are terrified by the joyful message of Jesus Christ, what will happen on the last day, when at the voice of the archangel and the terrible trumpet of God the dead will rise, and the Son of Man will appear in the glory of his heavenly Father to judge the living and the dead? Then all the tribes of the earth will wail, and they will feel themselves the most wretched of mortals, who now think they alone reign. Consideration of these things should stir us to a earnest and unceasing pursuit of holiness and innocence. Moreover, it should console us, so that we are not offended by the success of profane men, who do not hesitate to insult us.

units.la: Sed ad præsentis historiæ tractationem reuersi, videamus quid fecerit Dominus, postquam in vrbem venit. Occurrit hic primum, quod recta in templum diuertit, vt eo quoq; testaretur, se pro-missum illum Messiam esse, de quo Malachias dixerat: Subito ad templum suum veniet Domi-nus, quem vos quæritis, & legatus fœderis, quem vos desideratis. Et mirum videri poterat, illum non in palatium regium (quale tunc erat Antonia arx, quam magnificè extructam Herodes in Antonij honorem ita nominauerat) aut in prætorium, sed in templum potius diuertere voluisse. Ita vero testatus est, se non regni terreni causa in mundum venïsse, sed vt veritati testimonium ferret (sicut postea Pilato confessus est) & ea omnia compleret, quæ per templum & totum il-lum cultū, qui illic peragebatur, hastenus adumbrata fuerant. Quia tamé in tota hac actione Re-gem egit, exemplo suo docet, religionis curam ad viros principes potissimum pertinere. Nam etsi illa non huius sæculi armis, sed verbi prædicatione, & Spiritus Sancti virtute propagetur & fer-tur, quia tamen omnes, qui ad Reipub. gubernacula sedent, potestatem & authoritatem suam omnem a Deo acceperunt, iure hic ab illis hanc gratiam requirit, vt cultum suum inter suæ fidei creditos sartum tectum seruare studeant. Ideo olim liber legis regibus commendabatur, vt hunc descriptum haberent, & tunc in eo legerent, quando in folio suo sedebant, & potestate regia potie-bantur. At continet lex præcepta de puniendis blasphemis & falsis prophetis atq; seduétoribus, de Sabbati item & sacrorum prophanatoribus. Quorum omniū acerrimi vindices fuerunt reges, quorum fidem & pietatem Spiritus Sanctus prædicat. Sui ergo officij parum sunt memores, qui ista nihil ad se pertinere putant: imo ijdem suam dignitatem turpiter prostituunt, quæ in eo potis-simum consistit, quod Deus illos Ecclesiæ suæ nutritios fecit. Sed hoc etiam malè debemus {Pon-tificibus & Episcopis, qui vt ipsi soli dominetur, reges & principes a religionis cura, & sacrorum tractatione remouent, nisi vbi illorum authoritate sibi opus esse sentiunt, vt male vsurpatam ty-rannidem tueantur. Simul autem hoc Christi exemplo Anabaptistæ confutantur, qui neminem Christianum esse, & simul Magistratum gerere posse contendunt. Ergo ne præter officium fecit Christus, quando qui vt rex Ierosolymæ venerat, in templū rectæ diuertit, & illic collapsum Dei cultum restaurauit? Aut num peccasse dicemus Iosephum Arimathæum, Cornelium, Paulū, Ser-gium & similes, qui Magistratum gessere, postquam fidem in Christum professi sunt? Sed neq; Chri-stus quicquam temerè fecit, neq; peccarunt sancti illi homines Dei, dignitates & functiones politi-cas retinendo, quoad licuit, vt regnum Christi feliciùs possent propagare. Neminem ergo moueat fanaticorum hominum voces, qui dum sanctissimi videri volunt, Ecclesiam & religionem præsi-dijs suis spoliant, quibus illam Deus in hoc sæculo munire & confirmare solet.
units.tr: But returning to the treatment of the present history, let us see what the Lord did after he came into the city. Here first we notice that he went straight into the temple, to testify by this too that he is the promised Messiah of whom Malachi spoke: "Suddenly the Lord will come to his temple, whom you seek, and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire." And it might seem strange that he wished to go not to the royal palace (such as the fortress Antonia then was, which Herod had built magnificently and named in honour of Antony) or to the praetorium, but rather to the temple. Yet by this he testified that he came into the world not for the sake of an earthly kingdom, but to bear witness to the truth (as he afterwards confessed to Pilate), and to fulfil all those things which had hitherto been foreshadowed through the temple and the whole cult carried on there. Nevertheless, since in this whole action he acted as king, he teaches by his example that the care of religion pertains above all to princes and rulers. For although that religion is spread and advanced not by the arms of this age but by the preaching of the Word and the power of the Holy Spirit, still, since all who sit at the helm of the commonwealth have received all their power and authority from God, he rightly requires this favour from them, that they take care to keep his worship intact and secure among those entrusted to their faith. Therefore the book of the law was once commended to kings, so that they would have a copy of it and read in it when they sat on their throne and held royal power. Yet the law contains precepts about punishing blasphemers, false prophets and seducers, and likewise about profaners of the Sabbath and of the sacred things. The kings, whose faith and piety the Holy Spirit proclaims, were the fiercest avengers of all these. Those, therefore, who think these matters do not concern them are little mindful of their office. Indeed, they shamefully prostitute their own dignity, which consists chiefly in this, that God has made them nursing fathers of his Church. But we must also lament this in the pontiffs and bishops, who, that they alone may rule, remove kings and princes from the care of religion and the handling of sacred things, except where they feel they need the civil authority to defend a tyranny wrongly usurped. At the same time, by this example of Christ the Anabaptists are refuted, who contend that no one can be a Christian and at the same time hold the magistracy. Did Christ therefore act beyond his office when, coming as king of Jerusalem, he went straight into the temple and there restored the fallen worship of God? Or shall we say that Joseph of Arimathea, Cornelius, Paul, Sergius and others like them sinned, who held the magistracy after they had professed faith in Christ? But Christ did nothing rashly, nor did those holy men of God sin by retaining their dignities and political functions, as far as they were permitted, so that they might the more successfully propagate Christ's kingdom. Let no one, therefore, be moved by the voices of fanatical men, who, while they wish to appear most holy, strip the Church and religion of those protections with which God is accustomed to fortify and confirm them in this age.

units.la: Quid autem in templo fecit Dominus? Num obiter modò quid ibi fieret inspexit, intactaautem reliquit omnia? Imò reformatione fecit, & sublatis ijs, quæ improbi & auari Sacerdotes pri-uati quæstus ergo inuexerant contra Verbum Dei, ea substituit, quæ huius cultui vero, & homi-num saluti seruiunt. Nam eiecit omnes vendentes & ementes in templo: adhæc mensas numula-riorū & cathedras vendentium columbas subuertit. Quia vero idé ab illo factum esse scribit Io-annes sub initium statim prædicationis suæ in primo suo aduentu Ierosolymam, de corruptissimo qui tunc inter Iudæos fuit religionis statu historia ista nos admonet. Initiò priusquam cultus sui sedē fixam constituisset Deus, tabernaculum fieri voluit per Mosem, quod facile loco moueri, & prout necesse erat, hinc inde transferri poterat. Vsus huius erat, vt apud illud sacrificia sua osse-rent: illuc item conuenirent ad festa solennia, & ibidem precarentur publicè & vota sua persolue-rent. Postea Dauidi locum certum monstrauit Dominus, in quo templum ædificauit Solomō. Dif-ferē ferte autem cautum erat, vt sicut initio vnum modo tabernaculum fuit, ita huius loco vnicum modo templum extrueretur, ad quod ceu ad publicam & communem parochiam totus Israel conueniret, & vnicum haberent altare holocausti, vnicam aram thymiamatis, quibus vnus IESVS CHRISTVS figurabatur, vt ita omnes in vnius religionis consensu retinerentur, & scismata cauerentur, quae facile exoriri poterant, si in locis diuersis fuisset sacrificatum: Caeterum cum in toto cultu externo Christus obseruari deberet, qui solus tollit peccata mundi, Sacerdotes, vt quaestum facerent maiorem, satisfactionem pro peccatis & eorundem remissionem in externis hisce ferorum exercitijs monstrabant. Et coepit hoc fieri temporibus Prophetarum, sicut in horum sermonibus esse videre. Posteris vero temporibus autem est error, quando sub Romanis praesidibus sacerdotium venale factum, & annuae Sacerdotum vices introductae sunt. Simul enim humanis tra ditionibus locus datus est, quibus legis doctrina corrupta, & doctrina de Messia prorsus extincta est, vt rari inuenirentur, qui hunc recte agnoscerent, & salutis fiduciam in eo haberent collocatam. Et quia Iudaei iam tunc in gentes diuersas longe lateque dispersi erant, & ideo ex longinquis locis ad sacra & festa Ierosolymam veniebant, ne quid exteris & procul aduentantibus in mora esset, prope templum & in eius atrio pecora omnis generis venire coeperunt, & numulariij ibi dem suas mensas constituerunt, vt templum a foro prophano & emporio nihil differret. Ideo ementium & vendentium meminerunt Euangelistae, numulariorum item & eorum, qui columbas venales habebant.
units.tr: But what did the Lord do in the temple? Did he merely glance at what was going on there in passing and leave everything untouched? Rather, he effected a reformation: he removed what wicked and greedy priests had introduced there for private gain against the Word of God, and put in place of it what serves the true worship of this God and the salvation of men. For he drove out all who sold and bought in the temple; moreover, he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who sold doves. And this history warns us about the most corrupt state of religion that then prevailed among the Jews, since John writes that Christ did this right at the beginning of his preaching, at his first coming to Jerusalem. At first, before God had fixed the seat of his worship, he wished a tabernacle to be made through Moses, which could easily be moved from place to place and transferred hither and thither as need required. Its use was that they might offer their sacrifices there, and likewise gather there for the solemn feasts and pray publicly there and pay their vows. Later the Lord showed David a definite place, where Solomon built the temple. But there was a careful provision that, just as at first there was only one tabernacle, so in its place only one temple should be built, to which all Israel would come as to a public and common parish, and that they should have one altar of burnt offering and one altar of incense, by which Jesus Christ alone was figured, so that all might be kept in agreement in one religion, and schisms, which could easily arise if sacrifice had been offered in different places, might be avoided. But since in the whole external worship Christ ought to be observed, who alone takes away the sins of the world, the priests, in order to make greater gain, taught satisfaction for sins and their remission through these external exercises of the flesh. And this began to happen in the times of the prophets, as can be seen in their sermons. But in later times the error grew worse, when under the Roman governors the priesthood was made a matter of sale and yearly rotations of priests were introduced. For at the same time room was given to human traditions, by which the teaching of the law was corrupted and the doctrine about the Messiah was utterly extinguished, so that few could be found who rightly acknowledged him and placed their hope of salvation in him. And since the Jews by then were dispersed far and wide among diverse nations, and therefore came to Jerusalem for the sacred rites and feasts from distant places, lest anything be a hindrance to foreigners and those arriving from afar, cattle of every kind began to be brought near the temple and into its court, and money-changers set up their tables there too, so that the temple differed in nothing from a profane marketplace and trading centre. That is why the Evangelists mention those who buy and sell, and likewise the money-changers and those who had doves for sale.

units.la: At ista omnia eiecisse dicitur Christus, & tanta quidem seueritate, vt nulli vel personae vel rei pepercerit. Eijcit enim omnes qui vendunt aut emunt, cuiuscunque sint loci aut ordinis: sedilia columbarum confringit cum caueis & aliis, quae columbarijs seruiunt: adhaec mensas numulariorum subuertit, quod abstq; pecuniarum iactura irreparabili in tanta hominum turba fieri non potuit. Deniq; templum ab omni vsu prophano ita purgatum voluit, vt non patiatur ab vllo vas aliquod per illud deferri. Quod si vero cogites, quae sit humani ingenij natura, & quam impatientes iniuriarum sint omnes homines, & earum quidem in primis, quae cum aliqua fortunarum nostrarum iactura coniunctae sunt, fateberis hoc Christi factum inter miracula, quibus potentiam suam diuinam declarauit, non postremum censeri debere. Nunquam enim haec passi fuissent homines auari, & quorum mentes quaestus cupiditas occupauerat, quos deniq; magnatum fauor & patrocinium hucusq; tutos fecerat, nisi diuina virtus illos coercuisset, ne quid auderent.
units.tr: Yet Christ is said to have driven out all of these things, and with such severity that he spared neither persons nor property. He drove out everyone who was selling or buying, whatever their place or rank. He broke the seats of the dove-sellers, along with the cages and the other things used in the dove trade. He also overturned the money-changers' tables, which in such a crowd could not be done without irreparable loss of money. Finally, he wanted the temple so thoroughly cleansed of every profane use that he would not allow anyone to carry any vessel through it. If you consider the nature of the human mind, and how impatient of injury all people are, especially of those injuries that involve some loss of our property, you will admit that this act of Christ must be counted no small one among the miracles by which he declared his divine power. Greedy men, whose minds were held by the love of gain, and whom the favour and protection of the great had kept safe until then, would never have suffered this, unless divine power had restrained them from daring to do anything.

units.la: Ne vero furiosi inst ir hoc absque ratione fecisse putetur, facto huic doctrinam coniunxit (quod Matthaeus annotauit) dicens: Scriptum est, domus mea domus orationis vocabitur; at vos fecistis eam speluncam latronum. Scripturas allegat, quibus Dei Verbum & ipsam vitam aeternam continere, vulgus Iudaeorum fatebatur. Coniungit autem duos Scripturae locos, quorum prior ex Isaia esse sumptus est, & verum templi vsum tradit. Vaticinatur illic Propheta de vocatione gentium, quae omnes ad Ecclesiam accessurae sint, vt in ea Deum verum inuocent per Mediatorem Christum, & ait Dominus, Domus mea, domus orationis vocabitur omnibus populis. At quia Ecclesiae typus fuit templum illud Iudaicum, recte nunc huic applicatur, quod olim de Ecclesia dictum fuerat. Alter locus in Ieremia extat, quo templi abusum arguit, vt hunc merito corrigi & prorsus tolli ostendat. Corripit illic Dominus falsos sui cultus professores, qui templo & sacris externis ad licentiam scelerum abutebantur, & cum dixisset: Ecce vos confiditis verbis mendacibus, quae non proderunt vobis: Num furando, occidendo, moechando, peierando, Baali suffitum faciendo, Deos alienos sequendo, nihilominus venitis & statis coram me in domo ista, & dicitis, Liberati sumus, etiamsi omnia haec abominanda fecerimus? addit: Num spelunca latronum facta est domus ista quae meo nomine vocatur, in oculis vestris? Id est, Num templum meum instar antri esse putatis, in quod latrones post caedes factas & rapinas a viatoribus per vim extortas se recipiunt: vt vos quoque sub illius praetextu latere & abscondi posse putetis, &c. At reuera haec perfuasio tunc Iudaeorum prope omnium mentes fascinarat, vt nihil tam iniquum aut impium designari posse putarent, quod non expiaretur, si sacrificium aut donarium aliquod ad templum, aut ad Sacerdotes in Corbonam deferrent. Nam, vt supra audiuimus, filij quoq; neglecta pietatis in parentes officia hoc praetextu excusabant, vt iam de alijs nihil dicatur.
units.tr: Lest anyone think that he acted in a mad rage without reason, he joined teaching to the deed, as Matthew notes, saying: "It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers." He cites Scriptures, which even the common people of the Jews acknowledged to contain the Word of God and eternal life. He joins two passages of Scripture, the first of which is taken from Isaiah and states the true use of the temple. There the prophet foretells the calling of the Gentiles, who are all to come to the Church, so that in it they may call upon the true God through the Mediator Christ. The Lord says: "My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples." But since that Jewish temple was a type of the Church, what was once said of the Church is now rightly applied to it. The other passage is in Jeremiah, where he rebukes the abuse of the temple, to show that this abuse rightly must be corrected and utterly abolished. There the Lord rebukes the false professors of his worship, who abused the temple and the external rites as licence for their sins. He says: "Behold, you trust in lying words, which will not profit you. Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods, and yet still come and stand before me in this house and say, 'We are delivered,' even though you have done all these abominations?" He adds: "Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?" That is, do you think my temple is like a cave, into which robbers retreat after murders and plunder taken by force from travellers, so that you too may suppose you can hide and conceal yourselves under its cover? And indeed this belief had then bewitched almost the minds of all the Jews, so that they thought nothing so wicked or impious could be done that it would not be atoned for, provided they brought some sacrifice or gift to the temple, or to the priests at the Corban. For, as we heard above, even children used this pretext to excuse their neglect of the duties of piety towards their parents, not to mention others.

units.la: Ioan. 2. Matth. 21.
units.tr: John 2. Matt. 21.

units.la: [?]Veterem ergo expostulationem Dei illis in mentem reuocat Dominus, vt demonstret,tam Dei gloriam quam salutem publicam postulare, vt tandem prophanationi isti sacrorum finis impona-tur, & proprium templi atq; cultus diuini vsus instauretur. Quo loco admonemur, non omnem pie-tatis externa speciem Deo probari, etiamsi quoad ritus externos cum verbo eius conueniat, non autem ad eum finem dirigatur, quem ille nobis vult esse propositum, qui est obedientia fidei, & vt mortificatis carnis affectibus salutis meritum in vno Christo quaeramus, qui nobis ab illo iustitia & satisfactio datus est. Quid vero de imposturis, quae quaestus gratia sub religionis praetextu fiunt, grauius & horribilius dici poterat, quam quod illas speluncam latronum dicit Dominus? Et excitet nos ad huius disti diligentiorem considerationem, quod eius doctrinam miraculis quoq; confirmauit. Venerunt enim ad eum caeci & claudi, & sanauit eos.
units.tr: [?]The Lord therefore brings back to their minds God's old complaint, to show that both the glory of God and the public welfare demand that this profanation of the sacred things should at last be brought to an end, and that the proper use of the temple and of divine worship be restored. Here we are reminded that God does not approve of every outward show of piety, even if it agrees with his Word in external rites, when it is not directed to that end which he wishes to be our aim. That end is obedience of faith, and that, having mortified the affections of the flesh, we seek the merit of salvation in Christ alone, who has been given to us as our righteousness and satisfaction. Indeed, what could be said more gravely and more horribly about the impostures that are done for the sake of gain under the pretext of religion, than that the Lord calls them a den of robbers? And let this also stir us to consider this matter more carefully: he confirmed his teaching by miracles as well. For the blind and the lame came to him, and he healed them.

units.la: Debet autem ex hoc filij Dei exemplo generalis doctrina peti, quam in reformandis Ecclesijs sequantur Christiani principes, si quando religionem horrendis abusibus depravatam esse vi-dent. Disputatur de hac re hodie passim, & qui abusus & superstitiones neq; negare neq; defende-re possunt, ad hoc χπηοφυγετον siue suffugium sese recipiunt. Quod in nullius hominis auctoritate sit, Ecclesiae reformationem instituere, nisi ex vniuersalis concilij & summorum Pontificum consensione. At Christus in praesenti non expectat eorum decretum, qui tunc in cathedra Mosis sedebant, sed cum ipse a Deo Patre Rex constitutus esset super Zion montem sanctum, opus hoc non minus necessarium quam sanctum aggreditur, & huius exemplum postea Apostoli secuti, passim Iudaeos & gentes a consuetis erroribus ad fidem veram reuocarunt, imo in ipsa Ierosolyma Ecclesiam nouam constituerunt, quae Euangelij doctrinae responderet. Idem olim Moses fecit, cum totus Israel cum Pontifice Aarone Dei cultum corrupisset. Ita Gedeon a Deo Iudex Israelis eleuatus a reformatione cultus diuini initium fecit, non expectato Sacerdotum & Leuitarum consensu. Hos ergo & horum similes imitentur Christiani principes, & sui officij esse meminerint, vt religionem & cultum Dei a sordibus superstitionum repurgent, & de vera illius forma reducenda serio cogitent.
units.tr: From this example of the Son of God a general doctrine ought to be drawn, which Christian princes should follow in reforming the Churches, whenever they see religion depraved by horrible abuses. Today this matter is debated everywhere, and those who can neither deny nor defend the abuses and superstitions take refuge in this [χπηοφυγετον]. They say that it is not within the authority of any man to institute a reformation of the Church, unless by the consent of a universal council and of the supreme Pontiffs. But Christ, in the present case, did not wait for the decision of those who then sat in the chair of Moses. Since he himself had been appointed King by God the Father over the holy mountain of Zion, he undertook this work, no less necessary than holy. The Apostles afterwards followed this example, and everywhere they called Jews and Gentiles back from their accustomed errors to the true faith; indeed, in Jerusalem itself they established a new Church, which corresponded to the teaching of the Gospel. Moses did the same once, when all Israel with the high priest Aaron had corrupted the worship of God. So Gideon, raised up by God as judge of Israel, made a beginning of reforming the divine worship, without waiting for the consent of the priests and Levites. Let Christian princes therefore imitate these men and others like them, and remember that it is their duty to cleanse religion and the worship of God from the filth of superstitions, and to think seriously about restoring its true form.

units.la: Ne vero in eo erretur, certa regula opus erit, quam similiter suo exemplo Christus nobis monstrat. Etsi enim ipse sit aeternum & omnipotens illud Verbum, per quod omnia creata sunt, & cui authoritas sua ex scipso constat, ad Scripturas tamen Iudaeos remittit, & sui facti rationem ex illis reddit. Ergo ex illis peti debet regula, quam sequamur, si Dei cultum ad veram formam velimus reuocare. Etenim Ecclesia domus Dei est, cuius solius vox in illa sonare debet. Non alibi autem haec quam in Scripturis inuenitur. Errant igitur qui ad nescio quos canones aut Patres siue decreta respiciunt. Hic enim animae & conscientiae negotium agitur, quae in solo Dei verbo acquiescit, quando extra Deum nihil est, quod illi possit satisfacere.
units.tr: But lest error arise in this, a sure rule will be needed, which Christ likewise shows us by his own example. For although he is the eternal and almighty Word, through whom all things were created, and whose authority rests on himself, he nevertheless refers the Jews to the Scriptures, and gives the reason for his action from them. Therefore the rule we follow must be sought from them, if we wish to bring the worship of God back to its true form. For the Church is the house of God, in which the voice of God alone ought to sound. But this voice is found nowhere else than in the Scriptures. Those therefore err who look to I know not what canons, or to the Fathers, or to decrees. For here the matter concerns the soul and conscience, which rests in the Word of God alone, since outside God there is nothing that can satisfy it.

units.la: Non sufficit autem allegasse Verbum Dei ex Scripturis, sed manus operi admoueri debet vt secundum exemplum Christi omnia ea aboleantur, quae illi aduersa sunt, & quorum nullus in religione vsus est. In hunc censum veniunt omnia, quae ab hominibus instituta sunt, & quae super stitioforum quaestui seruiunt. Dei enim decretum est: Frustra me colunt docentes doctrinas homi-num. Item non erit Chananaeus, id est, mercator siue insitor in domo Domini. Ex verbi quidem praedicatione viuere licet illius administris, sicuti multis docet Paulus ad Corinthios. At ex donis Spiritus sancti quaedam facere, id nefas & impium est, & extant exempla Giezi & Simonis Magi, quae demonstrant, quid ijs sperandum sit, qui illud faciunt. Ad ista si quae in Papatu siunt, examines, quid obsecro poterit consistere? Quid enim illic non est venale? quid est, quod alio quam humanarum traditionum fundamento nitatur. De his ergo tollendis cogitent, qui in Magistratu sunt, & hic fidelem operam praestent doctores: Et vt Christus a templi reformatione initium fecit, & sub finem vitae denuo hoc opus semel atq; iterum aggressus est, & cum nihil apud Iudaeos obstinatos proficeret, per Romanos templum ipsum cum vrbe euertit: ita nobis quoq; haec studiorum nostrorum summa esto, vt e medio tollantur quaecunque contra Dei verbum irreperunt: & licet primus conatus non succedat, & personati praesules instaurare pergant, quae semel & iterum sublata sunt, non pigeat tamen eundem laborem repetere, nec dubitemus de Dei auxilio, qui facile potest coercere eos, qui verbo suo se contumaciter opponunt, & abusus per illud sublatos reducunt. In locum autem eorum, quae tolluntur, substituere studeamus vera pietatis exercitia, quae sunt syn cera Verbi praedicatio, fides in unum Deum, invocatio unius Dei, legitimus sacramentorum usus: quorum omnium hic nobis finis & scopus sit, ut intra mentes nostras illuminati, & novis viribus instaurati, omnem sublimitatem, quae adversus Dei cognitionem extollitur, per fidei obedientiam subigamus, & recto pede ambulemus in praeceptis Filii Dei IESV CHRISTI, & huic nos sistamus viventem hostiam, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: It is not enough, however, to have cited the Word of God from the Scriptures; the hand must be put to the work, so that, following the example of Christ, all those things are abolished which are opposed to him, and which have no use in religion. Everything that has been instituted by men, and that serves the gain of the superstitious, falls into this category. For God's decree is: "In vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines of men." Likewise, "there shall no longer be a Canaanite, that is, a merchant or dealer, in the house of the Lord." It is indeed lawful for the ministers of the Word to live from its preaching, as Paul teaches the Corinthians in many places. But to make some profit from the gifts of the Holy Spirit is wicked and impious, and the examples of Gehazi and of Simon Magus show what those who do this may expect. If you examine what is done in the Papacy by these standards, what, I ask, can stand? For what is not for sale there? What is there that rests on any foundation other than human traditions? Let therefore those who hold the magistracy consider how these things may be removed, and let the teachers render faithful labour here. And just as Christ made a beginning of reforming the temple, and at the end of his life undertook this work again, once and a second time, and when he achieved nothing among the obstinate Jews, the Romans overthrew the temple itself together with the city, so let this be the sum of our studies: that whatever has crept in against the Word of God be taken out of the way. And even if the first attempt does not succeed, and the masked prelates continue to restore what has been removed once and again, let us not be discouraged from repeating the same labour, nor doubt God's help, who can easily restrain those who stubbornly oppose his Word, and who restores the abuses removed by it. In place of the things that are removed, let us take care to substitute the true exercises of piety, which are the pure preaching of the Word, faith in the one God, the invocation of the one God, and the lawful use of the sacraments. Let this be the end and aim for all of us: that, enlightened in our minds and renewed with new strength, we may subdue through the obedience of faith every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and walk with a straight foot in the precepts of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, and present ourselves to him as a living sacrifice, to whom be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXLIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCXLIIII.

units.la: Cum vidissent autem principes Sacerdotum & Scribae miracula illa, quae fecerat, & pueros clamantes in templo, & dicentes, Hosanna filio David: indignati sunt, & dixerunt ei: Audis quid isti dicant? IESVS autem dixit eis: Etiam nunquam legistis, Ex ore infantium & lactentium perfecisti laudem? Et relictis eis exiit extra urbem in Bethaniam: & diversatus est illic.
