So if they allow those committed to their discipline either to be steeped in superstitions, or to be corrupted by licence of morals, or even corrupt them by their own example, what fruit will God be able to receive from them in time to come? Or what will those teachers be able to render to his tax collectors, if they are called to account?

units.la: Quia vero haec necessitas colonis omnibus incumbit, quorum opera in vinea sua excolenda Deus vtitur, vt huic rationem reddere teneantur pro omnibus, qui ipsorum curae commissi sunt, patienter idem ferendi sunt, si officium faciant, & operi dominico insistent. Etenim non sibi ipsis laborant, sed Deo, qui ad hoc ipsos vocauit. Tu vero quis es, qui seruos Dei opus, quod ipsis mandatum est, facere prohibeas? De Prophetis Amos dicebat: Leo si rugiat, quis non timebit? Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetaret? Ide posiunt de seipsis dicere qui in magistratu constituti sunt, ide etiam quibus iuuentutis cura & institutio commissa est, siue illi parentes, siue scholarum moderatores fuerint. Vrgentur hi omnes Dei mandato, cui nisi tu quoq; te accommodaueris, no poteris in vinea illius locum habere, vt vel arbor vel vitis fecunda dicaris, quae fructu suo herum exhilaret.
units.tr: Because this duty rests upon all tenants, whose work God uses in cultivating his vineyard, and they are bound to render an account of this for all who have been entrusted to their care, they must be patiently borne with when they do their duty and persevere in the Lord's work. For they labour not for themselves but for God, who has called them to this. But who are you, that you forbid the servants of God to do the work that has been committed to them? Concerning the prophets Amos said: "If a lion roars, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, who will not prophesy?" (Amos 3.8). The same may be said of themselves by those who are placed in office, and likewise by those to whom the care and instruction of youth is committed, whether they are parents or heads of schools. All of these are urged by the command of God; and unless you too adapt yourself to it, you will not be able to have a place in his vineyard, so as to be called a fruitful tree or vine that gladdens its master with its fruit.

units.la: Caeterum hic non tam consideranda quam acerbissimis lachrymis deploranda venit infelicis mundi ingratitudo & contumacia, qui Deo creatori & factori suo non solum fructus debitos negat, verumetiam pessimam gratiam rependit, vt plerisq; dici possit, quod Isaias de vinea Domini inter Iudaeos plantata canit: Expectauit Dominus, vt uuas ferret, sed reddidit labrusca. Expectauit iudicium, & ecce conspiratio: iustitia, & ecce clamor. In praesenti vero de colonis solis agit, qui ad se missos fructuum exactores indignissime tractarint, vt offendat, nullos acriores hostes esse gratiae Dei & verae pietatis, quam antistites & praesules, qui sub religionis praetextu res suas agunt. Nam, vt saepe monuimus, nulli luce veritatis minus ferre potuerunt, & ex historiis constat, hos omnibus saeculis primos fuisse authores persecutionum, quae aduersus germanos Dei seruos sunt excitatae. Et quod hic de Iudaeorum sacerdotibus sub colonorum exemplo dicitur, prolixe demonstratur in Prophetarum libris. In primis commentarij loco sunt, quae habentur 1. Reg.17.2. Par.36. Idem aut nostro quoq; saeculo experimur. Interim non isti soli reprehensione merentur, sed est ingratitudo haec vniuersalis, qua vulgo peccatur. Etenim est hoc proprium malae fidei debitoribus, quod creditores optime de se meritos oderunt, & exactores cum comunitis reijciant. Atqui natura tales sumus, qui cum a pueris in aere Dei simus, & noua quotidie beneficia ab illo recipiamus, quibus ille nos sibi magis obstrictos reddit, vix tamen vnquam solemus cogitare, quid illi referri debeat. Non ergo miru est, si indignis modis tractetur exactores, qui ius Dei vrgent, & vt ei satis faciamus, serio postulant. Exempla sunt ab origine rerum, quae his fide faciunt, & scimus, hac de causa fere omnes Martyres ab ingrato mundo crudeliter & impie necatos fuisse. Habet enim suos gradus impietas, per quot ad summum adscendit, vt grauiori lapsu ruat. Initium mali est, nolle fructum debitum Deo reddere, cui omnia nostra & nosipsos debemus. Hinc nascitur odium ministrorum, qui vt officium faciamus petunt. At odium hoc omni iniuriarum genere declarant impij: nec ante exatiantur, quam illos extinctos videant.
units.tr: Yet here it is not so much the ingratitude and obstinacy of the unhappy world that must be considered as lamented with the bitterest tears, which not only denies the fruit it owes to God its creator and maker, but even repays him with the worst ingratitude, so that what Isaiah sang of the vineyard of the Lord planted among the Jews may be said of many: "The Lord expected that it would bring forth grapes, but it brought forth wild grapes. He expected judgement, and behold, conspiracy; righteousness, and behold, a cry" (Isa. 5.2, 7). Here, however, he speaks only of the tenants who treated most shamefully the tax collectors sent to them; and so, to make the point plain, there are no fiercer enemies of the grace of God and true godliness than the leaders and prelates who pursue their own affairs under the pretext of religion. For, as we have often warned, none have been less able to bear the light of truth, and it is clear from histories that in every age these men were the first authors of the persecutions that have been stirred up against the true servants of God. And what is said here of the priests of the Jews under the example of the tenants is shown at length in the books of the prophets. Chief among these passages for comment are those found in 1 Kings 17.2 and 2 Chronicles 36. We experience the same in our own age as well. Meanwhile, these men alone do not deserve reproof, but this ingratitude is universal, and is the sin commonly committed. For it is a mark of bad faith in debtors that they hate creditors who have deserved best of them, and cast off the exactors along with the things they demand. Indeed, we are by nature such that, although from childhood we live in the air of God and receive new benefits from him every day, by which he binds us ever more closely to himself, we scarcely ever think about what ought to be rendered to him. It is no wonder, then, if those who press God's right and seriously demand that we satisfy him are treated in unworthy ways. There are examples from the beginning of the world that bear witness to this, and we know that for this reason nearly all the martyrs were cruelly and impiously put to death by the ungrateful world. Impiety has its steps, by which it climbs to the top, so that it may fall with a heavier collapse. The beginning of evil is to be unwilling to render to God the fruit owed to him, to whom we owe all that we have and ourselves. From this arises hatred of the ministers who demand that we do our duty. And the wicked declare this hatred by every kind of injury, nor are they satisfied until they see them dead.

units.la: Hic vero seruorum, de quibus in praesenti agitur, fortitudinem imitentur Christianae fortitudinis ... nes, quorum ministerio Deus vti dignatur. Caeditur ignominiose primus seruus a colonis. Non autem idcirco obsequium suum hero negat secundus: & cum hic quoq; indignius tractetur, alij, quorum aliqui crudelissime necati, aliqui lapidibus obruti sunt, non tamen horum exemplis reliqui terrentur, quo minus hero obtemperent, & ipsi quoq; periculum subeant. Fit quidem interdum, vt aliqui carnis infirmitate vincti atq; superati initio se difficiliores praebeant (quod Mosi etiam & nonnullis prophetarum accidit) sed ijdem postea alacres obsequuntur Deo, quando hunc ita velle vident, qui summũ in ipsos ius habet & imperium. Hos imitemur, ne illius mandatum detrectando periculis grauioribus nos intricemus. Neq; opus est, ut nostras rationes Deo opponamus. Nouit is omnia, & euentus rerum ipse regit. Si ergo per nos quid confectum velit, ipse facultatibus necessarijs nos instruet. Sin minus, beati tamen sunt, qui ipsius nomine periclitantur, & ducem habent Filium Dei IESVM CHRISTVM, cum quo olim in cœlis beata im mortalitate fruentur. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Here let those who are concerned imitate the courage of the servants of whom the present passage speaks, the Christian fortitude ... by whose ministry God deigns to be served. The first servant is shamefully beaten by the tenants. Yet the second does not on that account refuse obedience to his master; and when he too is treated more outrageously, others, some of whom were most cruelly killed and some stoned to death, nevertheless are not deterred by these examples from obeying their master, and they too undergo danger. It does sometimes happen that some, overcome and conquered by the weakness of the flesh, at first show themselves more unwilling (as also happened to Moses and to some of the prophets), but afterwards these same men obey God cheerfully when they see that he wills it so, he who has supreme right and command over them. Let us imitate these, lest by refusing his command we entangle ourselves in greater dangers. Nor is it necessary that we set our own reasons against God. He knows all things, and he himself governs the outcomes of events. If therefore he wishes something to be accomplished through us, he himself will furnish us with the necessary means. But if not, blessed nevertheless are those who are put in peril in his name, and who have as their leader the Son of God, Jesus Christ, with whom they will one day enjoy blessed immortality in heaven. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLI.
units.tr: Homily 251.

units.la: Postremo autem misit ad eos Filium suum, dicens: Reuerebuntur Filium meum. Agricolæ autem viso filio dixerunt inter se: Iste est hæres, venite, trucidemus eum, & obtineamus hæreditatem eius. Tunc captum eum eiecerunt extra vineam ac trucidarunt. Cum igitur venerit dominus vineæ, quid faciet agricolis illis? Dicunt ei: Malos ipsos male perdet, & vineam suam elocabit alijs colonis, qui reddent ei fructum temporibus suis.
units.tr: Last of all he sent his son to them, saying: "They will respect my son." But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance." So they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him. When the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants? They say to him: "He will put those wicked men to a wretched death and will let out the vineyard to other tenants, who will pay him the fruit in its season."

units.la: Interea quæ plerosque homines remorantur, quo minus IESVM CHRISTVM fide vera amplexentur, non aliud efficacius est, quàm quòd illum & eius doctrinam ab ijs contemni & hostiliter oppugnari vident, qui in mundo authoritate & potentia præstant. Obfuit hoc etiam vulgo Iudæorum, quando viderunt sacerdotes & Scribas, qui in Mosis cathedra sedebant, acerrimos illius hostes esse: & ex historia Euangelij per Ioannem descripta constat, hos eo potissimum argumento apud rudes & imperitos aduersus illum vsos esse, quòd nemo ex primoribus aut Pharisæis in illum crederet. Vt ergo hoc scandalum remoueretur, parabolam hanc illis publicè proponit, qua docet, non nouum aut insolens hoc esse quod faciant, cum idem olim fecerint patres & antecessores ipsorum, quorum mensuram (vt alibi ait) ipsi impleant. At quia non ignorabat, indignam suam morte, quam non multò post subituru erat, plerisq; scandalo fore, nunc de illa quoq; disserit, ne quid fortuito aut ipso ignorante putent fieri.
units.tr: Meanwhile, nothing hinders many people more from embracing Jesus Christ in true faith than seeing him and his teaching scorned and violently attacked by those who excel in authority and power in the world. This also harmed the common people of the Jews, when they saw that the priests and scribes, who sat in Moses' seat, were his bitterest enemies. And from the account of the Gospel written by John, it is clear that they used this argument above all against him among the simple and unlearned: that no one of the leaders or Pharisees believed in him. So, to remove this stumbling block, he publicly sets forth this parable to them, in which he teaches that what they are doing is neither new nor strange, since their fathers and forebears did the same thing, and they fill up the measure of those fathers (as he says elsewhere). But because he was not unaware that his death, which was not far off, would be a stumbling block to many because of its unworthiness, he now also discourses about that, so that they may not think anything happens by chance or without his knowledge.

units.la: Et primò quidem simpliciter exponit, qua occasione ipse ad eos venerit, quòd nimirum Deus se per Prophetas nihil proficere videret, & ideo Filium ad contumaces illos mittere voluerit. Apud Lucam Deus consultans aut deliberans inducitur, qui dixerit: Quid faciam? mittam Filium illum meum dilectum: forsitan cum hunc viderint, reuerebuntur. Dicuntur autem hæc de Deo ως θεῷ πoπάθως, id est, humano more, non quòd ille, qui rerum euentus nouit, & pro libito gubernat, anxius aut dubius de rebus agendis vel secum ipse, vel cum alijs deliberet: sed vt doceat, nihil in tota hac causa fortuitum esse, sed ex æterno Dei decreto omnia geri, qui ipsum (vt Petrus postea scripsit) priusquam mundus conderetur, ad hoc prædestinauit. Estq; diligenter cõsideranda hoc loco plus quàm paterna Dei bonitas, qui cum lapsum hominis præuideret, ab æterno Seruatore quoque prædestinauit: qui lapsos erigeret, & opem ferret de salute sua periclitantibus. Qui enim ad tuendam corporis valetudinem herbas, radices & omnis generis remedia creauit, priusquam mors cum morte ingressi sunt in mundum, noluit animabus deesse, quæ præstantior hominis pars est. Et cum hoc decretum suum optimo iure reuocare posset propter vniuersalem gentium impietatem & πολυθείαν, propter ingratitudinem item & contumaciam Iudæorum, qui ipsum in seruis suis Prophetis tam multis tamq; atrocibus iniurijs affecerant, illud tan ratum esse voluit, & præstini-to tempore in vineam illam ingratam ad colonos perfidos atq; sceleratos Filium vnigenitum misit, qui non tam exactor fructuum quàm sponsor esset, & iram eius iustam placaret. Docent ista nos ex gratuita Dei misericordia seruatos esse, qui ita dilexit nos, vt Filio suo vnigenito non peperce-rit, sed eum miserit in mundum, vt pro nobis morte indigna & acerba tolleretur. Estq; bonitas ista eò illustrior, quòd ad eos missus est Filius Dei, qui digni erant, vt carnifices aut milites vastato res illis submitterentur, qui perfidia & crudelitatis inexcusabilis pœnas de illis exigerent. Ser-
units.tr: First, he simply explains the occasion on which he came to them: namely, that God saw he was accomplishing nothing through the prophets, and so he wished to send his Son to those stubborn people. In Luke, God is introduced as taking counsel or deliberating, saying: "What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps when they see him they will respect him." These things are said of God [ὡς θεῷ πεπάθως], that is, in human fashion, not because he who knows the outcome of all things and governs them at his pleasure is anxious or doubtful about what to do, and deliberates either with himself or with others; but to teach that nothing in this whole matter is by chance, and that all things are carried out by the eternal decree of God, who (as Peter later wrote) predestined him for this before the world was made. Here we must carefully consider the more than fatherly goodness of God, who, foreseeing the fall of man, also predestined from eternity the Saviour who would raise up the fallen and bring help to those in danger of losing their salvation. For just as he created herbs, roots and remedies of every kind to preserve bodily health, before death entered the world along with sin, so he did not wish to leave souls without help, which is the more excellent part of man. And although he could most justly have revoked this decree because of the universal impiety and polytheism of the nations, and likewise because of the ingratitude and stubbornness of the Jews, who had treated his servants the prophets with so many and such atrocious wrongs, he nevertheless wished that decree to stand, and at the appointed time he sent his only-begotten Son to the ungrateful vineyard, to the faithless and wicked tenants, who was not so much a collector of fruit as a surety, and who would appease his just anger. These things teach us that we have been saved by God's free mercy, who so loved us that he did not spare his only-begotten Son, but sent him into the world to be taken away for us by an unworthy and bitter death. And this goodness is all the more remarkable because the Son of God was sent to those who deserved that the executioners or soldiers should be sent against them to lay waste their land, and who should exact punishment from them for their unpardonable treachery and cruelty.

units.la: Exod. 3. 4 Lev. 1. 1. Reg. 19. uiant ista consolationi in tentationibus, ne facile propter peccatorum multitudinem seu atrocitatem desperemus. Est enim fons gratiae Dei inexhaustus: neque potest ille Filij sui meritum reijcere, si eum audiamus, quem ipse dedit, et propter quem se nobis placatum esse, de coelo testatus est, ut iam de promissionibus prisciis et Prophetarum vaticinijs nihil dicatur. At simul nos officij admonet Dei Patris exemplum, ut nos similiter eorum saluti studeamus, qui nos grauissime offenderunt, nec locum demus vindictae cupiditati, quae par pari referre docet, et simultatum causa est, quibus charitas et concordia turbatur. Etenim Filij Dei dici et esse non poterunt, nisi qui eius ingenium referunt, et quid maneat eos, qui offensas non remittunt conferuis suis, qui in ipsos deliquerunt, supra Capite decimooctauo prolixe in parabola est demonstratum. In primis ad Verbi ministros haec consideratio pertinet, ne nimio zelo abrepti temere damnent eos, qui peccarunt, et in desperationis praecipitium abducant: quod non raro fit, si remissionem negent delinquentibus, aut nunquam finiendis satisfactionibus eos fatigent, quos pijs consolationibus debebant erigere et confirmare. Alia est continuacia ratio, qui cum scelerum suorum atrocitatem non agnoscant, sed potius scurriliter extenuent, minis acrioribus compellandi, et ad tribunal Dei citandi sunt, ut intra animos suos terrici discant ferio de gratia illius et vitae totius emendatione cogitare.
units.tr: Exod. 3. 4; Lev. 1; 1 Kings 19. These things should serve as a consolation in temptations, so that we do not easily despair because of the multitude or the atrocity of our sins. For the fountain of God's grace is inexhaustible, nor can he reject the merit of his Son, if we hear him whom he himself gave, and on account of whom he testified from heaven that he was reconciled to us; not to mention the earlier promises and the prophecies of the prophets. At the same time, the example of God the Father reminds us of our duty, that we likewise should care for the salvation of those who have most grievously offended us, and not give place to the desire for vengeance, which teaches us to repay like with like, and which is the cause of quarrels by which love and concord are disturbed. For those who do not forgive their fellow servants who have sinned against them cannot be called or be sons of God, unless they reflect his nature; and what awaits those who do not remit offences is set out at length in the parable above, in chapter eighteen. This consideration pertains especially to the ministers of the Word, so that, carried away by excessive zeal, they do not rashly condemn those who have sinned and drive them into the abyss of despair. This often happens if they deny forgiveness to offenders, or wear them out with satisfactions that never end, when they ought to raise them up and strengthen them with godly consolations. Another class of people must be dealt with differently: those who do not acknowledge the atrocity of their crimes, but rather make light of them in a buffoonish way. They must be confronted with sharper threats and summoned to the judgment seat of God, so that they may learn to be terrified in their hearts and to think about his grace and the amendment of their whole life.

units.la: Sed audiamus quid agricolae aut coloni isti fecerint. Pergunt in scelerata illa nequitia, et qui conseruos suos, qui hero fideles sunt, indignis modis tractarunt, idem sibi in herilem filium licere arbitrantur. Nam illo viso de eo occidendo consultant, neque aliquas causas praetexunt, quae in speciem videri possint iustae, utpote quod iniuriis ab illo passi sint, aut quod iam pridem ingenij superbi et crudelis specimina dederit, ut nihil aequum vel humanum de illo possint sperare: sed inter se dicunt: Ille est haeres, venite trucidemus eum, et obtineamus haereditatem eius. Quae ideo annotantur, ut constet illos non ignorantia deceptos, aut caeco animi affectu abreptos peccauisse, sed consulto et destinata malitia scelus tantum designasse. Agnoscunt enim illum esse filium herilem, et vineae atque bonorum omnium legitimum haeredem: nec potuerunt ignorare, illum idcirco dignum esse, quem reuereantur, et cui fidele seruitum praestent. At non seruire volunt, sed dominari potius cupiunt in vinea: quod cum illo viuo non possit fieri intelligant, crudele et iniquum de illo occidendo consilium capiunt, ut haereditatem et peculium, quod illi debebatur, ipsi obtinere possint. Ad amplificationem scelerus facit, quod non de facie modo filium herilem noverunt, sed quod hic suam bonitatem et virtutem saluifi cam docti nam simul et salutaribus beneficijs manifestarat, in quibus rude et imperitum vulgus sub vili habitu latentem Dei Filium et promissum Seruatorem agnoscere potuit. Huc respiciens Christus postea dicebat: Si opera non fecissem inter eos, quae nemo alius fecit, peccatum non haberent: nunc autem non habent quod praetexant peccato suo. Joannis decimoquinto Cap.
units.tr: But let us hear what those farmers or tenants did. They press on in their wicked villainy, and those who treated their fellow servants, who were faithful to the master, in unworthy ways, think it is likewise permitted to them against the master's son. For when they saw him, they plotted to kill him, and they put forward no causes that might appear just, such as that he had wronged them, or that he had already shown a proud and cruel disposition, so that nothing fair or humane could be hoped for from him. Instead they say among themselves: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance." These words are noted so that it may be clear they did not sin through ignorance, or carried away by blind emotion, but that they deliberately and with settled malice planned the crime. For they acknowledge that he is the master's son and the lawful heir of the vineyard and of all the goods; nor could they fail to know that he was therefore worthy to be revered and to be served with faithful service. But they do not want to serve; they rather desire to rule in the vineyard. Understanding that this cannot be done while he is alive, they adopt the cruel and unjust plan of killing him, so that they might obtain the inheritance and the property that was due to him. The wickedness is increased by the fact that they knew the master's son not only by sight, but that he had also made known his goodness and saving power by beneficial acts, by which the simple and unlearned crowd could recognise, beneath a humble appearance, the Son of God and the promised Saviour. Looking to this, Christ later said: "If I had not done among them works that no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin." John 15.

units.la: Est autem hoc loco obseruatu dignissimum, Ecclesiam haereditatem filij Dei dici. Est enim hoc frequens admodum in scripturis. In Psalmis dicitur: Beata illa gens, cuius Deus est Iehoua: et populus quem elegit sibi in haereditatem. Ratio huius nominis aut tituli indicatur ab ipso Deo quando is Filio dixit: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes, ut sint haereditas tua, etc. Et hinc est quod terra Canaan quoque, quae Deus Iudaeis, ad quos olim Ecclesiae titulus pertinebat inhabitandam dedit, haereditas Domini dicitur, et ideo in psalmis queruntur pij: Venerunt o Deus gentes in haereditate tuam, etc. Et prodest de eo diligenter et saepe cogitare. Ut enim haereditas ad filios legitime peruenit, ita Ecclesiae dominus verus et legitimus est filius Dei, et solus pro eius capite agnoscit debet. Potest aut ex eo peti dulcissima consolatio. Etenim qui homines frugi et suae existimationis ftu diofi sunt, maximi facere solent, quae ex haereditate paterna ad ipsos peruenerunt. Nam ea paruifaccere, et turpiter dilapidare, quae maiores virtute et industria sua acquisiuerunt, et diu cum laude possent: deriunt, animi leuissimi et inhonesti argumentum est. Vidit hoc Naboth, qui vineam a patrib. suis ipse reliquit regi quoque suo negare non est veritus. Quis ergo dubitet, Christus in summo pretio habere Ecclesiam quae ipsius haereditas est, quam et Pater ipsi aeterno testamento legauit, et ipse proprio sanguine pretio redemit? Nouit ille suos, ex quibus illa constat, et quos ipsi dedit Pater, nemo ei eripiet. Cur ergo mundum aut principem huius metuamus? Fremat hic cum membris suis ut lubet. Est tamen iam olim viſtus & contritus Christi virtute & merito, nec desunt huic vires, quibus tuea-tur omnes, qui ad ipsius haereditatem pertinent.
units.tr: Now the point most worthy of notice here is that the Church is called the inheritance of the Son of God. For this is very frequent in the Scriptures. In the Psalms it is said: "Blessed is that nation whose God is Jehovah, and the people whom he has chosen as his inheritance." The reason for this name or title is indicated by God himself when he said to the Son: "Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance," and so on. And hence the land of Canaan also, which God gave to the Jews, to whom the title of the Church once belonged, to dwell in, is called the inheritance of the Lord; and so the godly complain in the Psalms: "O God, the nations have come into your inheritance," and so on. And it is useful to think carefully and often about this. For just as an inheritance comes lawfully to the sons, so the true and lawful lord of the Church is the Son of God, and he alone must be acknowledged as its head. From this a most sweet consolation can be drawn. For men who are thrifty and careful of their reputation are wont to value most highly what has come to them from their paternal inheritance. To despise and shamefully squander what their ancestors acquired by virtue and industry, and what could have remained with praise for a long time, is a sign of a most frivolous and dishonourable mind. Naboth saw this; he kept the vineyard that he had left him by his fathers, and he did not hesitate to refuse it even to his king. Who, then, could doubt that Christ holds the Church in the highest esteem, since it is his inheritance, which the Father bequeathed to him by an eternal testament and which he himself redeemed with his own blood as a price? He knows his own, out of whom the Church is made up, and whom the Father gave him; no one will snatch them from him. Why then should we fear the world or its prince? Let him rage here with his members as he pleases. He has nevertheless already been conquered and crushed by the power and merit of Christ, and there is no lack of strength for him to protect all who belong to his inheritance.

units.la: Interim non minus de nostro officio ista nos admonent, ut nimirum memores nos vineam & haereditatem Filij Dei esse, nostram dignitatem fortiter tueamur, & neq; nosipsos vel alios alie-nemus a Christo. Faciunt hoc priuatim, qui seipsos ab illius seruitio subducunt, & diabolo manci-pant, dum pessimis affectibus indulgent, & ita viuunt, ut propter ipsos Dei nomen male audiat. Idem publice faciunt cum maiori scelere, qui alios a Christo abducunt, dum illicitarum superstitio-num traditionibus imperitos & incautos fascinant, aut etiam aperta vi fideles Christi ministos persequuntur, & eos fidem in hunc abnegare, aut saltem ea facere cogunt, quae cum fidei confessio-ne non possunt conuenire. Non ferent isti impune quod faciunt, & qui olim Nabotho factam in-iuriam & eius indignam necem tam graviter vltus est, minime impunitos abire sinet, qui ipsius haereditatem intercipere, & eos ab ipso alienare audent, quos tanto pretio sibi acquisiuit.
units.tr: In the meantime, these words admonish us no less about our own duty: that, remembering that we are the vineyard and the inheritance of the Son of God, we should bravely defend our dignity and not alienate ourselves or others from Christ. Those who withdraw themselves from his service and surrender themselves to the devil do this privately, indulging in the worst passions and living in such a way that the name of God is badly spoken of on their account. Those who lead others away from Christ do the same thing publicly, and with greater wickedness, when they beguile the untaught and the unwary with the traditions of unlawful superstitions, or when they persecute Christ's faithful ministers by open force and compel them either to deny the faith or at least to do things that cannot agree with the confession of faith. Such men will not get away unpunished for what they do. He who avenged so severely the wrong done to Naboth and his unworthy death will certainly not let pass unpunished those who dare to seize his inheritance and to alienate from him those whom he has acquired for himself at so great a price.

units.la: Praeterea admonet nos haec colonorum pessimorum consultatio, qua de causa homines Christum oderint & sublatum velint: Nimirum non quod aliquam ab illo iniuriam patiantur, aut passi sint, sed quod eius haereditatem ipsi ad se transferre cupiant. Apparet hoc euidenter in Iudaeorum sacerdotibus, qui per colonos ipsos adumbrantur. Etenim Deus Iudaeos sibi in peculium & sacerdotale regnum delegerat, dederat item promissiones amplissimas, cultus sui sedem inter illos constituerat, qui totus ceremonijs magnificis constabat, typus nimirum mysticus promissi Messiae, qui ex illis suo tempore erat nasciturus. At haec omnia illi sibi ipsis quae tum fecerunt, ut templum ab emporio nihil differret, & haereditatem Domini sub religionis praetexтy exactionibus quotidie nouis grauabant: denique (ut Christus de illis loquitur) sub praetextu precationum suarum deuora-bant domus viduarum atq; pupillorum. Arguebat illorum artes & dolos Christus, & ius suum contra illos perseq uebatur: multi etiam ex vulgo hunc agnoscebant, quae causa erat, quod ipsorum quae stui & existimationi multum quotidie decederet: neq; dubium est intolerabilem dolorem auaris & ambitiosis peperisse inexpectatum illud factum, quo vendentes & ementes templo eiecerat, & cum numulariorum mensis quasdam quoq; omnem eis euerterat. Ex eo enim sentire potuerunt, ipsum esse magnum illum legatum Dei, quem Malachias praedixerat subito venturum in templum su-um, ut filios Leui excoquat & emundet. Idcirco non putant rebus suis aliter consuli posse, quam ut ipse e medio tollatur. Et conuenit plane cum colonorum verbis, quae supra audiuimus, quod Pharisaei postea dixerunt in Concilio: Si sinamus eum ita, omnes credent, venientq; Romani, & delebunt tum locum nostrum tum gentem: Quibus Caiaphas subscribens addidit: Conducit nobis ut vnus homo moriatur pro populo, & tota gens non pereat. Itaq; priuati commodi & gloriae studium Iudaeorum sacerdotes aduersus Christum extimulauit. Eadem causa inter gentes quoq; Deorum & superstitionum mystas movit, ut religioni Christianae se opponerent. Videbant enim haec admissa Deorum cultus aboleri, oracula silere & superstitiones omnes ad nihilum redigi, quibus hactenus ipsi viros principes & populum passim dementarant. Vt ergo qui possessione patria aut auita decedere coguntur, inuiti id faciunt, & non sine fremitu: ita illi quoq; fecerunt, & nihil non tentarunt, ut infelices in ignorantia detinerent. Exempla huius rei Actorum liber in Demetrio Ephesio, in Simone Magno, in Philippensibus Pythonica puella dominis exhibet, qui omnes quae-stus sui ergo contra Euangelium tumultuati sunt. In ecclesiastica autem historia infinita huius generis occurrunt. Et hodie passim idem faciunt, qui in papatu ex superstitionibus dignitates obti-nent & diuites fiunt, in tanta denique existimatione sunt, ut pleriq; ipsorum seruitio sese sua sponte subijciant. Quia ergo hi quoq; per Christum, qui Sol iustitiae & lux mundi est, nebulas suas, quibus diu omnibus fucum fecerunt, argui sentiunt, hic ipsis omnium consiliorum finis & scopus est, ut illum cum Euangelij praedicatione procul arceant, vel potius prorsus e medio tollant. Et quia sibi ad hoc principum aut regum authoritate opus esse vident, hos quoq; falsa hac persuasione imbuunt, ut se non posse in regnis suis suam existimationem retinere arbitrentur, si Christi regnum admittant. Vt ergo olim Herodes illum recens natum extinguere conatus est, ut regnum suum in terris stabiliret: ita hodie hic error principes plerosq; aduersus Christi armat, quod hoc regnan-te regna sua consistere non posse sibi persuaserunt. Quid vero de principibus dicere attinet, quando priuatos homines ide furor exagitat. Etenim singuli in vinea Christi vites aut arbores fructiferas esse debebant, & seipsos illi per fidei obedientiam sistere viuentes hostias. Quam multos autem esse videre, qui vt transfugae aut defectores ferui totos se carnis cupiditatibus dedunt, neque volunt Christum super se regnare. Itaque de eius iugo excutiendo cogitant, & ideo eius ministros horaliter persequuntur.
units.tr: Moreover, the counsel of those wicked tenants warns us why men hate Christ and want him removed. Plainly it is not because they suffer, or have suffered, any injury from him, but because they desire to transfer his inheritance to themselves. This is clearly seen in the priests of the Jews, who are foreshadowed by those tenants. God had chosen the Jews for himself as a peculiar people and a royal priesthood; he had also given them the most ample promises, and had established among them the seat of his worship, which consisted entirely of magnificent ceremonies, the mystical type of the promised Messiah, who was to be born from them in due time. But the priests did everything for their own advantage, so that the temple was no different from a marketplace, and they burdened the inheritance of the Lord with new exactions every day under the pretext of religion. Finally, as Christ says of them, under the pretext of their long prayers they devoured the houses of widows and orphans. Christ exposed their tricks and frauds and pursued his own right against them. Many of the common people recognised this as well, and this was why their authority and reputation were daily diminishing. There is no doubt that that unexpected act, by which he drove out those who sold and bought in the temple and overturned the tables of the money-changers with all their wares, caused intolerable grief to the greedy and ambitious. From it they could perceive that he was that great messenger of God whom Malachi had foretold would suddenly come into his temple to purify and cleanse the sons of Levi. Therefore they thought that their affairs could be secured in no other way than by removing him from the midst. And the words of the tenants, which we heard above, plainly agree with what the Pharisees later said in the council: "If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and destroy both our place and our nation." Caiaphas assented to this and added: "It is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish." Thus the priests of the Jews were goaded by the desire for private gain and glory to act against Christ. The same cause moved the initiates of the gods and superstitions among the Gentiles to oppose the Christian religion. For they saw that, if this were admitted, the worship of the gods would be abolished, the oracles would fall silent, and all the superstitions by which they had hitherto deluded princes and people everywhere would be reduced to nothing. Just as those who are forced to give up a patrimony or an ancestral estate do so unwillingly and not without grumbling, so those men also acted, and left nothing untried so as to keep the unhappy people in ignorance. The book of Acts provides examples of this: in Demetrius of Ephesus, in Simon Magus, and in the Philippian slave-girl with a spirit of divination, whose masters stirred up tumult against the gospel for the sake of their gain. In ecclesiastical history, countless cases of this kind occur. Even today, people do the same everywhere: those who obtain dignities and become rich through superstitions in the papacy, and who enjoy such esteem that many of them willingly submit themselves to their service. Since these men too feel that through Christ, who is the Sun of righteousness and the light of the world, the mists with which they have long deceived everyone are being exposed, the sole aim and object of all their plans is to keep him far away from the preaching of the gospel, or rather to remove him entirely from the midst. And because they see that for this they need the authority of princes or kings, they also imbue these rulers with the false persuasion that they cannot keep their own honour in their kingdoms if they admit the kingdom of Christ. Just as Herod once tried to extinguish the newborn child so that he might establish his own kingdom on earth, so today this error arms many princes against Christ, because they have persuaded themselves that their kingdoms cannot stand while he reigns. But why speak of princes, when the same madness drives private individuals too? Each of us ought to be a vine or a fruitful tree in the vineyard of Christ, and to present himself to him, through obedience of faith, as a living sacrifice. Yet how many there are who, like deserters or runaway slaves, give themselves wholly to the lusts of the flesh and do not want Christ to reign over them! Therefore they plot to shake off his yoke, and for this reason they persecute his ministers hour by hour.

units.la: Sunt autem horum omnium idem conatus, qui colonis ipsis tribuuntur, & ijdem ex illis sermones audiuntur, quos ipsi effutierunt. Nam seipsos mutuo hortationibus contra Christum excitant. Venite (inquiunt) & e medio illum tollamus, vt nostra sit hereditas, id est, vt nobis pro nostro libito viuere liceat, neque morosorum ipsorum legibus parere cogamur. Et mox illos capiunt, id est legibus & edictis coercent, & praedicandi libertatem nouis finibus circumscribunt. Deinde eijciunt ex vinea, id est, ne videantur cum Dei Filio pugnam suscepisse, illos excommunicationis fulmine feriunt, & clamant haereticos esse, & ab Ecclesia alienos, quibus non sit aliqua falsa, neque pars in Deo. Et post quam hoc omnibus persuasum esse, & proinde illos impune occidi posse arbitrantur, vim manifestam parant, & usa bellis quidem abstinent, quibus totas gentes & vrbes excindere conantur. At hic admirabile Dei consilium nos animo repetere oportet, qui ista omnia olim Filio suo dilecto accidere passus est. Etenim hic cum ad suos veniret, sui eum non receperunt, nec locum apud eos inuenit, quos eius peculium esse voluerat Pater. Hi de Samaritanum & daemoniacum dixerunt, damnatum denique Pilato tradiderunt, vt dira crucis supplicio afficeretur. In illo autem ostendere voluit Deus, quid futurum sit de omnibus, qui huic credunt & obediunt. Etenim ipse ait: Non est discipulus supra doctorem, neque serus supra dominum suum. Si ipsum patremfamilias Beelzebul vocarunt, quanto magis domesticos eius? Si me persecuti sunt, & vos persequentur: si sermonem meum seruauerunt & veritatem seruabunt. Haec dixi vobis, vt non offendamini: Mouebunt vos Synagogis: imo veniet tempus, cum quisquis trucidabit vos, putabit se cultum praestare Deo, &c. Quid ergo minamur, si hodie persecutionem patimur? Si excommunicati pro haereticis habemur, si exibilamur? Si vt mundi ἀπόδουλοι omnibus spectaculo fumus? Tales pro suis agnoscit Dei Filius & a mundo eiectos & exclusos ipse colligit, vt in caeci nati historia apud Ioannem cernitur. Nobis ergo applicemus quod idem dicit: Beati qui persecutionem sustinent propter iustitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum. Beati eritis cum conuiciati fuerint vobis & persecuti fuerint, & mentientes dixerint quiduis mali aduersus vos propter me. Gaudete & exultate, &c. Matth. 5.
units.tr: Now all these men have the same endeavour that is attributed to those tenants, and the same words are heard from them that the tenants themselves uttered. For they stir one another up with exhortations against Christ: "Come," they say, "let us remove him from the midst, so that the inheritance may be ours, that is, so that we may be allowed to live as we please and not be forced to obey the laws of those tiresome men." And soon they seize his ministers, that is, they restrain them with laws and edicts, and they hem in the freedom to preach within new limits. Then they cast them out of the vineyard, that is, so that they may not seem to have undertaken a struggle with the Son of God, they strike them with the thunderbolt of excommunication, and they cry out that they are heretics and aliens from the Church, who have no part or lot in God. And when they think this has been persuaded to everyone, and that these men can therefore be killed with impunity, they prepare open violence; and sometimes they refrain from war, by which they try to lay waste whole nations and cities. But here we ought to call to mind the wonderful counsel of God, who once allowed all these things to happen to his beloved Son. For when he came to his own, his own people did not receive him, and he found no place among those whom the Father had wished to be his peculiar possession. They said that he was a Samaritan and possessed by a demon, and at last they handed him over to Pilate to be subjected to the dreadful punishment of the cross. In him God wished to show what will happen to all who believe in him and obey him. For he himself says: "A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call those of his household? If they have persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they have kept my word, they will keep yours. I have told you these things so that you will not be offended. They will put you out of the synagogues; indeed, the time will come when whoever kills you will think he is offering service to God," etc. Why then should we be dismayed if today we suffer persecution? If we are counted as heretics because of excommunication, if we are hissed at, if we are made a spectacle to all as the refuse of the world [ἀπόδουλοι]? The Son of God acknowledges such people as his own, and he himself gathers those who have been cast out and shut out by the world, as is seen in the story of the man born blind in John. Let us therefore apply to ourselves what he also says: "Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are you when people revile you and persecute you and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account. Rejoice and be glad, etc." Matt. 5.

units.la: Ad confirmationem huius consolationis facit, quod de poena quam subituri sint coloni isti, sequitur. Hos autem ipsos de ea interrogat Dominus, vt quod nuper fecit, nunc rursus proprij oris testimonio aduersarios conuincat. Ea enim est veritatis vis, vt ne impiissimi quidem hanc negare possint: & qui Christum improbe tentare voluerunt, vt eum in dictis suis capiant, nunc ipsi ab eo capti seipsos suo gladio iugulant. Nam in interrogante Domino: Cum igitur venerit Dominus vineae, quid faciet agricolis illis? Respondent illi: Malos ipsos male perdet, & vineam suam elocabit aliis agricolis, qui reddent ei fructus temporibus suis. Cum venerit Dominus vineae (inquit) quid faciet per fidis illis & ingratis? Iniuit ergo hac quaestione, illum certo venturum esse. Nam etsi Dominus interdum videatur alio proferre dissimulare quae aguntur, non deest tamen causae suae, neque inultos sinit eos, qui dolo malo agunt in sua Ecclesia. Et hoc illi fatentur, nimirum malos dignos esse, vt male pereant. Agnoscunt ergo multiplex scelus, quo illi peccarint: ingratitudine nimirum in Deum, inhumanitate in conseruos, crudelitate & iniustitia in herilem filium. Quoad poenam vero non exitium modo illis decernunt, verumetiam quod vinea ab illis transferenda sit, & locanda aliis: quod non potuit abs ipsorum ignominia fieri. At quia de his mox ipse Dominus differet, prolixiori iustorum expositione nunc non est opus. Sufficiat autem annotasse quod obseruatum dignissimum est, vineam ipsam propter perfidos & iniquos colonos non vastari aut excindi, sed aliis locari, qui eam bene colant, & hero meliorem gratiam referant. Soletur hoc, si quando multorum ingratitudo Ecclesiae toti fraudi aut exitio fore putatur. Est enim revera apud Deum discrimen inter iustum & iniustum, & (vt Abraham olim dicebat) qui iudex est vniuersae terrae, aequitatem seruat, neque piumper dit cum impio, & quia Filio regnum aeternum promisit, non postulat.
units.tr: This strengthens the consolation that follows from the punishment those tenants are about to suffer. The Lord questions these same men about it, so that by their own mouths he may once again convict his adversaries, as he has just done. Such is the power of truth that not even the most impious can deny it. Those who wanted to test Christ wickedly, so as to catch him in his words, are now themselves caught by him and cut their own throats with their own sword. When the Lord asks, "When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those husbandmen?", they answer, "He will miserably destroy those wicked men and let out his vineyard to other husbandmen, who will render him the fruits in their seasons." He says, "When the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those faithless and ungrateful men?" By this question he admits that the lord will certainly come. For although the Lord sometimes seems to delay and to conceal what is being done, he is not wanting in his cause, and he does not let go unpunished those who act with malice in his Church. The tenants themselves confess this, namely that wicked men deserve to perish miserably. They therefore recognise the many-sided crime of which they are guilty: ingratitude towards God, inhumanity towards the fellow servants, and cruelty and injustice towards the heir, the master's son. As to the punishment, they decree not only destruction for them but also that the vineyard is to be taken from them and let out to others, which could not happen without their own disgrace. But since the Lord himself will shortly speak of these things, there is no need for a lengthier explanation of the righteous now. It is enough to note what is most worthy of observation: the vineyard is not laid waste or cut down because of the faithless and wicked tenants, but is let to others who will cultivate it well and render a better return to the lord. This should console us whenever the ingratitude of many is thought to bring ruin or destruction upon the whole Church. For there truly is a distinction before God between the righteous and the unrighteous, and (as Abraham once said) the judge of all the earth keeps justice, does not join the pious with the impious, and, because he has promised the eternal kingdom to the Son, does not ask for it.

units.la: Mal. 3. Gen. 18. Psal. 80. rest vineam, id est, Ecclesiam suam destruere, quæ regni eius sedes est. Interim meminerimus, hanc non alligatam esse loco & genti, sed sæpe alio transferri propter ingratitudinem & perfidiam eorum, qui professioni suæ non respondent, & reiectis fidei Dei ministris male fidos sibi ipsis acquisierunt. Agnoscamus ergo nos Dei Filium IESVM CHRISTVM , & ad nos venientem per Euangelij prædicationem toto corde excipiamus, nosq; totos ipsius seruitio consecremus, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Mal. 3. Gen. 18. Psal. 80. He does not wish to destroy the vineyard, that is, his Church, which is the seat of his kingdom. Meanwhile let us remember that this vineyard is not bound to one place or nation, but is often transferred elsewhere on account of the ingratitude and faithlessness of those who do not live up to their profession and, having rejected the ministers of God, have brought ruin upon themselves. Let us therefore acknowledge the Son of God JESUS CHRIST , and receive him with our whole heart as he comes to us through the preaching of the Gospel, and let us consecrate ourselves wholly to his service, to whom be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: Dicit eis IESVS, Nunquam legistis in Scripturis, Quem lapidem reprobaverunt ædificantes, is factus est in caput anguli: A Domino factum est istud, & est mirabile in oculis nostris? Propterea dico vobis, fore vt tollatur a vobis regnū Dei, & detur genti quæ ferat eius fructus. Porrò qui ceciderit super lapidem istum conquassabitur: super quem vero ceciderit, dissipabit eum. Et cùm audissent principes Sacerdotum ac Pharisæi parabolas eius, cognouerunt hæc de se dici: Et cùm studerent eum præhendere, timuerunt turbam, quoniam vt Prophetam eum habebat.
units.tr: Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes'? Therefore I tell you, the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people producing its fruits. The one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and it will crush anyone on whom it falls." When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he was speaking about them. And although they wanted to seize him, they feared the crowds, because the crowds regarded him as a prophet.

units.la: Quia Dei Filius IESVS CHRISTVS , vt peccatores salvos faceret, in mundum venit & homo factus est, non obiter modò docet quæ ad salutem hominum faciunt, verumetiam singula ijs applicat, quibus cum agit, vt ea ad se pertinere intelligant, & illis emendari possint. Exemplum huius diligentiæ parabola tractatio, quam hucusq; vidimus, exhibet. Finis & scopus est, remouere scandalum, quod imperitis & rudioribus obijciebatur ex Sacerdotum & antistitum contumacia, qua Christo reluctabantur. Docet ergo non nonum aut insolens cuiquam debere videri, si qui Dei vinea dicuntur, fructus nullos ferant professione sua dignos. De eo enim iam olim Dominum conquestum esse per Prophetas: præcipuos autem huius mali authores semper fuisse Sacerdotes, qui male fidi coloni fuerint. Et ne dignitatis suæ fiducia efferrentur, illam non perpetuam fore ostendit, sed præsoribus adesse diem illum, quo suæ perfidiæ & malitiæ pœnas graues daturi sint. At quia de his obscurius sub parabola disseruerat, nunc ipsis propius applicat doctrinam hanc, ne putent illum de rebus alienis & nihil ad ipsos pertinentibus dicere.
units.tr: Because the Son of God, Jesus Christ, came into the world and became man in order to save sinners, he does not merely teach in passing what pertains to the salvation of men, but he also applies each point to those with whom he is dealing, so that they may understand that it concerns them and may be corrected by it. The treatment of the parable that we have seen so far provides an example of this diligence. Its purpose and aim is to remove the stumbling block that was placed before the unlearned and simpler folk by the obstinacy of the priests and leaders, with which they resisted Christ. He teaches, then, that no one should think it strange or unusual if those who are called the vineyard of God bear no fruits worthy of their profession. The Lord had long ago complained of this through the Prophets, and the chief authors of this evil had always been the priests, who were faithless tenants. So that they would not be puffed up by confidence in their dignity, he shows that it will not last forever, but that the day is at hand on which they will pay heavy penalties for their faithlessness and wickedness. But since he had spoken of these things rather obscurely under the parable, he now applies this teaching more directly to them, so that they will not think he is speaking of matters foreign to them and having nothing to do with them.

units.la: Non autem temere id fecisse Dominum, ex Luca apparet, qui illum ex aduersarijs occasionem arripuisse docet, vt ita faceret. Nam cùm illum audiuissent dicere, Veniet dominus vineæ, et perdet agricolas istos, & dabit vineam alijs: mox respondens, Absit. Intellexerunt ergo de se agi, id vero fateri nolunt, sed non sine detestatione negant: Absit (inquiunt) vt nos facinus tam indignum & immane designemus, aut vnquam multandi simus dignitate ista, quam tot sæculis perpetua successione quasi iure hæreditario possedimus. Nec enim poterit peculium & hæreditatem suam relinquere Dominus. Ita vero solent hypocritæ in ipso scelere deprehendi. Quem enim verean tur, qui Deum ipsum fallere in animum induxerunt? Nec satis est illis simpliciter negare quod s e cerunt, sed impudenter responsare solent, quasi Deus sibi ab ipsis metum incuti patiatur. Fecit hoc olim Cain, qui de fratre Abelo, cuius sanguine adhuc madebat, a Deo interrogatus, nō veritus est dicere: Num quid custos fratris mei ego sum? Similis fuit Iudæ proditoris impudentia, qui cùm au diret scelus suum, de quo iam passus erat cum Sacerdotibus, Christum non latere, & de eius atro citate & pœna admoneretur, tamen quærere ausus fuit, num si proditorem illum esse diceret. Est hoc vitium nimis vulgare inter homines. Quia enim pleriq; sibi ipsis blandiuntur in sceleribus atro cissimis, non facile illa in seipsis agnoscunt, nisi acriori redargutione & correptione ita constringantur, vt negare amplius non possint. In primis autē hoc in ijs fit, quorum errorem & vitia aliqua religionis specie palliantur. Hi enim quia religionem ex superstitionū splendore æstimant, fere in scelere spij videri volunt, quæ causa est, quòd admonitionem omnem procul reijciunt, correptione autem grauiori exasperantur. At non idèo illis cedendū est, sed oculis ipsorum ingeratur lux illa Verbi Dei, quæ occulta tenebrarum arguit, vt velint nolint cogantur delicta sua agnoscere.
units.tr: That the Lord did not do this rashly is clear from Luke, who tells us that he took the occasion for this from his opponents. For when they heard him say, "The lord of the vineyard will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others," they immediately answered, "God forbid." So they understood that they were the ones meant, but they are unwilling to admit it, and they deny it with no lack of protest: "God forbid," they say, "that we should plan so unworthy and monstrous a crime, or that we should ever be deprived of that dignity which we have possessed for so many centuries by a continuous succession, as if by hereditary right. For the Lord cannot leave his property and inheritance behind." This is how hypocrites are usually caught in the very act of their crime. For whom do they fear, who have resolved to deceive God himself? Nor is it enough for them simply to deny what they have done; they are accustomed to answer impudently, as if God would allow them to be struck with fear of themselves. Cain did this long ago: when God asked him about his brother Abel, whose blood was still on the ground, he did not hesitate to say, "Am I my brother's keeper?" Judas the traitor showed a similar impudence: when he heard that Christ was not unaware of his crime, which he had already agreed upon with the priests, and when he was warned of Christ's cleverness and punishment, he still dared to ask whether he was the one who would betray him. This vice is far too common among men. For since most people flatter themselves in the blackest crimes, they do not easily recognize them in themselves, unless they are bound tight by sharper rebuke and correction so that they can no longer deny them. This happens above all among those whose error and vices are covered over with some appearance of religion. For since they judge religion by the splendor of superstitions, they almost wish to appear pure in crime, and this is why they reject every warning and are exasperated by a more serious correction. But one should not yield to them for this reason; rather, the light of the Word of God should be thrust into their eyes, which exposes the hidden things of darkness, so that, whether they will or not, they are compelled to acknowledge their sins.
