units.la: Facit hoc in præsenti Dominus IESVS CHRISTVS, qui istos ad speculum Scripturæ reuocat, vt huius testimonio conuincantur. Nam ait illis: Nunquà legistis in Scripturis: Quem lapidem reprobarunt ædificantes, is factus est in caput anguli? Quasi diceret: Si tam aliemi estis ab illo scelere, quid ergo Spiritui Sancto respondebitis, qui vos tales fore, & ista factuetos esse olim prædixit? Anno in Psalmis ille vaticinatur, architectos, id est, antistites religionis reprobaturos esse electum illum & pretiosum lapidem, quem Deus destinauit vt supremum in Ecclesia sua ædi-ficio locum teneat, adeoq; ceu angularis lapis ædificium totum absoluat atq; constringat ne dis-soluatur? Num vero Dauidem, qui ex Spiritus Sancti suggestione hoc annotauit, mendacij ar-guetis? Atqui a Domino istud factum & huius decretum est, vt ita fiat. Cur ergo mirabile aut in credibile in oculis nostris videatur? Num vero impossibile erit Deo in istam dignitatem eum euehere, quem vos vt architecti inepti & improuidi reiecitis? Comodi autem testimonium hoc Do-minus ex eo Psalmo adducit, ex quo lætas illas acclamationes desumpserant, qui ipsum non mul-tò ante in vrbem cum regio apparatu deduxerunt, vt exoptatum illum Dauidis Filium, id est, promissum Messiam esse testarentur. Quòd si veterem historiam inspicias, verisimile est Psalmum hunc a Dauide scriptum fuisse sub regni sui initium, quando & gentes vicinæ aduersus illum tu-multuabantur, & ex Saulinus coniuratus adhuc reliqui erant, qui ipsum priusquam in regno confir-maretur, oppressum cupiebant. Et quis dubitet, tunc ex multis qui proceres in regno esse videban-tur, multa audita fuisse, quibus Danidem prosciderint, vt toti populo contemptum & inuisum red-derent. Itaq; in regno confirmatus istum Psalmum composuit, quo Deum celebrat, qui ipsi affue-rat, vt per tot tamq; graues difficultates eluctari posset: simul vero hoc agit, vt qui tam diu ipsi re-siterant, sese Deo restitisse agnoscerent, & nunc populus totus Regem, quem a Deo tuestum esse cøstabat, libentius amplesteretur. Ac quia Dauid promissi Messiæ typus fuit, qui ex illo nasci debuit, stylum huius ita direxit Spiritus Sanctus, vt non modo de iis, quæ ipsi acciderunt, diceret, sed etiam de iis vaticinaretur, quæ posterioribus demum temporibus in Christo impleri debuerunt. Inter quæ præcipuum est, quòd Dauid diu reiectus & ignominiosè trastatus ad regni fastigium per-uenit. Eandē enim Filij Dei in carne nati fortem postea fuisse, vt a Sacerdotibus reprobatus, a præside Romano damnatus & in crucem suffixus, per mortem ignominiosam in gloriam & re-gnum cœleste ingressus sit, & in terris quoq; regnum ad omnes gentes propagarit, vnanimis vete-ris & noui testamenti consensus testatur. Quia vero locus hic, quacunq; in vera Christi cognitio-ne nos instituunt, perfectè comprehendit, præstat singula diligentius expendere. Primum, quid lapidi conferatur: Deinde quæ huius lapidis fors sit: Præterea quid eos maneat, qui adhuc illi ob-luctantur.
units.tr: The Lord Jesus Christ does this now, calling them back to the mirror of Scripture, so that they may be convicted by its testimony. For he says to them: "Have you never read in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone'?" As if he were saying: If you are so far removed from that crime, what then will you answer to the Holy Spirit, who long ago foretold that you would be such men and would do these things? Does not David in the Psalms prophesy that the builders, that is, the leaders of religion, would reject that chosen and precious stone, which God has appointed to hold the highest place in his Church's building, and which, like the corner stone, completes and binds the whole building so that it does not fall apart? Will you accuse David of lying, who wrote this under the prompting of the Holy Spirit? Yet this was done by the Lord, and it is his decree that it should be so. Why then should it seem marvelous or incredible in our eyes? Will it be impossible for God to raise to that dignity the one whom you, as foolish and careless builders, have rejected? The Lord adduces this testimony fittingly from that Psalm, from which those who a little before had led him into the city with royal splendor had taken their joyful acclamations, testifying that he was the long-desired Son of David, that is, the promised Messiah. If you look into the ancient history, it is likely that this Psalm was written by David at the beginning of his reign, when the neighboring nations were rising up against him, and when some who had conspired with Saul were still left, who wanted him destroyed before he was established in the kingdom. And who would doubt that at that time many things were heard from the many who seemed to be nobles in the kingdom, by which they slandered David so as to make him despised and hated by the whole people? Therefore, once established in the kingdom, he composed this Psalm, in which he celebrates God, who had stood by him so that he could struggle through so many and such grave difficulties; at the same time he aims to make those who had resisted him so long recognize that they had resisted God, and that now the whole people would more willingly embrace the King whom they saw had been protected by God. And since David was a type of the promised Messiah, who was to be born from him, the Holy Spirit so directed the style of this Psalm that it speaks not only of what happened to David himself but also prophesies of those things which were to be fulfilled in Christ in later times. Among these the chief is that David, long rejected and shamefully treated, came to the summit of the kingdom. For the consensus of the Old and New Testaments, which is unanimous, testifies that the same lot later befell the Son of God born in the flesh: he was rejected by the priests, condemned by the Roman governor, fixed to the cross, and through a shameful death entered into glory and heavenly kingdom, and also spread his kingdom on earth to all nations. But since this passage fully embraces whatever instructs us in the true knowledge of Christ, it is better to weigh each point more carefully. First, what is compared to the stone; second, what the fate of this stone is; and further, what awaits those who still struggle against it.

units.la: Quoad primum, frequens admodum est, IESVM CHRISTVM lapidem dici, aut per la-pidem aut petræ typum adumbrari. Huc pertinet quod ante Legem Iacob in Mesopotamiam su-giens, lapidem, quem capiti loco ceruicalis supposuerat, a somno excitatus erestum oleo perfudit, vt hunc Messiæ ex ipso nascituri typum faceret. Et hæc non obscure ipse Christus testatur, quan-do cum Nathanaele colloquens in se completum iri dicit, quod per scalam, quam tunc Iacob in somnis viderat, adumbratum fuit. Sub Mose autem Christi typum suisse petram illam, quæ Israe-litis potum præbuit in deserto, Paulus diserte docet. In primis huc pertinet quod per Isaiam dixit ꝓstea Deus: En ego fundo in Zion lapidem, lapidem probationis, angularem, pretiosum, cui qui credit, non pudefiet. Et apud eundem Prophetam idem Christus lapis offendi uli & petra ruinæ dicitur, ad quem locum postea beatus ille Simeon allusit, cùm de Christo infante vaticinaretur: Ecce positus est iste in casum & resurrectionem multorum in Israele. Rursum de Christo exponi debet quod apud Zachariam dicit Dominus: Ecce lapis, quem posui ante Iofuam, super lapidem vnum septem sunt oculi: en ego cælo quod in illo cælatum est, ait Dominus exercituum, & ause-ram iniquitatem terræ illius vno die. In Daniele item lapidi absq; manibus reuulso & cœlitus de-lapso confertur. Ratio huius comparationis aut typi proprie ea est, quòd vt lapides aut petræ sir-mæ solidæ & tantum non immobiles sunt, & ideo in fundamentis ædificiorum collocantur, quæ illis solent superstruì: ita Christus fundamentum est Ecclesiæ suæ firmù & immobile, aduersus quod (vt ipse ait) ne inferorum quidem portæ aliquid possunt. Et ita Apostoli mysterium istud inserium xerum. xerunt. Ex quorum numero Petrus locum Isaiae, quem paulò ante adduximus verbotim de Christo exponit, & huic consentiens Paulus insuper addit, aliud fundamentum poni non posse, quàm Christum, quem Deus æterno decreto ad hoc destinarit. In præsenti tamen altius assurgit Dominus, ut se ædificij Ecclesiæ complementum quoque esse doceat, ut suo loco dicetur.
units.tr: As to the first, it is very common for Jesus Christ to be called a stone, or to be foreshadowed by a stone or the type of a rock. To this belongs what happened before the Law: Jacob, fleeing into Mesopotamia, when he was awakened from sleep, anointed with oil the stone which he had placed under his head as a pillow, so as to make it a type of the Messiah who would be born from him. Christ himself clearly bears witness to this when, speaking with Nathanael, he says that what was foreshadowed by the ladder which Jacob then saw in his dreams would be fulfilled in him. Under Moses, Paul plainly teaches that the rock which gave the Israelites drink in the desert was a type of Christ. Above all, this belongs to what God later said through Isaiah: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, and whoever believes in it will not be put to shame." And in the same Prophet, Christ is called a stone of stumbling and a rock of ruin, an allusion to which the blessed Simeon later made when he prophesied about the infant Christ: "Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel." Again, what the Lord says in Zechariah must be explained of Christ: "Behold the stone that I have set before Joshua; on one stone are seven eyes; behold, I will engrave its inscription, says the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day." In Daniel, too, a stone cut out without hands and falling from heaven is compared to him. The reason for this comparison, or type, is properly this: just as stones or rocks are firm, solid, and almost immovable, and are therefore placed in the foundations of buildings that are to be built upon them, so Christ is the firm and immovable foundation of his Church, against which (as he himself says) not even the gates of hell can prevail. And so the Apostles have rightly understood this mystery. Peter, one of their number, expounds word for word the passage of Isaiah that we quoted a little before, concerning Christ; and Paul, agreeing with this, further adds that no other foundation can be laid than Christ, whom God has appointed for this by an eternal decree. Yet in the present passage the Lord rises higher, so as to teach that he is also the completion of the building of the Church, as will be said in its place.

units.la: Nunc videamus prius, quæ eius inter homines fors sit. Exprimit hanc ipse, cùm Dauidis verba adsè transfert: Quem lapidem reprobarunt ædificantes, &c. Reprobatur ergo & reiicitur ab ijs, qui Ecclesiæ architecti & antistites esse putantur. Sunt hi Sacerdotes & Præsules, quibus dicuntur, quòd ipsorum sit Ecclesiam colligere & ædificare, quæ domus Dei est, teste Apostolo. Ædificatur ista, quando homines Christo adducuntur, ut huic fidant, & hic in eis habitet & agat suo Spiritu. Hoc olim sedulò præstiterunt Prophetæ, qui omnes de Christo vaticinati sunt, & in ipso uno monstrarunt quæcunque ad salutem necessario requiruntur. Debebant idem facere Sacerdotes, cùm eis credita esset Legis doctrina, quæ pædagogi instar ad Christum deducit, & idem sacris præessent, in quibus idem adumbrabatur. Sed longè diversum faciebant, tunc temporis. Etenim suis intenti, hæreditatem Filij Dei sibi ipsis vendicare studebant, & ut quæstum vberiorem facerent, traditiones nouas inuehebant, & sarcinis non necessarijs grauabant populum, sicuti illis Dominus exprobrat. Et quia hunc studijs suis obstare sentiebant, toti in eo erant, ut ab omnibus reprobatus locum nullum haberet in Ecclesia. Et quia idem ipsorum antecessores fecerant, de eo nunc illos admonet, ut offendat, hoc non nouum esse aut insolens. Quàm primum enim antistites religionem sibi ipsis quæstum faciunt, & huius sæculi gloria gloriæ Dei anteponunt, nulli hominum Veritatis lucem & huius authorem, IESVM CHRISTVM, minus ferre possunt. Exempla sunt omnium sæculorum, quibus id probari potest. Et debet hoc diligenter obseruari propter eos, qui hodie, ut fucum faciant simplicioribus, Romanos Pontifices & Ecclesiam Romanam errare aut falli posse negant: & hoc fundamento iacto superstitiones & quæuis commenta absurda & inepta obtrudunt, quibus libertas Christiana circumscribitur, & conscientia piorum grauantur. Atqui ij, de quibus in præsenti agitur, sedebant in cathedra Moisis, & eorum successores erant, de quibus olim Propheta dixerat: Labia sacerdotis custodient scientiam, legemq; ex ore eius requirent: Legatus enim est Domini exercituum. Verumtamen in capite salutis errarunt, & ut architecti inepti & male fidi eum reprobarunt, qui Ecclesiæ Dei fundamentum & caput est, & extra quem (ut Apostoli testantur) non est aliud nomen sub cælo inter homines datum, in quo nos oporteat saluos fieri. Quid ergo de nostris sperés, quorum mores idem sunt, & qui non minus quàm Iudæorum Sacerdotes & Scribæ religionem sibi quæstum & templum emporium fecerunt? Enimuero quàm nobis cauendæ sint illorum artes & doli, Spiritus sanctus abundè docet. Christus exoriturros dicit pseudoprophetas & pseudochristos, & ne eos sequamur monet, qui ipsum nobis certo loco monstrant. Apostoli itèm vaticinantur, venturos impostores, qui dæmoniorum doctrinas introducant, dum coniugij vsum prohibent, ciborum deleCtum mandant, & quod olim Plinius de imperitis medicis dixit, animas simplicium negotiantur, & ex mortuis tributum petunt, qui illis quæstum vberrimum pariunt. Et cùm hæc publicè fiant, tamen isti Ecclesia suam errare posse negant, & omnia sua pro oraculis haberi volunt, tunc quoq; quando Christum aperte damnant, doctrinam de fide in Christum reprobant, & huic vni fidentes ferro & igne persequuntur.
units.tr: Now let us see first what he is among men. He expresses this himself when he quotes the words of David: "The stone which the builders rejected," and so on. He is therefore rejected and cast out by those who are thought to be the architects and leaders of the Church. These are the priests and prelates, to whom it is entrusted to gather and build the Church, which is the house of God, as the Apostle testifies. That house is built when men are brought to Christ, to trust in him, and he dwells in them and works by his Spirit. The Prophets faithfully did this in former times. All of them prophesied about Christ, and in him alone they showed whatever is necessarily required for salvation. The priests ought to have done the same, since the teaching of the Law had been entrusted to them. The Law leads to Christ like a tutor, and the priests presided over the sacred rites in which the same thing was foreshadowed. But at that time they did something very different. Intent on their own affairs, they sought to claim for themselves the inheritance of the Son of God. To make greater profit, they introduced new traditions and burdened the people with unnecessary burdens, as the Lord rebukes them for doing. And because they saw that he stood in the way of their pursuits, they were wholly intent on ensuring that he, rejected by all, would have no place in the Church. Since their own predecessors had done the same, he now warns them, so that they may take offence, that this is nothing new or unusual. For as soon as leaders make religion a source of gain for themselves and put the glory of this world before the glory of God, they cannot bear the light of truth, nor its author, Jesus Christ, among men. There are examples from every age by which this can be proved. This should be carefully observed because of those who today, to deceive the simpler folk, deny that the Roman Pontiffs and the Roman Church can err or be deceived. Having laid this foundation, they foist upon us superstitions and all sorts of absurd and foolish inventions, by which Christian liberty is restricted and the consciences of the pious are burdened. Yet those of whom we are now speaking sat in the chair of Moses, and they were the successors of those of whom the Prophet long before had said: "The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts." Nevertheless, they erred regarding the very head of salvation, and like unskilled and faithless architects they rejected him who is the foundation and head of God's Church, and apart from whom (as the Apostles testify) there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved. What then can we hope of our own people, whose manners are the same, and who have made religion a source of gain and the temple a marketplace no less than the priests and scribes of the Jews did? Indeed, the Holy Spirit teaches abundantly how carefully we must beware of their arts and tricks. Christ says that false prophets and false Christs will arise, and he warns us not to follow those who point him out to us in some particular place. The Apostles likewise foretell that impostors will come, who will introduce doctrines of demons, forbidding marriage and commanding abstinence from certain foods. And, as Pliny once said of unskilled physicians, they trade in the souls of simple people and demand tribute from the dead, which brings them the richest gain. Although these things are done openly, they deny that their Church can err, and they want all their own pronouncements to be regarded as oracles, even at the very time when they openly condemn Christ, reject the doctrine of faith in Christ, and persecute with sword and fire those who trust in him alone.

units.la: Cæterum neminem ista offendant. Nam etsi ædificantes lapidem hunc pretiosum reiiciant, nihil tamen de eius pretio decederet, imò hac via ille ad suam dignitatem euehetur, ut sit caput angulì. Qua locutione duplex dignitas commendatur. Etenim caput dicitur, quia Rex & Sacerdos est: Rex, quem Deus constituit in monte suo sanctô Sion: Sacerdos autem secundum ordinem Melchisedech in æternum, de quo hoc quoq; olim Dauid vaticinatus est: De torrente in via bibet, & idèo attollet caput. Angulì verò caput dicitur, quòd ut angularis lapis duos muros contrarios aut concurrentes connectit: ita in Christo conuenerunt in vnam Ecclesiam duo diuersi & contrarij populi, Iudæi & gentes, qui prius sententijs, fide, placitis & studijs inter se pugnabant. Augebat ini micitiam inter hos Lex mandatorum quæ (ut Paulus scribit) in ritibus posita magis dissociabat.
units.tr: But let none be offended by these things. For although the builders reject this precious stone, nothing of its worth is lessened. Indeed, by this very means it is raised to its dignity, so that it becomes the head of the corner. By this expression a twofold dignity is commended. He is called the head because he is both King and Priest: King, whom God has set on his holy mountain Zion; and Priest after the order of Melchizedek forever, of whom David also prophesied long ago: "He shall drink of the brook in the way, and therefore shall he lift up the head." He is called the head of the corner because, like a corner stone, he joins two opposing or converging walls. So in Christ two different and opposed peoples, Jews and Gentiles, who had previously fought one another in opinions, faith, beliefs and pursuits, came together into one Church. The law of commandments, which (as Paul writes) consisted in rites and kept them further apart, had increased the enmity between them.

units.la: CAP. XXI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXI.

units.la: Sed huius ceu intergerini parietis septum ille per sanguinem suum dissoluit, & ex vtrisq; populū vnum fecit, vtrofq; cum Deo reconcilians, & pacem illis quoq; prædicans, qui prius longinqui aberant a pactis promissionum, adeoq; vnum corpus Ecclesiæ constituit, cuius ipse caput est vnicum. Hic honor in morte sua sese exerere capit, & ipsi saluus & integer manebit in æternum. In terris vero regnum quoq; habebit, quod nulla vis hostilis euertet. Prædicabitur enim Euangelium in toto orbe, & ipse suis indiuulsus aderit vsq; ad consummationem sæculi.
units.tr: But he, by his own blood, dissolved that partition wall, as it were, and made one people out of both, reconciling both to God and preaching peace to those who had formerly been far off from the covenants of promise. So he established one body of the Church, of which he alone is the head. This honour begins to show itself in his death, and he himself will remain safe and whole forever. On earth, too, he will have a kingdom, which no hostile force will overthrow. For the Gospel will be preached throughout the whole world, and he himself will be present with his own, undivided, until the end of the age.

units.la: Porro vt consolationem hanc magis confirmet, repetit & aduersariis applicat quod nuper de pœna colonorum improborum ex illorum ore elicuit. Nam sic dicit: Propterea dico vobis, fore vt tollatur a vobis regnum Dei, & detur genti quæ ferat eius fructus, Regno Dei vniuersum hu-mana redemptionis & salutis negotium significari sæpe diximus, cuius ergo ille in mundū venit, et cuius finis est, vt destructo diaboli regno, in libertatem filiorū Dei afferamur, & huius regnum in nobis instauretur. Minatur ergo fore vt Ecclesiæ titulum ab ipsis auferat Deus vna cum promissionibus æternæ salutis, & has ad gentes transferat, de quarum vocatione veteres Prophetæ multa vaticinati fuerunt. Vt vero hoc impletum sit, Actorum liber docet. Enimuero Euangelij prædicationem Hierosolymis inter Iudæos exorsi sunt Apostoli, & ex his reliquias collegerunt, quæ Ecclesiæ seminarium essent. Cum autem plerique in sua contumacia pergerent, & Apostolos hostiliter persequerentur, hi excusso (vt iusti erant) pedum puluere illis in testimonium, ad gentes conuersi sunt, ex quibus innumerabiles crediderunt, & sic vinea illa Domini, quæ prius angustiis Iudææ finibus continebatur, per omnes gentes propagata est. Vt ergo fiduciam eripit Iudæis, quæ sese efferebant: ita simul consolatur electos, ne de Ecclesia & regno Dei ipsum abiciant. Nam etsi ab huius societate excidant, qui eius titulo gloriabantur, potest tamen alios in horum locum excitare Deus, & quod Ioannes Baptista dicebat, ex lapidibus potest germanos filios Abrahami creare, per quos glorificetur. Matth.3.
units.tr: Moreover, to confirm this consolation the more, he repeats and applies to his opponents what he lately drew from their own mouths about the punishment of the wicked tenants. For he says: "Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation that will bring forth its fruits." We have often said that the kingdom of God signifies the whole business of human redemption and salvation. For this reason Christ came into the world, and the end of his coming is that, with the kingdom of the devil destroyed, we may be brought into the liberty of the sons of God, and his kingdom may be restored in us. He therefore threatens that God will take the title of the Church from them, together with the promises of eternal salvation, and transfer these to the Gentiles, concerning whose calling the ancient prophets prophesied much. That this was fulfilled, the Book of Acts teaches. For the apostles began the preaching of the Gospel among the Jews at Jerusalem, and from them gathered remnants, which were to be the seed of the Church. But when most of them persisted in their stubbornness and persecuted the apostles with hostility, the apostles, shaking off the dust of their feet as a testimony against them (as righteous men), turned to the Gentiles, among whom countless people believed. And so that vineyard of the Lord, which was formerly confined within the narrow limits of Judea, has been spread through all the nations. Thus he takes away the confidence of the Jews, who were puffing themselves up, and at the same time comforts the elect, so that they do not cast themselves away from the Church and the kingdom of God. For even if those who gloried in its title fall from its fellowship, God can still raise up others in their place. And what John the Baptist said, that God can from stones create true sons of Abraham through whom he is glorified, is still true. Matth. 3.

units.la: Quod autem de Iudæorum pœna dixit, in genere ad omnes accommodat, qui ipsi reluctantur. Qui ceciderit (inquit) super lapidem illum, conquassabitur: super quem vero hic ceciderit, dissipabit eum. Facit duo aduersariorum genera. Primum eorum, qui ad ipsum offendunt. Hi sunt, qui in salutis causa carnis rationem audiunt. Non potest hæc percipere quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, & offendit eos contempta & vilis Christi species, Euangelij prædicatio, quæ mundo stultitia videtur, persecutio item perpetua fidei comes. Fit his idem quod ijs, qui capite aut pede ad petra offendunt, quam quidem loco mouere non possunt, ipsi vero graviter læduntur: Ita isti Christo quidem nihil detrahunt, ipsi autem fidei iacturam faciunt, & proprias conscientias vulnerant. Alterum genus eorum est, super quos lapis ipse cadit, id est, qui eum hostiliter in se prouocant, vt qui lapide in alto positum in se detrahunt, cuius ruina & pondere conteruntur. Discrimen inter hæc duo genera in hoc vno est, quod de prioribus adhuc spes aliqua est. Nam vbi in illius cognitione instituuntur, per fidei obedientiam se illi subijciunt, & salutis in illo confortes fiunt. Alteri vero illi contumacia sua incurabili exitium sibi ipsis accersunt, dum in peccatis suis moriuntur, vt Iudæis ille alibi minatur. Docetur hoc apud Danielem typo lapidis, qui (vt ante diximus) abscq; manibus reuulsus statuam illam comminuit, quæ mundi Monarchias adumbrabat. Et sane constat omnibus illis exitio fuisse, quod tandem Ecclesiæ persecutionem & bellum mouerunt. Et apud Zachariam illa propter Christum lapidi oneris confertur, quem nemo impune aut illæsus loco moueat. Erit hoc perpetuum, & sunt nostri sæculi exempla, quæ ipsis possunt fidem facere.
units.tr: What he said about the punishment of the Jews he applies in general to all who resist him. "Whoever falls on that stone," he says, "will be broken; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him." He makes two kinds of opponents. The first are those who stumble at him. These are the ones who, in the matter of salvation, listen to the reasoning of the flesh. "The natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God," and the despised and lowly appearance of Christ offends them, as does the preaching of the Gospel, which seems foolishness to the world, and likewise the constant persecution that accompanies faith. For them, what happens is what happens to those who strike their head or foot against a rock: they cannot move the rock, and they themselves are badly hurt. So these people take nothing away from Christ, but they suffer loss of faith and wound their own consciences. The second kind is those on whom the stone itself falls, that is, those who provoke it against themselves hostilely, like people who pull down from on high a stone that has been set there, and are crushed by its fall and weight. The difference between these two kinds lies in this one thing: for the former there is still some hope. For when they are instructed in the knowledge of him, they submit themselves to him through obedient faith and become partakers of salvation in him. But for the latter, their incurable obstinacy brings destruction upon themselves, while they die in their sins, as he threatens elsewhere to the Jews. This is taught in Daniel by the type of the stone which, as we said before, was cut out without hands and shattered that statue, which foreshadowed the monarchies of the world. And it is certain that all those who finally stirred up persecution and war against the Church have come to ruin. And in Zechariah that stone is set as a burden on account of Christ, which no one can move without harm or without being hurt. This will be perpetual, and there are examples in our own age which can give them proof of it.

units.la: Sed Sacerdotum principes & Pharisæos videamus, qui auditis hís parabolis, ista de se dici intellexerunt. Tanta est veritatis vis, vt impiorum quoq; corda penetret. Non autem huic cedunt, sed illum captiuum facere conantur, vt vi aperta perdant, quem argumentis & rationibus confutari non posse vident. Ita semper in peius proficiunt impij, vt sæpe diximus: et idcirco opera nostra danda est, ne impijs desiderijs & odio veritatis indulgeamus. Nam qui hoc faciunt, inflar effrenis equi in proprium exitium ruunt. Sed consolationis plenum est, quod turbam timuerunt, nec ausi sunt facere quod maxime cupiebant. Ex eo apparet, impios non semper posse quod volunt, imo ne audere quidem quod videntur posse: cuius rei exempla alibi multa adduximus: Solet autem Deus antistites & principes viros hoc præpositos metu coercere, qui ipsum timere nolunt. Sic carnificum gladio pereunt degeneres & contumaces filij, qui parentum disciplinam reijciunt. Et frequenter fit, vt reprobi furias sibi accersant, quae ipsis omnia infesta faciunt. Nobis ergo iflorum, quae hucusque dicta sunt, vsus sit, vt memores dignitatis nostrae, in quam nos Deus euexit, qui vineam & haereditatem Filij sui IESV CHRISTI nos fecit, ab hoc nos excoli patiamur, & qui ab illo coloni constituti sunt, opus eius constanter vrgeant, vt Dei gloria in ipsis illustretur, & ipsi salui fiant in eo, extra quem salus nulla inuenitur. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum, Amen.
units.tr: But let us look at the chief priests and Pharisees, who, when they heard these parables, understood that these things were said about them. Such is the power of truth that it penetrates even the hearts of the impious. Yet they do not yield to it, but try to take him captive, so that they may destroy by open force the one whom they see they cannot refute by arguments and reasons. Thus the impious always make progress for the worse, as we have often said. Therefore our care must be taken that we do not indulge our impious desires and hatred of the truth. For those who do this rush headlong to their own destruction, like an unbridled horse. But it is a matter full of consolation that they feared the crowd and did not dare to do what they most wanted. From this it appears that the impious cannot always do what they want, indeed not even dare what they seem able to do. We have brought forward many examples of this elsewhere. God is accustomed to restrain by fear the bishops and princes set over these people, who are unwilling to fear him. So degenerate and stubborn sons perish by the executioner's sword, who reject the discipline of their parents. And it often happens that the reprobate bring furies upon themselves, which make everything hostile to them. Let us therefore use what has been said so far, mindful of the dignity to which God has raised us, who has made us the vineyard and inheritance of his Son Jesus Christ. Let us not allow ourselves to be cultivated by him, and let those who have been appointed by him as tenants steadily press forward his work, so that the glory of God may be displayed in them, and they themselves may be saved in him, outside of whom no salvation is found. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power forever. Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXII.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCLIII.

units.la: VNC respondens IESVS rursum locutus est eis per parabolas dicens: Simile est regnum coelorum cuidam Regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo: Et misit seruos suos, qui vocarent vocatos ad nuptias: sed noluerunt venire. Rursus misit alios seruos, dicens: Dicite vocatis, Ecce prandium meum paraui, tauri mei & altilia mea mactata sunt, & omnia parata: venite ad nuptias. Illi autem cum hoc neglexissent, abierunt: alius quidem in agrum suum, alius vero ad mercaturam suam. Reliqui vero praehensos seruos eius contumelijs affecerunt, & trucidarunt.
units.tr: Then Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who made a wedding feast for his son. He sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell those who have been invited, "Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and fattened fowl are slaughtered, and everything is ready: come to the wedding." But they neglected this and went away, one to his field, another to his business. The rest seized his servants, treated them with insults, and killed them.

units.la: Omnimus nosler IESVS CHRISTVS nuper in parabola de vinea & perfidis colonis Sacerdotum & Scribarum impietatem perstrinxit, vt scandalo mederetur, quod multi ex eo patiebantur, quod illum ab ijs reijci viderent, qui Ecclesiae antistites & architecti volebant haberi. Caeterum quia inter alia minatus erat, fore vt regnum Dei a Iudaeis transferretur ad aliam gentem, poterat quis ex eo obijcere: Ergone rudi & simplici populo extra omnem culpam agenti antistitum improbitas fraudi erit? Itaque nunc aliam parabolam de nuptijs subtexuit, qua eiusdem ingratitudinis & contumaciae vniuersam Iudaeorum gentem conuincit, ex quibus plerique salutem, quam ipsis in Christo Deus benigne offerebat, insolenter aspernabantur. Estque huius parabolae doctrina copiosa & multiplex, deque multis admonet, quorum cognitio nobis ad salutem perquam necessaria est. Partes eius sunt tres. Prima commendatur Dei bonitas & gratia, qua hic regnum suum Iudaeorum populo quantumuis indignissimo propositum, & salutis participes voluit fieri eos, qui sempiterno exitio digni erant. Deinde quam indigne illi hanc gratiam reiecerint, indicatur: Quo loco apparebit, quae causae fere homines remorentur, ne salui fiant. Praeterea docetur, regno Dei nihil derogari propter Iudaeorum contumaciam, sed quod ea occasione maiori cum foenore ad gentes sit transferendum, sic vt (quod Paulus postea scripsit) illorum ruina, facta sit mundi opulentia. Rom. 11.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ recently, in the parable of the vineyard and the wicked tenants, censured the impiety of the priests and scribes, in order to remedy the scandal which many suffered from seeing him rejected by those who wished to be regarded as the leaders and architects of the Church. But since he had threatened, among other things, that the kingdom of God would be transferred from the Jews to another nation, someone could object on this basis: So will the wickedness of the leaders be a loss to the simple and unassuming people, who are free of all fault? Therefore he now added another parable, about a wedding, by which he convicts the entire Jewish nation of the same ingratitude and obstinacy, many of whom insolently scorned the salvation which God graciously offered them in Christ. The teaching of this parable is rich and manifold, and it admonishes about many things, the knowledge of which is most necessary for our salvation. It has three parts. First, the goodness and grace of God is commended, by which he wished to set his kingdom before the Jewish people, however unworthy, and to make partakers of salvation those who deserved eternal destruction. Second, it is shown how unworthily they rejected this grace; in this place it will appear what causes commonly delay people from being saved. Moreover, it is taught that nothing is taken from the kingdom of God because of the obstinacy of the Jews, but that on that occasion it is to be transferred to the Gentiles with greater increase, so that (as Paul later wrote) their fall became the riches of the world. Rom. 11.

units.la: Pars prima sic narratur: Simile est regnum coelorum homini Regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo: Et misit seruos suos, qui vocarunt inuitatos ad nuptias. Regno coelorum denotatur vniuersum nostrae redemptionis negotium, cuius hic finis & summa est, vt ex diaboli regno & tyrannide erepti vitam in terris caelestem viuamus, tandem vero in coelis aeternum regnemus cum Christo nostro Seruatore: Conferatur autem id conuiuio nuptiali, eo quod salus nostra omnis in eo constitit, vt Filio Dei copulemur, qui vnicus & verus animarum sponsus est, & talis pasim in vtriusque testamenti libris describitur. Estque hoc infallibile bonitatis Dei argumentum, quod Filio suo, qui Rex gloriae, & cui omnis potestas data est in coelo & in terra, ex misero mortalium genere sponsam deligere voluit, quam illi vinculo indissolubili coniungeret & honorum regni sui aeterni ac coelestis consortem redderet. Est hoc maximum mysterium (vt Paulus vocat) quod nos & officij admonet, & plurimum consolatur. Quia enim in hunc dignitatis gradu nos euexit, decet vtique, vt
units.tr: The first part is narrated thus: The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who made a wedding for his son, and sent his servants, who called those who had been invited to the wedding. By the kingdom of heaven is signified the whole business of our redemption, whose purpose and sum is that, snatched from the kingdom and tyranny of the devil, we may live a heavenly life on earth and at last reign eternally in heaven with Christ our Saviour. This is compared to a wedding feast, because our whole salvation consists in this, that we be joined to the Son of God, who is the only and true bridegroom of souls, and he is so described throughout the books of both Testaments. And this is an infallible argument of God's goodness: he willed to choose for his Son, who is King of glory and to whom all power is given in heaven and on earth, a bride from the wretched race of mortals, whom he would join to him by an indissoluble bond and make a partner of the honours of his eternal and heavenly kingdom. This is the great mystery (as Paul calls it), which both reminds us of our duty and greatly comforts us. For since he has raised us to this degree of dignity, it is surely fitting that

units.la: Regnum coelorum est nostrae redemptio. eum omnis studio tueamur: neque verendum est, ne nobis aliquid deficri patiatur. Cur enim hoc faceret Dei Filius, qui, ut dignitatis huius capaces faceret, sanguinis sui pretio nos abluere & Spiritus sancti donis ornare & instruere dignatus est? Meminisse autem oportet, coniunctionem iam nostram cum Filio Dei in huius vitae curriculo inchoari, & nos ex Euangelio gustum aliquem gratiae caelestis percipere, beatitatem vero nostram in caelis demum perfici, quando sponsus ille noster nos ad se recipiet, ut bonis illis inenarrabilibus fruamur, quae ille nobis sua morte meriito acquisivit. Interea nobis patientia opus erit sub cruce, ad quam nos ille vocat, ne nostram formam temporis optemus meliorem esse, quam ipsius fuerit, neque ante tempus velimus triumphare, sed patienter feramus commune illud totius creaturae desiderium, quae quasi exerto capite revelationem filiorum Dei expectat. Quod ad vero primam parabolae huius partem, ut Dei bonitas clarius eluceat, videamus nunc qui primi ad nuptiale illud epulum vocati sint? quis item vocationis ipsius modus fuerit? ut Dei bonitas adhuc clarius eluceat.
units.tr: The kingdom of heaven is our redemption. we should guard it with all diligence, nor should we fear that he will allow anything to be lacking to us. For why would the Son of God do this, who, in order to make us capable of this dignity, deigned to wash us with the price of his blood and to adorn and equip us with the gifts of the Holy Spirit? But we must remember that our union with the Son of God begins in the course of this life, and that we receive from the Gospel some taste of heavenly grace, but our blessedness is at last perfected in heaven, when that bridegroom of ours receives us to himself, so that we may enjoy those ineffable goods which he acquired for us by his death as a merit. Meanwhile we will need patience under the cross, to which he calls us, lest we wish our condition to be better than his was, or want to triumph before the time; rather, we should patiently bear that common longing of the whole creation, which waits, as it were with head outstretched, for the revealing of the sons of God. As for the first part of this parable, so that God's goodness may shine forth more clearly, let us now see who were first called to that wedding feast, and what was the manner of the calling itself, so that God's goodness may shine even more clearly.

units.la: Ad primum pertinet quod dicitur, mittis fuisse seruos, qui vocatos debuerint accersere. Enim vero vocati innumeri fuerunt iam inde ab ipsa rerum origine. Quia enim Adamo parenti prima de Christo seruatore promissio facta est, in eodem simul omnibus hominibus salutis spes aperta est, ut illum omnes ad se pertinere dicerent. Et quamuis postea promissio illa ad Abrahamum, Isaacum & Iacobum refringeretur, attamen benedictio, quae ex semine ipsorum enasci debeat, ad omnes gentes extenditur. In Prophetis idem est videre, quae de gentium vocatione ad regnum Dei multa vaticinantur. In praesenti tamen Vocatorum aut Inuitatorum nomine potissimum Iudaei intelliguntur, cum quorum patribus foedus salutis, quod in Diluvio abrogatum videri potest, instauratum fuit, quorum item fuerunt adoptio, & gloria & Legis constitutio, & cultus, & promissiones, ex quibus deinde IESVS CHRISTVS, quoad carnem, nasci debuit. Ab his praedicationis Euangelicae, qua ad regni caelorum societatem homines vocantur, initium fieri debuit. Etenim Apostolus ille dicebat iam in caelum ascensurus: Vos eritis mihi testes Ierosolymae, & in tota Iudaea, Samaria, & usque ad ultimas terras. Sed & in Prophetis praedictum fuerat olim, Verbum Domini ex Ierusalem exiturum esse. Et huic mandato Domini Apostolos fideliter obsecutos fuisse, aliorum liber testatur, adeo ut non nisi inuiti ad gentes sese contulerint, nec sine publica proteatione: Vobis necesse fuit primum exponi sermonem Dei: postquam autem illum repellitis, & indignos vosipsos decernitis aeterna vita, ecce convertimur ad gentes. Debet autem diligenter observari haec Dei bonitas & indulgentia, qui post tot Prophetas (ut in vineae parabola audiinus) indignissime tractatos, & post Filium unigenitum crudeliter & iniuste occisum, adhuc tamen Iudaeos pro amicis habuit, & Euangelium illis primis praedicari voluit, quos ut hostes & per duelles reijcere & funditus extirpare poterat. Dicebat quidem illis Petrus: Deus patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Iesum, quem vos prodidistis & abnegastis in conspectu Pilati, &c.
units.tr: To the first point belongs what is said, that he sent servants to summon those who had been invited. Indeed, the invited were countless from the very beginning of things. For since the first promise about Christ the Saviour was made to our parent Adam, the hope of salvation was at the same time opened to all men, so that all could say that they belonged to him. And although that promise was afterwards restricted to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, nevertheless the blessing, which was to be born from their seed, extends to all nations. In the Prophets one sees the same thing, who foretell much about the calling of the Gentiles to the kingdom of God. In the present passage, however, under the name of the called or invited, chiefly the Jews are understood, with whose fathers the covenant of salvation, which might seem to have been abrogated in the Flood, was renewed; to them belonged likewise the adoption, the glory, the giving of the Law, the worship, and the promises, from whom Jesus Christ was to be born according to the flesh. The beginning of the evangelical preaching, by which men are called to fellowship in the kingdom of heaven, ought to be made from these. For that Apostle said, when about to ascend into heaven: You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth. Also it had been foretold of old in the Prophets that the word of the Lord would go out from Jerusalem. And that the Apostles faithfully obeyed this command of the Lord the book of Acts bears witness, so that they went to the Gentiles only unwillingly, and not without public protest: It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles. This goodness and indulgence of God ought to be carefully observed: after so many Prophets (as we heard in the parable of the vineyard) were most shamefully treated, and after the only-begotten Son was cruelly and unjustly killed, he still held the Jews as friends and wished the Gospel to be preached to them first, whom he could have rejected and utterly exterminated as enemies and traitors. Peter indeed said to them: The God of our fathers glorified his Son Jesus, whom you betrayed and denied in the presence of Pilate, etc.

units.la: Sed sermonem hunc durum mox mitigans, addit: At scio, fratres, vos per ignorantiam id fecisse, sicut & primores vestros, &c. Debet hinc consolatio peti, qua nos aduersus conscientiae tentationes confirmemus, si quando Satan de deliberatione remissione nos dubitare aut desperare iubet. Qui enim hostes ad nuptias Filii vocavit, num amicos negligat? Qui item inuitare voluit eos, qui adhuc Filii sanguine madebant, & quos sciebat non venturos esse, num nos aspernabitur aut excludet, qui epulum istud esurimus, & ad Sponsi nostri vocem exultamus?
units.tr: But soon softening this harsh speech, he adds: But I know, brothers, that you did it through ignorance, as also your rulers did, etc. From this a consolation should be drawn, by which we may strengthen ourselves against the temptations of conscience, if at any time Satan bids us doubt or despair of the forgiveness of our sins. For he who called enemies to the wedding of his Son, will he neglect friends? And he who wished to invite those who were still stained with the blood of his Son, and whom he knew would not come, will he spurn or exclude us, who hunger for this feast and exult at the voice of our Bridegroom?

units.la: Sed ut magis solida & efficacior sit consolatio ista, modum & rationem, quam in vocatione ista sequi voluit Dominus, oportet excutere. Etenim serui illi non semel duntaxat missi fuerunt, sed bis terque, idest, saepius venerunt, ut plane hic factum sit, quod olim per Isaiam se facturum praedixerat: Expandi manus meas tota die ad populum rebellem, qui incedit per viam non bonam. Deinde amica & nullis conditionibus gravis fuit inuitatio ista, quales saepe esse solent magnatum et virorum principum inuitationes, in quorum consperta sine munere pretioso comparere non satis tum est. At Apostoli simpliciter vocarunt omnes, nec aliud postularunt, quam ut accedant qui habent sese alienos a regno Dei praebuerunt. Quod ipsum olim Prophetae etiam fastidiverunt. Isaias certe clamabat: O vos omnes qui sitis, venite ad aquas: etiam vos quibus non est pecunia, venite comparate & comedite, emite (inquam) sine argento & sine pretio vinum & lac, &c. Et ipse
units.tr: But so that this consolation may be more solid and effective, we must examine the manner and method which the Lord wished to follow in this calling. For those servants were not sent only once, but twice and three times, that is, they came more often, so that here plainly came to pass what he had said he would do of old through Isaiah: I have stretched out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walks in a way that is not good. Then this invitation was friendly and not burdened with any conditions, unlike the invitations of great men and princes, which are often such that it is not enough to appear at their gatherings without a costly gift. But the Apostles simply called all, and asked nothing else than that those come who had made themselves strangers to the kingdom of God. This very thing the Prophets too once despised. Isaiah indeed cried out: O all you who thirst, come to the waters; you also who have no money, come, buy and eat; buy, I say, without silver and without price, wine and milk, etc. And he himself

units.la: {y} ipsi ipse Sponsus, cum tempus nuptiarum appropinquaret, desiderio epuli illius postremi se ardere te- stabatur, quod suam mortem proxime praecesset. Prius vero semel & iterum eos ut adse accede-rent, hortatus est, quos cunctari videbat. Eius enim voces fuerunt, Venite vos qui laboratis & onerati estis, & ego refocillabo vos. Item, Si quis sitit, veniat ad me & bibat. Quanta autem Apostolorum diligentia, quam ardens studium fuerit in vocandis Iudaeis, quos obstinatiores esse videbant, in Paulo est videre, qui optabat anathema a Christo separatus esse, pro illis, ut ipsi fierent, & idem dies ac noctes pro illis precabatur. Nec etiam dura aut difficilis ad IESVM CHRISTVM via est. Venitur enim ad eum per fidem, quae difficultates omnes facile superat: Eadem illum nobis coniungit, ut nos alat & recreet. Et cum extra Christum mundus hic totus laborum & molestiarum plenus sit, qui hoc iter ingrediuntur, hi a labore ad otium, a molestia ad gaudium veniunt quod incomparabile sentiunt, dum in hoc carnis mortalis carcere constituti, vitae caelestis & aeternae gustu fruuntur.
units.tr: The Bridegroom himself, when the time of the wedding drew near, declared that he burned with desire for that last feast which was to precede his death. Yet first, once and again, he urged those whom he saw hesitating to come forward. For his words were: "Come to me, you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you." Likewise: "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink." How great the diligence of the Apostles was, and how ardent their zeal in calling the Jews, whom they saw to be more obstinate, can be seen in Paul, who wished himself to be cut off from Christ as an anathema for their sake, that they might become his own, and who prayed for them day and night. Nor is the way to Jesus Christ hard or difficult. For we come to him through faith, which easily overcomes all difficulties. This same faith joins him to us, so that he may nourish and refresh us. And although apart from Christ this whole world is full of labours and troubles, those who enter this way pass from labour to rest and from trouble to joy, a joy beyond comparison, while, placed in this prison of mortal flesh, they enjoy a taste of the heavenly and eternal life.

units.la: Et hucfacit potissimum ratio sive causa, quam seruos suos allegare iubet Rex ille Deus, ut invitatos ad nuptias excitet. Dicite vocatis, inquit: Ecce prandium meum paravi: tauri mei & altilia mea macta sunt, & omnia parata: venite ad nuptias. Ista autem de Christo dicuntur, qui ab aeterno priusquam mundus hic crearetur ad hoc praedestinatus est, ut humani generis redemptor esset, & solus ad omnia sufficit, quae ad salutem nostram necessario requiruntur. Ipse enim est nobis factus a Deo sapientia, iustitia, & sanctificatio et redemptio. Ipse est agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi, & pascha nostrum, quod pro nobis immolatum ex Angeli exterminatoris manibus nos eripit. Ipse vitulus illesaginatus est, cuius mactatione tota domus caelestis exhilaratur, & filii perditi cum patre in gratiam redeunt. Idem vinum illud nouum est, quod vtribus nouis receptum homines exhilarat & Deum. Fons est aquae viuentis, ex quo quisquis bibit, non sitierit in aeternum. Panis item ille vivus est, qui caelo delapsus alit ad vitam aeternam omnes, qui ipsum cum fide manducant. Adhaec ipse mest via est, per quam ad nuptias illas venitur: lux est, quae tenebras et caliginem omnem diffutit: veritas deniq; est, quae nos errare non sinit. Et ne quid omittamus, ipse vestis est, qua induti in Dei conspectu consistere possumus. Quoties ergo Euangelium nobis praedicatur, semper in auribus nostris hanc vocem resonare putemus: Altilia mea macta sunt, & omnia abunde instructa sunt: Nec audiamus eos, qui alia salutis adminicula comminiscuntur, aut extra Christum nova fercula monstrant, quibus conscientiae famelicae saturentur. Sunt hi cupediarij & cocii inepti, vel potius venefici, sunt, de quibus apud Isa. sermo est, quod vendant non panem, & ea obtrudant quae non possunt facere. Et plus quam miseri & infelices sunt, qui relicto Christo sartores illos sequuntur, qui aconita miscent & lethalia toxica incautis propinant. Nos vno Christo contenti simus, extra quem nihil est, quod animum astuantem placare possit.
units.tr: The reason which that King God bids his servants declare, so as to rouse those invited to the wedding, bears especially on this point. "Tell those who are called," he says: "Behold, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and my fatted calves are slain, and all things are ready: come to the wedding." These things are said of Christ, who from eternity, before this world was created, was predestined to be the redeemer of the human race, and alone suffices for all the things that are necessarily required for our salvation. For he has been made for us by God wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption. He is that Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, and our Passover, who, sacrificed for us, snatches us from the hands of the destroying angel. He is the fattened calf whose slaughter gladdens the whole heavenly house, and the lost sons return into favour with the father. He is also that new wine, which, received into new wineskins, gladdens men and God. He is the fountain of living water, from which whoever drinks shall never thirst again. Likewise he is that living bread which, come down from heaven, nourishes unto eternal life all who eat him in faith. Moreover, he is the way by which one comes to that wedding; he is the light which dispels all darkness and gloom; he is, finally, the truth, which does not allow us to err. And, lest we omit anything, he is the garment by which, clothed, we can stand in the sight of God. Whenever the Gospel is preached to us, let us think that this voice always resounds in our ears: "My fatted animals are slain, and all things are abundantly prepared." Nor let us listen to those who devise other aids to salvation, or who display new dishes apart from Christ, with which hungry consciences may be satisfied. These are delicate-cooks and foolish cooks, or rather poisoners; they are those of whom Isaiah speaks, who sell not bread, and offer things which cannot make anyone well. And they are more than wretched and unhappy who, having left Christ, follow those tailors who mix aconite and deadly poisons and give them to the unwary to drink. Let us be content with Christ alone, apart from whom there is nothing that can calm a restless soul.

units.la: Sequitur secunda parabolae pars, qua narratur, quid Iudaei fecerint, quando Apostoli eos ad Christum vocarunt. Hoc ipsum nimirum, quod Ioannes testatur, dicens: In sua venit, & sui eum non receperunt. Nam primum vno quasi verbo ait: Noluerunt venire, quasi diceret: Etsi serui suos misisset Rex, & omnia lauti parata esse nuntiaret, non tamen ad illius mensam voluerunt accedere. Arguit hoc animos prophanos, quos nulla caelestium & sacrorum cura solicitos habet: quales hodie plurimi inueniuntur, qui instar Aesopici galli granum hordei margaritis pretiosissimis praeferunt. Quis enim alios dicat eos, qui coetibus sacris & concionibus doctrinae & consolationis plenis mensuram vini aut offam laute parata anteponere solent? Caeterum quod vno verbo dixerat, in plures quasi species diducit, & triafacit eorum genera, qui ad nuptias Filii Dei venire detrectarunt. Primos abiisse dicit in agrum suum, & (ut apud Lucam est videre) ij abunde se excusatos putant. Intelliguntur autem hi, quos rei domesticae cura remoratur. Et enim agricultura non modo licita, sed honesta & necessaria est. Hanc primo parenti iniunxit Deus, cum ei diceret: In sudore vultus tui comedes panem tuum. Sic opificia quoq; manuaria licita & honorifica sunt, & Psalmes beatum dicit eum, qui manuum labore parta edit, quem Apostolus quoq; hominibus Christianis commendans scribit: Qui furabatur, non amplius furetur, sed potius laboret operando manibus quod bonum sit, ut possit alijs quoq; impertiri, quibus opus fuerit. Et idem ethnico deterior- rem dicit eum, qui domesticis suis non prospicit. Peccatur autem in hac re nimia & anxia solicitudine, quam alibi Dominus prohibet: & quae cum fide pugnat, ut nos Deo non curae fore putemus, qui aues caeli alit, & flores in agris nascentes folijs & coloribus suis vestit & ornat. Qui huic soli citudini locum dant, hi sacros coetus negligunt, & extinctâ paulatim omni aeternae salutis cura, omne tempus sibi perijsse putant, quo no quaestum aliquem faciunt. Qui item ita affecti sunt, ijs num quam persuaseris, ut ex ijs locis discedant, in quibus superstitio & idololatria regnant, & vbi multa coguntur contra conscientiam facere.
units.tr: Next follows the second part of the parable, which tells what the Jews did when the Apostles called them to Christ. This is precisely what John attests, saying: "He came to his own, and his own did not receive him." For first he says, in one word, "they would not come," as if he were saying: although the King had sent his servants and announced that everything was splendidly prepared, they nevertheless were unwilling to approach his table. This points to profane minds, which are troubled by no care for heavenly and sacred things: such as are found today in great numbers, who, like Aesop's cock, prefer a grain of barley to the most precious pearls. For who would not call those men who are accustomed to prefer a measure of wine or a morsel of finely prepared food to sacred assemblies and sermons full of teaching and comfort? But what he said in one word, he spreads out, as it were, into several kinds, and makes three classes of those who refused to come to the wedding of the Son of God. He says the first went away to their farm, and (as may be seen in Luke) they thought themselves amply excused. Those are meant who are held back by the care of domestic affairs. For farming is not only lawful but honourable and necessary. God enjoined this upon our first parent, when he said: "In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread." So too manual crafts are lawful and honourable, and the Psalm calls blessed the one who eats what is gained by the labour of his hands; and the Apostle, commending this to Christian men, writes: "Let him who stole steal no more, but rather labour, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to give to those who need it." And the same Apostle says that he who does not provide for his own household is worse than an unbeliever. But sin is committed in this matter through excessive and anxious solicitude, which the Lord forbids elsewhere, and which fights against faith, as if we thought that God did not care for us, who feeds the birds of the air and clothes and adorns the flowers growing in the fields with their leaves and colours. Those who give place to this solicitude neglect the sacred assemblies, and, with all care for eternal salvation gradually extinguished, think that all the time is lost in which they make no gain. Likewise, to those so disposed you will never persuade them to depart from those places in which superstition and idolatry reign, and where they are compelled to do many things against conscience.

units.la: Secundi abeunt ad suam mercaturam, & in Luca boum iuga emisse dicuntur. Est mercatura quoque necessaria. Nam non omnis fert omnia tellus. Aliunde ergo inferantur oportet, quibus cubi deficiunt. Sed de ijs hic loquitur, qui opibus augendis ita student, ut caelestia & aeterna bona negligant immemores regulae Pauli, qui monet, ut qui emunt, sint tanquam non obtineant: & qui mundo vtuntur, curent ne eo abutantur. Nam nisi haec nobis cura fit, fieri nequit, ut duobus diuer sis heris, Deo & Mammonae simul seruiamus: sed plerunque fit, ut terrenis quam caelestibus addi-ctiores, non in charitatis modo & iustitiae leges peccemus, verum etiam diuini cultus & religionis iura violemus. Quia autem boum hic mentio fit apud Lucam, de ijs quoq; locus intelligi potest, qui pecuinis cupiditatibus dediti voluptates carnis sequuntur, neq; animos ad caelestia attollunt, de quo illos vel sola corporis statura debebat admonere.
units.tr: The second go away to their trade, and in Luke it is said that they bought yoke of oxen. Trade too is necessary. For not every land bears everything. Things which are lacking in one place must therefore be brought in from elsewhere. But here he speaks of those who so strive to increase their wealth that they neglect heavenly and eternal goods, forgetful of the rule of Paul, who admonishes that those who buy should be as if they did not possess, and those who use the world should take care not to abuse it. For unless this care is ours, it cannot happen that we serve at the same time two different masters, God and Mammon; but for the most part it happens that, more addicted to earthly things than to heavenly, we sin not only against the laws of charity and justice, but also violate the rights of divine worship and religion. And because mention is made here in Luke of oxen, the passage can also be understood of those who, given over to bestial desires, follow the pleasures of the flesh and do not lift their minds to heavenly things; the very stature of their body ought to admonish them of this.

units.la: Adduntur his tertij, qui vim & iniuriam faciunt feruis Dei. Nam prahensos contume-lijs affecerunt & trucidarunt. Et haec quidem omnia inter Iudaeos facta sunt cum euidenti salutis aeternae iactura, quam multi eorum fecerunt. In Sacerdotibus nimium rei domesticae studium & auaritiam Christus passim accusat. De mercatura quid attinet dicere, quando hanc in templum quoq; intulerunt, quod ab illis in emporium conuersum fuit contra illud Dei pronunciatum: Non esto Chananaeus in domo Domini. Neq; in his gradibus subsistit impietas: sed quia de quaestu & exti-matione sua periculum euidens imminere videbant, si Christo locum darent, & caelestes illas nu-ptias sectarentur, vim quoq; fecerunt eius feruis & Apostolos in carceres abduxerunt, virgis caesi derunt, plerofq; autem crudeliter trucidarunt. In tantam deniq; exarserunt rabiem, ut intolerabile ipsis videretur si quae ipsi nolebant admittere IESVM CHRISTVM, illic inter gentes praedicarent. Vide 1. Thess. 2.
units.tr: To these are added the third class, who do violence and wrong to the servants of God. For they seized them, subjected them to insults and slaughtered them. And all these things were done among the Jews with the clear loss of eternal salvation, which many of them incurred. Christ everywhere accuses the priests of excessive devotion to domestic affairs and of avarice. What need is there to speak of trade, when they even brought it into the temple, which they turned into a marketplace, contrary to that pronouncement of God: "Let there be no Canaanite in the house of the Lord." Nor does their impiety stop at these steps; but because they saw that the clear danger to their gain and reputation threatened, if they gave place to Christ and followed those heavenly nuptials, they also did violence to his servants, led the Apostles off to prison, had them beaten with rods, and many of them they cruelly slaughtered. Finally they blazed into such a rage that it seemed intolerable to them that Jesus Christ should be preached among the Gentiles, when they themselves would not admit him. See 1 Thess. 2.

units.la: Caeterum si quae per se non illicita sunt a regno Dei abducere possunt, si denique exitio fuerunt Iudaeis, ut nec veteris dignitatis memoria, nec maiorum exempla, nec recentia Christi beneficia eos potuerint in officio retinere, quin ex amicis & filijs Dei hostes & perduelles fatti sint: quid de ijs sentiri debet, quae palam iniusta & iniqua sunt? Si rei domesticae studium nocet, nisi charitatis & animi sua forte contenti aequitate gubernetur: quid fiet, si auaritiae habenas laxando, vt rius vế ribus, impositurus, monopolijs, rapinis, furtis indulgeas? Quid si militiae mercenariae tedas, quae non temere sceleram & omnis nequitiae scholam dixeris? Quis huic addictum a diris illis perabit, quas Deus ei comites indiuulsas adiunxit: Vae ei, qui adauget non sua? Vae ei, qui aedificat vrbem in sanguine, & instaurat ciuitatem cum iniquitate? Maledictus, qui accipit munus vt percutiat animam sanguinis innocentis: Et omnis populus dicat Amen. Si coniugalis amor fidei officit, quis hanc salua esse putabit, si libidinibus vagis defluamus, & corpora nostra, quae Spiritus Sancti debebant templa esse, scortationis membra faciamus. Securis multa obrepunt, quae nos a cura caelestium auocant, quid ergo fiat ebriosis & intemperantibus? Cum deniq; Dominus noster ijs ipsius abnegationem, mortificationem item carnis & totius hominis innouationem a nobis exigat, nec quisquam nisi renatus fit, regnum Dei videre queat, permitiosissime falluntur, qui hominem inter scelerum licentiam seruari posse sibi persuadent. Sic ergo in horum mentione versemur, ut nunquam excidat, eos qui sunt in Christo, nouam Creaturam esse, & Dei Filium ideo pro omnibus mortuum esse, ut qui viuunt posthac non sibi viuant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est & resurrexit. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum, Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, if things that are not unlawful in themselves can draw us away from the kingdom of God, if in the end they have proved ruinous to the Jews, so that neither the memory of their former dignity, nor the examples of their forefathers, nor the recent benefits of Christ could keep them in obedience, but they became enemies and traitors instead of friends and sons of God, what should be thought of those things that are plainly unjust and iniquitous? If zeal for domestic affairs does harm, unless it is governed by charity and by a fairness content with its own lot, what will happen if you loosen the reins of avarice and indulge in usury, exactions, monopolies, plunder and theft? What if you embrace mercenary soldiering, which one may not rashly call a school of crime and of every wickedness? Who will bring to an end the man given over to it, from those curses which God has attached to him as inseparable companions: Woe to him who increases what is not his! Woe to him who builds a city with blood and founds a state on iniquity! Cursed is he who takes a bribe to strike down the life of innocent blood; and let all the people say, Amen. If conjugal love hinders faith, who will think that faith is safe if we flow away into wandering lusts and make our bodies, which ought to be temples of the Holy Spirit, members of fornication? Many cares creep upon us which call us away from heavenly concerns; what then will become of drunkards and the intemperate? Since our Lord finally requires of us self-denial, the mortification of the flesh, and the renewal of the whole man, and since no one who is not born again can see the kingdom of God, they are most dangerously deceived who persuade themselves that a man can be kept safe amid the licence of sin. So let us dwell on these things in such a way that it never slips from our minds that those who are in Christ are a new creature, and that the Son of God died for all so that those who live henceforth should not live for themselves, but for him who died and rose again for them. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 254.

units.la: Rex autem hoc audito iratus est, & missis exercitibus suis perdidit homicidas illos, & urbem eorum incendit. Tunc dicit servis suis: Nuptiae quidem paratae sunt: sed qui vocati fuerant, non erant digni. Ite ergo ad compita viarum, & quoscunque inveneritis, vocate ad nuptias. Et egressi servi illi in vias, congregaverunt omnes quos invenerunt, malos pariter ac bonos: & impletae sunt nuptiae convivis.
units.tr: When the king heard this, he was angry. He sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he said to his servants: "The wedding is indeed prepared, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the crossroads, and invite to the wedding whomever you find." And those servants went out into the streets and gathered together all whom they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

units.la: Omnis nostra salus in eo consistit, ut Filio Dei aeterno, ceu unico spiritu animarum unimur. Etsi vero hic sese totum per Evangelium nobis offerat, & ad nuptias suas caelestes, id est, ad regni sui communionem liberaliter omnes invitet, plerique tamen hanc gratiam aspernantur, et accedere ad eum nolunt. Causam huius vitii ipse nuper monstravit in Iudaeorum exemplo, dum ex posuit, quid praetexuerint, qui ad nuptias Filii Dei accedere noluerunt. Nam alium domum suam abiisse ait, alium ad mercaturam suam se contulisse dicit, multos item in rubiem exarsisse, quae eo ipsa progressa fit, ut aliquos ex Dei servis trucidarint. Ita vero offendit rei domesticae studio & opum desiderio nimio plerosque impediri, ut divina & caelestia assequi non possint, multos voluptati huius saeculi inescari, ut belluarum instar animos hostiles concipiant adversus eos, qui studiis ipsorum se opponunt, & ipsos ad saniorem mentem reducere cupiunt. Quorum exemplis confirmatur illud Dei dictum, quod olim per Prophetam pronuntiavit: Perditio tua ex te est o Israel, salus autem tua ex me. Caeterum quia haec plerisque levia putantur, multi autem ad mundi exemplum respicientes adhuc praetextus quaerunt, praestat nunc videre, quid de Iudaeis statuerit Rex ille caelestis, Deus, ut discamus quid omnes maneat, qui salutem, quae in Christo ipsis offertur, fastidiunt.
units.tr: All our salvation rests on this, that we are united with the eternal Son of God, as with the one Spirit of our souls. Although he offers himself wholly to us through the Gospel, and kindly invites all to his heavenly wedding, that is, to fellowship in his kingdom, many nevertheless scorn this grace and refuse to come to him. He himself recently showed the cause of this fault in the example of the Jews, when he set out the excuses of those who refused to come to the wedding of the Son of God. For he says that one went off to his house, another betook himself to his trade, and many also raged with anger, which went so far that they murdered some of God's servants. Thus it is clear that many are hindered by a zeal for domestic affairs and by an excessive desire for wealth, so that they cannot attain divine and heavenly things; many are enticed by the pleasures of this age, so that, like beasts, they conceive hostile feelings against those who oppose their pursuits and want to bring them back to a saner mind. The example of these people confirms that saying of God which he once pronounced through the prophet: "Your destruction is from yourself, O Israel, but your salvation is from me." Yet because these things are thought by many to be trivial, and many, looking to the example of the world, still seek pretexts, it is worth seeing now what that heavenly King, God, decided about the Jews, so that we may learn what awaits all who despise the salvation offered to them in Christ.

units.la: Primo dicitur Rex audiisse, quam indigne ab invitatis tractati sint servi ipsius. Et est hoc consolationis plenum, quod Regem habemus, qui non otiosus ad cardines caeli ambulat, aut igna ut spectator nulla rerum cura tangitur, aut alioqui quid fiat aut dicatur, nescit: quale impii illusores sibi finguntur, in primis, quando ipsis cum Verbi praeconibus res est: quos quia toti mundo exosos esse vident, sibi licere putant illos pro sua libidine tractare. Scilicet hic superus labor est (inquiunt) haec cura quietos sollicitat, Verbi praecones quid patiantur. Qui cum totius studio se gaudia mundi turbent, non dignos dicas melioribus aliis. At longe alium nobis Deus sacra litera describunt. Nam etsi in caelis sublimis sedeat, demittit tamen se, & videt quae in caelo & in terra fiunt. Et cur ignorare putetur, quae servis suis tristia accidunt, cuius cura ad pullos coruorum extenditur, & absque cuius nutu ne passerculi quidem pereunt. Num hoc si digne expendatur, pios & fidos servos armabit, ut non possint sibi metuere ab hominibus, qui mortales sunt, & subito in pulverem reverti tur, si vitae spiritum eius Deus subtraxerit.
units.tr: First, the King is said to have heard how shamefully his servants were treated by those who had been invited. And this is full of comfort: we have a King who does not walk idly about the corners of heaven, nor sits idle like a spectator, untouched by any care for things, and ignorant of what is done or said elsewhere. Such is the picture the impious mockers invent for themselves, especially when they have to do with the heralds of the Word. Because they see that they are hated by the whole world, they think they may treat them as they please. Surely, they say, this lofty work is no concern of God's; this care does not disturb the quiet, what the heralds of the Word suffer. While they trouble the whole world by their pursuit of pleasures, you would not call them worthy of better things. But the sacred writings describe to us a God quite different. For although he sits enthroned on high in heaven, he nevertheless lowers himself and sees what happens in heaven and on earth. And why should it be thought that he is ignorant of what sad things happen to his servants, whose care extends to the young ravens, and without whose nod not even the sparrows perish? If this is weighed rightly, it will arm his pious and faithful servants so that they need not fear men, who are mortal and quickly return to dust when God withdraws the breath of their life.

units.la: Nec enim audit modo & novit quid suis fiat, sed irascitur si iniquius tractentur sui servi. Non ferunt homines, ut quis servus ipsorum obstrepat, quibus aliquid in mandatis dederunt. Cur ergo non offendatur Deus, si qui Evangelii sui praeconibus sese opponat, aut eosdem iniquius tractet? Quod enim his fit, sibi factum putat, & in ipsum redundat illorum contemptus. Ideo Samuel de Israelitis dicebat: Non te reprobant, sed me reprobarunt ne regnem super eos. Et quam graui ira excanduerit adversus Prophetarum hostes, qui hos olim violarunt sub finem historia Palipomenon est videre. Verumtamen gravius iudicium eos manet, qui novi testamenti ministros violare audent. Nam quo uberior est fons gratiae & salutis, qui per hos reducitur, eo maiorem poenam meretur contemptus, quo ille reiicitur. Et si verum fateri libet, cum illis reicitur aeternus ille & dilectus Filius Dei, in quo uno Pater placatus est. Idem si ad nuptias suas nos invitantem non audiamus, mendacij a nobis insimulatur. Incredulitatis enim iste non alia causa allegari potest, quam quod veracem esse non credimus. Ideo Ioannes Baptista dicebat: Pater diligit Filium, & omnia dedit ei in manum: Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam aeternam: qui vero non obtemperat Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum. Quid autem ira Dei gravius & atrocius fingi potest? Regis iram Solomon fremitum leonis vocat, ad quem omnia animalia expauescere dicuntur, adhaec eandem mortis nuntium esse dicit. Quid ergo de ira Dei dicemus, qui
units.tr: For he not only hears and knows what is done to his people, but he is angry if his servants are treated unjustly. Men do not tolerate it when someone among their servants, to whom they have given some commission, makes trouble. Why then should God not be offended if anyone sets himself against the heralds of his Gospel, or treats them unjustly? For he regards what is done to them as done to himself, and their contempt rebounds upon him. Therefore Samuel said of the Israelites: "They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, so that I should not reign over them." And how greatly God burned with anger against the enemies of the prophets, who long ago violated them, may be seen at the end of the history of the Chronicles. Yet a heavier judgment awaits those who dare to violate the ministers of the New Testament. For the richer the fountain of grace and salvation that is brought back through them, the greater the punishment deserved by those who scorn it, in proportion as that grace is rejected. And if we are willing to speak the truth, together with them that eternal and beloved Son of God is rejected, in whom alone the Father is appeased. Likewise, if we do not heed him when he invites us to his wedding, he is charged by us with lying. For no other cause of this unbelief can be alleged than that we do not believe him to be true. Therefore John the Baptist said: "The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand. He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not obey the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him." Yet what can be imagined more grievous and terrible than the wrath of God? Solomon calls the king's wrath the roar of a lion, at which all animals are said to tremble, and he says that it is also the messenger of death. What then shall we say of the wrath of God, who

units.la: Prov. 19. & 16. ignis consumens est. Hic si aduersus nos exardeat, quae vires, quae consilia nos ex eius manibus eripere, aut contra illum tueri poterunt.
units.tr: Prov. 19. & 16. is a consuming fire. If this blazes against us, what strength, what counsel will be able to snatch us from his hands, or to defend us against him?

units.la: Non autem iratum modo fuisse ait Regem, sed ne quis iram eius facile placari posse sperèt, exe-cutionem quoque illi tribuit, dicens: Et misit exercitibus suis perdidit homicidas illos, & vrbem eorum incendit. Dominus exercituum dicitur Deus, quia huic omnes creaturae obediunt, si earum opera in iudicijs suis exequendis vti velit. Aliant illi myriades Angelorum, quorum quàm in-superabiles vires sint, exempla in Aegyptios & Assyrios edita testantur. Nec bonis modo Angelis ministris vtitur, verumetiam malis, qui ita illi subijciuntur, vt nihil possint vel ausint facere, quàm quod ille permiserit, sicuti in Iobi & porcorum Gergesenorum historia cernitur. Similiter homines quoque tam pij quàm impij opera suam Deo praestant quando ipse vult: & eosdem ille armare nouit, si quando per illos iudicia sua vult exequi. Quid de hominibus & Angelis dico, quando Dei exer-citus sunt omnis generis bestiae & infectae, quorum nullum tam imbelle & infirmum est, quod non sufficiat potentissimus tyrannus debellandis, si ita vult Dominus? Sic vespis, crabronibus, ranis, muri-bus, pediculis Pharaonem & totam Aegyptum domuit, vt imperata facere cogerentur, qui aduersus ipsum & populum eius coniurauerant. Et vt ad coelos redeamus, habet illic exercitus terribiles nubium, ex quibus fulgura, tonitrua & fulmina emicant, quibus quacunque ab hominibus fiunt, cede-re coguntur. Serui deniq; Dei sunt tyranni impij, qui ipsi etiam non alia faciunt, quàm quae ille fa-cta vult. Sic seruus Dei dicitur Nabuchodonosor: quem in biuio stantem & dubium aduersus quos moueret, Ierosolymam versus direxit, vt de illa poenas impietatis & contempti Verbi sui sumeret. Et apud Israelitas Persas & Medos suos sanctificatos vocat eò quod horum copias ipse con-scripserat, vt Babylonem expugnarent, & Monarchiam orbis terrarum potentissimam euerterent, eodem sensu accipi debet, quod hic dicitur, Deus suos exercitus misisse & extirpasse vel perdidisse homicidas illos, qui seruos eius indignissime & crudelissime trucidauerant. Impletum autem est quod dicitur per Romanos, qui legionibus suis in Iudaeam missis regionem totam vastarunt, & ca-ptis prius aliis vrbibus, tandem Ierosolymam arctissima obsidione cinxerunt, & infelice ferro & fame afflixerunt, captam vero etiam inuito & reluctante Tito incenderunt milites. Ceciderunt in obsidione & expugnatione ista decies centena millia hominum, eorum autem qui captiui facti sunt, numerantur a Iosepho oculato, reste nonaginta septem millia, quorum alij ad triumphum seruati, alij in spectaculis pro more bestijs proiecti, innumeri gladiatorum ludis destinati sunt, vt mu-tuis vulneribus crudeliter sese conficerent.
