Et toto illo bello multa acciderunt, quae haec omnia Deo sic volente fieri testabantur: neque hoc Titus dissimulauit, qui non semel protestatus est, se vrbe & gentem seruatam cupere, illos autem sua contumacia sibi ipsis interitum accersere. Sed ita fieri oportebat, vt Dei auspiciis haec geri, toti orbi testatum fieret.
units.tr: He says not only that the king was angry, but, so that no one might hope that his anger could easily be appeased, he also assigns to him the execution, saying: "He sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city." God is called the Lord of hosts, because all creatures obey him, if he wishes to use their works in carrying out his judgments. He has at his command myriads of angels, whose unconquerable strength is attested by the examples displayed against the Egyptians and the Assyrians. He uses not only good angels as his ministers, but also evil ones, who are so subject to him that they can do nothing, or dare do nothing, except what he has permitted, as is seen in the history of Job and of the swine of the Gergesenes. Likewise men, both pious and impious, render their service to God when he wills it, and he knows how to arm them if at any time he wishes to carry out his judgments through them. Why speak of men and angels, when the armies of God are all kinds of beasts and insects, none of which is so feeble and weak that the most powerful tyrant cannot be overcome by it, if the Lord so wills? Thus by wasps, hornets, frogs, gnats and lice he subdued Pharaoh and all Egypt, so that those who had conspired against him and his people were compelled to do what was commanded. And to return to the heavens: there he has terrible armies of clouds, from which lightnings, thunders and thunderbolts flash, and to these all things done by men are compelled to yield. Finally, the impious tyrants are the servants of God, and they do nothing other than what he wishes to be done. Thus Nebuchadnezzar is called the servant of God, whom he set, standing undecided at the crossroads as to whom to attack, to march toward Jerusalem, so that he might take from it the punishment of its impiety and its contempt for his Word. And among the Israelites he calls the Persians and Medes his sanctified ones, because he himself had enlisted their forces to storm Babylon and overthrow the most powerful monarchy of the world. In the same sense must be understood what is said here: that God sent his armies and rooted out or destroyed those murderers who had most shamefully and cruelly slaughtered his servants. What is said was fulfilled through the Romans, who, sending their legions into Judaea, laid waste the whole region, and, after first capturing other cities, at last surrounded Jerusalem with a very close siege and afflicted it with the unhappy sword and famine; and when it was captured, the soldiers burned it, even though Titus was unwilling and resisted. In that siege and storming there fell one million one hundred thousand people. Of those who were taken captive, Josephus, an eyewitness, reckons ninety-seven thousand. Some of them were kept for the triumph, others were thrown to the beasts in the spectacles according to custom, and countless others were destined for the games of the gladiators, to butcher one another cruelly with mutual wounds. And throughout that whole war many things happened which testified that all this was done with God so willing. Titus did not conceal this; he declared more than once that he wished the city and the nation to be spared, but that they, by their own obstinacy, were bringing destruction upon themselves. But it had to happen in this way, so that it might be attested to the whole world that these things were carried out under God's direction.

units.la: Est hoc memorabile exemplum, quo docemur, quid gratia Dei contemptores maneat, qui Euangelij praedicationem, qua illos Dominus ad coelestes nuptias & regni sui haereditatem inuitat superbe & impie aspernantur. Non excluduntur solùm a regno Dei, vt spiritualibus donis mul-tentur, quae fere contemnunt, nec multum dolent eorum iactura, sed effundit in illos maledictione omnem Deus, vt in hoc etiam saeculo calamitosi & inglorij viuant, & tandem infelicius moriantur. Nec est quod in solo scelere, quod in Dei Filium Iudaei designarunt, haereamus, quasi huius modo tam horribiles poenas exoluerint: Nam propter Euangelium IESV CHRISTI reiectum & contemptam gratiam Dei haec tam dira & horrenda passi sunt: & semper nos meminisse decet, Deum in naturalibus ramis voluisse exemplum toti orbi proponere, quod ijs admonendis & ter-rendis seruiat, qui ex oleastro desumpti & gratia ipsius participes facti sunt. Poterat hoc nos ad-monere de causis calamitatum nostri saeculi, quas multi admirantur, quando terras prope omnes fame & penuria laborare, peste & morbis insolitis affligi, seditionibus turbari, bellis & incursio-nibus hostilibus atteri, a Turcis deniq; provincias Christiani nominis exhauriri, & regna potentis-sima occupari vident. At quid aliud fiat, quando salute & laetae pacis nuntiu pleriq; fastidiunt, alij impie contemnunt, multi hostiliter persequuntur? Quia precones Dei, qui ad nuptias coelestes et ad gaudia aeterna nos inuitant, audire dedignatur mundus infelix, immittit Deus suos exercitus, qui omnia pessundant, & lugere cogunt eos, qui cum Christo exultare & gaudere nolunt.
units.tr: This is a memorable example, by which we are taught what awaits those who despise grace of God, who proudly and impiously scorn the preaching of the Gospel, by which the Lord invites them to the heavenly wedding and to the inheritance of his kingdom. They are not only shut out from the kingdom of God, so that they are not enriched with spiritual gifts, which they largely despise, and do not grieve much over their loss. God also pours out every curse upon them, so that in this age they live wretched and inglorious, and at last die more wretchedly. Nor should we dwell only on the crime which the Jews committed against the Son of God, as if they paid such horrible penalties for that alone. They suffered these harsh and dreadful things for rejecting the Gospel of Jesus Christ and despising the grace of God. We should always remember that God, in the case of the natural branches, wanted to set an example before the whole world, one that serves to admonish and terrify those who were taken from the wild olive and made partakers of his grace. This could also warn us about the causes of the calamities of our own age, which many marvel at, when we see nearly all lands suffering from famine and want, afflicted by plague and unusual diseases, disturbed by seditions, worn down by wars and hostile raids, and finally Christian provinces being drained by the Turks and mighty kingdoms being seized. But what else is happening, when most people scorn the news of salvation and of joyful peace, others impiously despise it, and many persecute it with hostility? Because the wretched world refuses to hear the heralds of God, who invite us to the heavenly wedding and to eternal joys, God sends forth his armies, which lay everything waste, and compels to mourn those who are unwilling to rejoice and exult with Christ.

units.la: Porrò ne quis decretum Dei de regno suo instaurando & propagando Iudæorum incredulitate & excidio abrogari & prorsus impediri putaret (qua perjuasione illos potissimum fascinatos & deceptos fuisse, sæpe diximus) quid porrò fecerit Rex ille narratur. Primò causam reddit reiectionis aut repudij Iudæorum, seruis suis dicens: Nuptiæ quidem paratæ sunt: sed qui vocati fuerant, non erant digni. Sensus huius dicti est: Ego quidem non defui meo officio, neque per me stetit, quo minus pactis starem & beatos facerem eos, quibus id promissum erat. Venit in mundum Filius meus, per hunc mundum mihi placatus est, parata & transfacta sunt omnia, quæ omnibus seruandis poterant sufficere: missi sunt item gratiæ & salutis prædones ad eos, quibus primis ista nuntiari debuerunt, nec quisquam est, qui se præteritum esse, aut de mea morositate possit iure conqueri. Sed qui inuitati fuerunt, & quos præ aliis isto honore dignatus sum, non fuerunt digni, ut eo gauderent, id est, seipsos illo indignos fecerunt, & proinde propria culpa perierunt. Nec enim hoc ita accipi debet, ut aliquem ex se dignum putemus, ut ad nuptias Filij Dei admittatur mensæ & regni sui particeps fiat. Omnibus potius dicendum est: Non sum dignus Domine, ut tectum meum subeas. Digni autem censentur, qui gratiam sibi oblatam grato animo & fide sincera excipiunt, & sponsi voce gaudent, inque eius occursum se præparant, ut in virginum parabola infra sequetur. E contra indigni sunt, qui seipsos isto honore spoliant, dum Deo vocanti non obsequuntur. Ita Apostoli ipsi dictum hoc intellexerunt, quando Iudæis Antiochenis Euangelij prædicationem auersantibus dixere: Vobis necesse fuit primum exponi sermonem Dei: postquam autem illum repellitis, & indignos vosipsos decernitis æterna vita, ecce conuertimur ad gentes. Ita quæ propria culpa exciderunt dignitate sua Iudæi, & sibi ipsis interitus sui fuerunt authores: quod de omnibus dici debet, qui horum exemplum sequuntur.
units.tr: Moreover, lest anyone think that God's decree to establish and extend his kingdom has been revoked and entirely hindered by the unbelief and ruin of the Jews (by which persuasion, as we have often said, they were chiefly bewitched and deceived), let us see what that King is reported to have done next. First he gives the reason for the rejection or repudiation of the Jews, saying to his servants: "The wedding is indeed prepared, but those who were invited were not worthy." The sense of this saying is this: I indeed did not fail in my duty, nor was it through me that I did not keep my covenant and make happy those to whom it had been promised. My Son has come into the world; through this world he has been reconciled to me; all things are prepared and accomplished which could suffice for saving everyone. Heralds of grace and salvation have also been sent to those to whom these things ought to have been announced first, and there is no one who can rightly complain that he has been passed over, or that I have been capricious. But those who were invited, and whom I deigned to honour with this above others, were not worthy to rejoice in it; that is, they made themselves unworthy of it, and therefore perished through their own fault. Nor should this be understood as if we thought that anyone is worthy of himself, so as to be admitted to the wedding of the Son of God and become a partaker of his table and kingdom. Rather, everyone should say: "Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof." They are considered worthy who receive the grace offered to them with a grateful heart and sincere faith, who rejoice at the voice of the bridegroom and prepare themselves for his coming, as will follow in the parable of the virgins. On the other hand, those are unworthy who deprive themselves of this honour by not obeying God when he calls. The apostles themselves understood this saying in this way, when they said to the Jews of Antioch, who were resisting the preaching of the Gospel: "It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles." Thus the Jews, through their own fault, lost their dignity, and became the authors of their own ruin. This must be said of all who follow their example.

units.la: Pergit autem Rex ille cœlestis, & nouis mandatis seruos suos instruit, & ut apud Lucam narratur: Abi citò (inquit) in plateas & vicos vrbis, ac pauperes ac mancos, claudos & cæcos huc introducito. Et cum his introductis adhuc locus vacaret, iterum iubet ad compita via rum exire, ad sepes item, & quoscunque inuenerint, vocare ad nuptias: imò cogere iubet, ut tota domus impleatur. Quo loco diligenter obseruari debet, quòd etsi Iudæi inuitati venire recusent, non tamen idcirco nuptiæ turbantur, aut prandium corrumpitur, sed vocantur alij. Nihil ergo de cedit regno Dei & huius decreto, etiamsi pauci sint gratiæ contemptores, qui cotumaciter suis suis perstitionibus insistunt, neque vllis rationibus se ad eius communionem adduci sinunt. Est enim regnum Christi æternum, & nulli genti asfriction. Nec enim personam respicit Deus, & in regno Christi non est Iudæus nec Græcus, non Barbarus aut Scytha, non seruus aut liber, mas aut fœmina: & spiritus ille vbicunque vult. Quia denique Dei decretum est, ut nuptiæ istæ impleantur, quo minus id fiat, nemo obstare poterit, sed si qui nolint accedere, itur ad alios, quos facile est Christo vel inuitos cogere, si velit, vel ex inuitis spontaneos facere. Debent ex eo consolationem petere pij, nec aliorum contumacia offendantur, aut etiam de Ecclesia dubitent, si quos hoslitiler Euangelio reluctari videant. Nouit electos suos vbicunque sint Dominus, neque aliquem horum ex manibus suis sibi eripi sinit. Admonentur etiam Iudæorum exemplo omnes, quibus Euangelium prædicatur, ne Dei vocationem contemnant. Si enim hoc fecerint contumaciter, ipsi quoque graui ista sententia damnantur, quam apud Lucam contra Iudæos Dominus pronuntiat: Dico vobis, neminem virorum illorum, qui vocati fuerant, gustaturum cœnam meam.
units.tr: But that heavenly King goes on, and instructs his servants with new commands, and, as it is told in Luke: "Go quickly," he says, "into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind." And when these had been brought in and there was still room, he orders them again to go out to the crossroads and the hedges, and to invite to the wedding whomever they find; indeed, he orders them to compel them, so that the whole house may be filled. At this point we must carefully observe that, even though the Jews refuse to come when invited, the wedding is not therefore disturbed, nor is the feast spoiled, but others are invited. Therefore nothing is taken away from the kingdom of God and from this decree, even if there are few despisers of grace who stubbornly persist in their superstitions and allow themselves to be brought into its fellowship by no means. For the kingdom of Christ is eternal, and is bound to no nation. God does not regard the person, and in the kingdom of Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, neither barbarian nor Scythian, neither slave nor free, male nor female; and the Spirit blows where he wills. Finally, since it is God's decree that this wedding be filled, no one will be able to hinder it. If some are unwilling to come, one goes to others, whom Christ can easily compel even if they are unwilling, if he wills, or make willing from the unwilling. From this the godly should draw consolation, and they should not be offended by the stubbornness of others, nor doubt about the Church, if they see some hostile resistance to the Gospel. The Lord knows his elect wherever they are, and he does not allow any of them to be snatched from his hands. Everyone to whom the Gospel is preached is also admonished by the example of the Jews not to despise God's calling. For if they do so stubbornly, they too are condemned by that severe sentence which the Lord pronounces against the Jews in Luke: "I tell you, none of those men who were invited shall taste my supper."

units.la: Docet præterea hæc parabolæ pars, qui nam ad regnum Dei idonei sint, ut vocationi Dei obsequantur. Primò iubentur ex plateis vocari pauperes & manci, claudi & cæci. Intelliguntur per hos primùm qui a curis huius sæculi, quibus fere diuites grauantur, liberi & expediti sunt ad ingrediendum per iter regni Dei. Deinde qui simul pauperes spiritu se mancos & claudos atque cæcos esse sentiunt, nec ex semetipsis idoneos, qui aliquid boni cogitent. Qui tales sunt, hi nuptias illas eeruunt & fituunt, ijde medico sibi opus esse sentiunt, & auide cupiunt ab eo curari, quem alteri illi, quos propriæ iustitiæ fiducia inflat, fastidiunt. Idcirco nuper dicebat Christus publicanos & meretrices Pharisæis præire in regnum Dei. Et hodie videmus, milites & alios, qui licentiæ scelerum aliquandiuediti fuerunt, facilius conuerti, ut Christi iugo colla submittant, quàm Carthusianos & moniales aut alios quoscunque, qui se alijs sanctiores esse sibi persuaserunt.
units.tr: Furthermore, this part of the parable teaches who are fit for the kingdom of God, so that they may obey God's calling. First, the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind are ordered to be called in from the streets. By these are first understood those who are free and unencumbered from the cares of this age, by which the rich are mostly burdened, so that they may enter by the road of the kingdom of God. Next, those who at the same time feel themselves to be poor in spirit, maimed, lame and blind, and not fit of themselves to think of anything good. Such people perceive that the wedding is great and lovely, feel that they need a physician, and eagerly desire to be healed by him, whom those others, puffed up with confidence in their own righteousness, despise. For this reason Christ recently said that tax collectors and harlots go before the Pharisees into the kingdom of God. And today we see that soldiers and others who for some time were given over to licence in sin are more easily converted, so that they submit their necks to the yoke of Christ, than the Carthusians and nuns or any others who have persuaded themselves that they are holier than the rest.

units.la: {a}Quod vt melius explicetur, eos etiam introduci vult Dominus, qui ad vias aut compita, & sepes deiidunt. Notantur per hos ex gentibus ij, qui prae caeteris per auia errorum & superstitionum dispersi fuerunt, aut ad sepes peccatorum secuti quiescerunt, quibus interfepti non potuerunt in Dei conspectum venire, vt eius bonitate fruerentur. Intelliguntur item qui inter sepes & spinas traditionum delitescunt, & intra conscientias suas punguntur, vt quo se vertere debeant, ignorent. Hos autem non vocari modo & introduci, verumetiam cogi vult vt ingrediantur. Neq; alias causa sic loquitur Dominus. Quia enim diuersi hominum mores, ingenia item diuersa sunt, non eadem docendi aut praedicandi ratio omnibus conuenit. Sunt enim quibus simplicem institutionem & doctrinam adhibuisse sufficit, aliis admonitione seueriore, multis adhortatione, imo correptione & obiurgatione acriore opus est: & ideo supra Verbi ministros exactorum similes dixit. Fit etiam saepenumero, vt Magistratus authoritatem suam interponere oporteat, quando multorum pernicacia tanta est, vt aliter vinci non possit. Neq; audiendi sunt qui clamant, Fide donum Dei, nec aliquem ad Christum venire, nisi quem Pater traxerit: & inde colligunt, neminem cogi debere, vt conciones sacras accedat, aut Ecclesiae exercitijs interfit. Etenim minime valet consequentia. Nam etsi fides donum Dei sit, in eo tamen conferendo Deus certis medijs & hominibus minus stricte vtitur, quorum est Verbi praedicatione & Sacramentorum administratione quoquis vrgere, difficilia item cum Ecclesiastica tam publica constanter tueri, ne qua in re officio suo defuisse dici possint. Deinde non potest quidem cogi hominis voluntas aut mens, attamen in officio contineri poterit, ne quid faciat, quod cum scandalo communi fidei & religioni aduersetur. Et vt in aliis fieri solet, vt qui suopte ingenio ad furta, libidines, vindictam & alia scelera proclives sunt, non possint vlla vt externa cogi, vt ingenium mutent, legibus autem & poenis contineri possunt, ne furentur, ne moechentur aut caedes faciant: ita fide quidem animus mens possit imbui, at manifesta superstitiones, illiciti cultus, blasphemia & alia eius generis prohiberi possunt, adhaec cogi possunt prophani sacrorum contemptores, vt caeteris sacris intersint, Verbum Dei audiant, precentur: & constat multis exemplis frequenter fieri, vt ista occasione Christo & saluti lucrifaciant, qui in licentia & contumacia sua perirent, nisi frano seueriore coercerentur: quod olim D. Augustinus obseruauit.
units.tr: {a}So that this may be better explained, the Lord also wants those to be brought in who lurk in the ways, the crossroads and the hedges. By these are signified those Gentiles who, more than others, have wandered astray in the byways of error and superstition, or who, following the hedges of sins, have rested there, and who, hemmed in by them, could not come into the sight of God to enjoy his goodness. Also understood are those who hide among the hedges and thorns of traditions, and are pricked within their consciences, and do not know where they ought to turn. Now the Lord wants these not only to be invited and brought in, but also compelled to enter. He does not speak this way without reason. For since the customs of men are different and their dispositions are different too, one method of teaching or preaching does not suit everyone. Some are sufficiently instructed by simple teaching and doctrine; others need a sterner admonition, many need exhortation, and indeed sharper rebuke and reproof. For this reason he also said above that the ministers of the Word are like tax collectors. It often happens too that the magistrate must interpose his authority, when the obstinacy of many is so great that it cannot be overcome otherwise. Nor should we listen to those who cry out that faith is the gift of God, that no one comes to Christ unless the Father draws him, and from this conclude that no one ought to be compelled to attend the holy sermons or take part in the exercises of the Church. For the inference holds by no means. Even if faith is the gift of God, yet in bestowing it God uses certain means and men less strictly, and it is their task to press it by the preaching of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, and likewise to uphold steadily the difficult public matters of the Church, so that they cannot be said to have failed in their duty in any matter. Furthermore, the will or mind of a man cannot indeed be compelled, yet he can be restrained from doing anything that is contrary to the common scandal of faith and religion. And as is usually the case in other matters, those who are by their own nature prone to theft, lust, revenge and other crimes cannot be forced by any external means to change their disposition, but they can be restrained by laws and penalties from stealing, committing adultery or murder. Thus indeed the mind may be imbued with faith, but manifest superstitions, unlawful worship, blasphemy and other things of that kind can be prohibited; and profane despisers of holy things can be compelled to attend the other sacred rites, to hear the Word of God and to pray. And it is established by many examples that, on this occasion, people often gain Christ and salvation who would perish in their licence and stubbornness unless they were restrained by a stricter bridle. Blessed Augustine once observed this.

units.la: Vt ergo feruorum isti orum exemplo commendatur Apostolorum industria, qui accepto Filij Dei mandato exiuerunt in orbem vniuersum, & Euangelium toti creaturae praedicarunt, vt pariter malos & bonos, id est, promiscue & absque personarum respectu omnes adducerent ad nuptias: ita ministrorum Verbi etiam hodie est, nullam praedicandi occasione negligere, sed omnibus omnia fiant (sicuti de seipso Paulus scribit) vt quam plurimos lucrifaciant. Est hoc officium gratum Domino nostro IESV CHRISTO, qui seruorum suorum laboribus benedicit, vt plerunq; plus proficiant quam sperarunt. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Thus, following the example of the servants, the diligence of the Apostles is commended to us: when they had received the command of the Son of God, they went out into the whole world and preached the Gospel to every creature, so that they might bring in to the wedding feast, alike, both good and bad, that is, all people without distinction and without regard to persons. So too today it is the duty of the ministers of the Word not to neglect any opportunity for preaching, but "to become all things to all men" (as Paul writes of himself), so that they may win as many as possible. This duty is pleasing to our Lord Jesus Christ, who blesses the labours of his servants, so that they often make more progress than they had hoped. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLV.
units.tr: HOMILY 255.

units.la: Ingressus autem Rex vt spectaret conuiuas, vidit illic hominem non indutum veste nuptiali. Tunc dicit ei: Amice, quomodo huc introisti non habens vestem nuptialem? At illi os occlusum est. Tunc dicit Rex ministris: Ligatis pedibus & manibus eius, tollite eum, & conijcite in tenebras exteriores: illic erit fletus & stridor dentium. Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
units.tr: "But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who was not wearing a wedding garment. And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?' And he was speechless. Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his hands and feet, take him away, and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.' For many are called, but few are chosen."

units.la: Spiritus Sanctus in Scripturis ita disserit de Iudaeorum repudio & gentium adoptione, vt illos quidem iure reiectos, hos autem ex gratia adoptatos esse deceat. Vtrumq; Christus etiam in parabola ista adumbrat. Quoad enim Iudaeos, hos audiuimus prae alijs populu inuitatos fuisse ad nuptias illas caelestes, quibus aeterna salutis communio figuratur, excidisse autem propria culpa, eo quod sua placita & cupiditates regno Dei praeferendo ad ipsum accedere noluerunt. Quoad gentes horum vocationem gratuitam fuisse, ex eo apparet, quod cum per compita et auia vagarentur, ad sepes peccatorum desiderent, adhaec claudi, manci, caeci essent, promiscue tamen vocati sunt, boni & mali. In quo nobis suam bonitatem commendat Deus, qui (vt Paulus ait) vult omnes homines
units.tr: The Holy Spirit, in the Scriptures, so discourses on the rejection of the Jews and the adoption of the Gentiles that it is fitting to see the former as justly cast off and the latter as adopted by grace. Christ also portrays both in this parable. As for the Jews, we have heard that they were invited above other peoples to those heavenly wedding feasts, which signify the eternal fellowship of salvation, but that they fell away through their own fault, because they were unwilling to come to God, preferring their own pleasures and desires to the kingdom of God. As for the Gentiles, that their calling was free is clear from the fact that, though they wandered through crossroads and byways and sat at the hedges of sin, and were lame, maimed and blind, they were nonetheless called indiscriminately, good and bad alike. In this God commends to us his goodness, since (as Paul says) he wills that all men

units.la: Ioan. 6. minēs salūos fieri. Debet ergo hinc consolatio generalis peti, ne quis se a Deo reiectū & exclusum patet. Qui enim Iudaeis contumacibus tam mitem & benignum se præbuit, ut tota die expansis manibus renitentes inuitare & attrahere dignatus sit, qui item gentes de salute nihil cogitantes ipse quæsiuit, num gratiæ & salutis cupidos reiceret? Quia vero multos offendit, quòd in externa Ecclesiæ societate pijs & bonis malos permixtos esse, & ad mensam Domini improbos hypocritas accumbere vident, qui Ecclesiæ dedecori & communes macula sunt, ut olim de illis Apostoli scripsè runt, sequitur nunc postrema parabola pars, quæ quid de illis futurum sit, adumbratur. Summa tot eius loci est, Quod etsi in Ecclesia interdum videatur esse confusio quædam, & plus licere scandalorum authoribus quàm par sit, venturum tamen diem iam olim constitutum, quando separatio vniuersalis fiat, & scandala omnia ex regno Dei expurgentur. Vbi discemus, non satis esse ad beatitudinem veram consequendam, si in externo Ecclesiæ contubernio locum habeamus, si item inter eos censeamur, qui verbum audiunt, Sacramentis communicant, preces suas cum alijs coniungunt, sed necessario requiri, ut fidei professio syncera sit, & huic vniuersa hominis vita respondeat. Porrò singula videamus.
units.tr: John 6. to be saved. A general consolation should therefore be drawn from this, so that no one thinks himself rejected and shut out by God. For if he showed himself so gentle and kind to the stubborn Jews that he deigned to invite and draw them to himself all day long with outstretched hands, would he who likewise sought out the Gentils, who were thinking nothing of salvation, reject those who desire grace and salvation? But since many are offended that good and evil are mixed together in the outward fellowship of the Church, and that they see wicked hypocrites reclining at the table of the Lord, who are a disgrace and common stain upon the Church, as the Apostles once wrote about them, the last part of the parable now follows, in which what will become of them is foreshadowed. The sum of this passage is this: although in the Church at times there may seem to be a certain confusion, and the authors of scandals may be allowed more licence than is fitting, nevertheless the day, long ago appointed, will come when a universal separation will take place and all scandals will be purged from the kingdom of God. Here we learn that it is not enough for true blessedness to be obtained if we have a place in the outward fellowship of the Church, or if we are counted among those who hear the Word, take part in the sacraments and join their prayers with others; rather, it is necessarily required that the profession of faith be sincere and that the whole of a person's life correspond to it. But let us now look at the individual points.

units.la: Principio rex ingressus esse dicitur, ut spectaret conuiuas, & vidisse inter alios hominem non indutum veste nuptiali. Ergo etsi videri possit interdum Deus multa temere & inconsultò agere in Ecclesia, & absq; discrimine quosuis admittere, & ideo nonnulli cum hominibus prophanis apud Malachiam dicant, frustra seruiri Deo, nec esse discrimen inter iustum & iniustum, nihil tamen absq; certa ratione facit & discrimen illud olim toti mundo patebit. Ingrediet enim ille Rex regem palam, ut spectet quales conuiuas habeat, & qui nam, & quo singuli habitu ad nuptias suas accesserint. Fiet autem ingressus iste sub finem huius seculi, quando Filius Dei in gloria Patris venier cum angelis suis ad iudicandum viuos & mortuos. Tunc enim erunt multa agni, quæ plenam redemptionem nobis afferent. Tunc separatio ista fiet, qua tritico, putres & mali piscæ a bonis, fatuæ virgines a prudentibus distinguentur. Interea facies Ecclesiæ erit ea, quæ fuit ab origine rerum omnibus seculis, ut in ea inueniantur plures, qui non induti sunt veste nuptiali. Etenim sub vnum personam, cuius hic mentio fit, omnes alios comprehendit, qui non respondent professioni suæ. Talis fuit Ecclesia tempore Noæ in arca, in qua Cham quoq; locum habuit. Et totius veteris Testamenti tempore nunquam fine ziz-anijs fuit ager ille Ecclesiæ, ut in Mose & prophetis est videre.
units.tr: First, the king is said to have come in to see the guests, and to have seen among the others a man not wearing a wedding garment. So although God may sometimes seem to act carelessly and without deliberation in the Church, and to admit anyone whatever without distinction, and although some, with the profane people in Malachi, say that it is in vain to serve God and that there is no difference between the just and the unjust, yet he does nothing without a sure reason, and that distinction will one day be plain to the whole world. For that king will come in openly to see what kind of guests he has, and who they are, and in what dress each has come to his wedding. This coming in will happen at the end of this age, when the Son of God comes in the glory of the Father with his angels to judge the living and the dead. Then there will be that separation by which the chaff, the rotten and bad fish will be distinguished from the good, and the foolish virgins from the wise. Meanwhile the face of the Church will be what it has been from the beginning of the world in all ages, so that many are found in it who are not clothed in the wedding garment. For under this one person, whose mention is made here, he includes all the others who do not correspond to their profession. Such was the Church in the time of Noah in the ark, in which Ham also had a place. And throughout the whole time of the Old Testament that field of the Church was never without tares, as may be seen in Moses and the prophets.

units.la: Nec feliciore primitiuæ Ecclesiæ conditione fuisse constat. Hæc enim Ananias, Sapphiras, & quæ valos murmuratores habuit, ut iam nihil dicam de Corinthijs, quos Paulus vocatos sanctos qui dem dicit, in ijsdem tamen nō vulgaria vitia accusat, ut aliquì mirū videri possit, Ecclesia potuisse eos dici, qui tā multis tamq; fœdis criminibus polluti erat. Quò longius vero ab Apostolorum temporibus recedimus, eò plus vitiorū irrepsisse videbimus. Et prodest de eo sæpe ac diligenter cogitare, ne ijs, quæ hodie fiunt offendamur, neq; audiamus Anabaptistarum calumnias, qui Ecclesiam esse negant inter eos, qui non omnia secundum Christi institutionem recte instituta habent. Etenim hoc illud ipsum est, quod in præsenti per infelicem illum adumbratur, qui abs; veste nuptiali comparuit, & ideo eiectus est.
units.tr: Nor is it established that the condition of the primitive Church was more fortunate. For it had Ananias, Sapphira, and those murmurers, not to mention the Corinthians, whom Paul indeed calls saints, yet in the same church he accuses them of no ordinary vices, so that it may seem strange that they could be called a Church when they were polluted with so many and such foul crimes. Indeed, the further we move away from the times of the Apostles, the more we shall see vices creep in. And it is useful to think about this often and carefully, so that we are not offended by what happens today, nor listen to the slanders of the Anabaptists, who deny that those are the Church who do not have everything rightly ordered according to Christ's institution. For this is precisely what is foreshadowed in the present parable by that unhappy man who appeared without the wedding garment and was therefore cast out.

units.la: Quū vero istum eiecit? Rex ille magnus, qui non promissa fecit suo filio, neq; aliquid vel Ieruorum vel conuiuarum hoc ius sibi sumpsit. Conuenit hoc cū eo, quod supra Baptista dixit, IESVM CHRISTVM ventilabrum habere in sua manu, quo aream suam ipse repurget. Et idē non patitur alibi, ut seruiatur ziz-ania euellant ante tempus messis, ne dum ista euellere volunt, simul tritico aut segetibus bonis damnum dent. Non debet autē hoc ita accipi, quasi nemini liceat sese opponere scelerib-us aut scandalis apertis. Etenim officium sedulò facere debent omnes, quibuscunq; aliquid a Deo mandatū est. Parentibus præcipitur, ut ex se natos in vera Dei cognitione & timore instituant ut eosdem disciplina quoq; seueriori in officio cōtineant. Incumbant ergo muneri suo, & quantū in ipsis est curent, ut filij non obliuiscantur operum Domini, & ut fœdus eius sanctè custodiant. Sic ministrorum est sermonem Dei prædicare, docendo, arguendo, exhortando, obiurgando instare tempestiuè & intempestiuè. Ne quid ergo hic omittant, neue occasionem negligant, ne quando aliquibus perditionis, aut etiam publici alicuius scandali authores sint, quod caueri poterat, si ipsi officium facerent. Eadē est eorum ratio, qui ad Reip. gubernacula sedent. Animos quidē & voluntates hominum cogere non possunt, & fidem solius Dei donum esse, nuper diximus. Sunt autem scelera quaedam, quibus societas hominum turbatur, & omnes tum charitatis tum honestatis publicae leges dissoluuntur. Haec punire, imo excindere iussit Deus, et nisi id fiat, graves poenas negligentibus denuntiauit. In hoc genere censentur Pithonici, homicidae, adulteri, incestii, Sabbati transgressores falsi doctores, blasphemi & quicunque alij in lege Dei nominantur. Non debent ergo cessare in suo munere ij, quibus sua iudicia Deus credidit. At ex Ecclesiae societate & a regni Dei communione alios excludere nemo debet, qui non peculiare mandatum de eo acceperit. Cur enim quis eos excludat priuato arbitrio, quos Deus vocat & inuitat? Vel tu quis es, qui alienum famulum iudicas? Viderunt proculdubio serui regis illius, qui Apostolorum persona sustinuerunt, illum non minus decenter vestitum esse, non autem ipsi eum eiecerunt, sed quia iussi erant quosuis mancos, claudos, egenos, qui ad sepes desidebant, & incerti vagabantur, intro accersere, quod sui muneris erat fecere, iudicium vero de cuiusq; persona aut habitu hero permiserunt. Hoc ipsum Apostoli fecerunt postea, qui non abfq; peculiari Spiritus sancti suggestione ab Ecclesia segregarunt homines scelerატos, & Paulus Corinthios in hominem incestum nihil statuere voluit, nisi suo Spiritu praesente. Quod si posteris temporibus obseruatum fuisset, nunquam oppressa Ecclesiae libertate in tantum creuisset quorundam potentia, qui sub religionis praetextu quaestum priuatum quaesiuerunt.
units.tr: But when did the king cast him out? That great king, who made no promises to his son, and did not claim this right for himself over either the servants or the guests. This agrees with what the Baptist said above, that Jesus Christ has the winnowing fan in his hand, with which he himself cleans his threshing floor. And elsewhere he does not allow the servants to pull up the tares before the time of harvest, lest while they try to pull them up they also do damage to the wheat or the good crops. Yet this should not be understood as meaning that no one may oppose open wickedness or scandals. For all to whom anything has been commanded by God ought to perform their duty diligently. Parents are commanded to bring up the children born of them in the true knowledge and fear of God, and also to keep them in their duty by a stricter discipline. Let them therefore attend to their task, and let them take care, as far as lies in them, that their children do not forget the works of the Lord, and that they faithfully keep his covenant. So too it is the task of ministers to preach the word of God, to instruct, reprove, exhort and rebuke, being urgent in season and out of season. Let them therefore omit nothing here, nor neglect an opportunity, lest at some time they be the authors of someone's destruction, or even of some public scandal, which could have been avoided if they had done their duty. The same reasoning applies to those who sit at the helm of the commonwealth. They cannot compel the minds and wills of men, and we have just said that faith is the gift of God alone. But there are certain crimes by which the fellowship of men is disturbed and all laws of both charity and public decency are dissolved. God has commanded that these be punished, indeed rooted out, and he has threatened grave penalties on those who neglect this. In this category are counted soothsayers, murderers, adulterers, incestuous persons, Sabbath-breakers, false teachers, blasphemers, and whoever else is named in the law of God. Therefore those to whom God has entrusted his judgements ought not to cease in their office. But no one ought to exclude from the fellowship of the Church and the communion of the kingdom of God those whom he has not received a special command concerning. For why should anyone exclude by private judgement those whom God calls and invites? Or who are you, to judge another's servant? Undoubtedly the servants of that king, who bore the person of the Apostles, saw that the man was no less decently dressed; yet they did not themselves cast him out. Rather, since they had been ordered to bring in whatever maimed, lame, needy persons were sitting at the hedges and wandering uncertainly, they did what belonged to their office, and left the judgement about each person's dress and condition to the master. The Apostles themselves did this afterwards, when, not without a special prompting of the Holy Spirit, they separated wicked men from the Church; and Paul wished to decide nothing against the incestuous man at Corinth except with his Spirit present. If this had been observed in later times, the freedom of the Church would never have been so oppressed, and the power of certain men, who sought private gain under the pretext of religion, would never have grown so great.

units.la: Sed ipsam actionem videamus, quae regi cum sordido hoc & impudente intercessit: Amice (inquit) quomodo huc introiuisti non habens vestem nuptialem? Non quaerit qua via aut quo gestu corporis ingressus sit, sed de animo potius interrogat. Quasi diceret: Quae haec tua est impudentia vel audacia, ut in hunc celeberrimum confessum non veritus sis venire hoc habitu, qui animum arguit longe aliter affectum, quam ab ijs requiratur, qui in illis nuptijs locum habere cupiunt. Amicus vero dicit, quem poterat contumeliosius compellare, eo quod eum ipse amice inuitarat, culpa autem eiectionis penes ipsum erat, qui non debita reuerentia ad epulum hoc accesserat. Sic Iudam in osculum proditorium ad eius collum ruentem amicum dicit Dominus, propter priorem familiaritatem, & quod per ipsum non fleterat, quo minus illi omne amici officium praestaret. Interim arguitur & amplificatur eorum culpa, qui ad Filij Dei nuptias vocati gratiam hanc non digne aestimant. Quid vero ille? Obmutuit. Est hoc hominis propria conscientia testimonio condemnati indicium. Et sane in illo die non habebunt tales quod dicant. Nec enim negare poterunt ea, de quibus a proprio corde condemnantur. Nam non occulta erit ista condemnatio. Aperientur libri, ut apud Danielem & in Apocalypsi scribitur, id est, omnia cordium arcana patefient. Frustra igitur quis negabit, quod in omnium oculis versabitur. Nullus praeterea locus erit poenitentiae, quae culpa admissa farciatur. Quid ergo aliud faciant, qui in illo die deprehendentur in reatu, quam quod obmutescent, & ignominiam sempiternam subibunt.
units.tr: But let us look at the action itself that took place between the king and this filthy and shameless man. "Friend," he says, "how did you come in here without a wedding garment?" He does not ask by what route or with what bodily posture he entered, but rather questions his mind. As if he were saying: what is this impudence or audacity of yours, that you were not ashamed to come into this most celebrated assembly in such a dress, which shows a mind far differently disposed from what is required of those who wish to have a place at this wedding. The friend, however, is addressed as "friend," although he could have been addressed more insultingly, since the king himself had invited him as a friend; the blame for his expulsion, however, rested with him, since he had come to this feast without due reverence. So the Lord calls Judas "friend" when he rushes to his neck with the betraying kiss, on account of their former familiarity, and because through him he had not failed to render every friendly service. Meanwhile the guilt of those who, though called to the wedding of the Son of God, do not value this grace as they ought, is pointed out and magnified. And what does the man do? He falls silent. This is the sign of a man condemned by the testimony of his own conscience. And indeed on that day such people will have nothing to say. For they will not be able to deny those things by which they are condemned by their own heart. For this condemnation will not be hidden. "The books will be opened," as is written in Daniel and in the Apocalypse, that is, all the secrets of hearts will be laid open. In vain, therefore, will anyone deny what will be before the eyes of all. Moreover, there will be no place for repentance by which a sin committed may be made good. What else, then, will those do who on that day are found guilty, than fall silent and undergo everlasting shame?

units.la: Est autem obseruatu dignum, quod Rex non cum seruis expostulat, qui hominem male vestitum introduxerint, sed ipsum accusat, qui nuptias tantas indecenti habitu fadare ausus fuerit. Seruit hoc illis confirmandis, qui metuunt, ne aliorum peccata ipsis imputentur & fraudi sint. Itaque ut periculum hoc caueant, soliciti discedunt ab Ecclesijs, in quibus impune agunt homines vitijs polluti: aut si verbi administros ipsi agant, nimis curiosi vel etiam odiosi sunt in exagitandis aliorum vitijs, dum metuunt, ne propter ea ipsi damnentur. Non recte aestimant isti homines Dei bonitatem, quae inexhausta est. Cur enim aliena, quorum nos non authores sumus, nobis imputet, qui propria condonat benigne, si vere & ex animo poeniteamus? Paulus de Caena Dominica cum Corinthijs agens, eos quidem graviter accusat & terret, qui indigne ad illam veniebant, & ait: Qui edit & bibit indigne, iudicium sibi edit & bibit: nullam vero aliorum mentionem facit, qui eiusdem mensae cum illis communicant. Sufficiat ergo nobis propria conscientia, neque Deum tam iniquum putemus, ut nos propter alterius delictum punire velit, cuius nulla in nobis culpa haeret.
units.tr: It is worth noting, however, that the King does not complain to the servants who had brought in the man badly dressed, but accuses him who dared to dishonour so great a wedding with an unseemly garment. This serves to reassure those who fear that the sins of others may be imputed to them and be a cause of ruin. So, to avoid this danger, they anxiously withdraw from those churches in which men polluted by vices act with impunity; or, if they themselves are ministers of the Word, they are overly scrupulous or even hostile in censuring the vices of others, while they fear that they themselves may be condemned on account of them. These men do not rightly judge the goodness of God, which is inexhaustible. For why would he impute to us the faults of others, of whom we are not the authors, he who graciously pardons our own, if we truly and from the heart repent? Paul, when dealing with the Corinthians about the Lord's Supper, indeed severely accuses and terrifies those who came to it unworthily, and says: "He who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgement to himself"; but he makes no mention of others who share the same table with them. Let our own conscience therefore suffice us, and let us not think God so unjust as to wish to punish us for the offence of another, to which no fault of ours adheres.

units.la: Qui vero irreuerenter ad Ecclesiae mysteria irrumpunt, meminisse debent quid ipsi acciderit ex regis decreto. Ligatis (inquit) pedibus ac manibus eius tollite eum ac conijcite in tenebras exteriores. Dicitur hoc suppliciorum aeternorum ministris, spiritibus malis, qui nō minus quam boni praesto sunt illi, ut eius iudicia exequantur. Quod autem D. Hieronymus annotauit, manu ac pedum mendum mentionem facit Scriptura, quando de sempiternis infernorum cruciatibus agitur, vt eo argumento corporum resurrectionem confirmet. Nam etsi ineffabilia sint illorū tormenta, & omnem intellectus captū excedant, quia tamen ad membra pertingent, corporum resurrectio praecedat ne cesse est, & vt eadē cruciatuū iftorū capacia fiant, nec his cōsumantur, quemadmodū beatorū corpora beatitudinem sempiternā percipient. Additur fletus & stridor dentiū, qui cum corporis tormentis animi quoq; dolores irremissos coniunctos fore testantur, quibus in aeternum exercebuntur, qui ex regno Dei in tenebras exteriores, vbi damnatorū locus est, quem alibi Scriptura Tophet & gehenna vocat, eijcientur. Et ne quis putet satis esse bene coepisse, concludit parabolam breui di ßo, Multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi, qui vera fide instructi salutem quam semel amplexi sunt, constanter retineant, & quod proprium electionis signum est, in finem vsq; perseuerent.
units.tr: But those who irreverently burst in upon the mysteries of the Church ought to remember what happened to that man by the king's decree. "Bind his feet and hands," he says, "and take him and cast him into the outer darkness." This is said to the ministers of eternal punishments, the evil spirits, who are present to him no less than the good ones, to carry out his judgements. What Jerome noted, that Scripture makes mention of the hand and foot when it speaks of the eternal torments of hell, is intended to confirm the resurrection of the bodies by this argument. For although their torments are unspeakable and exceed all capacity of understanding, yet because they reach the limbs, the resurrection of the bodies must necessarily precede, so that they may be capable of these torments and not be consumed by them, just as the bodies of the blessed will receive everlasting blessedness. Weeping and gnashing of teeth are added, which testify that with the torments of the body the sorrows of the mind also will be joined without remission, in which they will be exercised for ever, who will be cast out of the kingdom of God into the outer darkness, where the place of the damned is, which Scripture elsewhere calls Tophet and Gehenna. And lest anyone think it enough to have made a good beginning, he concludes the parable with a brief saying: "Many are called, but few are chosen," namely those who, instructed in true faith, firmly hold on to the salvation which they have once embraced, and, which is the proper sign of election, persevere to the end.

units.la: Caeterum quia totius salutis cardo, quem haec parabola tradit, in eo versatur, vt vestē nuptiali amicitiam simus, quae nam illa sit, & quomodo induatur, aliquanto diligentius videndum erit. Deus Opt. Max. initiō hominem ad suam imaginem bonum creauit, & vestiuit innocentia. Ideo etsi nudus erat, non tamen erubescebat. Vt primum vero ex vetito pomo comedit, se nudum esse vidit, nec sua induistria quicquam potuit contexere, quod in Dei conspectu ipsum velare & tueri posset. Et quia posteritatem omnem in imagine seu conditione sua corrupta & vitiosa genuit Adamus, non potest melior nostrum omniū quam illius esse conditio. Ideo si in sua natura considerentur homines, ex seipsis nihil quam folia inania aut sordidos centones (vt pij apud Isaiā fatentur) humanae iustitiae contexere norunt. Quare Paulus de Christianis scribens, qui in hoc mundo peregrinantur, & domicilio quod e caelo est, superindui cupiunt, rectè quasi sub Correctionis specie interserit, nos voti nostri compotes tunc fore, si induti & non nudi reperiamur. Nuditatem ergo illam, quae ex Adamo ceu haereditario iure deriuata est, prius vestē idonea velari ac indui oportet, vt caelestis & immortalis gloriae capaces efficiamur. Et hoc dicendo Apostolus videtur ad vestem nuptialem alludere, de qua in praesenti Christus loquitur. Quam vero illam esse dicemus? Hic meminisse oportet, Deum primis parentibus vestes fecisse, quibus aduersus caeli iniurias defenderentur: cum illos ex Paradiso exturbare vellet. Ipsi folia ficus contexuerunt, quibus nequicquam sese tegebant, typo nimirū fucatae sanctimoniae & inutilis. Sed Deus pelliceas tunicas dedit, quo typo eos ad agnū illum immaculatum in e n fit, quem iam ante promiserat sub femine mulieris, vt qui caput serpentis conculcaturus erat, nostram quoq; nuditatem tegeret, adeoq; defenderet aduersus omne periculum. Ergo vestis illa nuptialis proprie est ipse Filius Dei, IESVS CHRISTVS, qui nobis a Deo Patre non solum sponsus, verum etiam iustitia, satisfactio, sanctificatio factus est.
units.tr: Moreover, since the hinge of the whole of salvation, which this parable teaches, turns on our being clothed with the wedding garment, we must consider somewhat more carefully what that garment is and how it is put on. God the best and greatest at the beginning created man good, in his own image, and clothed him with innocence. Therefore, although he was naked, he was not ashamed. But as soon as he ate of the forbidden fruit, he saw that he was naked, nor could he by his own industry weave anything that could cover and protect him in the sight of God. And since Adam begot all his posterity in his corrupted and vicious image or condition, the condition of all of us cannot be better than his. Therefore, if men are considered in their own nature, they know how to weave from themselves nothing but empty leaves or filthy patches of human righteousness (as the godly confess in Isaiah). Wherefore Paul, writing of Christians who are pilgrims in this world, and who desire to be clothed upon with the habitation which is from heaven, rightly introduces, as it were under the appearance of correction, that we shall be possessed of our desire then, if we are found clothed and not naked. Therefore that nakedness which has been derived from Adam, as by hereditary right, must first be covered and clothed with a fitting garment, so that we may be made capable of heavenly and immortal glory. And in saying this the Apostle seems to allude to the wedding garment of which Christ is now speaking. But what shall we say that garment is? Here it is fitting to remember that God made garments for our first parents, by which they might be defended against the injuries of heaven, when he wished to drive them out of Paradise. They themselves had woven fig leaves, with which they vainly covered themselves, a type, no doubt, of pretended and useless holiness. But God gave them tunics of skins, by which type he pointed them forward to that spotless Lamb, which he had already promised under the seed of the woman, so that he who was to crush the head of the serpent would also cover our nakedness and thus defend us against every danger. Therefore that wedding garment is properly the Son of God himself, JESUS CHRIST, who has been made for us by God the Father not only bridegroom, but also righteousness, satisfaction and sanctification.

units.la: Hunc nos induere oportet, quod per fidem fit, qua apprehensus nobis vnitur, & totus nostr fit. Ideo Apostolus de credentibus loquens, quos per fidem in CHRISTO IESV filios Dei fa-ctos esse dixerat, mox addit: Nam quicunq; in Christo baptizati estis, Christum induistis. Baptis-mi meminit, qui fidei & filiorum Dei externum Sacramentum est, adeoq; sigillum iustitiae fidei, sicut olim Circumcisio, in cuius locum successit. Quia ergo de vere credentibus agit, in quibus Bap-tismus efficax est, consulto Baptismum allegat, in cuius actione mysterium illud adumbrabatur. Qui vero ita baptizantur, vt sese efficacitas Baptismi per fidem exerat, ijdem Christum ita in-duunt, vt hunc non solum ore & verbis, verumetiam totius vitae conuersatione profiteantur, & (quod Paulus alibi ait) quod viuunt, non sibi viuunt, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est ac resurre-xit, vt cum eodem Apostolo dicere possint: Viuo non amplius ego, sed viuit in me Christus: & vi-tam quam nunc vivo in carne, viuo per fidem Filij Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me. Eodem pertinet quod ad Romanos scribit Paulus: An ignoratis, nos quotquot baptizati su-mus in CHRISTVM IESVM, in mortem eius baptizatos esse. Sepulti ergo sumus vna cum eo per Baptismum in mortem: vt sicut excitatus est Christus ex mortuis in gloriam Patris: ita & nos in nouitate vitae ambulemus. Quibus adde quod in eadem epistola ait: Nox processit, dies autem appropinquauit. Abijciamus igitur opera tenebrarum, & induamur habitu lucis: vt inter diu compositè ambulemus, non in comessationibus & ebrietatibus, non cubilibus & proteruijs, non lite & inuidia, sed induimini Domino IESV CHRISTO, & carnis curam ne habete ad ex-plendas cupiditates. His similia vide ad Ephes. 4. cap.
units.tr: It is necessary for us to put on this Christ, which is done through faith, by which, being apprehended, he is united to us and becomes wholly ours. Therefore the Apostle, speaking of believers, whom he had said through faith in CHRIST JESUS have been made sons of God, immediately adds: "For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ." He mentions Baptism, which is the outward sacrament of faith and of being sons of God, and so the seal of the righteousness of faith, just as formerly circumcision, in whose place it succeeded. Because therefore he is speaking of those who truly believe, in whom Baptism is effective, he deliberately alleges Baptism, in whose action that mystery was foreshadowed. But those who are so baptized that the efficacy of Baptism is displayed through faith, these same put on Christ in such a way that they profess him not only with mouth and words, but also in the whole course of their life, and (as Paul says elsewhere) that they live not to themselves, but to him who died and rose again for them, so that with the same Apostle they can say: "I live no longer, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me." To the same purpose pertains what Paul writes to the Romans: "Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into CHRIST JESUS have been baptized into his death? We were therefore buried with him through Baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead to the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in newness of life." To these add what he says in the same epistle: "The night is far spent, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light, so that we may walk becomingly as in the day, not in revellings and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envy, but put on the Lord JESUS CHRIST, and make no provision for the flesh to fulfil its lusts." For similar things see Ephesians chapter 4.

units.la: Itaque nuptiali veste induti sunt, qui Christum vera & constanti fide amplexi, eundem
units.tr: Therefore they are clothed in the wedding garment who have embraced Christ with a true and steadfast faith, and

units.la: {y} ... dictis & factis, adeo ut totius vitae conversatione referunt. Qui secum viuunt, multa quidem iactare possunt, sed olim cum rex ille regum venerit, in eius conspectu obmutescent, nec illis locum dabit in caelestibus nuptiis Dei Filius, sed procul abs se reiiciet. Venit ergo deploranda hoc loco infelix humani generis conditio, quando pauci sunt vestes illa induti, quae sola nos tuebitur, quando conuiuas suos, id est, sui nominis professores ille inuisset, ut veros a falsis distinguat & segregat. Quam multi enim sunt, qui prorsus nudi discurrunt, aut ridiculis ac inutilibus superstitionum ineptissimarum centonibus sese palliant? Quam multi vero qui habitum tenebrarum praeferunt luci? Quid de illis dicemus, qui cum quoties mane se vestibus induunt, de harum origine cogitare, & vilem illum amictum, quem parentes primi a Deo acceperunt, simul parabolam hac de veste nuptiali in mentem revocare debebant, omnium horum & suipsorum immemores, habitu luxurioso & molli diffluunt, ut interdum praestaret nudos discurrere, quam egenos tam multifariam offendere, & incautius tam varias & turpes libidinis & superbiae occasiones obicere? Sunt haec cum multiplici scelere coniuncta, nec desunt exempla iudiciorum Dei, quibus quod de infelici illo dicitur, qui in tenebras exteriores eiectus est, confirmatur. Memores ergo dignitatis nostrae, ad quam vocati sumus, & quod in nouissima tempora incidimus, induamus nos per fidem IESVM CHRISTVM, & eundem totius vitae cursu referamus, ut cum dies ille laetus electis omnibus aduenerit, nō nudi reperiamur, sed inter eos connumeremur, de quibus Angelus olim pronuntiauit: Beati, qui ad Caenam nuptiarum Agni vocati sunt. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: {y} ... in words and deeds, so that they show it forth in the whole course of their life. Those who live with him in secret may indeed boast of many things, but when that King of kings comes, they will fall silent in his presence, and the Son of God will not give them a place at the heavenly wedding, but will cast them far away from himself. Here, then, we must lament the wretched condition of the human race, since few are clothed in that garment which alone will protect us, when the King came to see his guests, that is, those who professed his name, so that he might distinguish and separate the true from the false. For how many are there who run about entirely naked, or cover themselves with the ridiculous and useless patches of the most foolish superstitions? And how many more who prefer the garb of darkness to the light? What shall we say of those who, every morning when they dress themselves, ought to think of where their clothing comes from, and to call to mind the poor garment which our first parents received from God, and at the same time this parable of the wedding garment, yet, forgetful of all this and of themselves, dissolve in luxurious and soft attire, so that at times it would be better to run about naked than to offend the needy in so many ways, and to expose, all too carelessly, so many varied and shameful occasions for lust and pride? These things are joined with manifold wickedness, and there are no lacking examples of the judgments of God, by which what is said of that unhappy man who was cast into the outer darkness is confirmed. Therefore, mindful of the dignity to which we have been called, and that we have fallen upon the last times, let us clothe ourselves through faith in Jesus Christ, and let us carry that same clothing through the whole course of our life, so that when that joyful day comes for all the elect, we may not be found naked, but may be numbered among those of whom the Angel once declared: Blessed are those who are called to the supper of the Lamb's wedding. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLVI.
units.tr: HOMILY 256.

units.la: Tunc profecti Pharisaei consilium coeperunt, ut illaquearent eum in sermone. Itaque mittunt ad eum discipulos suos cum Herodianis, dicentes: Praeceptor, scimus te veracem esse, & viam Dei in veritate docere, nec quenquam curare: non enim respicis in personam hominum. Dic ergo nobis, quid tibi videtur? Licet censum dare Caesari, an non?
units.tr: Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel how they might ensnare him in his words. So they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying: Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and that you care for no one, for you do not regard the person of men. Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

units.la: POstquam Matthaeus aliquot IESV CHRISTI conciones descripsit, in quibus partim diuersis verbis, partim elegantibus parabolis Iudaeorum contumaciam accusauit, qua mereantur, ut quod olim Deus minatus est, ipsis a regno Dei exclusis, gentes adoptentur: narrabit deinceps disputationes aliquot insidiosas, quibus aduersarii ipsum irretire conati sunt, ut vel in periculum adducerent, vel populo contemptum aut inuisum facerent. In quibus primum elucet hostium eius improbitas, qui vbi odio veritatis coeperunt indulgere, subinde in peius proficiunt. Deinde Christi potentia atque bonitas sese exerit, qui & omnibus hostium conatibus & astutiis superior fit, verumetiam illis bene vtitur. Nam ista occasione de multis disserit, admodum necessariis cognitu: De Magistratu nimirum & officio subditorum contra eos, qui sub religionis praetextu immunitatem & licentiam quaerunt: de resurrectione item mortuorum: de summo mandato: de persona Messiae, & quid de eo iudicari debeat. De quibus ita agit, ut hostes quoque ipsius sapientiam diuina agnoscere & fateri cogantur. In praesenti prima pars actionis de Magistratu narratur, in qua videre oportet, quando & a quibus, quomodo item haec instituta sit.
units.tr: After Matthew has described several sermons of Jesus Christ, in which, partly in plain words and partly in striking parables, he accused the Jews of their obstinacy, by which they deserved that, with them cast out of the kingdom of God, as God had once threatened, the Gentiles should be adopted in their place, he will now narrate several insidious disputes, by which his adversaries tried to entangle him, either to bring him into danger or to make him despised and hated by the people. In these, first, the wickedness of his enemies shines forth: once they had begun to indulge their hatred of the truth, they advanced ever further into evil. Then the power and goodness of Christ show themselves, for he prevails over all the attempts and cunning of his enemies, and indeed makes good use of them. For on this occasion he discourses on many matters that are very necessary to know: namely on the magistracy and the duty of subjects, against those who seek immunity and licence under the pretext of religion; likewise on the resurrection of the dead; on the greatest commandment; on the person of the Messiah and what should be judged about him. He treats these so that his enemies too are compelled to acknowledge and confess his divine wisdom. In the present passage the first part of the action is related, concerning the magistracy; in it we must see when and by whom it was instituted, and how.

units.la: A tempore orditur Euangelista, ut qua occasione quaestionem iam aduersarij mouerint, demonstret. Vno autem verbulo temporis circumstantiam notat, dicens: Tunc profecti sunt Pharisaei, &c. Quando nimirum Christus parabolas de vinea & colonis infidis: de nuptiis item proposuit, quibus causas repudij Iudaeorum & adoptionis seu vocationis gentium indicauit. Prima parabola de vinea narratione exacerbatos fuisse aduersarios, nuper docuit Matthaeus, quando dixit, illos studuisse ipsum prehendere, sed ne id facerent, metu vulgi prohibitos fuisse: nimirum quod propriae conscientiae testimonio conuicti sciRent se dignos esse supplicio, si quid aduersus eum auderent. Sed cum alteram quoque parabolam de nuptiis adderet, magis irritati sunt: sed tunc quoque quod aliquis est illis metus, qui eos cohibuit, ut manus ab eo abstinerent. Apparet hoc loco discrimen auditorum veritatis. Electi qui alias omnes Christi dicuntur, pastoris sui vocem norunt, & hac audita emendantur. Reprobi vero qui carnis affectibus morem gerunt, indurantur & praefra Stiores fiunt. Ut enim homo natura malus est, & legem peccati in membris suis gestat, quae affectibus pessimis illum ad omne scelus abripit: ita praeter verbum Dei frenum nullum est, quod illum in officio continere possit. Si ergo illud homini sordeat, ut eo se regi non sinat, fieri non potest, quin instar effrenis equi, quo illum caeca libido ducit feratur.
units.tr: The evangelist begins with the time, so as to show the occasion on which the adversaries raised this question. He notes the circumstance of time with a single word, saying: Then the Pharisees went away, etc. Namely, when Christ had put forward the parables of the vineyard and the faithless tenants, and likewise that of the marriage feast, in which he pointed out the causes of the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the Gentiles. Matthew has recently taught that the adversaries were exasperated by the first parable of the vineyard, when he said that they sought to seize him, but were prevented from doing so by fear of the crowd; clearly because, convicted by the testimony of their own conscience, they knew they deserved punishment if they dared to attempt anything against him. But when he added the second parable, of the marriage feast, they were more provoked; yet even then a certain fear restrained them, so that they kept their hands off him. Here the difference among hearers of the truth appears. The elect, whom all others call the sheep of Christ, know the voice of their shepherd, and when they hear it they are corrected. The reprobate, however, who indulge the desires of the flesh, are hardened and become more stubborn. For just as man is by nature evil, and carries in his members the law of sin, which by its wicked passions drags him into every crime, so there is no bridle besides the Word of God that can keep him in his duty. If therefore that word becomes distasteful to a man, so that he does not allow himself to be ruled by it, it cannot but happen that he is carried off like an unbridled horse, wherever blind lust leads him.

units.la: Euidentius hoc apparebit, si quinam hanc causam contra Christum egerint, videamus. Pharisaei nominantur, quos passim legimus acerrimos Christi hostes fuisse. Quia enim (ut saepe dixi-mus) propria iustitia sidebant, non poterant eum ferre, qui nobis a Patre iustitia factus est, & quo admisso omnis hominum iustitia euanescit. Coniungunt hi nunc sibi Herodianos, id est, aulicos Herodis, qui quales fuerint ex hero illorum licet colligere. Erat Herodes Antipas homo pro-phanus, voluptatibus deditus, incestus, & qui de mortuorum resurrectione non multo melius quam Sadducaei sentiebat. Cum enim metempsychosin, id est, animarum in alia atque alia corpora transmigratione crederet (ut supra in Ioan. Baptist. historia vidimus) non potuit de corporum resurrectione certum quid aut solidum credere. Quae enim ratio reddi poterit, cur anima, quae in diversis corporibus vixit, huic potius quam illi in resurrectione restituatur? Sui ergo similes aulicos habuit, qui omni religionis fundamento explos carnis libidini serviebant. Interim idonei erant, qui Pharisaeos in praesenti instituto iuuarent, cum non possent non tueri Caesaris partes, a quo Herodes suu regnu siue tetrarchiam quasi precario possideret, & ex illius nutu res administrare cogeretur.
units.tr: This will be more evident if we consider who pleaded this cause against Christ. The Pharisees are named, whom we read everywhere were the bitterest enemies of Christ. For because they trusted in their own righteousness (as I have often said), they could not bear him who has been made righteousness to us by the Father, and in whose presence all human righteousness vanishes. These now join to themselves the Herodians, that is, the courtiers of Herod, whose character may be gathered from that of their master. Herod Antipas was a profane man, given over to pleasures, incestuous, and who thought about the resurrection of the dead not much better than the Sadducees. For since he believed in metempsychosis, that is, the transmigration of souls from one body to another (as we saw above in the history of John the Baptist), he could not believe anything certain or solid about the resurrection of bodies. For what reason could be given why the soul, which lived in various bodies, should be restored in the resurrection to this one rather than that? He therefore had courtiers like himself, who, stripped of every foundation of religion, served the lusts of the flesh. Meanwhile they were fit to help the Pharisees in the present undertaking, since they could not but defend the cause of Caesar, from whom Herod held his kingdom, or tetrarchy, as it were on sufferance, and was obliged to administer affairs at his nod.

units.la: At non temere quis miretur, Pharisaeos sibi socios accersere voluisse, a quorum ingenio, moribus & religione ἁγιωσύνη ... (quod dici solet) dissidebant. Illi enim iustitiae & sanctitatis summa existimatione sibi vendicabant, & simul libertatis patriae acerrimi vindices erant, eo quod sub Alexandra Hircani & Aristobuli matre potentes facti tantum non regnauissent: hi aut (ut modo dixi-mus) quoad mores corruptissimi, adhaec Caesaris amici atque Romanae tyrannidis fautores essent.
units.tr: Yet no one should wonder that the Pharisees wished to summon the Herodians as allies, although they differed from them in disposition, manners and religion, in holiness [ἁγιωσύνη] (as it is commonly called). For the Pharisees claimed for themselves the highest reputation for righteousness and sanctity, and at the same time were the fiercest champions of the freedom of their country, because under Alexandra, the mother of Hyrcanus and Aristobulus, they had become powerful and had almost ruled. The Herodians, on the other hand, were (as I have just said) most corrupt in morals, and moreover were friends of Caesar and supporters of Roman tyranny.

units.la: Sed non est quod huc Syncretismu aut collusione inter istos admiremur: Etenim hoc ingenium est hominum impiorum, ut in studiis externis nunquam possint inter se convenire, dum quisque alteri praesta re cupit. At in veritatis oppressione omnes facile consentiunt, quia huius lucem omnes ex aequo oderunt. Sic paulo post Sadducaeos ferunt Pharisaei, qui mortuorum resurrectione aperte negabat, quasi sublata religio non poterit consistere. Sed ut ad Christum capiendum Sacerdotes cum suis servis & militibus convenisse Luc. annotauit, ita inter Pilatum & Herodem amicitia noua coaluisse scribit, quando de Christo extinguendo agebatur, ut in eo alius alij gratificaretur, cum prius inimici essent. Et in historia Ecclesiastica legimus Iulianum apostatam cum Iudaeis coiuraui sse aduersus Christum, ut hunc mendacij convincere, & omne eius verbis fide derogare posset. Et hodie inter principes similia exempla sunt, quorum aliquos non pudet cum Turcis pace sancire, aut inducias facere, ut interea coiunctis viribus Ecclesia Christi possint opprimere. Quis deniq; non videt monachos, qui mundo mortui videri volunt, in castris versari, & inter armatas militum acies volitare, ut ali qua veritatis extinguendae occasione inveniant? Sed ex eo agnoscamus Euangelij veritate, quando aduersus hanc solam conspirant, qui abfurdissimas quasque opiniones ferre possunt. Interim vigilemus ferio, neq; ex impiorum dissidijs nobis aliquid boni polliceamur. Deo aut fidamus, qui coiurationes eiusmodi facile dissipat, & gentium consilia (ut Psaltes canit) euertit, ipsius aut consilium durat in aeternum. Factum hoc nostro saeculo saepius, & adhuc viuit & regnat Deus ille & Dominus exercituum, cuius regnum nullis hominum viribus potest labefactari.
units.tr: But there is no reason for us to be surprised here at a syncretism or collusion between these men. For it is the nature of impious men that they can never agree with one another in outward pursuits, since each wishes to surpass the other. But in the suppression of the truth they all readily agree, because they all hate its light equally. So shortly afterwards the Pharisees bring in the Sadducees, who openly denied the resurrection of the dead, as though, if religion were abolished, it could not stand. But just as Luke noted that the priests came together with their servants and soldiers to seize Christ, so Luke also writes that a new friendship arose between Pilate and Herod, when the extinction of Christ was at issue, so that each might gratify the other, though before they had been enemies. And in the ecclesiastical history we read that Julian the Apostate conspired with the Jews against Christ, so that he might convict him of falsehood and be able to detract from all faith in his words. And today among princes there are similar examples, some of whom are not ashamed to make peace or truces with the Turks, so that meanwhile the Church of Christ may be crushed by their united forces. Who finally does not see monks, who wish to seem dead to the world, living in camps and flitting among the armed battle lines of soldiers, so as to find some occasion for extinguishing the truth? But from this let us recognise the truth of the Gospel, since those who can bear the most absurd opinions of every kind conspire against this alone. Meanwhile let us watch diligently, and let us promise ourselves nothing good from the dissensions of the impious. Let us trust in God, who easily scatters such conspiracies and overthrows the counsels of the nations (as the Psalmist sings), while his own counsel endures for ever. This has happened more than once in our own age, and that God and Lord of hosts still lives and reigns, whose kingdom can be shaken by no powers of men.

units.la: Sed praestat modu quoq; & ordine videre, quae isti in hac actione contra Dominum secuti sunt. Primo consilium inierunt, ut ipsum illa quaeret in sermone. Nihil ergo temere aut incosulto faciunt. Sunt enim filij huius saeculi prudentiores filijs lucis in sua generatione, & Daniel Antichristo oculos hominum, id est, astutiam & diligentia in rebus agendis tribuit. Dauid etiam etsi reges & principes terrae fremere dicat & vim parare, qua Christi iugum excutiant, tamen eosdem simul conuenire & meditari ait, quomodo effectum dent quod volunt. Finis autem illis propositus est, ut eu illaqueent in sermone, id est, eo deducant, ut aliquid incautius dicat, cuius occasione ipsum vel potestati praesidis tradere, vel populo inuisum & exosum facere possint. Deinde non ipsi accedunt ad Dominum, qui hactenus aperti hostes fuerant. Sed ut melius lateant mittunt e ad eum discipulos suos, & ex his non quosuis, sed insidiatores, ut Lucas tradit, qui se iustos & veritatis amantes simularent, quibus Herodianos, ut modo diximus, coniungunt. Et hi mirifice dolum atq; insidias possunt tegere. Nam non solum iustitiae & pietatis studium simulant, veruntamen quasi ipsius obseruantissimi sint, omnes boni ac fidi doctoris partes ei tribuunt. Nam ita eum compellant: Praeceptor, scimus te veracem esse, & viam Dei in veritate docere, nec quenquam curare: non enim respicis in personam hominum, &c. Praeceptorem dicendo se ipsius discipulos esse profitentur. Quid quid aliud erat, quam Pharisaismum abnegare? Et mirum est, illos de boni doctoris officio tam bene posse differere. Primo dicunt, scimus te veracem esse. Est hoc praecipua doctoris virtus. Quis enim fidem habeat homini vano & mendaci? Aut quis sperat eum de diuinis & caelestibus vera dicere, qui de iis quae omnibus nota sunt, mentiri non veretur? Deinde via Dei doceat. Dicitur sic vniuersa huius vitae & salutis aeternae ratio, quae Dei verbo traditur. Dei autem via dicitur, quia ad Deum deducit, & quod non satis sit eam tenere, sed ut in ea ambulemus necesse est. Ideo sancti precantur: Vias tuas notas mihi fac Domine, & aßuefacito me semitis tuis. Duc me in veritate tua: Doce me viam decretorum tuorum: Fac me incedere per semitam praeceptorum tuorum. Hanc ergo viam monstret doctor, & quia haec non alibi quam in Dei verbo inueniuntur, hoc unum praedicet, non sua aut aliorum hominum commenta sive traditiones, quibus nequicquam Deus colitur. Deinde in veritate doceat hanc viam, id est, recte & ita ut aedificationi auditorum seruiat, ne de illo dici possit, quod Isaias de sui seculi impostoribus queritur: populi mi, qui te dirigunt, aut beatum dicunt, sed ducentes sunt, & iter seminarum tuarum deprauant. Faciunt hoc qui gratiam Dei & salutem pollicentur iis, quibus correptione opus erat, & (ut apud Ezechielem de quibusdam dicitur) puluillos consuunt, quibus suauiter indormiant, qui ferijs admonitionibus ad resipiscentiae studium debebant excitari: E contra vero religionem sibi ipsis quasdam faciunt, & bellum contra eos sanctificant, qui non dederunt in os ipsorum. Vt vero possit in veritate doceri, ne esse est, ne quenquam curet doctor, nec in cuiusquam personam respiciat. Etenim qui id faciunt & hominibus placere volunt, ij Dei serui esse non possunt. Semper enim occurret, quod illos vel metu vel lucri spe transfuerfos abripiat. Meminerint ergo, se Dei seruos esse, apud quem non est personarum respectus. Deinde publicos esse & communes omnis loci & ordinis hominum doctores, quos toti suae domui praefecerit Dominus, & proinde non posse ab ipsis quenquam negligi abiicere, sed singulos doceri, admoneri, arguique ac corripi oportere, ut ea omnibus dicantur, quae ipsorum emendationi atq; saluti seruiunt. Et talem quidem constat fuisse Christum, de quo olim Propheta dixerat, Non est inuentus dolus in ore eius. Et ipse acerrimus suis hostibus dicere non verebatur: Quis ex vobis arguet me de peccato? Et quamuis ad eam perfectionem, quae in illo fuit, nemini mortalium pertingere detur, ut nullo vel dicto vel facto labatur, quoad doctrinam tamen anniti decet Ecclesiarum ministros, ut illa ipsis syncera sit, & nullo fuco adulteretur. Caeterum ut ad Christi aduersarios redeamus, in quem finem illi ista dicunt? Num ut eum sibi commendent?
