units.la: Rabbi a multitudine dicitur, & excellentem omni virtutis & doctrinae genere significat, qui unus multorum instar sit. Fuit ergo titulus hic nimium insolens & ambitiosus.
units.tr: Rabbi is said by the multitude, and signifies one who excels in every kind of virtue and learning, who alone is equal to many. This title was therefore exceedingly unusual and ambitious.

units.la: Turpe autem est, eos qui IESV CHRISTI ferui dicuntur, ipsa se exinaniuit forma serui accepta, ut nos in dignitatem caelestem eueheret. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: It is shameful, then, that those who are called servants of Jesus Christ should seek honours and titles of dignity; he who emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, so that he might raise us to heavenly dignity. To him belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY 266.

units.la: Vos autem ne vocemini Rabbi. Vnus enim est vester doctor, Christus: omnes autem vos fratres estis. Et patrem vestrum nemi-nem vocetis in terra: vnus est enim Pater vester, qui est in coelis. Ne vocemini doctores: vnus enim vester est doctor, nempe Christus: sed qui maximus est vestrum, sit minister vester. Porro qui se exaltet, deprimetur: & qui se demiserit, exaltetur.
units.tr: But you, do not be called Rabbi. For one is your teacher, Christ, and you are all brothers. And call no one on earth your father, for one is your Father, who is in heaven. Do not be called teachers, for one is your teacher, namely Christ. But whoever is greatest among you, let him be your minister. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

units.la: QVoniam omnes homines in peccato concepti & nati, atq; idcirco natura ad errores & pec-cata proclives sunt, nullus error tam absurdus, nullum delictum tam graue & atrox est, quod non in vnumquemq; nostrum cadere possit, si suam gratiam nobis subducat Deus, & nos se-curi nimis propriam salutem negligamus. Quapropter multa institutione & assiduis etiam admo-nitionibus est opus, nec sufficit, vt in Ecclesia manifesti errores & vitia eorum accusentur, qui Ve-ritati palam aduersantur, verumetiam pios & germanos Dei cultores admoneri oportet, vt ab ijsdem sibi caueant, nec malis aliorum exemplis se decipi aut seduci sinant. Hoc ordine fere Do-minus noster IESVS CHRISTVS in docendo vtitur. Exemplum illius euidens habetur hoc loco, quem modo recitauimus. Nuper enim grauiter monuit, vt Scribas & Pharisaeos, quoad recta docent, audiant quidem & ijs obediant, caueant autem sibi diligenter, ne eorum de mores aut ex-emplum imitentur. Rationes adiecit graues & necessarias, inter quas praecipua est, quod quacunq; faciunt, non in alium finem faciant, quam vt spectentur ab hominibus, & idcirco quando optimi & sanctissimi sunt, hypocritas esse, qui Deo & hominibus fucum facere conentur, & ambitione in tolerabili se aliis praeferant, dum in conuiuijs primos accubitus, in conuentibus sacris suprema subsellia appetunt, & titulis magnificis compellari volunt, & Rabbini dici, quasi omni eruditio-nis, doctrinae, pietatis & sanctitatis genere ita instructi sint, vt singuli multorum instar foli alijs omnibus erudiendis sufficiant. His in praesenti admonitionem grauem subtexit, qua quod de Scri-bis & Pharisaeis dixit, discipulis suis applicat, quos ab ambitioso illo gloriae priuata studio dehor-tatur. Omissis autem aut praeteritis ijs, quae de phylacteriis & fimbriis, de praesidentia item in con-uiuijs aut publicis coetibus dixerat, hoc repetit quod de titulis magnificis dictum fuit, eo quod his potissimum populo simplici imponebant, qui illorum magnifico splendore fascinatus, nefas esse putabat, si in aliquo contradicerent ijs, qui publice pro Rabbinis & Ecclesiae columnis agno-scebantur.
units.tr: Since all men are conceived and born in sin, and are therefore by nature prone to errors and sins, no error is so absurd and no offence so grave and atrocious that it cannot fall upon each one of us, if God withdraws his grace from us and we become too careless and neglect our own salvation. For this reason much instruction and constant admonition are needed. It is not enough that the manifest errors and vices of those who openly oppose the truth be denounced in the Church; the godly and true worshippers of God must also be warned to be on their guard against such people, and not allow themselves to be deceived or seduced by the bad examples of others. The Lord Jesus Christ generally uses this method in teaching, and a clear example of it is found in the passage we have just recited. For he recently gave a serious warning that the Scribes and Pharisees, insofar as they teach what is right, should indeed be heard and obeyed, but that people should take careful heed not to imitate their morals or example. He added weighty and necessary reasons, among which the chief is that whatever they do, they do for no other end than to be seen by men. Therefore, although they are at their most excellent and holy, they are hypocrites who try to deceive God and men, and with intolerable ambition set themselves above others: at banquets they seek the first couches, in sacred assemblies the highest seats; they want to be addressed with magnificent titles and to be called Rabbis, as if they were equipped with every kind of learning, doctrine, piety and holiness, so that each one alone sufficed to teach all others. To this he now adds a grave admonition, by which he applies to his disciples what he had said of the Scribes and Pharisees, and dissuades them from that ambitious private pursuit of glory. Passing over or setting aside what he had said about phylacteries and fringes, and likewise about precedence at banquets or public gatherings, he repeats what was said about magnificent titles, because these were especially imposed on the simple people, who, dazzled by their splendour, thought it wrong to contradict in anything those who were publicly acknowledged as Rabbis and pillars of the Church.

units.la: Dicit ergo: Vos autem ne vocemini Rabbi. Nec superuacanea videri debet admonitio ista apud Apostolos, qui habebant vitam priuatam egerant, nec a quoquam hoc titulo appellabantur. Etenim ex primis parentibus insitus est omnibus ambitionis affectus, quo fit, vt supra alios emi-nere cupiant, & illos iampridem eodem infectos & titillatos fuisse, ex contentionibus & rixis appa-ret, quae non semel inter ipsos exortae fuerunt. Ideo eos ne quid huius affectent, dehortatur. Vbi an-te omnia obseruari debet, de quibus titulis agatur. De Scribis & Pharisaeis sermo est, qui in Ec-clesia magisterium & dictaturam quodammodo sibi vendicabant. Ergo non debet extra institu-tum Christi hoc trahi, quasi nefas sit eos, qui in Magistratu Senatoria aut Tribunitia dignitate or-nati sunt, magistros aut dominos dicere, prout vulgo in aliqua gente receptum est. Nec etiam pro-hibetur, ne quis in ea arte, quam profitetur, magister dicatur, aut ne seruus herum suum honoratio-re nomine compellet. Imo vt qui in Ecclesia publice docent, doctores dicantur, non vetat Domi-nus: quod Diuum Paulum intellexisse constat, qui seipsum doctorem gentium dixit, eo quod ipsum gentibus Apostolum & Euangelij sui praeconem Christus destinauisset. Sed admonitionis istius sensus est, ne quis in religionis & aeternae salutis causa sibi eum honorem & authoritatem vendicet, quasi pro suo arbitrio Ecclesiae praescribere, & vicissim ipsi omnes simpliciter credere & obedire debeant. Et hunc sensum rationes quoq; nobis commendant, quibus dictum hoc Dominus confirmat. Prima est: Vnus enim est vester doctor, CHRISTVS. Altera, Omnes autem vos fratres estis.
units.tr: He therefore says: But you, do not be called Rabbi. Nor should this admonition seem superfluous among the Apostles, who lived private lives and were called by no one by this title. For ambition is implanted in all men from our first parents, so that they desire to stand out above others; and that these men had long been infected and tickled by this passion is clear from the quarrels and strife which arose among them more than once. Therefore he dissuades them from aiming at anything of this kind. Here, above all, it must be observed what kind of titles are meant. The discussion concerns the Scribes and Pharisees, who in a way claimed for themselves the teaching office and domination in the Church. Therefore this should not be drawn beyond the institution of Christ, as if it were wrong to call those who are adorned with a senatorial or tribunal dignity in the magistracy "masters" or "lords", as is commonly accepted in some nations. Nor is it forbidden for anyone to be called "master" in the art which he professes, or for a servant to address his master with an honorific name. Rather, the Lord does not forbid that those who publicly teach in the Church be called teachers; and it is evident that the divine Paul understood it this way, who called himself a teacher of the Gentiles, because Christ had appointed him an Apostle to the Gentiles and a herald of his Gospel. But the sense of this admonition is that no one should claim for himself that honour and authority in matters of religion and eternal salvation, as if he could prescribe to the Church at his own discretion, and in turn all should simply believe and obey him. The reasons that the Lord gives to confirm this saying also commend this sense to us. The first is: For one is your teacher, Christ. The second: And you are all brothers.

units.la: {y} 1. Tim. 1. estis. Priori omnem hanc authoritatem sibi soli vendicat Dominus, nec id iniuria. Ipse enim est magnus ille & catholicus Propheta, quem olim Moses promisit, & cui obedire iussit omnes, qui excindi nolunt ex populo Dei: & de quo Isaias quoq; vaticinatus est. De eodem etiam vox Patris coelitus intonuit: Ipsum audite. In ipso vno absconditi sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ ac cogni-tionis. Nemo igitur se Rabbinū aut Ecclesiæ doctorem absolutè dicere potest, quin Filio Dei IE-SV CHRISTO iniuriam faciat, cuius honorem in se transfert, qui suam gloriam se alij dare nē-gat. Violatur præterea Christiana fraternitatis vinculum, si qui illis superbè dominari velit, quos pro fratribus agnoscere debebat. Ideo Apostolus, etsi se doctore gentium a Christo constitutum sci-ret, tamen diligenter cauit ad Corinthios scribens, ne alicuius fidei dominari velle putaretur. Nam cum dixisset, se ideo hucusq; non venisse ad ipsos, vt ipsis parceret, mox quasi per Correctionē subiungit: Non quòd dominemur vestræ fidei, sed quòd administri simus gaudij vestri. Quasi di-ceret: Nemo quod dixi ita accipiat, quasi pro meo iure possim apud vos in religione & salutis causa quiduis statuere. Scio enim me Christi administrum modò esse, qui vos consolari & in fide e-rigere debeam. In quam sententiam alibi quoq; dicit, se potestatem a Deo accepisse ad ædificatio-nem, non autem ad euersionem ipsorum. Vehementer ergo peccant ministri, qui se ipse nimium esse-rendo sibi arrogant quod vnius Christi est. Sunt hi Sacerdotum similes, quos persidus colonus con-fert ille, qui herilem filium impiè occisum extra vineam eiecerunt. Nec minus ab ijs peccatur, qui tales ministros sibi accersunt, & eosdem stolida admiratione & ineptis laudibus infolentiores red-dunt, dum omnia quæ ab illis proueniunt, absq; delectu & iudicio approbant, adeoq; ab ipsis deno-minari volunt. Fuit hæc semper causa sectarum in Ecclesia, sicuti Corinthiorū exemplo admone-mur. Ita ergo in Ecclesia ministri versari debent, vt se non dominos, sed administros eorum, quæ Christus nobis meruit, esse meminerint: & eosdem ita obseruare & colere debent qui in Ecclesia sunt, vt IESV CHRISTO sua authoritas integra maneat, qui princeps pastorum est, cuius vo-cem ita agnoscere & sequi debent oues, vt ad eandem omnes doctrinas probent, neq; aliquem au-diant, quàm ex cuius ore summi illius pastoris vocem prodire intelligunt. Quotquot enim intra hos fines sese non continent, ij Ecclesiarum turbatores sunt, & Christo iniuriam faciunt, sibiipsis vero exitium accersunt. Quia ergo hæc res tanti momenti est, vt totius Ecclesiæ salus ex ea de-pendeat, idem huius admonitionis membrum postea repetet Dominus, secundò dicens: Ne vocemi-ni doctores: vnus enim vester est doctor, nempe CHRISTVS: quod ita ab illo dicitur, vt diser-tè eos etiam suo magisterio subijciat, qui in Ecclesia docendi munere funguntur. Summa igitur huius loci esto, neminem magistrum aut doctorem alia ratione dici debere, quàm quatenus in illo Christus loquitur.
units.tr: 1. Tim. 1. Brothers. By the first, the Lord claims all this authority for himself alone, and not without right. For he is that great and catholic Prophet whom Moses long ago promised, and to whom he commanded all to listen who did not wish to be cut off from the people of God; and of whom Isaiah also prophesied. The voice of the Father also thundered from heaven concerning the same one: Hear him. In him alone are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Therefore no one can absolutely call himself a rabbi or teacher of the Church without doing wrong to the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whose honour he transfers to himself, since he refuses to give his glory to another. Moreover, the bond of Christian brotherhood is violated if someone wishes to lord it proudly over those whom he ought to acknowledge as brothers. Therefore the Apostle, although he knew that he had been appointed by Christ as teacher of the Gentiles, nevertheless took care, writing to the Corinthians, that he not be thought to want to lord it over anyone's faith. For after saying that he had not yet come to them for the reason that he might spare them, he immediately adds by way of correction: Not that we lord it over your faith, but that we are workers for your joy. As if to say: let no one take what I have said as if by my own right I could decree anything among you in matters of religion and salvation. For I know that I am now only a minister of Christ, who ought to comfort you and raise you up in faith. To the same effect he says elsewhere that he had received power from God for building up, not for tearing down, them. Therefore ministers sin gravely when, by exalting themselves too much, they arrogate to themselves what belongs to Christ alone. They are like the priests whom that faithless tenant resembles, who threw out of the vineyard and killed the son of the master. Nor do those sin less who summon such ministers to themselves, and by foolish admiration and silly praises make them more arrogant, while they approve without discrimination or judgment everything that comes from them, and even wish to be named after them. This has always been the cause of sects in the Church, as we are warned by the example of the Corinthians. Thus ministers ought to conduct themselves in the Church so that they remember they are not lords of it but servants of those things which Christ has merited for us; and those who are in the Church ought to observe and honour them in such a way that the authority of Jesus Christ remains intact, for he is the chief of shepherds, whose voice the sheep ought to recognise and follow, so that they test all doctrines by it, and hear no one except the one from whose mouth they understand the voice of that supreme Shepherd to come. For whoever does not keep within these bounds are troublers of the Churches; they do wrong to Christ and bring destruction upon themselves. Therefore, since this matter is of such great importance that the salvation of the whole Church depends on it, the Lord repeats this part of his admonition afterwards, saying a second time: Do not be called teachers; for one is your teacher, namely Christ. He says this in such a way that he plainly subjects to his own teaching even those who fulfil the office of teaching in the Church. The sum of this passage, therefore, is that no one should be called master or teacher except insofar as Christ speaks through him.

units.la: Addit hïs aliud membrum, quod est: Et patrem vestrum neminem vocetis in terra: Vnus enim est pater vester, qui est in cælis. Quod similiter non eo sensu accipi debet, quasi parentum nomen inter homines abolere velit, quod Deus Pater in Lege confirmauit, dicens: Honora pa-trem tuum & matrem tuam, vt sis longæuus super terram, quam dat tibi Dominus Deus tuus. Itaq; hoc quoq; ad fidei & salutis æternæ causam restringi debet, ne in hac nobis aliquem patris loco honorandum accersamus, quàm Deum, qui solus Pater est, ex quo πᾶσα πατρια, id est, to-ta parentela siue cognatio & familia Ecclesiæ, quæ ex omnibus gentibus collesta est in Christo de-nominatur. Vt enim ex Adami filijs Dei filij efficiamur, regeneratione opus est, sine qua (vt Chri-stus Nicodemo dicebat) nemo videbit regnum Dei. Nihil autem in hoc mysterio tribui potest hominum industriæ aut viribus. Quomodo enim vel seipsum vel alios regenerabit homo, qui ne sia-tura quidem corporis sui aliquid addere, aut pilum capitis sui nigrum aut album facere potest? Et Isaias olim de Ecclesia & filiorum Dei generatione vaticinans, illam peperisse ait, priusquam parturiret, aut ὠδῖνας sentiret, id est, dolores, qui partu solent præcedere, & mox exclamat: Quis audiuit huic simile? quis huic simile vidit? Ita nimirum docens, mysterium hoc non vires modò hominis, sed captum quoq; ingenij humani excedere, neq; exempla aliqua in rerum natura extare quibus demonstrari aut confirmari possit. Inexcusabilis ergo fuerit eorum confidentia, qui se pa-tres dici velint filiorum Dei, imprudentia vero & ingratitudo detestabilis, si quis tantum Dei be-neficium homini mortali tribuat.
units.tr: He adds to these another clause: "And call no one your father on earth, for one is your Father, who is in heaven." This likewise must not be taken to mean that he wants to abolish the name of parents among men, a name which God the Father confirmed in the Law when he said: "Honour your father and your mother, that you may live long upon the earth, which the Lord your God gives you." Therefore this too must be restricted to the cause of faith and eternal salvation, so that we do not summon anyone else to the place of a father in this matter to be honoured, other than God, who alone is Father. From him every family [πᾶσα πατριά], that is, the whole kinship, lineage and household of the Church gathered from all nations in Christ, takes its name. For us to become children of God from the sons of Adam, regeneration is needed, without which (as Christ told Nicodemus) no one will see the kingdom of God. Yet nothing in this mystery can be attributed to human effort or strength. For how can a man regenerate himself or others, when he cannot add so much as a cubit to his stature, or make one hair of his head black or white? Isaiah too, long ago prophesying about the Church and the begetting of the children of God, says that she gave birth before she was in labour or felt the pains [ὠδῖνας], that is, the pangs that usually precede childbirth, and soon cries out: "Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen anything like it?" He thus teaches that this mystery surpasses not only human strength but also the grasp of the human mind, and that there are no examples of it in nature by which it could be demonstrated or confirmed. Therefore the confidence of those who wish to be called fathers of the children of God is inexcusable, and their folly and ingratitude are detestable if anyone attributes so great a benefit of God to a mortal man.

units.la: Neq; hi nobis aliquis Paulum obijciat, qui se Corinthios in CHRISTO IESV per Euan- gelium genuisse scribit, & idcirco se patrem illorum dicit, non pædagogum, quales erant reliqui do- ctores, qui se inter ipsos insolentius efferebant. Et alibi Galatis ait: Filioli mei, quos iterum par- turio, vsque quo formetur Christus in vobis. Ista enim ratione ministerij dicuntur, quo Deus in- filijs suis generandis atq; formandis vtitur, ita tamen, vt ipse suo Spiritu in ferus suis agat. Quod ipsum Paulus non obscure fatetur, cum se illos genuisse dicit in CHRISTO IESV per Euan- gelium. Et alibi cum dixisset, se plus quam alios omnes laborasse, per Correctionem se expo- nens addit: Non ego tamen, sed gratia Dei qua mecum est: nimirum quod sciret nihil esse eos, qui plantant & rigant, sed gloriam omnem vni Deo deberi, qui dat incrementum. Et hoc sensu vere res & orthodoxos Ecclesiæ Scriptores Pauli locum cum Christi verbis conciliauisse, ex D. Augustino apparet, qui in Breuiculo Collationum cum Donatistis scribit, hoc inter alia etiam Pauli verba ad Corinthios adduxisse, quasi hic Christi verbis, quæ hic habentur, contradixerit, quibus Catholici & orthodoxi ita respondunt, hoc honorificentia causa dictum propter euangelicum ministerium, quod disponsabat Apostolus. Nam patrem ad fidem salutem & æternam non esse, nisi Deum: neq; enim posset contrarium Christo Apostolus loqui, vt cum ille diceret: Ne vobis dicatis patrem in terra: vnus enim pater vester, Deus: contra Apostolus tanquam resistens verbis Christi, patrem se diceret eorum, quibus annuntiauerat Euangelium, nisi esset vtiq; distinguendum, quid diuina gratia, quid humana honorificentia causa dicere-tur, &c. Et in expositione Psal. 77. idem Augustinus scribit: Deus vnus pater, qui regnat Spiritu Sancto, quos facit filios ad æter- nam hæreditatem. At honoris gratia propter ætatem curam & pietatis patres aliqui dicuntur. Item quod Christus dixit: Ne vobis dicatis patrem in terra: vnus enim pater vester, Deus: non dictum est, vt hoc vocabulum honoris humani de loquendi consuetudine tolleretur, sed ne gratia Dei, qua in æternam vitam regeneramur, natura vel potestati, vel etiam sanctitati cuiusquam hominis tribueretur. Ideo cum diceret Paulus: Ego vos genui, prædixit, IN CHRISTO, & per Euangelium, ne ipsius esse putaretur, quod Dei est. Hæc omnia Augustinus adducere libuit, vt vi- deas non solum Scripturis, verumetiam veteris Ecclesiæ & Patrum orthodoxorum testimonijs confutari Monachos, qui contra disertum Christi mandatum in causa religionis & fidei patres sibi nouos accersunt, quorum seruitio & obedientia se mancipant, & quos peregrino nomine Abbates, id est, patres vocant. Hoc certe olim D. Hieronymo ita displicuit, vt in suis in Epistolam ad Galatas Commentarijs non veritus sit scribere: Cum ABBA pater Hebræo Syro sermone dicatur, & Dominus noster in Euangelio præcipiat, nullum patrem vocandum nisi Deum, nescio qua licentia in monasterijs vel vocemus hoc nomine alios, vel vocari nos acquiescamus, &c. En licentiam dicit Hieronymus id, in quo hodie plerique summam sanctitatem, & Christiana religionis colophonem constituere arbitrantur. Nec tamen illo tempore Monachorum luxus & fastus eò vsque excreuerant, vt viris principibus intolerabiles essent, quemadmodum hodie fieri constat. At nos procul relictis illis Penelopes sponsis, ab vno Deo Patre pendeamus, qui Filium suum Vnigenitum pro nobis Filium hominis fieri, & in mundum venire voluit, vt nos in filiorum suorum libertatem transferret, & per hunc nobis arrhabonem salutis dedit Spiritu adoptionis, in quo clamamus, Abba Pater. Ex eo igitur consolationem petamus, si qua tentatio grauior incidit. Qui enim sub dulcissimo patris nomine a nobis inuocari vult, procul dubio nos pro filijs suis dilectis agnoscet, & indulgentissimi patris instar nostri miserebitur, memor scilicet nos ex puluere creatos, & infirma aut fictilia vasa esse, qua indulgenter tractari oporteat. Interim meminerimus etiam nos fratres esse, & depositā inuidia & odio fraternam charitatem alij erga alios colamus: qua certissima nota est, ex qua discipulos suos agnosci, Christus testatur. Ioan.13.
units.tr: Nor let anyone object Paul to us, who writes that he begot the Corinthians in Christ Jesus through the gospel, and therefore calls himself their father, not their tutor, as the other teachers were, who puffed themselves up more arrogantly among them. And elsewhere he says to the Galatians: "My little children, for whom I am again in labour until Christ is formed in you." For in this sense they are called fathers by virtue of the ministry, through which God uses them to beget and form his children, yet in such a way that he himself works in his children by his Spirit. Paul himself does not obscurely confess this when he says that he begot them in Christ Jesus through the gospel. And elsewhere, after saying that he had laboured more than all the others, he explains himself by way of correction and adds: "Yet not I, but the grace of God which is with me." Doubtless he knew that those who plant and water are nothing, but all glory is due to God alone, who gives the increase. That the true and orthodox writers of the ancient Church reconciled Paul's words with the words of Christ in this sense appears from Augustine, who in the Breviculus of the Collations with the Donatists writes that the Donatists brought forward, among other things, these words of Paul to the Corinthians, as if they contradicted the words of Christ found here. To this the Catholics and orthodox replied that it was said for the sake of honour, on account of the evangelical ministry which the Apostle administered. For no one is a father for faith and salvation except God. The Apostle could not speak contrary to Christ, so as to say, in resistance to Christ's words "Call no one father on earth, for one is your Father, God," that he was father of those to whom he had preached the gospel. Rather, it must be distinguished what is said by divine grace and what by human honour, and so on. And in the exposition of Psalm 77, the same Augustine writes: "God is the one Father, who reigns with the Holy Spirit, and makes sons for the eternal inheritance. But for the sake of honour, some are called fathers on account of age, care and piety." Likewise, when Christ said "Call no one father on earth, for one is your Father, God," this was not said to remove this word of human honour from the custom of speech, but so that the grace of God, by which we are regenerated to eternal life, should not be attributed to the nature, power, or even holiness of any man. Therefore when Paul said "I begot you," he added IN CHRIST and through the gospel, lest it be thought that what belongs to God was his own. I have wished to adduce all these things from Augustine so that you may see that the monks are refuted not only by the Scriptures but also by the testimonies of the ancient Church and the orthodox Fathers. Against Christ's express command, in matters of religion and faith they summon for themselves new fathers, to whose service and obedience they surrender themselves, and whom they call by a foreign name, Abbots, that is, fathers. This certainly once displeased St Jerome so much that in his Commentaries on the Epistle to the Galatians he did not hesitate to write: "Since ABBA means father in the Hebrew and Syriac tongue, and our Lord commands in the Gospel that no one be called father but God, I do not know by what licence we in monasteries call others by this name, or consent to be so called ourselves," and so on. See, Jerome calls licence that in which most people today think the highest holiness and the crown of the Christian religion consists. Yet at that time the luxury and pride of the monks had not yet grown so far as to be intolerable to princely men, as is known to happen today. But let us, leaving far behind those suitors of Penelope, depend on the one God the Father, who willed that his Only-begotten Son should become a Son of man for us and come into the world, so that he might transfer us into the freedom of his sons, and through him gave us the pledge of salvation, the Spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, "Abba, Father." Let us therefore seek consolation from him if any heavier temptation befalls us. For he who wishes to be invoked by us under the sweet name of Father will undoubtedly acknowledge us as his beloved sons, and will have mercy on us as a most indulgent father, mindful that we were created from dust and are frail or earthen vessels, which ought to be handled gently. Meanwhile let us remember that we too are brothers, and, laying aside envy and hatred, let us cultivate fraternal love towards one another. This is the most certain mark by which Christ testifies that his disciples are known. John 13.

units.la: At ne quis putaret, Christum æqualitatem inter suos discipulos eiusmodi fanciuisse, qua omne discrimen personarum aboleat, adeò vt nemo alijs dignitate aut potentia vel authoritate superior aut præstantior censeri debeat, breui dicto amplius nos officij admonet, dicens: Qui maximus est vestrum, sit minister vester. Duo comprehendit, qua in hac causa probè obseruari debent. Primum est, fraternitatem illam, quæ inter Christianos est, nō abolere dignitates ordinarias, quæ alios alijs præstantiores aut superiores faciunt. Nam etsi idem omnium Spiritus sit (vt Paulus loius loquitur) discrimina tamen donorum sunt, & alius alio plus accipit, sicuti in talentorum para- bola Christus docebit. Ita licet idem sit Dominus, discrimina tamen ministeriorum sunt: & quàm- uis unus idem Deus sit, qui in quibusuis agit, discrimina tamen sunt facultatum. Qua causa est, quod in praesenti Christus de eo loquitur, qui inter discipulos suos sit maximus. At quomodo possit quis alijs maior, aut omnium maximus dici, si omnes pares aut aequales essent? Est hoc observandum, quia Christiana fraternitatis praetextu multi semper abusi sunt ad immunitatem & licentiam, quae ijs fraudi effet, quos Deus in gradum altiorem exaltavit. Sic olim serui heri rebelles fuerunt, & excussò iugo liberos se esse clamabant Christi beneficio: indignum ergo & iniquum esse, ut qui Filij Dei liberti sint, hominibus seruiant. Contra quos multa de seruorum officio scripserunt Apostoli. Et hodie Anabaptistae, furiosum hominum genus & turbandi Rebusque natum, libertatem Christianam in eo consistere, sed eius egregios vindices esse arbitrantur, si abs quo om- ni persona aut dignitatis respectu viros principes & alios qui in magistratu ad Rempub. gubernan- tula sedent, fratres dicant, & officia quaeque, etiam sordidissima, ab illis exigant, ipsi autem quae illis debentur, impudenter negent. Atqui non ita vult Christus Dominus. Nam quia ipsius regnum non est ex hoc mundo, ita huius mundi regna & horum iura atque leges minimè abrogavit: quae causa est, ob quam Apostolus vnumquemque in qua vocatione vocatus fuit, in ea manere iubet. Nec ferri debent, qui sub religionis praetextu vel Reipublicae ordinem vel familias turbant.
units.tr: But lest anyone think that Christ decreed such an equality among his disciples as would abolish every distinction of persons, so that no one could be deemed superior or more eminent than others in dignity, power or authority, he warns us of duty in a brief further saying: "Whoever is greatest among you, let him be your minister." It contains two points which must be carefully observed in this matter. The first is that the brotherhood which exists among Christians does not abolish the ordinary dignities which make some more eminent or superior to others. For although the Spirit is the same for all (as Paul says elsewhere), there are nevertheless differences of gifts, and one receives more than another, as Christ will teach in the parable of the talents. So although the Lord is the same, there are nevertheless differences of ministries; and although it is one and the same God who works in all, there are nevertheless differences of abilities. For this reason Christ now speaks of the one who is greatest among his disciples. But how could anyone be greater than others, or be called the greatest of all, if all were equal or alike? This must be noted, because many have always abused the pretext of Christian brotherhood to claim immunity and licence, to the detriment of those whom God has raised to a higher rank. Thus formerly rebellious slaves, having shaken off the yoke, cried out that they were free by Christ's benefit, and that it was unworthy and unjust for those who are free sons of God to serve men. Against them the Apostles wrote much about the duty of servants. Today the Anabaptists, a furious kind of men born for disturbance and upheaval, think that Christian liberty consists in this, and they reckon themselves its distinguished champions if, with no regard to person or dignity, they call princes and other men who sit in magistracy to govern the commonwealth "brothers," demand from them every duty, even the most menial, while themselves shamelessly deny what is owed to those men. But the Lord Christ does not will this. For since his kingdom is not of this world, he by no means abrogated the kingdoms of this world and their rights and laws. This is why the Apostle bids each one remain in the calling in which he was called. Nor should those be tolerated who, under the pretext of religion, disturb the order of the commonwealth or of families.

units.la: Interim (quod alterum est huius loci aut dicti membrum) docet Dominus, quid eos deceat, qui alijs praesunt. Qui maximus est (inquit) inter vos, sit vester minister. Idem alibi etiam dixit, & in vltima Coena hoc non verbis modò ijsdem fere repetijt, verumetiam proprio exemplo confirmauit, cum discipulorum & seruorum pedes ipse eorum magister & dominus abluerit. In praesenti sensu verborum Christi est: Ego vos fratres feci, non ea conditione vt alij in alios domi nium & imperium exerceatis, sed vt alius alij inseruiat: quod vt positis, mea dona inter vos distribuo. Qui ergo plura accepit, & hoc nomine alios excellit, veritum omnium minister fit. Vt enim inter seruos alijs praestat, qui pluribus seruit: ita non alia ratione in meo regno ad summum dignitatis fastigium peruenitur, quam si quis in illo prouehendo pluribus inseruiat. Conuenit hoc cum eo quod vulgò fit. Etenim non temere veteres dixerunt, in vnaquaque domo vnum modo seruum esse, ipsum patremfamilias, qui toti domui aut familiae praeest. Ad eundem modum qui in Ecclesia, quae Dei domus est, prae alijs eminent, sibi ò plus laboris & curarum sibi impositum esse meminerint, nec in dominium conuertant, quod Dominus seruitium & ministerium esse voluit. Non ignorant haec nostri faculti Pontifices, & ideo serui seruorum dici volunt: Sed cum interea non in conseruos modò & fratres imperium sibi vendicent, verumetiam Regibus imperent & eos ad pedum suorum oscula vocent, omnibus denique leges & iura praescribant, quid obsecro hoc aliud est, quàm Christo insultare, cuius vicarios se dicunt, & hominibus illudere? Pertulit ista rerum infulentiam & tyrannidem saeculi aliquot infelix mundus: sed non perpetuum fore quod sibi vsurparunt imperium docet Dominus.
units.tr: Meanwhile (which is the other part of this passage or saying) the Lord teaches what befits those who preside over others. "Whoever is greatest among you," he says, "let him be your minister." He said the same thing elsewhere too, and at the last Supper he repeated it, not only in almost the same words but also confirmed it by his own example, when he, the teacher and Lord of the disciples and servants, washed their feet. The sense of Christ's words is this: "I have made you brothers, not on the condition that you exercise dominion and power over one another, but so that one serves another; and I distribute my gifts among you so that you may be useful to one another." Therefore whoever has received more, and on this account excels the others, becomes the minister of all. For just as among servants the one who serves more people excels the others, so in my kingdom no other way leads to the highest summit of dignity than by serving more people in advancing it. This agrees with what commonly happens. Indeed the ancients did not say without reason that in every household there is only one servant, the father of the family himself, who presides over the whole house or family. In the same way, those who stand out above others in the Church, which is God's house, should remember that more labour and cares have been laid upon them, and not turn into lordship what the Lord wanted to be service and ministry. Our learned Pontiffs do not fail to know this, and therefore they wish to be called the servants of servants. But meanwhile they do not claim power only over fellow-servants and brothers; they even rule over kings, call them to kiss their feet, and finally prescribe laws and rights for everyone. What, I ask you, is this other than mocking Christ, whose vicars they call themselves, and making a game of men? The unhappy world has for some centuries endured the arrogance and tyranny of this age, but the Lord teaches that the empire they have usurped will not last forever.

units.la: Etenim huius loci admonitionem graui sententia concludit, dicens: Qui se extollet, deprimetur: & qui se demiserit, extolletur. Depromitur pronuntiatum hoc ex aeterno Dei decreto, quod ab orbe condito exemplis infinitis confirmatum est. Etenim vt in Psalmis canitur, Dominus quod humile est intuetur & respicit, & quod datum est eminus cognoscit; vt videlicet suo tempore illud deijciat. Celebrat hunc Dei morem in suo Cantico Maria Virgo dicens: Fortiter egit brachio suo, dissipauit superbos cogitatione cordis ipsorum: Detraxit potentes ex throno, & exaltauit humiles: Famelicos impleuit bonis, & diuites ablegauit inanes. His consentit quod Petrus scribit, Deum humilibus dare gratiam: superbis autem resistere. Si exempla requiras, ibi ista occurrunt. Primus parentibus peccati sue transgressionis simul & ruina causa fuit superbia, quae eos fascinauit Satan, vt Deo aequales esse cuperent. Saulem item propter superbiam ex regali throno deturbauit Dominus, & in illum euexit e caula pecorum Dauidem de cuius humilitate & modestia passim Scriptura testantur, & qui de semetipso dicere potuit: Domine, cor meum non superbiuit, neque oculi mei elati fuerunt, neque incedo in rebus magnis & mirificis supra me, &c. Similiter Sennacherib, Nabuchodonosor.
units.tr: Indeed he concludes the admonition of this passage with a weighty sentence, saying: "Whoever exalts himself will be brought low, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted." This statement is drawn from the eternal decree of God, which has been confirmed by countless examples since the foundation of the world. For as is sung in the Psalms, the Lord looks upon and regards what is humble, and knows from afar what is lofty, so that, clearly, in his own time he may cast it down. The Virgin Mary celebrates this custom of God in her canticle, saying: "He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts. He has pulled the mighty from their thrones and exalted the humble. He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty." Peter's words agree with this, that God gives grace to the humble but resists the proud. If you ask for examples, they present themselves there. Pride was the first cause both of the sin of our first parents and of their ruin, since Satan bewitched them with the desire to be equal to God. Likewise the Lord, on account of pride, cast Saul down from the royal throne and raised up David from the sheepfold; Scripture bears witness everywhere to David's humility and modesty, and David could say of himself: "Lord, my heart is not proud, nor are my eyes lofty; I do not walk in great matters or wonders beyond me," and so on. Likewise Sennacherib and Nebuchadnezzar.

units.la: Z buchodonosarem, Alexandrum Macedonem, Iulium Caesarem & innumeros alios ambitio perdidit, dum non contenti ijs quae Deus dederat, ad altiora fuspirarunt. Et fere omnes isti regnis potentissimis interitu attulerunt, quae vna cum ipsis euersa sunt. E contra omnibus facultis quae in mundo stulta, infirma, ignobilia, adeo nulla sunt, elegit Deus, vt sapientes & ea quae robusta & magnifica videbantur pudefaceret. Itaque optima & tutissima ratio emergendi ad altiora & stabiles honores est humiliari sub potenti manu Dei, & alios se praestantiores putare, atque omnibus praesta re fraternitatis Christianae officia ad exemplum Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI, qui cum esset in forma Dei, non duxit rapinam parem esse cum Deo: sed ipse se exinaniuit forma serui accepta similis hominibus factus, & habitu compertus vt homo ipse se submisit factus obediens vsq; ad mortem, morte autem crucis. Quapropter etiam Deus ipsum extulit in summam dignitatem, ac donauit ei nomen quod est supra omne nomen: vt ad nomen IESV omne genu se flectat caelestium, terrestrium ac subterraneorum, omnisq; lingua confiteatur Dominum esse IESVM CHRISTVM ad gloriam Dei Patris. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Ambition destroyed Nimrod, Alexander of Macedon, Julius Caesar and countless others, since, not content with what God had given them, they aspired to higher things. And almost all of these brought ruin upon very powerful kingdoms, which were overthrown together with them. On the other hand, out of all the things in the world that are foolish, weak, lowly and of no account, God chose those to shame the wise and what seemed strong and great. Therefore the best and safest way to rise to higher things and to lasting honours is to humble oneself under the mighty hand of God, to think others better than oneself, and to render to all the duties of Christian brotherhood after the example of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, though he was in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in human appearance he humbled himself, becoming obedient even to death, death on the cross. Wherefore God also exalted him to the highest dignity and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power forever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXVII.
units.tr: Homily 267.

units.la: Sed vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei, hypocritae: quoniam clauditis regnum coelorum coram hominibus: Vos enim non intratis, nec introeuntes finitis introire. Vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei, hypocritae, qui exeditis domos viduarum, idque in speciem vtentes longis precibus: propterea auferetis grauius iudicium.
units.tr: "But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation."

units.la: Dominus & Seruator noster IESVS CHRISTVS prima huius Capitis parte suos discipulos & populum Iudaicum grauiter monuit de statu & conditione Scribarum & Pharisaeorum, ne vel prophano contemptu ordine & functionem a Deo institutam aspernentur, neue eorundem inconsulta imitatione peccarent. Ideo illos quidem Legem tradentes audire iusit, caueere autem exemplum vitae, in quo hypocrisim & ambitiosam primatus affectatione accusauit. His praemiis nunc acerrime in illos inuehitur, & horrendum illud Vae illis imprecatur, quo animi & corporis pernities & damnatio continetur, vt offendat, dignos esse qui aeternum damnentur. Debet autem diligenter obseruari exemplum Filij Dei. Sciebat hic incurabilem esse istorum hominum contumaciam, & quod correptione irritarentur potius quam emendarentur. Nihilominus tamen tam duriter illos tractat: nimirum propter populum, vt simpliciores, qui habitenus ab illorum authoritate penderent, in viam reuocet, ne eodem cum illis exitio implicentur. Etenim nulla nocentior est salutis remora, quam stolida falsorum antiquitatis admiratio & reuerentia. Atqui ea tunc fascinati erant Iudaei, vt nefas putarent ab ijs deficere, quos habitenus secuti fuerant. Itaque ne esse erat, simplices admoneri, illos autem contemptos & exosos fieri, vt quamuis ipsi non respiscerent, minus tamen nocerent. Debet hoc ipsum hodie obseruari in Ecclesia, neque audiendi sunt, qui indignius ferunt, si impostores & superstitionum magistri liberius arguantur. Nam vt hoc fiat, summa necessitas exigit. Vt enim oues, stolidum & simplex pecus, seipsas luporum faucibus temere obijciunt, & in proprium exitium ruunt, nisi pastoris voce & pedo coerceantur: ita solent vulgo homines, nec possunt horrile quid timere ex impostoribus, qui rabiem suam ouillis pellibus occultant. Serio igitur tales oppugnandi sunt, neque manuetudini locus aliquis dari debet, vbi priuata & publica multorum falsa periclitatur: & reuera non manuetti, sed crudeles sunt, qui ouium per ditione & exitio non mouentur.
units.tr: The Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, in the first part of this chapter, gravely warned his disciples and the Jewish people about the state and condition of the scribes and Pharisees. He did so lest they should despise the order and office instituted by God through contemptuous irreverence, or sin by thoughtlessly imitating those men. Accordingly, he ordered them to hear the men who taught the Law, but to beware of their way of life, in which he condemned their hypocrisy and their ambitious pursuit of the first place. Now he rails against them with the utmost sharpness on account of these very faults, and calls down that dreadful "Woe" upon them, which contains the ruin and condemnation of both soul and body, so that he might show that they deserve to be damned eternally. Moreover, the example of the Son of God must be carefully observed. He knew that the obstinacy of these men was incurable, and that they were angered by correction rather than amended by it. Nevertheless, he deals with them so harshly, plainly for the sake of the people: so that he might call back to the right way the simpler folk, who up to that time had depended on their authority, and so that they would not be caught in the same ruin as those men. For nothing is more harmful to salvation than a foolish admiration and reverence for falsehoods that are old. Yet the Jews at that time were so bewitched by this that they thought it wicked to desert those whom they had followed until then. Therefore, it was necessary that the simple be warned, while those men were made despised and hated, so that, even if they themselves did not repent, they might at least do less harm. The same ought to be observed today in the Church, and we must not listen to those who take it more ill if impostors and teachers of superstitions are criticised with greater freedom. For this there is the greatest necessity. Just as sheep, a foolish and simple flock, rashly throw themselves into the jaws of wolves and rush to their own destruction unless they are restrained by the voice and staff of the shepherd, so people in general are accustomed to behave, and cannot fear what is truly dreadful in impostors who hide their savage rage under sheep's skins. Such men must therefore be attacked in earnest, and no place should be given to gentleness where the private and public welfare of many is endangered; and indeed those are not gentle but cruel who are not moved by the ruin and destruction of the sheep.

units.la: Status huius correptionis est, fugiendos esse Scribas & Pharisaeos, eo quod horribilis Dei ira & aeterna damnatio tam ipsis quam fautoribus ipsorum parata sit. Confirmatur haec tam grauis sententia enumeratione vitiorum, quibus interitum iam pridem meruerint. Sunt haec octo numero, quibus singulis Vae illud denuntiat.
units.tr: The point of this rebuke is that the scribes and Pharisees are to be shunned, because a dreadful wrath of God and eternal damnation are prepared both for them and for their supporters. This so grave sentence is confirmed by a listing of the vices for which they had long since deserved destruction. There are eight of these, and to each one he pronounces that "Woe."

units.la: Exorditur autem ab eo, quod reuera grauissimum erat, & quo caetera omnia continentur, ijs quæ nuper audiuimus hunc locum connectens ait: Sed Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi hypocritæ, &c. Rursus hypocrisim illius exprobrat, quod fuco pietatis potissimum imponerent populo, & illos fibijpsis quoq; placerent ita, ut resipiscentia sibi non opus esse putarent. Illu ergo eius abstergit; quasi diceret: Hæc enim quidem simulata sanctitatis specie vos ostentauistis, & adhuc videmini multis non sancti modo, sed beatissimi hominum esse, eo quod Moysis cathedram tenetis, & summa sit vestra authoritas in Ecclesia Dei: sed magno vobis constabit hæc perfuasio. Nec enim vos ad uersus Dei iudicium tuebitur, qui per meam illud terribile vobis minatur, quod vos manet in præsenti hoc & futuro sæculo. Et mox causam adducit, dicens: Quoniam claudit regnum cælorum coram hominibus. Et hoc ipsum amplificans, addit: Vos nō introitis, nec introeuntes finitis introire. Per regnum cælorum vitam & salutem æternam intelligi, sæpe iam dictum est. Itaq; sensus est, quod non suam modo propriam salutem negligant, verumetiam viam salutis præcludant aliis, ne ad vitam possint ingredi. Apud Lucam hoc ita enunciatur: Væ vobis Legis interpretibus: quoniam sustulistis clauem cognitionis: ipsi non introijstis, & eos qui introibant, prohibuistis. Luca undecimo.
units.tr: He begins with the thing that was truly the most serious, and in which all the rest are contained, linking this place to what we heard recently, and says: "But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites," etc. Again he upbraids their hypocrisy, because they especially deceived the people with the mask of piety and pleased themselves so much that they thought no repentance was needed for them. He therefore wipes that away, as if he were saying: "You have indeed displayed yourselves under a feigned appearance of holiness, and you still seem to many not only holy but most blessed men, because you hold the seat of Moses and your authority in the Church of God is very great. But this persuasion will cost you dearly. For it will not protect you against the judgment of God, who through me threatens you with that terrible thing that awaits you in this present age and in the age to come." And soon he gives the reason, saying: "Because you shut up the kingdom of heaven before men." And enlarging on this very point, he adds: "For you neither enter in, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in." It has often been said already that by the kingdom of heaven is meant life and eternal salvation. The meaning, then, is that they neglect not only their own salvation, but also block the way of salvation for others, so that they cannot enter into life. In Luke this is put thus: "Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered." Luke 11.

units.la: Hoc vt rectius intelligamus, tenendum est initio, viam aut ostium regni cælorum toti humano generi præ: lusum fuisse propter peccatum. Typus huius fuit gladius ille versatilis, qui ad ostium Paradisi appositus est Deus, ne primi parentes inde ieiuni illuc reuerterentur, & ex arbore vitæ ederent. Eo enim adumbrabatur, neminem posthac proprijs viribus aut meritis ingressurum ad vitam æternam aut in regnum cælorum, præter eum qui e cælo venient illic redditurus fit: qui est æternus Dei Filius, IESVS CHRISTVS, qui suæ mortis merito peccata nostra expiauit, & ascensione sua gloriosa cælos nobis reserauit. Hic Eliakim ille verus est, de quo apud Isaiam dicitur, quod gestet clauem domus Dauid, & de seipso ille dicit in Apocalypsi, quod habeat claues inferni & mortis, quod ita ipso claudente nemo aperiat, rursus ipso aperiente nemo claudat. De hoc olim Moses testatus est, & Prophetæ omnes vaticinati sunt. Eiusdem prædicatio olim Sacerdotibus Iudæorum commissa fuit, & postea Apostolis, quibus omnibus ille in Petro dixit: Tibi dabo claves regni cælorum, &c. Erant hæ tunc temporis penes Scribas & Pharisaos, quorum erat Legem interpretari, quæ pædagogus est ad Christum, dum nos peccati connexos mortis reos agit, & hunc amplecti docet, qui nobis sapientia, iustitia, vita & salus a Patre factus est. Huius igitur prædicatio clauis scientiæ & cognitionis dicitur, eo quod in illius cognitionem nos induxit, qui regnum Dei solus aperit, & huius facit hæredes. Vnde apparet, quam illa sit necessaria, cum sine illo impossibile sit aliquos saluos fieri. Non est enim in alio quoquam salus. Actor. 4. Ioan. 14.
units.tr: To understand this more correctly, we must hold at the outset that the way or door of the kingdom of heaven was closed to the whole human race because of sin. A type of this was that turning sword which God placed at the door of Paradise, so that our first parents, hungry, might not return there and eat from the tree of life. For it was thereby foreshadowed that no one would henceforth enter into eternal life or into the kingdom of heaven by his own strength or merits, except the one who would come down from heaven to restore it: that is, the eternal Son of God, Jesus Christ, who by the merit of his death expiated our sins and by his glorious ascension unlocked the heavens for us. He is that true Eliakim, of whom it is said in Isaiah that he bears the key of the house of David; and of himself he says in the Apocalypse that he has the keys of hell and of death, so that when he shuts, no one opens, and again when he opens, no one shuts. Moses bore witness to this long ago, and all the prophets prophesied it. The preaching of this was entrusted long ago to the priests of the Jews, and afterwards to the apostles, to all of whom he said in Peter: "To thee will I give the keys of the kingdom of heaven," etc. At that time these keys were in the hands of the scribes and Pharisees, whose task was to interpret the Law, which is our schoolmaster to Christ, while it holds us, bound by sin, guilty of death, and teaches us to embrace him who has been made by the Father our wisdom, righteousness, life and salvation. Therefore the preaching of this is called the key of knowledge and understanding, because it leads us into the knowledge of him who alone opens the kingdom of God and makes us its heirs. From this it is apparent how necessary it is, since without him it is impossible for anyone to be saved. For there is no salvation in any other. Acts 4; John 14.

units.la: Huc ergo respiciens Dominus ista de Scribis & Pharisæis pronuntiat, quos grauissimi & multiplicis scelerum accusat. Primo quod clauem scientiæ abstulerint aut suffurati sint: quod de suppressa aut sublata vera Legis doctrina debet intelligi, quæ tunc prorsus silebat apud Iudæos. Itaque hoc sacrilegium erat multo atrocius, quam si quis vniuersum templi aurum rapuisset. Deinde, quod qui fores regni cælorum populo referare debebant, has præcludant quibusdam: Fiebat hoc fini stra Legis interpretatione, de qua prolixe dictum est supra quinto Cap. Nec falsa doctrina modo occludebant regnum cælorum, verumetiam exemplo suo, quo in superstitionibus, & inani harum fiducia rudem & imperitam plebem detinebant. Accedebat his, quod non ipsi modo non ingredi-bantur in regnum Dei, sed ingredi volentes procul inde arcebant. Nam edicta minacia & ipsis quoq; principibus formidulosa vulgabant, quibus excommunicationem minabantur ijs, qui in IESVM CHRISTVM crederent. Taceo nunc impiam illorum temeritatem, qua sese hostiliter illi opposuerunt, Samaritanum & damoniacum vocando, vt omnibus exosum aut suspectum facerent: neq; ante quieuerunt, quam illo iniquè & crudeliter in cruce occiso, totum populum sanguinis Filij Dei reum fecerunt. Non ergo abfq; causa tam grauem aduersus illos sententiam pro nuntiat, vt nimirum qui inter Iudæos adhuc synceriores erant, & ferio salutis studio tenebatur, ab illorum doctrina & commercio auocaret.
units.tr: Looking to this, the Lord pronounces these things about the scribes and Pharisees, whom he accuses of very grave and manifold crimes. First, that they have taken away or stolen the key of knowledge; this must be understood of the suppression or removal of the true teaching of the Law, which at that time was utterly silent among the Jews. Accordingly, this sacrilege was far more atrocious than if someone had stolen all the gold of the temple. Next, that they, who ought to have unlocked the gates of the kingdom of heaven for the people, were shutting them off from some: this was being done by a perverse interpretation of the Law, of which we have spoken at length above in the fifth chapter. Nor did they shut the kingdom of heaven merely by false teaching, but also by their example, by which they kept the untaught and ignorant common people bound to superstitions and to a vain trust in them. In addition to this, they not only did not enter into the kingdom of God themselves, but also kept away at a distance those who wished to enter. For they published threatening edicts, which were dreadful even to the princes themselves, by which they threatened with excommunication those who believed in Jesus Christ. I say nothing now of their impious recklessness, by which they set themselves in hostile opposition to him, calling him a Samaritan and a demoniac, so as to make him hateful and suspect to all; nor did they rest until, with him unjustly and cruelly slain on the cross, they made the whole people guilty of the blood of the Son of God. It is not without cause, then, that he pronounces so grave a sentence against them, namely, so that he might turn away from their teaching and fellowship those who were still more sincere among the Jews and were held by a serious desire for salvation.

units.la: Debent autem ista nostri sæculi moribus applicari, vt videamus annon eadem de his quoq; dici possint, qui hodie primatum & imperium in Ecclesia sibi vendicant. Enimuero dedit Christus antiquis.
units.tr: These things must also be applied to the customs of our own age, so that we may see whether the same things can be said of those who today claim for themselves primacy and rule in the Church. Indeed, Christ said this to the men of old.

units.la: Scribæ occludunt regnum cœlorum. stius claues cognitionis Ecclesiæ, & harum administrationem Apostolis suis & horum legitimis successoribus credidit, vt nimirum syncera Euangelij prædicatione peccatorum remissionem polli ceantur, & regnum cœlorum omnibus patefaciant, qui serio resipiscunt & ipsum fide vera atque constanti amplexantur. Quid vero factum postquam Pontifices in Ecclesiam regnum vsurpa-runt? Primum claues illas abstulerunt & sublata prorsus Euangelij prædicatione, huius loco do minium quoddam substituerunt, quod totum fere absolutionum & damnationum demurmuratio-nibus consiat, quæ ab exorcismis magicis non multum differunt. Et vt maior siue augustior esset imperij male vsurpati maiestas, claues istas plus quam meretricia impudentia sibi ita vendica-runt, vt eas in suis insignibus vna cum triplici tiara aut corona ostentent. Quo prætextu Regi-bus quoque superbe imperant, & effreni peccandi licentia ac impunitate gloriantur. Præterea cum sibi vt Christi vicarijs datam esse dicant potestatem omnem in cœlo & in terra, ipsi tamen regni cœlorum cura nulla tanguntur, neq; in hoc introire student, cum IESVM CHRISTVM, qui solus in hoc via & ostium est, & huius prædicationem hostiliter oderint & persequantur: eiusdem vero meritum nugis suis & operum humanorum fiducia euacuent & inutile reddant. Interim vero omnia desinant, propter quæ homines a regno cœlorum excludi, Paulus ad Corinthios testatur. Quid, quod plerique illorum ludus & iocus sunt, quæcunq; de animarum immortalitate & mortuorum resurrectione traduntur. Neq; his contenti sunt, sed alijs quoq; obstant, ne ad vitam ingrediantur. Nam huius viam, quæ in solo Christo monstratur, traditionibus suis obstruunt, & infelices ad auia & diuerticula ablegant. Quod si qui animosiores diligentius inquirant in ipsorum commenta, & in mysterijs regni Dei rectius insitui cupiant, eos scurriliter eluðunt, & de illis non curiosius quæri debere respondent, eo quod eorum cognitio ad solos rasos & vnctos pertineat. Si quis fortius instet, in furorem & rabiem aguntur, & si homo priuatus sit, eum absq; ætatis aut sexus respectu crudeliter occidunt: sin tota gens aut ciuitas doctrinam Veritatis amplexetur, bellum contra eam sanctificant, & vt suæ tyrannidi consulant, cœlum terræ miscere non verentur. Quis ergo non eodem anathema ate illos deuoueat, quo Christus Scribas & Pharisæos deuouit? Quis non ab illorum doctrina & exemplo sibi non minori studio & diligentia cauen-dum putet, quàm olim Iudæorum Scribæ & Pharisæi cauere debuerunt? Et enim inexcusabilis so-cordia argumentum fuerit, si hos nobis ad regnum cœlorum duces deligamus, & sponte sectemur, quos propriæ salutis tam videmus esse negligentes.
units.tr: "The scribes shut up the kingdom of heaven" (Matt. 23:13). Christ gave the keys of the knowledge of the Church and entrusted their administration to his Apostles and their lawful successors, so that by the sincere preaching of the Gospel they might promise forgiveness of sins and open the kingdom of heaven to all who seriously repent and embrace it with true and steadfast faith. But what has happened since the Pontiffs seized rule over the Church? First they took away those keys, and, with the preaching of the Gospel utterly abolished, they put in its place a certain lordship, which consists almost entirely of muttered absolutions and condemnations, not much different from magical exorcisms. And so that the majesty of their ill-usurped power might be greater or more august, they claimed those keys for themselves with more than harlot's impudence, and display them on their coats of arms together with the triple tiara or crown. Under this pretext they also lord it proudly over kings, and they boast of their unbridled licence and impunity in sinning. Moreover, although they say that the power over all things in heaven and on earth has been given to them as Christ's vicars, they are not troubled at all by the care of the kingdom of heaven, nor do they strive to enter it, since they hostilely hate and persecute Jesus Christ, who alone is the way and the door, and his preaching; and they empty his merit and make it useless by their trifles and their trust in human works. Meanwhile they neglect all those things, on account of which, as Paul testifies to the Corinthians, people are shut out of the kingdom of heaven. And what of the fact that most of them treat as a joke and a jest whatever is taught about the immortality of souls and the resurrection of the dead? Nor are they content with these things, but they also stand in the way of others, so that they do not enter into life. For they block the way to it, which is shown in Christ alone, with their traditions, and they send the unhappy off to byways and side-tracks. If any more spirited people inquire more closely into their inventions and wish to be more properly instructed in the mysteries of the kingdom of God, they mock them with buffoonery and answer that such matters should not be inquired into too curiously, because knowledge of them belongs only to the shaven and anointed. If someone presses more vigorously, they are driven to fury and rage, and if he is a private person, they cruelly kill him without regard to age or sex. But if a whole nation or city embraces the doctrine of Truth, they sanctify war against it, and, to protect their tyranny, they do not hesitate to stir heaven and earth. Who then would not curse them with the same anathema with which Christ cursed the scribes and Pharisees? Who would not think that we must beware of their doctrine and example with no less zeal and diligence than the scribes and Pharisees of the Jews ought to have beware of? For it would be an inexcusable stupidity if we chose these men as our guides to the kingdom of heaven and willingly followed them, when we see them so negligent of their own salvation.

units.la: Sequitur alterum vitium, quod in Scribis & Pharisæis reprehendit, propter quod illos semiternō exitio dignos, & proinde pijs omnibus fugiendos esse docet. Væ vobis (inquit) Scribæ & Pharisæi, hypocritæ, qui exeditis aut devoratis domus viduarum, sub speciem vtentes longis precibus, &c. Summa & caput huius criminis est, quod religionem sibi quastum fecerint, & tunc postissimum peccent, quando religiosissimi esse videantur. Idem ergo hic illis exprobrat, quod alibi, quando eos templum in emporium commutasse ait. In præsenti autem vnam diuini cultus speciem adducit, preces nimirum, sub quibus alias omnes comprehendit. Et sane cultum suum in illis po-tissimum consistere Deus docet, quando reiectis sacrificijs & alijs ritibus externis in Psalmo di-cit: Sacrifica Deo laudem, & redde Altissimo vota tua: Et inuoca me in die tribulationis, & e-ruam te, & tu glorificabis me. At illos in precibus quidem assiduos fuisse, supra audiuimus, non autem ex fide vera orasse eos constat, quando in publico ipsos precari ait, vt ab hominibus spectentur. Itaq; ambitione & priuatæ gloriæ studio ad preces incitabantur, vt sanctitatis summæ existimationem sibi compararent. At hic altera etiam causa indicatur, auaritia, quæ illos cogebat quæ stum vænari precando. Hanc autem in illis insatiabilem & cum iniquitate summa coniunctam fuisse, imò inter precandum crudeles fuisse illos ex circumstantijs probat. Nam dicit illos deuorare domos ipsas, sub quibus reliquas facultates omnes compleƈtitur, vt ostendat eos paruo aut exiguo lucro non contentos esse, nisi domos quoque totas sibi vendicent. Quid vero reliquum faciet mise-ris, qui domum quoq; aussert? Deinde ad sceleris amplificationem facit, quod viduarum memi-nit, quas ita omnibus commendatas esse voluit Deus, vt in Lege prohibuerit, ne quis vestem viduæ pignoris loco accipiat. Fuit ergo auaritia hæc nefaria & crudelis, qua viduæ domibus suis cedere cogebantur. At non poterant ista fieri, nisi doctrinam Legis corrumperent, & traditionibus super-stitiostitiosis mulierculas, quarum conscientias peccatis grauatas esse animaduertebant, circumueni-rent, ut se Deo cultum gratissimum praestare, & animarum saluti consulere putarent, si sua Sacer dotibus largirentur, aut in corbonam deponerent. Hic ergo potissimum fiebat, quod supra in illis accusauit, quod Dei praecepta traditionibus suis irritas faciant, dum multis authores sint, ut quae in parentum alimoniam conferre debebant, his neglectis, in vsus superstitiosos conuertant. Et hoc nomine alibi eos merito fures & latrones vocat. In praesenti autem, quia deploratam & incurabilem sciebat esse ipsorum nequitiam, ad Dei tribunal eos citat, dicens: Propterea auferetis grauius iudicium. Et ita agendum est cum hypocritis, quos ementita sanctitatis perfuasio fascinat, ut intelligant, Deum qui hypocrisim & impostoras odit, non dormitare, sed horribiles de illis poenas fume re, qui ista sub plausibili religionis & nominis sui praetextu designant. Exempla sunt multa, quae huic comminationi fidem faciunt. Inter quae cumprimis memorabile est, Balaami, quod Petrus Apostolus adducit, quando de impostoribus agit, qui postremis temporibus per auaritiam fictis sermonibus animas simplicium negotiaturi sint, ut illorum ignorantia & simplicitate ad quaestum priuatum abutantur.
units.tr: Next follows the second vice, which he reproves in the scribes and Pharisees, on account of which he teaches that they are worthy of eternal destruction and therefore must be avoided by all the godly: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who devour the houses of widows, under the pretext of making long prayers," and so on (Matt. 23:14). The sum and head of this crime is that they made religion a source of gain, and sin most when they seem most religious. Here he therefore reproaches them with the same thing that he elsewhere says when he states that they had turned the temple into a marketplace. But here he mentions one form of divine worship, namely prayers, under which he includes all the others. And indeed God teaches that his worship consists especially in these, when, setting aside sacrifices and other external rites, he says in the Psalm: "Offer to God thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High; and call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me" (Ps. 50:14-15). But that they were constant in prayers we have heard above; yet it is clear that they did not pray from true faith, since he says that they pray in public so that they may be seen by men. Therefore they were driven to prayer by ambition and a desire for private glory, so that they might acquire for themselves a reputation for the highest holiness. But here another cause is also indicated, greed, which compelled them to hunt for gain by praying. The circumstances prove that this greed was insatiable and closely joined with great iniquity, and indeed that they were cruel even while praying. For he says that they devour the very houses in which all the rest of their goods are contained, to show that they are not content with a small or meagre profit unless they claim the whole houses for themselves as well. What then will be left to the wretched, if they carry off the house too? Then he adds to the enormity of the crime by mentioning widows, whom God wished to be so commended to everyone that he forbade in the Law that anyone should take a widow's garment as a pledge. This greed was therefore wicked and cruel, by which widows were forced to give up their houses. But these things could not be done unless they corrupted the teaching of the Law and, by their traditions, cheated the superstitious little women, whose consciences they noticed were burdened with sins, so that they would think they were offering God the most pleasing worship and caring for the salvation of their souls if they gave their property to the priests or laid it in the corban. Here, therefore, especially happened what he accused them of above, namely that by their traditions they make the commandments of God void, while they are the authors for many of turning to superstitious uses what ought to be given to support their parents, which is neglected. And for this reason he elsewhere rightly calls them thieves and robbers. But here, since he knew that their wickedness was desperate and incurable, he summons them before the judgment seat of God, saying: "Therefore you will receive the greater judgment." And so it must be done with hypocrites, whom a false persuasion of holiness bewitches, so that they may understand that God, who hates hypocrisy and imposture, does not sleep, but exacts terrible punishments from those who disguise these things under the plausible pretext of religion and his name. There are many examples that give credit to this warning. Among them the most memorable is that of Balaam, which the Apostle Peter cites when he speaks of impostors who in the last times, through greed, will trade in the souls of simple people with feigned words, so that they may abuse their ignorance and simplicity for private gain.

units.la: Ergo haec quoque ad nostrum saeculum transferri debent, ut hypocritae & impostores, qui hodie gregem Domini similiter auaritia & non minori cum crudelitate vastant & deuorant, agnosce-re & cauere discamus. At quid paßim fiat, lippis & conspicuis notum est. Quem enim fidei Christianae articulum dabis, quem Pontificij Romanenses suis figmentis & traditionibus non adulterarint. Fidei Christianae caput est, ut omnis salutis fiducia in vno Deo collocetur, vnus hic innocetur per vnum Mediatorem IESVM CHRISTVM, qui in se credentibus plenariam peccatorum remissionem & salutem certam pollicetur, & quod iidem quando hinc emigrant, non in aliquod iudicium veniant, sed a morte transeant in vitam. At illi nobis Diuos caelites finxerunt, quos & mundi gubernatores constituunt, & Filij Dei coadiutores faciunt, & quae huic soli debetur gloriam in illos distribuunt. Adhaec ignem lustralem siue Purgatorium commenti sunt, quo animae corporibus solutae expurgentur, prius quam ad sedes beatorum perueniant. Quae perfuasio sacrapro defunctis peperit, & in simplicium cordibus terrores excitauit, quibus superati facultates suas praeteritis legitimis haeredibus, monachis & sacrificulis legauerunt: quibus non satis fuit, vt uos fraudibus suis circumuenisse & spoliasse, nisi (quod prouerbio dicitur) a mortuis quoque tributum exigerent. Illorum certe artibus eo res deducta sunt, ut nihil in Ecclesia gratis fiat, neque hominibus Christianis gratis nasci aut mori liceat. Nam ut Erasmus verissime scripsit, non datur baptismus, id est, non licet fieri Christianum, nisi numeres: non audiunt poenitentium commissa, nisi sperent praemium: non psallunt gratis, no orant gratis, non imponunt manum gratis. Non consecrat saxum aut calicem, nisi data mercede. Et quid ex istis gratuitum speres, apud quos emitur & sepultura, etiam in alieno solo? Apud Ethnicos miseri plebi stabat commune sepulchrum, erat vbi gratis quos vellet, sepelires. Barbarus ille & gentilis Hebron offert Abrahamo, ignoto hospiti gratuitum sepulchri munus, & vix adduci precibus potest, ut oblatam accipiat pecuniam: at sacerdotes sepulturae ius vendunt in alieno: Vel potius quod publicum est, id ceu priuatum are locant. Adhaec pro defunctorum animarum salute annuos reditus exigunt, nec pudet illos annuis exactionibus testari, quam inutilia sint & nullius valoris, quae se facere gloriantur, ut animabus in purgatorio igne laborantibus succurrant. Atqui Deus olim per Zachariam dixit, non fore Chananaeum, id est, mercatorem in domo sua & Christus vendentes ac ementes e templo eiecit. Quid ergo eundem factorum putabimus, quando isti mensuram suam impleuerint? Horum memores, caueamus nobis ab horum impostura, & constanter tueamur libertatem, quam nobis sanguinis sui pretio acquisiuit IESVS CHRISTVS, Dominus & redemptor noster: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Therefore these things too must be carried over to our own age, so that we may learn to recognise and beware of the hypocrites and impostors who today likewise lay waste and devour the flock of the Lord with greed and no less cruelty. But what is done everywhere is known to the bleary-eyed and to those who are plain to see. For what article of the Christian faith will you name that the Roman Papists have not corrupted with their fictions and traditions? The head of the Christian faith is that all confidence in salvation is placed in the one God, and that he alone is invoked through the one Mediator Jesus Christ, who promises full forgiveness of sins and certain salvation to those who believe in him, and that when they depart hence they do not come into any judgment, but pass from death into life. But they have invented for us heavenly divinities, whom they also appoint as governors of the world and make into helpers of the Son of God, and they distribute among them the glory that is owed to him alone. Besides, they have devised a lustral fire, or Purgatory, in which souls, released from their bodies, are purged before they reach the seats of the blessed. This persuasion has produced sacrifices for the dead and has stirred up terrors in simple hearts, by which those who were overcome have bequeathed their goods to monks and little priests, passing over their lawful heirs. And it was not enough for these men to have deceived and despoiled you with their frauds, unless (as the proverb says) they also exacted tribute from the dead. Certainly, by their arts, matters have been brought to such a pass that nothing in the Church is done freely, nor is it permitted for Christians to be born or to die without payment. For, as Erasmus wrote most truly, baptism is not given, that is, it is not allowed to make someone a Christian, unless you pay; they do not hear the sins of penitents unless they hope for a reward; they do not sing psalms for nothing, they do not pray for nothing, they do not lay on hands for nothing. They do not consecrate a stone or a chalice unless a price is paid. And what can you hope to get for nothing from those among whom even burial is bought, even in another's land? Among the heathen a common tomb stood for the poor common people; there anyone could bury whomever he wished for free. That barbarian and Gentile Hebron offers Abraham, a stranger, the free gift of a tomb, and can hardly be persuaded by prayers to accept the money offered; but the priests sell the right of burial in another's land. Or rather, what is public they lease out as if it were private. Besides, they exact annual revenues for the salvation of the souls of the dead, and they are not ashamed to testify by these annual exactions how useless and worthless are the things they boast of doing to help souls labouring in the fire of Purgatory. And yet God once said through Zechariah that there would no longer be a Canaanite, that is, a merchant, in his house; and Christ drove the sellers and buyers out of the temple. What then shall we think will be done to these men, when they have filled up their measure? Mindful of these things, let us beware of the deceit of these men, and let us steadfastly guard the liberty which Jesus Christ, our Lord and Redeemer, has won for us at the price of his own blood, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.
