units.la: HOMILIA CCLXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCCLXVIII.

units.la: Væ vobis scribæ & Pharisæi, hypocritæ, quoniam circumitis mare & aridam, vt faciatis vnum proselytum: & cum fuerit factus, facitis eum filium gehennæ duplo magis quàm vos estis. Væ vobis duces cæci, qui dicitis: Quisquis iurauerit per templum, nihil est: quicunque autem iurauerit per aurum templi, reus est. Stulti & cæci, vtrum enim maius est, aurum, an templum quod sanctificat aurum? Et, Quisquis iurauerit per altare, nihil est: quicunque autem iurauerit per donum, quod est super ipsum, reus est. Stulti & cæci, vtrum enim maius est, munus, an altare quod sanctificat munus? Qui ergo iurauerit per altare, iurat per ipsum, & per omnia quæ super illud sunt. Et qui iurauerit per templum, iurat per ipsum, & per eum qui habitat in eo. Et qui iurauerit per cœlum, iurat per thronum Dei, & per eum qui sedet super ipsum.
units.tr: "Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves. Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor! Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold? And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor. Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift? Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon. And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein. And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon." (Matt. 23.)

units.la: Tota huius Capitis tractatione Dominus & redemptor noster IESVS CHRISTVS in Iudæorum Scribis & Pharisæis duo vitia præcipue accusat. Primo nimirum hypocrisim, sub quapriuatæ gloriæ studium comprehendit. Quia vero hoc mirifice dissimulabant, adeo vt vulgò sanctissimi homines esse putarentur, subinde repetit hypocritas esse: partim vt ipsos terreat, qui eò confidentiores erant, quòd suas artes adhuc occultas esse existimarent: partim nefuco illorum populus falleretur. Deinde auaritiam non minus accusat, qua religionem omnem sibi quæstum fecerant, & quæ nos Dei seruos esse non finit. Nec enim temere alibi a Domino dictum est, nos non possefimul duobus dominis diuersa iubentibus seruire: Deo videlicet & Mammonæ. Huius autem studium in ipsis regnare, nuper demonstrauit, quando dixit illos deuorare domos viduarum, dum in speciem prolixæ precibus vtantur: Quod vt fecerint, exemplo ex Cap. XV. adductio abundè ostendimus. Sequitur nunc aliud, quod eodem referri potest, & quod simul alia quoque completitur, quæ non minus reprehendi merentur.
units.tr: Throughout this whole chapter our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ charges the scribes and Pharisees of the Jews chiefly with two vices. First, hypocrisy, under which he includes the pursuit of private glory. Since they disguised this wonderfully, so that they were commonly thought to be the most holy men, he repeatedly calls them hypocrites: partly to terrify them, who were the more bold because they thought their arts were still hidden, and partly so that the people might not be deceived by their pretence. Then he accuses them no less of covetousness, by which they had made a profit out of all religion, and which does not allow us to be servants of God. For it was not without reason that the Lord said elsewhere that we cannot serve two masters giving contrary commands at the same time: God, that is, and Mammon. That this greed reigned in them he showed recently, when he said they devoured the houses of widows while using long prayers as a pretence. That they did this we have shown abundantly by example from chapter 15. Now follows another matter, which can be referred to the same heading, and which at the same time includes other faults no less deserving of rebuke.

units.la: Nam tertium illius vitium exprobrans ait: Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi, hypocritæ, quoniam circumitis mare & aridam, vt faciatis vnum proselytum, & cum fuerit factus, facitis eum filium gehennæ duplo magis quàm vos estis. Proselyti Latinis aduentitij dicuntur, qui religionis paartis superstitionibus, in quibus nati & a pueris instituti sunt, ad Iudaismum transeunt: De Scribis autem & Pharisæis dicitur, quòd mare ac aridam, id est terram circumeant, id est summo studio in hoc sint, vt vbiq; locorum occasiones quærant aliquos inescandi aut circumueniendi, vt Circumcisi ex Ethnicis Iudæi fiant. Impulit eos adhuc procul dubio non solùm lucrifpes quæ sese offerebat, verumetiam gloriæ studium & quod illud sibi honorificum esse, & vulgi fauore ipsis conciliare videbatur. Quia enim negasset illos zelo gloriæ Dei ardere, quos indefesso studio discurrere videbat, vt nonos subinde discipulos conquirerent? Quis non illos præ aliis eruditione & sapientia instructos esse dixisset, & de Ecclesia Dei indies bene mereri? At simul docet, quàm parum pro ficiant. Si quem inuenias (inquit) qui vobis aures præbeat & obsequatur, num vel accessione nouæ crescit Ecclesia, vel illius, vt quis est saluti consulitur? nequaquam. Imò Filium gehennæ, id est, perditionis & damnationis illum facitis duplo magis quàm vos estis. Durum hoc & graue fuit, filios gehennæ dici eos, qui in populo Dei primas tenebant, & summam sanctitatis & eruditionis laudem apud plerosque obtinebant. Dicit tamen, quia hæc multa & grauia vitia concurrebant. Erat nim hypocrisis erat quod faciebant, & non syncero, sed fucato regni Dei studio ducebantur. Deinde gloriam priuatam ambitiose quærebant. Adhæc habendi cupiditate inflammati, nouam quotidie prædam ex miseris & incautis venabantur, quos in suos casses videbant incidisse. Accedebat his falsa doctrina, & praua institutio. Cùm enim in Lege Dei illos instituere deberent, vt quæ Dei voluntas sit, intelligerent, & simul in illa ceu speculo naturæ suæ vitiositatem & humanarum vi- riurum rium inopiam intuerentur, atq; his cognitis ad thronum gratiæ perpromissum Seruatorem consu gerent: illi extincta & sublata prorsus vera legis doctrina, miseros in traditionibus suis instituebant, quas vel ipsi finxerant, vel ab hominibus æque ineptis & superstitiosis acceperant: & his imbutos ad sui arbitrij vires & suorum operum iustitiam atq; meritum remittebant, cuius fiducia postea turgidi sibi ipsis placebant, neq; soliciti erant de iustitia Dei, quam hic nobis in Filio suo I E S V C H R I S T O propinat. Fiebat deniq; , vt quo plus illi in nouo isto Iudaismo proficerent, eo longius a Christo recederent, imò vt suis illis præceptoribus gratificarentur, illius acerrimi hostes essent, & puriorem fidei atq; salutis doctrinam hostiliter persequerentur. Itaq; qui prius in gentilismo philosophorum placita secuti secundum legem naturæ viuebant, virtuti operam dabant, & cupiebant indies proficere, cum sentirent quantum ipsis deesset (vt Socratis exemplo docemur, qui se hoc vnum scire dicebat, quod nihil sciret) ij abiectis & relictis prioribus stimulis, circa otiosam & inanem legis contemplationem occupabantur, ad cuius verum sensum non poterant penetrare sine Christo, qui solus velum illud quod Iudæos in faciem Mosis intueri non sinit, remouet. Quare in dubio hærentes neq; Iudæi erant, qui secundū legis præcepta sanctè viuerent, neq; tam gnauiter virtuti operam dabant, quàm antea fecerant: sed legalium sacrificiorum & externi cultus fiducia ad omnem peccandi licentiam abutebantur. Itaq; ipsis seruiebat quod Apostolus scribit: Non qui in propatulo Iudæus, Iudæus est, nec ea quæ est in propatulo circumcisio in carne, circumcisio est: Sed qui in occulto Iudæus est, & circumcisio cordis in spiritu, non litera, cuius Iudæi laus non est ex hominibus, sed ex Deo. Adde hís, quod circumcisio debitores legis faciebat, quam cum non possent seruare iusta damnationis erat ipsis testimonium. Vide Gal.5.
units.tr: For in rebuking their third vice he says: "Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves." Proselytes are called in Latin newcomers, those who pass over to Judaism from the superstitions of their own religion in which they were born and brought up from boyhood. Of the scribes and Pharisees it is said that they go round the sea and the dry land, that is, the earth, that is, that with the greatest zeal they are intent on seeking everywhere opportunities to lure in or ensnare people, so that Gentiles may become circumcised Jews. Doubtless what impelled them was not only the greed for gain that offered itself, but also the desire for glory, and the fact that this seemed honourable to them and would win them the favour of the common people. For who would not have said, seeing them run about with tireless zeal to gain new disciples every day, that they burned with zeal for the glory of God? Who would not have said they were better taught than others in learning and wisdom, and deserved well of the Church of God day by day? But at the same time he shows how little they accomplished. "If you find someone," he says, "who lends you his ears and obeys you, does the Church grow by the addition of this new convert, or is the man's salvation cared for? By no means. Rather, you make him a child of hell, that is, of perdition and damnation, twice as much as you yourselves are." It was hard and grievous that those who held the first place among the people of God, and won the highest praise of holiness and learning from most, should be called children of hell. Yet he says it, because many great and grave vices came together in them. For what they did was hypocrisy, and they were led not by a sincere but by a feigned zeal for the kingdom of God. Next, they ambitiously sought private glory. Moreover, inflamed with the desire to possess, they hunted daily for new spoil among the wretched and the unwary, whom they saw had fallen into their nets. To these faults was added false teaching and a corrupt instruction. For while they ought to have instructed them in the Law of God, so that they might understand what God's will is, and at the same time see in it, as in a mirror, their own nature's corruption and the poverty of human strength, and having known these things, flee for refuge to the grace of the Saviour promised on the throne: they, having utterly extinguished and removed the true doctrine of the Law, taught the wretched people in their own traditions, which they had either invented themselves or received from men equally foolish and superstitious. And having imbued them with these, they sent them back to trust in the powers of their own will and in the righteousness and merit of their own works. Puffed up with this confidence, they pleased themselves and were not anxious about the righteousness of God, which he now offers to us in his Son Jesus Christ. In the end it came about that the more they advanced in this new Judaism, the further they withdrew from Christ; indeed, in order to please those teachers of theirs, they became his bitterest enemies, and hostilely persecuted the purer doctrine of faith and salvation. Therefore those who had earlier followed the opinions of the philosophers in heathenism and lived according to the law of nature, devoting themselves to virtue and desiring to make progress every day, when they perceived how much they lacked (as we are taught by the example of Socrates, who said he knew this one thing, that he knew nothing), these men, having abandoned and left behind their former incentives, were occupied with an idle and empty contemplation of the Law. They could not penetrate to its true sense without Christ, who alone removes that veil which does not allow the Jews to look upon the face of Moses. Hence, hanging in doubt, they were neither Jews who lived holily according to the precepts of the Law, nor did they pursue virtue as earnestly as they had before; but, trusting in the legal sacrifices and external worship, they abused it as a licence for every kind of sin. So what the Apostle writes applied to them: "He is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, in the Spirit and not in the letter, whose praise is not of men but of God." Add to this that circumcision made men debtors to the Law, and since they could not keep it, it was for them a testimony of just condemnation. See Gal. 5.

units.la: Quod autem in sui seculi Scribis & Pharisæis accusat Dominus, vtinam non hodie passim fieret apud eos, qui Christianæ religionis antistites & columnæ videri volunt. Quid enim aliud faciunt Monachi, qui hinc inde discurrendo, nunc hos nunc istos solicitant, vt relicto vitæ genere ad quod a Deo vocati sunt, & in quo huic simul & hominibus seruire poterant, sese votis monastiticis obstringant. Quod postquam fecerunt, ceu manicis & compedibus vincti vitam viuunt otiosam & quando optimi sunt, ignaui & nemini vtiles in lustris suis contabescunt, vel etiam dum se mundo mortuos esse arbitrantur inter assiduas cupiditatum carnalium flammas æstuant, seq; ipsos & corpora sua horribiliter fœdant & polluunt. Quid vero iis accidat, qui ab Anabaptistis seductis, relictis coniugibus & dulcibus liberis nouum illud vitæ genus sectantur, in quo solo sultissimi homines se seruari posse existimant, multi non absq; grauissimis conscientiæ certaminibus experti sunt. Quid vero de Iudæis fiat, præstat commemorare. Etenim sunt, qui maximam sanctitatis & erudi tionis laudem se mereri putent, si cui Iudæo persuadeant, vt Baptismo initiatus Ecclesiæ Papisti- cæ sese coniungat. Et mirum est, quanto studio, labore & ceremoniarum splendore res agatur, dum talis ad baptisterium adducitur, dum patrimi sistuntur, dum pro illo spondetur, dum tingitur, & reliqua fiunt, in quibus superstitiosi summam religionis consistere persuasi sunt. At si rem ipsam pro pius examines, quid aliud dici poterit, quàm quod de istis Christus pronunciauit, quod proselytum suum faciant, duplo magis filium gehennæ quàm ipsi sint. Etenim abolita quidem est in morte Christi Iudaica religio cum vniuersis ceremonijs legalibus, neq; abs huius iniuria porrò retineri potest. Attamen qualificunq; sit, in specie saltem scripturæ sacræ testimonijs nititur. Fundamentum habet fœdus Dei cum Abrahamo factum, promissiones, & harum sigillum Circumcisionem: & in his omnibus præclara continentur de IESV CHRISTO testimonia, imò typi quibus ille adumbratur. Accedunt sancti Patres, diuini Prophetæ, pijssimi homines cum innumeris regibus & principibus viris, qui olim ista obseruarunt, & sub horum inuolucris nobiscum eiusdem cibi spiritualis ac potus participes facti sunt. Quod si vero his abiectis Iudæus baptismo tinctus ad Papistas transit, quid apud hos inueniet, quod cum Mosaicis illis vel minima ex parte conferri queat? Nonne contra omnem legis authoritatem coram toties damnatis imaginibus genua flectere & ad eas preces fundere iubebitur? Nonne panis azymi crustulam pro æterno Dei filio adorabit? Nonne eundem quotidie pro delictis viuentium & mortuorum immolari credet, aut saltem se credere simulabit, vt ferè Christianum se esse, omnibus persuadeat? Nonne in hoc sudabunt eius doctores & magistri, vt Papam Filij Dei in terris vicarium esse, claues regni cælorum administrare,
units.tr: As for what the Lord accuses the scribes and Pharisees of in his own age, would that it were not everywhere done today among those who wish to be seen as the leaders and pillars of the Christian religion. For what else do the monks do, who run hither and thither, now soliciting these men and now those, so that, leaving the way of life to which they have been called by God, and in which they could serve both him and men, they bind themselves by monastic vows? Once they have done this, they live an idle life, as if bound in handcuffs and shackles, and when they are at their best they are slothful and useless to anyone, and they rot away in their haunts; or else, while they think themselves dead to the world, they burn amid the constant flames of carnal desires, and they horribly defile and pollute both themselves and their bodies. What happens to those who, seduced by the Anabaptists, leave their wives and sweet children and pursue that new way of life, in which alone they think the most sublime men can be saved, many have experienced, and not without the most grievous struggles of conscience. As for what happens to the Jews, it is worth recalling. For there are those who think they deserve the greatest praise of holiness and learning if they can persuade some Jew to be baptized and join the Papist Church. And it is remarkable with how much zeal, labour and splendour of ceremonies the business is carried out: while such a man is brought to the baptismal font, while godparents are presented, while they stand surety for him, while he is dipped, and the rest is done, in which the superstitious are convinced that the sum of religion consists. But if you examine the matter itself with devotion, what else can be said than what Christ pronounced about these men: that they make their proselyte twice as much a child of hell as they themselves are? For indeed the Jewish religion, with all its legal ceremonies, was abolished in the death of Christ, and it cannot rightly be retained any longer. Yet, whatever it was, in appearance at least it rests on the testimonies of holy Scripture. It has as its foundation the covenant of God made with Abraham, the promises, and circumcision as the seal of these; and in all these there are clear testimonies concerning Jesus Christ, indeed the types by which he is foreshadowed. To these are added the holy Fathers, the divine Prophets, the most pious men, together with countless kings and princely men, who in former times observed these things, and under their covering have become partakers with us of the same spiritual food and drink. But if, having cast these aside, a Jew baptized in water passes over to the Papists, what will he find among them that can be compared in the least degree with those Mosaic things? Will he not be commanded, against all the authority of the Law, to bend his knee before so many times condemned images and to pour out prayers to them? Will he not worship a little wafer of unleavened bread in place of the eternal Son of God? Will he not believe, or at least pretend to believe, that the same Son is daily offered in sacrifice for the sins of the living and the dead, so that he may persuade everyone that he is almost a Christian? Will not his teachers and masters sweat in this, to show that the Pope is the vicar of the Son of God on earth, administering the keys of the kingdom of heaven,

units.la: 1.Cor.10. peccata remittere, animas ex purgatorij flammis liberare, & easdem in cælum locare, aut ad inferos detrudere credat? Ista certè nisi intrepido ore confiteatur, Christianus aut certè catholicus non erit. At quas obsecro scripturas illi proferent ex Mosè, Prophetis & Apostolis, quibus hæc portenta illi persuadeant? Quid audiet præter traditiones, Canones, decreta, miracula & alia, quæ derisionem & libilum merentur? Quis ergo non detestetur hominis leuitatem, qui relicta Lege Dei, relictis Propheticis libris, in superstitiones transit, quas nulla sacra scriptura authoritate probari audit? Quis non execretur eorum improbitatem, qui infelici tam impudenter illudunt? Aut quis negabit, illos omnes simul a religione alienos & æterna damnationis filios esse?
units.tr: 1.Cor.10. to remit sins, to free souls from the flames of purgatory, and to place them in heaven or thrust them down to hell? Certainly, unless he confesses these things with a fearless mouth, he will not be a Christian, or at least not a Catholic. But what Scriptures, I beg you, will they bring forward from Moses, the Prophets and the Apostles to persuade him of these monstrosities? What will he hear besides traditions, canons, decrees, miracles and other things that deserve derision and ridicule? Who then would not detest the levity of a man who, having abandoned the Law of God and the books of the Prophets, passes over into superstitions which he hears are proved by no authority of Holy Scripture? Who would not execrate the wickedness of those who so shamelessly mock the unhappy? Or who will deny that all of them together are alien to religion and sons of eternal damnation?

units.la: Quid vero de Hispanis dicemus, qui pra aliis Catholici dici & haberi volunt, quanta cum crudelitate & inaudita rabie in nouo orbe & apud Indos sæuierint, & quidem eo prætextu, quasi pomeria regni Christi propagare voluerint? Constat enim ex relatione eorum, qui rerum oculati testes fuerunt, infelices tam indigne & immaniter tractatos fuisse, ut nominis Christiani odium ex eo conceperint, & ad eius mentionem exhorruerint, qui prius eos immortales Deos esse credebant: quod item multi marinus vndis Baptismum, quo tincti erant, abluerint, multi domus suas incenderint, multi seipsos crudeli manu interfecerint, ne Hispanis porro seruire cogerentur. Nec minori fæuitie Galli in maris glacialis infulis grassati sunt. Dei Filius Ua illud horrendum Scribis & Pharisæis denuntiat, qui contenti fallacijs & violentia & sanguine abstinebant. Quid ergo dicturum putabimus, si miseros armis ad idololatriam cogi videret, & sub Christiani nominis prætextu terras longè late patentes multo sanguine rigari? Non ita ille olim fastidiuit, quando Euangelium in toto orbe prædicari voluit. Apostolos emisit, qui doctrina suauitate & miraculis quosuis ad fidem & salutis consortium conuerterent.
units.tr: What shall we say of the Spaniards, who wish to be called and considered Catholic above all others, and with how much cruelty and unheard-of rage they have raged in the New World and among the Indians, and indeed under the pretext that they wished to extend the boundaries of Christ's kingdom? For it is established from the report of those who were eyewitnesses of these things that the unhappy people were treated so unworthily and savagely that they conceived a hatred of the Christian name and shuddered at its mention, they who had previously believed those men to be immortal gods. Likewise many, plunging into the waves of the sea, washed away the baptism with which they had been dipped; many set fire to their houses; many killed themselves with cruel hands, lest they be forced to serve the Spaniards any longer. Nor did the French rage with less savagery on the islands of the icy sea. The Son of God pronounced that dreadful woe upon the Scribes and Pharisees, who, content with deceits, violence and blood, held back from nothing. What then shall we suppose he would say if he saw wretched men forced by arms into idolatry, and lands stretching far and wide watered with much blood under the pretext of the Christian name? Did he not once disdain such things when he wished the Gospel to be preached throughout the whole world? He sent out Apostles who would convert anyone to faith and to the fellowship of salvation by the sweetness of their teaching and by miracles.

units.la: Non debet autem ofcitanter prætermiri locutio, qua proselytos istos duplò magis filios gehennæ fore ait Dominus, quàm Scribas, a quibus seducantur. Eorum enim errorem & noxiam perfuasio nem arguit, qui se extra culpam esse arbitrantur, si se ab alijs edoceri & duci sinant, & simpliciter duces suos sequantur. Hos enim ipsis omnem culpam præstare oportere. Atqui longè aliter se res habet. Enimuero graue eorum scelus est, qui alijs errorum & perditionis authores sunt, & scimus quid scandalorum authoribus supra Dominus minitetur. Sed fit interdum, ut qui se duci sinunt, duces suos malitia & impietate superent: quod non obscure in istis annotatur, de quibus hic sermo est: & tunc adeo non iuuat excusatio ista, ut potius istorum pœna aggrauetur. Quòd si vero ijsdem vestigijs incedant qui præeunt & sequuntur, rata erit sententia, quam alibi pronuntiauit Dominus: Si cæcus cæco dux fuerit, ambo cadent in foueam. Quamobrem qui conuerti & ab interitu liberari volunt, ad Dominum conuertantur (ut apud Ieremiam dicitur) & reliquis superstitionum laqueis & sceleribus, in via veritatis ambulent. Nihil proficiunt in salutis causa, qui ex vno cæni volutabro in aliud, aut ex vno scelere in aliud æque nocens & absurdum delabuntur.
units.tr: Nor should the expression be passed over carelessly, by which the Lord says that these proselytes will be twice as much sons of hell as the Scribes by whom they are seduced. For it indicts the error and harmful persuasion of those who think they are free of blame if they allow themselves to be taught and led by others and simply follow their leaders, for they suppose that all blame must rest on those leaders. But the matter stands far otherwise. Indeed, grave is the crime of those who are authors of error and perdition to others, and we know what the Lord threatens above against the authors of scandals. Yet it sometimes happens that those who allow themselves to be led surpass their leaders in wickedness and impiety, which is not obscurely noted in those of whom this discourse speaks; and then that excuse helps so little that rather their punishment is aggravated. But if those who lead and those who follow walk in the same footsteps, the sentence which the Lord pronounced elsewhere will hold: If the blind man leads the blind, both will fall into the pit. Therefore, those who wish to be converted and freed from destruction should turn to the Lord (as is said in Jeremiah), and, leaving the remaining snares and crimes of superstition, walk in the way of truth. They gain nothing for the cause of salvation who slip from one mire of filth into another, or from one crime into another equally harmful and absurd.

units.la: Sed pergamus in Christi sermone, qui quarto loco ipsos in religione nullo gloriæ Dei sensu tantum gi, sed solius commodi priuati studio duci, ostendit. Et quia non sibi solis peccabant, sed sua partim coniuentia, partim peruerso & præposiero de sacris iudicio, alijs quoque eiusdem impietatis erant authores, grauiter admodum aduersus illos exclamat: Va vobis duces cæci, qui dicitis, &c. Quasi diceret: Vultis videri & dici duces eorum qui sunt in tenebris, sed cæci estis, & in tenebras erorum & superstitionum abducitis eos qui vos sequuntur. Id vero demonstrat casu siue exemplo ex Lege petito, sic inquiens: Dicitis: Quisquis iurauerit per templum, nihil est, id est, non fit peccati reus: quicunque autem iurauerit per aurum templi, reus est, siue tenetur, ut quod iurauit, soluat. Et paulò post: Quisquis iurauerit per altare, nihil est: quisquis autem iurauerit per donum, quod est super ipsum, reus est, &c. Quem casum D. Hieronymus ita interpretatur: Sicut in phylacteriis & fimbriis dilatatis opinio sanctitatis captabat gloriam, & per occasionem gloriæ quærebat lucrum: sic alia traditionis stropha impietatis arguit præceptores. Si quis in contentione seu in aliquo iurgio, vel in causa ambiguo iuraffet in templo, & postea conuictus esset mendacij, non tenebatur criminis reus. Sin autem iurasset in auro & pecunia, quæ in templo sacerdotibus offerebatur, statim id in quo iurauerat, cogebatur exoluere. Rursus si quis iurasset in altari, periurij retum nemo retinebat. Sin autem periurasset in oblationibus, hoc est, in hostijs, in victimis, & in similia
units.tr: But let us proceed with Christ's discourse, which, in the fourth place, shows that they were led in religion not by any zeal for God's glory but solely by the pursuit of private advantage. And because they did not sin only for themselves, but partly by their connivance and partly by a perverse and preposterous judgment about sacred things, they were also authors of the same impiety to others, and he cries out very gravely against them: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, etc. As if he said: You wish to seem and be called leaders of those who are in darkness, but you are blind, and you lead into the darkness of errors and superstitions those who follow you. He demonstrates this by a case or example taken from the Law, saying thus: You say: Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing, that is, he does not become guilty of sin; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is guilty, or bound to pay what he swore. And a little later: Whoever swears by the altar is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is upon it is guilty, etc. Jerome interprets this case thus: Just as in phylacteries and enlarged fringes the opinion of holiness sought glory, and through the occasion of glory sought gain, so another quibble of tradition convicts the teachers of impiety. If anyone in a dispute or quarrel, or in some ambiguous matter, swore by the temple and was afterwards convicted of lying, he was not held guilty of crime. But if he swore by the gold and money that was offered to the priests in the temple, he was at once compelled to pay what he had sworn by. Again, if anyone swore by the altar, no one held him guilty of perjury; but if he perjured himself by the offerings, that is, by the victims, and in similar

units.la: Priuati commodi studium. simila & caeteris quæ offeruntur Deo super altare, hæc studiosissimè repetebantur. Itaq; Dominus illos stultitiæ & fraudulentiæ arguit, quòd hæc conniuentia communi superstitioni & errori occasionem præberent, vt nimirum vulgò aurum siue pecuniam, quæ in templo sub sacerdotum custodia asseruabatur, pluris quam illud ipsum templum fieret: victimæ item & sacrificia præstarent altari. Ita vero bifariam peccabatur. Primum iurando per ea, quæ non debebant in iuramentum adhiberi. Deus enim per suum nomen iurare iusserat, & supra capite quinto, ne per quid aliud iuretur, Christus ipse prohibuit. Peruersò iudicia item, & quòd lucri causa seuerius exigebantur iuramenta, quæ concepta erant per aurum & denaria quàm quæ per ipsum templum (nimirum quòd hæc redimi poterant, templi verò pretium maius erat omni redemptione.) Fiebat ergo vt templum & altare præ oblationibus vilescerent, & vulgò pluris facerent aurum, pecuniam & quodvis donarium, quàm ipsum altare aut templum. Id verò perperam fieri, communis sensus docebat: at quia illi id non animaduertebant, acri correptione eos reprehendens: Stulti & cæci, vtrum maius est aurum an templum, quo aurum sanctificatur? Itaque stulti & cæci, vtrum maius est munus, an altare quod sanctificat munus? Quasi diceret: Quæ haec stultitia, quæ cæcitas est, non videre, quòd omnis auri istius dignitas a templo, & omnis donariorum reuerentia ab altari pendet. Nisi ad altare ducerentur victimæ, & Deo consecrarentur, nihil ab alijs pecudibus differentes nisi templo, & per consequens Deo donarentur ista pecunia siue aurū, nō maior esset eius, quàm alterius communis auri & pecuniæ dignitas. Sed hic quoq; fiebat, quod de muneribus in lege pronunciatur, quòd excæcent oculos sapientum & peruertant causas iustas. Oblationum enim splendore & lucri desiderio fascinati sacerdotes inter res sacras non poterant distinguere, & ex illis error ad totum populum dimanabat.
units.tr: The pursuit of private gain. Things and others offered to God upon the altar were most eagerly sworn by. Therefore the Lord rebukes them for folly and deceit, because this connivance offered occasion to common superstition and error, namely that gold or money kept in the temple under the custody of the priests was valued more highly than the temple itself, and likewise that the victims and sacrifices were valued above the altar. Thus they sinned in two ways: first, by swearing by those things which ought not to be used in an oath (for God had commanded that oaths be sworn by his own name, and in chapter five Christ himself forbade swearing by anything else); and secondly, by perverse judgments, since for the sake of gain oaths were exacted more strictly when they were framed by gold and denarii than by the temple itself (namely because these could be redeemed, whereas the price of the temple was greater than any redemption). Thus it came about that the temple and the altar became cheap in comparison with the offerings, and commonly gold, money and any gift were valued more than the altar or the temple itself. That this was done wrongly, common sense taught; but because they did not notice it, he rebuked them with sharp reproof: Fools and blind, which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold? And so, fools and blind, which is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift? As if he said: What folly, what blindness is this, not to see that all the dignity of that gold depends on the temple, and all the reverence of the offerings on the altar. Unless the victims were led to the altar and consecrated to God, differing from other cattle in nothing but the temple, and consequently unless that money or gold were given to God, its dignity would be no greater than that of other common gold and money. But here also happened what is said of gifts in the law, that they blind the eyes of the wise and pervert just causes. For the priests, bewitched by the splendour of the offerings and the desire for gain, could not distinguish between sacred things, and from them the error flowed out to the whole people.

units.la: Admonet ergo locus hic, quantum mali in religione pariat antistitum auaritia. Non sinit hæc videre quod verù & rectum est: & qui quæstum facere student, non modò conniuent ad vulgi errores, verumetiam eos fouent & augent suis fabulis, vt maius lucrū faciant. Exempla huius generis multa passim extant. In papatu horrendi errores cum exorcismis, sputo, sale, oleo feruntur in Baptismo, quia hæc omnia sacrificulis lucrosa sunt. Maiori cum honore oscula deferuntur ossibus mortuorum incognitis, quàm sacrosancto Bibliorum Codici: quia ex illis vbere messem colligunt Sacerdotes. Pluris fit impurum cælibatus, quàm coniugij castitas: quia ex illo vectigal ingens decerpunt Episcopi. Traditiones de ciborum delectu & ieiunijs in maiori pretio sunt, quàm libertas Christiana, per quam omnibus cum gratiarum actione vesci licet: quia illæ alendis monachorum luxuriis inseruiunt. Missa priuata, quæ inani spectaculo populi oculos pascit, præfertur cænæ Dominica, in qua Dei Filius carnem & sanguinem suum credentium animabus propinat. Quid, quòd in multis locis Dei leges, sine quibus religio non potest consistere, impune licet violare, traditionum autem transgressores capite plectuntur? Si imaginem ligneam deflruxeris, inexcusabile scelus commisisti, & vix vna morte expiandum: si hominem viuum Dei viuentis imaginem deleueris vili & iniusto pretio conductus, Catholici nomen mereris. Si sacerdos concubinam alat, domum propriam spurijs compleat, alienis quoq; thoris infidelitur, dignus ecclesiastico munere habetur: Sin vxore vna & legitimè ducta contentus honestè viuat, viuus exuri merebitur. Sed dies me deficerit, si quæcunq; iniqua, absurda, impia hodie fiunt, ex ordine commemorare libeat. Quis ergo indignetur nobis, aut miretur, si cum Christo Domino clamemus, Væ vobis duces cæci?
units.tr: Therefore this passage shows how much harm the greed of prelates brings to religion. Greed does not let people see what is true and right. Those who strive to make gain not only connive at the errors of the crowd but also foster and increase them with their fables, so as to make greater profit. Examples of this kind are found everywhere. In the papacy, horrible errors involving exorcisms, spittle, salt and oil are carried over into Baptism, because all these things are profitable to the little priests. Bones of unknown dead are kissed with greater honour than the most holy codex of the Bible, because the priests gather a rich harvest from them. Impure celibacy is valued more highly than the chastity of marriage, because the bishops pluck a huge tax from it. Traditions about the choice of foods and fasts are held in higher esteem than Christian liberty, by which everyone may eat everything with thanksgiving, because those traditions serve to feed the luxuries of the monks. The private Mass, which feeds the people's eyes with an empty spectacle, is preferred to the Lord's Supper, in which the Son of God gives his flesh and blood to the souls of believers as drink. What of the fact that in many places God's laws, without which religion cannot stand, may be violated with impunity, while transgressors of traditions are punished by death? If you destroy a wooden image, you have committed an inexcusable crime, scarcely expiable by a single death; but if, hired for a vile and unjust price, you destroy a living man, the image of the living God, you earn the name of Catholic. If a priest keeps a concubine, fills his house with bastards, and unfaithfully sleeps in other men's beds, he is considered worthy of an ecclesiastical office; but if he is content with one lawfully married wife and lives honourably, he deserves to be burned alive. But the day would fail me if I wished to recount in order all the unjust, absurd and impious things done today. Who then will be indignant with us, or wonder, if with Christ the Lord we cry: Woe to you, blind guides?

units.la: Porrò subtexit huic loco de iuramentis grauem admonitionem: Fatui (inquit) & cæci, qui in rauerit per altare, iurat per ipsum & per omnia, quæ super illud sunt. Et qui iurauerit per templū, iurat per ipsum & per eum, qui habitat in eo. Et qui iurauerit per cælum, iurat per thronum Dei, et per eum qui sedet super eum. Non debent hæc ita accipi, quasi hoc loco probet iurandi formulas per cælum, terram, Ierosolymam, templum, caput tuum, quas alibi prohibuit, sed errorem quem hic corrigit, ad suum fontem reuocat, vt iurandi reuerentiam nobis commendet. Vnde enim præpostera hæc iurandi licentia exorta erat? Ex eo nimirum, quòd nō obseruabant, Deum in toto suo cultu & singulis eius partibus præsentem esse, & templum Dei domum esse, in quo suæ bonitatis indicia & testimonia nobis exhibeat, quemadmodum in cælo, tanquam throno regali, gloriæ & maiestatis suæ spectimen præbet. Quod qui recte expendunt, ij potius a iurando abstrerrebuntur, neque per villam creaturam iurabunt, quando cogitant Deum cœlos & terram implere, ac omnia effeint omnibus. Curabunt ergo, ne per aliquid iurando Dei nomine aut ijs quæ ad hunc spectant, temerè abutantur. Si quando autem iurare iubet necessitas, id sanctè & religiosè facient per nomen veri Dei, in fide Filij sui IESV CHRISTI Domini nostri, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, he appends to this passage a grave admonition about oaths: "Fools and blind men, whoever swears by the altar, swears by it and by all that is upon it. And whoever swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who dwells in it. And whoever swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it." These words should not be taken to mean that in this place he approves of formulas of swearing by heaven, earth, Jerusalem, the temple or your head, which he forbade elsewhere. Rather, he recalls to its source the error he corrects here, in order to commend to us reverence in swearing. For whence did this preposterous licence in swearing arise? Surely from this: that people did not observe that God is present in his whole worship and in each of its parts, that the temple is the house of God, in which he displays to us the evidences and testimonies of his goodness, and that from heaven, as from a royal throne, he shows a token of his glory and majesty. Those who weigh this rightly would rather be restrained from swearing, nor would they swear by any creature, since they reflect that God fills heaven and earth and effects all things in all. They will therefore take care not to abuse rashly, by swearing, the name of God or the things that pertain to him. If ever necessity bids them swear, they will do so holily and religiously by the name of the true God, in faith in his Son JESUS CHRIST our Lord, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXIX.
units.tr: HOMILY 269.

units.la: Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi hypocritæ, quoniam decimatis mentham & anethum & cuminum, & omittitis quæ graviora sunt Legis, iudicium & misericordiam ac fidem: hæc oportuit facere & illa non omittere. Duces cæci, qui excolatis culicem, camelum autem deglutitis.
units.tr: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and neglect the weightier matters of the Law: judgment, mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others. Blind guides, who strain out a gnat and swallow a camel.

units.la: NON temerè factu putemus, quod Dei Filius IESVS CHRISTVS Scribis & Pharisæis inter alia vitia hypocrisim potissimum exprobrat & propter hac illos exitio devovet. Quia enim Deus Spiritus & Veritas est, in spiritu & veritate coli & adorari vult, nec poterit ipsi gratus esse cultus, qui hypocrisi aut simulatione adulteratur. Quomodo enim ex animo illum timebit aut diliget, qui de illo non sublimius sentit, quam quod ei ab homine fucu fieri posse existimat? Ad hæc perfuasio ista errorum & vitiorum gravissimorum fons & origo est. Nam primo ambitionem parit, ut ab hominibus spectari & probari cupiant hypocritæ. Quod ubi se assecutos putant, solùm suis rebus intenti gloriam Dei facile negligunt, ut nuper in ijs vidimus, quæ de iuramentis Scribæ statuerunt. Accedit his commune vitium, quod de rebus leviculis soliciti, præcipua religionis capita, ex quibus salus omnis dependet non magni faciunt. Etenim dum hominum iudicio satisfaciant, gravissima delicta factisfactionibus nullius pretij, vel etiam ridiculis expiari posse arbitrantur. Et huius rei exemplum in præsenti proponitur.
units.tr: We should not think it without purpose that the Son of God, Jesus Christ, reproaches the scribes and Pharisees above all for hypocrisy, among their other faults, and on account of it consigns them to destruction. For since God is Spirit and Truth, he wills to be worshipped in spirit and in truth, and that worship cannot please him which is corrupted by hypocrisy or pretence. For how will a man fear or love from the heart one who thinks of God no more highly than that he can be deceived by human pretence? Moreover, this persuasion is the source and origin of very grave errors and vices. For first it produces ambition, so that hypocrites desire to be seen and approved by men. When they think they have achieved this, intent only on their own affairs, they easily neglect the glory of God, as we recently saw in the rulings the scribes made about oaths. To this is added a common fault: anxious about trifling matters, they make little of the chief heads of religion, on which all salvation depends. For while they satisfy the judgment of men, they suppose that the gravest sins can be expiated by satisfactions of no worth, or even by ridiculous ones. An example of this is set before us in the present passage.

units.la: Pergit enim in taxandis hypocritis istis Dominus, dicens: Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi hypocritæ, quoniam decimatis mentham & anethum & cuminum, & omittitis quæ graviora sunt Legis, &c. Quæ ut rectius intelligantur, aliquid de decimis dicendum erit, circa quas hodie etiam non uno modo peccari constat. Originem decimarum antiquissimam esse, Moses testatur, quando Abrahamum a clade Orientalium regum redeuntem Melchisedecho Regi Salem & Sacerdoti Altissimi decimas ex præda hostibus erepta dedisse scribit: & hoc ita narratur, ut satis appareat, id pijs hominibus in more fuisse, ut si quid ipsis ex animi sententia feliciter succesisset, aut singulares Dei beneuolentiam, decimarum oblatione gratitudinem sua testarentur. Et Iacob in Mesopotamiam fugiens Domino decimas vouebat omnium, quæ illic acquireret, si incolumis reverteretur: Postea cum inter Israelitas Templum & religionem constituisset Deus, legem tulit, ut ex proventu terræ decimas ipsi reddant. Et ut in Malachia nostro annotavimus, tria harum genera fuerunt. Primum enim quotannis decimæ Leuitis dabantur ex universis frugibus. Quia enim Leuitas sibi consecrauerat Deus loco primogenitorum omnium, ut suo cultui & Legis doctrinæ vacarent, & ideo illis, quos per omnes tribus dispersos habitare oportebat, propria pars terræ ut aliis tribubus assignari non potuit, primitias & decimas frugum omnium illis donavit Dominus, ne in publico ministerio divini cultus occupatus necessaria vitæ subsidia deessent. Deinde alterum genus decimarum erat, quas ex suis decimis Leuitæ, id est, inferior ministrorum ordo summo Sacerdoti solvebant. Tertium earum fuit, quæ tertio quoque anno ad pauperum viduarum, pupillorum & peregrinorum inopiam subleuandam reponebantur. Itaque decimarum vsus multiplex & reuerfanctus fuit. Per has enim admonebantur priusquam singulis a Deo dari fruges terræ, cui illi hac gratiam referri debeant, ut illis pie & religiose frui possint. Deinde ad conseruationem divini cultus faciebant, quapropter Deus illas sibi vendicabat, & ideo Leuitis dicebat: Cum acceperitis decimas a filijs Israel, quas ego de ipsis dedi vobis, ut sint hereditas vestra, &c. Et paulò post, Repu-tabitur vobis ut proventus area aut torcularis, comedetis ea in omni loco, vos & filij vestri: quoniam hæc est merces vestra pro ministerio vestro, &c. Præterea ex illis pauperes alebantur, qui non minima Ecclesiæ pars sunt. Idcirco Deus posteris temporibus seueriter decimas requisiuit, si quando in illis reddendis negligentiores aut parum fideles essent. Apud Malachiam certè sacrilegij illos accusat, & se ab illis spoliari, & ideo maledictos & execrationi obnoxios esse dicit, & vicissim vberem benedictionem pollicetur, si quod illi debetur, fideliter reddant. Adducite (inquit) omnes decimas ad domum thesauri, vt sit cibus in domo mea: atq; in hoc periculum quaso de mesumite, dicit Dominus exercituum, si non aperuero vobis fenestras cœli, & benedictionem deprompsero, vt non sit sufficientia, id est, vt frugibus colligendis & recondendis non possitis sufficere.
units.tr: For the Lord, in censuring these hypocrites, goes on to say: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and neglect the weightier matters of the Law, etc. So that these words may be understood more rightly, something must be said about tithes, in which it is plain that people even today sin in more than one way. Moses testifies that the origin of tithes is very ancient, when he writes that Abraham, returning from the slaughter of the eastern kings, gave Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the Most High, tithes of the spoil taken from the enemy. And this is narrated in such a way that it is clear enough that it was the custom of godly men, if anything had gone well for them according to their wish, or if they had received some singular goodwill of God, to bear witness to their gratitude by offering tithes. And Jacob, fleeing into Mesopotamia, vowed to the Lord tithes of all that he should acquire there, if he returned safely. Later, when God had established the temple and religion among the Israelites, he enacted a law that they should give him tithes from the produce of the land. As we noted in our commentary on Malachi, there were three kinds of these. The first: each year tithes of all the fruits were given to the Levites. For God had consecrated the Levites to himself in place of all the firstborn, so that they might be free for his worship and the teaching of the Law. Since they were to live dispersed among all the tribes, they could not be assigned a proper portion of land as the other tribes were, so the Lord gave them the firstfruits and tithes of all the produce, so that, occupied in the public ministry of divine worship, they would not lack the necessary supports of life. The second kind of tithe was that which the Levites, that is, the lower order of ministers, paid to the high priest out of their own tithes. The third was that which, every third year, was set aside to relieve the need of widows, orphans and strangers. Thus the use of tithes was manifold and religious. For through them the people were reminded, before each individual received the fruits of the earth from God, that they ought to render thanks to him, so that they might enjoy them piously and reverently. Then the tithes served to maintain divine worship, and for this reason God claimed them for himself. Hence he said to the Levites: When you have received from the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you from them as your inheritance, etc. And shortly after: It shall be reckoned to you as the produce of the threshing floor or of the winepress; you shall eat it in every place, you and your sons, for this is your reward for your ministry, etc. Moreover, the poor were fed from them, and they are no small part of the Church. Therefore in later times God demanded tithes strictly, whenever people were negligent or not faithful enough in paying them. In Malachi he certainly accuses them of sacrilege, and says that he is robbed by them, and therefore that they are accursed and liable to execration; and in turn he promises abundant blessing if they faithfully pay what is owed to him. Bring, he says, all the tithes into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house; and in this, I beg you, put me to the test, says the Lord of hosts: if I do not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing, so that there will not be sufficient room, that is, so that you cannot manage to gather and store the crops.

units.la: Debent hæc ad Ecclesiam noui testamenti transferri. Etsi enim Leuiticum sacerdotium abolitum sit, & sacra legalia cessarint, manet tamen ministerium Euangelij, quod absq; ministris ordinarijs non poterit consistere: neq; deerunt vnquam pauperes, quos suo loco substituit Dei Filius, vt in hos conferamus, quæ in ipsum collaturi essemus officia, si ille in terris viueret. Atqui ide Euangelij administros confert, quibus sua merces debeatur: & Paulus ad Corinthios scribens, prolixè docet tam iustum & æquû esse, vt ex Euangelio viuant, qui Euangelium prædicant, quàm iustum fuit olim, vt ex sacrario ederent, qui sacris operabantur, & altari assidebat. At quæ iustior ratio ministros alendi excogitari potest, quàm vt ex decimis viuant, qui publicæ salutis administri sunt? Etenim vt Origenes olim rectè monuit, nisi necessaria vitæ subsidia dentur sacerdotibus, ipsi in talibus occupati, minus vacabunt Legi Dei: his autem non vacantibus Verbo Dei, tu periclitaris: Obscurabitur enim lux scientiæ, quæ in illis est, te non subministrante oleum lucernæ. Nec est quòd aliquis decimarum legem cum ceremonijs abolitam esse dicat. Nam vt diximus, etiamsi illæ abrogatæ sint, durat tamen adhuc ministerium Ecclesiæ, & propter Verbi prædicationem, & Sacramentorum administrationem adhuc ministris opus est, quibus vt Deo mi litare possint, de victu prospici oportet, ne vitæ negotijs ad rem familiare pertinentibus implicentur. Quibus autem argumentis probari poterit, decimarum legem vnquam a Deo abrogatam esse. Illas quidem a Iudæorum Sacerdotibus impiè interceptas, & in vsus alios translatas esse legimus, sed cùm decimæ principibus quoq; debeantur, vt ex iure Regis apud Samuelem apparet, & Christiani reges atq; principes Ecclesiam frugum decimis & alijs redditibus annuis auxerint, sacri legij culpa non vacabit, qui aliquid horum ausus fuerit negare aut subtrahere. Idq; eò constantius affirmamus, quòd prædia fere ea conditione vel venduntur, vel ad hæredes legitimos perueniunt, vt decimæ annuorum prouentuum ex illis reddantur. Qui ergo has negant, vel in eis fraudem admittunt, multifariam peccant. Primò parni faciunt gratiam Dei, quando piget illos sumptum facere in ijs, per quæ ille seipsum & omnes regni sui thesauros nobis offert. Deinde illi negant quod debetur, cuius liberalitate toto anno aluntur: cui deniq; se totos debent & quicquid habent. Iniusti item operarijs mercedem suam, impij verò egenis Christi membris a Deo destinatam alimoniam negant. Obijciunt autem plerosq; decimis turpiter abuti: multos etiam illas transferre ad illicita & prophana studia, vt ex Ecclesiæ bonis comessentur, scortentur, vsuras faciant, & opes iniquas & iniustas congerant. At calua est hæc excusatio. De his enim Deo rationem reddent qui ista faciunt, non qui decimas reddunt. Aut quæ ratio excusabit eum, qui egenti necessarium victum surripit, ne forte eo abutatur ad ebrietatem & crapulam? Christiani hominis est ea reddere cuius quod debetur, non autem suam iniquitatem alterius culpa excusare velle.
units.tr: These things ought to be transferred to the Church of the New Testament. For although the Levitical priesthood has been abolished and the legal rites have ceased, the ministry of the Gospel remains, which cannot continue without ordinary ministers. Nor will there ever be lack of the poor, whom the Son of God has put in his place, so that what we would have offered to him, had he lived on earth, we may confer on them. Now he also grants ministers of the Gospel to whom their reward is due. And Paul, writing to the Corinthians, teaches at length that it is as just and fair that those who preach the Gospel should live by the Gospel, as it was once just that those who served in the sacred rites should eat from the temple, and those who attended the altar should share in it. But what more just plan can be devised for feeding ministers than that those who serve the public good should live on tithes? For, as Origen rightly warned long ago, unless the necessary supports of life are given to priests, they, being occupied with such things, will have less leisure for the Law of God; and if they have no leisure for the Word of God, you are in danger. For the light of the knowledge that is in them will be darkened if you do not supply oil for the lamp. Nor is there any reason for someone to say that the law of tithes was abolished along with the ceremonies. For, as we have said, even if those were abrogated, the ministry of the Church still endures, and on account of the preaching of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, ministers are still needed. They must be provided with food, so that they can serve God and not be entangled in the affairs of life that pertain to household matters. But by what arguments could it be proved that the law of tithes was ever abrogated by God? We read indeed that tithes were impiously seized by the Jewish priests and turned to other uses; but since tithes are also owed to princes, as is clear from the law of the king in Samuel, and Christian kings and princes have enriched the Church with tithes of produce and other annual revenues, whoever dares to deny or withhold any of these will not be free from the guilt of sacrilege. And we affirm this all the more firmly because estates are generally sold, or pass to lawful heirs, on the condition that the tithes of their annual yields are paid from them. Those, then, who deny these tithes, or commit fraud in them, sin in many ways. First, they make little of the grace of God, when they begrudge spending on the things through which he offers himself and all the treasures of his kingdom to us. Next, they deny what is owed to him by whose generosity they are sustained through the whole year, to whom in the end they owe themselves entirely and all that they have. They also deny wages to workers unjustly, and to the needy members of Christ the support God has appointed, wickedly. Many, however, object that people shamefully misuse tithes, and that many turn them to unlawful and profane pursuits, so that they eat, whore, lend at interest and heap up wicked and unjust wealth from the goods of the Church. But this excuse is worthless. For those who do such things will give an account to God for them, not those who pay the tithes. Or what reason will excuse the man who takes from the needy the food he requires, lest perhaps he misuse it for drunkenness and gluttony? It is the duty of a Christian to pay what is owed, not to seek to excuse his own wickedness by another's fault.

units.la: Sed tempus est, vt ad Christi verba accedamus, in quibus quæstio occurrit, cur in Scribis & Pharisæis reprehendat, imò execretur id quod per se licitum, & diserte a Deo mandatum erat? Etenim Legis diuinæ verba sunt: Decimando decimabis cunctos prouentus sementis tuæ, quos terra quottannis depromit. Sed facilis est responsio. Etenim primò operum suorum iustitiæ sidebant, & in eo meritum salutis statuebant, quòd decimas ex debito persoluerent. Exemplum huius fiduciæ Pharisæus in Euangelio præbuit, qui seorsim ceu iustior & sanctior alijs cœsistens precabatur: Deus gratias ago tibi, quòd non sim vt reliqui homines, rapaces, iniusti, vel vt iste publicanus, ieiuno bis hebdomade, decimo quacunque poßideo. Itaque etsi nihil vitij acceßiffet, sola hac fiducia in ftar fermenti opus illud perse bonum poterat Deo insipidum reddere: sicuti in ieiunijs & eleemosynis ipsorum factum fuisse supra capite sexto vidimus. Sed quod initio monuimus, in leuiculis occupati negligebant quae maioris momenti erant: & credibile est eos ex mentha quidem, anetho item & cumino & quouis olere viliori (vt apud Lucam annotatur) decimas dedisse, vt iustitiae eximiam opinionem sibi apud vulgus comparărent: interim non tam liberales & fideles fuisse in reliquis, quae maioris pretij erant. Certe quae grauiora erant, iudicium, misericordiam & fidem illos omisisse dicit. Quia enim auarissimi erant, quis dubitet illos hoc vnum spectasse, vt quam minimo dispendio Deo simul & hominibus fucum facerent. Quam absurda autem & praepostera sit illorum iustitia siue sanctitas, prouerbiali paramia docet, quando illos duces caecos dicit, vt nuper quoque, qui cum licem anxiè colare soleant, deglutiant autem camelum. Et talis est hodie quoque hypocritarum sanctitas, quos auaritia & quaestus priuati studium fascinat. Enimuero monachi in Papatu solicitè cauent, ne quid sui ordinis statutis aut regulis contrarium faciant in vestitu, esu, incessu, gestu, aut aliis quae nusquam requirit Dominus: Interim ijsdem nulla religio est falsa doctrina populum seducere, sub confessionis auricularis praetextu & inanibus iguis purgatorij terriculamentis haereditatem alienam intercipere, virgines constuprare, alienos thoros polluere, bella non necessaria cire, & orbem totum dissidijs capitalibus turbare. Imitantur hos quicunque illos sibi magistros & dolores fecerunt. His capitale scelus putatur, tempore quadragesimali aut diebus Venerij carnibus ouis aut lacticiniis vescendi, die festo opus aliquod honestum & necessarium facere, votum imprudenter & temere factum non exoluere, Missam negligere, aut quid aliud eius generis facere. At si per totum vitae tempus ex vsuris & sanguinis pretio helluentur, scortentur, luxu & fastu diffluant diris aut blasphemijs horrendis sacrosanctum Dei nomen proscindant, nulla tantorum scelerum conscientia tanguntur. Nec extra omnem culpam sunt qui Euangelij doctrinam & fidem profitentur. Etenim inter Verbi ministros inueniuntur, qui in concionibus leuicula & nihil ad ipsos pertinentia odiose vrgent, populi item pauperis vitia mirifice & plus quam tragicis clamoribus exagitant: tacent autem, quando Dei gloria & publica honestas aut salus periclitatur, & si prin-cipum scelera, quae cum publico scandalo coniuncta sunt, atgui & corrigi debeant, canes muti sunt. Offendunt ad hunc lapidem viri principes & qui in magistratu sunt constituti: dum quae ad suam existimationem spectant, tributa item, vectigalia & multas pecuniarias rigide & inclementer exigunt, dormitant autem in ijs, quae faciunt ad cultum Dei & publicam morum honestatem. Quae causa est, quod ipsorum quoque authoritas collabitur, secundum illud: Honorantes me honorabo, &c. Sed & in parentibus priuatim hoc vitium passim deprehendere licet, dum cauent ne quid faciant ipsorum liberi, quod ipsis obstare possit, ne ad coniugia opulenta & honorata admittantur: vt vero pie & sancte viuant, parum ipsis cura est. De his vero dixerim, eos liberis suis nihil plus prestare, quam fera & agrestes bellua suis catulis. Christianorum est in suis vitia morum corrigere, puriorem fidei doctrinam tenere aetati insillare, & in pietate vera instituere, quae si nos nostra forte contentos faciat, quaestus est longe vberrimus. Poterant haec latius diduci, vt de coniugibus quoque & seruis diceretur, sed sufficiat occasionem praebuisse pijs, qui serio pietatis sensu afficiuntur.
units.tr: But it is time to come to the words of Christ, in which the question arises why he reproves, indeed execrates, the Scribes and Pharisees for something that in itself was lawful and had been expressly commanded by God. For the words of the divine Law are: "You shall tithe all the produce of your seed, which the land brings forth year by year." But the answer is easy. First, they relied on the righteousness of their own works and placed the merit of salvation in the fact that they paid tithes as a debt owed. The Pharisee in the Gospel gave an example of this confidence, who, standing apart as though more upright and holier than others, prayed: "God, I thank you that I am not like other men, grasping, unjust, or like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all that I possess." So even if no fault had attached to it, this confidence alone, like leaven, could make that work, good in itself, unsavoury to God, as we saw above in chapter six concerning their fasting and almsgiving. But, as we noted at the outset, occupied with trifles they neglected what was of greater importance. It is believable that they tithed mint, dill, cumin and any cheaper herb (as Luke records), so as to win for themselves a great reputation for righteousness among the common people, while meanwhile they were not so generous and faithful in the weightier matters. Certainly he says they omitted judgement, mercy and faith, which were the more serious matters. Since they were extremely greedy, who would doubt that they aimed at this one thing, namely to deceive both God and men at the smallest cost? How absurd and perverse their righteousness or holiness was, the proverb teaches, when he calls them blind guides, who strain out a gnat with anxious care but swallow a camel. And the holiness of hypocrites is just as much like this today, those whom greed and the pursuit of private gain bewitch. Indeed, in the Papacy the monks take anxious care lest they do anything contrary to the statutes or rules of their order in dress, food, walking, bearing, or other matters the Lord nowhere requires; yet they have no scruple about seducing the people with false doctrine, under the pretext of auricular confession and with the empty terrors of the fires of purgatory, snatching others' inheritances, debauching virgins, defiling other men's beds, stirring up unnecessary wars, and throwing the whole world into turmoil with deadly divisions. Whoever has made these men their masters and idols imitates them. For these people a capital crime is thought to be eating meat, eggs or dairy in Lent or on Fridays, doing some honest and necessary work on a feast day, failing to fulfil a vow rashly and carelessly made, neglecting the Mass, or doing something else of that kind. But if throughout their whole life they gorge themselves on usury and the price of blood, indulge in fornication, overflow with luxury and pride, and tear the most holy name of God with dreadful oaths and horrible blasphemies, they are not troubled by any awareness of such great wickedness. Nor are those who profess the doctrine and faith of the Gospel free of all blame. For among the ministers of the Word there are those who in their sermons harshly press trifling matters that have nothing to do with their hearers, and who rebuke the vices of the poor people with wonderful and more than tragic outcries; yet they are silent when the glory of God, public decency or public welfare is in danger; and if the crimes of princes, which are joined with public scandal, must be corrected, they are dumb dogs. Men who are princes, and those set in the magistracy, stumble over this stone: they demand taxes, duties and fines rigidly and without mercy, insofar as these concern their own reputation, but they sleep through the matters that pertain to the worship of God and the public decency of morals. This is the reason why their own authority also collapses, according to the saying: "Those who honour me I will honour," etc. And this fault can be found everywhere in private parents too, who take care that their children do nothing that could stand in their way, lest they be admitted to rich and honourable marriages; but they care little whether they live piously and holily. Of these I would say that they give their children no more than wild and savage beasts give their whelps. It is the duty of Christians to correct the vices of their own households, to keep the purer doctrine of the faith, to instil it in their young and to train them in true piety; if this makes us content with what we have, it is a most abundant gain. These things could be spread out more widely, so that it might also be said of spouses and servants, but let it suffice to have offered an occasion to the godly, who are seriously moved by a sense of piety.

units.la: Audiamus vero Dei Filium IESVM CHRISTVM, qui paucis docet, in quo vera Legis obseruatio sive pietas consistat. Cum enim dixisset ipsos circa mentham, anethum & cuminum occupatos grauiora legis capita omittere, quae sunt iudicium, Misericordia, Fides vel Amor Dei, vt Lucas annotauit, breue dictum subtexit: Haec oportuit facere, & illa non omittere. Totius legis studium commendat, cuius praecepta differunt, vt alia sint leuiora, alia grauiora. Haec ita dicuntur, quod in eis cultus Dei & vita puritas consistat, & quod non nisi a germanis Dei filijs praestentur: quali assunt Decalogus totus, & quae paulo ante recitauimus. Leuiora dicuntur quae in solius corporis exercitio consistunt, & ab hypocritis quoque possunt fieri: quales sunt decimationes, feria, ieiunia, sacrificia denique & ceremonia omnes, si omisso mystico sensu secundum literam considerentur. Debet autem in verbis considerari hoc Christi dictum: vt nimirum in minimis quoque obsequium Deo praestemus. Etsi enim legis praecepta differant, vnus tamen & idem eorum author est.
units.tr: But let us hear the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who in a few words teaches in what the true observance of the Law, or piety, consists. For when he had said that they, occupied with mint, dill and cumin, omitted the weightier matters of the Law, which are judgement, mercy, faith, or love of God, as Luke noted, he added a brief saying: "These you ought to have done, and not to have left the others undone." He commends the whole zeal for the Law, whose precepts differ, so that some are lighter and others weightier. These are called weightier because in them the worship of God and the purity of life consist, and because they can be performed only by the true children of God; such are the whole Decalogue and the things we recited a little earlier. Those are called lighter which consist only in the outward exercise of the body, and which hypocrites too can perform; such are tithes, feasts, fasts, sacrifices, and in short all ceremonies, if they are considered according to the letter without the mystical sense. Moreover, in these words of Christ this should be considered: that we should also show obedience to God in the smallest things. For although the precepts of the Law differ, nevertheless they have one and the same author.

units.la: Obseruatio legis in quo consistat. est idem omnium finis & scopus, & ita cohærent, ut nemini liceat illa discerpere. Nam ut Iacobus ait, qui dixit, Ne mœcheris, dixit etiam, Ne occidas. Itaque si non fueris mœchatus, occideris autem, factus es transgressor legis: & quisquis totam legem seruauerit, offenderit autem in vno, omnibus tenetur, violata nimirum Legislatoris voluntate & authoritate, quæ in omnibus præceptis sacrosanctis nobis esse debebat. Et de eo non obscurè nos admonuit Moses, quando filijs Israel dixit: Maledictus omnis, qui non manserit in omnibus, quæ scripta sunt in libro Legis, ut faciat ea. Ergo nefas est negligere ea, quæ minoris momenti videri poterant. Et qui in paruis assuescunt peccare, ij plerunque viterius progrediuntur, sicut in Saulis exemplo est videre. Ideo de lictis etiam minoribus in speciem pœnæ capitales constitutæ fuerunt, ut si quis circumcisus non effet, fermentum gustasset diebus paschalibus, aut tale quid fecisset, quod carni leuiculum videtur. Interim ne obedientia nostra Pharisaica sit, præcipua illa non negligi debent, in quibus salus nostra potissimum versatur.
units.tr: In what the observance of the Law consists. The aim and purpose of all of them is the same, and they cohere so closely that no one is allowed to tear them apart. For as James says, he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not kill." So if you have not committed adultery but have killed, you have become a transgressor of the Law; and whoever has kept the whole Law but has offended in one point is bound by all, since the will and authority of the Lawgiver, which ought to be sacred to us in all precepts, has been violated. Moses also warned us of this plainly when he said to the sons of Israel: "Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them." Therefore it is wrong to neglect those things which might seem of less importance. And those who are accustomed to sin in small things usually go further, as is seen in the example of Saul. For this reason even for lesser offences capital penalties were established, as a kind of punishment: for example, if a man was not circumcised, or had eaten leaven during the Passover days, or had done something of that sort that seems trifling to the flesh. Yet, so that our obedience may not be Pharisaical, those weightier matters, on which our salvation chiefly depends, ought not to be neglected.

units.la: Sunt hæc tria numero. Primum est iudicium, id est, ipsa iustitia & æquitas, qua suum cuique tribuitur, & quæ cuiusq; decorum aut officium continet. Iudicium enim facere dicuntur, qui vnicuique reddunt quod suum est pro sua vocationis & conditionis ratione. Itaque per omnes hominum ordines & omnia vita genera hoc latissime extenditur. Etenim nullum inter hæc tam vile aut contemptum est, in quo non possis obsequium Deo gratum & acceptum præstare, si quid ille velit, diligenter attenderis. Alterum est misericordia. Alibi charitas siue dilectio requiritur: sed ne hæc in otioso affectu acquiescat, alienis periculis aut malis nos moueri, & beneficentia studium omni officio, quo proximum indigere videmus, testari oportet, sicuti in Samaritani parabola docet Dominus. Tertium est fides, quam plerique pro integritate aut (vt Cicero definiuit) pro dicto rum & conuentorum constantia & veritate sumunt, ne quid cum aliquo agatur dolo malo aut insidiose, vt solent, qui amorem simulant, & amicitias vtilitate metiuntur. Sed nihil obstat, quin longius ad Deum vsque extendatur fidei vocabulum, vt sub eo fiduciam intelligamus, quæ nobis in vno Deo reposita esse debet per Mediatorem IESVM CHRISTVM. Nam etsi noluerit Dominus subtiliùs hic disputare de toto fidei mysterio, non tamen dubium est, eum Scribarum & Pharisæorum vitijs voluisse mederi, qui cùm in fide erga Deum non integri essent (quæ illius aliorum scelerum præcipua causa erat) huic malo in primis remedium adhiberi oportuit. Comprehendit ergo hoc loco tribus hisce membris vniuersam veram pietatis doctrinam, & conuenit locus hic cum eo qui apud Micheam habetur, per quem olim hypocritis dixit Deus: Indicatum est tibi homo, quid bonum sit, & quid abs te requirit Dominus, nisi facere iudicium, diligere beneficentiam, & humiliari vt ambules cùm Deo tuo? Nobis vero loci istius vsus esse debet, vt procul relicta omni simulatione, Deo fidele præstemus obsequium, & quæ minoris momenti esse videntur in lege ita obseruemus, vt ne omittamus maiora ista, sed vnicuique demus quod ei debetur, benefici autem & misericordes simus erga omnes homines, fidamus autem vni Deo per Filium suum Vnigenitum IESVM CHRISTVM Dominum nostrum, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: There are three of these. The first is judgement, that is, righteousness and equity itself, by which each person is given what is his, and which contains the duty or obligation of each person. For those are said to do judgement who render to each what is his, according to their calling and condition. Thus this extends most widely through all the ranks of men and all kinds of life. For there is nothing so cheap or contemptible among these that you cannot render God a service pleasing and acceptable to him, if you diligently attend to what he wishes. The second is mercy. Elsewhere charity or love is required; but so that this does not rest in an idle feeling, we ought to be moved by the dangers and evils of others, and to show a zeal for kindness in every duty by which we see our neighbour in need, as the Lord teaches in the parable of the Good Samaritan. The third is faith, which most people take to mean integrity, or (as Cicero defined it) constancy and truthfulness in words and agreements, so that nothing is done with someone by deceit or treachery, as those do who feign love and measure friendships by advantage. But nothing prevents the word faith from being extended further, to God himself, so that under it we understand the trust that ought to be placed in the one God through the Mediator Jesus Christ. For although the Lord did not wish to dispute here more subtly about the whole mystery of faith, there is no doubt that by addressing the vices of the Scribes and Pharisees he wished to heal them, who, since they were not sound in faith toward God (which was the chief cause of their other crimes), needed above all a remedy for this evil. Therefore in these three members he comprehends the whole true doctrine of piety here, and this passage agrees with that which is found in Micah, through which God once said to the hypocrites: "It has been shown to you, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requires of you: only to do judgement, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God." For us the use of this passage ought to be that, having put aside all pretence, we render faithful obedience to God, and observe the things that seem of less importance in the Law in such a way that we do not neglect those greater matters, but give to each what is due to him, and be beneficent and merciful towards all men, and trust in the one God through his Only-begotten Son Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: DOminus noster IESVS CHRISTVS Scribis & Pharisaeis Vae illud horrendum intonans, illos exitio devovet, id vero sic facit, ut diferre causas etiam exponat, propter quas damnari merentur. Quod ut fieret, omnino necesse erat. Etenim in pretio & magna existimatione apud imperitum vulgus illi erant, & multos habebant fectatores. Ne quid ergo ex affectu aut odio adversus eos dicere putaretur, & ut omnes intelligerent dignos esse, qui cum suis fectatoribus male perirent, errores ipsorum & vitia publice argui & taxari oportuit, ne qui ab illis in fe seduci paterentur. Haec tenus autem defucata Janctitatis specie sine larua egit, qua sese in cultu externo venditabant, & docuit illos omnia ex ambitione & privati quaestus studio facere, & in minutis quidem anxios & folicitos esse, ut magni & ardentis zeli studium simulent, negligere autem praecipua vera pietatis capita, sine quibus Deo seruire & seruari impossibile fit. Quia vero quoad rem domesticam & catera, quae ad mores & externam vitae conuersationem faciunt, iusti & sanctitatis studiosissimi videbantur, eo quod omnem immunditiem legalem studiose cauerent, e contra autem purificationes legales anxie obseruarent: nunc ad ea transfit, & in his quoque illos scelerata hypocrisi simplicium oculos fallere ait, & foris mundition & iustitiam simulare, cum intus autem iniustitia & iniquitatis pleni sint.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ, thundering the dreadful "Woe" against the Scribes and Pharisees, devotes them to destruction, and he does so in such a way that he also sets out the reasons why they deserve to be condemned. For this to happen was entirely necessary. For they were held in high esteem and great regard by the untutored crowd, and had many followers. So that no one would think he spoke out of passion or hatred against them, and so that everyone might understand that those who perish along with their followers deserve it, it was right that their errors and vices be publicly exposed and censured, lest any be led astray by them. Moreover, he dealt with them without a mask, stripping away the deceptive appearance of holiness by which they boasted of their outward worship, and he taught that they did everything out of ambition and a desire for private gain; that they were anxious and fussy over trifles, feigning a zeal great and burning, but neglecting the chief heads of true piety, without which it is impossible to serve God or be saved. But since in domestic affairs and other matters that pertain to morals and outward conduct of life they seemed most scrupulous and devoted to holiness, in that they carefully avoided every legal uncleanness and on the other hand observed the legal purifications with anxious care, he now turns to these things too, and says that in these also they deceive the eyes of simple people with wicked hypocrisy, pretending to be clean and righteous outwardly, while inwardly they are full of injustice and iniquity.

units.la: Vae vobis (inquit) Scribae & Pharisaei, hypocritae, quoniam purgatis exteriorem poculi patinae partem, intus autem illa sunt plena rapina & intemperantia. Per exteriorem poculorum & patinarum partem fucum intelligit, quo se in rei domesticae & vitae fui ratione paliabant: & de ablutionibus crebris loquitur, quibus (ut Marcus annotauit) studebant, ut pocula, patinas, sextarios, aramenta, sedilia, lectos, omnia deniq; vasa & instrumenta domus purissima haberent, cum illa rapinis & intemperantia polluerent. Rapinas autem exprobrat, & his vasa ipsorum plena esse dicit, quod quasi ex rapto viuerent, & opes posiderent iniquissime partas, quas sub religionis & pietatis praetextu acquirebant. Intemperantia etiam accusat, quod gulae studiosi male partis ad luxum & ingluuiem abuterentur. Vnde apparet, eosdem Scribarum & Pharisaeorum mores tunc fuisse, quos olim in fui saeculi impostoribus Prophetae accusarunt. Et prodest locos eiusmodi diligenter obseruari ab iis, qui Ecclesiae ministri esse & dici volunt, ne hiis vitiis suam dignitatem, adeoque totius ministerij sacri authoritatem prostituant, quae in quouis homine vulgari vituperium merentur: auaritia nimirum & gula venitrifq; immodico studio. Quis enim fidelem caelestium bonorum dispensatorem dixerit eum, qui huius saeculi opes ita deperit, ut aliorum bona iniquis artibus ad se rapiat? Quis ferio pietatis studio eos ad caelestia contendere putet, qui quotidie comessantur, & ebrij multa vocatione sua indigna faciunt? Dominus Christus certe infidelem & improbum domus suae dispensatorem describens, illum cum ebrij edere & bibere dicit. Et Paulus de sui saeculi impostoribus loquens, Philippensibus scribebat: Multi incedunt (nimirum quasi Christi praeconese sint) quos saepe dixi vobis, nunc autem & flens dico, hostes esse crucis Christi: quorum finis est exitium, quorum Deus est venter, & gloria cum confusione ipsorum: qui terrestria curant. Phi-lipp.3.
units.tr: "Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites," he says, "for you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but within they are full of plunder and excess."
