By the outside of the cups and dishes he means the pretence by which they put on a show in the management of their household and their way of life. And he speaks of the frequent washings, which (as Mark noted) they practised, so that their cups, dishes, pitchers, utensils, couches, beds, and in short all the vessels and furnishings of the house would be perfectly clean, while they polluted them with plunder and excess. He reproaches them for plunder, and says that their vessels are full of it, because they lived as if on stolen goods, and possessed wealth most unjustly gained, which they acquired under the pretext of religion and piety. He also accuses them of excess, since those who were devoted to gluttony abused ill-gotten wealth for luxury and gorging. From this it is clear that the Scribes and Pharisees had the same character then as the prophets once accused the impostors of their own age of having. It is also useful for those who wish to be and be called ministers of the Church to study such passages carefully, lest they prostitute their dignity, and so the authority of the whole sacred ministry, to these vices, which deserve reproach in any ordinary man: namely avarice and gluttony, and immoderate devotion to the belly. For who would call a man a faithful steward of heavenly goods if he so squanders the riches of this age that he seizes the goods of others by wicked arts? Who would think that those who feast every day and, drunk, do many things unworthy of their calling, strive for heavenly things with earnest zeal? The Lord Christ, describing the unfaithful and wicked steward of his house, says that he eats and drinks with drunkards. And Paul, speaking of the impostors of his own age, wrote to the Philippians: "Many walk (no doubt as if they were heralds of Christ), of whom I have often told you, and now I tell you even weeping, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ; whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame: who mind earthly things." Phil. 3.

units.la: Est autem obseruatu dignissimum, quod de esculentis & poculentis loquens, quae patinis & poculis continentur, rapinas dicit: nimirum quod ex pecuniis rapto partu illa sibi pararent. Et go quaecunque auari raptores edunt, bibunt, quibuscunque induuntur, quaecunque possident, rapinae sunt Dei iudicio, qui non quo titulo illa habeas, aut quibus rationibus nunc illa excusles. sed quibus artibus illa acquisieris, reprobat. Sic pecuniam Iuda, propter quam hic Christum prodidit, Sacerdotes recte pretium sanguinis dixerunt, & singulari iudicio Dei factum est, ut ager quoque figuli pro sepultura peregrinorum ex eadem pecunia emptus, propria illorum lingua, qui tanti scelerij authores fuerant, Acheldama, id est, ager sanguinis dictus fit. Debet hoc ad omnia referri, quaecunque iniusti & iniqui homines ex rapinis acquirunt. Solent fere illi superbire aedificijs, praediis, vestitu magnifico, supellectile aurea & argentea, quam in conuiuijs ostentant: adhaec liberalitatis & munificentiae laude venantur ex eo, quod multos alios ad mensam suam inuitant, & interdum saepe etiam homines pios & sanctos Christi seruos: quod Pharisaeos quoque olim fecisse scimus, qui Christum ipsum aliquoties mensis suis adhibuerunt: sed hic pocula & patinas eorum rapinis impletas fuisse dicit, & ideo dignos iudicat, qui exitio æterno deuoueantur. Atqui rapina est, quicquid cum proximi detrimento contra ius & fas acquiritur & possidetur. Et quia hac ratione alijs vitæ substidia eripiuntur, rapinis fere vis vel aperta vel occulta Jubest, quæ iniquos illos raptores sanguinis quoque reos facit. Ideo Habakuk lapides ædificiorum & trabes aduersus eos alternis clamantes introducit. Væ ei, qui ædificat vrbem in sanguine & instaurat ciuitatem in iniquitate. Et apud Michæam opibus iniquè partis ignem diuini iudicij coniunctum esse Spiritus sanctus dicit. Audite (inquit) virgam, & eum qui decernit eam. Quasi diceret: Audistis iam sa-pius, quid vobis denuntiet Dominus, quid item ille a vobis requirat. Sed non mouent vos illius ad monitiones aut minæ. Alia igitur ratione vobiscum agit, & virgas suas exeret, si forte his mo-ueamini. Et mox causam huius comminationis subijcit: Annon adhuc ignis in domo impij thesau-rus iniquitatis? Ꝓipsa illos sceleris conuincit, & ostendit illos culpam neq; negare neq; excusare posse, cum thesauros iniustè quæsitos aut reconditos adhuc domi suæ habeant, quos iam pridem de-bebant restituisse. Et eosdem ignem dicit, eò quòd illis ira Dei coniuncta est, quæ plerunq; iustas quoq; opes cum iniustis deuorat, & simul corda excruciat & ignis illius inextinguibilis est Ꝓrae-ludium, quo olim iniqui omnes torrebuntur. Et ne quid dissimulet, artes quoq; & dolos accusat, quibus thesaurum hunc infelicem acquisierint. Nam Ephæ siue modij exigui aut minoris æquo meminit, bilancis item iniquæ & ponderum iniustorum, quibus vtantur: & seipsos iustificare aut pro insontibus habere posse negat, dum ista adhuc in ædibus suis habeant. Ad eundem planè mo-dum in præsenti Christus Scribas & Pharisæos damnationem mereri demonstrat, quòd pocula & patinas suas rapinis impleant, & simul fiduciam superstitiosam purificationum confutat, quam in ablutionibus vasorum suorum habeant collocatam. Ꝟidiculus merito diceretur, qui ex-teriorem poculi aut patinæ superficiem solicitè detergeret, interiorem verò, ex qua parte editur & bibitur, sordibus sædis pollutam non curaret. Atqui talis omnino (inquit) est Ꝓestra mundities aut sanctitas, qua vos rudi & simplici populo commendatis. In externis quippe hæret, quæ ad a-nimam minimè pertinguunt, interim ea negligitis, quæ hanc non polluunt modò, sed miserè gra-uant & damnant.
units.tr: It is most worthy of note that, speaking of food and drink contained in the dishes and cups, he calls them plunder: no doubt because they procured these things for themselves by seizing money. For whatever greedy plunderers eat and drink, whatever they wear, whatever they possess, is plunder in God's judgement; he disapproves not by what title you hold these things, or on what grounds you now excuse them, but by what arts you have acquired them. Thus the priests rightly called the money of Judas, for which he betrayed Christ, the price of blood; and by a singular judgement of God it came about that the potter's field, bought with the same money as a burial place for strangers, was called in their own language, the language of those who had been the authors of so great a crime, Akeldama, that is, the field of blood. This must be applied to everything that unjust and iniquitous men acquire from plunder. Such men are usually proud of their buildings, estates, magnificent clothing, and gold and silver furniture, which they display at their feasts; besides, they hunt for praise of generosity and munificence from the fact that they invite many others to their table, and sometimes even godly and holy servants of Christ. We know that the Pharisees also once did this, for they admitted Christ himself to their tables on several occasions. But here he says that their cups and dishes were filled with their plunder, and therefore judges them worthy to be devoted to eternal destruction. Now, plunder is whatever is acquired and possessed against right and law, to the loss of one's neighbour. And since by this means the means of life are taken from others, plunder almost always involves violence, open or hidden, which makes those wicked plunderers guilty even of blood. Therefore Habakkuk brings in stones of buildings and beams crying out alternately against them: "Woe to him who builds a city with blood and founds a town on iniquity." And in Micah the Holy Spirit says that fire of divine judgement is joined to wealth gained by wrong: "Hear," he says, "the rod, and him who appoints it." As if he said: "You have heard often enough what the Lord threatens you and what he likewise requires of you. But his admonitions and threats do not move you. Therefore he deals with you in another way, and will lift up his rods, if perhaps you may be moved by these." And soon he adds the cause of this threat: "Is there still fire in the house of the wicked, and treasure of iniquity?" He convicts them of their own crime, and shows that they can neither deny nor excuse their guilt, since they still have in their homes treasures sought or hoarded unjustly, which they ought long ago to have restored. He calls these same things fire, because the wrath of God is joined with them, which often devours even just wealth along with unjust, and at the same time tortures the heart; and that unquenchable fire is the prelude to that in which all the wicked will one day be burned. And lest he should conceal anything, he accuses them also of the arts and deceits by which they acquired this unhappy treasure. For he mentions the small or less than just ephah, and likewise the unfair scales and unjust weights which they use; and he denies that they can justify themselves or regard themselves as innocent, while they still have these things in their houses. In exactly the same way, at present, Christ shows that the Scribes and Pharisees deserve condemnation because they fill their cups and dishes with plunder, and at the same time he refutes the superstitious trust in purifications which they have placed in the washing of their vessels. He would rightly be called ridiculous who anxiously wiped the outer surface of a cup or dish, but did not care about the inner part, from which one eats and drinks, polluted with foul filth. "Yet such," he says, "is your pretended cleanness or holiness, by which you commend yourselves to the simple and unlearned people. For you cling to externals, which do not touch the soul at all, while you neglect those things which not only pollute it but miserably burden and condemn it."

units.la: Erat autem istorum culpa eò grauior, quòd plausibili religionis prætextu ad iniquitatem suam palliandam abutèrentur, & (vt supra dictum est) sub specie precum domos viduarum & orpha-norum deuorarent. Hoc ipsum ergo nostri quoque seculi hypocritis conuenit, quorum templa cum tota sua supellestile egregiè splendent, nec auro solum multo radiant, sed insuper omnia ad sanctì-tatis speciem composita sunt, interim verò in templis illis & annuis eorum redditibus nihil est, quòd non mendacijs, dolis, rapinis & alijs eius generis artibus malis sit acquisitum. Quòd si cæte-ros illorum mores spectes, quibus inter illos, in cœnobijs maximè viuitur, Deum immortalem, quàm fœda ingluuies, quàm insatiabile ingurgitandi studium, quàm effrenis libido illic regnat, vbi omnia foris tam solicitè purgantur. Applicent ista sibi quoq;, qui ex militia mercenaria opes immodicas colligunt, & sese postea sacrificijs & monachis lustrandos aut purificandos præbent. Student hi quoq;, vt in omnibus quæ faciunt puritatis studium singulare eluceat: sed quia omnia ista ex sanguinis pretio instituuntur, sanguinea & cruenta sunt omnia, & polluere potius solent, quàm purificare. Idem de Ꝟsurarijs & omnibus etiam alijs potest dici, qui quæstus ergo negotian-tur. Sunt apud hos quoq; inipsorum domibus & officinis omnia sic instituta, vt nihil illis orna-tius, nihil elegantius, nihil purius dici possit. At sub isto splendore fraudes, rapina & sanguines la-tent, quæ illos Deo inuisos & exosos reddunt.
units.tr: The fault of these men was all the greater because they abused a plausible pretext of religion to cover their wickedness, and (as said above) under the appearance of prayers they devoured the houses of widows and orphans. This applies also to the hypocrites of our own age, whose churches, with all their furnishings, shine splendidly, and glitter not only with much gold but are also arranged to look holy in every way; yet in those churches and in their annual revenues there is nothing that has not been acquired by lies, deceits, robberies and other evil arts of this kind. If you look at the rest of their conduct, in which life is lived most of all among them in monasteries, what a foul gluttony, what an insatiable eagerness for stuffing themselves, what unbridled lust reigns there, where everything outside is so carefully cleansed! The same applies to those who gather excessive wealth from mercenary soldiering and afterwards offer themselves to be purified or cleansed by sacrifices and monks. They too strive to make a singular zeal for purity shine forth in everything they do; but because all these things are set up with the price of blood, everything they do is bloody and cruel, and such things tend to pollute rather than purify. The same can be said of usurers and of all others who trade for gain. Among them too, in their homes and workshops, everything is so arranged that nothing could be called more ornate, more elegant or purer. Yet beneath this splendour lie frauds, robbery and bloodshed, which make them hateful and odious to God.

units.la: Sed pergit Dominus, & quid fieri debeat, docet: Pharisæi cæce, purga primùm quod est in-tra poculum & patinam, vt id quoque quod extra est, purum fiat. Quod de poculis & patinis di-xerat, nunc ad personas hypocritarum transfert, quos cæcos dicit, vt alibi quoque, quando cæcos cæcorum duces dixit. Et reuera cæci sunt, qui non vident, quanto melius sit interiores vasis par-tes purgare, quàm exteriores. Propositio autem huius loci est, eos qui Deo placere volunt, de cor-de potius quàm corpore aut ijs, quæ ad corpus pertinent, purgandis cogitare debere. Apud Lucam istud argumento eiusmodi confirmat: Nonne qui fecit quod foris est, etiam id quod intus est, fe-cit? Quasi diceret: Si corpus solum homini dedisset Deus, excusari poterat, qui de hoc abluendo &
units.tr: But the Lord goes on and teaches what ought to be done: "Blind Pharisee, first cleanse the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may also become clean." What he had said about cups and dishes he now applies to the hypocrites themselves, whom he calls blind, as he does elsewhere when he calls them blind guides of the blind. And indeed they are blind, for they do not see how much better it is to cleanse the inner parts of a vessel than the outer. The point of this passage is that those who wish to please God ought to be concerned first with cleansing the heart rather than the body, or the things that pertain to the body. Luke confirms this with an argument of this kind: "Did not he who made the outside also make the inside?" It is as if he were saying: if God had given man only a body, the one who was anxious about washing and cleansing it could be excused; but he takes no account of the soul.

units.la: 4 2 purgando folicitus, animi nullam rationem habet. Sed non corpus modo hominis formauit Deus, quin animum quoq; dedit, quae melior illius pars est. Igitur huius curam diligentiorem habere oportet. Facit ad huius argumenti confirmationem, quod alibi cor cogitationum, consiliorum, dictorum & factorum omnium fontem esse dicit, ex cuius abundantia os loquatur: neq; aliquid eorum, quod per os ingreditur, hominem polluere, pollui autem hunc per ea, quae ex illo egrediuntur. Quoad ergo cor rapax & doli plenum fuerit, nihil obstabit, quin dictis & factis Jesu declaretur, quae desiderijs illius iniustis respondeant. Rursus si cor innocens est & charitatis studiosum, ea quoque meditabitur, loquetur & faciet, quae cordis aequitas & innocentia dictabit. Frustra ergo corpus purgabit & abluet vs, cuius cor immundum fuerit.
units.tr: God formed not only the body of man but also gave him a soul, which is the better part of him. Therefore one ought to take more careful thought for it. In support of this argument, he elsewhere says that the heart is the source of all thoughts, counsels, words and deeds, and that out of its abundance the mouth speaks. He also says that nothing that enters through the mouth defiles a man, but that he is defiled by the things that come out of him. So long as the heart is greedy and full of deceit, nothing will prevent this from being shown in words and deeds that match its unjust desires. Conversely, if the heart is innocent and eager for love, it will also devise, speak and do what the fairness and innocence of the heart dictate. In vain, then, will a man cleanse and wash his body if his heart is unclean.

units.la: Quia vero rapinis plenos dixerat, quarum restitutio pasim exigitur, eam autem fieri non sem per possibile est, ad misericordiam seu beneficentiae Christianae opera nos remittit, vt ex iis iudicium faciamus de cordis nostri puritate & vera hominis purgatione. Nam apud Lucam priori dicto addit: Imo, ea quae adsunt, date eleemosynam, & ecce, omnia erunt vobis pura. Licet ergo ex his colligere, in quibus constat legitimus opum vsus, qui solus has nobis sanctificat, & ne illis polluamur prohibet. In eo primum, vt illas iuste & aequis rationibus acquiramus, & ab iniustitia tam alieni simus, vt ne concupiscamus quidem quae aliorum sunt. Deinde vt legitime partis & quaesitis non apponamus cor, sed iisdem recte vtamur cum gratiarum actione ad necessitatem. Nam gratiarum actione cibos quosuis nobis sanctificari, Paulus scribit. Praeterea vt ex iis, quae adsunt, vel quantum facultates ferunt beneficiemus, & largiamur egentibus. Quod si qui in primo peccauerint, & se iniustis rationibus diuites factos esse viderint, de restitutione ferio cogitent, ne iustam de ipsis quiritandi occasionem habeant perpetuo ij, qui per ipsos sunt spoliati. Quod si restitutionis occasio nulla est, in alios pauperes erogetur, quod non aliquo honesto titulo nobis reseruare non possumus: & simul praeterea ex nostro etiam quorumuis inopiam subleuemus, quos nostra ope videmus indigere. Sic Nabuchodonosor Daniel olim dicebat: Peccata tua redime iustitia, & iniquitates tuas beneficentia in pauperes, &c. De his etiam Zachaei exemplo admonemur, qui cum magister publicanorum fuisset, & proculdubio (vt ex eius confessione apparet) multis iniuriam fecisset, ad Christum conuersus dicebat: Ecce, dimidium bonorum meorum, Domine, do pauperibus: & si quid cuipiam per calumniam eripui, reddo quadruplum. Vidit nimirum Zachaeus Deo non probari eos, qui ex alieno vel falsificant, vel aliis benefaciunt, & fortasse audierat illud Christi: Si munus tuum attuleris ad altare, & illic memineris fratrem tuum habere aliquid contra te: omitte illic munus tuum, & abi primum reconciliator fratri tuo, & tum veniens offer munus tuum. Nihil ergo faciunt, quod laudem mereatur, aut ipsis ad salutem propriam conducat, qui postquam furtis, rapinis & aliis iniustis rationibus ingentes opes coaceruarunt, partem aliquam ex illis quasi ex pacto decidunt Deo, vt hunc sibi propitium reddant: aut obolaribus eleemosynis, quibus suae exiliationi potius consulere, quam egentibus subuenire volunt, restitutionem simulant. Est hoc non aliud quam cum Deo ludere, & de iflorum hominum eleemosynis dici potest, quod in praesenti de Pharisaeorum poculis & patinis dixit Christus, quod plenae sint rapina & intemperantia. Nam fere fit, vt sibi persuadeant, se cum Deo abunde transfigi, & proinde quoad cetera secuti ijs, quae ipsis restant, turpi licentia ad saltum & luxum abutantur. Itaque duplici nomine damnari merentur. Intemperantia enim & luxus per se peccatum, imo se celus est, si huic indulgeant ij, qui sua legitime acquisierunt.
units.tr: But because he had said that they were full of robbery, the restitution of which is demanded on every side and cannot always be made, he sends us instead to the works of mercy and Christian beneficence, so that from these we may judge the purity of our heart and the true cleansing of the man. For in Luke, after the earlier saying, he adds: "But rather give alms of what you have, and behold, all things will be clean for you." From this it may be gathered in what the lawful use of wealth consists, which alone sanctifies these things for us and keeps us from being defiled by them. First, we should acquire them justly and by fair means, and be so far from injustice that we do not even covet what belongs to others. Second, we should not set our heart on what has been lawfully gained and acquired, but use it rightly for our needs, with thanksgiving; for Paul writes that every food is sanctified to us by thanksgiving. Furthermore, we should do good with what we have, as far as our means allow, and give generously to the needy. But if those who sinned at first, and who see that they became rich by unjust means, should think seriously about restitution, so that those who have been despoiled by them do not have a just cause to complain forever. If there is no opportunity for restitution, what we cannot keep for ourselves on any honest ground should be given to other poor people; and at the same time we should relieve from our own resources the want of whoever we see is in need of our help. Thus Daniel once said to Nebuchadnezzar: "Redeem your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by mercy to the poor," and so on. We are also warned by the example of Zacchaeus, who, since he had been a chief of the tax collectors and without doubt (as his confession makes clear) had wronged many, turned to Christ and said: "Behold, Lord, I give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have taken anything from anyone by false accusation, I restore it fourfold." Zacchaeus clearly saw that God does not approve of those who either falsify with what belongs to others or do good with it to others; and perhaps he had heard Christ's saying: "If you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go first and be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift." Therefore those who, after gathering great wealth by theft, robbery and other unjust means, cut off some part of it and give it to God as if by a bargain, so as to make him favourable to themselves, do nothing that deserves praise or that helps their own salvation; nor do those who pretend to make restitution with small alms, by which they wish to provide for their own vanity rather than help the needy. This is nothing other than to play with God, and what Christ said just now of the cups and dishes of the Pharisees can be said of the alms of such men: that they are full of robbery and intemperance. For it generally happens that they persuade themselves they have amply satisfied God, and so, as far as the rest is concerned, they abuse what remains to them in shameful licence for feasting and luxury. Thus they deserve to be condemned on two counts. For intemperance and luxury are in themselves sin, and indeed a great sin if they are indulged in by those who have acquired their goods lawfully.

units.la: Quia autem Pharisaei non tam hypocrisi, quam impostura & deceptione simplicium peccabant qui doctrina ipsorum confisi, & exemplo eorundem decepti, in soueas periculosas & barathrum per ditionis abducebantur, aliud simile priori subiungit, quo latentem sub illorum hypocrisi malitiam amplius adumbrat. Dicit enim: Vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei hypocritae, quoniam assimiles estis sepulchris dealbatis, quae extra quidem apparent speciosa, intus vero plena sunt ossibus mortuorum, omnique immunditia, &c. Sepulchris magnatum & principum nihil sumptuosius, nihil magnificentius habetur. Tantum enim potest ambitio apud eos, qui huius seculi gloriam vnice quaerunt, vt nominis sui famam, si non alia ratione possunt, post mortem magnifica & sumptuosa sepulchri structura posteris commendare velint. Quam ambitionem in Sobna olim Isaias acriter taxauit, & dignam iudicauit, quam publico sermone corriperet. Et quis pius patienter ferat ea superbiam, quam ne mors quidem domare aut deprimere potest? Quis vero non rideat eorum stultitiam, qui postquam vermibus esca facti sunt, vt nihil ex ipsis praeter offa deformia reliquum sit, adhuc super hire cupiunt. Xenophon Cyrum regem iam morti vicinum filijs mandantem describit: Meum cor pus, filij charissimi, neq; in auro conditè, neq; in argento, neq; in alia re prorsus vlla: sed illud terra reddite quàm primum. Quid enim hac re beatius quàm terra misceri, quae pulchra omnia, bona omnia gignit & nutrit? At hodie inter Christianos inueniuntur Mausolea, quae torum stultitiam arguunt, quos prae caeteris sapere conueniebat. Sed quid iflorum stulti admiratores hoc suo praepostero studio conjequuntur? num sumptus aut fastus iste sepulchrorum eos a communi hominum sor te eximit? Nequaquam. Imo si illa aperiantur, teterrimum foetorem exhalant, nec in illis aliud, quàm a vermibus arroia offa reperiuntur. His similes dicit Christus Pharisaeos. Siquis (inquit) vos spectet, quales hominibus quoad habitum & studia vestra videri vultis, iustissimos & sanctissimos putabit. Phylacterijs enim & fimbrijs ardentissimum legis diuinae studium, magnificis patrum & Rabbinorum titulis eruditionem non vulgarem, minutissimorum holerum decimatione iustitiam omnibus numeris absolutam profitemini: At si quis mores & studia vestra excutiat, quid aliud quàm horribilem sub fallaci hypocrisi latentem spurcitiem inueniet: adeo vt de vobis dici possit, quod olim Dauid de hostibus suis cecinit: Non est in ore eorum sinceritas, intimum eorum prauitas, sepulchrum apertum guttur ipsorum, &c. Apud Lucam parabola ista paulo aliter enuntiatur. Illic enim sepulchris in terra effossis & sub cespite graminis latentibus illos confert, dicens: Vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei, hypocritae: quoniam estis vt monumenta quae non apparent, & quae nesciunt ij qui super ea ambulant. Ita vero de periculo admonet, quod sub doctrina & fucata sanctimonia ipsorum velo latebat, & sensus est: Vt quae humi effossa sunt sepulchra gramine & herbis super ea enatis leguntur, quae causa est, vt interdum qui se super illa tuto pede incedere arbitrantur, subito in foveam incidant: ita qui vos audiunt, & vestrum exemplum secuti externi cultus fiducia nituntur, dum se per vitae semitas tuto ambulare putant, ipse suae falsi in foueas errorum & exitij decidunt. Accidit idem hodie multis, qui hypocritarum fabulis decepti, operum suorum meritis, Diuorum intercessioni, indulgentijs, bullis, satisfactionibus, Purgatorij igniis lustrationi & fexcentis aliis huius farinae delirijs confidunt, sentiant tandem nihil in his omnibus praesidij esse & tandem conscientiae terroribus superati in desperationis barathrum decidant. Itaq; nos omnibus aliis relictis, de vera cordis purificatione serio cogitemus, & hanc fide constanti amplexemur in Filio Dei Vnigenito, Domino nostro Iesu Christo, qui solus est Via, Veritas & Vita. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: But because the Pharisees sinned less by hypocrisy than by deceiving the simple, who, trusting in their teaching and deceived by their example, were led by them into dangerous pits and the abyss of destruction, he adds another saying like the earlier one, by which he more fully shadows forth the malice hidden beneath their hypocrisy. For he says: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed sepulchres, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of the bones of the dead and of all uncleanness," and so on. Nothing is considered more sumptuous or more magnificent than the tombs of great men and princes. Indeed ambition is so strong among those who seek only the glory of this age that, if they cannot do so in any other way, they wish to commend the fame of their name to posterity after death by a magnificent and costly structure of a tomb. Isaiah once sharply censured this ambition in Shebna, and thought it worthy to be rebuked in public preaching. And what pious person could patiently bear that pride which not even death can tame or bring low? Who would not laugh at the folly of those who, after they have become food for worms, so that nothing of them remains but misshapen bones, still desire to be honoured above the dust? Xenophon describes King Cyrus, now near death, instructing his sons: "My body, dearest sons, is not to be laid in gold or silver, nor in any other thing at all, but return it to the earth as soon as possible. For what is more blessed than to be mingled with the earth, which begets and nourishes all beautiful and good things?" Yet today among Christians there are found mausoleums that prove the folly of those who ought to have been wiser than others. But what do the foolish admirers of these things gain by their perverse zeal? Does the expense or pride of these tombs exempt them from the common lot of men? By no means. Indeed, if they are opened, they breathe out a most foul stench, and inside them nothing is found but bones gnawed by worms. Christ compares the Pharisees to such tombs. "If anyone," he says, "looks at you, as you wish to appear to men in your dress and pursuits, he will think you most righteous and most holy. For with phylacteries and tassels you profess the most ardent zeal for the divine law; with magnificent titles of fathers and rabbis, a learning not common; with the tithing of the smallest herbs, a righteousness perfect in every respect. But if anyone examines your conduct and pursuits, what will he find but a horrible filth lying hidden under a deceitful hypocrisy? So that of you may be said what David once sang of his enemies: 'There is no sincerity in their mouth, their inward part is wickedness, their throat is an open sepulchre,' and so on." In Luke this parable is expressed a little differently. There he compares them to graves dug in the earth and hidden under a turf of grass: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like tombs which do not appear, and those who walk over them do not know it." He warns of the danger in these words, which lay hidden under the veil of their teaching and feigned holiness, and the sense is this: just as graves dug in the ground are unseen beneath the grass and herbs that grow over them, and for this reason those who think they can walk safely over them suddenly fall into a pit, so those who listen to you and, following your example, rely on the confidence of outward worship, while they think they walk safely along the paths of life, fall into the pits of their own false errors and ruin. The same happens today to many who, deceived by the fables of hypocrites, trust in the merits of their works, the intercession of the saints, indulgences, bulls, satisfactions, the fires of Purgatory for purification, and countless other delusions of this kind; they will at last perceive that there is no protection in all these things, and, overcome by terrors of conscience, they will fall into the abyss of despair. Therefore, leaving aside all other things, let us think seriously about the true purification of the heart, and embrace it with a steadfast faith in the Only-begotten Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, who alone is the Way, the Truth and the Life. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXI.
units.tr: HOMILY CCLXXI.

units.la: Vae vobis Scribae & Pharisaei, hypocritae, quoniam aedificatis sepulchra Prophetarum, & ornatis monumenta iustorum, & dicitis: Si fuissemus temporibus patrum nostrorum, non fuissemus eorum socij in caede Prophetarum. Itaque testamini aduersus vosmetipsos, vos esse filios eorum qui Prophetas occiderunt. Vos quoque complete mensuram patrum vestrorum. Serpentes, progenies viperarum, quomodo posssitis effugere iudicium gehennae. Propterea ecce, ego mitto ad vos Prophetas & Sapientes & Scribas & ex illis nonnullos trucidabitis & crucifigetis, & ex illis nonnullos flagellabitis in Synagogis vestris, & persequemini ex vrbe in vrbem.
units.tr: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, and say: "If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets." So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who killed the prophets. Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers. Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of hell? Therefore, behold, I send you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and pursue from city to city.

units.la: In religione & vniuersa humanae salutis negotio nihil nocentius & periculosius est hypocrisi. Vbi enim haec regnat, ibi veritas non potest locum habere, & ibidem religio intermoritur. De inde ofores & hostes veritatis facit hypocrisis, & quidem crudelissimos, eo quod veritatis lux fugit cum omnem simulationis abstergit & dissipat. Hinc ergo factum, vt omnibus seculis, non aliij acriores veritatis hostes fuerint, quàm qui ementito simulata religionis velo sese palliarunt. Exemplum eius rei in Scribis & Pharisaeis proponitur. Quia enim hucusque Dominus multa illis exprobrauit, quae minuta in speciem videbantur, & multi fortasse putabant illum immodestius agere adversus viros tanta existimationis. Ne ergo quae hucusque dicta sunt, non digna videretur, quae tanto cum stomacho exagitentur, pergit modo, & ostendit illos non solum circa fimbrias, phylacteria, salutationes, decimationes, & alium apparatum externum peccare, sed insuper partidas esse feruorum Dei, Prophetarum, & proinde dignos, qui funditus excindantur, & male perant. Ordo tractationis usque ad finem Capitis hic est. Primo in genere illos accusat praepositos obseruantia, qua Prophetas prosequebantur. Deinde reipsa probat illos mereri, ut durius tractentur. Postremo poenas graues interminatur, verbis videlicet & templi destructionem, quam totius gentis excidium comitabitur.
units.tr: Nothing is more harmful and more dangerous in religion, and in the whole business of human salvation, than hypocrisy. Where it reigns, truth cannot find a place, and religion there dies away. Moreover, hypocrisy makes enemies and foes of the truth, and indeed the cruelest ones, because the light of truth flees when it wipes away and dispels every pretence. Hence it has happened that in every age the fiercest enemies of the truth have been those who cloaked themselves in the lying veil of simulated religion. An example of this is set before us in the scribes and Pharisees. For the Lord had so far rebuked them for many things that seemed trivial, and many perhaps thought he was acting too harshly against men of such esteem. So that what has been said so far should not seem unworthy of being attacked with such bitterness, he goes on and shows that they sin not only in matters such as the fringes, phylacteries, salutations, tithings and other outward show, but also that they are the murderers of God's servants, the prophets, and therefore deserve to be utterly cut off and to perish. The order of the discourse to the end of the chapter is this. First, he accuses them in general of the honour they paid to the prophets whom they persecuted. Then he proves from the facts that they deserve to be treated more severely. Last, he threatens grave punishments, namely in words and the destruction of the temple, which will be accompanied by the ruin of the whole nation.

units.la: Quoad primum membrum ait: Va vobis Scribae & Pharisaei hypocritae, quoniam aedificatis sepulchra Prophetarum, & ornatis monumenta iustorum, &c. Id accusat, in quo illi laudem quaerebant: nimirum quod veterum seruorum Dei, Prophetarum monumenta colerent & venerarentur. Id vero per se non erat reprehensione dignum. Fuerunt enim sepulchra apud gentes non omnino Barbaras sacrofanda, & illa violare inexcusabilis barbaries iudicata fuit apud eos, qui non omnem humanitatis sensum exuerunt. Et Amos testatur, Moabitas exitij causam fuisse, quod Regis Idumaei offa improbe & inhumaniter violassent. Sed istius praepositi eru cultu exprobrat: & cum non possent ad Prophetarum monumenta propius accedere, quin Patrum suorum scelera ipsis in faciem exprobrarentur, qui illos impie & crudeliter occiderant, ex ipsorum ore eccasionem illos accusandi arripit, dicens: Vos quidem dum circa sepulchra seruorum Dei occupamini, ut egregii pij & religiosi putemini: soletis dicere: Si fuissemus temporibus Patrum nostrorum, non fuissemus eorum socij in caede Prophetarum. At hoc dicendo, testamini Patres vestros indignos Prophetarum caedibus sese polluisse, & vos ex parricidis genitos esse: adeoque vos Patribus vestris esse multo deteriores. Nam illi quidem occiderunt Prophetas, vos autem illos sepelitis, id est, totos obruitis, ut amplius emergere non possint. Et his per Sarcasmum addit: Vos quoque complete mensuram patrum vestrorum. Quasi diceret: Quando ita lubet, agedum pergite in vestra haec impietate, ut videamus tandem, quis ex eo ad vos fructus reuersurus sit, si ita cum larus lucrari libeat. Sed sententia aliquando, quid sit Deo velle fucum facere. At hoc dicendo, eadem opera simul aliud quoque demonstrat, quod ipsis exprobrari quam maxime erat necessarium. Etenim scimus Iudaeos Patrum titulis atque virtute potissimum gloriatos fuisse. Hos apud Ioannis baptismum Pharisaei & Sadducaei iactarunt, & Abrahamum Patrem ipsi Christo Iudaei obiecerunt, & ita illo gloriati sunt, ut nihil porro sibi ad salutem deesse putarent. Ut ergo hanc laruam ipsis detrahat, & ostendat inane esse quam in generis fiducia quaerant gloriam, ostendit, ex homicidis ipsos progenitos esse, quorum maiores iam olim Prophetarum sanguine sese polluerint, ipsos autem Patribus nihil esse meliores, sed deteriores. Veniunt autem hoc loco quaedam consideranda, quae diligentius excutiantur.
units.tr: As to the first part, he says: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous," and so on. He accuses them of that for which they sought praise: namely, that they cultivated and venerated the monuments of the prophets, the old servants of God. This in itself was not worthy of reproof. For tombs were regarded as sacred even among nations that were not wholly barbarous, and to violate them was judged an inexcusable barbarity by those who had not cast off all human feeling. Amos also testifies that the Moabites were brought to ruin because they had wickedly and inhumanly desecrated the bones of the king of Edom. But he rebukes the worship of these leaders: since they could not come closer to the monuments of the prophets without having the crimes of their own fathers thrown in their faces, who had impiously and cruelly killed them, he seizes the occasion to accuse them from their own mouths, saying: "You indeed, while you busy yourselves about the tombs of God's servants, so that you may be thought outstanding, pious and religious, are accustomed to say: 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.' But in saying this you testify that your fathers polluted themselves by the murder of the prophets, and that you are born of murderers, and so you are far worse than your fathers. For they indeed killed the prophets, but you bury them, that is, you cover them over completely so that they cannot rise again." And by way of sarcasm he adds: "Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers." As if he said: "Since it pleases you so, go on in this impiety of yours, so that we may at last see what profit will come back to you from it, if you want to gain so much by such a deception." But by saying this, he at the same time shows something else, which it was especially necessary to bring against them. For we know that the Jews boasted above all of the titles and virtue of their fathers. The Pharisees and Sadducees vaunted this at the baptism of John, and the Jews objected to Christ that they had Abraham as their father, and they so gloried in him that they thought nothing further was lacking to them for salvation. So, in order to strip away this mask and show that the glory they seek in confidence in their lineage is empty, he shows that they are born of murderers, whose ancestors had long before polluted themselves with the blood of the prophets, while they themselves are no better than their fathers, but worse. Now some matters worth considering more carefully arise at this point.

units.la: Primum est, praepositorum superstitiosorum aut filiorum huius saeculi de seruis Dei iudicium. Non possunt illi suum virtuti praemium negare, gloriam nimirum & honorem, qui virtutem, ut umbra corpus sequitur. Veruntamen idem anxie cauent, ne sanctorum gloria ipsis aliquo modo officiat. Qua causa est, quod hac vita defunctos in honore & pretio habet mundus, quos viuentes odit & extinctos cupit. Exempla huius generis in prophanis historiis multa occurrunt, & in Luca nostro Socratem & Aristidem adduximus, quorum obitum Athenienses magno & acerbo luctu prosecuti sunt, quos viuentes hostiliter oderant. Et quoties in exilium eiecerunt Romani, quos procul absentes anxie quaesiuerunt? Nusquam tamen hoc frequentius fit, quam quando fidei aut religionis, & cultorum Dei causa agitur. Nam ut huius loci argumento insistamus, Prophetarum offa & tumulos Iudaei venerabantur: at aeternum Dei Filium IESVM CHRISTVM, eadem docentem, quae olim Prophetae promiserant, non minori odio prosequebantur, quam quo illos prisci Patres persecuti fuerunt. Et quid obsecro aliud hodie solet fieri? Recitantur publice in templis Legenda Sanctorum, annua celebrantur Martyrum memoria, eorundem
units.tr: The first is the judgment of superstitious leaders, or of the children of this age, concerning the servants of God. They cannot deny to virtue its reward, namely glory and honour, for as the shadow follows the body, so honour follows virtue. Yet at the same time they anxiously take care lest the glory of the saints should in any way stand in their way. This is the reason why the world honours and esteems those who have departed this life, whom while they lived it hated and after their death it desires. Many examples of this kind occur in profane histories, and in our Commentary on Luke we have brought forward Socrates and Aristides, whose deaths the Athenians mourned with great and bitter grief, though while they lived they had hated them with hostility. And how often did the Romans drive men into exile, and then anxiously seek them out when they were far away? Yet nowhere does this happen more often than when the cause at stake is faith or religion and the worshippers of God. For, to keep to the argument of this passage, the Jews venerated the bones and tombs of the prophets, but they persecuted with no less hatred the eternal Son of God, Jesus Christ, teaching the same things that the prophets of old had promised, than the ancient fathers had shown in persecuting the prophets. And what, I ask, is commonly done today? The Legends of the Saints are publicly read in the churches, the yearly memorials of the martyrs are celebrated, and the same...

units.la: Praepositeraм Prophetarum ob eruantium accusat.
units.tr: The leaders are accused of the observance of the prophets.

units.la: Amos 2.
units.tr: Amos 2.

units.la: Superstitiosorum de sanctis peruersa iudicia. Tundem sepulchra longis itineribus per terras & maria inuisuntur, nec desunt qui arida defunctorum ossa, vestem, soleam, calc eos, cineres item & quamuis aliam materiem inanimatam, quae ad illos aliquando pertinuisse creditur, proni & cernui adorant, & ijs feruiliter osculafigunt: deniq; in defunctorum animas absentes preculas & hymnos certatim demurmurant. At si quis eandem cum illis fidem profiteri dicat: Credo in vnum Deum omnipotentem, Creatorem caeli & terrae: Credo vnum Deum inuocari & adorari debere per vnum Filium Dei IESVM CHRISTVM, qui solus non bis a Deo Patre factus est Sapientia, Iustitia, Satisfactio, Sanctificatio, extra quem nullum est nomen sub Caelo hominibus datum, in quo homines oporteat saluos fieri: Si quis (inquam) eiusmodi confessionem fidei edat, mox ea occasione ab ripient Haeretica prauitatis inquisitores illum pro fundius & curiosius examinandi. Et quid sentiat de invocatione & intercessione Diuorum caelitum? quid de sacrificio Altaris aut Missae? quid de Igne purgatorio? quid de indulgentijs, Clauibus, reliquijs, imaginibus, votis monasticis, & sexcentis alijs, quorum nulla in Scripturis fit mentio, & de quibus ne gry quidem orthodoxi Patres scripserunt. Quod si cum illis tesentire & crederedicas, & CHRISTO IESV gloriam tuam saluam & integram seruare conberis, mox ab illis condemnaberis, neq; ad eludendas istorum execrationes aeternus Dei Filius satisfecerit, cui omnis potestas data in caelo & in terra. Vera me dicere fatebuntur, quotquot in istorum vngues aliquando inciderunt. Itaq; nostrae etiam tempestatis Pharisaei & Scribae, vt olim, Prophetarum & Apostolorum sepulchra colunt, & simul hos nouos Christi Martyres addunt, quos non terra modo, sed igne & mari defodiant.
units.tr: The perverse judgments of the superstitious about the saints. Finally, tombs are visited over long journeys by land and sea, and there are not lacking those who prostrate themselves and bow down before dry bones of the dead, clothing, sandals, shoes, ashes likewise, and any other lifeless material believed at some time to have belonged to them, and kiss them with servile devotion; and at last they vie with one another in murmuring prayers and hymns for the souls of the absent dead. But if anyone says that he professes the same faith as they do: "I believe in one God, almighty, Creator of heaven and earth"; "I believe that the one God ought to be invoked and adored through the one Son of God, Jesus Christ, who alone was made by God the Father, not twice, Wisdom, Righteousness, Satisfaction, Sanctification, outside whom there is no name under heaven given to men by which men must be saved": if anyone (I say) puts forward a confession of faith of this kind, the inquisitors of heretical depravity will at once seize the occasion to examine him more deeply and more closely. And what does he think about the invocation and intercession of the heavenly saints? What about the sacrifice of the altar or of the Mass? What about purgatory? What about indulgences, keys, relics, images, monastic vows, and six hundred other things, none of which is mentioned in the Scriptures, and about which not even the orthodox Fathers wrote a word? But if you say that you do not agree with them and do not believe as they do, and you strive to keep your glory safe and whole for Christ Jesus, you will at once be condemned by them, and the eternal Son of God will not be enough to frustrate their curses, he to whom all power is given in heaven and on earth. All who have at some time fallen into their claws will confess that I speak the truth. So also the Pharisees and scribes of our own time, as of old, honour the tombs of the prophets and apostles, and at the same time add these new martyrs of Christ, whom they bury not only in earth but in fire and sea.

units.la: At miretur aliquis non solum vnde ista vecordia & peruersitas hominibus nascatur, verumetiam, quod Sanctorum hominum scripta ex tot rogis & incendijs euadunt, & qui viuam fidei veram Confessionem ferre nolunt, libros authenticos scripturae, ex quibus fides discitur, non in vniuersum abolent? Aut qui fit, inquis: vt Diui isti caelites in toto orbe in pretio sint, quorum testimonijs & exemplis aduersarij nostri confutantur, & omne illud Chaos superstitionum euertitur, in quo illi proram puppimque salutis collocatam habent? Sed facilis est ad haec responsio. Nam primo multi magistri, qui in libris nobis cum colloquuntur, minus molesti sunt, quam viui, qui animos acutius penetrant, & importunius instant ijs, quos semel vrgere coeperunt. Deinde non possunt semper impij hostes quod volunt, & seruat piorum aut sanctorum suorum memoriam Dominus, vt tunc quoq; in ipsis vera fides & religio floreat, quando passim alibi conculcatur, neq; ipses aliqua vera cognitionis videtur esse superstes. Quod in eum finem obseruari debet, ne impiorum conatibus offendamur, qui interdum regnum Christi promouent, dum illud volunt euertere, in semetipsos autem conspuunt, qui in Solem expuere audent.
units.tr: But someone may wonder not only where such madness and perversity among men comes from, but also why the writings of holy men survive so many pyres and fires, and why those who will not bear a living confession of the true faith do not abolish altogether the authentic books of Scripture, from which faith is learned. Or how is it, you ask, that these divine heavenly ones are held in such honour throughout the whole world, by whose testimonies and examples our adversaries are refuted, and that chaos of superstitions is overturned, in which they have set the prow and stern of their salvation? But the answer to these questions is easy. First, many teachers who speak with us in books are less troublesome than the living, who penetrate minds more sharply and press more insistently those whom they have once begun to press. Next, the impious enemies cannot always do what they want, and the Lord preserves the memory of the pious and of his saints, so that true faith and religion flourish even then, when they are trampled underfoot everywhere else, and when no trace of true knowledge seems to survive among men. This must be observed to this end: that we should not be offended by the efforts of the impious, who sometimes advance the kingdom of Christ while they want to overthrow it, and who spit upon themselves when they dare to spit at the Sun.

units.la: Admonet praeterea locus hic, vt in quo nam Diuorum Caelitum, qui vita in terris defuncti sunt, cultus confiteatur, videamus. Non vtiq; in sacrificijs, quae iam olim in Christo omnia abolita sunt: non in suffitu, cuius eadem est, quae victimarum ratio: non in imaginibus, quae Deo vero & eius caelitibus abominationi sunt: non in adoratione, quae nulli Creaturae fine blasphemia potest tribui: Quotquot enim spiritus boni sunt (vt D. Augustinus annotauit) nequaquam se adorari volunt, sed idem cum Angelo in Apocalypsi sentient, qui Ioanni ipsum adoraturo dicebat: Vide ne secueris: Conseruus enim tuus sum, & fratrum tuorum Prophetarum, & eorum qui obseruant verba libri huius. Cultum Diui qui in caelis beati viuunt, non alium postulant, quam quo delectati sunt, cum in terris viuerent. Tunc vero toti horruerunt, si qui diuinos honores ipsis voluerunt impendere. Petrus Cornelio Centurioni coram ipso procidenti, dicebat: Surge, & ego ipse homo sum. Paulus vero & Barnabas ceu mente capti diruptis pallijs in turbam Lystrenfium, qui ipsis sacri sacrare volebant, insilierunt, alta voce clamantes: Viri, cur ista facitis? nos quoq; sumus homines, ijsdem quibus vos affectionibus obnoxij, &c. Quis ergo Diuis cultus gratus erit? Is nimirum, si doctrina Verbi credatur, qua vni Christo conantur Deo adducere homines, si item exemplo obediatur, quo illi nobis praeiuerunt, & si ea quibus illis porro non opus est, in vita Dei templa conferamus officia, egentes nimirum, quos hic nobis vnice commendauit. At hodie inuenias aliquos, qui vt lignā & lapides vestiant, homines vinos exumere & spoliare non verebuntur. Sed in loci recitati expositione progrediamur.
units.tr: This passage also prompts us to see what worship of the heavenly saints who have departed this life in the earth is confessed. Certainly not in sacrifices, which were all abolished long ago in Christ; not in incense, whose principle is the same as that of the victims; not in images, which are an abomination to the true God and his heavenly ones; not in adoration, which can be given to no creature without blasphemy. For all good spirits (as Augustine observed) by no means wish to be adored, but think the same as the angel in the Apocalypse, who said to John when he was about to worship him: "See that you do not do it, for I am your fellow servant, and of your brethren the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book." The blessed who live in heaven ask for no other worship than that in which they delighted when they lived on earth. Indeed, they have wholly shuddered at any who have wished to bestow divine honours upon them. Peter, when Cornelius the centurion fell down before him, said: "Stand up; I myself am also a man." Paul and Barnabas, as if out of their minds, tore their garments and leapt into the crowd of the Lystrans, who wanted to sacrifice to them, crying with a loud voice: "Men, why do you do these things? We too are men, subject to the same passions as you," and so on. What worship, then, will be pleasing to the saints? Surely that, if the teaching of the Word is believed, by which they strive to lead men to God through Christ alone; likewise, if we obey the example by which they went before us; and if we bestow on the living temples of God those services which they no longer need, namely to the needy, whom he has especially commended to us here. But today you will find some who will not hesitate to strip and despoil living men, so that they may clothe wood and stones. But let us proceed with the exposition of the passage quoted.

units.la: Quia enim patribus peiores esse dixerat, qui Prophetas trucidarant: ita reipsa aut factio probat, quae omnium certissima est demonstratio. Nam confert inter se bonitatem & facilitatem Dei, cum illorum contumacia, quam hic diutissime pertulerit. In primo membro Propositionem proponit, dicens: Serpentes, progenies viperarum, quomodo possitis effugere iudicium gehennae? Serpentum & viperarum similibus, adhaec interrogatione admirationis plena sermone veslit, ut demonstret, impietatem ipsorum ad summum apicem usque peruenisse, ut neque corrigi possit amplius, neque curari. Et ut hoc Comparatione manifestum fiat, sic ait: Propterea ecce, ego mitto ad vos Prophetas & Sapientes & Scribas, &c. Possunt haec exponi de toto anteacto tempore, quo Deus cum Iudaeorum gente coepit agere, ut eos instituret: vel ad ea referri, quae deinceps Christus per Apostolos cum ipsis egit. Vtrobique bonitas plus quam paterna elucet. Etenim si annos mille, qui ab obitu Solomonis usque ad natum in carne IESVM CHRISTVM effluxerunt, consideres, nullum saeculum vnquam effluxit, quo no plures dederit Iudaico populo Deus, per quos in vita bene & feliciter gubernanda instituerentur: adeo ut ne exilij quidem Babylonici tempus, per omnia vacuum fuerit, sed tunc quoque priuatim & publice multos haberent, per quos edocerentur. Cum vero appropinquaret aurea illa aetas, qua Dei Filius in carne nasciturus est, tanta Spiritus Sancti vbertas redundauit, quantam Ioel olim promiserat, & quantam ethnici quoque Poetae suis carminibus celebrarunt. Et si prophanos Scriptores, qui illo saeculo floruerunt, excutere libeat, nulla aetas mundi ingeniorum fecunditate, solertia, facundia, eruditione ita floruit, ut ea, quae Dei Filium hominem verum nasci vidit. Et cum iam mortis Christi tempus appropinquaret, accessit reliquus Apostolorum chorus, quo nihil laetius, beatius sol hic vidit, qui primo tota Iudaeam, deinde vniuersum terrarum orbem percurrerunt, ut Euangelij tuba totam mundi machinam personarent. Et in his quidem omnia inuenire licet, quae in praesenti Dominus pollicetur. Dicit se mittere velle Prophetas. Hos si requiras, en inter Apostolos tibi damus vates diuinos, qui vniuersa fata Ecclesiae usque ad finem mundi euidentissime ediderunt, nec CHRISTI IESV modo mysteria expediunt, sed Antichristi quoque tenebras ita excutiunt, ut nemo offendere aut errare possit, nisi qui sciens perire velit. Sin sapientes videre cupias, rursus Paulum audi: Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos, sapientiam autem non saeculi huius, neque principum saeculi huius, qui abolentur: sed loquimur sapientiam Dei in mysterio, id est, occultam illam, quam praefinierat Deus ante saecula ad gloriam nostram. Etenim Christus omnibus nobis a Patre sapientia factus est. Idem nobis Scribas misit Apostolos, vere expeditos & doctos, qui de suo thesauro nobis deprompserunt nova & vetera, id est, omnem abundantiam, quae nos ad veram beatitatem instruat. Est autem haec bonitas Dei eo illustrior, quod etsi illo saeculo ea vberior redundauit, non tamen exaruit tunc fons ille, sed alijs quoque temporibus fluxit, & adhuc hodie fluit omnibus qui ad Christum accedunt, ex quo aquam viuentem hauriunt, quotquot in illum credunt.
units.tr: For since he had said that those who slew the prophets were worse than their fathers, the fact itself proves this, which is the most certain demonstration of all. For he compares the goodness and kindness of God with the obstinacy of those whom he has endured for so long. In the first member he sets out the proposition, saying: "Serpents, brood of vipers, how can you escape the judgement of hell?" By the likeness of serpents and vipers, and by a question full of wonder, he expresses it, so as to show that their impiety had reached the highest peak, so that it could be corrected no further, nor cured. And to make this plain by comparison, he says: "Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets and wise men and scribes," and so on. These words may be explained of the whole past time, in which God began to deal with the nation of the Jews in order to instruct them, or they may be referred to what Christ afterwards did with them through the apostles. In both cases his goodness shines forth more than paternal. For if you consider the thousand years that ran from the death of Solomon until Jesus Christ was born in the flesh, no age has ever passed in which God did not give the Jewish people more men through whom they might be instructed in living well and happily. So much so that not even the time of the Babylonian exile was wholly empty, but then too they had many, both privately and publicly, through whom they might be taught. But when that golden age drew near, in which the Son of God was to be born in the flesh, such an abundance of the Holy Spirit overflowed as Joel had long ago promised, and as even the pagan poets celebrated in their songs. And if one cares to search the profane writers who flourished in that age, no age of the world flourished so much in the fertility of talent, skill, eloquence and learning as the one which saw the Son of God born as true man. And when the time of Christ's death was already near, there came the rest of the band of apostles, than whom the sun has seen nothing more joyful or blessed. They first ran through the whole of Judaea, and then through the whole orb of the earth, that they might sound the trumpet of the Gospel through the whole machinery of the world. And in these men one may indeed find all the things which the Lord promises in the present passage. He says that he wishes to send prophets. If you seek these, behold, among the apostles we give you divine seers, who set forth most clearly all the fates of the Church until the end of the world, and who not only expound the mysteries of Christ Jesus but also so dispel the darkness of Antichrist that no one can take offence or err, unless he wishes knowingly to perish. But if you wish to see wise men, hear Paul again: "We speak wisdom among the perfect, yet not the wisdom of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are brought to nothing; but we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, that hidden wisdom which God predestined before the ages for our glory." For Christ has been made wisdom to us all from the Father. The same God sent us scribes, apostles truly equipped and learned, who from their treasure have brought forth for us things new and old, that is, all the abundance that instructs us in true blessedness. This goodness of God is the more illustrious because, although it overflowed more richly in that age, that fountain did not dry up then, but flowed also in other times, and still flows today for all who come to Christ, from whom they draw living water, as many as believe in him.

units.la: Quid vero fecerunt Iudaei vi fa hac bonitate, qua gratia sua fontes illis reserauit Deus? De futuris illis loquitur Dominus, ut quid potissimum debeant cauere, admoneat: Ex illis (inquit) nonnullos trucidabitis & crucifigetis, & ex eis nonnullos flagellabitis in Synagogis vestris, & persequemini ex vrbe in vrbem. Facta haec olim tempore Prophetarum. Quantum sanguinis effudit (putas) Achab & Iezabel, priusquam Elias posset dicere: Filij Israel reliquo fecerunt tuo aras tuas diruerunt, & Prophetas tuos gladio occiderunt, & ego solus relictus sum? Quantum rursus Manasses effudit, priusquam impleret Ierusalem ab ore vsque ad os? Sed omittamus tempora Prophetarum ad Christum Dominum, & quae huic secuta sunt tempora, de quibus in praesenti sermo est, transeamus, qui dicet nos exempla desiderare eorum, quae hic euentura praedicantur? Simon Petrus inuerso ad terram vertice in crucem affixus est. Philippus eodem martyrio affectus est apud Persepolim. Iacobum Zebedaei filium gladio percussit Herodes Agrippa. Alterum Iacobum, fratrem Domini & cognomento Iustum, de pinna templi praecipitatum fullonis fuste tru cidarunt. Marcum Euangelistam vnco tractum esse, veteres tradiderunt. Sed longum foret omnium Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI feruorum obitus beatos commemorare, quibus illi fidei sua doctrinam obsignarunt. Quis enim nescit Stephanum diro lapidum grandine obrutum fuisse, & a Paulo aduersus Ecclesiam grassante, innumeros male multatos, multos etiam blasphemare coactos fuisse? Sed aliunde petant aliorum historias, qui certius & prolixius velint omnia cognoscere.
units.tr: But what did the Jews do in the face of this goodness, by which God unlocked for them the fountains of his grace? The Lord speaks of those future things so as to warn them what they must especially beware of: "Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and you will persecute them from city to city." These things were done of old, in the time of the prophets. How much blood do you suppose Ahab and Jezebel shed, before Elijah could say: "The children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and slain your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left"? How much again did Manasseh shed, until he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other? But let us pass over the times of the prophets down to Christ the Lord, and the times that followed him, of which the present discourse speaks, and who will say that we lack examples of those things which are here predicted to come? Simon Peter was fixed to a cross with his head turned down to the ground. Philip suffered the same martyrdom at Hierapolis. Herod Agrippa struck James, the son of Zebedee, with the sword. Another James, the brother of the Lord, surnamed the Just, was thrown down from the pinnacle of the temple and beaten to death with a fuller's club. The ancients have handed down that Mark the Evangelist was dragged with a hook. But it would be long to recount the blessed deaths of all the servants of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, by which they sealed the teaching of their faith. For who does not know that Stephen was buried under a dreadful hail of stones, and that, while Paul was raging against the Church, countless men were cruelly punished, and many were even compelled to blaspheme? But let them seek the histories of others elsewhere, those who wish to know everything more certainly and at greater length.

units.la: Nunc autem obseruari debet ministrorum Christi fors, vt quid nos in mundo hoc sperare con- ueniat, intelligamus. Constat mundus hic maxima ex parte primum hypocritis iustitiarijs, deinde Epicureis, qui prorsus mundo & carni dediti, cælestia facile negligunt. Vtrumq; hominum genus Christum odit, nec facile fert Euangelij facem in Christo nobis prælucentem. Etenim priores iu-stitiam suam nolunt argui, alteri vero disciplinam oderunt, qua carnis lasciuientis studia in ordi-nem cogi sentiunt. At qua Euangelij lucem extinguere non possunt, quæ Spiritus slabello indies magis inflammatur, vtrumque genus facile inter se conueniunt, & quamuis dissimillimis stu-diis ferantur, operas tamen suas coniungunt vt Veritatis doctrinam si qua ratione possint oppri-mant. In quo conatu alij alijs progrediuntur, prout Domino visum fuerit omnia recte guber-nanti. Imprudens nobis videbitur qui oues suas temere periclitari sinat. Sed rationem ouium sua-rum habet bonus ille pastor, qui nullam esua manu eripi sinit. Nec ideo misera est ministrorum Verbi fors, qui cum Christi Domini sυνεργοι sint, eiusdem Spiritu reguntur, & eandem cum illo fortem subeunt. Tyranni vero persecutor es interim nunquam assequentur quod volunt, amit-tunt autem prætextum omnem excusationis, horribili autem iudicio prementur, quod mox illis Christus denuntiabit. Interim nos consoletur, quod nihil inscio aut inuito Deo nobis accidit, qui fi-delis est, neq; nos supra vires tentari sinit: Qui autem cum Filio Dei IESV CHRISTO patien-tur, cum eodem regnabunt, qui cum illo morientur, cum eodem viuent. Illi debetur benedictio, ho-nor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Now it must be observed what lot the ministers of Christ have in this world, so that we may understand what we ought to hope for here. This world consists for the most part first of hypocritical self-justifiers, and then of Epicureans, who, wholly given over to the world and the flesh, easily neglect heavenly things. Both kinds of men hate Christ, and they do not easily bear the torch of the Gospel shining before us in Christ. For the former do not want their own righteousness to be called into question, while the latter hate discipline, by which they feel the desires of a wanton flesh being brought into order. But these men, who cannot extinguish the light of the Gospel, which is kindled more and more each day by the bellows of the Spirit, easily come together, and although they are carried along by most dissimilar pursuits, they nevertheless join their efforts to suppress the doctrine of the Truth by whatever means they can. In this attempt some advance further than others, as the Lord, who governs all things rightly, sees fit. He would seem an imprudent shepherd to us who allowed his sheep to be rashly endangered. But that good shepherd has regard for his sheep, and he suffers none of them to be snatched from his hand. Nor is the lot of the ministers of the Word therefore wretched, for they are fellow-workers with Christ the Lord, are ruled by his Spirit, and undergo the same lot with him. But the tyrannical persecutors will never attain what they wish in the meantime, and they will lose every pretext for excuse, and they will be overwhelmed by a dreadful judgment, which Christ will soon announce to them. Meanwhile let this console us, that nothing happens to us without the knowledge or against the will of God, who is faithful and does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength. Those who suffer with the Son of God, Jesus Christ, will reign with him; those who die with him will live with him. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCLXXII.

units.la: Vt veniat super vos omnis sanguis iustus, effusus super terram a sanguine Abel iusti vsque ad sanguinem Zachariæ filij Barachiæ, quem occidistis inter templum & altare. Amen dico vobis, venient hæc omnia super nationem istam.
units.tr: "That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you slew between the temple and the altar. Truly I say to you, all these things shall come upon this generation." Matt. 23.

units.la: Postremum, quod Dominus noster IESVS CHRISTVS Scribis & Pharisæis exprobra-uit, est immanis crudelitas, qua gratiæ Dei & salutis præcones persecuti sunt. Vt autem hæc eui dentius cognosci retur, initio Dei facilitatem exposuit, qui omnibus sæculis illos ad se pellicere stu-duerit: & illi incurabilem eorum contumaciam opposuit. Docemur autem illorum exemplo, hypo-critas non leniter modo errare & superstitiosis opinionibus seduci, sed tandem impios gratiæ Dei hostes fieri. Postquam enim homo sibi persuasit, se suis operibus seruari posse, neminem in eo sibi con-tradicentem ferre potest. Sibi enim decedere arbitratur, quicquid Dei gratiæ tribuitur. Nulli er-go acriores Veritatis hostes sunt, neq; in alios magis sæuiunt, quam qui Dei gloriam afferere, & fontes salutis in illius bonitate monstrare sedulo student. Cæterum quia iniquitas ista multos offen-dit, & electi quoq; Dei cultores non raro de Dei longanimitate quiritantur, vt in Ieremiæ, Asa-phi & aliorum exemplis apparet, Dei Filius in præsenti Iudæorum Scribis adeo, toti populo gra-ues pœnas denuntiat, cuas de illis Deus sumere statuerit. Est, locus hic per quam memorabilis. Omnia quippe continet, quæ ad commendationem diuinæ bonitatis faciunt, simul, docent, quid tan-dem eius contemptores maneat. Ne pigeat ergo singula ordine intueri.
units.tr: The last charge that our Lord Jesus Christ brought against the scribes and Pharisees is their monstrous cruelty, by which they persecuted the heralds of God's grace and salvation. So that this may be recognised more clearly, he first set out God's readiness, who had been eager in every age to draw them to himself, and he set against it their incurable obstinacy. We are taught by their example that hypocrites not only go astray in a minor way and are led off by superstitious opinions, but eventually become enemies of God's grace and impious towards it. For once a man has persuaded himself that he can be saved by his own works, he cannot bear anyone who contradicts him in this. He thinks that whatever is given to God's grace is taken away from himself. Therefore there are no fiercer enemies of the truth, nor do any rage more against others, than those who diligently strive to assert God's glory and to show the fountains of salvation in his goodness. Moreover, since this wickedness offends many, and even God's elect worshippers not infrequently complain about God's patience, as appears from the examples of Jeremiah, Asaph and others, the Son of God, in the present case, threatens the scribes of the Jews and the whole people with grievous punishments, which God has determined to exact from them. This passage is most memorable. For it contains everything that serves to commend the divine goodness, and at the same time teaches what finally awaits its despisers. Let us not hesitate, then, to consider its parts one by one.

units.la: Principio, quia hypocritæ zelum religionis prætexunt sceleri, & in impietate pij videri vo-lunt, vt hanc laruam illis detrahat, quid faciant diserte docet, & scelus ipsorum quasi definit, di-cens, fore vt super eos veniat omnis sanguis iustus, effusus super terram, a sanguine Abel iusti vsq; ad sanguinem Zachariæ filij Barachiæ, quem (inquit) occidistis inter templum & altare. Quibus verbis hoc vult dicere: Vos quidem dum ista facitis, Legis & religionis patriæ æmulatores videri vultis, & vos Deo cultum præstare arbitramini. Sed vultis dicam qui sitis & quid de vobis sen-tiat Deus? Hic vobis imputat omnem sanguinem iustum siue innoxium, qui iam inde ab origine rerum contra ius & fas effusus est. Itaq; Dei iudicio crudelissimi homicidæ & nefarij latrones estis, qui omnium cædium, quotquot vnquam iniustè factæ sunt reatu tenemini. Et omnium feruorum Dei sanguis, quotquot unquam pro veritate et pietate trucidati sunt, a sobis requiretur. Duos autem non absque causa diserte nominat, Abelum et Zachariam, sub quibus ceu extremis terminis alij omnes comprehenduntur, qui in hunc censum veniunt. Abel enim primus germanus Dei cultor ex Adamo natus per fidem praestantius sacrificium Deo obtulit, et hoc nomine a Caino impie casus est. Ab hoc orditur, ut simul scandalo, quod hic occurrit, medeatur, et offendat, non novum aut insolens hoc esse, si veri Dei cultores iniquis tractentur ab impijs hypocritis. Illi opponit postremo loco Zachariam, de quo inter interpretes disputatur. Ego simpliciter Christi verbis insisto, qui Barachiae filium dicit: et quia in Scripturis non alium sic nominari audio, quam eum qui inter duodecim minores Prophetas penultimus postreditum ex Babylone sub Zorobabele prophetavit, et hunc a patribus occisum fuisse sentio inter templum et altare, id est, in atrio templi: ut non opus sit Ioiadem Zachariae Prisci, qui sub Ioachae s patrem, binomine sin gere, vel ad alia commenta confugere, quae alij de Zachariae Ioannis Baptistae patre finxerunt. Nec obstat, quod cadis huius in historia sacra non fit mentio, cum plures aliae taceantur, maioris momenti. Sufficiat nobis Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI authoritas, qui cum Martyrum veterum Testamenti catalogum ab Abele exorsus sit, nequaquam credibile est, illum voluisse eum in Zachariæ Ioiadae filio, ceu in medio cursu subsistere, cum constet post huius obitum demum Manassem longe immanissimam feruorum Dei lanienam instituisse, qua (ut nuper diximus) Ierosolyma impleuit innocenti sanguine ad supremam usque labra. Et facit postremi huius Zachariae cades plurimum ad amplificandam Iudaeorum impietatem, qui post exilium diuturnum, quo ipsos Deus in Babylone exercuit vix dum rursus constitutos sedibus, ad ingenium tam cito reuerti iunt, et non solum alienigenis uxoribus ductis femen sanctum prophanarunt, fratres item egenos vsuris vora-cibus aggrauarunt, in templi denique aedificatione aquo segniores fuerunt, verumetiam sanctissimum Dei seruum, quem hic ipsis operis istius plus quam necessarij fidelissimum ἐπιόσκοπον et praefectum dederat, crudeliter praeter omne meritum trucidarunt, ut nec loci maiestate, nec temporis aut recentis liberationis memoria, se a tanto scelere paterentur reuocari. Quibus cum paulo post indignissima Filij Dei cades acciderit, in quem omnes Prophetae et iusti respexerunt, quot ab exordio rerum vixerunt, non temere illis minatur, fore, ut omnis effusi sanguinis iusti reatus ipsis imputetur. Nec contentus id semel dixisse, hoc ipsum graui adiuratione confirmat, adiens: Amen dico vobis, venient haec omnia super aetatem istam. Qua locutione hoc significare videtur, quod istius saeculi homines tantorum scelerum poenas luituri sint, ut non debeant sibi ex mora aliquam impunitatis spe polliceri. Etenim ex historijs constat, vrbis et templi excidiu in annum a Christi morte trigesimum octauum incidisse, cum priusquam innumeris calamitatibus et continuis malis essent exagitati. Est autem ista comminatio atrocior multo quam putetur. Quid grauius dici potest, quam quod Deus ipse caelitus Cainum de fratris cade compellans, ab ipso huius rationem requirit, et aduersus illum terram teste loco producens ait: Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat de terra ad me. Non erat aliquis tanti scelaris confeius, qui vel causam illam agere, aut de facto testari posset. At rudis tellus hoc officium insonti praestat, quae prius innoxium sanguinem quasi eius com miserans exceperat, et nunc immanem homicidam eijcit, ut indignum, quem porro ferat aut alat. Et quod tunc pronuntiauit Deus, postea Lege perpetua confirmatum est: Qui effundit sanguinem hominis per hominem effundetur. Quod de ordinario magistratu dictum esse, non est dubium, cuius est homicidia capitalibus poenis vlcisci: quod tanta seueritate mandatur, ut omnem aliam tanti sceleris redemptionem aut expiationem reiciat Dominus. Nam in libro Numerorum aix Moses: Ne accipiatis pretium pro anima homicida, qui est nocens ut moriatur: sed moriendo me-rietur, ne polluatis terram, quam incolitis. Quia sanguis polluit terram, neque expiabitur terra a sanguine, qui in ea effusus est, nisi per sanguinem illius, qui effudit illum. Qua ergo ratione cum Deo reconciliabitur, quem hic ipse sanguinis reum egerit? Non abfq; causa igitur homicidium incerto authore factum tam folicita et operosa expiatione a senioribus et iudicibus et ab omnibus alijs, in quorum finibus cadauer occisi inuentum fuerit, publice expiari voluit, ut vel sola ista actio docere posset, quam vehementer a sanguinis effusione abhorrere debeant, qui Deo propitio volunt frui. Qua etiam causa est, quod Prophetam ad officium serio faciendum obstringere vo-lens, milens, minatur se ex eius manu requirere velle sanguinem eorum, quos ille suo silentio aut ignavia perdiderit. Quod si vero sanguinis reus fit, qui tacendo alicui mortis causam praebet, neque sermone revocat ab exitio eos, qui volentes pereunt: quid de illis fiet, qui invitos contra ius & fas occidunt, neque alia de causa occidunt, quam quod Dei servi sunt ad vitam aeternam? Et quod nam supplicium illorum sceleri digne puniendo sufficiet? Necinanes aut frigidas fuisse istas minas, rem cuentum docuit, & excidij Ierosolymitani historia abunde testatur.
units.tr: First, since hypocrites use the zeal of religion as a cover for their crime, and wish to be seen as pious in their impiety, he plainly teaches what they are doing, in order to strip away this mask, and as it were defines their wickedness, saying that there shall come upon them all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom (he says) you slew between the temple and the altar. By these words he means this: You, while you do these things, wish to appear as zealous for the law and the religion of your fathers, and you think you render worship to God. But shall I tell you who you are and what God thinks of you? He imputes to you all the blood of the righteous, or of the innocent, which has been shed contrary to right and law from the beginning of the world. Therefore, in God's judgment, you are the most cruel murderers and wicked robbers, and you are held guilty of all the slaughters that have ever been done unjustly. The blood of all the servants of God, as many as have ever been slaughtered for truth and piety, will be required of you. He names two in particular, and not without reason, Abel and Zechariah, between whom, as between the extreme limits, all the others who belong to this number are included. For Abel, the first righteous worshipper of God, born of Adam, offered a more excellent sacrifice to God through faith, and for this reason was impiously slain by Cain. He begins with him so that, at the same time, he may remedy the scandal that arises here, and show that it is no new or strange thing for true worshippers of God to be treated badly by wicked hypocrites. Last of all he sets Zechariah against them, about whom the interpreters dispute. I simply keep to the words of Christ, who calls him the son of Barachiah. Since in the Scriptures I hear of no other so named than the one who, among the twelve minor prophets, prophesied next to last, after the return from Babylon under Zerubbabel, and since I judge that this man was killed by his own people between the temple and the altar, that is, in the court of the temple, there is no need to imagine Jehoiada's son Zechariah, the priest of earlier times, who under Joash was said to have two names, nor to take refuge in other fictions that others have invented about the father of John the Baptist. Nor does it count against this that the mention of this murder is absent from the sacred history, since many other things of greater importance are passed over in silence. The authority of the Son of God is enough for us. Since he began his catalogue of the martyrs of the Old Testament with Abel, it is by no means credible that he meant to stop at the son of Jehoiada Zechariah as if in the middle of the course, when it is clear that only after his death did Manasseh institute by far the most monstrous butchery of the servants of God, by which (as we said recently) he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood up to the very brim. And the slaughter of this last Zechariah contributes greatly to magnifying the impiety of the Jews, who, after the long exile in which God had exercised them in Babylon, were scarcely restored to their homes before they returned so quickly to their former character.
