Id vero omnes alias pœnas completitur. Quid enim prætexet coram Dei tribunali, qui à proprio corde condemnatur? Deni que vt Isaias ait, iusti colliguntur ante diem malum, quo infelicis mundi scelera punire Deus statuit, vt alibi exemplis pluribus demonstrauimus.
units.tr: 1 John 5; John 3. The impiety of the world is refuted. 1 Cor. 1; Gal. 5. Book 2 of the Institutes, chap. 19. These things happen. Chap. 4. This is like the way that grain is threshed with flails to separate it from the chaff, and is also put under the millstone, so that by being ground it becomes flour fit for eating. Thus the godly, separated from the impious, become the pure bread of the Lord, just as St Ignatius once wrote about himself when he was led from Asia to Rome to be ground by the teeth of wild beasts. This happens first for the godly as a testimony, as is noted in Luke. For while they do not hesitate to shed their blood for the doctrine of the Gospel and for confession of faith in JESUS CHRIST, and do not shrink from dreadful torments of death, it is sufficiently clear that they are earnestly persuaded of the faith of Christ, and that what they preach is not an opinion rashly formed. For this reason the martyrs of old were also called witnesses. Next, this same thing serves as a testimony against the Gentiles and the persecuting tyrants, so that they may have no pretext of ignorance by which to excuse themselves. For by these martyrdoms of the saints they are convicted of having rejected the doctrine of salvation offered to them, and therefore of deserving to pay the penalty for their obstinacy, a matter discussed more fully above in chapter 10. This, moreover, completes all the other punishments. For what will a man who is condemned by his own heart plead before the tribunal of God? Finally, as Isaiah says, the righteous are gathered in before the evil day, the day on which God has determined to punish the crimes of the unhappy world, as we have shown by many examples elsewhere.

units.la: Cæterum subijcit his aliud signum, ex quo imminens templi excidium & populi totius dissipatio nem debeant agnoscere. Nam tunc (inquit) offendentur multi. Scimus enim plerosq; homines sub religionis prætextu priuatu commodum quærere, & hoc vitium adeò frequens & commune est, vt ne Apostoli quidem eius immunes fuerint, sicuti illorum de primatu & regno contentiones abundè testantur. Fieri ergo non potest, quin multi grauiter offensi fuerint, quando videbant, Apostolos, quos Christus lucem mundi & salem terræ dixerat, quosq; Euangelij sui pracones & totius orbis doctores constituerat, videbant doctissimos & potentissimos quibusq; inuisos esse, pauperiem & aduersa perpeti, & (vt Paulus scripsit) tanquam morti addictos spectaculum esse mundo & Angelis & hominibus. Et hodie offenduntur multi, quando vident eos, qui in pretio & authoritate fuerant, cum superstitionibus dediti essent, ad Christum conuersos contemni & explodi. Quem enim non offenderent ista, quando Christum ipsum lapidem offensionis fore prædixit Simeon, ad quem multi offendant? Sed & Paulus ait, Apostolos Christum prædicare, Iudæis quidem scandalum, Græcis verò stultitiam. Et tritum est illud Christi, qui Ioannis discipulis dicebat: Beatus qui in me non offenditur. Matth. 11.
units.tr: Further, he adds to these another sign, by which they ought to recognise the imminent destruction of the temple and the dispersal of the whole people. "For then," he says, "many will be offended." For we know that many people, under the pretext of religion, seek their own private advantage, and this vice is so frequent and common that not even the Apostles were free of it, as their contentions about primacy and kingdom abundantly bear witness. It cannot therefore be that many were not gravely offended when they saw the Apostles, whom Christ had called the light of the world and the salt of the earth, whom he had appointed heralds of his gospel and teachers of the whole world, seeing them most learned and powerful yet hated by all, suffering poverty and adversity, and (as Paul wrote) made a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men, as men condemned to death. And today many are offended when they see those who were held in esteem and authority, once devoted to superstitions, converted to Christ and despised and cast off. For who would not be offended by these things, since Simeon foretold that Christ himself would be a stone of offence, at which many would stumble? Paul also says that the Apostles preach Christ, a stumbling-block to the Jews indeed, but foolishness to the Greeks. And that saying of Christ is well known, who said to the disciples of John: "Blessed is he who is not offended in me." Matt. 11.

units.la: In præsenti verò de his admonet, vt nobisipsis caueamus, ne quid huius nobis accidat. Ideo a-pud Marcum præmittit admonitione: Cauete vobisipsis. Et mox subtexit: Tradent enim vos in consessus & synagogas. Et hic quoq; docet quàm graues scandalorum occasiones occursuræ sint. Alius (inquit) alium prodet. Fit hoc dum spe sua frustrantur. Tunc enim alij contra Christum exacerbati minùs honorificè de illo sentire incipiunt. Alij odij flammas aduersus Ieruos huius cocipiunt. Alij prophani fiunt, & paulatim omnem pietatis sensum exuunt, & mundo placere volunt, vt per petuas molestijs persecutionum & odiorum sese liberent. Expertus est hoc Paulus, quando Romæ captiuus agens queritur, in prima defensione neminè sibi affuisse, sed omnes ipsum deseruisse. Item Demas dereliquit me, amplexus præsens seculū. Et alibi quoq; falsorū fratrum mentionem facit, ex quibus molestiam multam accepit. Qui verò non vsq; eò progrediuntur, vt piorum fratrum delatores aut proditores fiant, illos tamen contemnunt, & ab Euangelij mentione abhorrent, dum videlicet subinde aliquid periculi ex illo metuunt. Hic ergo prudentia & diligenti cautione opus est, præparatione item, qualem nobis Dominus in Luca sub eorū parabolis comendat, qui vel bellum gerere, vel ædificia maiora ædificare statuerunt. Ad præparationem verò hanc opus erit certa & solida IESV CHRISTI cognitione, quæ nos incertis & dubijs opinionibus fluctuare non sinet, neq; falsis imaginationibus nos decipiet. Meminerimus item nihil nouum aut insolens accidere, cùm hæc omnia Dominus iam olim prædixerit. Nec dubitemus nobis in cœlis retributionem paratam esse, vbi momentanea leuitas afflictionum huius seculi pondere excellenter excellentiùs gloriæ compensabitur. Domini enim promissio facta est omnibus, qui cum ipso permanent in tentationibus: Ego paciscor vobis, prout pactus est mihi Pater meus, vt edatis & bibatis in mensa mea in regno meo. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: Here, however, he warns about these things, so that we may take care for ourselves, lest any of this happen to us. Therefore in Mark he prefaces his warning: "Take heed to yourselves." And soon he adds: "For they will deliver you up to councils and synagogues." Here too he teaches how grave the occasions of offence will be that will meet us. "One will betray another," he says. This happens when men are disappointed in their hopes. For then some, exasperated against Christ, begin to think less honourably of him. Others catch fire with hatred against his servants. Others become profane, and little by little cast off every sense of piety, and wish to please the world, so that they may free themselves from the constant troubles of persecutions and hatreds. Paul experienced this, when, a prisoner at Rome, he complains that in his first defence no one stood by him, but all deserted him. Likewise Demas forsook me, embracing the present age. And elsewhere too he speaks of false brethren, from whom he suffered much trouble. Those who do not go so far as to become informers or betrayers of pious brethren nevertheless despise them and shrink from the mention of the gospel, while, of course, they fear some danger from it from time to time. Here therefore prudence and diligent caution are needed, and also preparation of the kind the Lord commends to us in Luke under the parables of those who have decided either to wage war or to build greater buildings. For this preparation there will be need of a certain and solid knowledge of Jesus Christ, which will not allow us to waver in uncertain and doubtful opinions, nor deceive us with false imaginations. Let us also remember that nothing new or strange is happening, since the Lord foretold all these things long ago. Nor let us doubt that a reward is prepared for us in heaven, where the momentary lightness of the afflictions of this age will be recompensed with an exceeding and more exceeding weight of glory. For a promise has been made by the Lord to all who remain with him in temptations: "I covenant with you, just as my Father has covenanted with me, that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom." To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: Luc.11. 1.Ioan.3. Ifa.57. Multi offendentur. Matth.13.20. Luc.12. Matth.5. 1.Cor.4. Luc.2. 1.Cor.1. Finis admonitionis de scandalis. Marc.13. 1.Tim.4. 2.Cor.11. Luc.14. 2.Cor.4. Luc.12.
units.tr: Luke 11.1; John 3; Isa. 57. Many will be offended. Matt. 13.20; Luke 12; Matt. 5; 1 Cor. 4; Luke 2; 1 Cor. 1. End of the admonition concerning offences. Mark 13; 1 Tim. 4; 2 Cor. 11; Luke 14; 2 Cor. 4; Luke 12.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXVII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCLXXVII.

units.la: Et multi pseudoprophetæ surgent, ac seducent multos. Et quoniam multiplicata erit iniquitas, refrigescet charitas multorum. Sed qui sustinuerit in finem, hic salvus erit. Et prædicabitur istud Evangelium regni in universa terra, ut sit testimonio omnibus gentibus, & tunc veniet finis.
units.tr: And many false prophets shall rise and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall grow cold. But he who endures to the end, the same shall be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world, as a testimony to all nations, and then shall the end come.

units.la: Dominus & Seruator noster de iis turbis & periculis vaticinans quæ templi & urbis excidium atque mundi huius consummationem præcesserunt, de iis præcipue admonet, quæ in fidei & religionis causa simpliciores possunt offendere. Inter hæc memorabile est, quod nuper aliquot gauderent, fore nimirum, ut alii alios prodant, & inter eos quoque odia & inimicitiæ glisceant, qui Evangelij doctrinam & fidem Christianam profitentur. Quia enim homines vulgo sub religionis prætextu temporaria commoda quærunt, non possunt non eos odisse, a quibus se falsos esse suspicantur. Ea vero causa est, ut paulatim prophanescant, & sensum religionis exuant, si ipse sua nonnihil fructrentur. Et solent fere acerrima esse odia, quæ inter eiusdem religionis socios iue confortes existunt. Sequuntur nunc alia duo scandala, quæ imperitos offendunt, quibus consolationem duplicem subtexit, qua nos confirmemus.
units.tr: Our Lord and Saviour, prophesying about those disturbances and dangers that were to precede the destruction of the Temple and the city and the consummation of this world, warns especially about those things which can cause offence to simpler people in matters of faith and religion. Among these it is worth noting what some recently rejoiced at: that people will betray one another, and that hatreds and enmities will flare up even among those who profess the teaching of the Gospel and the Christian faith. For since people commonly seek temporal advantages under the pretext of religion, they cannot but hate those whom they suspect of being false. This is the reason they gradually become profane and lose all sense of religion, if they reap some benefit from it themselves. And the bitterest hatreds are usually those that arise among companions and partners in the same religion. Now follow two other scandals, which offend the unskilled, and to these he adds a twofold consolation, by which we may be strengthened.

units.la: De primo sic ait: Et multi pseudoprophetæ surgent, ac seducent multos. Nuper de impostoribus monuit, qui Messias mentiti sunt, & se principes sive reges dixerunt, adeoque libertatis promissione multos deceperunt, atque seditionum sive bellorum fuerunt authores. Nunc exituros dicit, qui doctrinam salutis et religionis corrumpant, quales omnibus seculis fuisse constat. Etenim in ipsa Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI cognitione infinitæ & horribiles hæreses exortæ sunt. Quia enim hæc est Vita æterna, ut cognoscamus illum solum verum Deum, & quem misit IESVM CHRISTVM, ab initio statim Ecclesiæ huius cognitioni Satan insidiari cæpit, ut eam obscuraret & opinionibus pravis corrumperet. Constat is Deo & homine. Nam qui æternus Dei Filius est, ex Virgine Hominem assumpsit, & nunc in una eademque persona Deus & Homo est, ut inter Deum Patrem & homines Mediator sit, & sublata, quam Diabolus inuexit, inimicitia, nos illi reconciliet. At hic multifariam erraverunt corrupta mentis homines, dum aut æternam Filij Dei naturam negaverunt, aut Hominis assumpti Veritate in dubium vocarunt, aut personæ unitatem violarunt, vel naturarum distinctionem confuderunt. In Divinitate erraverunt ex antiquioribus Noetus, Praxeas, Hermogenes, Sabellius, quibus etiam Berillus & Marcellus adnumerantur, quos omnes Patripassianorum nomine comprehendunt, & Unionitas dixerunt, eo quod in Trinitate non tres Personas, sed tantum tres voces agnoscebant. Hinc Arius, Photinus, Artemon Filium cœpisse, non ab æterno fuisse affirmarunt, & de illo dicebat Arius ἦν ποτε ὅτε οὐκ ἦν. Rursus Euomius & Aetius Filium dissimilem Patri finxerunt. Quem errorem dum vitare volunt Ebion, Basilides, Cerinthus, Carpocrates, Paulus Samosatenus, Theodotio, in calcaria incidunt, & Dei Filium merum hominem assumpsisse dixerunt. Rursus Cerdon, Martion, Manichæus, Valentinus illum phantasma putarunt, aut corpus cœlitus attulisse, Apelles sydereum. Appollinarius corpus sine mente, ipse reuera mentis expers & demens, vel Verbum in carnem mutatum. Quorum omnium deliria hodie ab hominibus phanaticis ab inferis reducuntur. Eutyches potissimum, qui carnem sive corpus Christo deificatum tribuebat. Cuius furores quidam ita tuentur, ut nisi quis idem cum ipsis fateatur, Maiestatem IESV CHRISTI & Dei Omnipotentiam negare dicetur. A quibus diuersum plane sentientes Nestorianos personas duas fingunt, & τὸν λόγον homini Christo adesse per assistentiam dicunt. Quæ omnia commemoro, ne Dominus nos frustra de falsis Prophetis admonuisse videatur. Quid enim in fide & religione integrum nobis permanebit, si doctrina de persona Christi adulteretur. Priusquam tamen hæc monstra aut portenta prodirent, ut quibus adhuc Apostolis falsi Prophetæ exortifunt, qui Legem cum Euangelio miscentes meritum Christi prorsus euacuarunt, & (ut Paulus ad Galatas scribit) inutile fecerunt. Quid vero postremis
units.tr: Concerning the first he says: And many false prophets shall rise and shall deceive many. Previously he warned about the impostors who falsely claimed to be the Messiah and called themselves princes or kings, and so deceived many with promises of liberty and became the authors of revolts and wars. Now he says that there will come those who corrupt the teaching of salvation and religion, as is known to have been the case in every age. Indeed, from the very knowledge of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, endless and dreadful heresies have arisen. For since this is eternal life, that we know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent, from the very beginning Satan began to lie in wait against this knowledge of the Church, to obscure it and corrupt it with depraved opinions. The question concerns God and man. For he who is the eternal Son of God took man from the Virgin, and now in one and the same person he is God and Man, so that he may be the Mediator between God the Father and men, and, the enmity introduced by the Devil being removed, may reconcile us to him. But here men with corrupted minds have erred in many ways, either denying the eternal nature of the Son of God, or calling into doubt the truth of the assumed man, or violating the unity of the person, or confusing the distinction of the natures. Regarding the Godhead, among the older writers Noetus, Praxeas, Hermogenes and Sabellius erred, and Beryllus and Marcellus are also counted among them. All of these they include under the name of Patripassians and call them Unionites, because they acknowledged in the Trinity not three persons but only three names. From this, Arius, Photinus and Artemon affirmed that the Son began to be, and was not from eternity; and Arius said of him: [ἦν ποτε ὅτε οὐκ ἦν] "there was when he was not." Again, Eunomius and Aetius devised a Son unlike the Father. In trying to avoid this error, Ebion, Basilides, Cerinthus, Carpocrates, Paul of Samosata and Theodotus stumbled on the rocks, and said that the Son of God assumed a mere man. Again, Cerdo, Marcion, Manichaeus and Valentinus thought that he was a phantasm, or that he brought a body from heaven; Apelles said a celestial body. Apollinaris said he had a body without a mind, being himself truly without mind and senseless, or that the Word was changed into flesh. The raving of all these is today being brought back from the dead by fanatical men. Above all Eutyches, who attributed to Christ a flesh or body made divine. Some defend his frenzies in such a way that whoever does not confess the same as they do is said to deny the majesty of Jesus Christ and the omnipotence of God. Those who think quite differently from these, the Nestorians, invent two persons, and say that the [τὸν λόγον] Word is present with the man Christ by way of assistance. I recall all these things so that it may not seem that the Lord warned us about false prophets in vain. For what in faith and religion will remain sound for us if the doctrine concerning the person of Christ is corrupted? Yet before these monsters or portents appeared, false prophets had already arisen even in the time of the Apostles, who, mixing the Law with the Gospel, utterly nullified the merit of Christ, and (as Paul writes to the Galatians) made it of no effect.

units.la: Pseudoprophetæ surgent.
units.tr: Pseudo-prophets will arise.

units.la: Ioan. 17.
units.tr: John 17.

units.la: Hæreses circa personam Christi.
units.tr: Heresies concerning the person of Christ.

units.la: Gal. 5. postremis hisce temporibus factum fit, postquam Filius ille perditionis, sede regni sui in ipso templo Dei collocata, sese supra omne, quod dicitur Deus aut numen, extulit, sicut notum est. Nam ut D. Petrus praedixit infiniti pseudoprophetae exorti sunt, qui haereses exitiales inuexerunt, etiam Dominum, qui ipsos mercatus est abnegantes, & Ecclesiam Christi in fidas innumeras scissa est, ut prorsus lusus iocusque dici possit, quod olim apud Corinthios factum fuit, cum alii Cephisa, alii Pauli, alii Apolloniani dici vellent.
units.tr: Gal. 5. What has happened in these last times, after that son of perdition set up the seat of his kingdom in the very temple of God and exalted himself above everything that is called God or divinity, is well known. For, as St Peter foretold, countless false prophets arose who introduced destructive heresies, even denying the Lord who bought them, and the Church of Christ has been split into innumerable factions, so that it may truly be called a game and a joke, as once happened among the Corinthians, when some wanted to be called Cephas's, some Paul's, and some Apollos's.

units.la: Nec temere hos inter scandalorum authores numerat Dominus. Etenim quia IESVS CHRISTVS lux mundi est, & Sol iustitiae, in cuius alis (ut Malachias ait) est sanitas, portento simile videtur, exorto Sole tenebras orbem terrarum occupare. Et hodie non pauci inueniuntur, qui si ad primum Euangelij iubar non statim omnes Veritati cedant, & superstitiones deserant, non volunt pro Dei Verbo agnoscere quod praedicatur, maxime, si qui ministri doctrina & authoritate pra alijs commendentur. Et audiuntur voces istae: Sperabam Veritati omnes subscripturos, sed vi deo plus esse diffidi rum quam unquam. Non video ergo quid huic Euangelio debeat tribui. Itaque offensi aut non satis instructos putant ad docendum quos tantopere commendari audiuerunt, & proinde non dignos, quibus fides habeatur: aut aduersarijs plus aequo tribuunt, qui Euangelij doctrinae contumacius reluctantur.
units.tr: Nor does the Lord number these among the authors of scandals without reason. For since Jesus Christ is the light of the world and the Sun of righteousness, in whose wings (as Malachi says) is healing, it seems a portent that, when the Sun has risen, darkness should occupy the orb of the earth. And today there are not a few who, if at the first dawn of the Gospel they do not at once yield to the truth and abandon their superstitions, are unwilling to acknowledge as the Word of God what is preached, especially if certain ministers are commended above others for their teaching and authority. And these voices are heard: I hoped that all would subscribe to the truth, but now there seems to be more distrust than ever. I do not see, therefore, what ought to be attributed to this Gospel. So, offended, they think that those whom they have heard so highly commended are not sufficiently instructed to teach, and therefore not worthy of being trusted; or they attribute too much to the adversaries, who resist the teaching of the Gospel more stubbornly than is right.

units.la: At isti omnes sibi ipsi scandalorum authores sunt, dum humani ingenij acumine & industria regni Dei mysteria inuestigari posse putant. At tenendum erat, neminem nosse Filium nisi Patrem, neque Patrem quenquam nosse, nisi Filium. Et ipse Dominus, cum apud Ioannem ingens eorum multitudo deficeret, qui doctrina de carnis sua manducatione offendebantur, ne quem hoc moueat, monet. Nec enim aliquem ad ipsum venire, nisi Pater ipsum traxerit, & olim a Propheta hoc praedictum esse, Dei filios oportere a Deo edoceri, qui solus in corda hominum ius habeat. Nimium autem iniqui sunt, qui cum Deus Veritatem ipsis liberaliter offerat, ipsi oculos sibi ipsi ponte claudunt, interim de huius obscuritate conqueruntur.
units.tr: But all these people are themselves the authors of their own scandals, while they think that the mysteries of the kingdom of God can be investigated by the sharpness of human intellect and diligence. Yet it should have been held that no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son. And the Lord himself, when in John a great multitude of those who were offended by the teaching about eating his flesh fell away, warns them, lest this disturb anyone. For no one comes to him unless the Father draws him, and it was foretold long ago by a prophet that the sons of God must be taught by God, who alone has the right over the hearts of men. But they are exceedingly unjust who, when God offers them the truth freely, themselves shut their eyes with a bridge of their own making, and meanwhile complain about its obscurity.

units.la: Sunt autem plures admodum, qui hoc faciunt, & quorum tam peruersa mens est, ut tenebris potius quam luce, erroribus magis quam veritate delectentur. Non mirum ergo, si Deus iusto suo iudicio efficacem deceptionem illis immittit. Nam ut interdum exoriente Sole simul nubes & nebulae spargun tur, quae illius radios obnubilant, ita saepe fit, ut sincerior Veritatis doctrina repentinis tenebris obscuretur, Deo ita nos exstimulante, ut languorem nostrum nobis excutiat. Et mirum est, quam ea sit quorundam audacia, qui non verentur in aperta & plus quam meridiana luce incautis tenebras offundere.
units.tr: There are indeed very many who do this, and whose minds are so perverse that they delight in darkness rather than light, and in errors rather than truth. It is therefore no wonder if God, by his just judgment, sends upon them an effective delusion. For as sometimes, when the Sun rises, clouds and mists are spread about which obscure its rays, so it often happens that the purer doctrine of the truth is darkened by sudden shadows, God so stirring us up that he may shake off our lethargy. And it is remarkable how great is the audacity of some, who do not hesitate to cast darkness upon the unwary in an open light, brighter than midday.

units.la: Nemo autem his offendi debet. Nam neque nouum est hoc, neque ea est Satanae potestas, ut pro suo arbitrio possit Ecclesias falsis doctrinis turbare, & quoscunque velit seducere: sed sua prouidentia frenos seductorem spiritum regit Deus, & cancellis suis constringit, inter quos sese contineat. Obseruari potius debet paterna Dei cura, qua hic Ecclesiae sua prospicit, ne errores indomiti graf fentur, & plerunque praedicit exorituros, ut caeteri possint ab ijs, quibus salus sua cordi est. Factum hoc omnibus seculis. Per Mosem olim non modo Legem dedit Deus, verumetiam quomodo cauen dint docuit falsi doctores, qui falsos Deos introducunt, & cultus siue religiones nouas instituunt.
units.tr: No one, however, should be offended by these things. For this is neither new, nor is it within Satan's power, to disturb the Churches with false doctrines at his own pleasure and to seduce whomever he wishes; rather, by his providence God restrains the seducing spirit with a bridle and confines him within his own bars, so that he remains within them. Rather, the fatherly care of God should be observed, by which he watches over his Church, so that unbridled errors do not spread, and he generally foretells that they will arise, so that others may be on guard against them, those whose salvation is dear to their hearts. This has happened in all ages. Through Moses God not only gave the Law of old, but also taught how to beware of the false teachers who introduce false gods and set up new cults or religions.

units.la: In Prophetis etiam non diligenter modo, verumetiam graviter oppugnantur falsi Prophetae, & ne eis locus detur, admonemur. Et Apostolis non satis fuit, si fui seculi impostores confutarunt, verumetiam de post exorituris vaticinati sunt. Non temere aut hoc ab illis fieri putabimus. Sed ad monitionum istarum hic nobis vsus esse debet, ne falsis doctrinis seducamur. Peccatur in eo a multis, quod leue illis videtur doctrina quamuis admittere, quod perinde est, ac si quis per syluam infinitus ambagibus, & Labyrinthus intricatam iter faciens, nihil referre putet, quam semitam sequatur. Longe alia mens fuit sanctis Dei seruis, quorum preces ardentissimae fuerunt: Vias tuas fac me scire Iehoua, semitas tuas doce me. Item dirige me in veritate tua. Et aeternus Dei filius, se vt am & oflium esse pronuntiat, per quod nos ad vitam ingredi oporteat. Cui ergo leuis error videbitur a via salutis exorbitare? Eo certe in Dei Filium peccatur, cui honor suus eripitur, & non fine sacrilegio in vanissima hominum commenta transfertur. Excitent nos descriptiones foedae & horribiles pseudoprophetarum & seductorum, qui alicubi venenatis & loricatis locustis, immundis ranis, draconi deniq; rufo, qui diaboli typus est, coferuntur. Quo beatus Epiphanius respexit, quandosingulas hæreses singulis nocentissimorum serpentum generibus siue speciebus similes dixit. Et sane nulla aspis, nulla vipera, nullus regulus siue basilisci tantum rei Christianæ nocuissed, quantum hominum saluti nocuerunt Ariani, Valentiniani, Nestoriani, & quotquot hodie puriorem fidem Christianæ doctrinam aut nouis errorum portentis aut veteribus & ex inferis postliminio revocatis corrumpunt. Sunt vero quidam hodie eo nocentiores, quod Pontificum authoritate arma ti Ecclesias passim inuadunt, & sacra prophanis miscentes omnia turbant, mirificis artibus fratres quoq; vnanimes implacabilibus odijs inter se committere norunt. Nec absq; causa dixit Dominus: Multi pseudoprophetæ jurgent, & seducent multos. Quod enim prophanus ille sapiens dixit, ψευδῆς καὶ καλοί, id est, plures mali, hoc ipsum inter eos, qui spirituales dici & haberi volunt, in primis fieri solet. Excitet autem nos huius consideratio, ut nullum studium nimium esse putemus. Nam etsi Argo vigilantiores simus, semper tamen erit, quod negleximus, neq; ulla cura nobis sufficiet, nisi quæ nos a sacris literis non patietur longius euagari. Omnis Scriptura utilis est ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutionem, quæ est in iustitia. Ut primum vero abs q; Scripturis sapere voluerimus, nos turpissime fallifentiemus.
units.tr: In the Prophets too, false prophets are attacked not only with diligence but with severity, and we are warned not to give them any opening. Nor was it enough for the Apostles to refute the impostors of their own age; they also prophesied about those who would arise later. We should not think they did this rashly. Rather, we ought to use these warnings so that we are not seduced by false doctrines. Many people sin here by thinking it a slight matter to admit any doctrine at all, just as if someone wandering through an endless forest or a tangled labyrinth thought it made no difference which path he followed. The holy servants of God had a far different mind, and their prayers were most fervent: "Show me your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths. Lead me in your truth." And the eternal Son of God declares himself the way, the truth and the door through which we must enter into life. So who will think it a slight error to stray from the way of salvation? Certainly it is a sin against the Son of God, whose honour is snatched from him and, not without sacrilege, transferred to the emptiest inventions of men. Let the foul and horrible descriptions of the false prophets and seducers stir us: they are compared in one place to poisonous, armoured locusts, unclean frogs, and finally to the red dragon, who is a type of the devil. To this, blessed Epiphanius looked when he said that each heresy is like one of the most harmful kinds of serpent. Indeed, no asp, no viper, no basilisk or little king-snake has harmed the Christian cause as much as the Arians, the Valentinians, the Nestorians, and all who today corrupt the purer faith of Christian doctrine, either with new monstrous errors or with old ones recalled from the dead by postliminy. Yet some today are more harmful still, because, armed with the authority of the Pontiffs, they invade churches everywhere, mix holy things with profane, and throw everything into confusion; with remarkable skill they also know how to set even brothers against one another with implacable hatreds. The Lord did not speak without cause when he said: "Many false prophets will arise and will deceive many." For what that profane sage said, πολλοὶ καὶ κακοί [many and bad], that is, "many evil men," happens especially among those who wish to be called and considered spiritual. Let this consideration stir us, so that we think no zeal excessive. For even if we were more watchful than Argus, there would always be something we had neglected, and no care would be enough for us, unless it kept us from wandering far from the sacred letters. "All Scripture is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness." But as soon as we want to be wise apart from the Scriptures, we shall most shamefully deceive ourselves.

units.la: Caterum alterum scandali genus attigit, apriori diuersum. Solent enim pseudoprophetæ pietatis & sanctimoniæ fuco sese palliare, ut authoritatem sibi concilient. At in præsenti ait Dominus: Quoniam multiplicata erit iniquitas, refrigescet charitas multorum. Ita inter homines communi paratum est, ut quamuis plerique pessimis cupiditatibus abripiantur, honesti tamen & pij videri velint, & falso prætextu sese venditent. At rursus Euangelij luce (ut alibi Christus ait) arguitur humani ingenij prauitas, & detegitur eos non tam integros & fideles nobis esse, qui erga nos recte & probe animati esse videbantur. At non leue scandalum est, ab intimis falli, aut ab iis, de quibus meliora meriti sumus: nec aliud est, quod nos a beneficentia studio magis renocet, quam si beneficia nobis perire arbitramur, si nimirum in perfidos & ingratos conferantur. Nec in eo subsistit hoc scandali genus, sed in Euangelium quoq; & infidei siue salutis æternæ doctrinam redundat. Nam hac multi putant homines corrumpi, & vel inhumanos vel ingratos fieri. Absurdum vero videtur vulgo doctrinam probare, quæ bonis moribus officiat, & homines non ad virtutem cicuret, sed contumaciores reddat. Tale quid fuit, quando Christus Dominus a Iuda dolo mestico discipulo proditus, a reliquis omnibus turpifuga desertus, a Petro autem abnegatus, imo abiuratus est. Et hodie multos grauiter offendit incurabilis morum, vel potius scelerum licentia, quæ in mundo dominatur. Sonat quidem ubiq; Dei Verbum & Euangelij vox, quo Deus homines ad se vocat, ut ex illo renati in nouas creaturas renascantur. Sed quo magis nos vrget Dei Spiritus, eo pleriq; magis in vetitum nitimur, quasi cum Deo certamen suscepimus. Fit ergo, ut priuatis commodis dediti, aliena negligant pleriq;, odijs iniustis indulgeant, libidines cæcas & turpes sequantur, iras implacabiles concipiant, & qui optimi videri possunt comessationibus & immodico perpotandi studio tam animi quam corporis vires corrumpunt, ut prorsus in bestias degenerent. Non honor debitus parentibus habetur, non inter coniuges coniugij fides seruatur, nec quæ inter heros & seruos, Magistratus & subditos, vtrinq; præstari debebant officia seruantur. Nec multum sane errauerit, si quam tempore diluuij fuisse corruptionem morum dicit prophanus Poeta, nostro corruptissimo seculo accommodes: Viuitur ex rapto, non hospes ab hospite tutus, Non socer a genero, fratrum quoq; gratia rara est: Imminet exitio vir coniugis, illa mariti, Lurida terribiles miscent aconita nouercæ, Filius ante diem patrios inquirit in annos. Vitta iacet pietas, & virgo cæde madentes Vltima cœlestum terras Astræa reliquit: & quæ sequuntur.
units.tr: Next he touches on a second kind of stumbling block, different from the first. False prophets are wont to cloak themselves in the paint of piety and holiness, so as to win authority for themselves. But in the present passage the Lord says: "Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold." So among men it is commonly the case that, although most are carried away by the worst desires, they still want to seem honest and pious, and they sell themselves under a false pretence. On the other hand, by the light of the Gospel (as Christ says elsewhere) the wickedness of human nature is exposed, and it is revealed that those who seemed to be upright and well-disposed toward us are not so sound and faithful after all. Yet it is no small stumbling block to be deceived by those closest to us, or by those to whom we have done good service. Nothing else calls us back from the zeal for beneficence more than the thought that our benefits are wasted when they are bestowed on the faithless and ungrateful. Nor does this kind of stumbling block stop there; it also spreads to the Gospel and to the doctrine of faith and eternal salvation. For many think that by this doctrine men are corrupted and become either inhuman or ungrateful. Yet it seems absurd to the common people to approve a doctrine that harms good morals and does not tame men toward virtue, but makes them more stubborn. Something of the kind happened when Christ the Lord was betrayed by Judas, a disciple from his own household, was abandoned in shameful flight by all the rest, and was denied, indeed sworn away, by Peter. And today the incurable licence of morals, or rather of crimes, which holds sway in the world, gives great offence to many. The Word of God and the voice of the Gospel sound everywhere, by which God calls men to himself, so that they may be born again from it into new creatures. But the more the Spirit of God presses us, the more many of us strive against what is forbidden, as if we had taken up a contest with God. The result is that, given over to private advantages, many neglect the affairs of others, indulge unjust hatreds, pursue blind and shameful lusts, conceive implacable angers, and those who might seem the best wear down the strength of both mind and body with carousing and an immoderate zeal for drinking, so that they utterly degenerate into beasts. The honour due to parents is not shown; faithfulness in marriage is not kept between spouses; nor are the duties owed on both sides between masters and servants, magistrates and subjects, observed. Nor would he surely be far wrong who applied to our most corrupt age what the profane poet said of the corruption of morals before the flood: "Life is lived by plunder; no guest is safe from his host, no father-in-law from his son-in-law; even the bond of brothers is rare. Husbands plot the ruin of their wives, wives of their husbands; the livid stepmother mixes terrible poisons; a son seeks his father's years before their time. Piety lies prostrate, and maiden Astraea, drenched in slaughter, has at last left the earth to the heavenly ones." And what follows.

units.la: Quibus non immerito illud Hoseæ addes: Audite verbum Domini filij Israelis, quoniam lis est Domino cum habitatoribus terræ: Quia neq; Veritas neq; beneficentia, neq; notitia Dei est in terra: peierare, mentiri, occidere, furari & mæchari perruperunt, & sanguines sanguinis tetigerunt. Est autem obseruatu dignum, quòd iniquitatis abundantiam & charitatis extinctionem aut defectum coniungit: & sunt, qui duo haec membra ordine inuerso ponita putent. Etenim vt charitas totius legis complexio est, ita si haec inter homines refrigescat, in officio suo omnis lo- ci & ordinis homines cessabunt. Nunquam ergo recte constituentur res hominum, nisi vulgo alij aliis praestiterint, quae omnibus ex charitatis officio debentur. Et est hoc magnum corruptionis nostrae argumentum, quòd cum charitate mutua nihil magis necessarium, nihil item vtilius & sua vitae fit, eademque omnes vitae humanae actiones condiat, plerisque tamen illam negligunt, & se mutuo edijs, inuidia, inimicitijs, contentionibus & pugnis fatigant. Necesse autem est, vt aduersus hoc scandalum probè armati simus, ne nos ex statione deiici patiamur. Fere enim generosiores animos vincit publica iniquitas, quando pro beneficijs fere malam gratiam sibi referri videant. Ideo Apostolus grauiter monebat Galatas, ne benefaciendo defatigarentur. Et quia vix aliud diffi- lius est, quàm in officio constantem esse, si neminem tibi respondere videas, vt aequum est, primum cogites oportet, non nouum aut insolens hoc esse, si nouissimorum temporum mores corruptissimi sint. Nam vt singuli homines cum aetate in peius proficiunt, ita mundus quoque, & testatur id Christus, quando in hac ipsa tractatione nouissimorum temporum mores similes fore dicit moribus, quibus temporibus Noe & Lothi olim homines vixerunt. Et quod in praesenti Dominus duobus verbis dixit, Paulus prolixè exponit in 1.ad Thimotheum scribens: Illud autem scito, fore, vt extremis diebus instent tempora molesta: Erunt enim homines sui amantes, auari, gloriosi, superbi, maledici, parentibus immorigeri, ingrati, prophani, charitatis expertes, nescij foederum, calumniatores, intemperantes, immites, minimè amantes bonorum, proditores, praecipites, inflati, voluptatum amantes potius quàm amantes Dei, habentes formam pietatis, sed qui vim eius abnegarint, &c. Nec debet offendi aliquis, quando constat inter primas mundi aetates, semper deteriores melioribus successisse. Meminerimus item scelerum occasiones non ex Euangelio & fidei vera doctrina enasci, sed ex hominibus pullulare, qui natura ad malum proclives sunt. Fit etiam frequenter, vt quibus non licet pietati operam dare, excussa omni religione, deuota impietate in scelera & interitum ruant. Ipse mundus ergo sibi scelerum & calamitatum author est. Dum enim alij verbi praedicationem impediunt, alij friuolis & ridiculis superstitionibus circumducuntur, quas ne ipsimet quidem probant, fieri non potest, quin cum religione sensum quoque communem amittant. Ex his ergo principijs nascuntur homines, qui neque homines neque Deum curant, quales hodie innumerabiles sunt, & ijs quidem authoribus, qui prae alijs de incurabili mundi contumacia conqueruntur.
units.tr: To these one may fittingly add the words of Hosea: "Hear the word of the Lord, you children of Israel, for the Lord has a controversy with the inhabitants of the land: because there is no truth, no kindness, and no knowledge of God in the land. They have broken out into swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and adultery, and blood has touched blood." It is worth noting that he joins the abundance of iniquity with the extinction or failure of love, and some think these two members are put in reverse order. Indeed, just as love is the sum of the whole law, so if it grows cold among men, all men of every rank and station will cease to do their duty. Therefore the affairs of men will never be rightly ordered unless people generally give to one another what is owed to all by the duty of love. And this is a great proof of our corruption: although nothing is more necessary than mutual love, nothing is more useful, and nothing sweeter to life, and although it seasons every action of human life, many neglect it and wear one another down with hatreds, envy, enmities, quarrels and fights. It is necessary, then, that we be well armed against this stumbling block, so that we do not allow ourselves to be cast down from our post. For public wickedness usually overcomes more generous minds, when they see that for their kindnesses they usually get back bad will. So the Apostle earnestly warned the Galatians not to become weary in doing good. And since there is scarcely anything more difficult than to remain steadfast in duty when you see no one responding to you as is right, one must first reflect that it is not new or unusual that the morals of the latest times should be most corrupt. For just as individual men grow worse with age, so the world does too, and Christ bears witness to this, when in this very discourse he says that the morals of the last times will be like those of the times in which Noah and Lot once lived. And what the Lord said in two words, Paul sets out at length, writing in 1 Timothy: "Know this, that in the last days difficult times will come. For men will be lovers of themselves, covetous, boastful, proud, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, profane, without love, unfaithful to covenants, slanderers, intemperate, fierce, not lovers of good, betrayers, headstrong, puffed up, lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God, having a form of godliness but denying its power," and so on. Nor should anyone be offended, since it is established that among the first ages of the world each has always been worse than the one before. Let us also remember that the occasions for sins do not spring from the Gospel and the true doctrine of faith, but arise from men who are by nature prone to evil. It often happens too that those who are not permitted to devote themselves to piety, having cast off all religion, rush headlong into sin and ruin in devoted impiety. The world, then, is itself the author of its own crimes and calamities. For while some hinder the preaching of the Word, others are led about by frivolous and ridiculous superstitions, which they do not even approve themselves; it cannot be but that, along with religion, they lose common sense as well. From these principles, therefore, arise men who care neither for men nor for God, and there are innumerable such today, and indeed they are the offspring of those authors who, above all others, complain of the incurable obstinacy of the world.

units.la: Porrò scandalis istis consolationes quoque subtexit Dominus, quibus pios confirmat. Prima est: Sed qui sustinuerit in finem vsque, is seruabitur. Multiplex periculum monstrarat. Coperat ab ijs, quae corpori imminent, vbi multa nuper concurrere vidimus. Grauius est, quod a falsis Prophetis impendet, quibus non omnes respondere possunt. Augetur autem hoc quoque, quando vulgo homines in peius proficiunt, vt abundante iniquitate charitas refrigescat. Etenim si teste Cicerone Solem e mundo tollunt, qui amicitiam ex vita hominum auferunt, quid fiat, si charitas sublata fuerit, sine vlla amicitiae ne mica quidem reliqua esse poterit. At omnibus istis periculis opponitur haec consolatio, Saluum fore, qui in finem vsque perseuerauerit. Apud Lucam rationis loco addit: Perpatientiam vestram possidete animas vestras. Est praeceptum hoc cum ratione efficacissima coniunctum. Etenim qui amicos habent homines fidos & authoritate praeditos, non facile terrentur, sed aequius ferunt omnia. Cur ergo non exultent & gaudeant, qui se in Dei tutela esse sciunt, cuius fides tunc quoque non fallit, vbi pater & mater nos deserunt. Est enim reuera fidelis, qui nos supra vires tentari non finit. Et facit ad huius promissionis cofirmationē, quod apud Lucam habetur, et quod propter falsos prophetas omnino addi necesse fuit. Sunt enim quida fatis fortes et intrepidi ad omnia, parati item ad omnia ferenda, metuunt autem, ne factis parati sint ad causam pro se dicendam, & ne sua infantia religioni officiat. Idcirco grauiter consolatur dicens: Habete fixu in cordibus vestris. Id est, hoc vobis persuasum fit, nec vllu periculu suo terrore vos ab hac fiducia dimoueat. Qua vero illa esse debet? Non opus esse aliqua praemeditatione, aut
units.tr: Moreover, the Lord also adds consolations to these scandals, by which he strengthens the godly. The first is: "But he who endures to the end, he shall be saved." He had shown the manifold danger. He began with those things which threaten the body, where we have recently seen many things come together. More serious is what hangs over us from false prophets, to whom not all are able to reply. This is increased also when men commonly grow worse, so that "because iniquity abounds, the love of many grows cold." For if, as Cicero testifies, those who take friendship out of human life take away the sun from the world, what would happen if love were removed? Not even a trace of friendship could remain. But against all these dangers this consolation is set: that he who perseveres to the end will be saved. In Luke, as a reason, he adds: "In your patience possess your souls." This precept is joined with a most effective reason. For those who have faithful friends endowed with authority are not easily terrified, but bear all things more calmly. Why then should not those rejoice and be glad who know that they are under God's protection, whose faithfulness does not fail even when father and mother forsake us? For he is indeed faithful, who does not allow us to be tempted beyond our strength. And to the confirmation of this promise contributes what is found in Luke, and what had to be added altogether on account of the false prophets. For there are some who are fairly strong and fearless in all things, and likewise ready to bear all things, but they fear lest they be unready in deeds to plead the cause for themselves, and lest their inexperience hinder religion. Therefore he consoles them severely, saying: "Fix it in your hearts." That is, let this be firmly persuaded to you, and let no danger move you from this confidence by its terror. But what confidence ought that to be? That there is no need of any premeditation, or...

units.la: CAP. XXIII.
units.tr: Chapter 23.

units.la: cura, ne ut par esset, causam vestram possitis tueri. Nec enim vestra est, sed Dei Patris vestri, qui vos non deseret. Scitis me vobis alias dixisse: Non vos esse, qui loquimini, sed Spiritum Patris vestri, et hunc vobis daturum in illo momento quod loquamini. Id nunc repeto. Et quod plus est: Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt contradicere neque resistere omnes, qui si vobis opponent. Comprehendit autem duobus vocabulis omnes dicendi facultates. Et quam certa fuerit huius promissionis veritas, non Apostolorum modo Acta, verumetiam Ecclesiastica historia testantur.
units.tr: ...anxious about how you might defend your cause as you should. For the cause is not yours but that of your Father, God, who will not forsake you. You know that I have told you elsewhere that it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father, and that he will give this to you at the very moment you speak. I now repeat this. And what is more: "I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all who oppose you will not be able to resist or contradict." He sums up all the powers of speaking in two words. How certain the truth of this promise was is attested not only by the Acts of the Apostles but also by Ecclesiastical history.

units.la: Debent autem haec latius extendi, ut non in conventibus solum publicis, ubi sub iuris et legum praetextu agitur, verumetiam in disputationibus Ecclesiasticis non dubitemus de illarum eventu, si quando nobis cum hominibus acutis et exercitatis sophistis res sit. Exemplum, quo confirmemur apud Eusebium in Actis Nicaenae Synodi narratur. Erat philosophus quidam in stropha dialecticus exercitatissimus, qui nullis argumentis vinci autConstringi poterat, quo minus anguis instar elaberetur. Hunc cum quidam Christianae fidei professor, qui nihil quam IESVM CHRISTVM, et hunc crucifixum noverat, nostris insultantem vidisset, et callida disputandi arte superbum, sibi aduersus illum dicendi locum dari postulauit. Tum vero nostri, qui simplicitatem viri et infantiam nosse nescient, metuere, ne forte ludibrio esset ipsum et causam Christianam exponeret. At hic praesenti animo in instituto perseverans: In nomine Domini (inquit) philosophe, audi quae vera sunt: Deus unus est, qui fecit caelum et terram, qui hominem, quem de terra limo formauerat, spiritum dedit: Vniuersa quae videntur et non videntur, virtute verbi sui creauit, et spiritus sui sanctificatione firmauit. Hoc verbum ac sapientia, quem nos Filium dicimus, humanos miseratus errores, ex virgine nasci, et per passionem mortis a perpetua non morte liberauit, ac resurrectione sua aeternam nobis contulit vitam: Quem et expectamus iudicem omnium, quae gerimus esse venturum. Credis haec ita esse philosophe. At ille veluti si nullum unquam sermonem contradicendi didicisset, attonitus et mutus ad omnia, hoc solum potuit respondere, ita sibi videri, nec aliud verum esse quam quod ille dixerat. Tum senior: Si haec ita esse credis, surge et sequere me ad Dominicum, et huius fidei signaculum suscipe. Et philosophus conversus ad discipulos suos, et ad eos, qui audiendi gratia convenerant: Audite, inquit: Donec verbis mecum gesta res est, verba verbis opposui, et quae dicebantur dicendi arte subuerti. Ubi vero pro verbis virtus processit ex ore dicentis, non potuerunt verba virtuti resistere, nec homo aduersari potuit Deo. Et hoc memorabile exemplum, quo docemur simplicem Spiritum Sancti infantiam efficaciorem esse altitudine humanarum argutiis, nec multum formidandum esse, qui linguas suas aduersus Deum garrire assuefecerunt. Vincet enim semper et triumphabit veritas, cuius fere simplex est oratio.
units.tr: These things ought to be extended more widely, so that we need not doubt their outcome not only in public assemblies, where matters are conducted under the pretext of law and statutes, but also in Ecclesiastical disputations, whenever we have to do with clever men and practised sophists. As an example by which we may be strengthened, there is a story in Eusebius, in the Acts of the Synod of Nicaea. There was a certain philosopher, most practised in dialectic, who could not be overcome or pinned down by any arguments, but slipped away like a snake. When a certain professor of the Christian faith, who knew nothing but Jesus Christ, and him crucified, saw him insulting our people and proud of his skill in the art of disputing, he asked that a place be given him to speak against the philosopher. Then indeed our people, who did not know the simplicity and childlike nature of the man, feared that he might become a laughingstock and expose the Christian cause to ridicule. But he, persevering in his purpose with a ready mind, said: "In the name of the Lord, philosopher, hear what is true: God is one, who made heaven and earth, who gave the spirit to man, whom he had formed from the clay of the earth. He created all things visible and invisible by the power of his Word, and established them by the sanctification of his Spirit. This Word and Wisdom, whom we call the Son, having pitied human errors, was born of a virgin, and by his passion and death delivered us from eternal death, and by his resurrection gave us eternal life; and we await him as the judge of all that we do, who is to come. Do you believe these things to be so, philosopher?" But the other, as if he had never learned to contradict any speech, stunned and speechless at everything, could only answer that it seemed so to him, and that nothing was true except what the other had said. Then the old man said: "If you believe these things to be so, rise and follow me to the Lord's table, and receive the seal of this faith." And the philosopher, turning to his disciples and to those who had gathered to listen, said: "Hear me. As long as the matter was conducted in words, I opposed words with words, and overturned what was said by the art of speaking. But when power came forth from the mouth of the speaker instead of words, words could not resist power, nor could a man oppose God." This is a memorable example, by which we are taught that the simple childlikeness of the Holy Spirit is more effective than the subtleties of human cleverness, and that those who have accustomed their tongues to chatter against God need not greatly be feared. For truth will always conquer and triumph, and its speech is almost simple.

units.la: At quia non semper eodem successu illa vincere videtur, et ea tunc tempora fuerunt, ut impossibile putaretur, Euangelium inter tanta obstacula praedicari, hanc quoque promissione repetit dicens: Et praedicabitur illud Euangelium regni in universa terra, ut sit testimonium omnibus gentibus: et tunc veniet finis. Ita vero hoc pronuntiatur, ut sit in vatu esse doceat, nec posse aliter fieri, cum ita decreuerit Deus, quo aliquid decernente, nemo illud poterit irritum facere. Atqui cum huic operi manum deberent admoliri, nihil minus effecturi videbantur. Praeter linguam enim Syriacam nullam noverant, artis dicendi imperiti erant. Adhuc ex obscura et inuisa gente oriundi inter suos quidem aliqua pollebant authoritate. Attamen una et altera concione multa milia Iudaeorum ad fidem converterunt IESVM CHRISTO nomen dederunt. Nec multo post Petrus visione caelesti euocatus Cornelio Centurioni Euangelium praedicauit. Accessit huic ex Antiochia cum Barnaba emissus Paulus, qui intra paucos annos ex Arabia et Syria in Illyricum usque omnia Euangelij doctrina compleuit. Tanta denique fuit Apostolorum industria, ut ad Colosenses idem scribens Euangelium in toto mundo praedicatum esse testetur. Et ne de incerta aliqua doctrina loqui putetur Christus, diserte Euangelium regni dicit, ut ostendat se non de alio loqui, quam eo, de quo in principio suae praedicationis dixerat: Impletum est tempus, et appropinquauit regnum Dei: resipiscite et credite Euangelio. Est hoc miraculum inter Filij Dei miracula longe maximum. Quod enim nullis armis perfici potuisset, ut noua totius mundi facies induceretur, et hominum animi atque voluntates mutarentur, id Christus per duodecim viros obscuros et idiotas effectum dedit. Elucet in eo quanta sit Euangelij potentia,cui nulli hominum infirmitas aut imperitia derogat. Quanta enim tunc imperij Romani Maiestas & potentia fuerit, quanta impera torum vires,qui Euangelij praedicationem extinctam voluerunt, nemo est qui ignoret. At nihil in rerum natura fuit,quo Euangelij cursus potuerit impediri. Et quis dubitet,huius dicti consideratione confirmatos fuisse Apostolos, ut quamuis multa inciderent, quae ipsos terrere potuerant,de successu tamen non dubitarent. At nemo putet Euangelij potentiam minorem esse hodie, quam olim fuerit. Adhuc enim potentia Dei est ad salutem omni credenti. Adhuc coniunctam sibi habet Spiritus Sancti virtutem,qui spirat ubi vult, ut in omnem orbem sonus illius exeat. Et quod olim factum est,nostro quoque seculo factum vidimus, & simile quid experti sunt fortissimi maiores nostri,viri Tigurini,qui cum Euangelij praedicationem admitterent primi, licet omnia moueret Satan,quae illam impedire posse videbantur,successit tamen feliciter quod illi voluerunt, & intra paucos annos regnum Christi non per Heluetiam modo,verumetiam Europam longe lateque propagatum est. Debet domesticum exemplum nos consolari hodie,ne nunc impossibile putemus,quod iam pridem factum est. Viuit adhuc Christus,manet insuperabile verum,Dum perit immenso quicquid in orbe furit. Et non desunt nobis promissiones, ex quibus ipsi quoque idem speremus. Paulus non obscure Iudaeis nouam spem facit vocationis ad regnum Dei, & Christus Ecclesiam vsque ad consummationem seculorum permansuram ait, cum se ad eum vsque diem cum illa fore promittat. Durabit ergo Ecclesia quam diu mundus hic erit. Haec enim est Verbi Dei hospitium,columna & stabilimentum Veritatis. Curent modo omnes, ut Euangelium audiant in testimonium salutis,non condemnationis iusta, quae omnes manebit qui vel non credunt, vel gratia doctrina ad carnis licentiam abutuntur. Quibus vero datum est, Verbum gratiae audire, pro eo gratis int Deo, & Dominum IESVM CHRISTVM viua & constanti fide apprehendant, & in eodem feruentur, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: But because it does not always seem to prevail with the same success, and because those times were such that it was thought impossible for the Gospel to be preached amid so many obstacles, he repeats this promise too, saying: "And this Gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world, as a testimony to all nations; and then the end will come." This is stated in such a way as to teach that it will certainly happen, and cannot happen otherwise, since God has so decreed; and when God has decreed something, no one can make it void. Yet when they were about to set their hands to this work, they seemed least able to accomplish anything. For apart from the Syriac tongue they knew no other, and they were unskilled in the art of speaking. They were also born of an obscure and despised people, and among their own they had some influence. Yet at one sermon or another they converted many thousands of Jews to the faith and gave their names to Jesus Christ. Not long afterwards Peter, called by a heavenly vision, preached the Gospel to Cornelius the centurion. Paul also joined this work, sent out from Antioch with Barnabas, who within a few years filled all the regions from Arabia and Syria even to Illyricum with the teaching of the Gospel. So great, finally, was the diligence of the Apostles that, writing to the Colossians, he testifies that the Gospel had been preached throughout the whole world. And lest Christ be thought to speak of some uncertain doctrine, he plainly calls it the Gospel of the kingdom, to show that he speaks of nothing other than what he had said at the beginning of his preaching: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe the Gospel." This is by far the greatest of the miracles among the miracles of the Son of God. For that which could not have been accomplished by any arms, namely that a new face of the whole world should be brought in, and men's minds and wills be changed, this Christ has brought about through twelve obscure and unlearned men. In this the power of the Gospel shines forth, against which the weakness or inexperience of no man can detract. For how great the majesty and power of the Roman empire was then, and how great the strength of the emperors, who wished the preaching of the Gospel to be extinguished, no one is unaware. Yet there was nothing in the nature of things by which the course of the Gospel could be impeded. And who would doubt that the Apostles were strengthened by the consideration of this saying, so that, although many things befell them which could have terrified them, they nevertheless did not doubt the outcome? But let no one think that the power of the Gospel is less today than it once was. For the power of God still is unto salvation for everyone who believes. Still it has joined to itself the power of the Holy Spirit, who blows where he wills, so that its sound may go out into the whole world. And what was done of old, we have seen done also in our own age, and our bravest forefathers, the men of Zurich, experienced something similar: when they were the first to admit the preaching of the Gospel, although Satan stirred up everything that seemed able to hinder it, what they desired nevertheless succeeded happily, and within a few years the kingdom of Christ was spread far and wide, not only through Helvetia but through Europe. The example of our own people ought to console us today, so that we do not now think impossible what was done long ago. Christ still lives, the unconquerable truth remains, while whatever rages in the vast world perishes. Nor are we lacking promises by which we too may hope for the same. Paul clearly gives the Jews a new hope of being called to the kingdom of God, and Christ says that the Church will remain until the consummation of the ages, since he promises to be with her until that day. The Church, therefore, will endure as long as this world lasts. For she is the dwelling place of the Word of God, the pillar and stay of the truth. Let all take care only that they hear the Gospel as a testimony of salvation, not as a just ground of condemnation, which will remain for all who either do not believe, or abuse the doctrine of grace as a license for the flesh. But to those to whom it has been given to hear the Word of grace, let them pray for it, freely, to God, and let them lay hold of the Lord Jesus Christ with a living and steadfast faith, and be kept in him, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXVIII.
units.tr: HOMILY 278.

units.la: Cum ergo videritis abominationem desolationis quae dicta est a Daniele Propheta, positam in loco sancto, qui legit,animaducrtat. Tunc qui in Iudaea fuerint, fugiant in montes: Qui supra domum non descendat, ut sumat quicquam de domo sua: & qui in agro non reuertatur,ut sumat vestimenta sua. Vae autem vterum ferentibus & lactantibus per illos dies. Orate vero ne fiat fuga vestra hyeme, neque Sabbato. Erit enim tunc afflictio magna, qualis non fuit a principio mundi ad hoc vsque tempus,neque erit. Et nisi contracti fuissent dies illi,perirct omnis caro. Sed propter electos contrahentur dies illi.
units.tr: "When therefore you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let him who is on the housetop not come down to take anything out of his house, and let him who is in the field not turn back to take his clothes. Woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days. But pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the Sabbath. For there will be then great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, and never will be. And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened."

units.la: Debebant homines de ijs quaerere,quae cognitu necessaria sunt: At licet fere circa inutilia vel etiam noxia occupentur,tanta tamen est Dei bonitas,ut de ijs nos edoceat,sine quibus salus nostra non potest consistere. Exemplum diuinae vel potius paternae fidei huius ista tractatio nobis exhibet. Quaesiuerunt discipuli de verbis & templi excidio atque fine mundi. Sed non de inutilibus respondet Dominus, quae humani ingenij curiositas scrutari solet,sed ita ut de periculis & scandalis exoriturus admoneat & quomodo ea possint euitari. At cum hac fide erga discipulos vsus sit Christus,cum illi curiositati carnis indulgerent,cur Deum nobis defuturum putemus, si ea quaeramus,quae ille quaeri vult. Qui sapientiam quarunt sicut argentum, & timorem Dei sine religione vera cui salus coniuncta est,procul dubio inuenient eam. At non minima sapientiae pars est,de nouissimis temporibus recte institutum esse. Hanc in praesenti tradit,& ad praecipuum huius quaestionis caput transit de templi excidio & cultus externi inter Iudaeos abrogatione. Quo loco di scemus ira Dei signa agnoscere,& quae optima sit eius declinanda ratio.
units.tr: Men ought to ask about those things which are necessary to know. But although they are almost always occupied with useless or even harmful matters, God's goodness is so great that he teaches us about those things without which our salvation cannot stand. This passage sets before us an example of the divine, or rather fatherly, faithfulness. The disciples asked about the words concerning the destruction of the temple and the end of the world. But the Lord does not answer about useless things, which human curiosity is accustomed to search out, but in such a way as to warn of the dangers and stumbling-blocks about to arise, and how they may be avoided. Since Christ dealt with his disciples in this faithful way, even when they indulged the curiosity of the flesh, why should we think God will fail us if we seek those things which he himself wishes to be sought? Those who seek wisdom as silver, and the fear of God without true religion, with which salvation is joined, will undoubtedly find it. And it is no small part of wisdom to have been rightly instructed about the last times. He now hands this down, and comes to the chief point of this question, namely the destruction of the temple and the abolition of external worship among the Jews. Here we learn to recognise the signs of God's wrath, and what is the best way to avoid it.

units.la: Praemittit autem signum, quo discant excidium urbis & templi imminere. Opus illo erat, eo quod plerisque non credibile videbatur locum tam celebrem & venerandae maiestatis plenum perire. Et quia urbes interdum periclitantur, saepe etiam dira & horrenda patiuntur, non tamen tota intercidunt, & statim rursus instaurantur, ne quid tale sibi ipsis quoque Iudaei polliceréntur, Ierosolymae aliud praedictum fuit: nimirum excidium, quo funditus excindenda sit. Cum videritis (inquit) abominationem desolationis, positam in loco sancto. Id est, cum Romanae legiones (sic apud Lucam interpretatur) ad urbem sanctam castrametabuntur, non vulgaris haec erit objectio, sed quam expugnatio & excidium urbis sequetur. Olim quidem a Senacherib obsessa, at non capta est. Nunc autem tempore postremi & fatalis illius belli, longe aliam fore urbis fortem docet, eo quod & ipsa mensuram iniquitatis impleverit & cultus ille Leviticus sive mysticus finem sumum attigerit. Quod non obscure Veli scisso in morte Christi facta portendit. Iudaeos autem, qui contumacius inhaerebant superstitionibus, quibus in Lege affuerant, ad Danielis locum remittit, ut intelligant, se frustra in illis aliquid spei constituere, cum Deus iam olim illis denuntiarit exitium. Unde colligitur, frustra salutem sperare eos, quibus Deus irascitur. Horrendum est incidere in manum Dei viventis. Et exempla sunt eorum, qui eo ipso excidium accersunt, quo se tueri & ab interitu vindicare volunt. Accidit hoc omnibus, qui contra Veritatem hostiliter insurgunt, & Filium Dei oderunt, quem oculari debebant. Gloriantur hi fere maiorum potentia, viribus, munitionibus, vetustate: Habuerunt haec omnia Iudaei, & quid de Ierosolyma Scripturae pronuntient, & ipse Christus, qui Civitatem magni principis nominat, notum est. Sed nihil profuerunt ista. Et hodie eadem est fors terrarum orbis, adeoque nationum fere omnium, quae ad interitum vergunt, dum sibi inter medias calamitates omnem felicitatem pollicentur. Itaque ne decipiant seipsos, nec officiantes sint in excutiendis Prophetarum oraculis: sed sirmenter diligenter quae futura sunt, & minas iudiciorum Dei conferant cum iudiciis eius, quae (ut in Psalmis canitur) sunt iudicia & veritas. Psal. 116.
units.tr: He first gives a sign by which they may learn that the destruction of the city and temple is at hand. This was necessary because many did not think it credible that so famous a place, full of venerable majesty, would perish. Cities are sometimes endangered and often suffer dreadful and horrible things, yet they are not wholly destroyed and are soon rebuilt. So that the Jews might not promise themselves such a thing, something else was foretold about Jerusalem: namely a destruction by which it would be utterly overthrown. "When you see" (he says) "the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place." That is, when the Roman legions (so Luke interprets it) encamp about the holy city, this will not be an ordinary siege, but one that will be followed by the storming and destruction of the city. Indeed it was once besieged by Sennacherib, but it was not taken. But now, in the time of that last and fatal war, he teaches that the city's fate will be far different, because it has both filled up the measure of its iniquity and that Levitical, or mystical, worship has reached its final end. This was clearly foreshadowed by the tearing of the veil at Christ's death. But he sends the Jews, who clung more stubbornly to the superstitions in which they had been brought up under the Law, back to the passage in Daniel, so that they may understand that they place their hope in these things in vain, since God long ago announced their ruin. From this it is gathered that those with whom God is angry hope for salvation in vain. It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. And there are examples of those who bring on destruction by the very means by which they want to protect themselves and save themselves from ruin. This happens to all who rise up hostilely against the Truth and hate the Son of God, whom they ought to have cherished as the apple of their eye. These people boast mostly of the power, strength, fortifications and antiquity of their ancestors. The Jews had all of these things, and what the Scriptures say about Jerusalem, and Christ himself, who calls it the city of the great King, is well known. But these things did them no good. And today the lot of the world is the same, and indeed of almost all nations that are heading to ruin, while they promise themselves every kind of happiness in the midst of calamities. Therefore let them not deceive themselves, nor be remiss in examining the oracles of the prophets, but let them firmly and diligently compare what is to come, and the threats of God's judgments, with his judgments, which (as is sung in the Psalms) are judgment and truth. Psal. 116.

units.la: Sed prodest etiam scire, quid inter calamitates facere oporteat. Hoc in iis, quae sequuntur, docet. Qui in Iudaea fuerint, fugiant in montes: Qui supra domum, non descendat, ut sumat quicquam de domo sua: & qui in agro, non revertatur, ut sumat vestimenta sua. Iudaea montibus cincta & munita est: & per hos loca munitiora intelligit, quo se conferant. Vita vero tam praesens periculum fore dicit, ut nihil tam iucundum & utile sit, nihil item tam necessarium, quod vita praefertur. Quid enim proderit suppellectilem, vestes, vasa item pretiosa ex hostibus aut flammis hostilibus rapuisse, si vitam amittas, sine qua nullus omnium quae in terris sunt vsus est? Et haec quidem secundum literam fieri debuerunt: & ideo Ecclesia Christianorum trans Iordanem Pellam migravit, ubi seruata est: quam in montanis sitam fuisse apparet. Et contra Iudaeorum gens in urbem confugit cateruatim: partim templo & sacris confisi, partim munitionibus, quibus inuicta vi debatur. Id vero illus pessime cessit. Nam ut Iosephus ex hostibus pascalibus numerat, toto tempore obsidionis numerata sunt captorum nonaginta & septem millium: caeterorum autem aut iugulato rum decies centena millia. Nec obscure Christus Dominus miseriam exemplo carentem exprimit apud Lucam: quando vallo cingendam dicit, vna cum filiis sine habitatoribus, ut ne lapis quidem super lapidem relinquatur. Vsus autem huius exempli esse debet, ut ne nobis inter iudicia aut poenas blandiamur. Nam si Deus (Paulo teste) naturalibus ramis non pepercit, an nobis parcet, qui ex oleastro decerpti sumus?
units.tr: But it is also useful to know what one ought to do amid calamities. He teaches this in what follows: "Let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let him who is on the housetop not come down to take anything out of his house, and let him who is in the field not return to take his clothes." Judea is girded and fortified by mountains, and by these more fortified places he means the places to which they should betake themselves. Life is in such present danger that nothing is so pleasant or useful, nor likewise so necessary, that it is not to be preferred to life. For what will it profit to have snatched furniture, clothes and precious vessels from enemies or hostile flames, if you lose your life, without which there is no use of anything on earth? And indeed these things ought to have been done according to the letter. Therefore the Christian Church migrated across the Jordan to Pella, where it was preserved; and this place appears to have been situated in the mountains. On the contrary, the Jewish nation crowded into the city, partly trusting in the temple and sacred rites, partly in the fortifications, which were thought invincible in strength. But this turned out very badly for them. For, as Josephus counts the people who came up for the Passover, during the whole time of the siege there were counted ninety-seven thousand captives, and of the rest, those slaughtered, a million. Nor does Christ the Lord obscurely express a misery without parallel in Luke, when he says that the city will be surrounded by a rampart, together with its children, and that it will be without inhabitants, so that not even one stone will be left upon another. The use of this example should be that we do not flatter ourselves amid judgments or punishments. For if God (as Paul bears witness) did not spare the natural branches, will he spare us, who have been plucked from the wild olive?

units.la: Interim Symbolica putemus haec praecepta, ut discamus, quid faciant, qui rebus affligatur sibi consultum volunt. Qui in Iudaea sunt, id est, qui Iudaicis superstitionibus addicti viuunt, vel huius mundi viribus fidunt, ad montes fugiant: eos nimirum de quibus Dauid loquitur in Psalmis: Attollo oculos meos ad montes, unde veniat auxilium mihi? Auxilium meum a Iehovah, qui fecit caelum & terram. Montes hi per Euangelium in IESV CHRISTO monstrantur, qui apud Danielem dicitur lapis auulsus absque manibus, qui creuit in montem magnum. Et ipse est vocat petram fortem, cui portae inferorum non possint praevalere. Qui ergo extra hunc vagantur, hi hostis Satanae praeda sient. Qui vero in latibulo Dei excelsi habitat, in umbra Omnipotentis commorabitur. Dicet Iehova, Protectio mea es, Deus meus es, in te sperabo. Rursum, qui inter impios verjanversantur, emigrent. Vt enim incendio in domo exorto, absq; mora exilire eos oportet, qui seruari volunt, ita separationem fieri necesse est ab illis, qui cum improbis perire nolunt. Et errant vehe menter, qui id putant superuacaneum esse. Etenim vt electus suus consuleret, a Caino separationem coepit Deus, & hunc a suis segregauit, qui proprio iudicio se se damnans dicebat Domino: En eieci- sti me hodie e terra, & a facie tua abscondar, vt sim vagus & profugus in terra. Et cum augescen te multitudine hominum, tam filiorum Dei, qui ex Setho descendebant, quam filiorum hominum, qui ex Caino nascebantur posteri, & artibus inuentis & vrbibus conditis florerent, permixti vi- uerent, tanta exorta est morum corruptio & licentia, vt hæc diluuij causa fuerit, quæ totum genus humanum sustulit, vno Noe cum suis erepto, quem Deus arcæ beneficio seruauit. Et quod tunc Noe mandauit Dominus, hoc ipsum in Apocalypsi præcepit, vt sui electi ex Babylone exeant, ne participes sint peccatorum eius, & pœnarum eius consortes siant. Non potest enim aliqua esse communio lucis & tenebrarum, Christi & Belialis. Qui vero semel euaserunt, non redeant amplius, ne posteriora siant peiora primis. Erant hæc hodie multa consideratione digna, quando de rebus hu manis & harum studijs varie disputatur. Pleriq; ad hominum fœdera respiciunt, nec desunt, qui neq; Ecclesias neq; Respub. saluas esse posse existimant, nisi se totos Regibus sanguinarijs & idolo- latris mancipent. Sunt item, qui postquam maiorum virtute & pietate sese ex horum laqueis ex- tricauerunt, nō desinunt mundi artes & consilia probare, donec seipsos & suos rursus perdiderint. Et ne mundo infelici displiceant, ad superstitiones quoq; sibi redeundum esse putant, vt cum ijs possint in gratiā redire, quibus se exosos esse sentiunt. Sunt hæc stultissima carnis consilia. Male dictus enim qui sidit homini, & facit carnem brachium suum. Qui vero firmum salutis præsidium assestant, Dominum expestant, qui sibi fidentes non deserit, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile let us consider these precepts as symbolic, so that we may learn what those do who want to be counselled in their afflictions. Those who are in Judea, that is, those who live devoted to Jewish superstitions, or who trust in the powers of this world, let them flee to the mountains. These are the ones of whom David speaks in the Psalms: "I lift up my eyes to the mountains; from where shall my help come? My help is from Jehovah, who made heaven and earth." These mountains are shown through the Gospel in Jesus Christ, who in Daniel is called the stone cut out without hands, which grew into a great mountain. He himself is also called the strong rock, against which the gates of hell cannot prevail. Those, therefore, who wander outside of him will become prey to Satan's enemies. But whoever dwells in the secret place of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty. Jehovah will say, "You are my refuge, you are my God; in you I will trust." Again, those who live among the wicked should emigrate. For just as, when fire breaks out in a house, those who wish to be saved must leap out without delay, so separation must be made from those who do not want to perish with the wicked. And those greatly err who think this superfluous. For in order to provide for his elect, God began the separation from Cain, and set apart from his own people the one who, condemning himself by his own judgment, said to the Lord: "Behold, you have driven me out today from the earth, and I shall be hidden from your face, and I shall be a wanderer and fugitive on the earth." And when, with the multitude of men increasing, both the descendants of the sons of God, who came down from Seth, and the descendants of the sons of men, born from Cain, flourished with the arts they had invented and the cities they had founded, living mixed together, such a corruption and licence of morals arose that this became the cause of the Flood, which swept away the whole human race, with only Noah and his family snatched out, whom God preserved by means of the ark. And what the Lord then commanded Noah, the same he commands in the Apocalypse: that his elect come out of Babylon, lest they share in her sins and become partakers of her punishments. For there can be no fellowship of light and darkness, of Christ and Belial. Those who have once escaped should not return again, lest the last things become worse than the first. These matters are today worthy of much consideration, when people dispute in various ways about human affairs and the pursuits connected with them. Many look to alliances with men, and there are not lacking those who think that neither churches nor commonwealths can be safe unless they wholly give themselves over to bloodthirsty kings and idolaters.
