There are also those who, after they have extricated themselves from these snares by the virtue and piety of their ancestors, do not cease to approve the arts and plans of the world, until they have again ruined themselves and their own. And lest they displease the unhappy world, they think they must return also to superstitions, so that they may be restored to favour with those by whom they feel hated. These are the most foolish counsels of the flesh. For cursed is he who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm. But those who hold fast to the firm safeguard of salvation wait for the Lord, who does not forsake those who trust in him, etc.

units.la: Cæterum amplificat pericula circumstantiarum enumeratione. Væ (inquit) vterum ferenti- bus & lactantibus per illos dies. Væ istis imprecatur, non quod sceleus aut per se execratione di- gnum sit, vterum ferre aut lactare: sed vt ostendat eam fore inuersione rerum, vt fœcunditas & numerosa soboles inter maledictiones tristes numeretur & miserijs atq; calamitatibus grauissimis accenseri debeat. Quid enim tristius est, quam in proprijs liberis, qui nobis fere propria carne cha- riores sunt ea ferre, quæ nobis morte ipsa duriora videntur? Ideo Hoseas Israelitis mala impreca turus clamabat: Da eis Domine: Quid dabis? Da eis vterū abortiente & vbera arentia. Et quia milites vulgo muliebri sexui parcunt, oportet graue calamitate esse, quæ fœcunditate maledictio- ne ferit. Tale quid Dominus, cum adsupplicium duceretur mulieribus Hierosolymitanis denun ciat. Nos vero hinc discimus, nihil tam lætum & iucundum esse, quod non in tristitiam conuerta tur, si Deus nos dignis pœnis multare velit. E contra nihil tam durum, tam acerbum & calami- tosum Deum diligentibus accidit, quod non illis in bonum conferat.
units.tr: Moreover, he magnifies the dangers by listing the circumstances. "Woe," he says, "to those who are pregnant and nursing in those days." He invokes woe upon these women not because bearing or nursing a child is in itself a crime deserving curses, but to show that by the reversal of things fruitfulness and a large offspring will be counted among the sad curses, and will have to be reckoned among the most grievous miseries and calamities. For what is more dreadful than having to endure, for one's own children, who are almost dearer to us than our own flesh, things that seem harder to us than death itself? Therefore Hosea, when he was about to pronounce evils upon the Israelites, cried out: "Give them, O Lord. What will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts." And since soldiers generally spare the female sex, the curse that strikes at fruitfulness must be a grievous calamity. The Lord announced something similar to the women of Jerusalem when they were being led to punishment. From this we learn that nothing is so joyful and pleasant that it will not be turned into sadness, if God wishes to chastise us with deserved punishments. On the contrary, nothing so hard, so bitter and so calamitous befalls those who love God that it does not turn to their good.

units.la: Interserit autem precatiunculam Dominus, qua discipulos instruit, dicens: Orate vero, ne fiat fuga vestra, hyeme, neq; Sabbato. Et hanc rationem a tempore confirmat, cuius summa est: Tanta fore calamitate, vt cum ea fit ineuitabilis, anxiè precandum esse, ne fuga vel tempestate, vt hy- berno tempore fieri solet, vel religione impediatur, vt die Sabbati, quando non licebat, longius quàm duorum millium passuum iter ingredi, vt quidam supputant. Etenim mons Oliueti iter Sab bati ab vrbe distat, vt liber Actorum testatur. Bethania autem quæ ad latera montis illius sita est, teste Ioanne Euangelista, a Ierosolyma abest quindecim stadijs, quæ fere plus minus duo mil- lia passuum conficiunt. Sufficit autem hic locus ad confutandum eos, qui omnem fugam illicitam esse contendunt, in qua opinione Tertullianum olim fuisse alibi diximus. Cur vero, vt fuga tem- pus commodum Dominus concederet, precari iuberet si omnino non liceret fugere? Sed licet sese feruare melioribus temporibus si id saluâ religione licet. Vt vero ad preces efficacius hortetur, etiam quid nobis hic faciendum sit, propius inspicere oportet: Erit enim tunc afflictio ma- gna, qualis non fuit a principio mundi ad hoc vsque tempus, neque erit. Loquitur autem de ira Dei, quæ contra Iudæorum gentem exardescet, propter sceleus in Filium Dei IESVM CHRISTVM commissum, quo nihil grauius & atrocius fieri poterat. At hic consolationis ple- num est, quod subiexitur. Et nisi contracti fuissent dies illi, periret omnis caro. Sed propter electos contrahentur dies illi. Est hic memorabilis locus. Docet scriptura, propter pios & electos gentes & Respublicas seruari, & Deum numquam ita irasci quin suorum rationem habeat. Itaq; ne modum excedere videatur in puniendis, qui grauius puniri merentur, tempus poenarum decurtat. Adeo verum est, quod Apostolus ait: Fidelem esse Deum, qui suos tentari non sinat, supra quam ferre possint. Commendat hoc nobis pietatis studium, vt si non propter nos illud colimus, saltem alios magnificiamus, quos pietati studere videmus. Etenim plenum laboris est pietatis studium. At qui hoc in aliis amant & venerantur, aliorum labores & curas in se transferunt, & ita Deo propitio vtuntur. Nam Christi promissio est: Qui recipit Iustum nomine Iusti, mercedem Iusti accipiet. Magna autem elucet mundi improbitas, qui nullos magis odit, quam pios Dei cultores, propter quos caelestis ille Pater vniuersam huius mundi machinam vel perdit, vel seruat. Loth olim priusquam cum suis Sodoma exiuisset, non potuit exitio deuotam regionem Dominus perdere. Et cum idem pro Zoan oppidulo sollicite intercederet, exaudiuit eum Deus, ac benigne respondit. In hac quoque re exaudiuit te, vt nolim subuertere oppidulum illud, de quo locutus es: Fefi na & illic seruare: nec enim facere possum quicquam, donec tu illuc venias. Huius generis multa fiunt, & saepe fit, vt qui aliis praesunt, contemptui sint & odio ijs, qui sine ipsis commode viuere non possunt. Discamus ergo huius loci occasione, in pretio habere pios homines & imitari. Persuadent sibi interdum prophani homines, nullum esse discrimen inter piuum & impium, & ideo sese mundo accommodant, ac caecis carnis affectibus ducuntur. Sed non potest falli Deus, & iusta sunt iudicia eius. Studeamus ergo fidem in IESVM CHRISTVM, Dominum nostrum colere, qui sibi fidentes non deseret, & omnibus malis aut aduersis superiores faciet. Confirmet nos in hac fide iste locus: quo docemur Deum tunc quoque seruaturum electos suos in Christo, etiamsi cum Ierosolyma totus quoque orbis terrarum perierit. In illo ergo fortes & constantes simus: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: The Lord also inserts a short exhortation by which he instructs the disciples, saying: "But pray that your flight not be in winter, nor on the Sabbath." He confirms this reason from the time, the sum of which is this: the calamity will be so great that, since it cannot be avoided, we must pray anxiously that our flight not be hindered either by the storms that usually come in the winter season, or by religious observance, as on the Sabbath day, when it was not permitted to walk further than two thousand paces, as some reckon. For the Mount of Olives is a Sabbath day's journey from the city, as the book of Acts testifies. Bethany, which lies on the slopes of that mountain, according to the evangelist John, is fifteen stadia from Jerusalem, which make roughly two thousand paces more or less. This passage is enough to refute those who maintain that every flight is unlawful, an opinion which we have elsewhere said Tertullian once held. Why, indeed, would the Lord bid us pray that flight be granted a convenient time, if flight were not lawful at all? But one may preserve oneself for better times, if this is permitted without loss of religion. Yet, so that he may exhort us more effectively to prayer, we must also look more closely at what we ought to do here: "For there will then be great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor will be." He speaks of the wrath of God, which will blaze against the nation of the Jews on account of the crime committed against the Son of God, Jesus Christ, than which nothing more grievous and atrocious could be done. But what follows is full of consolation: "And unless those days had been shortened, every flesh would perish. But for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened." This is a memorable passage. Scripture teaches that for the sake of the pious and the elect, nations and commonwealths are preserved, and that God never is so angry that he does not take account of his own people. Therefore, lest he seem to exceed measure in punishing those who deserve to be punished more severely, he cuts short the time of the punishments. So true is what the Apostle says: that God is faithful, who will not allow his own to be tempted beyond what they can bear. This zeal for piety commends itself to us, so that if we do not cultivate it for our own sake, we may at least honour others whom we see to be zealous for piety. For the zeal for piety is full of labour. But those who love and venerate this in others take upon themselves the labours and cares of others, and so they make use of God's favour. For the promise of Christ is: "Whoever receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive the reward of a righteous man." Yet the wickedness of the world shines out greatly, since it hates no one more than the pious worshippers of God, for whose sake that heavenly Father either destroys or preserves the whole machinery of this world. Lot, before he had gone out of Sodom with his own people, could not be destroyed by the Lord, since the region was doomed to ruin. And when he likewise pleaded anxiously for the little town of Zoar, God heard him and answered him kindly: "In this matter also I have heard you, that I will not overthrow that little town of which you have spoken. Hurry and be saved there, for I can do nothing until you get there." Many things of this kind happen, and it often happens that those who preside over others are despised and hated by those who cannot live well without them. Let us learn therefore, on the occasion of this passage, to hold pious men in esteem and to imitate them. Sometimes profane men persuade themselves that there is no difference between the pious and the impious, and so they accommodate themselves to the world and are led by the blind affections of the flesh. But God cannot be deceived, and his judgments are just. Let us therefore strive to cultivate faith in Jesus Christ our Lord, who will not forsake those who trust in him, and will make them superior to all evils or adversities. Let this passage confirm us in this faith, by which we are taught that God will then also preserve his elect in Christ, even if the whole circle of the earth should perish along with Jerusalem. Let us therefore be brave and steadfast in him, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXIX.
units.tr: Homily 279.

units.la: Tunc si quis vobis dixerit: Ecce hic Christus, aut hic: ne credite. Surgent enim pseudochristi & pseudoprophetae: & dabunt signa magna & miracula: ita vt seducant (si fieri potest) etiam electos. Ecce praedixi vobis. Itaque si dixerint vobis, Ecce in deserto est: ne egrediamini. Ecce in conclaviibus: ne credite. Sicut enim fulgur exit ab oriente, & apparet vsque in occidentem, ita etiam erit aduentus Filij hominis. Vbicunque enim fuerit cadaver, illuc congregabuntur aquilae.
units.tr: "Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is Christ,' or 'there he is,' do not believe it. For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect. Behold, I have told you beforehand. So if they say to you, 'Behold, he is in the desert,' do not go out. 'Behold, he is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it. For just as the lightning comes out of the east and shines even into the west, so also will the coming of the Son of man be. For wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will gather."

units.la: HAggaeus propheta, vt Iudaeos ex Babylone reuersos ad templi aedificationem adhortaretur, secundi huius aut posterioris templi gloriam sine maiestatem maiorem fore dicit, quam prioris per Solomonem extructi fuerit. Id vero propter Christum dixit, qui in posteriori templo exhibitus, hoc suis concionibus & salutaribus signis sine miraculis illustrauit. Id vero plerique Iudaeorum ad externum regnum transtulerunt: quo errore discipuli quoque decepti sub praetextu regni Dei per Christum instaurandi aureram aetatem somniarunt, & sibi delitias finxerunt, quibus cum laeta pace in hac vita frui debeant. Contra quem errorem illos grauiter praemonet, & nuper ex Daniele docuit, vrbem cum templo horribiliter excindi & vastari oportere. Et licet hoc contra eam persuasionem dictum sit, quae tunc multis impulsit, vt in IESV CHRISTO regnum huius seculi somniarent, non minus tamen ad nos pertinet, qui vulgares Ecclesiae calamitates diligenter obseruare debemus. Est enim frequens admodum, quod delirijs & ineptijs nostris delitias nobis fingimus, dum in religione consensum & pacem huius mundi, pacem stabilem inter principes, victorias item & dulce otium sperramus. Sed plerunque fit, vt quo suauiori ipsae nosipsos lassamus, eo graviora certamina aduersus nos surgant: quae deinde nos grauissime offendunt. Idcirco vt ad ea diligenti praemeditatione praeparemur, opus est. Idcirco Dominus noster Christus nunc tertio repetit, quae de signis & periculosis motibus dixerat, qui excidium vrbis & templi praecessurus sint. rifint: vel potius qua de illo solo dicta videbantur, propius ad consummationem mundi & nouissi-ma tempora accommodat. Vbi haec nobis ordine consideranda sunt. Primo quid de posterioribus tem-poribus praedicatur, videamus. Deinde cur de iis praemoneat? Et quid tunc nobis de Ecclesia sen-tiendum aut iudicandum sit.
units.tr: The prophet Haggai, to urge the Jews who had returned from Babylon to build the temple, says that the glory of this second or later temple, or rather its greater majesty, will surpass that of the former temple built by Solomon. He said this on account of Christ, who appeared in the later temple and illuminated it by his sermons and by his saving signs and miracles. Yet most of the Jews applied this to an external kingdom. By this error even the disciples were deceived; under the pretext that the kingdom of God would be restored through Christ, they dreamed of a golden age and imagined for themselves pleasures with which they would enjoy a joyful peace in this life. Against this error he gravely warns them, and he recently taught from Daniel that the city and the temple must be terribly cut down and laid waste. And although this was said against that expectation which then moved many to dream of a worldly kingdom in Jesus Christ, it pertains no less to us, who ought to observe carefully the common calamities of the Church. For it is very common that we fashion for ourselves pleasures by our own follies and fancies, while we hope for agreement in religion and the peace of this world, a stable peace among princes, and likewise victories and a sweet leisure. But it usually happens that the sweeter the things with which we lull ourselves, the more grievous the struggles that rise against us, which then strike us most severely. Therefore we need to prepare ourselves for these by diligent meditation. For this reason our Lord Christ now repeats for the third time what he had said about the signs and dangerous movements that would precede the destruction of the city and the temple, or rather he adapts what seemed to be said only of that event more closely to the consummation of the world and the last times. Here we must consider these things in order. First, let us see what is foretold about the later times. Then, why he warns us about them, and what we ought to think and judge about the Church at that time.

units.la: Quoad primum, ait: Tunc si quis vobis dixerit, Ecce hic Christus, aut hic, non credite. Duo di-cit. Primum, fore dicit aliquos, qui Christos novos hinc inde monstrent. Alterum ne illis fides ha-beatur monet. His rationis loco subtexit: Surgent enim pseudochristi et pseudoprophetae, et edent signa magna & miracula, ita ut seducant (si fieri possit) etiam electos. Et adjeuerationis ergo ad-dit. Ecce praedixi vobis. Comprehendit his omnis generis pericula, quae circa fidem & salutis aeter-nae causam incident, dum differentiones exoriuntur, & Christus in partes scinditur, & quisque Christo gloriatur, plerique autem Christum sibi fingunt pro suo arbitrio longe alium, quam revera sit. Etenim verus Christus est aeternus Dei filius, qui ex Maria virgine homo factus omnia praestitit, quae re-gis & sacerdotis munera sunt, & ad humani generis redemptionem faciunt. Et de quo Apostoli prosi-tentur, quod solum verba vitae aeternae habeat, quod non in ipso vno salus sit, neque aliud nomen inter homines sub caelo hominibus datum sit, in quo nos servari oporteat. Falsi ergo Christi sunt, quaecunque alia fingunt salutis media, aut qui illum honore sibi ipsis vendicant contra illud Christi per prophetam dicentis: Ego Dominus, hoc est, nomen meum & gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Inprae-senti ergo CHRISTI nomen primo ponitur, pro salute ipsa & iustitia, cuius nobis Christus vni-cus author est: deinde pro ipsa persona Christi, quae Deo & homine constat, ex Maria virgine na-ta. Ut vero ante vrbis & templi excidium exorti sunt, qui se Messias esse dixerunt, & Iudaeorum gentem falso promissionum & prophetiarum sensu fascinatum, in loca deserta eduxerunt, & pu-blicarum seditionum fuerunt authores: quae res multis exitium et interitum peperit. Ita nouissimis temporibus fore ait, ut infinita salutis media & innumeri redemptionis modi excogitentur ab ho-minibus superstitiosis, qui Christi meritum & quae huic debetur gloriam, vel in seipsos vel in alias creaturas aut media transferunt.
units.tr: As to the first point, he says: "Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is Christ,' or 'there,' do not believe it." He says two things. First, he says that there will be some who will point out new Christs here and there. Second, he advises that they should not be believed. As the reason for this he adds: "For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect." And for emphasis he adds: "Behold, I have told you beforehand." He thereby includes every kind of danger that arises concerning faith and the cause of eternal salvation, when divisions break out, Christ is torn into parts, each man boasts of Christ, and many fashion for themselves a Christ quite different, at their own pleasure, from what he really is. For the true Christ is the eternal Son of God, who, made man from the Virgin Mary, performed all the offices of king and priest and everything that pertains to the redemption of the human race. Of him the Apostles testify that he alone has the words of eternal life, that salvation is not in anyone else, and that there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved. Therefore those are false christs who invent other means of salvation, or who claim his honour for themselves, contrary to that saying of Christ through the prophet: "I am the Lord; that is, my name and my glory I will not give to another." So in the present passage the name of Christ is first put for salvation itself and righteousness, of which Christ is the sole author; then it is put for the person of Christ himself, who consists of God and man, born of the Virgin Mary. Now, before the destruction of the city and the temple, there arose men who called themselves the Messiah, and who, bewitching the Jewish people with a false sense of the promises and prophecies, led them out into the desert and were the authors of public seditions, which brought ruin and destruction to many. So he says that in the last times there will likewise be devised infinite means of salvation and countless modes of redemption by superstitious men, who transfer the merit of Christ and the glory due to him to themselves or to other creatures or to means.

units.la: Caepit hoc mox post Christi ascensionem, praedicantibus adhuc plerisque Apostolorum. Quid enim aliud fecerunt, qui doctrinae fidei legem admisericuerunt, & homines partim fide in Christum par-tim ex legis operibus iustificari & seruari docuerunt. Hi certe non falsum modo Christum finxe-runt, sed illum (ut Paulus scribit) prorsus fecerunt inutilem. Secuti sunt mox alij, qui Diuorum merita Christo coniunxerunt. Inuenti deniq; qui sua opera aut merita in eandem dignitatem effer-re ausi sunt. Accesserunt his monasticorum votorum cumulus, in quibus aeternae salutis meritum homi-nes superstitiosi monstrarunt. Et in his tandem primatum tenuit Deus ille Mayzim Antichristi fi apud Danielem, qui revera Christus novus & falsus est. Finxit enim Romanus Pontifex ex farina crustulam, quam quinque vocului transubstantiari docuit in verum corpus & sanguinem IESV CHRISTI, & hunc verum Deum & hominem esse, qui pro peccatis viuentium & mor-tuorum immolatur. Est hic revera (ut dixi) falsus Christus, quem nemo patrum agnouit, & quem Antichristus sub Innocentio III. demum confirmato in Lateranensi concilio transubstantiationis dogmate confirmauit. Honorius autem tertius aediculam sacris & pretiosis, quas ciboria vocant, decorauit, & cuius festum diem Vrbanus quartus demum sub annum nati in carne aeterni Filij Dei M. CC. LXIIII. instituit. Abeo tempore IESVS CHRISTVS monstrari coepit hinc in-de in terris non in tabernaculis modo, id est, in ciboriis aut locis reconditis, aris, fatellis & locis aliis, qui aliqua singulari sanctitate sive religione commendabantur, verumetiam cucullis, imaginibus statuis, membranis, aqua benedicta, campanis, ossibus mortuorum, et sexcentis alijs, quae nihil non andens superstitio excogitauit. Eo deniq; excreuit superstitio, ut miretur aliquis, eo dementia vn-quam adduci potuisse homines non omnino dementes, ut ea crederent, quae neq; rationibus aut ar-gumentis neq; scripturarum testimonijs demonstrari potuerunt.
units.tr: This began soon after the ascension of Christ, while many of the Apostles were still preaching. For what else did those do who admitted the law along with the doctrine of faith, and taught that men are justified and saved partly by faith in Christ and partly by the works of the law? Certainly they not only falsely made Christ, but (as Paul writes) made him altogether useless. Soon others followed, who joined the merits of the saints to Christ. Finally some were found who dared to raise their own works or merits to the same dignity. To these was added the heap of monastic vows, in which superstitious men displayed merit for eternal salvation. And in these things at last that god Mayzim of Antichrist, mentioned by Daniel, held the first place; he is truly a new and false Christ. For the Roman Pontiff fashioned from flour a little wafer, which he taught that five words transubstantiate into the true body and blood of Jesus Christ, and that this is the true God and man, who is offered for the sins of the living and the dead. This, as I have said, is truly a false Christ, whom none of the Fathers recognised, and whom Antichrist, under Innocent III, confirmed by the dogma of transubstantiation in the Lateran Council. Honorius III adorned a little shrine for the sacred and precious vessels, which they call ciboria; and Urban IV at last, in the year 1264 after the birth in the flesh of the eternal Son of God, instituted a festival day for it. From that time Jesus Christ began to be shown here and there on earth, not only in tabernacles, that is, in ciboria or hidden places, altars, niches, and other places which were commended by some singular sanctity or religion, but also in cowls, images, statues, parchments, holy water, bells, bones of the dead, and six hundred other things, which superstition, leaving nothing untried, devised. Finally superstition grew to such a pitch that one may wonder that men who were not wholly mad could ever be led to such madness as to believe those things which could be demonstrated neither by reasons and arguments nor by the testimonies of the Scriptures.

units.la: Sed quod olim de Pseudoprophetis dictum fuit, qui Dei ministros falsis signis & magicis prae-stigijs oppugnarunt, hoc ipsum de illis dici potest. Aegyptij magi Pharaone ementitis signis sedu-cebant, ut ipsis potius quam Dei monitis parerent. Et Deus olim pseudoprophetis permittebat, ut filios Israelis, qui disserti ipsius mandatis parere detrectabant, falsis miraculis tentarent. Hoc
units.tr: But what was once said of the false prophets, who attacked the ministers of God with false signs and magical tricks, can be said of these men. The Egyptian magicians deceived Pharaoh with counterfeit signs, so that he would obey them rather than the warnings of God. And God once permitted the false prophets to test the sons of Israel, who refused to obey his commands, with false miracles. This

units.la: 4 ipsum de Antichristo quoq; olim Paulus praedixit: fore nimirum, ut efficacia illusione imponant iis, qui veritate non dignantur admittere. Sunt autem miraculorum plena omnia, quorum alia prorsus falsa et fictitia sunt, alia manifesta Satanae illusione fiunt. Et dies me deficeret, si quae circa transfubstantiationem, circa imagines aut apparitiones Divorum, aut Spiritus facta sunt, commemorare velim. Alibi enim statuas in alium locum concessisse dixerunt monachi, alibi eas de sanguine suda fecisse, alibi humano sermone locutas esse, aut alia quaedam insolita et miraculosa fecisse. In his autem omnibus meminerint pij, medacia et super stitiones signis et prodigiis nequaquam confirmari, nisi difer to Dei verbo commendentur. Ideo Christus sua miracula scripturae testimonijs probare solebat: et quoties adversarij miraculis gloriantur, tu huius loci recordator, et ex eo collige, non tutum esse miraculis credere, nisi prius per vera fidei principia probetur, quod aliqui prodigijs probare conantur.
units.tr: 4 very thing Paul also once foretold about Antichrist: that, of course, with the working of error they would impose on those who did not deign to admit the truth. Now all things are full of miracles, of which some are altogether false and fictitious, and others are produced by Satan's manifest delusion. And the day would fail me if I wished to recount what has been done concerning transubstantiation, concerning images or the apparitions of the saints or of spirits. For in one place the monks have said that statues moved to another place, in another place that they sweated blood, in another that they spoke in human speech, or did certain other unusual and miraculous things. But in all these things let the godly remember that lies and superstitions are by no means confirmed by signs and prodigies, unless they are commended by the word of God. Therefore Christ used to prove his miracles by the testimonies of Scripture; and whenever adversaries boast of their miracles, remember this passage and gather from it that it is not safe to believe in miracles unless what they try to prove by prodigies is first tested by the true principles of faith.

units.la: Habet autem dulcissimam consolationem locus hic. Dum enim exceptione utitur Christus, quia electos seducere posse negat: non obscure docet, tentari hos quidem, a salute autem excidere non posse. Dona enim et vocatio eiusmodi sunt, ut Deum ipsorum poenitere non possit. In Christo enim radices sive fundamentum habent, qui filius ille dilectus est in quo nos sibi gratos et acceptos fecit. Appa ret hoc in electis omnibus, qui cum Paulo consentiunt dicunt: Quis nos separabit a dilectione Dei? Et quia omnia adversa vincuntur in Christo, qui ipsos corroborat, multo minus promissis aut blandi tijs huius mundi cedunt, quibus Satan incautos solet inseqare. Arguit hoc illorum ignauiam, qui hodie Iesuitarum impostura tam facile succumbunt, ut propter ementita et fictitia miracula admittant illicitos cultus et cum manifestis scripturae testimonijs pugnantes idolomanias.
units.tr: This passage offers a most sweet consolation. When Christ adds the qualification that the elect cannot be led astray, he clearly teaches that these people may indeed be tempted, but cannot fall from salvation. For the gifts and the calling are of such a kind that God cannot repent of them. They have their roots and foundation in Christ, that beloved Son in whom he has made us pleasing and acceptable to himself. This is evident in all the elect, who agree with Paul and say: "Who shall separate us from the love of God?" Since all adversities are overcome in Christ, who strengthens them, they yield much less to the promises and enticements of this world, with which Satan is accustomed to pursue the unwary. This exposes the cowardice of those who today give in so easily to the deceit of the Jesuits, that on account of lying and fabricated miracles they accept unlawful forms of worship and idolatries that fight against the plain testimonies of Scripture.

units.la: Caeterum cur de iustis nos praemoneat Dei filius, probe observari debet. Si enim nihil in rerum natura fortuito fit, multo minus in ecclesia, qua hic nihil pretiosius habet temere fieri patietur. Ut vero ipse omnia suo freno gubernat atque moderatur, ita ipsa prius quam fiant praedicere voluit, ut credentes in fide promissionum confirmentur: ne quando motus et turbas vel confusiones istiusmodi videant, de providentia Dei dubitent et omnia temere ferri cogitent, adeoque superuacaneas esse atque ritas preces atque invocationem. Est igitur hoc ingens divinae bonitatis argumentum, quod defutu ris nos praemonere dignatur, ne incerti et inutilibus speculationibus nos ipsos lactemus.
units.tr: Moreover, we must carefully observe why the Son of God forewarns us about the righteous. For if nothing in the nature of things happens by chance, much less will he allow anything to happen carelessly in the Church, which he holds more precious than anything here. Just as he himself governs and directs all things with his rein, so he wished to foretell them before they happen, so that believers may be strengthened in faith in the promises, lest at some time, when they see such movements, disturbances and confusions, they doubt God's providence and think that everything is carried along at random, and so consider prayers and invocation vain and useless. Therefore this is a great proof of divine goodness, that he deigns to forewarn us of future events, so that we do not weary ourselves with uncertain and useless speculations.

units.la: Vbi in primis observari debet, quod apud Lucam a Pharisaeo quodam interrogatus Dominus respondit, regnum Dei non ita venturum esse, ut observari possit, id est, cum externo maiestatis splendore, ex quo possit agnosci. Regni Dei nomine intelligitur totum nostrae salutis aut redemptionis negotium, cuius hic finis est, ut defructa diaboli tyrannide homines asserantur in libertatem filiorum Dei. At tunc concionaes omnes Ioannis Baptistae, Christi, Apostolorum non aliud quam regnum Dei crepabant. Id vero Iudaei somniabant terrenum, et certo loco alligabant, deniq; tribuebant illi externum splendorem, ex quo agnosci possit. Et hoc errore Apostolos quoq; deceptos fuisse fatimus. Eum ergo Christus confutat, et nihil huius de suo regno cogitandum esse docet. Praedicuntur quidem in prophetis multa, ex quibus aduentus Christi primus agnosci potuit: fe cundus quoq; signus cerus denotatur, quae in praesenti tractatione et alijs scripturae locis explicantur. Sed ut diximus, hic de certo loco aut apparatu externo et splendore Jermo est: ne videlicet putemus ecclesiae loco certo aut certis hominibus alligatam esse. Non est enim regnum Christi de hoc mundo, sed spirituale est, et in cordibus hominum sedem sive locum habet: et eiusdem aduentus secundus ut prior in humilitate, sed in gloria demonstrandus erit. Stultum est ergo in parvo loco aut abscondito quaerere eum qui totius mundi lumen est. Quo argumento confutantur omnes superstitiones quibus salutis ratio aut Dei cultus loco certo, aut ecclesiae successioni certorum hominum alligatur. Itaque dicit Christus: Si dixerint vobis, Ecce in deserto est, ne egredimini: Ecce in conclavibus, ne credi te. Et rationis loco addit: Sicut enim fulgur exit ab Oriente, et apparet usque in Occidente, ita etiam erit aduentus filij hominis. Quod de novissimo quidem aduentu Christi potest exponi, qui subitus et improvisus veniet: interim spiritualiter quoq; intelligi debet de Spiritus Christi gratia, quae subiit electorum mentes irradiat, neq; vllis remoris impediri potest, quo minus spiret, vbi ipse vult.
units.tr: Here, first of all, it must be observed that in Luke, when a certain Pharisee asked the Lord, he answered that the kingdom of God would not come in such a way that it could be observed, that is, with outward splendour of majesty by which it could be recognised. By the name of the kingdom of God is understood the whole business of our salvation or redemption, whose aim is that, with the tyranny of the devil overthrown, men may be claimed for the liberty of the sons of God. Yet all the sermons of John the Baptist, of Christ and of the Apostles cried out about nothing other than the kingdom of God. The Jews, however, dreamed of an earthly kingdom and bound it to a certain place, and finally attributed to it an outward splendour by which it could be recognised. We admit that the Apostles too were deceived by this error. Christ therefore refutes this, and teaches that nothing of this sort should be thought about his kingdom. Many things indeed are foretold in the prophets, from which his first coming could be recognised, and his second coming too is clearly indicated; these are explained in the present treatment and in other passages of Scripture. But, as we have said, here the discussion concerns a fixed place or external display and splendour, lest we suppose that the Church is tied to a fixed place or to fixed men. For the kingdom of Christ is not of this world, but is spiritual, and has its seat or place in the hearts of men; and his second coming, like the first, will be in humility, yet it will be displayed in glory. It is foolish, then, to seek in a small or hidden place him who is the light of the whole world. By this argument all superstitions are refuted, by which the way of salvation or the worship of God is tied either to a certain place or to the succession of certain men. Thus Christ says: "If they say to you, Behold, he is in the desert, do not go out; behold, he is in the inner rooms, do not believe it." And, as a reason, he adds: "For as lightning comes out of the east and appears even in the west, so also will be the coming of the Son of man." This can indeed be explained of the final coming of Christ, which will be sudden and unforeseen; yet in the meantime it must also be understood spiritually, of the grace of Christ's Spirit, which enters and illumines the minds of the elect, and which cannot be hindered by any obstacle from breathing where it wills.

units.la: Incidit autem hic quaestio admodum necessaria, quae hodie multos turbat. Vbi nimirum sit ecclesia? Vt enim Respub. esse putamus, vbi sunt principes et magistratus, e contra autem seditiosos dicimus, qui ab his differunt: ita quando scismata exoriuntur, plerique ijs se coniungunt, penes quos est titulus Ecclesia, quales fere sunt Pontifices, Episcopi, Præsules, & hos errare pos- se negant. At nos teneamus diuersam esse rationem Ecclesiæ & Reipub. Hæc enim ex hominibus constat etiam nondum renatis, & humana quoq; prudentia regitur, & proinde ei certa fede, tri- bunali & iudiciorum subsellijs atq; alijs opus est, sine quibus regnare nequit. Ecclesia vero per to tum orbem extenditur, nec vlli loco certo alligata est, vt neq; Dei cultus & inuocatio. Veri enim adoratores, in Spiritu & veritate adorant, & quouis loco puras manus attollunt absq; ira Dei & disceptatione. Nec tamen Ecclesia fingi debet inuisibilis, qualem Enthusiastæ fingunt, qua exter nis pietatis exercitijs destituatur. Etenim Deus ideo homines creauit & redemit, vt ipse ab illis inuocetur & colatur, vtq; inter illos in Filio suo IESV CHRISTO innotescat. Ecclesia ergo esse oportet, in qua confessio fidei publica ædatur, & quæ sponso suo cultu debitum præstet. Hæc et si visibilis est, & in suos cœtus conuenit (quos alibi frequentiores, alibi tenuiores aut rariores colli git, adeo vt sicuti apud Isaiam, interdum de macilentia quoq; sua conqueratur) tamen hinc inde dispersa est, nec simili regno aut Reip. quæ fere sedi certa, aut successioni & legibus humanis aut consuetudinibus astricta est. Sed Ecclesia proprie est cœtus omnium electorum, qui amplestitur ver- bum Dei, per Prophetas, Christum & Apostolos traditum, nec pertinaciter defendit idola & er- rores cum verbo Dei pugnantes. Ecclesia ergo est, vbi verbum Euangelij prædicatur, & auditur. Quod non obscurè Christus testatur, dicens: Oues mæ vocem meam audiunt, & ego eas agnosco, & sequuntur me. Et ego vitam æternam do eis, &c. Item: Amen amen dico vobis, qui sermonem meum audit, & credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, &c. Et rursum: Si manseritis in me, & verba mea in vobis manserint, quicquid voluerit is, petite, & fiet vobis.
units.tr: Here arises a question of great necessity, which troubles many today: where, indeed, is the Church? For just as we consider there to be a commonwealth wherever there are princes and magistrates, and on the other hand we call those seditious who differ from these, so when schisms arise, most people join themselves to those who hold the name of Church, such as, for the most part, the popes, bishops and prelates, and they deny that these can err. But let us hold that the Church and the commonwealth have a different structure. For the commonwealth consists of men, even those not yet reborn, and is governed also by human prudence; and therefore it needs a certain seat, a tribunal and benches for judgments, and other things, without which it cannot rule. The Church, however, is spread throughout the whole world and is tied to no fixed place, just as neither is the worship and invocation of God. For true worshippers worship in spirit and truth, and in any place they lift up pure hands without anger and dispute. Yet the Church ought not to be imagined as invisible, as the Enthusiasts imagine it, deprived of the outward exercises of piety. For God therefore created and redeemed men, that he might be invoked and worshipped by them, and that he might be made known among them in his Son Jesus Christ. The Church must therefore exist, in which the public confession of faith is made and which pays due worship to its Bridegroom. This Church, although it is visible and gathers into its assemblies (which it gathers in some places more numerous, in others smaller or thinner, so that, as in Isaiah, it sometimes complains even of its own leanness), is nevertheless scattered here and there, and is not bound to a kingdom or commonwealth that has a fixed seat, nor to a succession and human laws or customs. But the Church properly is the assembly of all the elect, who embrace the Word of God, handed down through the prophets, Christ and the Apostles, and who do not obstinately defend idols and errors that fight against the Word of God. Therefore the Church is where the Word of the Gospel is preached and heard. Christ clearly bears witness to this, saying: "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. And I give them eternal life," etc. Likewise: "Truly, truly I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life," etc. And again: "If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatever you will, and it shall be done for you."

units.la: At hic meminisse oportet, Ecclesiam externam non semper omnibus numeris absolutam, & (vt a Paulo dicitur) absq; ruga & macula esse. Nam, Christo teste, instar retis aut sagenæ est, quæ pisces bonos atq; putres trahit, & agro similis, in quem bono semine consitum hostis noster Sa tan zizania sua aspergit, quæ simul excrescunt. Quod ergo disputatur, num errare possit Ecclesia, superuacaneum est. Quatenus enim verbum Dei audit, & sponso suo fidem feruat, errare nequit. At quia frequenter suis placitis indulget, & opinionibus prauis ducitur, fieri non potest, quin ossi cij immemor exorbitet. Fit deniq;, vt interdum in externa Ecclesiæ societate regnent porci & asi- ni, qui portenta errorum, & manifestas idolomanias defendunt. Sic Christi tempore Ecclesiæ titu lus penes Iudæos erat, in qua numerabantur Zacharias, Elizabet, Simeon, Anna, Maria virgo, Ioseph, & quidam alij, de quibus merito dixerus, illos nequaquam pernitiose aut impie errauisse, fue runt tamen alij, quos communis ignorantia seduxit: alij item, quos Sadducæorum impietas safci nauit, vt errores horribiles secuti sint. Et notus est Pauli locus, quo alij supra fundamentum IESVM CHRISTVM, aurum, argentum, gemmas, lapides: alij fœnum, stipulas, putria ligna ex truere dicuntur, quæ in igne examinus diuini pereunt, manente interim fundamento. Quoad hos ergo, errant quidem illi, errores vero non defendunt pertinaciter, sed in Christum intenti, huic se to tos consecrant: & cum de fidei examine agitur, cum Apostolis dicunt: Domine, quo ibimus? Tu habes verba vitæ æternæ: Et nos credimus & nouimus te esse Christum illum Filium Dei viuentis. Et huc pertinet quod apud Lucam interrogantibus discipulis, vbi ipsi mansuri sint, aut quo se re- cipere debeant, si a regno Dei nolint excidere, respondet Dominus: Vbicunq; fuerit cadauer, illuc congregabuntur aquilæ. Aquilas dicit vere credentes, qui fidei alis super terra & omnia quæ in terris pretiosa sunt eueẽti cœlestia asseẽtant. His in seipso portu tutum monstrat, in quæ sese re cipiant, & ad ipsum etiam colligentur in nouissimo die, quando mortui resurgent, & qui tunc su- perstites erunt, vna cum eis simul in nubes rapientur in occursum Domini, & ita semper cum Do- mino erunt. Stulti & miseri, qui alio confugiunt, aut iam morituri animas suas alij, quam vnico redemptori Christo commendant.
units.tr: But here we must remember that the external Church is not always perfect in every respect, and (as Paul says) without wrinkle or spot. For, by Christ's testimony, it is like a net or dragnet, which draws in both good and rotten fish, and like a field in which our enemy Satan scatters his tares among the good seed sown there, and they grow up together. Therefore the question whether the Church can err is idle. For insofar as it hears the Word of God and keeps faith with its Bridegroom, it cannot err. But because it frequently gives in to its own pleasures and is led by corrupt opinions, it cannot but happen that, forgetful of its duty, it goes astray. Finally it comes about that sometimes in the external fellowship of the Church pigs and asses rule, who defend monstrous errors and manifest idolatries. Thus in Christ's time the title of Church belonged to the Jews, among whom were counted Zechariah, Elizabeth, Simeon, Anna, the Virgin Mary, Joseph, and certain others, of whom we rightly say that they did not err in a pernicious or impious way; there were others, however, whom common ignorance led astray, and others again whom the impiety of the Sadducees had shipwrecked, so that they followed horrible errors. And the well-known passage of Paul is relevant, where some are said to build upon the foundation of Jesus Christ gold, silver, precious stones, and marble, and others hay, stubble and rotten wood, which perish in the fire of divine examination, while the foundation remains. As for these latter, they indeed err, but they do not obstinately defend their errors; intent upon Christ, they devote themselves wholly to him, and when the examination of faith is at issue they say with the Apostles: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. And we believe and know that you are Christ, the Son of the living God." And to this belongs what the Lord says in Luke: when the disciples asked where they would remain, or to what place they should withdraw if they did not want to fall from the kingdom of God, he answered: "Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered." By eagles he means truly believing people, who, borne on the wings of faith, rise above the earth and assert heavenly things above all that is precious on earth. To these he shows in himself a safe harbour into which they may withdraw, and they will also be gathered to him on the last day, when the dead will rise, and those who are then still alive will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord, and so they will always be with the Lord. Foolish and wretched are those who flee to another refuge, or who, about to die, commit their souls to anyone other than the one Redeemer, Christ.

units.la: Habet autem doctrina hæc multiplicem consolationem, qua nosipsos confirmare debemus, ne inter pericula, quæ nobis accidunt labascamus. Hic enim nobis firmum & ratu sit, quod vbicunq; sunt qui Euangelij Verbum amplestuntur, hi membra Ecclesiæ sunt, & a Christo pro discipulis agnoscuntur. Exsemine enim Verbi Dei nascitur Ecclesia. Deinde quod Dei Filius Ecclesiæ propugnator aderit, vt easferuet vsq; ad consummationem sæculorum. Ipse enim est verus ille Michael, quem prophetā Daniel dicit stare ducem pro populo suo. Tertio quod inter nouissimorum temporum sanctas non deficiet doctrina veritatis, sed rata & stabilis manebit promissio, quae per Isaiam olim data est a Domino: Spiritus meus, qui super te est, & verba mea, quae inserui ori tuo, nunquam recedent de ore tuo, neque de ore feminis tui, neque de ore nepotū ac pronepotū tuorum. Postremo quod Dei filius sese mundo manifestabit, ut Ecclesia suam glorificet: tunc huius similes erimus, impiosque autem abiciet in stagnum ardens igne & sulphure. Simus ergo constantes in fide, & accincti sancto obedientiae fidei studio, praeparemus nos ad occursum IESV CHRISTI redemptoris nostri, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: This doctrine offers a manifold consolation, by which we ought to strengthen ourselves, so that we do not waver amid the dangers that befall us. For here it is firm and certain for us that wherever there are those who embrace the Word of the Gospel, these are members of the Church, and are acknowledged by Christ as his disciples; for the Church is born from the seed of the Word of God. Second, that the Son of God will be present as the defender of the Church, to preserve her until the end of the ages. For he is that true Michael whom the prophet Daniel says stands as the prince for his people. Third, that among the holy of the latest times the doctrine of truth will not fail, but the promise given long ago by the Lord through Isaiah will remain sure and stable: "My Spirit, which is upon you, and my words, which I have put in your mouth, shall never depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of the seed of your seed" [cf. Isa. 59]. Lastly, that the Son of God will reveal himself to the world, so that he may glorify his Church; then we shall be like him, and he will cast the impious into the lake burning with fire and sulphur. Let us therefore be steadfast in the faith, and girded with a holy zeal for obedience to the faith, and let us prepare ourselves to meet Jesus Christ, our redeemer, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXX.
units.tr: HOMILY CCLXXX.

units.la: Statim autem post afflictionem dierum illorum Sol obscurabitur, nec dabit luna splendorem suum, & stellae cadent e coelo & potestates coelorum concutientur. Tunc apparebit signum Filii hominis in coelo: & tunc omnes tribus terrae plangent, & videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus coeli cum potentia & gloria multa. Is vero mittet angelos suos cum tuba voce magna, & cogent electos eius a quatuor ventis, a coelorum extremo ad extremum eorum.
units.tr: "Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven shall be shaken. Then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth shall mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great trumpet, and they shall gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other."

units.la: ALtera discipulorum quaestio, quam Domino nostro IESV CHRISTO propposuerunt, est de totius seculi consummatione, quam illi mox post templi & cultus Leuitici abrogationem fore arbitrabantur. Ad hanc nunc transitum facit Dominus, & primo signa quaedam recensét, ex quibus colligi possit vniuersam hanc mundi machinam ruituram esse. Deinde aduentum suum describit, & quae tunc futura sit hominum conditio. Praeterea vaticinio huic argumentum aliquot fidem facit. Vsus loci huius praecipuus est, ut per finem mundi admoneamur, nihil in terris inter homines stabile esse, nec quenquam debere offendi victoriis aut aliis successibus impiorum, qui sibi perpetuam felicitatem pollicentur. Quantacunque enim & qualiscunque sit huius seculi prosperitas, sequetur tamen retributio, & fere eo grauiori lapsu ruunt, quo altius cadunt, qui supra alios aseenderunt.
units.tr: The second question which the disciples put to our Lord Jesus Christ concerned the end of the whole age, which they thought would come soon after the abolition of the temple and the Levitical worship. The Lord now turns to this question. First he recounts certain signs from which it may be inferred that this whole frame of the world will collapse. Then he describes his coming and what the condition of men will then be. Moreover, several arguments give credit to this prophecy. The chief use of this passage is that, by the end of the world, we are warned that nothing among men on earth is stable, and that no one should be troubled by the victories or other successes of the wicked, who promise themselves lasting happiness. For however great and of whatever kind the prosperity of this age may be, retribution will follow, and those who have risen above others generally fall with a heavier downfall the higher they have climbed.

units.la: Porro a signis orditur, ut luculentior sit vaticinij fides. Statim autem post afflictionem dierum illorum Sol obscurabitur, nec Luna dabit splendorem suum, & stellae cadent e coelo. Loquitur autem de afflictione dierum illorum, quas Ierosolymae minatus fuit. Et solent Prophetae per obscurationes Solis & Lunae atque stellarum calamitates haud vulgares intelligere, quae miseros mortales consilij & anxilij incertos reddunt. Non temere autem dicit, haec breui secutura esse. Nec tamen intelligit Eclipses Solis aut Lunae vulgares, quales ex orbium coelestium ordinario motu solent contingere, sed eas potius, quae praeter consuetum ordinem contingent. Nam virtutes coelorum (inquit) vel potestates concutientur. Vbi discimus ruinas & occasus rerum publicarum & magnarum timitatum, maximarum calamitatum momenta portendere. Etenim agricolae tempestatum praesagia habent, & Poeta pastores colloquentes inducit: Saepe malum hoc nobis, si mens non laeva fuisset, De coelo tactas memini praedicere quercus.
units.tr: Next he begins with the signs, so that the certainty of the prophecy may be clearer: "Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven." He speaks of the tribulation of those days, which he had threatened for Jerusalem. The prophets are accustomed to understand by the darkening of the sun and moon and by the calamities of the stars extraordinary disasters, which leave wretched mortals uncertain of counsel and help. He does not say this lightly, as though it would follow after a long interval. Yet he does not mean ordinary eclipses of the sun or moon, such as usually happen through the regular motion of the heavenly spheres, but rather those which occur beyond the customary order. For he says, "the powers of heaven shall be shaken." Here we learn that such portents foreshadow the ruin and fall of commonwealths and great kingdoms, and the crises of the greatest calamities. Indeed, farmers have their forecasts of the weather, and the poet introduces shepherds conversing: "Often, I remember, if our minds had not been perverse, the oaks struck from heaven foretold this evil to us."

units.la: At si non incerta extant portenta futurorum in istis, quae longo vsu rerum obseruata homines admonuerunt, quis non putet, diligentiori consideratione digna esse occasus regnorum & vrbium quae praeter expectationem accidunt? Est hic obseruanda nobis Dei bonitas, qui solidiores huius mundi partes in nobis admonendis & excitandis occupatas habet, ne vel ex improuiso opprimamur, vel in periculis omni consilio destituamur. At quia miss-io Spiritus Sancti Apostolis facta, etiam in hoc tempus incidit, nō temere Ioel hanc praedicere volens, signorum meminit, quae tunc fieri oportebat: Eadem (inquit) miracula in coelo sursum et signa in terra deorsum, sanguine et igne et vapore fumi. Sol conuertetur in tenebras, et luna in sanguine, priusquam veniat dies ille Domini magnus & illustris. Sic in Apoc. quoque cum aperuisset sigillum sextum agnus, terraemotus ingens factus est, et sol factus est niger tanquam saccus cilicinus, & Luna tota sanguinea est sicut sanguis, & stellæ de cœlo cecidepunt super terram, sicut ficus abijcit grossos suos cum a vento mouetur. Et cœlum recedit sicut liber, qui circumvoluitur, & omnis mons & insulæ de locis suis motæ sunt, &c. At nos quoties ista accidere videmus, non hæc fortuito aut temere fieri putabimus, sed in mentem reuocemus quod Christus paulo ante dixit de nouissimorum temporum moribus: Quoniam multiplicata est iniquitas, refrigescet charitas multorum. Item Filius hominis cum venerit, num reperturus est fidem in terra? Et paulo post audiemus regnaturam inter homines supinam & deploratam securitatem, intemperantiæ & voluptatis studium cum crapula & Venere, a quibus si semel regnent religionis contemptus, procul abesse non potest. Cum ergo in terris omnis generis scelera hodie regnent, iustitia & pietas exulent, luxus, licentia, libido, auaritia apud omnes loci & ordinis homines dominentur, quid mirum videtur, si elementa & mundi partes nobis minus propitias experiantur? Si anni vices inuerti, & tempestatum ordinem proꝛsus immutari sentiamus? Cur ergo legibus certis pareat cœlum & aer, si nos, in quorum gratiam hæc Deus condidit, exleges viuere volumus? Ex moribus ergo nostris discamus de iis, quæ nobis accidunt iudicare. Et pudeat nostræ contumaciam a cœli facie argui, & id meminerimus fieri, quod Ieremias olim dixit: Transite ad insulas Chitim, & videte: mittite in Kedar, & considerate diligenter, atq; inspicite, num simile quid factum sit. Num gens aliqua mutauerit Deos, qui tamen non sunt Dij. At populus meus mutauit gloriam suam in eo, qui non prodest. Propter hoc obstupescite cœli, exhorrescite & vehementer exhorrescite ait Dominus: quoniam duo mala fecit populus meus: me deseruerunt fontem aquæ perennium, vt effoderent sibi puteos, puteos inquam pertusos, qui aquas continere non possunt. At quid hodie est vulgarius? Pius & religiosus habetur, qui ingenij acumen in hoc intendit, vt quæ Dei sunt vel suis viribus vendicet, vel superstitiones veteres reducat, & simul in nefandissimorum scelerum licentia omnes impudenter ruunt. Irascuntur ergo nobis cœlorum orbes, & iniquo sidere nos Sol & Luna aspiciunt, & si nostrorum temporum historiam euoluas, nullum sæculum inueniet, quod plures eclipses Solis & Lunæ terruerint, quo plures cometæ arserint, pareque plura fulserint, terra sæpius tremuerit, quo deniq; cœlum toties arserit, aut aliis prodigiis horruerit. Accedunt his astus maris, qui multis opulentissimis regionibus interitum & inopiam extremam adduxerunt. Quæ ita nos obseruare decet, vt discamus vniuersam mundi machinam Deo arma præbere, quibus pœnitere nescios puniat. Et vtinam obseruarent omnes, quæ in creatu ris passim omnibus iudiciorum Dei indicia extant, & viderent pleriq; Deum tunc quoq; iudicium suorum memorem esse, quando horum omnino oblitus esse videtur.
units.tr: But if the portents of future events in these things, which men have observed through long experience and which have warned them, are not uncertain, who would not think that the fall of kingdoms and cities which happens beyond expectation is worthy of closer consideration? Here we must observe the goodness of God, who has the more solid parts of this world occupied in admonishing and arousing us, so that we are neither overwhelmed unexpectedly nor left without counsel in dangers. But since the sending of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles also fell at this time, Joel, wishing to foretell it, rightly mentions the signs which were then to appear: "I will show wonders in heaven above and signs on earth beneath, blood and fire and a vapour of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord comes." So also in the Apocalypse, when the Lamb opened the sixth seal, there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black as a sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood, and the stars of heaven fell upon the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when it is shaken by a wind. And the heaven departed like a scroll that is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place, and so on. But whenever we see these things happening, let us not think that they happen by chance or at random, but let us recall what Christ said shortly before about the morals of the last times: "Because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold." Likewise: "When the Son of man comes, will he find faith on the earth?" And a little later we shall hear that a careless and despairing security will reign among men, with a devotion to intemperance and pleasure, with drunkenness and lust, and once these reign, contempt of religion cannot be far away. Therefore, since every kind of wickedness now reigns on earth, justice and piety are banished, and luxury, licence, lust and avarice hold sway among people of every place and rank, what wonder is it if we experience the elements and parts of the world less favourable to us? If we perceive the seasons of the year overturned and the order of the weather utterly changed? Why then should heaven and air obey fixed laws, if we, for whose sake God made these things, wish to live lawless? Let us therefore learn from our own morals to judge what befalls us. And let us be ashamed that our obstinacy is reproved by the face of heaven, and let us remember that what Jeremiah once said has come to pass: "Pass over to the isles of Chittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully and look closely whether anything like this has happened. Has any nation changed its gods, which are yet not gods? But my people has changed its glory for that which does not profit. Be astonished, O heavens, be horribly afraid and utterly appalled, says the Lord, for my people has done two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, to dig for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns, which cannot hold water." But what is more common today? He is considered pious and religious who applies the sharpness of his wit to claim for his own powers what belongs to God, or to revive old superstitions; and at the same time all rush shamelessly into the licence of most abominable crimes. The spheres of heaven are therefore angry with us, and the sun and moon look upon us with an unfavourable star; and if you unroll the history of our own times, you will find no age in which more eclipses of the sun and moon have alarmed people, in which more comets have blazed, and in which the earth has trembled more often, and finally in which the heavens have so often burned or been terrified by other portents. To these are added the tides of the sea, which have brought destruction and utter poverty to many very wealthy regions. We ought to observe these things in such a way that we learn that the whole machinery of the world furnishes God with weapons by which he punishes those who do not know how to repent. And would that all would observe what evidences of God's judgments are everywhere present in creatures, and that many would see that God, even when he seems to have utterly forgotten these things, still remembers his judgments.

units.la: Cæterum euidentius de suo aduentu loquitur Christus. Tunc apparebit (inquit) signum Filii hominis in cœlo, & tunc omnes tribus terræ plangent, & videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli cum potentia & gloria multa. Alludit ad rem militarem & morem principum, qui aduersus hostem egressuri arma sua proferunt, dumq; vexilla militaria exerunt, vindictam ui-stam minantur. Pleriq; veterum crucem interpretantur, cuius imago (teste Eusebio) cum hac inscriptione apparuit Constantino Magno, IN HOC SIGNO VINCES, quando aduersus Maxentium bellum mouit, vt Ecclesiam adiuuaret, quæ proꝛsus deserta videbatur. Quia enim Christus per crucis meritum vicit omnem aduersariam potestatem, crucis quoq; signum victoriæ nostræ præ aliis conuenit, & per eandem ipsi quoq; vincemus. Prodest in huius consideratione diligenter & sæpe versari, & pudeat aliquid aduersum timere, cum ipsa Crucis vox nobis victoriam certam polliceatur.
units.tr: Christ speaks more plainly about his coming: "Then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth shall mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory." He alludes to military affairs and the custom of princes who, about to go out against an enemy, display their arms, and while they raise their military standards, threaten avenging victory. Most of the ancients interpret this as the cross, whose image (according to Eusebius) appeared to Constantine the Great with this inscription, IN THIS SIGN YOU WILL CONQUER, when he waged war against Maxentius, in order to help the Church, which seemed utterly forsaken. For since Christ by the merit of the cross conquered every adverse power, the sign of the cross also fittingly belongs to our victory above all others, and through the same sign we too shall conquer. It is profitable to dwell carefully and often on this consideration, and we should be ashamed to fear anything adverse, since the very word of the cross promises us certain victory.

units.la: Sed describit aduentum suum Christus, dicens: Videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cœli. Videbunt (inquit) venientem. Ergo conspicuus veniet. Et huc facit, promissio Angelorum, qui illo ascendente dixerunt: Hic IESVS qui sursum receptus est a vobis in cœlum, ita ve-niet quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in cœlum. Cui consentit quod Propheta Zacharias dixit: Videbunt in quem pupugerunt. Si quos ergo offendit contemptibilis Christi hominis species, quæ in Cruce pependit, hic in nubibus cœli redeuntis gloriam animo concipiat, cuius pedibus omnes ceu scabellum pedum subijcientur. Ad gloriam Christi pertinet, quod disserte, quæ nofra conditio futura sit, docet, tam piorum minimum quam impiorum. Ad impios enim pertinet,
units.tr: But Christ describes his coming, saying: "They will see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven." They will see (he says) him coming. So he will come visibly. This agrees with the promise of the angels, who, as he ascended, said: "This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven." The prophet Zechariah agrees: "They will look on him whom they have pierced." So if the contemptible appearance of Christ the man, who hung on the Cross, has offended some, let them conceive in their minds the glory of him returning in the clouds of heaven, under whose feet all things will be put, as a footstool. It belongs to the glory of Christ that he plainly teaches what our condition will be in the future, both of the godly, the least of them, and of the ungodly. For it is for the ungodly that

units.la: Vsus signorum cœlestium. Luc. 18. quod hic apud Matthaeum ait: Et tunc omnes tribus terrae plangent. Luctum illis tribuit, qui nul lum sensum gaudij illis aliquem integrum relinquet. Quomodo enim iudicem ferre poterunt, qui Seruatorem & Redemptorem ferre & agnoscere noluerunt? Exempla sunt in Iudaeis hodie, qui IESV CHRISTI vindicem potentiam sibi in mortis articulo infestam esse queruntur, & se hanc sentire aiunt. In desperatis item, qui interdum sibi ipsis mortem violentam inferunt, vt illius vindicem manum effugiant. At quae nunc sentiunt infelices, ludus & iocus sunt, praesijs, quae fient in nouissimo die, quando simul animo & corpore torquebuntur.
units.tr: the use of heavenly signs (Luke 18). Matthew says here: "And then all the tribes of the earth will mourn." He assigns them mourning, and leaves them no sense of joy at all. For how will they be able to bear the Judge, who were unwilling to bear and acknowledge the Saviour and Redeemer? There are examples of this among the Jews today, who complain that the avenging power of Jesus Christ is hostile to them at the point of death, and say that they feel it. Likewise among the desperate, who sometimes bring a violent death upon themselves in order to escape the avenging hand of that One. But what the unhappy feel now is play and jest compared with the terrors that will happen on the last day, when they will be tormented at once in soul and body.

units.la: At longe alia erit piorum & electorum conditio. De his enim dicitur: Videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus caeli cum potentia & gloria multa. Quo autem haec maior & illustrior erit, eo latior erit consolatio, quam illi percipient, & retributionis spes vberior. Nec aliena nobis spes esse potest certa salutis, quam quae in illo die nobis affulgebit, qui nos ad patriae coelestis possessionem deduxerit. Nam ad eum vsque diem exulabit Ecclesia & incertis sedibus iactabitur. Sed tunc illam ad se colliget Christus, & Benedictos Patris sui pronunciabit eos, quos alij odio dignos & pro maledictis habent. Angelos autem suos se emissurum dicit, qui electos colligant, vt nos ad omnipotentiam Dei remittat. Impossibile olim videbatur Israelitis in Aegypto, vt qui per omnes fere familias dispersi erant, in vnum conuenirent & terram promissam occupa-rent. Et hodie de resurrectionis historia & ordine cogitantibus incredibile videtur, tam multos quos tyranni diuersis tormentorum generibus excruciarunt, corporibus suis restitui. At hoc faciet ei, qui primum parentem ex limo terrae condidit, & alia quoque omnia solius verbi sui virtute creauit. Facit huc Apocalypsis locus, qui non terram modo, verumetiam mare & omnes mundi partes mortuos suos reddidisse docet. Apoc. 20.
units.tr: But the condition of the godly and the elect will be far different. For of these it is said: "They will see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and glory." The greater and more illustrious this will be, the wider the consolation they will receive, and the richer the hope of reward. Nor can the sure hope of salvation be foreign to us, since it will shine upon us on that day, which will lead us into possession of the heavenly homeland. For until that day the Church will be exiled and tossed about in uncertain dwelling-places. But then Christ will gather her to himself, and will pronounce blessed those whom others, out of hatred, deem worthy of contempt and count as accursed. He says that he will send forth his angels to gather the elect, so that he may restore us to the omnipotence of God. Once it seemed impossible to the Israelites in Egypt, who were scattered through almost every family, that they should come together into one and occupy the promised land. And today, to those who think about the history and order of the resurrection, it seems incredible that so many whom tyrants tortured with various kinds of torments should be restored in their bodies. But he who first formed our parent from the clay of the earth, and created all other things by the power of his word alone, will do this. The passage of the Apocalypse also bears on this, which teaches that not only the earth but also the sea and all parts of the world gave back their dead. Rev. 20.

units.la: Caeterum quia diem illum diem restitutionis omnium & perfectae redemptionis Scripturae vocant, probe obseruari debet, quod apud Lucam Dominus addit: Cum autem haec fieri incipient, erigite & attollite capita vestra: quoniam appropinquat redemptio vestra. Est hoc certae salutis testimonium, quam nobis in aduentu suo gloriosa Christus pollicetur. Huius seculi filij non aliam beatitudinem norunt, quam quae in huius se vlli delicijs confiliit, & tunc subito euanescit, quam maxime arridere videtur. At quanta est credentium felicitas, quae totius mundi ruina paratur? Quis ergo dubitet, bona illa, quae Deus praeparauit diligentibus ipsum, omnem captum humani ingenij & sensus superare? Non pigeat ergo Euangelij doctrinam quae nobis illa in CHRISTO IESV monstrat, omnibus praeferre, quae hominibus pretiosa habentur. In hoc igitur exultent pij, quibus siue viuant, Domino viuunt, siue moriantur, Domino moriuntur. Adhoc enim CHRISTVS IESVS & mortuus est & resurrexit & reuixit, vt & mortuis & viuentibus dominetur. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, since the Scriptures call that day the day of the restoration of all things and of complete redemption, it must be carefully noted what the Lord adds in Luke: "But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near." This is a testimony of sure salvation, which Christ promises us gloriously at his coming. The children of this age know no other blessedness than that which rests on the pleasures of this world, and which then suddenly vanishes, though it seems most to smile upon them. But how great is the happiness of believers, which is being prepared amid the ruin of the whole world? Who then could doubt that those good things which God has prepared for those who love him surpass every grasp of human understanding and sense? Let us not hesitate, then, to set the doctrine of the Gospel, which shows us these things in Christ Jesus, above all things that men hold precious. In this, therefore, let the godly rejoice: whether they live, they live to the Lord, or whether they die, they die to the Lord. For to this end Christ Jesus both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and of the living. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCLXXXI.
units.tr: HOMILY 281.

units.la: A ficu autem discite parabolam: cum iam ramus eius tener est, & folia germinat, noftis prope esse aestatem: Ita & vos, cum videritis haec omnia, scitote illum prope esse & ad fores. Amen amen dico vobis, nequaquam praeterierit aetas haec vsquedum omnia ista facta sunt. Coelum & terra praeteribunt: sermones autem mei nequaquam praeteribunt. De die autem illo & hora nemo scit, ne Angeli quidem coelorum, sed Pater meus solus.
units.tr: "Learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branch is now tender and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is near. So also you, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors. Truly, I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away until all these things have happened. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away. But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father alone."

units.la: Via huius seculi studio potissimum homines a coelestium meditatione & salute aeterna abstrahuntur, no tam vtile quam necesse est, vt de consummatione mundi & nouissimo ac glorioso filij Dei IESV CHRISTI aduentu probe instrui simus: adeo vt certo nobis persuasum sit, nihil in hoc mundo stabile & perpetuum esse, & simul certa habeamus indicia, ex quibus intelligamus finem. mus finem mundi appropinquare. Est ergo digna admodum consideratu huius Cap.tractatio, in qua hucusq; multa audiuimus huc pertinentia, quibus nunc hic locus subijcitur, qui tria continet, in primis memorabilia. Quando enim de nouissimo die aut mundi consummatione sermo est, plerique hanc fore non credunt, & vel in longum tempus omnia reijciendo eludunt scurriliter quacunq; dicuntur, vel etiam indigne ferunt his finem imponi debere, in quibus plerique religionem & salutem omnem consistere arbitrantur. Idcirco apud Iudaeos periculosum fuit Hierosolymae aut templo exci- dium minitari, & hoc nomine olim Ieremiae, postea Dei Filio, Stephano item necem paratam fuisse, constat: Et Romani omnes exitio dignos putarunt, qui Romam, quam ipsi vulgo aureum & aeternam dicebant, aliquando periturum dicerent. Quis ergo credat homines qui tota a carnis sensu pendent, aequo animo ferre posse, ut aliquis totius mundi machinam corruituram, aut in nihilum redigi oportere affirmet. Quapropter in praesenti asseueratione grauem subtexit, quam simul ex rerum natura petito confirmat. Deinde ne qua mora diuturnior, quae fidem omnem huic vaticinio derogatura esse videatur, intercessura putetur, asseuerationem illam inreiurando, & comparatione partium mundi solidissimarum amplius confirmat. Praeterea curiositati medetur, qua fere homines abripiuntur, ut de futuris & nihil ad se pertinentibus folicite quaerendo interim magis necessaria negligant. Finis & vsus omnium istorum nobis hic esto, ut verbis Christi fidem habeamus, & reliquis terrenis aspiremus ad caelestia. Ad primam huius loci partem pertinet: A ficu autem discite parabolam, &c. Simile sumit ex re rum natura & arboribus ficus, quibus in illis terris nihil vulgarius & frequentius est, ut ipsos qua sti testes sistat eius, quod vulgo dicere. Id autem dicere videtur: Nemini hoc impossibile aut absurdum videri debet, cuius exempla vobis rerum natura exhibet. Aspicite salte arbores, & inter has ficus, quae aliis teneriores sunt. Nam etsi hyems aspera has extinxisse & omne vigore naturale perdidisse videatur, ut nihil ex illis sperari possit, nemo tamen adeo ineptus aut vaecors est, qui quando Vere nouo noua terrae facies redit, & arbores succu plenae parturiunt & gemmas extrudunt, non intelligat, haec certa ajlatis iam propinquae indicia esse, & his laetari incipiat. Agnoscunt enim omnes Dei decretum irreuocabile, quod est (vt Moses & Ieremias scribunt) vt quoad haec mundi machina durat, sit aestas & hyems tempore suo, tempora item sementis & messis atq; partes anni suis vicibus inter se permutentur. Atqui mundo etiam toti Deus suum Ver & aestatem destinauit, quae certis legibus sibi succedent. Itaq; nemo obstare poterit, quo minus facies mundi innouetur, quando vix aliquid huius sperari poterit. Eleganter autem praesentis & futuri seculi status parabola ista adumbratur, quae doctrinam multiplicem & dulcissimam consolationem continet. Etenim si Dei filios consideres, qui ex Dei Verbo virtute Spiritus sancti renati Deo viuunt, hyems censeri potest & vniuersum illud tempus, quod ipsis in hoc mundo transigitur. Vt enim hyems frigore, gelu, pruinis ac nimbis aspera est, terram gramine, floribus, plantis, arboresque foliorum ornatu, fructu deniq;, animalia calore, quo vegetantur & mouentur, spoliat. Itaq; piis hominibus nouae quotidie tempestates surgunt. Nam odit hos infelix mundus propter Verbi lucem. Nasci tur hinc contemptus, audiuntur conuicia & calumniae, iniuriae omnis generis ac persecutiones, quae interdum illis ipsam vitam acerbam reddunt: & vt ita fiat necesse est, vt mundi huius taedium nobis oboriatur, ne huius voluptatibus ac studijs immersi caelestia negligamus. Vt vero hyemem aestas laeta & frugifera certo sequitur, cuius praecursor est Ver, quo (vt paulo ante diximus) tota mundi facies innouatur: Ita conditioni rerum tristissimae, quae nos nunc fatigat, succedet suo tempore nouissimus dies, quo Dei Filius in nubibus caeli apparebit, & redemptione laetam atq; numeris omnibus absolutam nobis afferet. Vtq; inter hyemem & aestatem intercedit Vernum tempus, quod plerunq; varijs tempestatibus turbatur: ita quae mun di consummationem proxime praecedent tempora, afflictionum plena erunt. In quibus nos meminisse oportet, afflictiones piorum & furores impiorum gemmas atq; flores plantarum esse, quibus Dominus testatur, adesse tempus illud fatale, quod miserijs omnibus finem imponet: & quia idem fidelis est, neq; suos supra vires tentari finit, dies istos (vt supra promisit) abbreuiabit, vt aduentum suum maturet. Interim singuli priuatim sibi ista applicent, & certo sibi persuadeant nunquam defuturam consolationem pijs, quae crucem & aduersa mitiget, quibus illos in hoc mundo Deus
units.tr: The ways of this age draw people away, above all by their eagerness, from meditation on heavenly things and from eternal salvation. It is as useful as it is necessary that we be thoroughly taught about the consummation of the world and the last and glorious coming of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, so that we are persuaded that nothing in this world is stable and everlasting, and at the same time have certain signs by which we may understand that the end of the world is drawing near. This treatment of the chapter is therefore very worthy of consideration. So far we have heard much that pertains to it, and to this we now add this passage, which contains three things of note in particular. When the talk is of the last day or the consummation of the world, most people do not believe it will come, and either put it off to a distant time and mock whatever is said with buffoonery, or else take it badly that an end should be set to those things in which most people think all religion and all salvation consist. Hence it was known to be dangerous among the Jews to threaten Jerusalem or the temple with destruction; for this reason Jeremiah was once in danger, and afterwards the Son of God himself, and Stephen likewise was marked for death. And all the Romans thought worthy of destruction those who said that Rome, which they commonly called golden and eternal, would one day perish. Who then would believe that men who depend entirely on the senses of the flesh can bear with equanimity someone's assertion that the whole machinery of the world must fall or be reduced to nothing? Therefore, in the present solemn assertion he adds an oath, which he also confirms by drawing on the nature of things. Next, lest any longer delay, which seems likely to undermine all faith in this prophecy, be thought to intervene, he confirms that assertion further by the oath and by comparison with the most solid parts of the world. Moreover, he cures the curiosity by which people are usually carried away, so that while anxiously seeking about the future and things that do not concern them, they neglect what is more necessary. The aim and use of all these things for us here is that we may trust the words of Christ, and that we may aspire from earthly things to heavenly. To the first part of this passage belongs: "Learn a parable from the fig tree," etc. He takes the likeness from the nature of things and from fig trees, which in those lands are nothing more common and frequent, so that he sets before them the very witnesses of what is commonly said. He seems to say: "Nothing of this should seem impossible or absurd to anyone; nature sets before you examples of it. Look at the trees, and especially the figs, which are more tender than the others.
