Nam Herodes Magnus extincta veteri stir pe sacerdotum, viles & obscuros homines substituerat, quorum nulla erat authoritas, ne ipsius pra uis consilijs possent obsistere, quibus populi libertatem partim astute, partim violenter opprimebat. Et huius spiritu agitantur, quotquot hodie in Præsules Ecclesiasticos euehunt homines contemptos, qui neq; doctrina aut eruditione, neq; dignitate, imo ne morum quidem innocentia aliquam laudem merentur: quibus posteapro sua libidine præscribunt, & dicendi vel tacendi leges dant. Successerunt Herodi Præsides Romani, sub quibus Respublica & religio venalis fasta. Cum enim Sacerdotij administratio cum quæstu non paruo coniunca esset, illam pro vt ipsis libebat, nunc huic nunc illi conferebant, & tandem annuum sacerdotium fecerunt, vt sicuti apud Romanos Consules, ita apud Iudæos Sacerdotes quotannis noui crearentur. At quia ijdem Sacerdotium mercabantur, sacra vicissim vendebant, & templum in domum mercatus couerterant. Quod cum sine doctrina corrupta fieri non posset, hanc quoq; adulterarunt. Arguebat ipsa Christus, & cum ipse Rex simul & Sacerdos esset æternus, manus quoq; operi admouebat, vt templum a sordibus & religionem ab imposturis & mendacijs repurgaret. Hinc odium illius ordinis exarsit, quod tandem ex miraculo resuscitati Lazari vires concepit, & in vim apertam erupit: vt apud Caiaphan de illo occidendo serio consultarent. Ioan. 11.
units.tr: Among those who, moved by human counsels, killed Christ, the first to come forward are the priests with the scribes and the elders of the people, who took counsel about killing him. Yet this could seem strange and astonishing, since it was their office to bring the people to Christ. For they were the guardians of the law and of divine worship. But the goal and purpose of the law is Christ, and all worship consisted in sacrifices and external rites, all of which led to Christ. What could be more absurd, then, than that they, whose religion and whose life depended on him, should become the enemies of Christ? But religion had long since been extinguished, and the order of priests had abandoned its post. For Herod the Great, having destroyed the old stock of the priests, had put in their place base and obscure men who had no authority, so that they could not withstand his wicked counsels, by which he oppressed the liberty of the people, partly cunningly, partly by force. And by this same spirit are moved all those today who raise to ecclesiastical prelacies men who are despised, who deserve no praise either for learning or erudition, or even for innocence of character, and to whom they afterwards prescribe according to their own lust, and give laws for speaking or keeping silent. After Herod came the Roman governors, under whom the commonwealth and religion became venal. For since the administration of the priesthood was bound up with no small profit, they conferred it now on this man and now on that, as it pleased them, and at last made the priesthood annual, so that, just as among the Romans consuls were newly created each year, so among the Jews new priests were appointed each year. But because these same men bought the priesthood, they in turn sold sacred things, and had turned the temple into a market-house. Since this could not be done without corrupting doctrine, they also adulterated doctrine. Christ himself rebuked this, and since he was himself the eternal King and Priest, he also laid hands to the work, to cleanse the temple of filth and religion of impostures and lies. Hence the hatred of that order blazed up, which at last gathered strength from the miracle of the raising of Lazarus and broke out into open violence, so that they seriously consulted with Caiaphas about killing him. John 11.

units.la: Videmus in hac narratione, qui nam acerrimi veritatis hostes sint: Antistites nimirum & præsules, qui religionem sibi quæstum faciunt. Nulli enim alij Veritatis lucem minus ferre possunt. Hi olim Prophetis Dei sese opposuerunt: & de illis potissimum Apostoli admonuerunt. Et hucsa ciunt, quæ a Petro & Iuda Thaddæo scribuntur: vt eorum non meminerimus, quæ Paulus non vno loco tradit. Sed & Christus, vt nobis caueamus monet a lupis, qui pellibus ouium amiciuntur. Ne ergo offendamur, si quid simile hodie fiat. Quin potius agnoscamus bonitatem Dei, qui nos stro seculo, quando ijdem plane sunt mores præsulum, tam multos passim conuertit, qui veritatis lucem admittunt.
units.tr: We see in this narrative who are the most bitter enemies of the truth: namely the prelates and presidents who make religion a source of gain. For no others can bear the light of truth less. Such men once set themselves against the prophets of God, and the apostles warned chiefly against them. To this belong the things written by Peter and by Jude Thaddaeus, so that we need not recall what Paul hands down in more than one place. Christ too warns us to beware of wolves who are clothed in sheep's skins. Let us not, therefore, be offended if something similar happens today. Rather let us acknowledge the goodness of God, who in our age, when the manners of the prelates are exactly the same, converts so many everywhere who admit the light of truth.

units.la: Sed vt hanc causam egerint, videamus. In domo Pontificis Caiaphæ illos conuenire scribitur. Vbi cum diuersæ essent sententiæ, & fortassis plerique metu conscientiæ impediti hæsitarent, Caiaphas Pontificia authoritate turgens, cum ipsis satis pro imperio expostulat. Vos (inquit) nihil scitis. (Infantiam exprobrat ijs, quorum labia debebant custodire scientiam.) Nec cogitatis conducere nobis, ut unus homo moriatur pro populo, & non tota gens pereat. Quae verba propter sacerdotalem dignitatem, quam tunc indignus licet sustinebat Caiaphas, sic ceciderat scribit Ioannes, ut evidens vaticinium hoc fuerit de Christo, qui unus mortis suae merito genus humanum redempturus erat. Ut vero pontificis maximi aula contra Christum consultatur: ita hodie Veritas illic damnatur, ubi maxime debebat regnare: & quidem eodem praetextu: quod nimirum, nisi coluerit pax publica non posset consistere. Ne ergo calumniis temere credatur, quas praetexunt ad verfarij.
units.tr: But let us see how they pleaded this cause. It is written that they gathered in the house of the High Priest Caiaphas. When their opinions differed, and perhaps most of them hesitated, hindered by fear of conscience, Caiaphas, puffed up with pontifical authority, pressed them with considerable imperiousness, as one who commands. "You," he says, "know nothing." (He reproaches them with infancy, when their lips ought to have kept knowledge.) "Nor do you consider that it is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish." John writes that these words, because of the priestly dignity which Caiaphas, though unworthy, still held, so fell from him that this was a plain prophecy about Christ, who by the merit of his own death was to redeem the human race alone. But just as the court of the chief pontiff took counsel against Christ, so today Truth is condemned in that very place where it most ought to reign, and indeed under the same pretext: namely, that public peace could not stand unless they cherished it. Let no one therefore rashly believe the calumnies which they put forward as a pretext against their adversaries.

units.la: Est autem consolationis plenum, quod etsi magna confidentia Caiaphas hoc pronuntiet, non desunt tamen qui quam periculosum hoc sit, intelligunt. Dicunt enim: Non in festo, ne tumultus fiat in populo Suo indicio sese ut sorices produnt: quod nimirum seditionum & tumultuum ipsi autores sint. Tam facile potest Deus tyrannus, qui veritati resistunt, obicem obycere, & quantum ut ferocientes terrere, ut tunc sibi timeant, quando omnia tuta videntur. Et fere hoc metu praepo[nunt]; ut ero pauci iniquos magistratus, qui iniusta designant, ut eos timeant, quibus ipsi formidini esse debant. Interim non proficiunt in bono impij, sed conceptas pietatis scintillas excutiunt rursus, ut impietatis mensuram compleant. Oremus hodie Dominum, ut hostium suorum ferociam similiter terreat: consilia mala dissipet, & suo spiritu nos gubernet ad sui nominis gloriam, & Ecclesiae suae aedificationem.
units.tr: Yet it is full of consolation that, although Caiaphas pronounces this with great confidence, there are not lacking those who understand how dangerous it is. For they say: "Not during the feast, lest there be a tumult among the people." By their own admission they betray themselves like mice: clearly they are the very authors of sedition and tumult. God can very easily place an obstacle before tyrants who resist the truth, and by a small thing terrify the fierce, so that they fear precisely when everything seems safe. And for the most part they are held back by this fear, so that the unjust magistrates, who plan unjust things, fear those by whom they ought themselves to be feared. Meanwhile the wicked do not make progress in good, but rather they again extinguish the sparks of piety that have been kindled, so that they may fill up the measure of their impiety. Let us today pray the Lord that he may likewise terrify the fierceness of his enemies, dissipate their evil counsels, and govern us by his Spirit to the glory of his name and the edification of his Church.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXCIII.
units.tr: Homily 293.

units.la: Cum autem Iesus esset Bethaniae in domo Simonis leprosi, venerat ad eum mulier, habens alabastrum unguenti gravis pretij, & effudit super caput ipsius discumbentis. Videntes autem discipuli eius indignati sunt, dicentes: Quorsum perditio haec? Potuit enim istud unguentum venundari magno, & dari pauperibus. Cum autem hoc cognovisset Iesus, ait eis: Quid molestiam exhibetis isti mulieri? Opus enim bonum operata est in me. Semper enim pauperes habebitis vobiscum: me vero non semper habebitis. Quod enim haec unguentum hoc iniecit corpori meo, ad sepeliendum me fecit. Amen dico vobis, Ubicunque praedicatum fuerit hoc Euangelium in toto mundo, etiam quod haec fecit, dicetur ad memoriam ipsius. Tunc profectus unus ex duodecim, qui dicebatur Iudas Iscariotes, ad principes sacerdotum, ait eis: Quid vultis mihi dare, & ego eum vobis tradam? Ipsi vero appenderunt ei triginta argenteos numos. Ex eo tempore quaerebat opportunitatem, ut eum proderet.
units.tr: When Jesus was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came to him with an alabaster flask of very costly ointment, and poured it over his head as he reclined at table. But when his disciples saw it, they were indignant and said, "Why this waste? For this ointment could have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor." When Jesus perceived it, he said to them: "Why do you trouble this woman? For she has done a good work for me. For you will always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me. For in pouring this ointment on my body she has prepared me for burial. Truly I say to you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her." Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and said, "What will you give me if I hand him over to you?" And they weighed out to him thirty pieces of silver. From then on he sought an opportunity to betray him.

units.la: Inter eos, qui ex hominibus mortis IESV CHRISTI authores fuerunt, primi numerantur sacerdotes & scribae Iudaeorum, & nonnulli ex senioribus, penes quos aliqua erat politica potestas. His accessit Iudas ex priuatorum discipulorum numero, qui illum sacerdotibus prodidit. Dicitur hic unus ex duodecim, quos sibi adoptarat Dominus. Quod ideo observari debet, ut discamus nullum hominum ordinem per omnia sanctum & integrum esse, sed pauISSIM bonae fegeri filiorum Dei Satanam sua zizania aspergere. Non debent ergo bona Dei institutaa propter aliquot malos damnari. Errant in eo turpiter, qui magistratus damnant propter nonnullos, qui legum & iuris praetextu contra omne ius & fas abutuntur: qui item coniugij vsum omnè prohibent, eo quod multos suae libidinis maiorem quam honestatis rationem habere videant. At turpior est illorum error, qui totas Ecclesias damnant, in quibus aliqui admixti sunt, qui aduersus disciplinae Christianae leges aliquid desiguant. Faciunt hoc non minus iniquè quam impudenter Anabaptistae, qui hodie Donatistarum furores in Ecclesiam reducunt, dum hanc certo loco astringunt, & eam prorsus nullam esse sinunt, dum nimia cura cauent, ne qui indigniores in illa tollerentur. Admonentur autem Iudae exemplo etiam officij, ne sibi nimis placeant, qui in aliquem gradum sublimioretur. tem euestifunt. Iudam cum aliis comprehendit Christus, cum in synagoga Capernaitica diceret: Nonne ego vos duodecim elegi, & vnus ex vobis diabolus est? Non seruauit errgo Iudam, quod inter Apostolos electus fuit, quos olim Prophetae seruatores dixerunt, & qui oradoctores esse debuerunt: quo minus diabolus esset, & dux fieret iis, qui Iesum coprehenderunt. Cum enim Deus angelis qui peccauerant, non pepercit, sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis tradidit, & Iudas ex Apostolo diabolus factus sit, certe non minus necessario quam grauiter monuit D. Paulus in priori epist. ad Cor. 10. cap. Qui sibi videtur stare, videat ne cadat. In praesenti vero Caena, quam Christus Bethaniae ante postremum in vrbem ingressum habuit, mentionem facit Matthaeus, vt occasionem quae Iudam ad tam immane facinus impulit, exponat. Idcirco quedam hic ex Ioanne inferenda erunt.
units.tr: Among those who were the authors of the death of Jesus Christ, the first to be counted are the priests and scribes of the Jews, and some of the elders, who held a certain political power. To these was added Judas, one of the private disciples, who betrayed him to the priests. He is described as one of the twelve whom the Lord had chosen for himself. This ought to be noted so that we may learn that no order of men is wholly holy and sound in every respect, but that Satan, even among the children of God, sows his tares among a very few good people. Therefore the good institutions of God should not be condemned on account of a few wicked men. They err shamefully who condemn the magistracy because of some who abuse the pretext of laws and justice against all right and equity; and likewise those who forbid the use of marriage altogether, because they see that many people put their own lust before a proper regard for honour. But more disgraceful is the error of those who condemn whole churches in which some have been mixed in who act against the laws of Christian discipline. The Anabaptists do this no less unjustly than shamelessly, and today they revive the frenzy of the Donatists when they confine the Church to a certain place and allow that it is altogether nothing, while they take excessive care to prevent the more unworthy from being tolerated within it. But we are also warned by the example of Judas about office, that those who are raised to some higher rank should not be too pleased with themselves. Christ had already rebuked Judas together with the others, when in the synagogue at Capernaum he said: "Did I not choose you twelve, and yet one of you is a devil?" Therefore the fact that Judas was chosen among the apostles, whom the prophets of old called guardians and who ought to have been teachers, did not keep him from becoming a devil and leader of those who seized Jesus. For when God did not spare the angels who had sinned, but cast them down into hell and delivered them to chains of darkness, and when Judas was made a devil out of an apostle, Saint Paul gave a warning in his first epistle to the Corinthians, chapter 10, which is no less necessary than it is weighty: "Let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall." Now in the present supper, which Christ held at Bethany before his final entry into the city, Matthew makes mention of it in order to explain the occasion that drove Judas to so monstrous a deed. For this reason some things must be added here from John.

units.la: IESVS Bethaniae fuisse dicitur, quo illum sex ante pascha diebus venisse, Ioannes scribit. Qui ergo prius ob insidias Pharisaeorum secesserat, nunc instante mortis hora fatali redit, & quidem discipulis trepidantibus, vt alibi annotatur. Qui ergo ab his retrahebatur, a nemine autem cogebatur, ipse illic iuit, vt Patri obediret. Asseritur hic salutis nostrae certitudo. Nec enim po test nos negligere Dei Filius, qui pro nobis mori desiderauit. Meminerimus autem huius suo exem plo nobis praeuiisse, vt quid sub mortis horam nobis agendum sit discamus. Est haec via vniuersae terrae, terribilis quidem carni, quia peccati poena est. Sed ne eius terrori succumbamus, cogitemus horam eius nobis quoque a Deo constitutam esse, & per Christi meritum nobis factam translatam ex hac mortali vita in patriam caelestem. Ergo ipse patriae confirmati, obuiam eiprocedamus, & cum Apostolo cupiamus hinc soluere, vt cum Christo simus. Phil. 1.
units.tr: Jesus is said to have been at Bethany, to which John writes that he came six days before the Passover. He who had earlier withdrawn because of the plots of the Pharisees now returns, as the fatal hour of death draws near, even though the disciples were afraid, as is noted elsewhere. He therefore went there of his own accord, though he was held back by them and compelled by no one, so that he might obey the Father. Here the certainty of our salvation is affirmed. For the Son of God, who desired to die for us, cannot neglect us. Let us remember, however, that he went before us in his own example, so that we may learn what we ought to do at the hour of death. This is the way of all the earth, dreadful indeed to the flesh, because it is the punishment of sin. But so that we do not yield to its terror, let us think that his hour has been appointed for us too by God, and that through the merit of Christ it is made a transition for us from this mortal life to the heavenly fatherland. Therefore, being confirmed in the hope of the fatherland, let us go out to meet it, and with the Apostle let us desire to depart and be with Christ (Phil. 1).

units.la: Caeterum quid in Christi gratiam Bethanienses fecerint narratur. Vbi multa verae fidei officia concurrunt. Et enim caena illi parant in domo Simonis leprosi, qui sic dicitur quod aliquando leprosus Christi aut beneficio esset a lepra purgatus. Et videtur vir nouus vulgaris & obscurus fuisse Simon hic, cui Lazarus inter eos, qui discubuerunt numeretur, & huius soror Martha discumbentibus ministrauerit, & altera soror Maria, ne ἀτιμβόλ effet, vnguento pretioso Christi in ungere digita fit. Sunt haec amicitiae singularis indicia, & constantis fidei & gratitudinis exem plum ibi exhibent. Decet haec omnes, quos a peccato, cuius typus est lepra emundauit Dei Filius, nec quenquam eius pudere debet, quem non puduit pro nobis hominem fieri. Et praeclarum est humilitatis exemplum, quod Martha honesta & dines matrona in aliena domo non veretur ministrare ei, quem Pharisaeus & principibus sacerdotii sciebat innuisse esse. Superat tamen alios Maria, quae Dominum vnxit. Nam etsi verisimile fit hoc illam pro more gentis fecisse, tamen propter mysterium commendatur eius factum. Et vt haec pedes Christi lauit & vnxit: adhaec capillis extersit: ita nos pauperibus Christi, in quibus hic nos conuenit, charitatis officia praestemus, & quicquid nobis redundat, & capillorum inflar superfluum est, ideo nobis datum esse putemus, vt aliorum inopiam & egestatem farciat. Hic deniq; nobis praecipuus facultatum huius faculti vsus fit, vt salutiferum Euangelicae doctrinae odorem in domo domini, id est, Ecclesia excitemus. Hoc enim ille potissimum deleßatur, & multi feruantur.
units.tr: Moreover, we are told what the people of Bethany did out of regard for Christ. Here many duties of true faith come together. For they prepare a supper for him in the house of Simon the leper, who is called that because he had once been a leper and had been cleansed of his leprosy by the kindness of Christ. This Simon seems to have been an ordinary and obscure man, since Lazarus is counted among those who reclined at table, and his sister Martha served those who were reclining, while the other sister, Mary, anointed the hands of Christ with precious ointment, lest it be [ἀτιμία] dishonourable. These are signs of a special friendship, and they present an example of steadfast faith and gratitude. All whom the Son of God has cleansed from sin, of which leprosy is a type, ought to follow this, and no one should be ashamed of that Son, whom it did not shame to become man for us. Martha, an honourable and wealthy matron, also offers a notable example of humility, for in another's house she does not hesitate to serve him whom she knew the Pharisees and chief priests had marked out for death. Yet Mary surpasses the others, who anointed the Lord. For although it is likely that she did this according to the custom of her people, her deed is nonetheless commended because of its mystery. Just as she washed and anointed the feet of Christ and wiped them with her hair, so we should render the duties of charity to the poor of Christ, in whom he meets us here; and whatever overflows to us, and is superfluous like hair, let us think it has been given to us so that it may supply the want and need of others. This, finally, is the chief use we should make of the wealth of this present life: to spread the saving fragrance of the evangelical doctrine in the house of the Lord, that is, in the Church. For by this above all he is pleased, and many are saved.

units.la: Sed memorabile est, quod ex eo quod pie factum erat, & honestis rationibus poterat excusari murmurandi & calumniandi occasionem quidam arripiunt. Adeo alte nobis inhaeret alios repraehendendi cupido, vt vitiorum occasiones ex iis petamus, quae nos ad virtutes incitare debebant. Et potuit vnus murmurator Iudas conuiuium hoc sanctissimum turbare, & mulieri, cuius fidem alibi etiam Christus summis laudibus vehit, moleste exhibere. Quam sedulo igitur nos cauere oportet, ne quid temere aut inconsulta animi cupiditate faciamus praeter officium. Nec abs que Ioannes quod Matthaeus conuiuii simul omnibus tribuit, ad solum Iudam reflringit, qui anaritiae aestro percitus in haec verba erupit: Quorsum perditio haec? Adeo illum excaecauit hendi cupido, vt perditum putet, quod Christo impenditur. Interim priuatae cupiditati pauperes praetexit. Pulchre autem hic praelusum fuit, quae in terra Christi fors semper futura fit. Non desunt illi inter Bethaniae cives amici, qui sua liberalitate eum iuuant & excipiunt. Sed quae- florem habet Iudam, qui quae isti largiuntur, suffuratur & intercipit. Fit idem omnibus faculis. Sunt paucim electi, qui fide in Christum accensi, seipsos & sua omnia illi consecrant, & ne quando in verbi fui ministri aut egenis ipsi quid defit, sedulo curant. Possem hic commemorare de nationes principum, illustrium virorum, matronarum, nobilium, plebeiorum, omnium deniq; loci & ordinis hominum, qui suis facultatibus Ecclesias, Collegia, Scholas locupletarunt. Sed fere interci-pere solent aliari homines quae Ecclesia legata sunt: & hi quidem pauperes in ore habent, adhaec Ecclesiam, Diuos caelites, fraternitates, societates Mariae virginis Domini Iesu, & fi quae alia sunt huius farinae. At hoc praetextu illud vnum agunt, vt Euangelicae praedicationis fragrantiam ex Ecclesia auferant, & abfurdiffimarum superstitionum commentis animos simplicium inebriatos a Christo & vero salutis tramite abducant. Suspecti ergo sint pijs omnes qui religionis praetextu ad aucupandum diuitias abutuntur. Quamprimum enim religio diuitias parit, filia matrem deuorat.
units.tr: But it is notable that out of what was done piously, and could have been excused on honourable grounds, certain people seize an occasion for grumbling and slander. So deeply is the desire to rebuke others rooted in us that we seek occasions for vices out of things that ought to have stirred us to virtues. Judas, a single grumbler, could have disturbed this most holy banquet and caused trouble to the woman whose faith Christ praises with the highest commendation elsewhere. How carefully, therefore, we ought to guard ourselves, lest we do anything rashly or out of unconsidered greed of mind beyond our duty. Nor without reason does John restrict to Judas alone what Matthew ascribes to all the disciples together at the banquet: Judas, stirred by the heat of avarice, burst out in these words, "Why this waste?" So completely did the desire to find fault blind him that he thinks what is spent on Christ is wasted. Meanwhile he uses the poor as a cover for his private greed. Now it was beautifully foreshadowed here what would always be the case in the Christian world. There are never lacking among the people of Bethany friends who help and receive him by their generosity. But there is always a Judas who steals and intercepts what these people give. The same happens in every age. There are a few chosen people who, kindled with faith in Christ, consecrate themselves and all they have to him, and who take care that nothing is ever lacking to the ministers of the Word or to the needy. I could mention here the many princes, illustrious men, matrons, nobles and commoners, in short, people of every place and rank, who have enriched churches, colleges and schools with their means. But other men usually intercept what is bequeathed to the Church; they keep the poor on their lips, and in addition the Church, the blessed in heaven, fraternities, the societies of Mary the Virgin and of the Lord Jesus, and whatever else is of this sort. Yet under this pretext they do only one thing: they seek to remove the fragrance of evangelical preaching from the Church, and to lead away from Christ and from the true path of salvation the minds of simple people, who have been intoxicated by the inventions of most absurd superstitions. Therefore all the godly should be suspicious of those who use the pretext of religion to hunt for riches. For as soon as religion produces riches, the daughter devours the mother.

units.la: Sed bene habet fratres. Est quidem impudens iflorum hominum audacia & insatiabilis patientia: sed nunquam fallent oculos Christi, qui Iudae dolos & furta detexit, & Mariae, quae in praesenti omnium electorum personam juftinuit, suum patrocinium detulit. Indignabundus enim dicit: Quid molestiam exhibetis mulieri? Addit argumenti loco: Opus enim bonum erga me opera ta est. Et ne pauperum praetextu abuti pergeret, docet eo nequaquam nunc opus esse. Restare enim abunde amplam occasionem benefaciendi pauperibus, qui (vt Moses quoq; olim praemonuit) nunquam defuturi sint. Nunc vero aliam rem agi. Instare enim mortu horam, quam proxime jequutura fit ipsius sepultura, ad quam corpus ipsius praeparari ita oportuerit, cum propter resurrectionem ipsi nihil huius praestari queat. Nunquam ergo Dominus suis deerit. Nam gloriam quoq; & laudem perpetuam Mariae pollicetur, cum grauiaffeueratione dicens: Amen dico vobis, vbicunq; praedicatum fuerit hoc Euangelium in toto mundo, etiam quod haec fecit, dicetur ad memoriam ipsius. Et postea Iudam ex discipulorum grege exclusum, horribiliter peiffe constat, qui exitus omnes manebit, qui eius vestigijs insistunt.
units.tr: But be of good cheer, brothers. The impudence of those men is indeed shameless, and their patience is insatiable; yet they will never deceive the eyes of Christ, who laid bare the tricks and thefts of Judas, and who took Mary under his protection, since she represented in the present case the person of all the elect. For he speaks indignantly: "Why do you trouble the woman?" and, as a reason, adds: "For she has done a good work toward me." And lest they should go on abusing the pretext of the poor, he teaches that there is by no means any need for this now. For there remains an ample and abundant opportunity of doing good to the poor, who (as Moses also warned long ago) will never be lacking. But now another matter is in hand: the hour of his death is at hand, and his burial will follow shortly, for which his body ought to be prepared in this way, since nothing of this kind can be done for him on account of the resurrection. The Lord, therefore, will never be wanting to his own. For he also promises Mary glory and perpetual praise, saying with solemn assurance: "Truly I say to you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her." And afterwards it is certain that Judas, cast out from the company of the disciples, perished dreadfully; all who follow in his footsteps will share the same end.

units.la: Nam neq; istis, quae tunc dicebantur, neq; ijs quae post illi dicta sunt, motus est Iudas, sed in instituto perseuerans rectà ad principes sacerdotum contendit quibus ait: Quid vultis mihi dare? & ego eum vobis tradam. Magnae impudentiae argumentum quod fe offert ad immane, prodendi hominis ufli, facinus, & praemium non ipse sibi constituit, sed sacerdotum arbitrio permittit. Simul elucet hic quid possit auaritia, quam Paulus non fine causa radicem omnium malorum dixit. Nam cum ipsi pepigissent triginta argenteos numos fiue denarios, qui florenos Rhenanos quatuor aut bazios Germanicos circiter sexaginta conficiunt, studiose omnem eius prodendi opportunitatem seu occasionem quaesiuit. Itafolet auaritia fiue habendi cupido iudicium animi auferre, pudorem extinguere, venalia facere quaecunq; nullo auro compensari possunt. Et vt aliàs diximus, quia haec Iudae quaestio hodie regnat, nihil nobis integrum manet in vllo hominum ordine. Oremus ergo Dominum, vt caelestium bonorum desiderio animos nostros accendat, vt praecepti IESV CHRISTI memores ante omnia quaeramus regnum Dei, & tunc reliqua quibus opus est, nobis adijcientur. Matth.6.
units.tr: For Judas was moved neither by what was said then nor by what was said afterwards, but persisting in his purpose he went straight to the chief priests, to whom he said: "What will you give me? And I will hand him over to you." It is a sign of great impudence that he offered himself for that monstrous deed of betraying a man, and he did not fix the reward himself but left it to the judgment of the priests. Here at the same time it becomes clear what avarice can do, which Paul not without cause called the root of all evils. For when they had agreed on thirty silver coins, or denarii, which make about four Rhenish florins or some sixty German batzen, he eagerly sought every opportunity or occasion of betraying him. Thus avarice, or the desire of having, is wont to take away the judgment of the mind, to extinguish shame, and to make things for sale which cannot be bought with any gold. And as we have said elsewhere, because this question of Judas now reigns, nothing remains untouched in any order of men. Let us therefore pray the Lord that he may kindle our minds with desire for heavenly goods, so that, mindful of the precept of JESUS CHRIST, we may seek above all things the kingdom of God, and then the rest that we need will be added to us. Matth. 6.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXCIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CCXCIIII.

units.la: Primo autem die azymorum venerunt discipuli ad Iesum, dicentes ei: Vbi vis paremus tibi ad vescendum pascha? Ipse vero dixit: Abite in vrbem ad quendam & dicite ei, Magister dicit, tempus meum prope est, apud te faciam pascha cum discipulis meis. Et fecerunt discipuli sic vt praeceperat eis Iesus, & parauerunt pascha. Cum autem ferum diei effet, recubuit cum duodecim. Et edentibus ipsis dixit: Amen dico vobis, vnus vestrum me prodet. Tunc contristati vehementer coeperunt dicere singulì eorum ei, Num ego sum Domine? Ipse vero respondens ait: Qui intingit mecum manum catino, iste me proditurus est. Filius quidem hominis abit, sicut scriptum est de eo: væ autem homini illi, per quem Filius hominis proditur: bonum erat homini illi, si natus non fuisset. Respondens autem Iudas, qui prodebat eum, dixit: Num ego sum, rabbi? Dicit ei: Tu dixisti.
units.tr: On the first day of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus and said to him: Where do you want us to prepare the Passover for you to eat? And he said: Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, The Master says, My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples. And the disciples did as Jesus had commanded them, and they prepared the Passover. When evening had come, he sat down to eat with the twelve. And while they were eating he said: Amen I say to you, one of you will betray me. Then they were deeply grieved and each one began to say to him, Is it I, Lord? But he answered and said: He who dips his hand into the dish with me, he will betray me. The Son of man indeed goes, as it is written of him; but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! It would have been good for that man if he had never been born. Then Judas, who was betraying him, answered and said: Is it I, Rabbi? He says to him: You have said it.

units.la: Passionis & mortis IESV CHRISTI historiam Euangelistæ fere narrare incipiunt a Cœna, quam priusquam moreretur, cum discipulis in terra postremam habuit, celebrauit in ea epulum paschale, quo redemptio, cuius ipse nobis author futurus erat, olim adumbrabatur, & illo ab rogato suam Cœnam instituit, cuius mysteria tunc demum recte intelligemus, si cum veteri illa diligentius conferantur. Quia aut ritus epuli paschalis vulgo notissimus erat, & haud dubie Christus ab eo, qui inter veros & pios Dei cultores receptus erat, discedere noluit, illi non diu immorantur Euangelistæ, utpote quibus sufficit annotauisse, nihil eorum omissum fuisse a Domino, quæ illo tempore adhuc in vsu erant. Quia vero huius capitis initio Matthæus Christum discipulos loquentem introduxerat: Scitis intra duos dies paschafore, & Filium hominis tradendum ut crucifigatur: In præsenti discipulos producit, qui primo die azymorum Christum accesserint, quæ rentes vbi sibi parari velit ad vescendum pascha?
units.tr: The Evangelists begin the history of the passion and death of Jesus Christ almost with the Supper, which he held with his disciples on earth before he died as his last meal. In it he celebrated the Passover feast, by which the redemption, of which he himself was to be the author, was foreshadowed long ago; and having abrogated that feast, he instituted his own Supper. We shall understand its mysteries only if we compare them more carefully with the old rite. Since the rite of the Passover feast was very well known to the people, and Christ, who had been received among the true and pious worshippers of God, undoubtedly did not wish to depart from it, the Evangelists do not linger long on it, since it is enough for them to note that nothing of those things which were still in use at that time was omitted by the Lord. Since at the beginning of this chapter Matthew had introduced Christ speaking to the disciples: You know that after two days there is the Passover, and the Son of man will be handed over to be crucified; now he brings forward the disciples, who on the first day of unleavened bread came to Christ, asking where he wished the Passover to be prepared for him to eat.

units.la: Est hoc euidens industriæ & obedientiæ, quæ in administratione sacramentorum Deo debetur, argumentum. Nam vt alij annotarunt primus azymorum dies in decimum quartum primi mensis cadebat: & quia Christo solenne erat omnia secundum legem Patris, non secundum hominum traditiones post demum introductas facere, discipuli quæstionem hanc non putarunt differri debere, sed eo ipso die voluerunt suam operam Domino offerre, quo agnus secundum legem mactabatur, & præparabantur ea, quibus ad epulum illud opus erat. Nec abstertet ipsos tristis mortis memoria, cuius mentionem Dominus fecerat. Arguit hoc Sacramentorum contemptores, qui tunc demum se vere pios & religiosos esse arbitrantur, si Dei instituta prophano contemptu negligant. Abutuntur illi locis, qui salutem & quæcunque ad hanc pertinent, ita vni Deo & huius gratia tribuunt, vt nobis nihil relinquant. Etenim Christi dictum est: Nemo venit ad me, nisi Pater meus traxerit eum. Item, Omnia mihi tradita sunt a Patre meo: & nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, neque Patrem quisquam novit nisi Filius, & cuicunque voluerit Filius retegere. Quibus consentiunt Apostolica illa: Non est volentis aut currentis, sed miserentis Dei, ad Romanos nono Capite. Nihil est qui plantat, neque qui rigat: sed Deus qui dat incrementum. Cæterum is qui plantat & is qui rigat vnum sunt, &c. Quibus addunt, Fidem donum Dei esse. Quod autem inde colligunt, prædicationem verbi non esse necessariam, & Sacramentorum vsum inutilem, non minus impium quam falsum est. Deus enim cui omnis gloria debetur, & qui solus agit in cordibus hominum, Verbo & sacramentis vtitur, & ideo Paulus itidem dicebat, Romanos decimo. Fides ex auditu est, auditus autem per Verbum Dei. Et Christus similiter duo hæc coniungit, dicens: Amen dico vobis, qui audit verba mea & credit ei qui misit me habet vitam æternam & in iudicium non venit. Et hunc ordinem ab origine rerum obseruauit Deus, nec ab eo recessit Dei Filius IESVS CHRISTVS, cum homine assumpto in mundum veniret. Nam octauo a partu die secundum legem circumcisus est, & postea ab Ioanne Baptista quoque baptizari voluit, vt omnem iustitiam impleret: festa item diligenter coluit, & nunc morituris maturat epuli paschalis adornationem, ne quid prorsus eorum omittat, quæ tunc in vsu erant. Atqui ipsi illius non opus erat, cum ipse noster pascha sit, noster circumcisio, & omnium quæ tunc adumbrabantur, complementum. Nam pascha noster pro nobis immolatus est Christus. Cur ergo nos superuacaneum putemus, quod Dei Filius negligere noluit? Agnoscamus potius a Deo institutum ordinem, & ne quid ex nostro arbitrio mutemus. Qui enim olim testatus est, frustra se coli hominum traditionibus aut figmentis, ne hodie quidem aliquid probabit, quod absque verbi sui authoritate fiet, Isaiæ 29. cap. Matth. 15. Quod Paulus obseruans, negabat Corinthios Cœnam Domini manducare, cum eam alio ritu & ordine administrarent, quam a Christo esset tradita.
units.tr: This is clear evidence of the diligence and obedience that are owed to God in the administration of the sacraments. For, as others have observed, the first day of unleavened bread fell on the fourteenth day of the first month; and since it was customary for Christ to do all things according to the law of the Father, and not according to the traditions of men introduced later, the disciples did not think this question should be postponed, but wished on that very day to offer their service to the Lord, on which the lamb was slaughtered according to the law and the things needed for that feast were being prepared. Nor did the sad memory of death, which the Lord had mentioned, deter them. This refutes the despisers of the sacraments, who think they are truly pious and religious only if they neglect God's ordinances with profane contempt. They abuse those passages which ascribe salvation and all that pertains to it so entirely to God alone and to his grace that they leave nothing to us. For Christ said: No one comes to me unless my Father draws him. Likewise: All things have been delivered to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him. The apostolic words agree with these: It is not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy (Romans, chapter nine). Neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase. Moreover, he who plants and he who waters are one, etc. To these they add that faith is the gift of God. But what they infer from this, that the preaching of the Word is not necessary and the use of the sacraments is useless, is no less impious than it is false. For God, to whom all glory is due, and who alone works in the hearts of men, uses the Word and the sacraments; and so Paul likewise said (Romans, chapter ten): Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the Word of God. And Christ similarly joins these two, saying: Amen I say to you, he who hears my words and believes him who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment. God has observed this order from the beginning of things, nor did the Son of God, Jesus Christ, depart from it when he came into the world with an assumed humanity. For on the eighth day after his birth he was circumcised according to the law, and afterwards he also willed to be baptized by John the Baptist, that he might fulfil all righteousness. Likewise he diligently observed the festivals, and now, about to die, he hastens the preparation of the Passover feast, lest he omit anything at all of those things which were then in use. Yet he had no need of them, since he himself is our Passover, our circumcision, and the fulfilment of all those things which were then foreshadowed. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed for us. Why, then, should we consider superfluous what the Son of God was unwilling to neglect? Let us rather acknowledge the order instituted by God, and let us change nothing by our own judgment. For he who long ago testified that he was worshipped in vain with the traditions or inventions of men (Isaiah, chapter 29; Matthew 15) will not approve today anything that is done without the authority of his Word. Paul observed this and denied that the Corinthians ate the Lord's Supper when they administered it with a rite and order other than that which had been delivered by Christ.

units.la: Respondet autem discipulis de paschali epulo quærentibus & locum, vbi illud pararent, monstrat. Abite in vrbem (inquit) ad quendam. Designat certum quempiam, cuius tamen nomen monstrat mirabile culose. nomen neq; domum expreßit, sed miraculo certo ostendit, vbi habitet: dum ipsis occursurum ait quendam qui hydriam aquæ gestet quem sequi, & illuc diuertere debeant, vbi ille ingrediatur, & eius loci patremfamilias compellare. Vbi multa diminutatis argumenta concurrunt, quæ scanda- lis medentur, quæ fidem nostram labefactare possunt, dum videmus quàm multa indigne & iniquè pajjus sit Christus. Nam procul absens ab vrbe videt quid in illa fiat, quidq; discipulis hanc in- gressus euenturum sit. Nec videt modo, verumetiam agit in cordibus hominum. Ita vero docet, se qui moxsit in crucem infamem suffigendus nihil latere, & qui tam facile sibi hospitium parare potuit, facile etiam tam dirum supplicium declinare potuisse, nisi vltro voluisset se pro nobis in mortem tradere.
units.tr: Now he answers the disciples, who ask both about the Passover feast and where they should prepare it, and points them out. Go into the city, he says, to a certain man. He designates a particular person, yet he points him out in a wonderful way. He does not express his name or his house, but by a clear sign he shows where he lives, saying that a man carrying a pitcher of water would meet them, whom they should follow, and that they should turn aside to the place where he entered, and address the master of that house. Here many arguments come together that heal scandals and that can shake our faith, when we see how many unworthy and unjust things Christ suffered. For, though far away from the city, he sees what is happening there, and what will befall the disciples when they enter it. He not only sees but also acts in the hearts of men. And so he teaches that he, who was soon to be fixed to the infamous cross, was hidden from nothing; and that he who could so easily prepare a lodging for himself could also easily have avoided so cruel a punishment, unless he had willingly handed himself over to death for us.

units.la: Hinc vero nobis consolatio vniuersalis petenda est, ne dubitemus, Filium Dei IESVM CHRISTVM nos nouisse & videre, etiamsi procul ab illo in terris hisce peregrinemur, ipse autem in cœlis ad dexteram Patris sedeat. Qui enim mortali adhuc corpore amicus Centurionis famulum & aulici regij filium sanare potuit, multo magis nobis adesse videatur. Nec in nobis modo, verumetiam illis agit, quibus cum nobis res est, vt eorum mentes inclinare, & vt nobis serui re velint moueat. Imò ex inimicis amicos reddere & nobis conciliare potest. Ita olim in Canaanæorum mentibus tonabat: Nolite tangere Vnctos meos. Quam vocem hodie adhuc sonare in multorum cordibus, non est dubium, qui cum Christum oderint, non audent tamen eius seruos affligere aut ladere vt vellent.
units.tr: From this we must draw a universal consolation, so that we do not doubt that the Son of God, Jesus Christ, knows and sees us, even though we are pilgrims in this earth far away from him, while he himself sits in heaven at the right hand of the Father. For he who, while still in mortal body, could heal the servant of the centurion and the son of the royal official, surely is present to us much more. And he acts not only in us but also on those with whom we have to do, to incline their minds and move them to wish us well. Indeed, he can turn enemies into friends and reconcile them to us. Thus long ago he thundered in the minds of the Canaanites: Do not touch my anointed ones. That this voice still sounds today in the hearts of many is not doubtful, for although they hate Christ, they do not dare to afflict or harm his servants as they would wish.

units.la: Præterea officij nos ista admonent, ne vnquam nobis excidat, nos in illius consessu versari qui in quouis opere occupatos videt, & vel punit, si quid præter officium faciamus, vel defendit & tuetur sibi seruientes. Nec actiones solum nostras videt, verumetiam quo animo omnia fiant, & ideo facile ipsi est calumniatorum iudicia confutare, quibus illi nobis molestiam exhibent. Hæc ergo sibi ipsis applicent omnis loci & ordinis homines, qui iniquis hominum improborum iudicijs grauiter offenduntur. Imitemur autem discipulos istos, qui etsi multa obijcere poterant, simpliciter obediunt Domino: hospitem item hunc, cui cum incommodum & periculosum videri posset, Christo locum dare domi suæ, tamen huic morem gerit. Ut vero vtrisq; bene hoc cesserit, ita qui Christum semel receperunt, si in eo retinendo fortes & alacres sint, illum fidelem remuneratorem & defensorem inuenient.
units.tr: Moreover, these things remind us of our duty, so that it never slips from our minds that we live in the presence of him who sees us occupied in any work, and either punishes us if we do anything beyond our duty, or defends and protects those who serve him. He sees not only our actions but also with what intention everything is done; and therefore it is easy for him to refute the judgments of slanderers, by which they cause us trouble. Let all men of every place and rank, who are grievously offended by the unjust judgments of wicked men, apply these things to themselves. Let us imitate those disciples, who, although they could raise many objections, simply obey the Lord; likewise this host, who, though it might seem inconvenient and dangerous to give Christ a place in his house, nevertheless complies with him. And just as this went well for both of them, so those who have once received Christ, if they are strong and eager to hold on to him, will find him a faithful rewarder and defender.

units.la: At noluit Dominus discipulorum opera & ministerio frustra abuti, sed cum ferum diei esset, venit cum duodecim & recubuit: & postquam peracto epulo pascha illud abrogauit, vt Lucas scribit, cum Iuda actionem instituit, quæ diligentem considerationem meretur. Docemur enim hoc exemplo quid hodie fieri debeat, si quando in Ecclesiam & ad sacramentorum communionem irrepunt hypocritæ aut palam scelerati: ne vel indulgentia nimia peccemus, vel rigore aut seueritate immodica infirmiores abstreamus.
units.tr: But the Lord did not want to make use of his disciples' labour and ministry in vain. When it was late in the day, he came with the twelve and reclined at table. After the meal was finished, he set aside that Passover, as Luke writes, and instituted an action with Judas, which deserves careful consideration. For by this example we are taught what ought to be done today if hypocrites or openly wicked people creep into the Church and into the communion of the sacraments: we must neither sin through excessive indulgence nor drive away the weaker brethren by harshness or immoderate severity.

units.la: Enimuero Christus cum Iuda actionem eiusmodi instituit, vt nec connueat ad eius scelus, neque infamem reddere velit, sed eius saluti & honori consultum cupiat. Nam primum in genere facinus, quod iam animo conceperat, & magna ex parte designarat, arguit, dicens: Amè dico vobis, vnus vestrum me prodet. Et hoc quidem non sine tristi mentis perturbatione illum dixisse, Ioannes testatur. Mouit illum Iudæ perditio: & suo exemplo præceptum de diligendis inimicis exponit. Nam quia impunitatis spe multi pergunt peccando, arguit proditionis scelus, vt se non latere intelligat Iudas, & tamen eius nomini parcatur. Deinde quia sciebat ipsum non moueri, propius illum ferit, addens: Qui intingit mecum manum catino, ipse me proditurus est: Quo dicto scelus amplificat. Graue & horrendum est prodere innocentem. Grauius autem hominem notum & familiarem vel domesticum & commensalem. Etenim gentibus quoq; nefas visum est mensam & salem transgredi. Huic vero sceleri pondus accessit, quod epulum sacrum violauit Iudas, & ita in Deum quoq; perfidus factus est. Voluit autem Dominus in seipso experiri, quod alibi suis discipulis euenturum denuntiat, fore vt domesticos suos inimicos sensurifint. Caterum ne his quidem flecti aut frangi Iudam sciebat: Quapropter excusatione quoq; aufert, quam sub prouidentia Dei prætextu fere impij venantur & pœnam illi horribilem minatur. Filius quidem hominis abit, sicut scriptum est de eo: Væ autem homini illi, per quem Filius hominis proditur. Et ne in hoc so- lum secu-
units.tr: Indeed Christ instituted such an action with Judas, so that he neither connived at his crime nor wished to make him infamous, but desired to care for his salvation and his honour. First he rebukes the crime in general, which Judas had already conceived in his mind and had largely planned, saying: "Truly I say to you, one of you will betray me." John testifies that he said this not without a sad disturbance of mind. The ruin of Judas moved him, and by his own example he sets out the command to love one's enemies. For since many keep on sinning in the hope of impunity, he rebukes the crime of betrayal, so that Judas understands that he is not hidden, and yet his name is spared. Then, because he knew that Judas was not moved, he strikes him more closely, adding: "He who dips his hand with me in the dish, he will betray me." By these words he magnifies the crime. It is grave and dreadful to betray an innocent man; more grave still to betray a known and familiar man, a household companion and table-fellow. Indeed even the Gentiles thought it wicked to break bread and salt. To this crime was added a further weight, that Judas violated the sacred feast, and so became faithless also toward God. The Lord wished to experience in himself what he announces elsewhere will happen to his disciples, that they will find their own household to be their enemies. But he knew that Judas would not be bent or broken even by this. Therefore he also removes the excuse which wicked men commonly hunt under the pretext of God's providence, and he threatens him with a dreadful punishment: "The Son of Man indeed goes away, as it is written of him: But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed." And so that he should not think that punishments are prepared for himself only in this world, he adds:

units.la: Matth.26. ūm seculo pœnas sibi parratas putet, addit: Bonum erat homini illi, si natus non fuisset. Ex eo enim colligi potest in futuro quoq; seculo pœnas daturu n esse, quæ ad animam quoq; redundent. Non debet ergo infelix sibi ipsi delitias facere, quòd omnia prouidentiæ Dei decreto gubernentur. Eo enim non excusantur scelera, cùm Deus voluntatem suam abundè manifestarit, quòd non sit Deus, qui probetur iniquitas aut cum quo habitet malitia. Quapropter etsi nihil mihi accidat, quàm quodex æterno Patris decreto fiet, non tamen impune id feret, qui tantum facinus designabit. Nam hunc sua quoq; maledictio manebit, & ultio Dei persequetur eum. At quia Iudas his quoq; nonemolliretur, sed contumacior & impudentior factus, interrogaret, Num ego sum? aperte & diserte illi Christus respondet: Tu dixisti, id est, vt dicas ita se res habet, & reuera proditor ille es. Etiam in lucem protrahi iustum erat sceleratum, qui non poterat diutius latere, cùm plus quàm camina impudentia seipsum manifestaret. Et sic agere oportet cum incurabilibus & pœnitere nesciis. Errant ergo vehementer qui neminem volunt arguí, & quidem minimè omnium eos, qui in dignitate aliqua sunt constituti. Atqui non debet vnus hominis dignitas multorum saluti præferri. Sed & charitatis lex publicam salutem multorum priuato honori iubet anteponere.
units.tr: Matth. 26. he thinks punishments are prepared for himself in this world; he adds: "It would have been good for that man if he had not been born." For from this it can be gathered that he will also pay penalties in the future age, which reach even to the soul. The unhappy man ought not, therefore, to flatter himself that all things are governed by the decree of God's providence. For crimes are not excused by this, since God has abundantly made his will known, and he is not a God in whom iniquity is approved, nor with whom wickedness dwells. Therefore, even if nothing befalls me except what will happen by the eternal decree of the Father, nevertheless he who plans so great a crime will not bear it with impunity. For his own curse will remain upon him, and the vengeance of God will pursue him. But because Judas was not softened even by these words, but, made more obstinate and shameless, asked, "Is it I?", Christ answers him plainly and clearly: "You have said it," that is, "So it is, as you say, and you are indeed that betrayer." It was also right that the wicked man, who could no longer lie hidden, should be dragged into the light, since he revealed himself more than brazen impudence. And this is how one ought to deal with the incurable, who know not how to repent. Those therefore err greatly who wish that no one be rebuked, and least of all those who have been placed in some dignity. Yet the dignity of one man ought not to be preferred to the salvation of many. Indeed the law of charity also commands that the public salvation of many be put before the private honour of one.

units.la: Quid vero reliqui discipuli fecerint, non oscitanter obseruari debet. Ad primam tanti sceleris mentionem contristati cœperunt singuli quærere, num ipsi sint de quo agebatur. Eadem meretur quòd contristantur tanti sceleris mentione, & suo exemplo nostri seculi saporem arguunt, quibus non multa in cordi est, si quotidie multa fiunt contra Christum. In eo autem isti omnes peccant, quòd alij alios intuentur, nemo autem illorum in seipsum descendit, vt seipsum exploret & de suiipsius emendatione cogitet. Ita solet fieri si quando scelera in genere accusantur, quæ fere causa est, quòd pauciores ex concionibus publicis meliores redeunt. Dum enim in alijs quærunt, quod in ipsis emen dari debebat, ipsi in eodem luto subinde hærent & sibi ipsis blanduntur.
units.tr: Nor should we carelessly observe what the remaining disciples did. At the first mention of so great a crime, they each began to be saddened and to ask whether they themselves were the one of whom he was speaking. Their sorrow at the mention of so great a crime deserves the same praise, and by their example they show a taste for our own age, in which little is cared for in the heart, though many things are done every day against Christ. Yet all of them sinned in this, that they looked at one another, but none of them descended into himself, to examine himself and to think about his own amendment. So it usually happens when wicked deeds are accused in general; this is the reason why fewer people return from public sermons better. For while they seek in others what ought to be amended in themselves, they cling again and again to the same mire and flatter themselves.

units.la: Admonet vero nos Iude exemplū de impudenti & immani hypocritarū audacia. Diu ille fur fuerat, & peculator sius sacrilegus; sed latere potuit, vt nemo talem esse potuerit deprehendere. So let hoc frequenter fieri, & id multos vehementer offendit, & audaciores plerunque fiunt hypocritæ, dum successu aliquo in dolis suis vtuntur. Sed temporaria est lætitia hypocritæ, & spes eius peribit. Qui seruari volunt veritati studeant, & Deū ex corde precentur, vt impostores improbos arguat, suos autem in luce sua dirigat ad sui nominis gloriam & Ecclesiæ suæ ædificationem. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover the example of Judas warns us of the shameless and monstrous audacity of hypocrites. For a long time he had been a thief, and a sacrilegious embezzler of funds; yet he was able to remain hidden, so that no one could detect that he was such a man. This often happens, and it greatly offends many, and hypocrites for the most part become bolder while they use their deceits with some success. But the joy of the hypocrite is temporary, and his hope will perish. Those who wish to be saved should strive for the truth and pray to God from the heart that he will expose wicked impostors, and direct his own people in his light, to the glory of his name and the building up of his Church. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXCV.
units.tr: HOMILY CCXCV.

units.la: Edentibus autem eis, accepit Iesus panem: & cùm benedixisset, fregit, deditq; discipulis, & ait: Accipite, comedite: hoc est corpus meum. Et accepto poculo, ac gratias actis dedit eis, dicens: Bibite ex hoc omnes. Hoc est enim sanguis meus noui Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Dico autem vobis: Non bibam ab hoc tempore ex hoc fructu vitis, vsque ad diem illum, cùm ipsum bibam vobiscũ nouum in regno Patris mei. Et cùm hymnum cecinîssent, exierunt in montem olearum.
units.tr: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it, he broke it, gave it to the disciples, and said: "Take, eat; this is my body." And when he had taken the cup and given thanks, he gave it to them, saying: "Drink from it, all of you. For this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. But I tell you, I will not drink again from this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom." And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

units.la: Quamuis Deo, qui Spiritus est, nullis externis aut corporalibus exercitijs siue ritibus opus sit, propter nos tamen qui externis ducimur, & infirmi sumus, ac variè tentamur, iam in ab exordio rerum aliquas ceremonias & ritus tradidit, quibus salutis promissiones de Christo obsignauit, vt fidem in nobis excitaret & confirmaret, simulq; homines sibi obstringeret & de officio admoneret. Et veteres quidè quia venturum Seruatorem expectarunt, plura habuerunt quæ redemptionē ipsis adumbrabant, quo minus de illa dubitarent. At Dei Filius IESVS CHRISTVS, etsi reipsa implere & præstare vellet, quod multifariam promissum & præsiguratum fuit, doctrinæ tamen rationem & modum, quo olim vsus fuerat, non mutauit, sed nouum illud fœdus, cuius ipse sponsor & executor venerat, nouis mysterijs sanciuit, quæ aspectu & vsu iucundiora & significatione propius in rem quasi præsentem deducerent. Inter hæc vsitatissima est Cœna Domini, quam in memoriam mortis suæ instituit, & vniuersum nostræ redemptionis mysterium ita nobis ob oculos statuit, vt de omnibus admoneat, quæ nobis cognita & obseruatu sunt necessaria. Quod autem de χιτανίς bona segeti aspersis in Euangelio Christus admonet, circa Cænam præcipue factum est. Quam enim ipse in memoriam sacrificij, quo seipsum pro nobis obtulit, instituit, alii in sacrificium commutarunt, quo omne mortis eius meritum euacuatur. Alij quod societatis Christianæ vinculum esse debebat, contentionis pomum fecerunt: multi dum sub huius prætextu excommunicationem vrgent, conscientiarum carnificinam instituunt ex eo, quo illi in falsa tefua confirmari debebant. Idcirco nos in præsenti rem ipsam propius inspiciemus, & vt hæc nobis rectius & melius pateat, primo videbimus, quid illud sit quod Christus discipulis, & in his Ecclesiæ suæ dedit. Deinde quo ritu & modo id instituerit. Postremo quod nostrum sit in hoc Sacramento vsurpando officium.
units.tr: Although God, who is Spirit, has no need of any external or bodily exercises or rites, yet for our sake, who are led by external things, who are weak and variously tempted, he has from the beginning of the world handed down certain ceremonies and rites, by which he sealed the promises of salvation concerning Christ, in order to kindle and strengthen faith in us, and at the same time to bind men to himself and remind them of their duty. The ancients, indeed, because they awaited the coming Saviour, had many things that foreshadowed redemption for them, so that they would doubt it less. But the Son of God, Jesus Christ, although he wished to fulfil in fact what had been promised and prefigured in many ways, did not change the manner and method of teaching that he had used before. Rather, he confirmed that new covenant, of which he had come as surety and executor, with new mysteries, which by their appearance and use are more pleasing and, by their meaning, bring the thing itself more nearly before us, as if present. Among these the most common is the Lord's Supper, which he instituted in memory of his death, and so set before our eyes the whole mystery of our redemption that it reminds us of all things that are necessary for us to know and observe. What Christ admonishes in the Gospel concerning the tares sown among the good seed was done especially with regard to the Supper. For others have turned into a sacrifice what he instituted in memory of the sacrifice by which he offered himself for us, and so the whole merit of his death is annulled. Others have made into an apple of discord what ought to have been the bond of Christian fellowship; many, while they press excommunication under this pretext, set up a torture of consciences from that which should have confirmed them in the true faith. Therefore, in the present discussion we will look more closely at the thing itself, and so that these matters may be clearer and better understood, we will first see what that is which Christ gave to his disciples, and in them to his Church. Then, with what rite and manner he instituted it. Lastly, what our duty is in using this Sacrament.

units.la: Quoad primum in Ecclesia Cœnæ nomen receptum est, & Paulus Dominicam dixit, vt a vulgari aut a prophana distingueret. Mansit autem Cœnæ vocabulum, licet matutino tempore sub auroram fere celebretur, quia hanc Dominus vesperi instituit, cum epulum pascale, quod inter vesperas sumebatur, cum discipulis comedisset. Ne vero vulgarem Cœnam putemus, verba Christi, quibus in eius institutione vtitur, & cum verbis actionis quoq; diligentius obseruari debent. Primo panem accepit IESVS, & gratijs actis, sive cum benedixit, fregit etiam. Benedicendi autem vocabulo aut gratiarum actione consecrationem intelligi constat, qua panis communis aut vulgaris in sacrum mutatus est, vt mysterio seruiret. Id vero nos admonet, quam reuerenter ad hanc mensam accedere debeamus, & quam serio de eo nos cogitare oporteat, vt pro his donis nos satis gratos præbeamus. Deinde fregit panem, quod mortificationis symbolum fuit, sine qua Christus pro nobis impendi non poterat. Ideo de morte sua loquitur, quoties se pro nobis traditum dicit: & nos non possumus vicissim ipsi impendere, nisi affectus carnis mortificemus, vt ipsi viuamus. Tertio panem fractum dedit discipulis, dicens: Accipite, comedite, hoc est corpus meum. Et apud Lucam addit: Quod pro vobis datur: hoc facite in mei recordationem. De poculo autem dicit Dominus: Bibite ex eo omnes. Hoc est sanguis meus noui Testamenti, id est, ut quo novum Testamentum, quod olim promissum fuit, sancitur. Addit autem expositionis loco: Qui effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Quia enim sedum Dei & Testamentum vetus per peccatum irritum factum fuit, non aliter instaurari potuit, quam sanguine, qui peccatorum remissionem impetraret, & sempiternam iustitiam reduceret, vt olim Daniel Propheta prædixerat. Daniel 9. Cap.
units.tr: As to the first point, the name "Supper" has been received in the Church, and Paul called it "the Lord's," to distinguish it from a common or profane meal. The word "Supper" has remained, although it is celebrated in the morning, about dawn, because the Lord instituted it in the evening, after he had eaten the Passover meal with his disciples, which was taken between the evenings. Lest we think it an ordinary supper, the words of Christ, by which he uses them in its institution, must be observed carefully, together with the words of his action. First, Jesus took bread, and, having given thanks, or, as it were, when he had blessed it, he also broke it. Now it is agreed that by the word "blessing," or by the giving of thanks, is understood the consecration by which ordinary or common bread was changed into a holy thing, to serve a mystery. This indeed admonishes us how reverently we ought to approach this table, and how seriously we ought to think about it, so that we may show ourselves sufficiently thankful for these gifts. Next he broke the bread, which was a symbol of mortification, without which Christ could not be given up for us. Therefore he speaks of his death whenever he says that he was delivered up for us; and we cannot in turn give ourselves up, unless we mortify the desires of the flesh, so that we may live for him. Thirdly, having broken the bread, he gave it to the disciples, saying: "Take, eat; this is my body." And in Luke he adds: "which is given for you; do this in remembrance of me." Concerning the cup the Lord says: "Drink from it, all of you. This is the blood of my new covenant," that is, the new covenant, which was promised long ago, is ratified by it. He adds, by way of explanation: "which is poured out for the forgiveness of sins." For since the covenant of God and the old Testament were made void through sin, it could not be restored except by blood, which would obtain the remission of sins and bring back everlasting righteousness, as the prophet Daniel had foretold long ago. Daniel 9.

units.la: Ex his autem colligi potest definitio Cœnæ, vt dicamus esse actionem sacram, in qua ex Christi mandato panem & vinum inter nos distribuimus in memoriam mortis suæ, qua ille nouum Testamentum impleuit, vt hæredes regni Dei faceret. Etenim redemptio nostra ab antiquo sub Testamenti forma comprehensa fuit, vt Deum nobis Patrem, & nos illi filiorum loco esse sciremus: & hinc nobis certa & indubitata esset salutis fiducia. Ideo in Lege Moses populum sanguine aspergens docebat: En sanguis Testamenti, quod pepigit Dominus vobiscum super cunctis hisce sermonibus. At quia Iudæi non perstiterunt in fædere, vel Testamento, quod Deus cum Patribus illorum fecerat, nouum promisit Deus, & ideo abdicatis veteris Testamenti ritibus nouum successit. Non rata autem sunt testamenta, nisi mors testatoris interueniat: At Deum mori impossibile est. Id vero in assumpta carne præstitit æternus Dei Filius, vt rata fieret Testamenti noui promissio. De hoc igitur mysterio debet intelligi, quod in præsenti Christus noui Testamenti mentionem fecit. Ita enim voluit dicere: Scitis qua fuerit hominum conditio. Omnes peccauerant, & deficiebantur gloria Dei, vt omnibus precandum esset: Ne introeas in iudicium cum seruis tuis Domine: Si peccata obseruer Domine, quis subsistet? Deplorata ergo res fuit, nec aliqua salutis spes erat, quam quæ in noui Testamenti promissione affulgebat. Sed dilata hucusque res fuit, & multi iusti & Prophetæ cupierunt videre quæ vos videtis, nec viderunt. Nunc autem venit dies ille optatus, quem & ego tandem illucescere desideraui, vt hoc epulum vobiscum edertem, & vobis sancirem lætam redemptionis vestræ memoriam. Præstabo enim nunc quod promisi, dum carnem meam dabo pro mundi vita, & sanguinem meum in remissionem peccatorum vestrorum effundam. Et ne quid dubitetis, En accipite haec sacratissima mei corporis & sanguinis Symbola. En hic panis corpus meum est, quod pro vobis traditum vos pascet & alet ad vitam aeternam. En hoc poculo vobis propinatur sanguis ille Noui Testamenti, qui pro peccatis vestris effusus fi-tim animarum reflinguet, & laetitia sempiterna exhilarabit. Quod ergo nunc facitis, in posterum quoq; facite: Quoties autem feceritis, semper mei recordemini, nec dubitate, me corpus & sanguinem pro vobis tradidisse, vt vos redemptos seruem & alam in aeternum.
units.tr: From these things a definition of the Supper can be drawn, so that we may say it is a sacred action, in which, by Christ's command, we distribute bread and wine among ourselves in memory of his death, by which he fulfilled the new covenant, so as to make us heirs of the kingdom of God. For our redemption was comprehended from of old under the form of a covenant, so that we might know God as our Father and ourselves as in the place of his children; and from this a certain and undoubted confidence of salvation would be ours. Therefore, in the Law, Moses, sprinkling the people with blood, taught: "Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord has made with you concerning all these words." But because the Jews did not persist in the covenant or testament that God had made with their fathers, God promised a new one, and therefore, the rites of the old Testament having been abrogated, the new succeeded. Now testaments are not valid unless the death of the testator intervenes; but it is impossible for God to die. This, however, the eternal Son of God accomplished by taking on flesh, so that the promise of the new Testament might be made valid. It is of this mystery, therefore, that Christ's mention of the new Testament in the present passage must be understood. For he meant to say: "You know what the condition of men was. All had sinned and were lacking the glory of God, so that all must pray: 'Enter not into judgement with your servants, O Lord'; 'If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, who could stand?'" The matter was therefore desperate, and there was no hope of salvation except that which shone forth in the promise of the new Testament. But the matter had been delayed up to now, and many righteous men and prophets desired to see what you see, and did not see it. But now that longed-for day has come, which I too have desired to dawn, so that I might eat this feast with you and seal for you the joyful memory of your redemption. For now I will do what I promised, while I give my flesh for the life of the world, and pour out my blood for the forgiveness of your sins. And so that you may have no doubt, behold, take these most holy symbols of my body and blood. Behold, this bread is my body, which, given up for you, will feed and nourish you to eternal life. Behold, this blood of the new Testament is offered to you in this cup, which, poured out for your sins, will quench the thirst of souls and gladden them with everlasting joy. Therefore, what you now do, do also in the future; and as often as you have done it, always remember me, and do not doubt that I have given up my body and blood for you, so that I may keep and nourish you, redeemed, for ever.

units.la: Hic ergo probe obseruari debet, Dominum sic de pane & vino loqui, vt discipulos ab his ad suum corpus & sanguinem renocet: nec simpliciter aut obiter corporis, sed corporis pro nobis tra-diti aut fracti, & sanguinis pro peccatis nostris effusi meminisse. Quia nisi illud pro nobis in mortem traditum, & hoc pro peccatis nostris effusum esset, ori ingesta & faucibus deglutita nihil prosuissent. Nam aduersus eos, qui his opinionibus crassis Capernaitarum more detinentur, perpetuo ratum erit Christi dictum, Ioannis sexto: Spiritus est qui viuificat, caro non prodest quicquam. Obseruetur ergo hoc propter eos, qui Symbolis panis & vini inhaerent, & in his vel transsubstantiationem vel confubstantiationem somniant, vt illa aut pro nobis offerri, aut oraliter (vt ipsi loquuntur) manducari & in fauces demergi asserant. Christus enim qui mensae assidebat corpore suo, quod ex Maria Virgine natum fuit, de pane & vino, quae manu tenebat & discipulis porrigebat, dixit: Hoc est corpus meum, Hic est sanguis meus, &c. & (vt paulo ante diximus) de corpore in mortem tradendo, & de sanguine pro peccatis nostris effundendo loquutus est. At quia neutrum tunc factum fuit, cum ista diceret, certe neq; panis ille corpus, neq; poculum istud eius sanguis esse potuit: nisi aut Christum bicorporem dicere libeat, aut discipulos non idem nobiscum corpus Domini comedisse sentiamus: Quibus addi debet, quod in praesenti non alium Coenae vsum & finem tradit, quam quod ista facere iubet in sui recordationem: quod Apostolus 1. Cor. 11. adhunc modum interpretatur: Quotiescunq; editis hunc panem, & poculum hoc bibitis, mortem Domini annunciatis, donec veniat. Ita quoad Christum finis Coenae praecipuus est, quod redemptionis nostrae beneficium nobis obsignat, & salutis certos reddit, deniq; se totum nobis obstringit. Et ideo hoc ritu vti voluit, qui tanto & tam multiplici mysterio seruiret.
units.tr: Here, therefore, it must be carefully observed that the Lord speaks of bread and wine in such a way as to call the disciples from these to his own body and blood; and he speaks not simply or in passing of the body, but of the body delivered or broken for us, and of the blood poured out for our sins. For unless that had been given to death for us, and this poured out for our sins, what was put into the mouth and swallowed down the throat would have profited nothing. For against those who, in the gross manner of the Capernaites, are held fast by these carnal opinions, the saying of Christ in John 6 will always stand firm: "It is the Spirit that gives life; the flesh profits nothing." This therefore is to be observed on account of those who cling to the symbols of bread and wine, and dream of either transubstantiation or consubstantiation, and who assert that the body is either offered for us, or, as they themselves say, eaten orally and swallowed down the throat. For Christ, who sat at the table with his body, which was born of the Virgin Mary, spoke concerning the bread and wine, which he held in his hand and offered to the disciples: "This is my body; this is my blood," etc., and (as we said a little before) he spoke of the body to be delivered to death and of the blood to be poured out for our sins. But since neither of these had yet been done when he said these things, certainly that bread could not be his body, nor that cup his blood; unless we are willing to say that Christ has two bodies, or we judge that the disciples did not eat the same body of the Lord as we do. To these must be added that in the present passage he gives no other use and end of the Supper than that he bids us do these things in remembrance of him; which the Apostle, in 1 Cor. 11, explains in this way: "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes." Thus, as far as Christ is concerned, the principal end of the Supper is that it seals to us the benefit of our redemption, makes us certain of salvation, and finally binds him wholly to us. And therefore he wished to use this rite, which would serve so great and so manifold a mystery.

units.la: Conuenit enim cum discipulis in vnum locum, vt eo conflaret, se nihil priuatum tradere, sed ad totam Ecclesiam pertinere quod hic traditur. Ideo Paulus se toti Ecclesiae tradidisse scribit, quod a Domino acceperit. Deinde de morte sua diligenter & prolixe concionatus est. Praeterea panem & vinum distribuit, vt se testatur panem esse, qui fortificat cor hominis, vinum item quod exhilarat Deum & homines. Vt vero Christus panem accepit & fregit, postquam gratias egisset: ita eundem discipulos quoq; accipere & frangere voluit, vt ita singuli admonerentur, hunc ad se priuatim pertinere, se item necis eius authores esse, adhaec debitores omnibus aliis, vt eos in Christi atq; salutis, quae in ipso habetur, societatem adducant. De poculo peculiare quid mandatur, vt ex eo omnes bibant: & omnes ex eo bibisse. Marcus annotauit: Quia enim sciebat quid futurum esset nouissimis temporibus, quod nimirum Antichristus sacrilega audacia alteram Sacramenti speciem Ecclesiae erepturus esset, cauere voluit, ne quis tanti scelerиc occasionem ex eius institutione arriperet. Sed non tantum valuit apud istos homines Christi authoritas, quin in Concilio Constantiensi aut fuerint statuere, vt poculo sacro abstineant, quos Dei Filius non minus sanguinis quam corporis sui vult participes facere.
units.tr: For he gathered the disciples into one place, to show that he handed over nothing private, but that what is delivered here belongs to the whole Church. For this reason Paul writes that he delivered it to the whole Church, having received it from the Lord. Then he preached diligently and at length about his death. Moreover, he distributed bread and wine, and testified that he is the bread that strengthens the heart of man, and likewise the wine that gladdens God and men. And just as Christ took the bread and broke it, after giving thanks, so he willed that the disciples likewise should take and break it, so that each one might be reminded that this belongs to him personally, that he too is the author of Christ's death, and moreover that he is bound to all others to bring them into the fellowship of Christ and of the salvation that is had in him. Concerning the cup a particular command is given, that all should drink from it, and that all did drink from it. Mark has noted this. For since he knew what would happen in the last times, namely that Antichrist, with sacrilegious audacity, would snatch away the second kind of the sacrament from the Church, he wished to guard against anyone seizing on the occasion of such a crime from his institution. But the authority of Christ did not prevail so far with those men that at the Council of Constance they decreed that those whom the Son of God wills to make partakers of his blood no less than of his body should abstain from the holy cup.

units.la: Sed constanter obseruari debet a Christo traditus ritus, qui procul dubio optimus & plenus mysteriorum est. Hunc enim (vt ex Paulo apparet) Apostoli Ecclesijs tradiderunt a Christo ac ceptum. Fiat ergo coetus publicus, nec aliquid priuatum putetur id, quod quaestum Missae priuata totum abolet. Deinde non sine concione sacra celebretur Coena. Sacramenta enim sine verbo Dei non constant, cum (vt D. Augustinus ait) accedente verbo ad elementum, fiat Sacramentum. Et si Verbum auferas, perinde fit, ac si quis tabulas scriptas a sigillo auferat. Quid vero tunc illo obsignabitur? Imo sine praecedente concione sacra celebratur Coena, Christus ipse a sua Coena remouetur, nec habebit fidelis animaquo fruatur. Deinde, Hoc facite (inquit Christus) in mei recordationem: quod scilicet ego feci vobis in exemplum. At rusticum videtur, si quius plebeius sacra symbola manibus contrectet, ori inferat, proximo assidenti porrigat. Sed assioni huic rusticae in speciem profunda mysteria subsunt. Nam, vt nuper diximus, dum in manus nostras sumuntur symbola ex ipsius Domini mandato, testatur is, fe nostrum esse velle. Fractio panis, & infusio vini in pocu-lum, peccatorum confessioni feruit, nos videlicet ex eorum numero esse, qui Filium Dei in crucem suffiximus, & sanguinem eius effudimus.
