Then he blazed with passion and all but incited the rest, crying, "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?" The outcome of his fighting was laughable. He cut off only the ear of the high priest's servant, though he had aimed at his head. At last, having entered the high priest's courtyard, he was frightened by a servant girl's voice and yielded to the questions of the servants, and shamefully denied Christ. Here is a type of all those who, carried away by unadvised zeal and the desires of the flesh, without being called by God, undertake great matters. Would that today there were not many similar things done, which grievously offend the simpler and godly, and make the impious fiercer. Meanwhile Malchus, the high priest's servant, teaches by his example what usually befalls those who give themselves into the service of antichristian prelates. In the Scriptures the ear is the symbol of obedience and faith. But such men lose their right ear, so that they either do not hear the Word of God at all, or hear it only with the left ear, and become worse for it.

units.la: Porro Christum audiamus, qui initio discipulos simul omnes coercet, ut quiescant, dicens: Sinite hucusq;. Deinde Petrum compellat: Conuerte gladium tuum in locum suum. Et huius praeceptt rationem reddit hanc: Quicunq; enim acceperint gladium, gladio peribunt. Quod de illis dicitur, qui ex priuata temeritate gladio pugnant: & consentit cum Lege veteri, quae caedes iniustas prohibet, & cum eo, quod Christus in Apocalypsi pronunciat: Qui in captiuitatem ducit, in captiuitatem abit: qui gladio occiderit, eum oportet gladio occidi. Perperam ergo hoc dictum Anabaptistae aduersus legitimum gladij vsum detorquent, qui iudicibus datus est & principibus viri, ut scelera puniant, & Ecclesiam defendant. Addit autem in praesenti Dominus aliud argumentum, quo demonstrat defensione ista Petri sibi non opus esse. An putas (inquit) me non posse precari Patrem meum, qui huc sistat mihi plures quam duodecim legiones Angelorum? Nam vt alibi ait, ipsi data est omnis potestas in caelo & in terra. Et rursum: Mea omnia Pater tua sunt, & tua mea sunt. Et hoc praecipue Angelis in mandatis datum esse confirmat, vt Filio Dei seruiant, & eundem non defendant modo, verumetiam in manibus ferant. Facile ergo erat Christo Angelorum praesidia a Patre impetrare. Sed quia regnum eius non est de hoc mundo, non voluit seruos habere in terris, qui pro ipso pugnarent: quod postea Pilato quoq; dixit. Continetur autem hoc doctrina generalis, neminem sub religionis praetextu temere debere arma arripere, nisi de Dei vocatione certus fit. Scimus equidem quid regibus alibi dictum fit: sed nolim ego temere cuiquam author esse, vt bellum moueat absq; peculiari Dei iussu. Etenim constat bellum nullum tam iustum esse, quin multa in eo fiant, quae iustitiae & religioni Christianae aduersantur: & ideo bellorum euentus esse dubios & periculosos, & raro tuta esse quae de illis monendis ineuntur consilia. Viderunt hoc plerique veterum, inter quos Lactantius aduersus gentes differens, quae suos cultus arma defendendas esse putabant, de vera religionis defensione inter alia sic scribit: Defendenda sunt (inquiunt) sacra publice sancta. O quam honesta voluntate miseri errant. Sentiunt enim nihil esse
units.tr: Next let us hear Christ, who at the start restrains all the disciples together, that they be still, saying, "Suffer ye thus far." Then he addresses Peter: "Put up your sword into its place." And he gives this reason for the command: "For all who take the sword will perish by the sword." This is said of those who fight with the sword from private rashness, and it agrees with the Old Law, which forbids unjust slaughter, and with what Christ declares in the Apocalypse: "He who leads into captivity will go into captivity; he who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword." Therefore the Anabaptists wrongly twist this saying against the lawful use of the sword, which has been given to judges and princes, that they may punish crimes and defend the Church. But in the present case the Lord adds another argument, by which he shows that Peter's defence is not needed for him. "Do you think," he says, "that I cannot pray to my Father, who would at once send me more than twelve legions of angels?" For, as he says elsewhere, all power in heaven and on earth has been given to him. And again: "All that is mine is yours, Father, and what is yours is mine." He also affirms that this was especially given to the angels in commission, to serve the Son of God and not only defend him but bear him in their hands. Thus it was easy for Christ to obtain the protection of the angels from the Father. But because his kingdom is not of this world, he did not wish to have servants on earth to fight for him, as he later said to Pilate. This teaches a general doctrine: no one should lightly take up arms under the pretext of religion unless he is certain of God's calling. We certainly know what is said elsewhere to kings, but I would not willingly be the author for anyone of making war rashly, without a special command of God. For it is agreed that no war is so just that many things are not done in it which are opposed to justice and the Christian religion; and therefore the outcomes of wars are doubtful and dangerous, and the counsels given about them are rarely safe. Most of the ancients saw this, among them Lactantius, who, disputing against the heathen, who thought their cults had to be defended by arms, writes among other things on the true defence of religion as follows: "The sacred things, they say, must be defended publicly as holy. O how wretchedly they err, though with an honourable intention! For they perceive that nothing is more excellent than religion among human affairs, and that it must be defended with the utmost force; but they are mistaken both about religion itself and about the kind of defence.

units.la: {1} De iustitia lib. 5. cap.20. nihil esse in rebus humanis religione praestantius, eamque summa vi oportere defendi: sed vt in ipsa religione, sic in defensionis genere falluntur. Defendenda enim religio est non occidendo, sed moriendo: non saevitia, sed patientia: non scelere, sed fide: illa enim malorum sunt, haec bonorum. Et necesse est bonum in religione verti, non malum. Nam si sanguine, si tormentis, si malo religionem defendere velis, iam non defendetur illa, sed polluetur atque violabitur. Nihil est enim tam voluntarium quam religio, in qua sit animus sacrificantis auersus est, iam sublata, iam nulla est. Recta igitur ratio est, vt religionem patientia vel morte defendas: in qua fides conseruata, et ipsi Deo grata est, et religioni addit authoritatem, etc. Confirmantur haec exemplis martyrum, quorum omnium sanguine religio Christiana obsignata et confirmata est. Quod autem in praesenti Christus Petro dixit, Scripturarum testimonio confirmari docet, dum addit: Quomodo autem implerentur scripturae, quae dicunt sic oportere fieri? Ita docens, omnibus scripturis eos aduersarios, qui neglecta aut abiecta cruce religionem vi et armis potius defendere volunt, quam ab ipso nobis monstratam viam ingredi. Addit his exemplum charitatis, quo amplius confirmat, quod docuit. Nam miraculose medetur Malcho, ostendens se medicum esse, qui animorum aures nobis aperiat. Hunc ergo oremus, vt nobis quoque medeatur, et hodie etiam Ecclesiam suam aduersus vim hostilem inter pericula, quae hanc circumstant, tueatur ad nominis sui gloriam et multorum salutem. Amen.
units.tr: {1} On Justice, book 5, chapter 20. Nothing among human affairs is more excellent than religion, and it must be defended with the utmost force; but they are mistaken both about religion itself and about the kind of defence. For religion must be defended not by killing but by dying, not by cruelty but by patience, not by crime but by faith; for the former are the acts of the wicked, the latter of the good. And it is necessary that the good be turned into religion, not evil. For if you wish to defend religion with blood, with torments, with evil, then it will not be defended but polluted and violated. For nothing is so voluntary as religion; where the mind of the one sacrificing is averse, it is at once taken away, and is no longer anything. The right course, then, is to defend religion by patience or even by death, in which faith is preserved, and is pleasing to God himself, and adds authority to religion," and so on. These things are confirmed by the examples of the martyrs, by whose blood alone the Christian religion has been sealed and confirmed. But that Christ in the present case said to Peter, "But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen thus?", he shows is confirmed by the testimony of the Scriptures. In so teaching, he sets against all the Scriptures those adversaries who, neglecting or rejecting the cross, prefer to defend religion by force and arms rather than to walk in the way shown to us by himself. He adds to these an example of love, by which he confirms more fully what he taught. For he miraculously heals Malchus, showing himself to be the physician who opens the ears of our minds. Let us therefore pray to him that he would heal us also, and today too protect his Church against hostile violence, amid the dangers that surround it, to the glory of his name and the salvation of many. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCXCIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CCXCIX.

units.la: In illa hora dixit Iesus turbae: Vt aduersus latronem existis cum gladijs et fustibus, vt comprehenderetis me: quotidie apud vos sedebam, docens in templo, nec deprehendistis me. Hoc autem totum factum est, vt implerentur scripturae prophetarum. Tunc discipuli omnes relicto eo, fugerunt. Illi vero praehensum Iesum abduxerunt ad Caiaphan pontificem maximum, vbi scribae et seniores coacti erant. Petrus autem sequebatur eum procul vsque in aulam pontificis maximi: et ingressus intro sedebat cum ministris, vt videret finem.
units.tr: At that hour Jesus said to the crowd: "Have you come out against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? Day after day I sat among you teaching in the temple, and you did not lay hands on me. But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left him and fled. But those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had been gathered. Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest; and going inside he sat with the attendants to see the outcome.

units.la: Quoniam Dominus noster IESVS CHRISTVS nuper inter cenandum cum Iuda proditore agens, diserte testatus est, illum non aliud facturum, quam quod in Scripturis praedictum fit, et nuper Petrum, qui ipsum armata manu defendere conabatur, reprehendens, iterum monuit, ita fieri oportere, vt captus in hostium potestatem veniat, vt ita scripturae impleantur, colligat ex his aliquis recte fecisse illius hostes, Sacerdotes et Scribas cum Senioribus, qui Iudaeis et aliis eorum authores fuerunt, quae aduersus Filium Dei designarunt. Non temere ergo in praesenti ad illos simul omnes conuersus, eos corripit, vt discamus illos per prouidentiam Dei consilium sive decretum non excusari, nec extra culpam esse. Simul autem narrat Euangelista, quid praeteriterint discipuli, quando Dominum captiuum factum et Petrum pro illo non admodum feliciter pugnauisse viderunt. Quibus subrexitur nouum Petri consilium sive institutum, quod illi non ut gravioris lapsus occasionem praebuit.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ, having recently spoken during the supper with Judas the traitor, plainly declared that he would do nothing other than what was foretold in the Scriptures. Shortly afterwards, rebuking Peter, who tried to defend him with an armed hand, he again warned that it must happen this way, that he should be taken into the power of his enemies, so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled. From this one may rightly conclude that his enemies, the priests and scribes with the elders, who were the authors of the plot among the Jews and others against the Son of God, did not act well. So now, turning to all of them together, he rebukes them, so that we may learn that they are not excused by God's providence, that is, his counsel or decree, and are not free from guilt. At the same time the evangelist tells us what the disciples did when they saw their Lord taken captive and Peter fighting for him not very successfully. Here a new plan or resolution of Peter's presents itself, which did not give them an occasion for a more serious fall.

units.la: Ad primum pertinet quod turbae ex Sacerdotibus et horum servis atque militibus aduersus ipsum collectae dixerunt: Vt aduersus latronem existis cum gladijs et fustibus, vt comprehendere me. Atqui quotidie sedebam apud vos, docens in templo, nec deprehendistis me. Apud Lucam addit: Sed haec est hora illa vestra et potestas tenebrarum. Accusat hostium iniustitiam, et eos ab surde et inique facere, argumentis probat. Primum a forma et modo sumit, cuius hic sensus est: Qui vi et armis rem agunt, quando his minime opus est, ij se causam malam agere testantur, nec eam aliter defendi posse. Tanta enim est iustitia et veritatis maiestas, vt pessimi quique, iustitiae et veritatis amantes videri velint. At vos forma eam aduersus me sequimini, qua minime opus erat. Venitis enim ad me capiendum cum gladijs et fustibus. Atqui his non erat opus, cum ego inermis sim, neque vllum sit a meis discipulis periculum, quos ego pro me armis pugnare nolo. Deinde
units.tr: To the first point belongs what the crowd, gathered against him from the priests, their servants and the soldiers, said: "Have you come out against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? Yet day after day I sat among you teaching in the temple, and you did not lay hands on me." In Luke he adds: "But this is your hour, and the power of darkness." He accuses his enemies of injustice and proves by arguments that they act unjustly and wickedly. First he takes his argument from the manner and method of their action, the sense of which is this: those who carry out their business by force and arms, when there is no need for such means at all, thereby testify that their cause is bad and cannot otherwise be defended. For such is the majesty of justice and truth that even the worst men wish to appear as lovers of justice and truth. But you pursue me in a way that is quite unnecessary. For you come to seize me with swords and clubs. Yet there was no need for these, since I am unarmed, and there is no danger from my disciples, whom I do not want to fight with weapons on my behalf. Next,

units.la: Christus aduersarios accusat et corripit. a loco quoq; argumentatur, addens: Quotidie sedebam apud vos in templo docens. Doctorem hactenus egi, & docui loco consueto, vbi doceri debet. Ibi ergo me aggredi, & erroris conuincere debebatis. At illic me non deprehendistis. Nunc autem foris extra portas me quaeritis, & quidem intempestanoste, quando homines nocentes graßantur, cum ego nullum prorsus specimen dederim, propter quod vobis suspectus fieri debuerim. Tertio rationem a tempore sumptam fortius vr- gens, quales sint, docet, cum dicit. Hac est hora illa vestra, & potestas tenebrarum. Conuenit hic quod aliquando Nicodemo dixerat: Quisquis peruerse agit, odit lucem, nec venit ad lucem, ne ar- guantur ipsius opera. Cum e contra qui veritati operam dat, ad lucem veniat, vt facta eius manifesta fiant, quod secundum Deum, id est, ex diuina voluntate praescripto facta sint. At vos nocturnum tempus vobis delegistis, & tenebrarum caligine hoc occultari cupitis quod agitis. Ergo non lucis, sed tenebrarum filij estis: & vobis hac hora conuenit. Imo hac potestas, qua pugnatis te nebrarum potestas est. At tenebrarum potestas est diaboli, quem principem tenebrarum vocat Apostolus, & ideo tenebrarum opera dicuntur, quae ex diaboli suggestione aduersus Dei voluntatem atque praecepta fiunt, cum quibus ne Christiani homines vllum commercium habeant, Paulus prohibet. Quid ergo in hos grauius dici poterat a Christo, qui lux mundi & Sol iustitiæ est, quàm quod eos potestatem tenebrarum vocat. Ita enim diaboli satellites esse innuit, & dignos, qui a suo regno prorsus excludantur.
units.tr: Christ accuses and rebukes his adversaries also from the place, adding: "Day after day I sat among you in the temple teaching." Up to now I have acted as a teacher and taught in the customary place, where teaching ought to be given. There, then, you ought to have confronted me and convicted me of error. But there you did not lay hands on me. Now you seek me outside, beyond the gates, and indeed at night, when guilty men go about their crimes, although I have given no sign at all that would have made me justly suspect in your eyes. Thirdly, pressing more strongly the argument taken from the time, he shows what sort of men they are, when he says: "This is your hour, and the power of darkness." What he once said to Nicodemus applies here: whoever acts wickedly hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds be exposed; but whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they have been done according to God, that is, in accordance with the divine will. But you have chosen the night for yourselves, and you wish what you do to be hidden by the darkness of shadows. Therefore you are not sons of the light but of the darkness, and this hour suits you. Indeed, this power by which you fight is the power of darkness. The power of darkness is the devil's, whom the Apostle calls the prince of darkness; and therefore those works are called works of darkness which are done at the devil's prompting against the will and commands of God, with which Paul forbids Christians to have any fellowship. What, then, could be said more severely of these men by Christ, who is the light of the world and the Sun of righteousness, than that he calls them the power of darkness? For thereby he implies that they are the devil's henchmen, and worthy to be wholly shut out of his kingdom.

units.la: Debet autem considerari hoc loco vera charitatis siue dilectionis & patientiae Christianae ratio. Est verissimum exemplar perfectissimum Christus, qui pro hostibus suis precatus est, & omni iniuriarum & contumeliorum genere lacessitus non aperuit os suum. At idem se insontem armis hostilibus circumueniri, & vt latronem nocturno tempore capi queritur, seq; excusat, & hostium insultitiam arguit. Non vetat ergo Christiana religio, quo minus nostram innocentiam istis ratio-nibus tueamur: gloriam Dei item a calumniis asseramus, & aduersarios arguamus, impiorum item conuitia & iniquitatem, qui dum nobis obtrectant, & contra nos pugnant, Veritati officere student. Nec leuis illorum error est, qui hodie sub patientiae praetextu suae ignaviae patrocinantur. Hi enim fere Dei gloriam intercidere sinunt, & simplicium salutem negligunt, quorum fides inte-rea labefactatur, dum veritatis doctrina, non eo, quo necesse erat, zelo defenditur. Idcirco D. Hie-ronymus olim nolebat in haereseos suspicione, nedum crimine, aliquem esse patientem. Tunc enim non priuata, sed publica causa agitur, quam nemo negligere potest, quin in Deum simul & ho-mines peccet. Fit igitur fere iusto Dei iudicio, vt qui causam Dei non defendunt, neq; huic neq; ho-minibus placeant. Cur enim apud homines in aliqua authoritate & pretio sit, cui Dei gloria & authoritas sordet.
units.tr: Here we ought to consider the true nature of Christian charity, love and patience. The most perfect and truest example is Christ, who prayed for his enemies, and who, though assailed with every kind of injury and insult, did not open his mouth. Yet the same Christ complains that he, innocent, is surrounded by hostile arms and seized like a robber at night, defends himself, and exposes the insolence of his enemies. Therefore the Christian religion does not forbid us from defending our innocence by such reasons, nor from vindicating the glory of God against slanders, nor from confronting our adversaries, nor from opposing the reproaches and injustice of the wicked, who, while they disparage us and fight against us, strive to hinder the truth. Nor is the error of those small who today shelter their own laziness under the pretext of patience. For they allow the glory of God almost to perish, and neglect the salvation of simple people, whose faith meanwhile is weakened, while the doctrine of the truth is defended without the zeal that was necessary. For this reason Saint Jerome once would not allow anyone to be patient in the face of even a suspicion of heresy, let alone of the crime itself. For then it is not a private but a public cause that is at stake, which no one can neglect without sinning both against God and against men. So it happens, almost by the just judgment of God, that those who do not defend the cause of God please neither God nor men. For how can someone be held in any authority or esteem among men when the glory and authority of God is held in contempt by him?

units.la: Docet praeterea locus hic quid iudicari debeat de magistratibus, qui veritatem & iustitiam oppugnant. Magistratus a Deo instituti sunt, & eos quoq; ex Deo esse, qui inter prophanas gentes hoc munere funguntur, Apostoli diserte testantur, & ideo Christianos homines Imperatoribus & ab his constitutis praesidibus obedire olim iusserunt, ne religio propter eorum contumaciam & pro-teruiam male audiret. Caeterum vt alia Dei instituta Satan peruertit & corrumpit, vt quae Dei gloria & hominum saluti debebant seruire, vtriq; officiant: ita etiam frequenter fit magistratibus si superbia, ambitioni, tyrannidi & aliis sinistris affectibus se decipi aut abripi patiantur. Tunc enim non Dei, sed diaboli ministri sunt, non alij, sed daemones sunt. Quod in eum quoq; finem obser-uari debet, vt habeamus, quod ijs responderi possit, qui magistratibus simpliciter obedire volunt, qualiacunq; sint, quae illi mandant. Hoc enim falso dici, hoc vno demonstrari potest, quòd magi-stratus quoq; non solum errare possunt, verumetiam Deo aduersa & iniqua decernere. Quod si fiat, Apostolorum regulã sequi debent homines Christiani, quae est, Deo potius obediendum esse quàm hominibus. Hanc tot millia martyrum vtriusq; Testamenti suo sanguine obsignarunt, vt portentum videri possit, si eam negent, qui Christi nomen profitentur.
units.tr: This passage further teaches what ought to be judged about magistrates who attack truth and justice. Magistrates have been instituted by God, and the apostles plainly testify that those who discharge this office among profane nations are also from God. Therefore they once ordered Christians to obey emperors and the governors appointed by them, lest religion be badly spoken of because of their stubbornness and insolence. Yet, just as Satan perverts and corrupts other institutions of God, so that those things which ought to serve the glory of God and the salvation of men instead harm both, so it often happens with magistrates, if they allow themselves to be deceived or carried away by pride, ambition, tyranny and other sinister passions. For then they are not ministers of God but of the devil; they are not magistrates but demons. This must also be observed for this purpose: that we may have an answer for those who wish to obey magistrates simply, whatever they may command. For it can be shown plainly, by this one point, that this is false: magistrates too can not only err, but also decree things adverse and unjust to God. If this happens, Christians ought to follow the rule of the apostles, which is that God must be obeyed rather than men. This rule so many thousands of martyrs of both Testaments sealed with their blood that it would seem a monstrous thing if those who profess the name of Christ should deny it.

units.la: Sed quid discipuli praeterea fecerint, videamus, postquam Dominum viderunt captiuum fa-ctum in hostium suorum manus venijse, qui toties iam vita eius insidiati fuerant. Id vero paucis absoluit Matthaeus, inquiens: Tunc discipuli omnes relicto eo fugerunt. Ita factuoros praedixerat Christus: Ecce veniet tempus, & iam venit, cum dispergemini, vnusquisque ad suos, & me solum relinquetis, &c. Debuit autem hoc fieri propter mysterium redemptionis nostræ, vt huius gloria vni Christo accepta ferretur. Nam si quis discipulorum cum illo captus & abductus, vel modica ex parte perpessionum eius consors fuisset factus, quàm amplam & optatam ansam habuisset Satan decipiendi simplices & superstitiosos homines, vt quæ vni Christo debetur salutis gloriam discipulis communem faceret? Hoc ergo vt caueret Dominus, solus capi & vinciri, solus iudicio sisti & damnari, solus deniq; in crucem suffigi & mori voluit.
units.tr: But let us see what the disciples did afterwards, once they saw their Lord taken captive and delivered into the hands of his enemies, who had already so often plotted against his life. Matthew sums this up briefly, saying: "Then all the disciples left him and fled." Christ had foretold that this would happen: "Behold, the time will come, and it is already here, when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave me alone, etc." This had to happen because of the mystery of our redemption, so that the glory of it might be ascribed to Christ alone. For if any of the disciples had been seized and led away with him, or had been made a partaker of even a small part of his sufferings, how large and welcome an opening Satan would have had for deceiving simple and superstitious people, so as to make the glory of salvation, which is owed to Christ alone, common to the disciples! Therefore, so that this might be prevented, the Lord willed to be taken and bound alone, to stand alone before judgment and be condemned alone, and finally to be alone nailed to the cross and to die. leave me alone, etc.

units.la: Obseruari autem debet in hac fuga, quàm multa concurrunt, quæ eius indignitatem arguunt & amplificant. Primò enim fugiunt discipuli, quos ipse ex gratia sibi delegerat, quos non seruorum facta n adisci-sed amicorum loco habuerat, quos nihil celarat, quibus nihil vnquam passus fuerat desieri, adeò vt de eo interrogati in vltima Cœna, libere confessi sint, sibi nihil defuisse: Fugiunt deniq; qui se cum ipso mortem adire velle promiserant. Et inter hos Petrus, qui paulò ante tyrocinium egregium dederat, quando Dominum gladio arrepto contra armatam cohortem defendere instituit. Hi(in-quam) fugiunt. Et a quo nam? Relicto eo (inquit Euangelista) fugerunt. De IESV CHRISTO autem loquitur, de quo Petrus aliquando confessione omnium nomine facta publicè dixerat: Domine, quò ibimus? tu verba vitæ æternæ habes: quem item Dominum suum & magistrum dixe-rat, in cuius nomine Euangelium prædicarunt, dæmonia eiecerunt. Fugiunt autem iam capto illo & eum in medio hostium, imò in vnguibus & faucibus luporum relinquunt, quem inter amicos re- linquere ipsis graue & molestum esse debuisset, nisi subitus metus ipsis omnem officij sui memoriam abstulisset. Apparet igitur in hoc exemplo, quanta sit carnis infirmitas in electis quoq;, & vt hæc in sanctissimis interdum fidei etiam ipsorum præualeat, nisi spiritu suo Dominus illos sustentet & confirmet. Discamus ergo de nobis modestè sentire, neq; vnquam obliuiscamur admonitionis Apostolicæ: Qui sibi videtur stare, videat ne cadat. Si enim hoc dilectis discipulis, si Petro, in quo tantùm zeli ardor flagrauit, si Ioanni præ cæteris dilectio, accidit, quid nobis fiat, qui nihil de nobis possumus sperare, quo illi abundarunt. Est quidem magna spiritus alacritas in electis: sed carnis infirmitas maior, maximè, si quando ipse Christus in periculum venit, aut hi causam eius deseruisse videntur, de quibus maxima quæq; sperabamus. Deinde nemo quoq; de alijs desperet, quos im-becilliores esse videt: Nam hic in primis locum habet quod proverbio dicitur: Vir fugiens denuo pugnabit. Et qui hic tam turpiter fugerunt relicto Christo, postea gloriosam pro illo mortem oppe-tierunt. Et huius generis exempla posterius seculis multa edita sunt. Cur ergo temerè damnemus hodie aliquos, aut de nobis ipsis desperemus, si nos sentiamus nonnihil labascere? Qui hos olim con-firmare potuit, idem in nobis faciet, si nostram operam sibi gloriosam fore intellexerit. Præterea hinc consolationem petamus, si quando intimi nos deserunt, in quibus maxima nobis erat fiducia. Tunc in mentem nobis veniant Christi verba, quæ paulò ante adduximus. Nam etsi omnes dis-fugiant, nos solos relinquant, non sumus tamen soli, quia Filius Dei non relinquit nos orpha-nos, sed ipse nobiscum est vsq; ad consummationem seculi. In illo ergo fortes simus, qui si pro nobis stet, tutò nobis dicere licebit: Quis contra nos? Dominus lux mea & salus mea, a quo nam timebo? Psal.27.
units.tr: It should also be noted in this flight how many circumstances combine to show and increase its disgrace. First, the disciples flee: those whom he had chosen for himself out of grace, whom he had not taken as servants but had regarded as friends, from whom he had hidden nothing, and who had never lacked anything while with him, so that when they were asked at the last supper, they freely confessed that they had lacked nothing. Finally, those who had promised to go with him to death flee as well. Among them is Peter, who had shortly before given a splendid proof of his courage when he drew his sword to defend the Lord against the armed cohort. These, I say, flee. And from whom? The Evangelist says: "Having left him, they fled." He is speaking of Jesus Christ, to whom Peter once spoke publicly on behalf of all, saying: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life." They had also called him their Lord and Teacher, in whose name they had preached the gospel and cast out demons. And they flee when he has already been seized, leaving him in the midst of enemies, indeed in the claws and jaws of wolves. To leave him among his friends should have been painful and distressing for them, had not sudden fear taken away all memory of their duty. This example therefore shows how great the weakness of the flesh is, even in the elect, and how it sometimes prevails even over the faith of the most holy, unless the Lord sustains and strengthens them by his Spirit. Let us learn, then, to think modestly of ourselves, and never forget the apostolic warning: "Let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall." For if this befell the beloved disciples, if it befell Peter, in whom the ardour of zeal blazed so fiercely, and John, who was preeminent among the rest in love, what will become of us, who can hope for nothing from ourselves in which they abounded? There is indeed great eagerness of spirit in the elect, but the weakness of the flesh is greater, especially when Christ himself comes into danger, or when those seem to have deserted his cause from whom we expected the greatest things. Furthermore, let no one despair of others whom he sees to be weaker. For here the proverb applies: "A man who flees will fight again." Those who fled so shamefully here, leaving Christ, afterwards met a glorious death for him. Many examples of this kind have been recorded in later ages. Why, then, should we rashly condemn anyone today, or despair of ourselves, if we feel that we are somewhat wavering? He who was able to strengthen these men then will do the same in us, if he understands that our labour will be glorious to him. Moreover, let us seek comfort from this, when those closest to us desert us, in whom we had the greatest confidence. Then let the words of Christ, which we quoted a little while ago, come to mind. For even if all flee and leave us alone, we are not alone, because the Son of God does not leave us orphans, but is with us himself until the end of the age. Let us therefore be brave in him; if he stands for us, we may safely say: "Who is against us?" The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? Ps. 27.

units.la: Nunc quid de Christo factum sit, videre oportet. De aduersarijs eius dicitur, quòd captiuum factum abduxerint ad Caiaphan Pontificem maximum, vbi scribæ & seniores coacti erant vt cæ-tus ipsorum concilij generalis faciem referret, eoq; plus haberet authoritatis. Vt ergo priùs de illo accidendo consultarunt & decretum fecerunt in concilio post Lazarum a mortuis resuscitatum: ita nunc in concilium abducitur, vt huius authoritate damnatus Rom.præsidi tradatur, qui ipsum in crucem suffigat. Annotantur hæc diligenter ab Euangelistis, vt discamus non nimium tribuere concilijs falsorum antistitum, qui sub primatu ecclesiastico priuatam authoritatem & quastu quæ-runt. Etenim istos in populo Dei primatum tenuisse constat. Sedebant in cathedra Mosis Christo teste, & lege Dei omnis ipsorum authoritas nitebatur: adeò vt capitale esset sententiæ summi sa-cerdotis contradicere. Atqui turpiter & pernitiosè errarunt, idq; in præcipuo fidei & salutis capi-te, eum damnando in quo vno salus & redemptio humani generis habetur, & ignorantes implent, quod olim prædictum erat, dum ipsi, qui Ecclesiæ architecti haberi volebant, lapide illum pretiosum reijciunt, quæ æterno suo decreto Deus prædestinauerat, vt esset fundamentum Zionis simul & ca-Psal.118. put angeli. Idem facturos esse successores quoque ab ipso Christo praedictum est. Nam Apostolis dixit: Tradent vos in concilia et in synagogis alienos facient et excludent: Quod de nullis aliis potest intelligi, quam iis qui in Ecclesia praesident, ut penes illos sit concilia cogere et ea pro suo arbitrio gubernare. Expertifiunt horum tyrannidem Apostoli, quam primum caeperunt praedicare, ut liber Actorum testatur. Nec meliores fuerunt, qui posteris temporibus sub Christiani nominis et Apostolicae successionis praetextu primatum in Ecclesia sibi vsurparunt. Vetus quidem mos est, ut controversiae Ecclesiasticae Concilijs indictis dirimantur, et eorundem authoritate errores atque haereses confutentur et tollantur e medio. Sic factum, quando aliqui Legem Evangelio miscuerunt, ut doctrinam de fidei iustificatione adulterarent et in nihilum redigerent: Et Apostolorum vestigijs insisterunt patres, qui in Nicena, Ephes. Chalcedonen. Constantinopol. et his similibus Synodis convenerunt.
units.tr: Now we must see what was done to Christ. It is said of his enemies that they led him away as a prisoner to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered so that their assembly might have the appearance of a general council and thus greater authority. Just as they had earlier consulted about his death and made a decree in the council after Lazarus was raised from the dead, so now he is led into the council, so that, condemned by its authority, he may be handed over to the Roman governor, who would nail him to the cross. The Evangelists note these things carefully, so that we may learn not to attach too much weight to the councils of false prelates, who under the pretext of ecclesiastical primacy sought private authority and gain. For it is evident that these men held the primacy among the people of God. They sat in the seat of Moses, as Christ testified, and all their authority rested on the law of God; so much so that to contradict the sentence of the high priest was a capital offence. Yet they erred shamefully and destructively, and that on the chief point of faith and salvation, condemning him in whom alone the salvation and redemption of the human race is found. In ignorance they fulfilled what had been foretold long before, when they, who wished to be regarded as the architects of the Church, rejected that precious stone which God had predestined by his eternal decree to be the foundation of Zion and the chief corner stone. Ps. 118. It was also foretold by Christ himself that his successors would do the same. For he said to the apostles: "They will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will make you strangers and exclude you." This cannot be understood of anyone other than those who preside in the Church, so that it is in their power to convene councils and to govern them according to their own judgment. The apostles experienced the tyranny of these men as soon as they began to preach, as the book of Acts bears witness. Nor were those any better who in later times usurped primacy in the Church under the pretext of the Christian name and apostolic succession. It is indeed an old custom that ecclesiastical controversies should be settled by councils convened for the purpose, and that errors and heresies should be refuted and removed by their authority. This was done when some mixed the law with the gospel, corrupting the doctrine of justification by faith and reducing it to nothing. And the Fathers, who met at Nicaea, Ephesus, Chalcedon, Constantinople and similar synods, followed in the footsteps of the apostles.

units.la: At tunc legitime conuocabantur concilia, imperatorum authoritate regebantur, qui Episcoporum quoque concertationes et affectus priuatos coercebant: et ut omnia ex Dei verbo decernerentur, curabant. At quid posteris temporibus factum sit, et quid hodie fiat postquam Romani pontifices sibi in Ecclesia imperium acquisierunt, res ipsa loquitur. Pontificia authoritate concilia indicuntur et reguntur. Nec alios quam in sua verba iuratos vocat Papa: alij vt rei et haeretici citantur. Praeiudicijs aguntur omnia, quod ex bullis ipsorum abundè demonstrari possent, quibus illa indicuntur. Canones, decreta Patrum, temporis longi praescriptio, consuetudines, et si qua alia sunt huius generis, verbo Dei et scripturis praeferuntur. Ideo Conciliorum exitus funesti sunt, et quia his non possunt acquiescere conscientiae hominum dubiae, fere ad arma concurritur, ut proverbio vulgari dicatur, Omne Concilium parit bellum.
units.tr: But in those days councils were lawfully convened and governed by the authority of the emperors, who also restrained the quarrels and private ambitions of the bishops, and took care that everything was decided according to the Word of God. But what has happened in later times, and what is done today, since the Roman pontiffs have acquired dominion over the Church, the matter itself makes plain. Councils are convened and presided over by papal authority. The Pope summons only those who have sworn to his words; others are cited as accused persons and heretics. Everything is decided in advance, as can be amply demonstrated from their bulls by which the councils are called. Canons, decrees of the Fathers, long-standing prescription, customs, and whatever else is of this kind, are placed above the Word of God and the Scriptures. Hence the outcomes of their councils are disastrous, and since the consciences of doubting people cannot rest on them, men almost take up arms, so that the common saying holds: "Every council brings forth war."

units.la: Et voluit Dei Filius proprio exemplo docere, quid ex Pontificum concilijs sperari debeat. Abhis ergo caveant sibi Christiani magistratus et principes. Horum enim authoritati Ecclesias et doctrinam subijcere, veritatem prodere est.
units.tr: And the Son of God wished to teach by his own example what ought to be expected from the councils of the Pontiffs. Christian magistrates and princes should therefore beware of them. For to subject the Churches and their doctrine to the authority of these men is to betray the truth.

units.la: Caeterum interseritur hoc loco aliquid de Petro, quod huic occasionem turpissimi lapsus praebuit. Nam Dominum qui abducebatur a longe sequutus est vsq; in aulam Pontificis maximi: et hanc ingressus quoque, consedit cum ministris, ut finem rei videret. Quod illum pio et sancto zelo ferri, non est dubium. Decipitur autem sua confidentia, qua prius inter cænandu peccauerat. Nam etsi iam expertus esset se nihil fortiorem et praestantiorem esse alijs, cum quibus ipse quoque reliquo Christo fugerat, adhuc tamen talis videri vult, et locum eum accedit, qui ipsi merito subesse esse debebat, illis item sese sociat, qui manus iam iniecerunt Domino. Immemor item verborum Domini, cepit videre quid futurum sit, cum diserte hic praedixisset. Scitis intra duos dies Paschaf fo re, et Filium hominis tradendum vt crucifigatur. Quod si de eo dubitabat propter Christi maiestatem et diuinam virtutem, quae ipsum de illo iubebant sublimius quid sperare, non debebat eius obliuisci, quod de ipso fidem abnegaturo ei praedixerat, cum iam ex fuga et metu ignauo sententiret, quid porro posset sequi. Sed quam turpiter falsus fit sua opinione, posteaquam loco audiemus. Nobis suspectum sit quicquid carnis affectus iuggerit, et precemur Deum Patrem miserationum, ut nos suo spiritu confirmet fidei constantia, ut in finem vsq; perseueremus. Amen.
units.tr: Meanwhile, something about Peter is inserted at this point, which provided the occasion for his most shameful fall. For he followed the Lord from afar, as he was being led away, all the way into the court of the high priest; and having entered there too, he sat down with the servants so that he might see the outcome of the affair. There is no doubt that he was carried along by a pious and holy zeal. But he was deceived by his self-confidence, by which he had earlier sinned at the supper. For although he had already learned that he was in no way stronger or more outstanding than the others with whom he too had fled after leaving Christ, he still wished to appear so, and he approaches the place which he ought rightly to have kept at a distance, and joins himself to those who had already laid hands on the Lord. Forgetful also of the Lord's words, he began to see what would happen, when he had clearly foretold it here: "You know that after two days it is the Passover, and the Son of man will be handed over to be crucified." If he doubted this because of the majesty of Christ and his divine power, which led him to hope for something more sublime from him, he ought not to have forgotten what Christ had foretold, that he would deny him. Since he was already thinking, out of flight and cowardly fear, about what might follow next, let him see how shamefully he was deceived in his own opinion, as we shall hear in its place. Let us regard with suspicion whatever the desires of the flesh suggest to us, and let us pray to God the Father of mercies that he strengthen us by his Spirit with constancy of faith, so that we may persevere to the end. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCC.
units.tr: Homily 300.

units.la: Principes autem Sacerdotum & Seniores & totus consessus quaerebant falsum testimonium contra Iesum, ut eum morte multarent: Atqui non inuenerunt: etiam cum multi falsi testes accesserunt, non inuenerunt. Postremo vero aduenientes duo falsi testes dixerunt: Iste dixit, Possum dissoluere templum Dei, & triduo ipsum aedificare. Et surgens pontifex maximus, dixit ei: Nihil respondes? quid illud est quod isti aduersum te testificantur? Iesus autem silebat. Et respondens pontifex maximus, dixit ei: Adiuro te per Deum viuentem, ut dicas nobis an tu sis Christus ille Filius Dei. Dicit ei Iesus, Tu dixisti: quinetiam dico vobis, ab hoc tempore videbitis Filium hominis sedentem ad dexteram potentiæ Dei, & venientem in nubibus cœli. Tunc Pontifex maximus dirupit vestimenta sua, dicens, Blasphemauit, quid amplius egemus testibus? ecce, nunc audistis blasphemiam eius. Quid vobis videtur? Ipsi vero respondentes dixerunt: Tenetur mortis poena: Tunc insputerunt in faciem eius, & colaphos ei inflixerunt, alij vero bacillis eum ceciderunt, dicentes: Vaticinare nobis Christe, quis sit qui te percussit.
units.tr: Now the chief priests, the elders and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus, that they might have him condemned to death. Yet they found none, even though many false witnesses came forward. At last two false witnesses came up and said: "This man said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days.'" The high priest stood up and said to him: "Do you answer nothing? What is it that these men testify against you?" But Jesus kept silent. Then the high priest answered and said to him: "I adjure you by the living God, tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God." Jesus said to him: "You have said it. Moreover, I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of God and coming on the clouds of heaven." Then the high priest tore his garments, saying: "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? See, now you have heard his blasphemy. What do you think?" They answered and said: "He deserves the penalty of death." Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists, and others struck him with rods, saying: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?"

units.la: AVdiimus Filium Dei IESVM CHRISTVM captum & vinctum in domum Caiapha Pontificis abductum fuisse, vt illic ad mortem damnaretur. Vt vero hoc factum sit, de inceps narratur. Sunt autem narrationis istius tria Capita. Primum docet qui Iudices fuerint, qui in causam Christi inquirere & de illa pronuntiare debuerunt. Alterum, qua forma aut modo processum huius actionis instituerint. Postremum quam indignis modis & quam inhumaniter damnatum tractarint. Porrò summa omnium istorum haec est, IESVM CHRISTVM propter veritatis confessionem iniquè & iniustè damnatum esse eius impietatis, cuius nos rei eramus, vt nostra peccata suæ mortis merito expiaret, & per illum nos seruaremur.
units.tr: We have heard that the Son of God, Jesus Christ, was seized and bound and led into the house of Caiaphas the high priest, so that there he might be condemned to death. How this came about is now narrated. This narrative has three parts. The first shows who the judges were, who ought to inquire into the cause of Christ and pronounce on it. The second, by what form or manner they set in motion the proceedings of this action. The last, how unworthily and how inhumanly they treated the condemned man. The sum of all these is that Jesus Christ was condemned unjustly and wrongfully, for confessing the truth, on the charge of that impiety of which we were guilty, so that by the merit of his death he might expiate our sins and through him we might be saved.

units.la: Quoad primum nominantur principes sacerdotum, & inter hos Caiaphas, qui eius anni Pontifex erat, vt alibi dictum est. Et quoties multorum mentio fit, qui Pontifices aut Sacerdotum principes fuerunt, toties Iudæorum impietas & audacia notatur, qui contra Dei Legem plures in statuerunt, cum vnicus esse deberet, qui Christi persõnam referret, qui Ecclesiæ suæ sacerdos est in æternum, & nec successorem, neque vicarium habet, qui ipsius vices obeat. Sub Sacerdotum nomine Scribæ etiam censentur, qui Legis interpretes erant. Accesserunt his Seniores viri, nimirum politici, qui Rempublicam Iudaeam administrabant, quantum illis licebat per Romanos, qui illos iam pridem suæ libertate spoliatos non patiebantur suo iure viuere, nisi quatenus quoad sacra & religionem illis aliquam ἀυτονομίαν permittebant: quam durare oportuit vsque ad Christi tempora, in quo typica omnia impleri debuerunt, quibus impletis & abrogatis, Respub. quoque Iudaica cessauit. Sæpe autem horum mentio fit, quoties de Christi aduersariis agitur, vt appareat quam in digna sit eius in terris fors siue conditio. Vt enim olim cum ad suos veniret, ab eis non receptus est, sed hostes acerrimos habuit, quotquot in Ecclesia & Repub. authoritate & exîstimatione excellebant: ita hodie fieri solet, vt vbiq; gentium inuisa & contempta sit doctrina Christi apud eos, qui in aliquo sunt pretio, abijs autem solis ametur & colatur, quorum nulla est in mundo authoritas. Id verò nos adeo non offendere debet, vt potius in fide confirmari debeamus. Ex eo enim apparet, religionem & doctrinam Christianam non ex hominibus, sed ex Deo esse, nec humana, sed diuina authoritate niti. Verè ergo a Christo dictum est olim, Cælum & terra præteribunt, ex verbis autem meis non cadet iota vel apex.
units.tr: As to the first point, the chief priests are named, and among them Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, as was said elsewhere. And whenever mention is made of the many who were high priests or chief priests, the impiety and audacity of the Jews is noted, for they appointed several against God's Law, when there ought to have been only one, who would represent the person of Christ, who is priest of his Church forever and has neither successor nor vicar to discharge his office. Under the name of priests the scribes too are counted, who were interpreters of the Law. To these were added the elders, that is, the civil men who administered the Jewish commonwealth as far as the Romans allowed them. The Romans, having long since stripped them of their liberty, would not let them live under their own law, except that in sacred matters and religion they granted them some [αὐτονομίαν] self-government. This had to last until the time of Christ, in whom all the typical things were to be fulfilled; when these were fulfilled and abrogated, the Jewish commonwealth also came to an end. Mention of these men is made often, whenever Christ's adversaries are discussed, so that it may appear how unworthy his lot or condition was on earth. For just as once, when he came to his own, he was not received by them, but had as his most bitter enemies all who excelled in authority and esteem in Church and commonwealth, so today it commonly happens that everywhere among the nations the doctrine of Christ is hated and despised by those who hold some standing, and is loved and cultivated only by those who have no authority in the world. This ought not to offend us at all; rather we ought to be strengthened in faith. For from this it appears that the Christian religion and doctrine is not from men but from God, and rests not on human but on divine authority. Truly, then, it was said by Christ long ago: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but not one iota or stroke of my words will fall."

units.la: Quoad formam verò & ordinem fiue processum actionis, quem isti secuti sunt, merito reprehendi debent. Nam cum prius mortis sententiam aduersus illum decreuerint, nunc demum quarunt quo prætextu illum velint occidere. Præiudicio ergo agunt, quod eo iniquius est, quod cum rationibus iustis sedestitui videant falsa testimonia conquirunt, quibus iustum & innocentem opprimant. Et testes quidem falsos plures & varios aduersus Christum productos fuisse ex contextu historiæ Euangelicæ potest colligi. Nam dicitur quod etsi multi falsi testes fierentur, non inuenisse tamen præsides istos. Concilij, quod ipsis potuerit sufficere. Tam ergo absurda fuerunt illa testimonia, vt eorum ipsos puderet, neque saluo pudore illorum vel apud vulgus vel apud Præsidem Romanum possent meminisse. Tandem duo falsi testes prodeunt, qui illum dixisse aiunt: Possum dissoluere templum Dei, & triduo ipsum ædificare. Habet horum testimonium aliquam veritatis aut probabilitatis speciem. Nam tale quid Christum dixisse, apud Ioannem legitur. Cum Ioan. 2. enim peterent Iudæi, vt signo aliquo probaret, se diuina authoritate facere quæ faciebat, respondit: Destruite templum hoc, & tribus diebus excitabo illud. Id verò falsum testimonium fuisse, Matthæus scribit, & ipsos falsos testes vocat. Et tales fuisse constat, si rem propius inspicias, & verba diligenter cum verbis conferas. Tunc enim multiplex falsitas deprehenditur. Primum
units.tr: As to the form and order, or process, of the action which they followed, they deserve to be rightly blamed. For since they first decreed a sentence of death against him, only then do they seek what pretext they may use to kill him. They therefore act by prejudgment, which is all the more unjust since, seeing they cannot sit in judgment on just grounds, they seek out false testimonies with which to crush the just and innocent man. That many false witnesses of various kinds were produced against Christ can be gathered from the context of the Gospel history. For it is said that although many false witnesses came forward, those presidents of the council did not find anything that could suffice for them. Those testimonies were so absurd that the witnesses themselves were ashamed, and without losing face they could not repeat them either before the people or before the Roman governor. At last two false witnesses come forward, who say that he said: "I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days." This testimony has some appearance of truth or plausibility, for we read in John that Christ said something of the kind. When in John 2 the Jews asked him to prove by some sign that he did these things by divine authority, he answered: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up." Matthew writes that this was a false testimony and calls these men false witnesses. And that they were such is clear if you look at the matter more closely and carefully compare the words with the words. For then the manifold falsity is detected. First,

units.la: {y} 1 4 enim quod Christus de templo corporis sui dixit, isti de templo externo, quod lapidibus & alia materia conflabat, exponunt. Non potuit ergo verumq; quod dicebatur, verum esse. Deinde non de seipso locutus erat Dominus, quod ipse vel posset, vel velit templum destruere, sed quid ipsi fasuri sint, praedixerat, Sηλίκως dicens: Destruite templum HOC, quasi diceret: Quandoquidem ita vobis animus est, ut me occidere omnino statuerint, agite facite ut lubet, quod & fasuri estis, destruite hanc corporis mei fabricam, id est, occidite me: sed nihil proficietis: quia ex mortuis resurgam. Praeterea in hoc etiam postremo membro, nō dixerat, ut isti testes: Pojjum triduo aedificare templū: sed excitabo illud. Itaq; multifaria est falsitas in verbis, etiamsi de sensu alieno nihil dicatur, quem illi verbis Christi affingunt, ut impie dictum esse euincant: quod etsi ita dixisset, ut ipsi interpretabantur, non tamen impium, sed temerarium modo & insolens nimium videri poterat. Et non aliter illud tunc Iudaei interpretati sunt, quibus satis visum est respondisse: Quadraginta & sex annis aedificatum est templum istud, & tu tribus diebus illud erigesf? At hic in alium sensum detorquent isti & Caiaphas cum suis Concilij assessoribus, ut Christi templi & cultus extermini hostem esse euincant, qui ruinam & excidium illi interminatus sit: quo crimine postea Stephanum quoq; accusatum fuisse in Actu legimus.
units.tr: what Christ said of the temple of his body, they explain as referring to the external temple, which was built of stone and other material. So what they reported could not be true. Next, the Lord had not spoken of himself, that he himself could or would destroy the temple, but had foretold what they themselves would do, saying "Destroy THIS temple," as if he said: "Since you have so resolved that you will altogether kill me, go on and do as you please, for you will destroy this fabric of my body, that is, kill me; but you will accomplish nothing, because I shall rise from the dead." Moreover, in this last clause also he did not say, as those witnesses did, "I can build the temple in three days," but "I will raise it up." Thus the falsity is manifold in the words, even leaving aside the alien meaning which they attach to Christ's words in order to prove that he spoke impiously. For even if he had spoken as they interpreted him, it could seem not impious but merely rash and unusually insolent. Nor did the Jews then understand it otherwise, for it seemed enough to them to reply: "This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?" But these men, together with Caiaphas and his assessors on the council, twist it into another sense, so that they may prove him an enemy of Christ's temple and worship, one who threatened its ruin and destruction. Stephen too was later accused of this crime, as we read in Acts.

units.la: Hoc ergo exemplo docemur, quia nam falsi testes censeri debeant. Est hæc doctrina observatu digna & necessaria. Nam testium vsus ab ipso Deo institutus & confirmatus est, qui in Lege pronunciauit: In ore duorum aut trium testium stabit omne verbum. Idque vero graviter praecipit, ne vnius testis sermo iudicibus sufficiens esse putetur, & testem falsum talionis lege punire iussit. Solomon vero Deum odisse ait, testem mendacem: & ideo certe periturum, qui hoc scelere se polluerit. Ideo multa cura & diligentia opus est magistratibus, ne quosfuis temere ad testimonium in iudicio dicendum admittant: nec leue peccatum est, si iusiurandum, quo testes vulgo obstringi solent, hominibus nullius fidei credatur, quibus nemo facile pecuniam vilem crederet. Qui vero jiftuntur ad dicendum testimonium, ijs quae viderunt, & probe nouerunt bona fide insistant, vt nihil affingant, nihil taceant in alicuius gratiam: neue aliquid in sensum alienum detorqueant.
units.tr: From this example we are taught who ought to be counted false witnesses. This doctrine is worth observing and necessary. For the use of witnesses was instituted and confirmed by God himself, who pronounced in the Law: "On the word of two or three witnesses every matter shall stand." He also commanded this in earnest, that the word of a single witness should not be thought sufficient for judges, and he ordered that a false witness be punished under the law of retaliation. Solomon says that God hates a lying witness, and so surely he who has polluted himself with this crime will perish. Magistrates therefore need great care and diligence, lest they rashly admit whomever they please to give testimony in court. Nor is it a small sin if an oath, by which witnesses are commonly bound, is trusted to men of no good faith, men to whom no one would readily entrust even a paltry sum of money. Those who are summoned to give testimony should keep to what they have seen and know well, in good faith, so that they add nothing, pass over nothing for anyone's favour, and twist nothing into an alien sense.

units.la: Vt vero in praesenti typus Antichristiani Concilij proponitur, in quo praesident, qui vt ipsi rei sisterentur, iam pridem mernerant, & praeiudicio veritas damnata est, & nunc falsos testes sistunt, qui hos & omnem iniustitiam procul arcere debebant: Ita scimus eandem hodie adhuc veritatis Euangelicae, & eorum fortem esse, qui hanc profitentur & praedicant. Fere enim fit, vt in causis, quae ad religionem & Ecclesiam spectant iudices sint, qui religionem omnem oderunt, & indigni sunt qui postremum Ecclesiae locum habeant. Hi deinde praeiudicijs suis excaecati, falsis criminibus innocentes grauant, calumniis impudentissimorum hominum aures praebent patulas. Imo fit interdum, ut viris pijs & bonis non tutum sit veritati testimonium ferre, nisi viros principes & iudices offendere, & periculum aliquod sibi accersere velint. Sed tunc Christum imitemur, qui tacuisse dicitur, etiamsi a Pontifice maximo ad respondendum prouocaretur. Nihil enim pro fecisset loquendo aduersus iuratos Dei & veritatis hostes. Deinde tam absurda emnt & putida illorum calumnia, ut nullam consolationem mererentur. Adhaec iam aduenerat hora sua, qua ipsum mortem subire, & seipsum pro mundi vita tradere debebat. Ita nos si quando infimili angustia nos constitutos videmus, taciti rem omnem Deo committamus, qui animi nostri recessus & cogitationes nouit. Et si vero nunc iniuria nobis atrox fiat, & nominis quoq; nostri fama periclitetur, erit tamen aliquando dies, in quo arcana cordium reuelabuntur, & qua suorum memoriam Deus afferet.
units.tr: Now, as the type of the Antichristian council is set before us in this passage, in which those preside who had long since deserved to be brought to trial themselves, and in which the truth has been condemned in advance by prejudice, and false witnesses are now produced, when these men and every injustice ought to have been kept far away: so we know that the same lot still befalls the Gospel truth today, and those who profess and preach it. For it generally happens that, in cases which concern religion and the Church, there are judges who hate all religion and are unworthy to hold even the lowest place in the Church. Then these men, blinded by their prejudices, burden the innocent with false charges and lend open ears to the calumnies of the most shameless men. Indeed it sometimes happens that it is not safe for pious and good men to bear witness to the truth, unless they are willing to offend the princes and judges and bring some danger upon themselves. But then let us imitate Christ, who is said to have kept silent even when he was challenged by the High Priest to answer. For he would have gained nothing by speaking against those sworn enemies of God and of the truth. Moreover, their calumnies were so absurd and foolish that they deserved no answer. Besides, his hour had already come, the hour in which he had to undergo death and give himself up for the life of the world. So too, if we ever see ourselves placed in a similar distress, let us silently commit the whole matter to God, who knows the secret recesses and thoughts of our minds. And even if now a grievous wrong is done to us, and the reputation of our name is endangered, there will nevertheless come a day in which the secrets of hearts will be revealed, and God will restore the memory of his people.

units.la: Sed quia falsis testibus nihil profici videt Caiaphas, maiori gravitate opus esse arbitratur, & e solio surgens, & ad artes conuersus, ex ipsius Christi ore aliquid elicere conatur, ex quo eius damnandi occasionem inueniat. Nam cum Pontificali authoritate ait illi: Adiuro te per Deum viuentem, ut dicas nobis, an tu fis Christus ille Filius Dei? Duo quaerit, quorum vtrumq; impijs calumniatoribus yberrimam materiam calumniarum suppeditare poterat. Primum an sit Christus, id est, ynctus ille Dei, promissus populi Seruator, Rex & Sacerdos tot seculis a Patribus expectatus. Alterū, num sit Dei Filius? vt in Christi etiam nomine nouam habeat caullandi ansam.
units.tr: But since Caiaphas sees that nothing is gained by false witnesses, he judges that greater seriousness is needed; rising from his throne and turning to craft, he tries to elicit something from the very mouth of Christ, by which he may find an occasion to condemn him. For with pontifical authority he says to him: "I adjure you by the living God, tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God." He asks two things, either of which could supply the impious calumniators with a most abundant matter for slander. First, whether he is the Christ, that is, the anointed one of God, the promised Saviour of the people, the King and Priest awaited by the Fathers through so many ages. Second, whether he is the Son of God, so that they might also have an opening for accusation in the very name of Christ.

units.la: Qui falsi testes censeri debeant. Deut. 17. 19. Pro. 6. 19. fam. Scimus enim Sacerdotes & Scribas Iudæorum tunc temporis cognitionem Messiæ multis figmentis & opinionibus crassissimis & carnalibus obscurauisse. Nam ita sentiebant Dauidis filium, vt vix aliquid sublimius & homine maius de illo sentirent, Dei Filium certe prorsus ignorabant. Fuit autem captiosa plane hæc adiuratio & quæstio. Si enim affirmat Christus, habent quod quærunt, & ille captus tenetur. Sin negat de multis accusare possunt, quæ prater officium ex priuata temeritate fecerit. Sin taceat, iam non Pontificalis modo dignitatis, verumetiam diuini nominis prophanus contemptor dicetur. Tanta est hypocritarum astutia, tanta impietas & audacia, vt subDei nomine sanctis imponere norint, neque illo impie abuti vereantur, & hoc sciant, nunquam impune fieri.
units.tr: Who ought to be counted false witnesses. Deut. 17. 19. Prov. 6. 19. For we know that the priests and scribes of the Jews at that time had obscured the knowledge of the Messiah with many fictions and very gross and carnal opinions. For they so thought of David's son that they hardly conceived anything more sublime and greater than a man concerning him; the Son of God they utterly did not know. This adjuration and question was, moreover, plainly captious. For if Christ affirmed it, they had what they were seeking, and he would be seized and held guilty. But if he denied it, they could accuse him of many things, namely that he had acted from private rashness beyond his office. If he kept silent, he would be called not only a profane despiser of pontifical dignity but also of the divine name. So great is the cunning of hypocrites, so great their impiety and audacity, that they know how to impose on the saints under the name of God, and do not hesitate to abuse it impiously, yet they know that this is never done with impunity.

units.la: Quid vero Christus? Veritatem neque negat aperte, neque turpiter dissimulat, sed simpliciter respondet, Tu dixisti: vt offendat, tam certo constare, ipsum esse promissum Dei Filium & seruatorem, vt ne ipsi quidem negare possint, sed tunc aperte fateantur, quando negare volunt. Sed quia vili assumpta humanitatis specie illos offendi sciebat, ad futuram gloriam illos remittit, adeoque ad suum tribunal citat, addens: Quin etiam dico vobis, ab hoc tempore videbitis Filium hominis sedentem ad dexteram potentiæ Dei, & venientem in nubibus cœli. Quasi diceret: Iam coram vobis stoo reus, & mea vita ac mortis arbitrium penes vos esse videtur; sed rerum vicissitudo erit. Sum enim is, quem Pater sibi a dextris considere iussit, & quem Daniel in nubibus cœli ad iudicium venire vider. Tunc ipsi meo iudicio sistemini, vt pœnas vestræ impietatis feratis. Haec tenus ergo non ignauo metu deuictus causa sua defuit Dominus, sed vt Patri obediret, tacuit: docet autem suo exemplo, quid fieri debeat cum apertis & incurabilibus fidei veræ aduersariis. Liberaliter & syncera veritatis confessio & scripturarum testimoniis, quoad eius fieri potest, confirmata. Admoneantur item graviter, vt sibi cum Deo iudice rem esse sciant, &ferocire desinant.
units.tr: But what did Christ do? He neither openly denies the truth nor shamefully dissembles it, but simply answers: "You have said it." Thus, so that he might offend them, he affirms with such certainty that he is the promised Son of God and Saviour that they themselves cannot deny it, but then they openly confess it precisely when they wish to deny it. But since he knew that they would be offended by the humble appearance of the assumed humanity, he refers them to future glory, and thus summons them to his own tribunal, adding: "Moreover I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of the power of God, and coming in the clouds of heaven." As if he were saying: "Now I stand before you as a defendant, and it seems that my life and death lie in your hands; but there will be a change of circumstances. For I am the one whom the Father has bidden sit at his right hand, and whom Daniel saw coming in the clouds of heaven to judgment. Then you yourselves will be brought before my judgment, so that you may bear the penalties of your impiety." Thus the Lord, not overcome by any cowardly fear, did not fail his own cause, but kept silent in order to obey the Father. He teaches, moreover, by his own example what ought to be done with open and incurable adversaries of the true faith: a frank and sincere confession of the truth, confirmed by testimonies of Scripture as far as that is possible. Let them also be solemnly warned that they have to do with God as judge, and let them cease to be fierce.

units.la: At non monuit hæc Caiapham hypocritam, qui audito Christo, diffrupit vestes & illum blasphemiæ dam iat. fe vero blasphemiæ omnis, qua hominis mortales diuinos honores sibi arrogant, impatientissimum esse simulat. Factum eius reliqui sequuntur, & mortis reum esse confusis moribus testantur. Ita vero Christus propter veritatis confessionem impietatis extremæ damnatur, quasi templum Dei destruere voluerit, & diuinitatem improbe affectarit: vt nimirum nostram culpam expiet, qui corpora nostra, quæ Deo consecrata templa sunt, quotidie prophanamus & aduersus Deum peccando nos illi præferimus. Vtinam vero Caiaphæ exemplum diligentius expenderent, qui hodie Pontificum & multorum aliorum blasphemias, quibus Dei gloriam sibi vendicant, non modo patienter ferunt, verumetiam defendunt & propugnant, suæ fidei denique creditos illis subscribere armis cogunt. Sentient illi aliquando Dei Filium fœuerissimum suæ maiestatis vindicem.
units.tr: But this did not admonish Caiaphas the hypocrite, who, having heard Christ, tore his garments and condemned him for blasphemy. Yet he pretends to be most impatient of every blasphemy by which mortals arrogate divine honours to themselves. His companions followed his deed, and by their confused conduct they testified that he was guilty of death. And so Christ, on account of his confession of the truth, is condemned for the utmost impiety, as if he had wished to destroy the temple of God and wickedly claimed divinity; surely in order to expiate our fault, we who daily profane our bodies, which are temples consecrated to God, and by sinning against God prefer ourselves to him. Would that they weighed more carefully the example of Caiaphas, those who today not only patiently endure the blasphemies of the Pontiffs and of many others, by which they claim God's glory for themselves, but even defend and champion them, and finally compel those entrusted to their faith to subscribe to them with weapons. Some day they will feel that the Son of God is the most fierce avenger of his majesty.

units.la: Ac non quieuit hypocritarum furor, etsi Christum solenniter damnatum, & post paucas horas crudeli supplicio moriturum nescierunt, sed volunt, vt a ferus quos sui similes habebant, indignissime & iniquissime tractetur. Hi enim in faciem eius insputant, colaphos item illi infringunt, eandem bacillis cædunt, quod maximæ contumeliæ signum erat antiquitus. Et quia maiori igno-miniæ ergo faciem eius primus velauerunt, ne videri posset a quo feriretur, per ludibrium interrogant: Vaticinare nobis Christe, quis sit, qui te percussit. Quia illum sciebant populo magni Prophetæ loco habitum fuisse, hoc scurrili contemptu populi de Christo iudicium damnant. Et hoc est, quod se passurum esse olim per Isaiam prædixerat: Corpus meum præbui percutientibus, & genas meas vellicantibus: faciem meam non abscondi a contumeliis & sputo. In his vero cogitemus, hæc omnia propter nos facta esse: & licet generosis animis contumeliæ eiusmodi intolerabiles videantur, nos tamen, si quid huius nobis accidat, non offendamur: Ita enim nobis parata est facies Dei, in qua est satietas gaudiorum, quæ olim cum CHRISTO IESV fruemur.
units.tr: Nor did the fury of the hypocrites rest, although they did not know that Christ, solemnly condemned and destined to die a cruel death within a few hours, was to be treated most unworthily and most unjustly by the ferocious men whom they had as like themselves. For they spit in his face, also strike him with their fists, and beat him with staves, which was a sign of the greatest insult in antiquity. And because they had covered his face for greater disgrace, so that he could not see by whom he was struck, they mockingly ask him: "Prophesy to us, Christ, who is it that struck you." Because they knew that he had been regarded by the people as a great prophet, they pass their judgment on Christ with this scurrilous contempt. And this is what he had foretold long before through Isaiah that he would suffer: "I offered my body to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who plucked at them; I did not hide my face from insults and spittle." Let us consider in these things that all these were done on account of us; and although such insults seem intolerable to generous minds, let us not be offended if anything of this kind happens to us. For thus the face of God is prepared for us, in which is the fullness of joys, which we shall one day enjoy with Christ Jesus.

units.la: HOMILIA CCCI.
units.tr: HOMILY CCCI.

units.la: Petrus autem sedebat extra in aula: & accessit ad eum quaedam ancillula, dicens: Et tu cum IESV Galilaeo eras. Ipse vero negauit coram omnibus, dicens: Nescio quid dicas. Eum autem egredientem in vestibulum vidit alia ancilla, & dixit iis qui erant illic: Et iste erat cum Iesu Nazareno. Tunc rursus negauit cum iureiurando: Non noui hominem. Paulo post autem accesserunt qui astabant, & dixerunt Petro, Vere & tu ex ipsis es: nam & loquutio tua te manifesta facit. Tunc coepit seipsum detestari & iurare, dicens: Non noui hominem. Et statim gallus misit vocem. Tunc meminit Petrus verborum Iesu, qui dixerat ei, Priusquam gallus vocem mittat, ter me abnegabis. Et egressus extra, fleuit amare.
units.tr: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came to him and said, "You also were with Jesus the Galilean." But he denied it before them all, saying, "I do not know what you are talking about." When he had gone out into the porch, another servant girl saw him and said to those who were there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth." Again he denied it, with an oath: "I do not know the man." A little later those who stood by came up and said to Peter, "Surely you also are one of them, for your speech betrays you." Then he began to curse and swear, saying, "I do not know the man." And immediately the cock crowed. Then Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said to him, "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times." And going out, he wept bitterly.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus non solum egregia sanctorum facta, verum etiam eorundem vitia & lapsus narrat, non ut eorum existimationi aliquid detrahat, sed ut Scripturarum veritas confirmetur, & quod eiusmodi exempla plurimum faciunt ad nostram institutionem. Primo enim nostra nos infirmitatis admonent, ut eo diligentius vigilemus. Deinde solantur aduersus conscientiae tentationes, ne quando lapsi desperemus, sed meminerimus nobis non aliud accidisse, quam quod olim sanctis quibusdam passis fuit, quos Deus in gratiam recepit. Adhaec paenitentiae vere exempla & formulas traduunt, quas tuto sequamur. Docent item nos nulli hominum fidere debere, nec quemquam in tanta affirmatione habere, quasi errare aut labi non possit. In multis enim labimur omnes & omnis homo mendax est: & ideo maledictus & infelix est, qui fidit homini, & facit carnem brachium suum. In solo CHRISTO IESV est veritas, & idem fundamentum est Prophetarum & Apostolorum, quod tuto niti possunt, quicunque seruari volunt. Haec omnia cum in Petri lapsu habeantur, qui Christum turpiter abnegauit, illum dignum iudicauit Spiritus sanctus, qui ab Euangelistis omnibus diligenter describeretur. Vt vero nobis melius seruiant in institutioni quae hic acciderunt abnegationes singulas sic videre oportet, & singularum occasiones probe expendamus.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit relates not only the outstanding deeds of the saints but also their faults and falls. He does this not to diminish their reputation, but so that the truth of the Scriptures may be confirmed, and because such examples greatly serve our instruction. First, they remind us of our own weakness, so that we may watch all the more carefully. Second, they console us against the temptations of conscience, so that when we fall we do not despair, but remember that nothing has happened to us other than what once happened to certain saints who fell, and whom God received back into favour. Moreover, they set forth true examples and patterns of repentance, which we may safely follow. They also teach us that we must trust no one, nor place such confidence in anyone as if he could not err or fall. For we all stumble in many things, and every man is a liar; therefore cursed and unhappy is he who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm. In Jesus Christ alone is truth, and this is the one foundation of the Prophets and Apostles, on which all who wish to be saved may safely rest. Since all these things are found in Peter's fall, when he shamefully denied Christ, the Holy Spirit judged him worthy to be described carefully by all the Evangelists. So that these denials may serve us better for instruction, we ought to look at each one in this way and weigh carefully the occasion of each.

units.la: Primum autem & occasio omnis malifuit (vt nuper annotauimus) quod Petrus grauissimarum admonitionum Christi immemor, hunc cum abducerentur, a longe secutus, & atrium quoque Pontificis ingressus, cum eius seruis consedit, vt rei finem videret. Hic mox alia atque alia occasiones inciderunt, ex quibus subinde in deterius prolapsus est. Etenim adhuc extra in aula sedentem accedit ancilla ostiaria (vt Ioannes illam dicit) & illum compellans ait: Et tu cum IESV Galilaeo eras. Nec acerbius de eo altera loquitur, quae astantibus dixit: Et iste erat cum IESV Nazareno. Fuit haec leuicula ad tam graue scelus occasio. Nam si personam ancillarum spectes, ridiculum fuit tantum Apostolum ad vocem mulieris perterrefieri. Deinde verba quoque nihil minarum aut terrificum sonabant. Nam etsi cum Iesu illum fuisse dicerent, nihil tamen periculi ex eo timeret. Fuerant enim hactenus multi omnis loci & ordinis viri & mulieres cum Christo, quibus omnibus nihil mali ex eius consortio acciderat. Cur ergo sibi metuerat Petrus, qui paulo ante ad montem Oliveti pugnans tutus ex medijs hostibus euaserat? Sed ita solet carnalis confidentia in tutissimum metum degenerare, si primum conatum successu carere videat: id eo magis fit, si carnem in consilium adhibeamus: quod hic Petrum fecisse videmus. Nam prima ancilla ita respondet, vt illi suffugia quaesiuisse constet. Vult enim rei huius ignarus videri, cum dicit: Nescio quid dicas. Ebo nescis iam Petre quid sit IESVS hic Galilaeus? Nescis eum esse de quo nondum prius dixerat, Verba vitae aeternae habes: & nos credimus & nouimus te esse Christum illum Filium Dei viuentis? Nunc vero nunc te pudet eius, quem pauperis & miseri piscatoris non puduit? Et quae alia causa reipublicae tam ambigui potest adduci. Sed nihil proficit sic respondendo. Tu quidem sic eludere vis ancillulam, ne Christum libere confitendo in periculum venias, nec tamen eum negasse dicaris: sed audi Spiritum sanctum de tuo facto pronuntiantem: Ipse vero negauit coram omnibus dihuc dicens: Nescio quid dicas. Ergo Christum negauit, non coram muliercula vili & ancillula obscura, sed coram omnibus, ijs nimirum quõ, quorum fauorem tibi demerendum esse putauisti, &c. Debet hinc dogma generale peti, Christum non modo disertis verbis, verum nescio an dissimulatione abnegari: Huius vero quasi mater est carnis prudentia, quae ut causam fidei, ceu nihil ad nos pertinentem a nobis reijciamus iubet. Quod hodie tam vulgare est, ut multi suum nam in pruden tia laudem in eo quaerant, si quando de fide interrogentur. Sed illis ferae illud Domini: Quicunque puduerit mei ac meorum sermonum in gente ista adultera & peccatrice, eius pudebit etiam Filium hominis, quando venerit in gloria Patris sui cum angelis sanctis. Nam solet alia quoque consilia suggerere carnis ratio, si senes in consilium adhibeatur: quod Matthaeus de altera quoque ancilla dicturus non obscure docet. Nam in Petrum in vestibulo exiisse scribit: nimirum ut peccandi occasiones, quas caeperat sentire, declinaret. Videbat enim sibi non tutum fore in Pontificis domo versari. Sed cum ut ex incendio deberet subito exilire, eiusmodi secessionem vult facere, quae ipsum non suspectum faciat, nec novi periculi causa sit. Paulatim ergo & quasi aliud agens vult se subducere. Sed hic quoque adeo nihil profecit, ut iam diserte Christum abnegaret, cuius illum caeperat pudere. Nam cum iureiurando dicit, Non novi hominem. Itaque in non modo ignavus fidei dissimulator, sed palam mendax, sed periurus est. Et hi confidentia & prudentia carnis fructus sunt, quibus fere regi solent, qui principum huius saeculi & praefulam Antichristianorum aulas sequi solent, ut inter horum satellites calefiant, id est, lucrum faciant.
