units.tr: First, he takes the occasion of freeing and releasing Christ from the old custom, which was that at the Passover feast one of the prisoners was released for the people's favour. This custom seems to have crept in by stealth [κλεῖαν], by which they wished to imitate, in superstition, the example of God, who at that time long ago had delivered the fathers out of Egypt and the harsh tyranny of Pharaoh. Here they ought at the same time to have remembered that at that same time the law was given, by which God claims men wholly for his own service, and commands that evildoers be punished and killed. It was therefore wrong that they established some worship of God in the release of criminals. Flesh's reason is wont to be seditious, when in divine matters it wishes to be wise from itself. And the Romans seem to have left this custom to them so that they might use the people, who were more inclined to sedition, as more compliant. But now Pilate seeks from this an occasion which he could have used well, if, armed with the fear of God, he had been eager to please God rather than men. For since Barabbas, notoriously wicked (for he had done these same things in a sedition that had recently broken out), was held among the captives, he compared him with Jesus and gave the people a free choice of whom they wished. He did not think that they would be so wicked or so foolish as to prefer the most worthless of men to a holy and innocent man, indeed to so great a benefactor. But he could have used this occasion vigorously, and admonished the people, or even compelled them by his authority, that they should not abuse the custom granted to them by favour for seditions and for protecting the authors of them. Or what necessity compelled him to class Jesus, whom he knew to be innocent, among the criminals? But since he had once begun to go astray, he partly wishes to obtain from the people, imprudently, what was in his own power, and partly he subjects to the unjust judgment of the people the man whom he himself, by his office, ought to have defended. It was altogether shameful that, having recently forgotten the majesty of the Roman empire, he sent Christ to Herod. But it is more shameful that he now compares the same man with a robber and a seditious person, whose innocence he had understood was commended by Herod's testimony. Certainly the Evangelist, in order to make Pilate's guilt graver, teaches that Pilate was convicted by the testimony of his own conscience. For he knew (he says) that they had handed him over out of envy.

units.la: Sed accedit aliud, quo illius scelus magis amplificatur, & illum non modo imprudentè & iniustum, sed contumacem quoq; & incurabilem fuisse docetur. Nam sedente eo pro tribunali, misit ad eum vxor eius, & monuit, ne se actionis huius iniquissimæ aduersus iustum hunc institutæ partici-pe faceret. Et rationem adduxit, quam homo Ethnicus non poterat contemnere, quod propter il-lum noctem insomnijs tristibus sibi infaustam senserit. Fuit hæc admonitio non pia modo, sed gra-uis admodum, quæ merito pondus habere debuit. Adhibet enim eam vxor, quam illi charam fuisse vel ex præsentis historia poterit colligi. Et quis putet, matronam prudentem & cordatam absque graui-bus causis tale quid voluisse nuntiare marito pro tribunali sedenti inter iudices in publico foro. Deinde non potuit Pilatus hoc putare superstitiosæ mulierculæ delirium esse, cum somniasi-bi infesta fuisse diceret, quæ gentes diuinitus submitti vulgò crediderunt, & Christum iustū voca-ret, qualem Pilatus propriæ conscientiæ testimonio conuictus agnoscebat. Est hoc luculentum bonitatis Dei argumentum, qui homines vult saluos fieri, & in veritatis cognitionem venire. Id-circo plerunq;, in tempore admonet, & per eos, quorum fides non poterit temere contemni. Fiunt huius generis multa quotidie, & simul exemplo hoc vxores omnes officij admonentur, vt maritos placare studeant, si quando illis peccandi occasiones vident obijci. Nisi enim id faciant, sæpe tam his quàm sibi ipsis & toti familiæ malum & exitium accersunt: quod olim Iezabelem, Saram Ha-ni vxorem, Herodiadem & alias similes fecisse legimus. Interim communi omnium institutio ut hoc exemplum seruiat, ne pias admonitiones propter authorē vilem aut obscurum contemnat.
units.tr: But there is added something else by which his crime is further magnified, and he is shown to have been not only imprudent and unjust, but also obstinate and incurable. For while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him and warned him not to make himself a partner in this most unjust action taken against this righteous man. And she gave a reason which a heathen man could not despise: that because of him she had felt a night of sad dreams, unlucky for herself. This admonition was not only pious but very weighty, and it ought rightly to have carried weight. For the admonition came from his wife, whom it can be gathered even from the present history was dear to him. And who would think that a prudent and sensible matron would wish to announce such a thing to her husband, sitting as judge in public before the court, without serious causes? Then Pilate could not think this the delirium of a superstitious little woman, since she said that she had been troubled in dreams, which people commonly believed were sent by God to subdue the nations, and since she called him righteous, as Pilate, convicted by the testimony of his own conscience, acknowledged him to be. This is a striking proof of the goodness of God, who wishes men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Therefore he often admonishes in time, and through those whose faith cannot be rashly despised. Many things of this kind happen every day, and at the same time from this example all wives are admonished of their duty, that they should strive to please their husbands, if ever they see occasions of sin being thrown in their way. For unless they do this, they often bring ruin and destruction upon their husbands, themselves and the whole family alike, as we read that Jezebel, Sarah the wife of Haman, Herodias and others like them did long ago. Meanwhile the common teaching of all is that this example should serve, so that no one should despise pious admonitions because of an author who is base or obscure.

units.la: 1.Tim.2. 1.Reg.19. Heist.5. Mar.6. 1.Reg.§. Naamano militiæ Syrorum præfecto puellula captiua & serua salutare consilium suggesserit, & cum hoc confirmantibus aliis seruis ille obsequeretur, a lepra purgatus est. Et vt proverbio dicitur, holitor sibi opportuna locutus est. Pilatus certe si uxoris consilio attendisset, animæ confuisset, ne tam infando scelere aduersus Dei Filium commisso se pollueret.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 2. 1 Kings 19. Esth. 5. Mark 6. 2 Kings 5. A little servant girl, a captive and a slave, suggested a salutary counsel to Naaman, commander of the army of the Syrians, and when he followed this, with other servants confirming it, he was cleansed of his leprosy. And as the proverb says, the gardener spoke at the right moment. Pilate certainly, had he heeded his wife's counsel, would have saved his soul, and would not have polluted himself with so impious a crime committed against the Son of God.

units.la: Sed prophanus homo & religionis omnis contemptor suæ rationis consilijs indulgens, dum mundo potius quam Deo placere studet, in instituto pergens, populum furiosum denuo compellat, dicens: Utrum e duobus illis vultis vt vobis dimittam? Illi vero a principibus sacerdotum persuasi, Barabbam sibi donari petunt: quo exemplo docemur, quantum mali dent falsi antistites, qui religionem sibi quæstum fecerunt, & de eo retinendo cogitant. Hic certe authores sunt sceleris populo Iudaico, quod toti genti excidium peperit. Quid ergo hodie fiat, quando vulgus & viri principes eos audiunt, qui tam in Republica quam Ecclesia priuato commodo omnia metiuntur. Pilatum certe inexpectato populi rephonso obstupuisse credibile est. Ideo vt eos aliquo modo in viam revocaret, quæstionem de Christo repetit. Quid igitur faciam de Iesu, qui dicitur Christus? Quasi diceret: Non de Barabba solum quæstio est, quem quia vobis dari vultis, non erit in me mora. Nolim enim quicquam facere quod vestris priuilegijs aut consuetudinibus fit aduersum. Sed maior quæstio & gravior restat, quid de Iesu fiat: quem hactenus vulgo Christum siue vnctum dixitis, quique se seruatorem esse beneficijs & miraculosis operibus publice declarauit? Quid vero opus erat hanc quæstionem mouere? Etenim licet Barabbam dimitti vellent Iudæi, tamen propterea minime necesse erat Christum occidi: nec propterea Iudæos aduersus hunc iudices constituit oportuit. Pilatus ergo etsi nihil aliud fecisset, quam quod hic fecit, sanguinis & mortis Christi reus fuit.
units.tr: But the profane man, a despiser of all religion who indulges the counsels of his own reason, while he is eager to please the world rather than God, persists in his course and once more addresses the raging people, saying: "Which of these two do you want me to release to you?" They, persuaded by the chief priests, ask that Barabbas be granted to them. By this example we are taught how much harm false prelates do, those who have made religion a source of gain and think about keeping it so. These men were certainly the authors of the crime against the Jewish people, which brought ruin upon the whole nation. What, then, happens today, when the common people and the men in authority listen to those who measure everything, in the commonwealth as in the Church, by private advantage? It is certainly credible that Pilate was astonished at the unexpected answer of the people. So, in order to bring them back to the right course in some way, he repeats the question about Christ: "What then shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?" As if he were saying: the question is not only about Barabbas, whom you want released to you, and in that I will not delay. For I would not wish to do anything that is contrary to your privileges or customs. But a greater and more serious question remains: what is to be done about Jesus, whom until now you have called the Christ, that is, the Anointed, and who has publicly declared himself the Saviour by his benefits and miraculous works? Indeed, why was there any need to raise this question? For even though the Jews wished Barabbas to be released, it was by no means necessary that Christ be put to death, nor was it necessary that Pilate set up the Jews as judges against him. Therefore Pilate, even if he had done nothing else than what he did here, would have been guilty of the blood and death of Christ.

units.la: Nam hac occasione populus clamat, Crucifigatur. Reclamat quidem præses: Enimuero quid mali fecit? Sed nequicquam iste mouet eos, qui cum sacerdotibus impijs coniurarunt: nec enim pudet ad dirum crucis supplicium eum postulare, quem de nullo maleficio accusare possunt. Et hoc tanta importunitate faciunt, vt res ad seditionem & tumultum spectare videatur. Nam vt Ioannes scribit, cum Pilatus aliquo modo se illis opponeret, nō absq; commINATIONE grauis specie clamant: Si hunc absoluueris, non es amicus Cæsaris. Quo loco non tam ingratitudo quam crudelitas Iudæorum observari debet, vt videas, quid speres de ijs, qui Antichristianis præsulibus gratificari cupiunt. Tantus enim spiritus Antichristiani furor est: vt nullis rationibus curari possit, imo qui hoc agitantur, ne politicorum quidem virorum, quos sibi magistratus datos esse agnoscunt consilijs acquiescunt. Hæc enim faciunt, qui non itaque clamarunt: Hosanna, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Non ergo iniustis modo, sed seditiosis quoq; clamoribus eorum opprimitur Christus, pro quorum salute se totum impendere cupiebat. Et qui nos miseros in cœlos euehere voluit, eò vsq; deprimitur, vt nullius inter viros bonos locus sit, sed latroni & seditioso postponatur. Ne ergo miremur aut offendamur, si quid huius hodie fiat. Retinebit ingenium suum mundus, & vix quicquam tam vulgare est, quam quod seductores, scurras, scortas & scelera turpissima, mundus deniq; qui totus in malo iacet, Christo præferuntur.
units.tr: For on this occasion the people cry out, "Let him be crucified." The governor indeed objects: "Why, what evil has he done?" But he moves those who had conspired with the impious priests to no purpose: for they are not ashamed to demand for him the dreadful punishment of the cross, though they can accuse him of no crime. And they do this with such importunity that the matter seems to tend toward sedition and tumult. For, as John writes, when Pilate somewhat opposed them, they cried out with a not unthreatening tone: "If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend." At this point we should observe not so much the ingratitude as the cruelty of the Jews, so that you may see what you should hope from those who wish to curry favour with the Antichristian prelates. For such is the fury of the Antichristian spirit that it cannot be cured by any reasons; indeed, those who are driven by it do not yield even to the counsels of prudent men in public office, whom they acknowledge to have been set over them by the magistrate. For those who do these things did not cry out before: "Hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." Therefore Christ is oppressed not only by their unjust but also by their seditious outcries, for whose salvation he was willing to give himself wholly. And he who wished to raise us wretched men to heaven is cast down so far that he has no place among good men, but is placed behind a robber and a seditious man. Let us not, then, be astonished or offended if anything of this kind happens today. The world will keep its nature, and scarcely anything is so common as that seducers, buffoons, harlots and the most shameful crimes, and in short the world, which lies wholly in evil, are preferred to Christ.

units.la: Refert, quo ritu Christum præses damnarit. Accepta aqua publice coram omnibus abluit manus cum graui protestatione, qua huius sceleris culpam abs se remouere vult. Dicit enim: Innoxius ego sum a sanguine huius iusti: Vos videritis. Et admirabili Dei consilio factum est, vt ab eodem iudice prius absoluatur Christus quam damnetur: nimirum vt nos coram Deo absoluamur: ne quæ condemnatio ijs metuenda sit, qui ipsi per veram fidem sunt insiti. Et prodest hic obseruare quam multis testimonijs ad miraculum vsque Christi innocentia sit approbata. Primum Iudas ille perhibuit, dicens Sacerdotibus: Peccauì prodito innoxio sanguine. Secundum præses Pilatus, qui illo diligenter examinato, Iudæis dixit: Ego nullum inuenio crimen in eo. Tertium ipsius conscientia ei præbuit, vt sciret Iudæos illum per inuidiam tradidisse. Quartum Herodes tulit, & hoc quoq; Pilatus approbatum Iudæorum Sacerdotibus obiecit. Accessit quintum vxoris Pilati, quod & ipsum diuina authoritate confirmatur, quà Ethnici quoq; agnouerunt. Sequitur nunc aliud Pilati iam pro tribunali sedentis, qui publice & de innocentia eius testatur & culpa mortis eius ita abominatur et horret, vt tunc quoq; quando imperatoria maiestatis nomine ad iudicandum consedit.
units.tr: It is reported with what ceremony the governor condemned Christ. Taking water, he publicly washed his hands before everyone, with a solemn protestation by which he wishes to remove from himself the guilt of this crime. For he says: "I am innocent of the blood of this just man; see to it yourselves." And by the wonderful counsel of God it came about that Christ was acquitted by the same judge before he was condemned: plainly so that we might be acquitted before God, and that no condemnation should be feared by those who are themselves engrafted through true faith. It is useful here to observe how Christ's innocence was attested by so many testimonies, almost to the point of a miracle. First, that Judas himself bore witness, saying to the priests: "I have sinned in betraying innocent blood." Second, the governor Pilate, who, having examined him carefully, said to the Jews: "I find no crime in him." Third, his own conscience provided him with the knowledge that the Jews had handed him over out of envy. Fourth, Herod gave his testimony, and Pilate, too, having approved this, threw it in the face of the chief priests of the Jews. To these came a fifth, the wife of Pilate, which is confirmed by divine authority, and which even the heathen recognised. Now follows another testimony, that of Pilate himself, already seated on the judgment seat, who publicly bears witness to his innocence and so abhors and shudders at the guilt of his death that even then, when he sat down to judge in the name of the imperial majesty, he wished it to be held that he was innocent, and he confirmed this by the solemn ritual of washing his hands. All these things serve to confirm the merit of Christ and the certainty of our salvation, if at any time this should be called into doubt in the most grievous temptations.

units.la: {a} consedit, se innoxium haberi velle, protestetur: idq; ritu solenni ablutionis manuum confirmet. Faciunt haec omnia ad meritum Christi confirmandum & salutis nostrae certitudinem, si quando haec in tentationibus gravissimis in dubium venit.
units.tr: {a} [The governor], sitting as judge, wishes to be held innocent, and he confirms this by the solemn rite of washing his hands. All these things serve to confirm the merit of Christ and the certainty of our salvation, if at any time this comes into doubt in the gravest temptations.

units.la: Sed multum fallitur Pilatus, qui sceleris abs se commissi culpam leviculà ista manuum ablutione expiari posse putavit. In innocentia enim manus ablui debent, ut suo exemplo David monet. Sed hoc peiores sunt tyranni, qui hodie quando rivos Christiani sanguinis effundunt, abs qu omni metu laudem & gloriam sibi ex eo pollicentur. Pilatum quoq; impietate superant Judaei, quos Sacerdotum hypocrisis & authoritas ita fascinavit, ut Pilato protestationem tam gravem & horribilem interponenti respondeant: Sanguis eius super nos & filios nostros. Tales fiunt, qui falsis pontificibus se regendos praebent. Iusto igitur iudicio Deifactum, ut Pilatus ipsis dixerit, quod sacerdotes primum Judaeae dixerunt: Tu videris. Ut enim haec illi desperationis causa fuit: ita Judaeos illa adhuc angit & absorbet, dum relicto Christo in seipsos respiciunt. Quid vero de illis dicemus, qui dum falsis doctrinis & superstitionibus simpliciores decipiunt, tamen animas suas audacissime devouent, & sibi fidem habere volunt. Credant illis, quibus perire libet. Nos Deum timeamus, qui filii sui sanguinem a Judaeis iam olim requisivit, & adhuc hodie requirit. Et simul ad hunc diligendum nos accendat eius dem bonitas, qui tam multos ex Judaeis per Filium suum servavit: & per eundem indesinenter precemur, ut nos per spiritum suum illuminatos in via veritatis dirigat: ut in nobis glorificetur nomen eius & nos per illum in caelis viuamus & regnemus.
units.tr: But Pilate is greatly mistaken who thought that the guilt of a crime he had committed could be expiated by this slight washing of the hands. For hands ought to be washed in innocence, as David advises by his example. But the tyrants of today are worse, who, when they pour out streams of Christian blood, without any fear promise themselves praise and glory from it. The Jews also surpass Pilate in impiety, whom the hypocrisy and authority of the priests so bewitched that they answered Pilate, who made so grave and dreadful a protestation: "His blood be upon us and upon our children." Such become those who offer themselves to be ruled by false prelates. Therefore it was by a just judgment of God that Pilate said to them what the priests of Judaea had first said: "See to it yourselves." For as this was the cause of his despair, so it still torments and swallows up the Jews, while, having abandoned Christ, they look only to themselves. But what shall we say of those who, while they deceive the simpler sort with false doctrines and superstitions, nevertheless most boldly devote their souls and want to be trusted? Let them be believed by those to whom it pleases to perish. Let us fear God, who long ago required the blood of his Son from the Jews, and still requires it today. And at the same time let the goodness of him who has saved so many of the Jews through his Son kindle in us the love of him; and through the same Son let us constantly pray that he, having enlightened us by his Spirit, may direct us in the way of truth, so that his name may be glorified in us, and that through him we may live and reign in heaven.

units.la: HOMILIA CCCV.
units.tr: HOMILY CCCV.

units.la: Tunc milites praesidis, cum abduxissent IESVM in praetorium coegerunt ad eum universam cohortem: Et cum exuissent eum, circumposuerunt ei chlamydem coccinam: & coronam ex spinis contextam imposuerunt eius capiti, & arundinem in dexteram eius: & genu ante eum submissi illudentes ei, dicentes: Ave rex Iudaeorum. Et cum inspuissent in eum, acceperunt arundine illam, & verberabant caput eius. Et cum illusissent ei, exuerunt eum chlamyde, induerunt quae vestimentis suis, & abduxerunt eum, ut crucifigerent. Exeuntes autem invenerunt quendam Cyrenaeum, nomine Simonem, hunc angariauerunt ut portaret crucem eius.
units.tr: Then the soldiers of the governor, when they had led Jesus into the palace, gathered together the whole cohort around him. And when they had stripped him, they put a scarlet cloak about him, and set a crown plaited of thorns on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and kneeling before him they mocked him, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" And when they had spat upon him, they took the reed and struck his head. And when they had mocked him, they took off the cloak, put his own clothes on him again, and led him away to crucify him. As they went out, they found a Cyrenian named Simon, and they compelled him to carry his cross.

units.la: DOminus noster IESVS CHRISTVS, immaculatus ille agnus Dei, in cuius ore non est inuentus dolus, non solum falso accusatus & ab iniquo iudice iniuste damnatus est, ut nostra iustitia factus nos ab aeterna damnatione redimeret, verumetiam secus quam vulgo inter homines fieri solet, qui ergo facinorosos quoq; propter communem humanitatis sensum aliqua commiseratione tanguntur, inhumanissime & contumeliosissime tractatus est a Iudaeis & gentibus & (ut Isaias olim praedixerat) nouissimus vel contemptissimus virorum factus est, ut suo meritonos in gloriam filiorum Dei & regni caelestis consortium eueheret. De his in praesenti agitur, vbi duo potissimum commemorantur. Primum quid possit latam a Pilato capitis sententiam cum Christo actum sit in praetorio. Alterum quomodo ad supplicium ductus sit, quidq; inter eundem in via acciderit. De quibus breuiter ex ordine dicemus. Ad primum pertinet, quod praeses postquam relicto iustitiae tramite ad artes conuersus est, ne Iudaeos offenderet, innocentiam quidem Christi luculentum tulit testimonium, simul autem (ut apud Lucam annotatur) intulit: Caesigatum igitur illum dimittam. Et mox militibus, qui ipsum flagellarent tradidit. Quod post pronunciatam damnationis sententiam demum factum esse, nuper Matthaeus noster non obscure innuit, cum diceret: Dimisit eis Barabbam, Iesum autem flagellatum tradidit ut crucifigeretur. Erat autem flagellatio non leue tormentum, sed cum dolore gravissimo ignominiam habebat coniunctam. Etenim per se turpe & contumeliosum est, hominem ingenuum & honestum denudari: at simul miserum est, si hoc propter poenam fiat, quae sane grauis erat. Nam le...
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ, that spotless Lamb of God in whose mouth no deceit was found, was not only falsely accused and unjustly condemned by an unjust judge, so that, made our righteousness, he might redeem us from eternal damnation. He was also treated otherwise than is customary among men, for even criminals are usually spared some pity out of common human feeling. He was treated most inhumanly and most shamefully by the Jews and the Gentiles, and (as Isaiah had foretold long before) he became the lowest and most despised of men, so that by his merit he might raise us to the glory of the sons of God and to fellowship in the heavenly kingdom. These matters are the subject of the present passage, in which two things are chiefly recalled. The first is what was done with Christ in the palace after Pilate had pronounced the sentence of death. The second is how he was led to execution and what happened to him on the way. We shall speak briefly of these in order. As to the first, after the governor had left the path of justice and turned to devices, in order not to offend the Jews, he indeed bore a clear testimony to Christ's innocence; at the same time, however (as Luke notes), he said: "I will therefore chastise him and release him." And soon after he handed him over to the soldiers to be scourged. That this was done only after the sentence of condemnation had been pronounced our Matthew lately hinted plainly, when he said: "He released Barabbas to them, but having scourged Jesus he delivered him to be crucified." Now scourging was no light torment; it carried the greatest disgrace along with the great pain. For in itself it is shameful and humiliating for a free and respectable man to be stripped, and it is wretched too when this is done as a punishment, which was certainly severe. For the...

units.la: {m} ... non virgis modo aut flagellis vulgaribus, sed futicis caedebantur fontes, qui poenas capitales meruerant, quibus in lorum summitatibus aculei et vnci aerei aut ferrei annexi erant, quibus miseri ad offa vsq; et coitas lacerabantur: sicuti multis martyribus factum fuisse legimus. Itaq; ipsa morte gravius erat illud tormentum. Hoc ergo subire voluit Dei Filius, partim vt flagella morbo rum et dolorum, quibus carnem lasciuientem castigare in nobis solet Deus, sanctificaret: partim vt nobis exemplum patientiae praeberet. Cur enim nobis grave et molestum sit, si acutissimi mor bi suis aculeis artus nostros infestent et depascantur, viscera item calore diro torreant, vitam de niq; nobis acerbam faciant, ita deniq; nobis faciem et corpus totum deturpent, vt pleriq; ad con- spectum nostrum exhorreant, et nos aspicere dedignentur. Etenim hoc ipsum passus est Dominus ex iniqui et prophani iudicis decreto, qui ipsum postea toti populo spectaculum exhibuit: sperans ni mirum, Iudaeorum rabiem ita mitigari posse, ne quid gravius velint in illum statui. At plurimum spe sua falsus est, et in illo Spiritus sanctus exemplum praebet eorum, qui ignavia et carnis sua prudentia decepti, sub liberationis praetextu iniquius tractari sinunt eos, quos ex officio tueri debe bant. Hi enim non aliud proficiunt, quam quod crucifigere et crudelioribus supplicijs subijcere co guntur, quos ante flagellarunt. Huius ergo memores Christum in membris suis pro virili adiuue- mus et defendamus. Quod si nihil proficias apud impios pietatis hostes, protestationem sanctam interponito, ex qua omnes intelligant, te illorum consilijs non consentire, multo minus communica re sceleribus, quibus illi se polluunt. Sic olim Iosephus Arimathaeus fecit, quem Euangelica historia hoc nomine commendat.
units.tr: ...not only with rods or common whips, but with the scourge; those who had deserved capital punishment were beaten with thongs to whose ends were attached spikes and hooks of bronze or iron, by which the wretches were torn down to the bones and sinews. We read that this was done to many martyrs. So this torment was in fact more grievous than death itself. The Son of God chose to undergo it partly so that he might sanctify the lashes of the diseases and sufferings with which God is accustomed to chastise our wanton flesh, and partly so that he might give us an example of patience. For why should it be hard and troublesome for us if the most painful diseases attack and consume our limbs with their stings, if they burn our inner parts with dreadful heat, make our life bitter, and finally so disfigure our face and whole body that most people shrink from the sight of us and disdain to look at us? Indeed, the Lord himself suffered this by the decree of an unjust and profane judge, who afterwards displayed him as a spectacle to the whole people, hoping, no doubt, that the fury of the Jews could be so softened that they would not wish anything more severe to be decreed against him. But he was greatly deceived in his hope. In this, the Holy Spirit gives an example of those who, deceived by sloth and their own worldly prudence, under the pretext of setting people free allow those whom they ought to protect from office to be treated more unjustly. For these men achieve nothing other than being compelled to crucify, and to subject to crueler punishments, those whom they had first scourged. Mindful of this, then, let us help and defend Christ in his members to the best of our power. But if you accomplish nothing among the impious enemies of piety, then lodge a holy protest, by which everyone may understand that you do not consent to their counsels, and much less share in the crimes with which they pollute themselves. So once Joseph of Arimathea did, and the Gospel history commends him for this.

units.la: Sequitur nunc quod hoc loco narratur, quid nimirum milites praesidiarij fecerint, cum ad cru cis supplicium ex sacerdotum voluntate Dominum condemnatum esse intelligerent: quid item praeterea de illo fieri passus sit praeses. Non satiata fuit illorum crudelitas, nec ad miserationem eos movit iniuria et iniquitas, qua illum circumuentum et oppressum videbant: Sed abduxerunt in praetorium, et coegerunt illuc vniuersam cohortem, vt nouis contumelijs et iniurijs illum obrue- rent. Nec temere locus nominatur, vbi hoc factum sit, et a quibus. In praetorium enim abduxerunt. Ergo vt nuper in Pontificis aula Christo illuserunt sacerdotum seruuli, ita nunc in praetorio suo curia praesidis iniuste et contumeliose tractatur ab ijs, qui praesidio esse debebant bonum et malorum audaciam sine petulantiam iustis armis coercere. Ita vero adumbratur Christi seruos neq; in pra- sulum aulis, neq; principum politicorum palatijs tutos fore, si illi excusso Dei timore semel aduer- sus illum proteruire coeperint. Ab vtrisq; ergo sibi cauerant, quicunq; Christo vere et seriò nomen dederunt, et non abfq; graui causa dictum esse putent: Exeat ex aula qui pius esse velit.
units.tr: Now follows what this place narrates: what the soldiers of the garrison did when they understood that the Lord had been condemned by the will of the priests to the punishment of the cross, and what the governor further allowed to be done to him. Their cruelty was not satisfied, nor did the injustice and iniquity they saw him beset and overwhelmed by move them to pity. Instead they led him into the palace and gathered the whole cohort there, so that they might crush him with new insults and injuries. Nor is the place named without reason, where this was done and by whom. For they led him into the palace. Therefore, just as lately in the high priest's hall the servants of the priests mocked Christ, so now in the governor's own praetorium he is unjustly and shamefully treated by those who ought to be the guard, to restrain by just arms the audacity of the wicked, not their wantonness. Indeed, this shows in advance that the servants of Christ will not be safe either in the courts of prelates or in the palaces of political rulers, if once they have cast off the fear of God and begin to act insolently against him. Therefore let all who truly and earnestly have given their name to Christ take care against both, and let them think that this was said not without grave cause: let him who wishes to be godly depart from the court.

units.la: Quid vero fecerunt isti milites? Exuerunt eum suis vestibus, circumposuerunt autem chlamy- dem coccineam et coronam ex spinis contextam imposuerunt capiti eius, et arundinem dederunt in dextera eius. Singula haec in contemptum fiunt, et vt illi illudant. Purpura cum induunt, quam regiam vestem olim fuisse scimus. Hanc autem non togam aut trabeam esse volunt, sed chlamydem quam milites solebant vti. Coronam etiam imponunt, quae diadema regiu nomine referat: sed hanc non ex auro conflatam aut gemmis ornatam esse volunt, sed ex spinis contexunt. Sceptro quoq; manum ad dexteram armant, sed arundineo. Ex quibus apparet, illos Christo regu persona tri- buisse, sed per ludibrium. Occasionem vero ex eo arripiunt, quod illum regni affectati accusatum fuisse audiissent et scirent Iudaeos vulgo Messiam sperare, qui ipsis regnum esset instauraturus. Quare hac illusione suum in afferenda Rom. imperij maiestate studium publice testari, et simul Iudaeorum genti vniuersae insultare volunt. Et hunc illis animum fuisse, non obscure ex eo patet, quod flexo poplite et genu submissoper ludibrium salutant illum, dicentes: Aue Rex Iudaeorum. Adhaec inspuunt in eius faciem, quae extrema contumelia putatur, caput deniq; illius sceptro illo a- rundineo percutiunt. Ita vero rursus Christus poenam eam subit, quae nostris peccatis debebatur. Etenim Adam Deo similis fieri volens regnum aduersus hunc affectauit: et huius cupiditatis se- mina in nobis adhuc haerent. Et haec omnis generis peccata parit, et superbia illa est, qua Sapiens ille peccati principiu esse dixit. Cu ergo propter hanc ex regno Dei expelli et relegari mereremur Christus tam ignominiose et tanto cum ludibrio contemni voluit, vt nostra ambitionis scelus expiaret, qui adhuc non veremur aduersus Deum insurgere, et eius edictis, quae nobis Verbo suo praedicantur contradicere.
units.tr: But what did those soldiers actually do? They stripped him of his garments, and put a scarlet cloak about him and a crown plaited of thorns on his head, and gave him a reed in his right hand. Each of these things was done in contempt, to mock him. They put on him purple, which we know was once the royal garment. But they wish this to be not a toga or a trabea, but the cloak which soldiers were accustomed to wear. They also place a crown on him, which bears the name of the royal diadem; but they do not wish it to be made of gold or adorned with gems, but woven of thorns. They also arm his hand at the right with a sceptre, but one of reed. From these things it is clear that they assigned Christ the role of a king, but in mockery. They seized the occasion from this, because they had heard that he was accused of aspiring to the kingdom, and knew that the Jews commonly hoped for a Messiah who would restore the kingdom for them. Therefore by this mockery they wish to proclaim publicly their zeal for upholding the majesty of the Roman empire, and at the same time to insult the whole Jewish nation. That this was their intention is clear from the fact that, bending the knee and kneeling, they salute him in mockery, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" Besides, they spit in his face, which is considered the extreme of insult, and at last they strike his head with that reed sceptre. Thus again Christ undergoes that punishment which was owed for our sins. For Adam, wishing to become like God, aspired to a kingdom against him, and the seeds of this desire still cling to us. It gives birth to every kind of sin, and it is that pride which the wise man called the beginning of sin. Since we deserved to be cast out and banished from the kingdom of God because of this, Christ willed to be despised so shamefully and with such great mockery, so that he might atone for the crime of our ambition, we who still do not fear to rise against God and to contradict his edicts which are proclaimed to us in his Word.

units.la: Christus a militibus crudeliter illuditur.
units.tr: Christ is cruelly mocked by the soldiers.

units.la: Christus pecunam, quae nobis debebatur, luit.
units.tr: Christ pays the debt that was owed to us.

units.la: Interim hoc typo docemur, quale sit regnum Christi huius mundi iudicio. Est illi omnis potestas data in caelo & in terra, & regni eius non est finis, teste Angelo Gabriele. Sed longe aliud est hominum huius saeculi iudicium. Chlamydem siue paludamentum militare illi circumdant, quod putent esse regnum, quod perpetuis turbis & bellis infestetur. Praeterea corona Christi non auro & gemmis radiat, sed spinis horret: quia qui in illo volunt pie viuere, persecutionem patiuntur, & ideo curis, laboribus & periculis continuis exercentur. Praesidia item regni huius in mundo rara & infirma, adeoque arundinea sunt in terris: & quotidie nobis infelix mundus exprobrat, quod pio Regi Ezechiae impius Rapsakes. Sed neminem ista offendant. Est quidem nobis perpetuo luctandum cum mundo & eius principe; sed vicit hunc Christus, & nostra victoria fides est, qua ille a nobis apprehenditur. Curarum & laborum spinis perpetuis pungimur: sed in Christo gaudiis perpetuis exhilaramur, adeo ut in medijs afflictionibus gloriemur & exultemus. In mundo spes praesidij & auxilij nulla, sed Dominus est petra & arx nostra, quae nos aduersus portas inferorum tutos seruat. Et obserua hic admirabile Dei consilium, quo factum est, ut per milites Romanos Christus Rex designetur, qui illum & regnum eius maximis contumelijs obruere voluerunt. Nam quod illi per ludibrium fecerunt, Deus serio impleuit, & paulo post Pilatum mouit, ut publica authoritate hoc confirmaret, quando per inscriptionem Crucis IESVM Nazarenum dixit Iudaeorum regem esse, neque vllis Sacerdotum postulationibus sibi persuaderi passus est, ut hanc inscriptionem mutaret. Et quotidie videmus fieri, quod in Psalmis dicitur, quod etsi vilis & contemptae sit coram mundo Christi & regni eius conditio, adeo ut de torrente in via bibat, idem tamen in caelis ad dextram Patris considens, hostes suos scabellum pedibus suis subijcit, & super draconem & leones ambulat: deniq; qui sceptrum eius vix arundineum esse putant, illud ferreum esse experiuntur, dum ipse eos ut vasa fictilia comminuit. Ista nos consolentur, quorum eadem plane fors est. Insultat nobis mundus, & qui aliquo honore nos dignari videntur, id per ludibrium faciunt, & amaris Sarcasmis salutationes suas condiunt, adeoque spinis coronat nos: sed olim dabitur nobis corona iustitiae, quam Dominus reddet omnibus, qui illustrem suum aduentum expectant. Interim excitet nos exemplum Christi, ut coram illo humiliemur. Turpe enim & iniquum est, eos vel altum de scipsis sapere, vel superfluis ornamentis, & fastuoso corporis ornatu & cultu superbire, qui omnem salutis spem in Domino tam ignominiose flagellato, deluso & consputo habent repositam.
units.tr: Meanwhile this type teaches us what kind of kingdom Christ's is, by the judgment of this world. All power in heaven and on earth has been given to him, and of his kingdom there will be no end, as the angel Gabriel testifies. But the judgment of the men of this age is quite different. They put a soldier's cloak about him, because they think his kingdom is one that is troubled by constant tumults and wars. Moreover, Christ's crown does not shine with gold and gems but bristles with thorns, because those who want to live godly lives in him suffer persecution and are therefore kept busy with constant cares, labors and dangers. Likewise the defenses of this kingdom in the world are few and weak, and so in the earth they are as frail as a reed. Every day the unhappy world reproaches us, just as the impious Rabshakeh reproached the pious King Hezekiah. But let none of these things offend anyone. We must indeed wrestle continually with the world and its prince; but Christ has conquered him, and our victory is faith, by which he is grasped by us. We are pierced continually by the thorns of cares and labors, but in Christ we are cheered by perpetual joys, so that in the midst of afflictions we glory and exult. In the world there is no hope of protection or help, but the Lord is our rock and fortress, who keeps us safe against the gates of hell. And observe here the wonderful counsel of God, by which it came about that through the Roman soldiers Christ was designated king, though they wished to overwhelm him and his kingdom with the greatest insults. For what they did in mockery, God carried out in earnest, and shortly afterwards he moved Pilate to confirm this by public authority, when by the inscription on the cross he declared that Jesus of Nazareth was king of the Jews; and he allowed himself to be persuaded by no demands of the priests to change this inscription. And every day we see fulfilled what is said in the Psalms: although the condition of Christ and his kingdom is mean and despised before the world, so that he drinks from the brook by the way, yet he, sitting at the right hand of the Father in heaven, makes his enemies a footstool for his feet, and walks upon the dragon and the lions. Finally, those who think his scepter is scarcely a reed find that it is iron, while he crushes them like earthen vessels. Let these things console us, whose lot is clearly the same. The world insults us, and those who seem to think us worthy of some honor do so in mockery, and they season their greetings with bitter sarcasms, and so they crown us with thorns. But one day the crown of righteousness will be given to us, which the Lord will render to all who look for his glorious coming. Meanwhile let the example of Christ move us to be humbled before him. For it is shameful and wrong for those who have all their hope of salvation laid up in the Lord, so shamefully scourged, mocked and spat upon, either to think highly of themselves, or to take pride in superfluous ornaments and the showy adornment and care of the body.

units.la: Sed alterum quoque huius loci caput videamus. Exutum postea illa ludibria chlamyde purpurea, & suis vestibus rursus amictum ducunt extra urbem in locu supplicij. Vbi rursus multiplex nostrae redemptionis mysterium latet. Nam agnosci ab omnibus voluit Christus dum pateretur, neque illum puduit ignominiosae mortis, quam propter nos subiuit. Et proprijs vestibus indutus ducitur, ut sese in proprio corpore pati, & proprium sanguinem pro nobis fundere, denique nos proprio ipsius non alieno aut alterius merito, aut opera meritoria redemptos esse, testetur. Praeterea educitur extra urbem, ut nos in regnum caeleste introducat, & huius municipes faciat. Crucem quoque ipse effert extra portam, ut maledictionem, quae nobis ex peccato incumbit, a nobis auferat, ne posthac nobis illa imputetur.
units.tr: But let us also look at the second point of this passage. After the mockeries were finished, they strip him of the purple cloak and dress him again in his own garments, and lead him outside the city to the place of execution. Here again lies hidden the manifold mystery of our redemption. For Christ willed to be recognized by all while he suffered, and he was not ashamed of the ignominious death which he underwent on our account. He is led out clothed in his own garments, to testify that he suffered in his own body, shed his own blood for us, and that we have been redeemed by his own merit, not by that of another, nor by meritorious works. Moreover, he is led outside the city so that he may lead us into the heavenly kingdom and make us citizens of it. He himself also carries the cross outside the gate, so that he may take from us the curse which lies upon us because of sin, lest it be imputed to us henceforth.

units.la: Asi vbi urbem egressi fuerunt, obuium habent Simonem Cyrenaeum, ex agro (ut Marcus scribit) redeuntem, quem angariauerunt, ut crucem IESV portaret: nimirum, quod ijs, quae huc usque passus erat, defessus & viribus exhaustus, labori isti non amplius sufficeret. Adumbratur hic sanctorum & seruorum Dei fors. Sunt Cyrenaei, id est, peregrini in terris: studium vero ipsorum est, ex agro in urbem caelestem Ierosolymam contendere. Dum vero id faciunt, mox illis obuius venit Christus crucem gestans, & eos vocans, ut eandem ipsi quoque subeant. Id vero carni graue est, quae ab omnibus abhorret, quae vitae praesentis commoda & gaudia nobis turbant. Opus ergo est aliquibus, qui nos ut Simonem hunc, etiam inuitos cogant hanc operam Christo praestare. Sed non desunt hi. Habentur enim vbique gentium, qui Christum oderunt, & ideo perseguuntur omnes, qui in illo volunt pie viuere. Hic meminerimus, nos Filij Dei crucem ferre, & patientes simus. Quia vero Christi crux est, quicquid ferimus & patimur, huic quoque acceptam feramus nostrae salutis gloriam. Gestat quidem Christi crucem Simon, sed solus Dominus in eam suffigitur, non Simon, vt impurus Mahumet postea somniauit. Domino igitur soli omnis debetur gloria: quem precari debemus, vt ipse carnem nostram subigat, & ex inuitis & resistentibus in ferenda cruce eius sponte oblatos faciat, vt ipsum magnis pastibus subsequi & regnum illud beatum in cælis tandem ingredi possimus.
units.tr: And when they have gone out of the city, they meet Simon of Cyrene, returning from the field (as Mark writes), whom they compel to carry the cross of Jesus; clearly because he, worn out and exhausted in strength by what he had already suffered, was no longer equal to that labor. Here is depicted the lot of the saints and servants of God. They are Cyrenians, that is, strangers on earth; but their aim is to hasten from the field into the heavenly city, Jerusalem. And while they do this, Christ, carrying the cross, soon comes to meet them and calls them to undergo the same. This, however, is burdensome to the flesh, which shrinks from everything and which troubles us with the comforts and joys of the present life. Therefore there is need of some who, like this Simon, compel us even against our will to render this service to Christ. Yet such men are not lacking. For everywhere among the nations there are those who hate Christ, and therefore they persecute all who wish to live godly lives in him. Here let us remember that we, the sons of God, must bear the cross and be patient. And since it is Christ's cross, whatever we bear and suffer, let us bring it also to him, and attribute to him the glory of our salvation. Simon indeed carried Christ's cross, but the Lord alone was fastened to it, not Simon, as the impure Mahomet later dreamed. To the Lord alone, therefore, all glory is due; and we ought to pray that he himself subdue our flesh, and make us, who are unwilling and resisting, offer ourselves willingly to bear his cross, so that we may follow him with great steps and at last enter that blessed kingdom in the heavens.

units.la: HOMILIA CCCVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CCCVI.

units.la: Et cum venissent in locum, qui dicitur Golgatha, quod est Calvariæ locus, dederunt ei acetum bibendum cum felle mistum: & cum gustasset noluit bibere. Postquam autem crucifixerunt eum, partiti sunt eius vestimenta sortem iacientes, vt impleretur quod dictum est a Propheta: Partiti sunt sibi vestimenta mea, & super vestem meam iecerunt sortem. Et sedentes obseruabant eum illic. Et imposuerunt super caput eius crimen ipsius scriptum, Hic est IESVS Rex ille Iudæorum. Tunc crucifiguntur cum eo duo latrones: vnus ad dexteram, & alter ad sinistram. Qui vero prætereibant, conuitiabantur ei, mouentes capita sua, & dicentes: Tu qui destruis templum & triduo ædificas, serua temetipsum: si Filius Dei es, descende e cruce. Similiter autem etiam principes Sacerdotum illudentes cum Scribis & Senioribus, dicebant: Alios seruauit, seipsum non potest seruare: Si Rex Israel est, descendat nunc e cruce, & credemus ei: Confidit in Deo, liberet eum nunc si vult eum: dixit enim, Filius Dei sum. Idipsum autem etiam latrones, qui crucifixi erant cum eo, exprobrabant ei.
units.tr: And when they had come to the place called Golgotha, which is the place of the Skull, they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall; and when he had tasted it, he would not drink. After they had crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots, so that what was spoken by the Prophet might be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my vesture they cast lots." And they sat and watched him there. And they set over his head the charge written against him: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews." Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and the other on the left. Those who passed by reviled him, wagging their heads and saying: "You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself; if you are the Son of God, come down from the cross." Likewise also the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes and elders, said: "He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusts in God; let God deliver him now, if he wills it; for he said, I am the Son of God." The robbers who were crucified with him also reproached him in the same way.

units.la: Quoniam Dominus noster IESVS CHRISTVS non solum pro peccatis nostris passus est, vt ea sua mortis merito expiaret, verumetiam exemplar nobis præbuit, quod imitemur. Euangelistæ ex Spiritus sancti suggestione, quæcunq; in tota passionis & mortis eius historia acciderunt, diligenter ac prolixe describunt, vt exemplum hoc nostræ institutioni & consolationi magis seruiat. Vidimus id hucusq; in iis, quæ de eius captiuitate & vinculis dicta sunt, quam item iniquè & crudeliter in Sacerdotum concilio, in prætorio item a Iudæis & gentibus tractatus & damnatus sit. Sequitur in præsenti præcipua historiæ huius pars, qua supplicium, quod propter nos sustinuit, describitur. Summa omnium, quæ dicuntur, hæc est: Dei Filium morte omnium contumeliosissima multatum esse, & acerbissimos corporis & animi cruciatus sustinuisse ab hq; omnium commiseratione, insultantibus interim illi plerisq; omnis loci & ordinis hominibus. Ita vere implectum est, quod discipulis suis prædixerat: Amen amen dico vobis, flebitis & lamentabimini, mundus autem gaudebit. Sed vt minus offendamur, si quid huius nobis aut aliis in illum credentibus accidit, præstat singulas huius loci partes propius ex ordine considerare.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ suffered not only for our sins, so that by the merit of his death he might make atonement for them, but he also set before us an example to imitate. The Evangelists, at the prompting of the Holy Spirit, describe carefully and at length everything that happened in the whole history of his passion and death, so that this example may serve more fully for our instruction and comfort. We have seen this so far in what was said about his capture and bonds, and how unjustly and cruelly he was treated and condemned before the council of the priests and likewise in the praetorium, by the Jews and the Gentiles. In the present passage follows the principal part of this history, in which the punishment that he endured for our sake is described. The sum of all that is said is this: the Son of God was punished with the most shameful of deaths, and endured the most bitter torments of body and mind, while all pitied him, and meanwhile men of almost every place and rank mocked him. Thus truly was fulfilled what he had foretold to his disciples: "Amen, amen, I say to you, you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice." But so that we may be less offended if any of this happens to us or to others who believe in him, it is better to consider the individual parts of this place more closely, in order.

units.la: Primum locus notatur, quo Christum abduxerunt: Golgatha nimirum, id est, Calvariæ locum, fie haud dubie dictum a caluariis & ossibus mortuorum illic dispersis. Fuit ergo publicus locus supplicij extra vrbem, in quo fontes plectebantur, vt nomine infamis, ita aspectu quoq; horribilis. Facit hoc ad ignominiam mortis, quæ fere homines ingenui vehementius quam supplicio ipso dolent. Ita vero Deus Filium suum ex vrbe eijci voluit, quasi indignum hominum consortio, vt nobis in cælis locum & ciuitatem permanentem pararet. Ita hoc Apostolus exponit, qui ad veterem typum hoc referens ad Hebræos scribit: Quorum animalium sanguis per Pontificem infertur pro peccato, horum corpora exuruntur extra castra: Ideo & IESVS, vt sanctificaret per proprium sanguinem populum, extra portas passus est. Præterea suo exemplo & sanguine locos publicos supplicitorum sanctificauit, ne qui infamiam, quæ ex illis timetur vulgo, ad martyres sanctos redundare, aut etiam fontium & maleficorum saluti officere putet. Nam cum pro his quoq; mortuus sit Dominus, ipsi quoq; per illius meritum seruantur, si delictis suis ferio panitentiam, & illum fide vera ampliectantur.
units.tr: First, the place is noted to which they led Christ: Golgotha, that is, the place of the Skull, so called without doubt from the skulls and bones of the dead scattered there. It was therefore a public place of execution outside the city, where the guilty were punished, a place as infamous in name as it was horrible to behold. This has to do with the disgrace of death, which free men commonly grieve over more bitterly than the punishment itself. Thus God willed that his Son be cast out of the city, as if he were unworthy of fellowship with men, so that he might prepare for us a place and an abiding city in heaven. The Apostle explains it this way, referring it to the old type when he writes to the Hebrews: "The bodies of those animals whose blood is brought by the high priest as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp. Therefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside the gate." Moreover, by his example and his blood he sanctified the public places of execution, so that no one should think that the infamy that the common people fear from them reflects upon the holy martyrs, or even hinders the salvation of the guilty. For since the Lord also died for these, they too are saved through his merit, if they earnestly repent of their sins and embrace him with true faith.

units.la: Deinde

units.la: HOMILIA CCCVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CCCVI.

units.la: Deinde dederunt ei acetum bibendum cum felle mixtum, quod Marcus myrrhatum vinum dicit, quod inter vina aromatibus condita Plinius numerat, qualia reis ad mortem damnatis data solita fuisse, ex eo colligi potest, quod Solomon scripsit: Date siceram morituro, et vinum iis, qui amaro sunt animo. Marcus ergo myrrhatum vinum dixit, ad id respiciens, quod vulgo fiebat: Matthaeus vero clarius docet qualis potus fuerit: mistura videlicet amara, quae turbaret mas gis maerentem quam refocillaret: et ita nim obscure perstringit Iudaeorum ingratitudinem et barbaram militum petulantiam, qui contra morem vulgo receptum, hoc quoque solamen Christo negarunt, quo sceleratii et facinorosi recreari solebant. At hoc etiam seruiebat nostrae redemptionis mysterio. Debuit etiam Dei Filius omni solatio destitui in terris, ut nos in illo omni consolatione repleremur, et nobis in conspectum Patris sui accessum liberum faceret, in quo (ut David ait) esse satietas laetitiarum. Sed cum potum nunc gustaUisset noluit bibere: non quod aliquid eorum detestari ferre, quae ipse Pater aeterno decreto ininuxerat: sed ut exemplo suo doceret, licere interdum nobis adversa et incommoda declinare, quando nimirum abs fandalo publico, et falsa conscientia potest fieri. Ideo alibi fugam quoque discipulis concessit: nec vult, ut nos temere in pericula non necessaria conijciamus.
units.tr: That they then gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink, which Mark calls wine mixed with myrrh, can be gathered from the fact that Solomon wrote, "Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to those who are bitter of soul." Pliny counts wines seasoned with aromatics among the wines of his time, and it seems such drinks were usually given to criminals condemned to death. Mark therefore spoke of wine mixed with myrrh, having regard to what was commonly done. Matthew teaches more clearly what kind of drink it was: a bitter mixture, which would trouble the sufferer more than refresh him. In this way he obscurely points out the ingratitude of the Jews and the savage wantonness of the soldiers, who, contrary to the custom commonly received, denied Christ even this comfort, which criminals and wrongdoers were accustomed to be given. But this too served the mystery of our redemption. The Son of God had to be deprived of every comfort on earth, so that we might be filled with all consolation in him, and so that he might open for us free access into the presence of his Father, in whom (as David says) there is fullness of joys. But when he had tasted the drink, he would not drink it. This was not because he refused to bear anything that the Father himself had decreed by his eternal counsel, but so that by his example he might teach us that it is sometimes lawful to avoid adversity and hardship, namely when this can be done without public scandal and with conscience intact. For this reason he also elsewhere permitted his disciples to flee, and he does not want us to throw ourselves rashly into dangers that are not necessary.

units.la: Postquam propinatum ei potum hunc, in crucem illum suffixerunt, quo loco crucis supplicium confidenter adeundum venit. Fuit hoc (ut alibi monuimus) dirum et infame, et cum maledictione coniunctum, ut ex Mose apparet, qui cum iuberet fontium corpora ante Solis occasum ex cruce tollere, hanc rationem adduxit: Maledictus Deo est, qui pendet in ligno. At Paulo interprete, maledictio fieri voluit Christus pro nobis, ut nos in illo benediceremur, qui est promissum illud Abraha mi femine. Itaque crux illi altaris loco fuit. Nam in eo seipsum Patri immolavit pro peccatis nostris: et simul cruces omnes, quae nobis adhuc incumbunt, sanctificavit, ne animarum saluti noceant. Interim hoc tam diro Filii Dei supplicio, arguitur peccati atrocitas, quae non aliter potuit expiari, et offenditur, inutiles et vanas esse omnes alias, quae extra Christum finguntur, peccatorum expiationes: Si quae enim alia esset, nunquam hanc tam diram decreuisset Deus, qui et sapientia et charitas ipsa est. Vno igitur Christo contenti, interim sanctitati studeamus, nec nos rursus pollua mus sceleribus, a quorum sordibus nos tanto pretio redimi oportuit. Caeterum iam in crucem suspenso Filio Dei, ista facta sunt, de quibus deinceps dicetur.
units.tr: After they had offered him this drink, they fastened him to the cross, the place where he came willingly to endure the punishment of the cross. This punishment was (as we have shown elsewhere) dreadful and infamous, and joined with a curse, as appears from Moses, who, when he commanded that the bodies of those hanged be taken down from the cross before sunset, gave this reason: "He who hangs on a tree is accursed of God." But, as Paul interprets, Christ willed to become a curse for us, so that in him we might be blessed, he who is that promised seed of Abraham. Thus the cross was for him in the place of an altar. For on it he offered himself to the Father for our sins, and at the same time he sanctified all the crosses that still press upon us, so that they may not harm the salvation of our souls. Meanwhile, by this so dreadful punishment of the Son of God, the atrocity of sin is shown, which could not otherwise be expiated, and it is shown that all other expiations of sins that are invented apart from Christ are useless and vain. For if there were any other, God, who is wisdom and love itself, would never have decreed this so dreadful a thing. Therefore, content with Christ alone, let us meanwhile strive for holiness, and let us not defile ourselves again with crimes, from the filth of which we ought to have been redeemed at so great a price. Moreover, now that the Son of God was already hanging on the cross, these things were done, which will be spoken of next.

units.la: Primum fuit, quod milites vestimenta eius inter se partiti sunt: quod ex publico more factum esse, non dubium est: quia autem inter illa erat tunica inconsutilis, quae commode dissecari non poterat, maioris autem pretij videbatur, quam ut vni soli deberet cedere, forte iecerunt super illam, ut Ioannes annotavit. Ita vero implevit est, quod olim in typo acciderat Davidi, et quod in Psal mo non obscure praedictum fuit. Quo loco pauperas Christi consideratur: qui dum in terris viuret, non habuit, ubi caput suum reclinaret: nunc vero nudus quoque in cruce pendet, et adhuc vivus videt suas vestes in barbarorum militum manus peruenire, qui earum aliquas infamis aleae forti subiiciunt. Ita vero ad ignominiam, quam subiuit Dei Filius, hoc quoque accessit. Pertinuit autem iste ad nostrae redemptionis mysterium. Etenim Adam Dei mandatum transgressus, innocentiae vestes, quae illum ornauerat Deus, amisit: et ex eo infamis nuditas ad nos peruenit, ut nec coram Deo consistere, neque inter nos absque molestia, quam vestitus necessitas parit, honeste versari possimus. At Christus sua nuditate nobis meruit, ut et coram facie Dei coparere nobis liceat, et ut ex paupertate et inopia spiritualium bonorum, nihil ad animas nostras incommodi redeat. Propter nos enim pauper factus est Dei Filius, ut nobis caelestium opum thesauros acquireret, et in caelis divites faceret. 2. Cor. 8.
units.tr: First, the soldiers divided his garments among themselves. That this was done according to public custom is not in doubt. But since among them was the seamless tunic, which could not conveniently be cut up, and which seemed too valuable to belong to one man alone, they cast lots over it, as John noted. In this way what had once happened in type to David was fulfilled, and what had been foretold not obscurely in the Psalm. Here the poverty of Christ is considered. While he lived on earth, he had no place where he might lay his head; now, naked, he hangs on the cross, and while still alive he sees his garments pass into the hands of the barbarous soldiers, who stake some of them on a shameful game of dice. Thus this also was added to the disgrace which the Son of God endured. Moreover, this pertained to the mystery of our redemption. For Adam, having transgressed God's command, lost the garments of innocence with which God had adorned him, and from that time the shameful nakedness came down to us, so that we could neither stand before God nor live honourably among one another without the trouble that the need for clothing brings. But Christ by his nakedness merited for us that it should be lawful for us to appear before the face of God, and that, from the poverty and want of spiritual goods, no harm should come to our souls. For the Son of God became poor for our sake, so that he might acquire for us the treasures of heavenly riches and make us rich in heaven. 2 Cor. 8.

units.la: At simul suo exemplo nobis patientiam commendat, ne nobis graue fit, si quando facultates nostrae hostibus praedae fiunt. Militibus cedunt vestes Domini, et hoc quidem non ipso solo, sed Matre et Ioanne dilecto discipulo spectantibus. At patienter hoc ille tulit, non quid humanus affectus aut carnis ratio dictaret, respiciens, sed quid Pater constituisset, qui de hoc olim suam voluntatem revelarat. Ita nos cogitemus fluxa esse et incerta quaecunque in terris possidemus: aeternam autem et certam esse eorum haereditatem et possessionem, quae nobis in caelis reposita sunt. Itaque ad ea aspiremus, terrestres autem exuuias, si ita velit Deus, relinquamus ijs, qui a caelestibus exclusi sunt. Ne ergo curemus, in cuius manum et potestatem toties deveniant: sed Deo illa commendemus et aequis oculis hostes etiam intueamur, si hoc illa Deus dederit. Nec dubium nobis sit, hunc nostra distribuere pro sua bona et iusta voluntate. Haec autem nobis praecipua cura sit, ne luxus, vestitus et fastus superbo, qui huc fere comitatur, Dei oculos offendamus. Nec enim hunc in nobis feret Deus, qui Filium in cruce nudum videre voluit. Et insolens nimium et turpis est eorum luxus et fastus, qui Christi nudi merito confidunt et gloriantur, illo adhuc in tot membris suis egente et algente.
units.tr: At the same time, by his example he commends patience to us, so that it may not be grievous to us if at any time our possessions become plunder for our enemies. The Lord's garments fall to the soldiers, and this happened not only in the sight of the soldiers but also of his Mother and of the beloved disciple John. Yet he bore it patiently, not looking to what human feeling or the reason of the flesh might dictate, but to what the Father had determined, who had long before revealed his will concerning this. So let us consider that whatever we possess on earth is fleeting and uncertain, but that the inheritance and possession that are laid up for us in heaven are eternal and sure. Therefore let us aspire to those things, and let us leave earthly spoils, if God so wills, to those who have been shut out from heavenly things. Let us not, then, be anxious into whose hand and power they come so often; rather let us commend them to God, and look even on enemies with an equal eye, if God has given them these things. Nor let there be any doubt that he distributes our goods according to his good and just will. Let this, however, be our chief care: that we not offend God's eyes by luxury, dress and pride, which commonly accompany such things. For God will not bear this in us, he who willed his Son to be seen naked on the cross. Excessively insolent and shameful is the luxury and pride of those who trust in and boast of the merit of the naked Christ, while he is still in want and cold in so many of his members.

units.la: Deinde de militibus et eorum praefecto et sociis dicit Evangelista, quod sedentes illinc Christum servarint. Id vero etiam non sine certa causa et divina providentia consilio factum est. Solet hoc vulgo fieri, ut si qui propter facinora aliqua mortis supplicio plectantur, publici magistratus tuam servi aut milites locum supplicij custodiant, donec illi expiarint, et sententia contra eos lata satisfactam sit. Nec dubium est idem hic voluisse Iudaeorum sacerdotes, cum postea, ut milites sepulchro apponantur, postularint. Sed altius praeterea mysterium hic subest. Nam inter hos aliquos electos fuisse postea patebit, qui visis ijs, quae mortem Christi secuta sunt, expansa fide confessionem adiderunt: Ilios hac occasione illic retinere voluit Deus, ut mors Christi certo omnibus constaret (quod et milites postea apud Praesidem testificati sunt) et maiorem illi omnes ad poenitentiam haberent occasionem. Nihil ergo putemus temere fieri, etiamsi non semper prima fronte appareat, quae sit consilij divini, quo omnia gubernantur, ratio.
units.tr: Next, the Evangelist speaks of the soldiers, their commander and their companions, that sitting there they kept watch over Christ. This too was done not without a definite cause and by the counsel of divine providence. It is customary for this to be done commonly: when some are punished by death for certain crimes, public magistrates' servants or soldiers guard the place of punishment until those men have expiated their guilt and the sentence passed against them has been carried out. There is no doubt that the chief priests of the Jews wished the same thing here, when afterwards they asked that soldiers be placed at the tomb. But there is also a deeper mystery here. For it will later become clear that some of these men were chosen, who, having seen the things that followed the death of Christ, openly confessed their faith. God wished them to remain there for this occasion, so that the death of Christ might be established with certainty for all (as the soldiers also later testified before the governor), and so that all might have a greater occasion for repentance. Let us therefore think that nothing is done rashly, even if the reason of the divine counsel, by which all things are governed, does not always appear at first sight.

units.la: Sequitur, quod qui Christum crucifixerunt, super caput eius crimen, id est, titulum sive schedam, in qua crimen vel causa, propter quam crucifixus esset, impositum fuerit. Quod etiam ex more publico factum fuit. Cum autem non aliud haberet, quod scriberet Pilatus, scripsit: HIC EST IESVS REX IVDAEORVM. Quod illum in Iudaeorum contumeliam scripsisse, ex Ioanne apparet. Displicuit enim sacerdotibus hoc scriptum, quod nimirum ipsos adhuc regis illius puderet. Sed Pilatus tandem importunitatis et iniquitatis illorum pertaesus, cum respondisset, ab hero eos reiecit: Quod scripsi, scripsi. Manifit ergo titulus ille supra caput Christi in cruce pendentis, et quidem tribus linguis, quae tunc in toto orbe praecipuae erant: Ita nimirum Spiritu Sancto rege mente manum Praesidis, ut huius testimonio Christus toti orbi notus fieret, ipsum regem esse omnium, qui ipsum fatentur et talem fore perpetuo, obstrepentibus licet et frementibus omnibus, qui aduersus ipsum tumultuantur. Quia enim prophani iudicis animum confirmavit Deus, ut quod scripserat, perferat, noluerit mutare in pontificum gratiam, multo magis rata esse perpetuo voluit, quae ipsi notarij et amanuenses, Prophetae et Apostoli ex Spiritus Sancti inspiratione scripserunt. Quae consideratio nos consolari et infide confirmare debet, si quando pontifices cum regibus aduersus Christum conspirasse videmus. Hoc enim Dei decretum est, ut ipse in Sion monte suo sancto regnum teneat. Psal. 2.
units.tr: There follows the fact that those who crucified Christ placed above his head the charge, that is, the title or placard, on which the crime or cause for which he was crucified was written. This too was done according to public custom. Since Pilate had nothing else to write, he wrote: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS. That he wrote this to mock the Jews appears from John. For the chief priests were displeased with this inscription, since they were evidently ashamed of that king. But Pilate, at last weary of their importunity and injustice, when they had objected, dismissed them with the answer: "What I have written, I have written." That title was therefore placed clearly above the head of Christ hanging on the cross, and indeed in three languages, which were then the chief ones in the whole world. Thus, undoubtedly, by the Holy Spirit guiding the mind of the governor's hand, through this testimony Christ was made known to the whole world: that he is the king of all who confess him and will be such forever, though all who rage against him rage and clamour. For since God strengthened the mind of the profane judge so that he might let stand what he had written, and would not change it for the favour of the chief priests, much more did he will that those things be established forever which the scribes, the prophets and apostles wrote under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. This consideration ought to comfort us and confirm us in faith, whenever we see the high priests conspiring with kings against Christ. For this is God's decree, that he himself should reign on his holy mountain, Zion. Psalm 2.

units.la: Annotatur praeterea, qui nam Christo supplicij tam diri et infamis socij fuerint? Duo nimirum latrones, quorum unus ad dexteram eius, alter ad sinistram suspensus est, ipso nimirum medio et in altiore cruce pendentes. Ita impletum fuit, quod Isaias praedixerat, ipsum maleficis et facinorosis adnumerandum fore. Ita enim debebat illi fieri, qui totius mundi peccata in se recepit, ut illorum reatum expiaret. Nos vero dum ista audimus, semper ferio cogitemus, quanti constiterit humani generis redemptio, et quam ferio nobis adiugilandum sit, ne ipsidem laqueis nos rursum circumvenat Satan, ex quibus nos liberavit Dei Filius.
units.tr: It is further noted who the companions were of Christ in so dreadful and infamous a punishment. Two robbers, namely, one hanging on his right hand and the other on his left, while he himself hung in the middle, on the higher cross. Thus was fulfilled what Isaiah had foretold, that he would be numbered among evildoers and criminals. For so it had to happen to him who took upon himself the sins of the whole world, in order to expiate their guilt. When we hear these things, let us always think seriously about how costly the redemption of the human race was, and how earnestly we must be on guard, lest Satan ensnare us again in the same snares from which the Son of God has freed us.

units.la: Restat ultima huius loci pars, qua spectatorum de Christo iudicia narrantur, et hos quidem omnes consensisse apparet in eo, quod eum improbe contempserunt. Nam qui praeteribant (in quit Evangelista) convicitabantur ei, monentes capita sua, et dicentes, etc. Convicitia maligni animi odium et inimicitiam implacabilem indicant. Caput vero motio petulantiam arguit, quae eo usque progressa est, ut (quod nemo bonus et honestus facit) non convicitari modo sint homines, tam poenas exoluenti pro delictis, verumetiam verbis simul et gestibus immodestis illi illuserunt. Et hoc quidem omnes in genere fecerunt: quo exemplo arguitur ingenium omnium, qui carnis sensu in religionis causa ducuntur. Solent hi ex praesenti statu et fortuna indicare, quod hodie frequentissimum est, et multos turpiter fallit. Caeterum inopiam iudicij et impium odij concepti virus alij alijs acutius & amarulentius produnt. Alij quod de templo dixerat, & quod falsi testes calumniose in sinistrum sensum detorquerant, exprobrant, vt in crucem suspenso maiorem inuidiam conflent: Tu qui destruis templum & triduo aedificas, serua teipsum. Similes sunt, qui hodie quicquid animo se dictum est a pijs, ipsis insidiose exprobrant, si quando finistre illis res succedunt. Alij maiori cum impietate fidem eius tentant, vt se falsa perfuasione deceptum putet, dicentes: Si Filius Dei es, descende e cruce. At quid hi aliud dicunt quam Satan, qui in deserto esurienti, dicebat: Si Filius Dei es, dic lapidibus istis, vt fiant panis. Rursus autem non contenti eo, insuper vt aliorum quoque fidem labefactent, etiam miracula omnia, quibus multi crediderant, in dubium trahunt, cum dicunt: Alios seruauit, seipsum non potest seruare. At quoties fit, vt qui alios saepe seruauit, ipse periclitetur? Num vero beneficijs quae in alios contulit, nulla debetur gratia? Alij item crassius & impudentius aiunt: Si Rex Israel est, descendat nunc e cruce, & credemus ei. Atqui maius miraculum aediderat in Lazari ex mortuis refuscitatione, qua visa adeo non credidérunt, vt magis exacerbati sint, & de Lazaro etiam occidendo cogitarint. Maius item fuit, quod postea ex mortuis resurrexit, & ne tunc quidem illi crediderunt. Deniq; sunt, qui fidem in Deum illi exprobrent, quam nemo facile reprehendit, qui communi sensu ducitur. Neq; Sacerdotes modo & Scribae atq; Seniores cum militibus & vulgo ignorante haec exprobrant, verumetiam latrones cum illo crucifixi. Narrantur autem ista, ne offendamur, si quid huius hodie fiat: sed firmiter credamus Dei promissiones semper ratas fore, & illarum veritatem non pendere ab euentis huius seculi: quos Deus moderatur, prout illos suae gloriae, & multorum institutioni ac saluti conducere nouit. Porro incidit hic memorabilis latronum actio, de qua cum in Luca copiose dictum sit, nolumus hoc loco plura addere. Oremus autem Deum Patrem miserationum, vt fidem suorum electorum confirmet aduersus similes illusiones, & hostium suorum conuitia & sannas coerceat, vt tandem desinant maledicere veritati, & nomen Filij sui glorificetur cum multorum aedificatione ad salutem aeternam. Amen.
units.tr: What remains is the last part of this passage, in which the judgments of the onlookers concerning Christ are related. It is clear that all of them agreed in this, that they shamelessly despised him. For those who passed by (says the Evangelist) reviled him, wagging their heads and saying, etc. Reproaches reveal a malicious mind and an implacable hatred. Wagging the head indicates wantonness, which went so far that (as no good and decent person does) they not only reviled a man who was paying the penalty for his crimes, but also mocked him with insolent words and gestures. All of them in general did this, and by this example the disposition of all those is exposed who are led by carnal sense in matters of religion. They are accustomed to judge from present circumstances and fortune, which is very common today and shamefully deceives many. Moreover, they betray their lack of judgment and the venom of impious hatred, some more sharply and bitterly than others. Some throw back at him what he had said about the temple, and what the false witnesses had maliciously twisted into a wrong sense, so as to stir up greater hatred against the one hanging on the cross: "You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself." They are like those who today insidiously throw back at the godly whatever has been said by them in good faith, whenever things go badly for them. Others test his faith with greater impiety, so that he may think himself deceived by a false persuasion, saying: "If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross." But what do these say other than Satan, who said to the hungry one in the desert: "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread." Again, not content with this, and in order to weaken the faith of others also, they call into doubt all the miracles by which many had believed, saying: "He saved others; he cannot save himself." But how often does it happen that one who has often saved others is himself in danger? Surely no gratitude is owed for the benefits he conferred on others? Others again say more crudely and shamelessly: "If he is the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him." Yet he had performed a greater miracle in raising Lazarus from the dead, and though they saw it they did not believe, but were so much more enraged that they even planned to kill Lazarus. Greater still was his later resurrection from the dead, and even then they did not believe in him. Finally, there are those who reproach him for his faith in God, which no one of ordinary sense would easily find fault with. And these things are said not only by the chief priests, scribes and elders along with the soldiers and the ignorant crowd, but also by the robbers crucified with him. These things are related so that we may not be offended if anything of the kind happens today; rather, let us firmly believe that God's promises will always stand, and that their truth does not depend on the outcomes of this age, which God governs as he knows to be useful for his glory and for the instruction and salvation of many. Moreover, the memorable act of the robbers occurs here, about which, since it has been related at length in Luke, we do not wish to add more in this place. Let us pray to God the Father of mercies that he will confirm the faith of his elect against similar mockeries, and restrain the reproaches and sneers of his enemies, so that at last they may cease to speak evil of the truth, and the name of his Son may be glorified, with the building up of many unto eternal salvation. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CCCVII.
units.tr: Homily 307.

units.la: A sexta autem hora tenebrae factae sunt super vniuersam terram vsq; ad horam nonam. Circiter vero horam nonam exclamauit IESVS voce magna, dicens: Eli, eli lama sabachthani? Hoc est, Deus meus, Deus meus, cur deseruisti me? Quidam autem ex iis qui illic stabant, cum hoc audissent, dicebant, Eliam vocat iste. Et statim currens quidam ex eis, cum acceptam spongiam impleuisset aceto, & circumposuisset calamo, dedit ei vt biberet. Reliqui vero dicebant: Sine videamus an veniat Elias seruaturus eum. Iesus autem cum rursum clamasset voce magna, emisit spiritum. Et ecce, aulaeum templi scissum est in duas partes a summo vsq; ad imum: & terra mota est, & petrae fissae sunt. Et monumenta aperta sunt: & multa corpora sanctorum qui dormierunt, surrexerunt. Qui egressi e monumentis post resurrectionem eius, introierunt in sanctam urbem & apparuerunt multis. Centurio autem & qui cum eo erant seruantes IESVM, visso terraemotu & ijs quae facta erant, timuerunt vehementer, dicentes: Vere Filius Dei erat iste.
